# Source analysis вЂ” Terraria 1.4.5.8

All figures below come from decompiling the retail `Terraria.exe` (v1.4.5.8, 25.4 MB) with
ILSpy into `decompiled/` (1 549 `.cs` files) and `ReLogic.dll` into `decompiled-libs/ReLogic`
(167 files).

## World file format (`.wld`)

Reference: `Terraria.IO.WorldFile.LoadWorld_Version2` (line 1784) and `LoadWorldTiles`
(line 2543); v2 sectioned format, supported here for version в‰Ґ 87 (current saves are 279+).

```
i32 version
[20 bytes FileMetadata]                (version >= 135)
i16 sectionCount
i32 sectionPointers[sectionCount]      header, tiles, chests, signs, NPCs, ...
u16 tileTypeCount
bit-packed bool[importance]            which tile types store explicit frames
--- section 0: header ---
string name
string seed, u64 worldGenVersion      (version >= 179)
16 bytes GUID                          (version >= 181)
i32 worldId, left, right, top, bottom
i32 maxTilesY      <-- note: Y comes first
i32 maxTilesX
... world flags
--- section 1: tiles ---
for x in 0..maxTilesX:                 column-major, RLE per column
  b4 flags: active, wall, liquid type, RLE length bits
  optional b1/b2/b3 bitfields (frame importance, paint, actuator, slope...)
  tile type (u8 or u16), frameX/frameY (i16) only for important types
  wall id, liquid amount, RLE repeat count
```

Tile flags we map 1:1 into a packed 16-byte struct (`tr-core/src/tile.rs`): active,
half-brick, actuator, inactive, fullbright, liquid kind, liquid amount, slope, paint, wall,
plus the computed wall autotile cell (`wall_col`, `wall_row`).

### The tile section's four wire bits (S1-J-1, 2026-11-14)

The C# keeps the four wire colours inside the tile's own headers: `wire()`,
`wire2()` and `wire3()` are `sTileHeader` bits 0x80/0x100/0x200
(`Tile.cs:623-672`) and `wire4()` is a `bTileHeader` bit 0x80
(`Tile.cs:437-452`). `SaveWorldTiles` writes them into the chained header
bytes вЂ” `b2` 0x02/0x04/0x08 for the three `sTileHeader` wires and `b3` 0x20 for
`wire4()` (`WorldFile.cs:1508-1532`) вЂ” and `LoadWorldTiles` restores them
(`:2614-2632`, `:2651-2654`), with `CopyFrom` (`:2711`) copying them into every
row of an RLE run.

The port stores the colours in the sparse `World.wires` table (the packed
12-byte `Tile` has no header space вЂ” see the wiring deviation below), so the
writer reads them from there and the reader writes them back. The bytes are
the C#'s: the tile section of a fixture world is byte-identical to the output
of a `dotnet` run of the decompiled `SaveWorldTiles` (the golden fixture in
`wld/mod.rs::s1_j_1_the_tile_section_matches_the_csharp_bytes`).

The second half of the fix is the **batching equality**: `Tile.isTheSameAs`
compares the packed `sTileHeader` (`Tile.cs:161`), and the wire bits live in
it вЂ” so two tiles that differ only by a wire are **not** batched
(`WorldFile.cs:1577`). The port's `encoded_same` now compares the four colours
too, which makes the RLE run boundaries match the C#'s.

### The eleven sections (all eleven ported, both directions вЂ” M6-SAVE-1, 2026-11-09)

`SaveWorld_Version2:1150-1165` / `LoadWorld_Version2:1760-1851`: a 70-byte prologue
(`i32 326` + the 20-byte `FileMetadata` + `i16 11` + the eleven `i32` section **end**
offsets), then the sections in this order, then the footer triple
`(true, worldName, worldId)`. `wld/mod.rs` assembles/backfills the table;
`wld/sections/<name>.rs` is each codec; the reader's end-offset assertions are
reproduced (`bad section pointer N`).

| # | Section | Wire shape | Rust |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | file-format header | `u16 TileID.Count` + the 95-byte importance bitmap | `sections/header.rs` |
| 1 | world header + flags | name, seed text + generator version, GUID, world id + bounds, `maxTilesY` before `maxTilesX`, then the ~2200-byte flags block in `LoadWorldFlags` order | `sections/header.rs` + `flags.rs` (incl. the rain and sandstorm snapshots) |
| 2 | tiles | column-major RLE (see above) | `sections/tiles.rs` |
| 3 | chests | `i16 count` (+ the shared `i16` slot count below 294), then per chest `(i32 x, i32 y, string name, i32 maxItems, maxItems Г— i16/i16/i32/u8)`; the duplicate-position and tail passes, the `<115` dresser pass, `Chest.FixLoadedData`, and the save-side dead-anchor pre-pass | `sections/chests.rs` + `tr-app/chest.rs::{from_wld,to_wld,fix_dresser_chests,destroy_invalid_anchors}` |
| 4 | signs | `i16 count`, then `(string text, i32 x, i32 y)` per sign over `Main.sign[0..31999]`; the tile check + dup + tail passes on load | `sections/signs.rs` (the store lives on `World.signs`) |
| 5 | NPCs | the shimmer bitmap's truth indices (`>= 268`), the terminator-delimited town list (`i32 netID` or the `<190` name, `string GivenName`, `Vector2`, `bool homeless`, the home pair, a `BitsByte` gating `townNpcVariationIndex` `>= 213` and `homelessDespawn` `>= 315`), then the four-tower list (`>= 140`) | `sections/npcs.rs` + `tr-app/npc.rs::{from_wld,to_wld}` |
| 6 | tile entities | `i32 count`, then per entity `(u8 ty, i16 x, i16 y)` + the type's `ReadExtraData`; the id reassignment, the `InWorld`/`CheckValidTile` drop pass, `OnWorldLoaded`, and the display doll's payload skip-reads | `sections/tile_entities.rs` |
| 7 | pressure plates | `i32 count`, then `(i32 x, i32 y)` per pressed point (the `bool[255]` weights are runtime state) | `sections/pressure_plates.rs` (`World.pressure_plates`) |
| 8 | TownManager rooms | `i32 count`, then `(i32 npcID, i32 x, i32 y)` pairs | `sections/town_rooms.rs` + `tr-app/town.rs::TownRooms` |
| 9 | Bestiary | three sub-lists: kills (`i32 count` + `(string creditId, i32 count)`), sights and chats (`i32 count` + one credit id each) | `sections/bestiary.rs` + `tr-core/bestiary.rs::WorldBestiary` (`App.bestiary`) |
| 10 | CreativePowers | **terminator-delimited**: `{ bool true; ushort id; payload }` repeated until `bool false`; toggles write `bool Enabled`, the two sliders write the `[0,1]` `_sliderCurrentValueCache` | `sections/creative_powers.rs` + `tr-app/creative.rs` |

The C#'s own section numbering is 0-based in `positions[]` and 1-based in the prose;
`WorldFile.SaveBestiary:3396` is the **1-based 10th** section (pointer 9), and
`SaveCreativePowers:3412` is the 11th (pointer 10).

The app glue (M6-SAVE-1 phase 7): `app/mod.rs::load_world` calls
`wld::load_with_sections` (one read: world + sections) and applies the world-state
halves in the C#'s order вЂ” signs, tile entities, pressure plates вЂ” before the framing
passes; `App::new` applies the App-owned halves вЂ” chests (the file's store displaces the
load-time re-roll, the `<115` dresser fix-up gated on the file version), the NPC list
(replacing the startup spawns, then `FixAgainstExploits:1861`'s home re-validation with
the town rooms), the shimmer bitmap, the bestiary tracker and the creative powers.
`saveglue::save_world` dispatches on the extension: `.trwld` в†’ the native writer plus the
sidecars (unchanged), `.wld` в†’ `wld::save` with every section built from the live state
(the chests' dead-anchor pre-pass first, as the C# runs it). The autosave, F9, close and
quit paths all funnel through `save_world`.

The autosave cadence is `Main.DoUpdate_AutoSave` (`Main.cs:19737-19771`, called from `Main.Update`'s
`!WorldGen.generatingWorld` guard, `Main.cs:16943-16946`). Its three arms: `!gameMenu &&
netMode == 1` в†’ 300 s, `saveToonWhilePlaying` (a player+map save); `!gameMenu && (autoSave ||
netMode == 2)` в†’ 600 s, `saveToonWhilePlaying` (skipped on the server, `Main.cs:19660-19663`) then
`saveAndPlay` (world+player+map); and the menu arm (`Main.cs:19767-19769`), which only *stops* the
timer. The port is single-player (`netMode == 0`), so the 300 s arm is unreachable and the menu arm
has nothing to stop. The port therefore implements only the 600 s arm вЂ” `frame.rs`'s `!gameMenu &&
auto_save` tick, whose nets-to-`auto_save` condition is the exact single-player reduction вЂ” and
`save_world` already covers the arm's full output for a `.trwld`. This closes the "S1-J-6: the
300 s single-player player-only save is unverified" premise as **refuted**: the 300 s branch is a
multiplayer-client path, never a single-player or menu one (research/42, finding 42-6).

### Deviations (every deliberate departure from the C#, phases 2-7)

- **Unowned flag fields** are written with the C# defaults derived from
  `LoadWorldFlags:1981`'s `< gate` branches rather than being modelled (assumption-1's
  fallback); the reader keeps its own width.
- **`LastPlayed` is 0** and the creation-time pair is zero-filled вЂ” the port has no
  play-time accounting; `FileMetadata`'s revision increments per save, as vanilla
  (`IncrementAndWrite`), and is the file's only clock-adjacent value.
- **The weather snapshot is written** (wld-roundtrip, 2026-11-17): the rain triple
  (`_tempRaining`/`_tempRainTime`/`_tempMaxRain`, `:1312-1314`) and the sandstorm
  quad (`_tempSandstorm*`, `:1369-1372`) come from `World.{raining, rain_time,
  max_raining}` and `World.sandstorm_*`, which `save_world` fills from `App.rain`
  and `App.sandstorm` (`SetTempToOngoing:1053-1059`) and `App::new` restores
  (`SetOngoingToTemps:159-172`). Both were written as C# defaults before, so a
  `.wld` save reset an in-progress rain/sandstorm. `World.sandstorm_*` is not yet
  in the native `.trwld` flags block (a format bump, out of this slice).
- **Wires are written** since S1-J-1 (the four bits ride the tile headers through
  `World.wires`; see "The tile section's four wire bits" above).
- **GUID and worldId are 0** вЂ” the port keeps neither (the footer's worldId likewise).
- **Seed text**: the port's `u64` seed is persisted as its decimal text; a non-numeric
  seed reads as 0 (`SeedText` is `WorldFileData.cs:355`'s own convention).
- **Non-important tiles and kind 144**: a non-important kind reads back with
  `frameX/frameY = -1` (`LoadWorldTiles:2605`) and kind 144's `frameY` is forced to 0 on
  write (`SaveWorldTiles`) вЂ” an asymmetry preserved verbatim.
- **Chests**: a banned item's `(type, prefix, stack)` triple is not written at all
  (unreachable through the app вЂ” the fix-up turns it to air first); the latent
  `> 8000`-chest count asymmetry between the writer's `i16` count and the displacement
  pass; a non-40 `maxItems` chest is not threaded into the click hit-test.
- **NPCs**: a `SavesAndLoads` tower record (422/507/493/517) is parsed, its bytes
  consumed and the entity discarded (no ported kind is a tower); the `version < 251`
  recompute of the eight `unlocked*Spawn` flags is not ported (live spawning state); a
  homeless record's stale home coordinates are not carried into live state.
- **Tile entities**: the dummy's and the logic sensor's payloads are carried from the
  file even though nothing reads their runtime halves; the display doll's payload is
  carried too since S1-L-7a (`TEDisplayDoll.WriteExtraData` `TEDisplayDoll.cs:157-213`
  writes the nine equip slots, the nine dye slots, the misc slot and the pose byte, so
  the doll is storable and a `.wld` round-trip is byte-exact again); the kite/critter
  anchors' `IsTileValidForEntity` is the anchor
  kind alone (`TEKiteAnchor.cs`/`TECritterAnchor.cs`), which the shared head check
  settles.
- **Signs and plates**: the store is the positional `Vec<WldSign>` (exactly the non-null
  signs in slot order), not the C#'s 32 000-slot array; a duplicate plate point is
  refused rather than overwritten (`LoadWeightedPressurePlates`' dictionary key).
- **Collections**: the C#'s `Dictionary`/`HashSet` enumeration order is unspecified; the
  port stores sorted maps/sets, so a save is deterministic and differs from a vanilla
  file only in order, never in content.
- **Bestiary**: the sightings/chats stay empty until the recording behaviour lands
  (owner decision, state + IO only); the kill clamp is one-sided (the file keeps the raw
  value, the in-memory tracker clamps it).
- **Bestiary kill-credit + progression wires (S1-I-5)**: three deliberate gaps, all
  recorded rather than faked:
  (a) `NPC.interactedWithPlayerLocally` (`NPC.cs:6089`) is **not** ported вЂ” its only
  reader is `Player.AnyBossHindersRespawnTime` (`Player.cs:39100`), which the port has
  not ported; the field's writer (`NPC.cs:81266-81269`) is skipped with it
  (`npc.rs::player_interaction`'s `ponytail:` comment).
  (b) `NetBestiaryModule` carries **only** the `Kill` unlock kind
  (`NetBestiaryModule.cs:16-23`/`:49-56`); the `Sight`/`Chat` bodies
  (`:25-39`) are never sent and their tag bytes are rejected on read, because
  `NPCWasNearPlayerTracker`/`NPCWasChatWithTracker` are not net-synced (see the
  Bestiary collection bullet above).
  (c) `AchievementsHelper.NotifyNPCKilled`'s SP arm (`:202-208`) and its MP fan-out
  (`:210-216`) are both keyed on `playerInteraction[]`, but the host's own slot has no
  client outbox вЂ” the port relies on `Server::send` to a non-existent slot being a
  no-op, where the C#'s `i < 255` bound simply excludes the server. Same net effect.
- **Creative powers**: the id-8 slider is a `[0,1]` cache on the wire and the ported rate
  1..24 in memory вЂ” the codec remaps both directions
  (`ModifyTimeRate.UpdateInfoFromSliderValueCache:877-880`); the three ids the port has
  not ported (freeze rain 9, freeze wind 10, difficulty 12) are never written.
- **Save/load asymmetry**: the C#'s `SaveChests:1609-1642` dead-anchor pre-pass mutates
  `Main.chest`; the port does the same to its live store (through `&mut self`), so the
  file and the store agree.
- **A `.wld` load carries no player or map sidecar**: the kills ride the world file
  (owner decision), the `.trplayer`/`.map` sidecars stay the `.trwld` path's вЂ” a vanilla
  player file has no port format yet (the follow-up row).
- **`.trwld` TE/chest parity** is not done: the port's own format carries neither, so a
  `.trwld` world loses its tile entities and chests on reload (M6-SAVE-1b).

## Autotiling

`num6` / `Tile.frameNumber` and `wallFrameNumber` **are not stored in the save file** (the
tile header only carries frame X/Y for important tiles; `SaveWorldTiles`
`WorldFile.cs:1432-1604` never writes the runtime `bTileHeader2` bits 4-7 вЂ”
S1-A-3 verified the claim in `docs/research/08-tile-framing.md`'s deviation row that they
are "stored in the save" is wrong). The C# keeps them in the runtime `Tile.bTileHeader2`
(`Tile.cs:464-482`), rolls them from `WorldGen.genRand.Next(0, 3)` at reset events
(`TileFrame`'s `resetFrame` arm, `WorldGen.cs:81705-81709`; `Framing.WallFrame`'s,
`Framing.cs:389-395`) and reuses the stored value otherwise (`:81713`, `Framing.cs:399`).

The port (S1-A-3) follows the same mechanism вЂ” no position hash anywhere:

- **Storage**: `World::variants` packs the two 2-bit fields per tile (`bTileHeader2`
  bits 4-7 verbatim); `Tile` stays 12 bytes.
- **The full-world passes** (`frame_world`/`frame_walls` вЂ” the app's load-time and
  worldgen framing) roll one `UnifiedRandom::Next(0, 3)` per framed tile **in band
  order** and store it, mirroring the reset arm. **Deviation (deliberate):** the C#
  frames incrementally during worldgen with `genRand` draws interleaved between every
  other pass; the port frames in one parallel pass, so a shared sequential stream is
  impossible вЂ” each 128-row band seeds its own stream `seed + band_index` instead
  (the same per-pass stand-in M5-GEN-1 documents). Same seed в†’ same bands в†’ identical
  frames; the variants will still differ from a C# world's until S1-A-7's parity work.
- **Edit reframes** (`reframe_area` = `SquareTileFrame(i, j, resetFrame)` with the
  default `true`, `WorldGen.cs:80185`): the centre tile/wall re-rolls from
  `World::frame_rng` (a `UnifiedRandom` seeded from the world seed вЂ” vanilla seeds
  `Main.rand` from the clock on load, `Main.cs:6461-6463`, so the port's deterministic
  seeding is *stricter* than vanilla, per the S1-L-6c wiring precedent); the ring
  re-frames with the stored values. Per-site `reset` flags follow each call site's C#
  counterpart (`SquareTileFrame` default true at place/kill tails, plain `TileFrame`
  default false at the door loops and `RangeFrame`).
- **The large-frame lookups** replace the variant per position exactly as the C#:
  tiles `tileLargeFrames` 1/2 (`WorldGen.cs:81719-81729`, override without re-storing
  вЂ” the roll stays in the field), walls `wallLargeFrames` 1 (phlebas) / 2 (lazure)
  (`Framing.cs:378-388`, override WITH re-storing вЂ” the lookup value lands in the
  field and can be 3, hence `wallFrameLookup`'s fourth column per row).
- **Wall 21 quirk** (`Framing.cs:390-394`): the reset roll draws `Next(0, 3)` then
  `Next(2)` and forces variant 2 half the time вЂ” the extra draw is consumed only for
  wall 21 (the RNG-order contract).
- **Save persistence (W4-d109, the save half of S1-A-3)** — *deliberate port-only
  extension*. The C# `.wld` never serializes the runtime `bTileHeader2` bits 4-7
  (`SaveWorldTiles` `WorldFile.cs:1432-1604`), so a vanilla load resets and re-rolls
  them. The port's own `.trwld` **v18** tail persists `World::variants` as a dense
  `width*height` row-major byte block; a v18 load restores it and sets
  `World::variants_from_save`, and the full-world passes (`frame_world`/`frame_walls`)
  then **reuse** the stored values (`TileFrame`/`WallFrame` with `resetFrame: false`,
  `WorldGen.cs:81713` / `Framing.cs:399`) instead of re-rolling — a load-after-quit
  keeps the rolled `frameNumber`/`wallFrameNumber`. Generated worlds, retail `.wld`
  loads and pre-v18 `.trwld` files keep `variants_from_save = false` and re-roll (the
  C#'s own reset semantics). **Old → new:** before W4-d109 a `.trwld` load dropped the
  variants and re-rolled every tile/wall; now a v18 save/load round-trips them
  byte-for-byte (witness `w4_d109_the_framing_variants_round_trip_in_v18`). The
  world-hash pins are **UNCHANGED**: `generate()` runs only the pipeline steps and
  never frames (framing is the app-side post-pipeline seam, `app/mod.rs`), and
  `variants` is not a hashed `Tile` field — the pins hash un-framed worlds.

Ported pieces (`tr-core/src/framing.rs`):

1. **Block frames** вЂ” the 20-entry generic `if/else` chain at `WorldGen.cs:85929вЂ“86319`,
   each row selecting one of three 16Г—16 frames on the 18 px tile grid. Tile-type
   normalisation (`Main.tileStone` в†’ stone, `668` в†’ dirt, `697` в†’ `51`) and slope-side
   clearing match the original.
2. **Merge families** вЂ” `TileID.Sets.Dirt`, `Mud`, `Ash`, `ForcedDirtMerging`,
   `NeedsGrassFraming` (+ `NeedsGrassFramingDirt`), `OreMergesWithMud`, moss/moss-brick,
   `BlockMergesWithMergeAllBlock`, plus 2 228 directed pairs extracted mechanically from the
   per-type `switch (num)` cases in `TileFrameCosmetic`.
3. **Wall frames** вЂ” the complete `wallFrameLookup` (20 masks Г— 4 variants),
   `centerWallFrameLookup` and the 36 px cell geometry; comparisons use the wall's own
   visibility rules minus invisible walls.
4. **Large frames** вЂ” `Main.tileLargeFrames` 1 (4-row pattern) and 2 (2Г—2 pattern)
   override the rolled/stored variant, and `Main.wallLargeFrames` 1 (phlebas) / 2
   (lazure) do the same for walls (S1-A-3).
5. **Grass family** вЂ” the full `TileFrameCosmetic` grass path (`WorldGen.cs:82184-84836`):
   the merge preparation (dirt normalisation, grassв†”ore, the Weird merge of non-solid
   neighbours into "open"), the base selection (`NeedsGrassFramingDirt`, mud for jungle
   grass, stone for moss), the five override chains (edges, interior corners, overhangs,
   base-corner mixes and the `(i + j) % 2` mowed checkerboard), the `-2` base marker
   (WorldGen.cs:83380), the `-1`/`-2` merge tables (83419-84242) and the generic chain
   fallback with the base rejoined (84398-84784). Grass no longer merges with its base
   dirt in the generic pass вЂ” the transition frames are what make grass blend into dirt
   masses and wrap steps. `tools/GenTileData` additionally emits `Sets.Ore`,
   `Conversion.Grass` and `ChecksForMerge` for the gates.

   Documented quirks and deviations of the grass port:
   - `TileMergeCulling` (WorldGen.cs:4065, applied at 82215/83392/84396) culls neighbours
     whose `invisibleBlock` state differs from the tile's own. The port stores no
     invisible blocks (coatings are a TILE-DRAW-4 item), so the cull is a no-op and is
     not ported.
   - The left-edge override's second branch (WorldGen.cs:82314) repeats the first
     condition verbatim and is unreachable in the original; the port keeps only the live
     branch. The right edge's odd `down == num && right == up` condition (82353) is
     ported verbatim.
   - `WorldGen.mergeUp/Down/Left/Right` are output flags consumed by
     `TileMergeAttemptFrametest` (the cross-type merge tests for snow/ice/sand вЂ” not the
     grass family) and by the neighbour re-frame cascade (84795), which the full-world
     re-frame and `reframe_area` already cover; they are not modelled.
   - `TileID.Sets.HasSlopeFrames` (84245) has no grass-family member; the slope-frame
     block is not ported. The large-frame `frameNumber == 3` row shift (84785) cannot
     trigger either вЂ” no grass-family tile sets `tileLargeFrames`.
   - The ore side of the grassв†”ore merge (WorldGen.cs:82147-82150) still falls into the
     known gap of the merge-relation extractor (top-level `TileMergeAttempt` calls):
     ore tiles next to grass show edge frames where the original merges them.

6. **SelfFrame8Way** (W4-d110) — `Framing.SelfFrame8Way` + `BlockStyle`/`FindBlockStyle`/
   `WillItBlend` (`Framing.cs:9-23, 92-98, 141-144, 180-324`) and the full 47-row
   `selfFrame8WayLookup` (`Framing.cs:45-91`, const-built 256-mask table). Dispatch:
   `frame_of_variant` routes ids 255-268 AND 385/446/447/448 to it — the C#'s
   `case 385/446/447/448: break` exits the inner switch and falls into `goto case 255`
   (`WorldGen.cs:81409-81413`, `:84818`), so the crystal block and silly balloons ride
   the same arm (the research-08 row only named 255-268). Side slots join only when both
   blocks present the touching side (`blockType`: half brick hides top, slope s hides
   the two sides of `blockStyleLookup[s+1]`); corners need both adjacent sides joined
   plus the corner's two facing sides. `WillItBlend` verbatim: ForcedDirtMerging→dirt,
   tileBrick×tileBrick (which blends ALL gemspark groups — every gemspark id is
   `Main.tileBrick`, `Main.cs:9455-9470`), then the `GemsparkFramingTypes` equality.
   The reset roll stays with the pass functions (the d109/S1-A-3 variant mechanism is
   untouched — this task adds merge logic only). **Deviation:** an unlisted mask (only
   reachable for sloped/half-brick gemsparks whose style combination has no
   `Add8WayLookup` row) is a null row in the C# (it would throw); the port returns
   `None` and leaves the stored frame. Generated worlds never hammer gemsparks.
7. **WallFrame head gates** (W4-d110) — `wall_frame_head` ports `Framing.cs:328-342`:
   `wall >= WallID.Count` clamps to 0 BEFORE any roll, and a wall-less tile runs
   `wallColor(0)` + `ClearWallPaintAndCoating()` (`Tile.cs:911-916` — wall paint +
   invisibleWall + fullbrightWall bits; the block-side coating survives). Runs in
   `reframe_area` for every tile of the square (the C# `SquareWallFrame` calls
   `WallFrame` on all nine) and in `frame_walls`' copy phase for the skipped cells.
   The pure read `wall_frame_of_variant` treats an out-of-range id as wall-less.
   **Deviation:** `frame_walls` computes all masks from the pre-pass state, then runs
   the heads in the copy phase — the C# interleaves clamp/reset with mask reads, so a
   wall-less echo-coated TruncatesWalls tile mid-pass could differ for one framing
   pass (the same band-parallel stand-in as the variant streams). The remaining two
   gates of the research-08 list (TruncatesWalls neighbour term, invisibleWall term)
   already landed with S1-P-i33; the wall-21 roll and phlebas/lazure arms with S1-A-3.

Not yet ported: the per-type special-case branches (cactus, vines, `TileFrameImportant`
multi-tile objects). Those are listed in the roadmap.

`tools/GenTileData` parses `Terraria.ID/TileID.cs`, `Main.cs` and `WorldGen.cs` and emits
the `tiledata/` modules; rerun it after touching those tables.

## Slopes and half bricks

Slope/half-brick tiles are no longer skipped by the framer: the generic 20-rule chain frames
them with the same slope-aware neighbour rules as `TileFrameCosmetic` (a slope hides its two
open sides, and sloped neighbours stop contributing a side). The draw pass ports
`TileDrawing.DrawBasicTile`:

- slopes 1/2 (ground) and 3/4 (ceiling) are eight 2 px columns plus a 2 px strip, each
  sampling the tile's normal frame with the original source/destination offsets;
- half bricks keep the top 8 rows of the art and sit on the bottom 8 px of the cell.

Slope tiles still receive flat per-tile light, as the original's slope path does.

## Trees

Trees are tile id 5 columns (plus the gem/vanity/ash variants). The trunk sheet is not on
the 18 px block grid: `Tiles_5.png` uses **22 px cells with 20Г—20 sprites**, drawn at
`x*16 - 2`. `TileDrawing.GetTileDrawData` also shifts `frameX` by `176 Г— (biome + 1)`; the
biome comes from the ground tile under the trunk. Top and branch tiles (`frameX` 22/44/66,
`frameY >= 198`) are transparent markers, not art: `DrawTrees` replaces them with:

- canopy вЂ” `Tree_Tops_{style}`, source `treeFrame Г— 82, 0, 80Г—80` (jungle 114Г—96, hallow
  80Г—140), anchored at `(x*16 + 8 - w/2, y*16 + 16 - h)`;
- branches вЂ” `Tree_Branches_{style}`, source `(0 | 42, treeFrame Г— 42, 40Г—40)`, offset
  `(-24, -12)` or `(0, -12)`.

`tr-core/src/tree.rs` carries the marker/biome/style tables; the app draws foliage after
the tile pass. Forest world-style randomisation (`TreeTops.GetTreeStyle`, a later save
section we do not parse) is approximated as style 0; gem/vanity/palm trees are not composed.

### The tree kill cascade (BUG-16, 2026-11-11)

`TileFrameImportant` dispatches the tree kinds to `WorldGen.CheckTree` (the forest
tree 5), `CheckTreeWithSettings` (the gem/vanity/ash variants) and `CheckPalmTree`
(323) вЂ” `WorldGen.cs:85876-85911`. Those routines kill the tree cells that lost
their support; the `KillTile` chain is what makes a felled tree fall instead of
floating. The port's `tr-core/src/edit.rs::check_tree` / `check_palm_tree` run the
same machine; the ground test is the only parameter (`TreeVariant::ground_type` /
`ground_valid` вЂ” the forest tree folds the grass family onto plain dirt, the
variants use `GemTreeGroundTest`/`VanityTreeGroundTest`/`AshTreeGroundTest`).

Two deviations:

- **The palm's canopy re-roll** (`CheckPalmTree`, `:54385-54388`) draws
  `genRand.Next(7, 10) * 22` into the cell's `frameX`. The core has no RNG
  stream, so `TileKill::palm_frame_rolls` records the request and the app
  resolves it after the cascade. The C#'s neighbour ring does not fire for that
  arm (`frameY` is unchanged), so the deferral changes nothing but the moment
  the frame is written.
- **`noItem`.** The C#'s `CheckTree` calls `WorldGen.KillTile(i, j)` with the
  default `noItem: false`, so a tree cell killed by the cascade always drops
  its wood. The port propagates the ambient `noItem` like the other `Check*`
  kills, so the worldgen pass (which suppresses the drops) stays quiet. In
  play `noItem` is false either way.

The drop rolls follow the house RNG seam: one `item_rng` throw per event seeds
the `FastRandom` that stands in for the C#'s `genRand` stream and the
`Main.rand` roll spends the item stream directly. Note that in the C#
`WorldGen.genRand` **is** `Main.rand` (a property, `WorldGen.cs:4445`), so the
C# draws its four tree-drop rolls from one stream and the port draws them from
two — the same approximation the pot and pile loot already use.

### The axe arm census (S1-P-i30, 2026-11-20, code-only — tests written NOT run)

The C# axe arm is `Player.ItemCheck_UseMiningTools_ActuallyUseMiningTool`'s
`Main.tileAxe` branch (`Player.cs:45706-45771`): the chop damage is
`(int)(axe * 1.2f)` (the cactus 80 triples the axe first, `:45708`), the
`getGoodWorld` seed multiplies it by 1.3 (`:45709-45712`), `hitTile.AddDamage`
accumulates to 100 and `WorldGen.KillTile` fells the cell — the whole-tree fall
is the `CheckTree`/`CheckCactus` cascade, not the axe arm itself. Census
verdicts against the port:

- **WRONG (fixed): the gem trees were not axe tiles.** `tr_core::tool::is_axe_tile`
  listed only 5/72/80/323/488/596/616/704 — the seven gem trees 583-589
  (`Main.tileAxe`, `Main.cs:7217-7223`) were missing, so the mining gate refused
  an axe on a gem tree and the pick gate mined it instead. The set is now the
  full 16-kind table.
- **WRONG (fixed): the gem-tree drops were unported.** `KillTile_GetItemDrops`'s
  gem cases (`WorldGen.cs:65699-65746`) roll `SetGemTreeDrops` (`:66094-66108`):
  `Main.rand.Next(10) == 0` → the gem, else Stone 3; the canopy marker
  (`frameX >= 22 && frameY >= 198`) rolls `Next(2) == 0` → the gemcorn seed; the
  case body then rolls the stone's `Next(1, 3)` stack. All `Main.rand`, in that
  order (gem, seed, stack). The port now records `TreeDropEvent::Gem` per cell
  and resolves the rolls app-side (`gem_tree_drops`).
- **WRONG (fixed): the mushroom tree (72) had no support check or drops.**
  `TileFrameImportant`'s `case 72` (`WorldGen.cs:85837-85874`) kills a cell whose
  below is neither 72 nor the mushroom grass 70, and re-rolls the top cell's
  canopy (`genRand.Next(3)` → frame (18, 0/18/36)). The drop is `case 71/72`
  (`:65642-65652`): `Next(40) == 0` → the seeds 194, else `Next(2) == 0` → the
  mushroom 183, else nothing. The port now runs `check_mushroom_tree` and
  records `TreeDropEvent::Mushroom` + `mushroom_frame_rolls`.
- **WRONG (fixed): the cactus (80) had no cascade.** `WorldGen.CheckCactus`
  (`:54116-54158`, reached through `TileFrame`'s non-solid arm `:81368-81373`,
  NOT the frame-important dispatch) walks the cactus column down to its sand
  base and kills the cells that lost support — the whole plant collapses. The
  port now runs `check_cactus` in the kill cascade and records
  `TreeDropEvent::Cactus` (the flat Cactus 276, `case 80` `:64717-64719`) per
  cell; the app's `cell_drops` suppresses 80 so the hit cell is not doubled.
- **WRONG (fixed): the Don't Starve cactus chop did not hurt.** `Player.cs:45721-
  45724` hurts the chopper `DamageVar(6, -luck)` when the world carries the seed
  and the chop damage is positive — on EVERY damaging hit, not only the break
  (the prior attempt landed it only at the break point). The port now lands it
  inside `axe_tile_hit` before the accumulation (before the kill's drop draws,
  the C# order).
- **WRONG (fixed): the Acorn Axe (5295) did not replant.** `Player.cs:45744-
  45753` reads `IsBottomOfTreeTrunkNoRoots` (`:45784-45802`) before the kill and
  calls `TryReplantingTree` (`:45804-45822`) — a sapling 20 through
  `TileObject.CanPlace`/`Place`. The port now does both (`try_replanting_tree`).
- **UNCHANGED (verified): the trunk/palm drop order.** `trunk_tree_drops`
  already mirrors `KillTile_GetTreeDrops` (`:66189-66261`): the canopy acorn
  `Next(2)`, the mushroom `Next(2)`, the bonus wood `Next(35) <= axe` with the
  `Main.rand.Next(3)` second chance (short-circuited). The palm `case 323`
  (`:65232-65266`) wood + the `88..=132` acorn marker match.
- **WRONG (fixed): the chainsaw channel was unported.** The chainsaws
  (383/384/387/1190/1197/1204/1232/2342/3098 + the lunar 2773/2778/2783/3463)
  carry `channel: true` and a `shoot` whose `DefaultToDrillOrChainsaw`
  (`Projectile.cs:10732-10742`) sets aiStyle 20 — the SAME machine as the drills.
  The port now (a) adds the 13 chainsaw `proj_data` rows (57/58/61/214/217/220/
  224/369/427/429/431/509/610, the per-type boxes/scales of `Projectile.cs`
  `SetDefaults`; the Butcher's 509 carries idStatic-10, `:5793-5794`), (b) widens
  the i29 drill channel gates (`drill_channel_start`/`drill_live`/the throw gate)
  from `pick > 0` to `pick > 0 || axe > 0`, so a held chainsaw spawns its blade on
  the press, latches `Player.channel` and chops on the `toolTime` channel
  countdown (`Player.cs:43582-43586`), and (c) corrects the four lunar chainsaw
  item rows through the `ITEM_CORRECTIONS` seam (the GenItemData placeholder band
  left them `axe: 0`; `lunar_chainsaw` transcribes `Item.cs:26486-26506` +

- **MISSING (documented): Lucy the Axe's messages** (`Player.cs:45727-45742`,
  `LucyAxeMessage`) and the `IntentionGuesser` tracking (`:45715`/`:45754`) —

The chop PACING is now the C#'s exact `hitTile` damage-accumulator model
(S1-P-i30, stacked on the i29 `tr_core::hit_tile` book): `axe_tile_hit`
(`world_sim/editing.rs`) runs `tr_core::tool::axe_damage` (the `:45708-45712`
ladder — the f32 1.2 scale with int truncation, the cactus 80 integer triple
FIRST, the `getGoodWorld` f64 1.3 on the sum), the `CanKillTile` refusal
(`:45717-45720`), the Don't Starve hurt on EVERY damaging hit (`:45721-45724`),
the `>= 100` break with the `IsBottomOfTreeTrunkNoRoots`-gated Acorn Axe replant
(`:45744-45753`), the fail-tick prune (`:45758-45767`) and the `ApplyItemTime`
cadence re-arm (`:45768` — `useTime` verbatim; `pickSpeed` only when the item also
carries pick power, the Drax 579). The old time-per-tile stand-in
(`base * 7.0 / axe`, the M3-TOOL admission) is GONE. The `getGoodWorld` 1.3× chop
multiplier folds into the damage ladder, not the drop RNG. The per-tick
`KillTile(fail: true)` sound/dust stays the recorded i29 deviation (the damage

`HitObject(x, y, 1)` runs before the arm split); the hammer arms keep their

### The hammer interaction census (S1-P-i31, 2026-11-20, code-only — tests written NOT run)

`task/S1-P-i31-hammer-slopes` (stacked on the i29→i30 `HitTile` mining chain,
HEAD `0c888e89`) censuses the hammer interaction: the hammer arm of
`ItemCheck_UseMiningTools_ActuallyUseMiningTool` (`Player.cs:45665-45704`),
the pound cycle `TryPoundingTile` (`:45969-46311`), the wall passes
`TryFindingWallToHammer`/`TryHittingWall`/`PickWall` (`:45832-45967`) and the
`WorldGen.CanPoundTile`/`ForbidsSloping`/`SlopeTile`/`PoundTile` family
(`WorldGen.cs:80695-80838`). Census verdicts against the pre-i31 port:

- **WRONG (fixed): the pound/slope cycle was entirely absent.** No
  `poundRelease` latch, no `TryPoundingTile`, no player-path
  `CanPoundTile`/`SlopeTile`/`PoundTile` — only the ungated worldgen slices
  (`temple.rs::slope_tile_p2`, `tileobject.rs::slope_tile_flatten`, both kept
  as-is: their generation-time contracts are unchanged). The port now has
  `crates/tr-core/src/edit/hammer.rs` (the gated family + the whole pound
  cycle as `try_pound_tile`, returning a `PoundOutcome` the app seam acts
  on) and the `App.pound_release` latch wired in `update_editing` in the C#
  order: the non-target clear (`:45608-45615`, BEFORE the reach return),
  the mining action, the release set (`:45635-45638`), the wall pass
  (`:45639-45643`).
- **WRONG (fixed): the wall removal ignored `CanPlayerSmashWall`.** The old
  wall arm broke any wall but 350 on a time-per-tile pacing. The C#
  (`Player.cs:45917-45940`) refuses an INTERIOR unsafe wall (every 3×3
  neighbour the same unsafe wall) and the port now ports the rule verbatim
  (`edit::can_player_smash_wall`), the finder's banker's-rounded mouse
  quadrant 2×2 scan with the last-cell overwrite quirk
  (`edit::try_finding_wall_to_hammer`, `:45832-45906` — `Math.Round` is
  to-even, so the scan side flips with the tile's parity), and `PickWall`'s
  `(int)(hammer * 1.5f)` accumulation in the WALL book with
  `itemTime = useTime / 2` (`:45912-45913`). The `TryHittingWall` gate's

- **WRONG (fixed): the altar refusal did not hurt.** `Player.cs:45675-45679`
  zeroes the damage AND lands `Hurt(ByOther(4), statLife / 2, -direction)`
  on a sub-80 hammer or a pre-hardmode world. `hammer_tile_hit` now lands
  the hurt through the port's `Player::hurt` lane (the `-direction`
  hitDirection maps to a knockback origin on the facing side; the dodge
  rolls ride `UpdatePlayers`). The altar smash itself keeps the

- **UNCHANGED (verified): the `tileHammer` set.** {26, 695, 31, 696}
  (`Main.cs:7204-7207`) — `tool::is_hammer_tile` and
  `tileobject::tile_hammer` both match.
- **UNCHANGED (verified): the platform pound is the PLAYER inline copy.**

  (`:80840-80889`, zero callers in the decompile): the last step gates on

Deviations (deliberate, recorded):

- **The 470/314 pound seams.** `TEDisplayDoll.TryChangePose`
  (`TEDisplayDoll.cs:894-921`) and `Minecart.FrameTrack(pound: true)`

- **The wall finder's out-of-world reads** fall to wall 0 (the C# array
  would throw at the world edge; walls never generate there) — the edge
  cell stays breakable, the same outcome as the C#'s interior rule.

RNG: the hammer/pound/wall ticks draw NO gameplay RNG except the altar
self-hurt's dodge rolls, the Dig-0 sound variation/pitch and the
`smash_altar` ore draws — all on the `UpdatePlayers` stream (`Main.cs:17754`,
the `Player.ItemCheck` swap). The `HitTile` book itself is RNG-free (the
crack-style/wobble rolls are the render-side i29 deviation). No stream
reordered; the worldgen pins are untouched (the player-path edits never run
during generation).

## Lighting

Terraria's light is a **tile light map**, not a per-vertex shader effect:
`Terraria.Graphics.Light.LightingEngine` walks the visible area plus a 28-tile border,
`TileLightScanner` writes a seed colour per tile, and `LightMap.Blur` spreads those seeds with
directional sweeps. Everything is drawn multiplied by `Lighting.GetColor(x, y)`; in Color
mode solid blocks are further split into 3Г—3 (or 2Г—2) light slices.

Ported in `tr-core/src/lighting/`:

1. **Region** вЂ” `AREA_PADDING = 28` around the visible tile rect, `NON_VISIBLE_PADDING = 18`
   rows/columns that the sweeps stop before, exactly as `LightingEngine` does.
2. **Seeds** (`TileLightScanner.GetTileLight`), per tile in this order:
   - `ApplySurfaceLight` вЂ” for `y <= column_surface(x)` (the first solid tile of that
     column; the original uses the global `worldSurface`, which leaves hills above the
     average dark). The light colour is `Main.tileColor`
     (`ApplyColorOfTheSkiesToTiles` of the sky colour) and it only passes where
     `Main.wallLight[wall]` (or wall 73/227, or an invisible wall) and the tile does not block
     sun (`Main.tileNoSunLight`, with the slope/half-brick liquid rule), plus the gem-wall
     colour override.
   - `ApplyHellLight` вЂ” below `height - 200`: `0.55 + sin(tВ·2)В·0.08` warm glow.
   - `ApplyWallLight` вЂ” the `Main.wallLight` table (16 glowing wall types) with per-type
     colours extracted by `tools/GenTileData`, plus the crystal-wall random flicker and the
     disco walls (44, 346).
   - `ApplyTileLight` вЂ” the full 147-case switch (see "Per-type tile light" below).
   - `ApplyLiquidLight` вЂ” lava/shimmer self-illumination; the original compares every
     channel against the unscaled base and then stores the scaled value.
3. **Decay per tile** (`LightDecayThrough*`): air `0.91`, solid `0.56`, cracked bricks `0.8`,
   water `(0.88, 0.96, 1.015)В·0.91` with a per-cell jitter, honey `(0.75, 0.7, 0.6)В·0.91`.
   This is why surface dirt is already ~half as bright one tile under the grass вЂ” `0.56` per
   solid tile is the game's own value, and it is what makes torches mandatory underground.
4. **Blur** (`LightMap.BlurPass`, run twice): four sweeping lines (topв†’bottom, bottomв†’top,
   leftв†’right, rightв†’left), each carrying the brightest colour seen so far and multiplying it
   by the next tile's decay. The original's `0.0185` per-channel cutoff is kept, so dim light
   stops propagating instead of tinting the whole map.
5. **Smooth blocks** (`Lighting.GetColor9Slice` / `GetColor4Slice`,
   `DrawSingleTile_SlicedBlock`): a solid block in Color/White mode is drawn as nine quads
   (4/8/4 px) whose tints average the block's light with the corresponding neighbour; below
   the medium threshold it is four 8Г—8 quads, and below that one flat quad. A slope or half
   brick is not sliced.
6. **Modes** вЂ” `LightMode::{Color, White, Retro, Trippy}` match
   `Terraria.Graphics.Light.LightMode`. `LightStyle` says whether blocks are sliced, whether
   light is grayscale, quantisation steps, time-dependent channel perturbation and the
   shader aberration hook. `GlobalBrightness = 1.2` is applied when shading (`Lighting`'s
   default). Adding a mode (Sepia, Monochrome, ...) is a variant plus a style; the draw pass
   needs no new path.

   The brightness is also a G6 key input (S1-H-15): `Lighting.UpdateGlobalBrightness`
   (`Lighting.cs:108-116`) drops it 1.2 в†’ 1.0 while the Darkness debuff's `blind` flag
   holds, and `LightStyle::shade` multiplies every tile tint by it, so the bit-exact
   brightness rides `WorldFrameKey::brightness` вЂ” a blind gain/loss invalidates the
   cached world range instead of serving the old tints. The buff bar itself redraws in
   the uncached UI pass (the chat draws there too; the emote wheel/bubbles now draw вЂ”
   S1-E-26 wave B вЂ” and likewise ride the uncached UI pass, so neither needs a key
   entry), so this is the only HUD-state input the world range carries today.

Verified numerically with `TR_LIGHT_AT`: at midday the stored world reports
`light at 3200,402 = 0.560,0.560,0.560` for the first dirt row under the grass вЂ” exactly
`Main.tileColor` (white) Г— `0.56`; the renderer multiplies that by `GlobalBrightness`.

### Per-type tile light (M1.5-LIGHT-2)

`tr-core/src/tile_light/scanner.rs` is a case-for-case port of `TileLightScanner.ApplyTileLight`
(147 top-level `case` labels in the decompiled source, ~2 800 lines), plus
`ApplyWallLight`, `ApplySurfaceLight` and `ApplyHellLight`. It replaces the earlier
`EMISSIVE`-table approximation, which only covered the 43 types whose colour is a plain
constant and silently missed every conditional arm.

What the port covers:

- **Frame-selected colours** вЂ” torches (4), candles (33), lamps (93), chandeliers (34),
  lanterns (42, 100, 173), campfires (215), chinese lanterns (405), living fire (592-594),
  gemspark (429), rainbow bricks (719), and the gem tiles whose colour lives in the parent
  tile's packed `frameY` bits (171).
- **Animated colours** вЂ” `Main.DiscoR/G/B` (disco torches, gemspark, painted lamps),
  `Main.demonTorch` (demon torch and its hsl variant), `Main.mouseTextColor` (every flicker
  term), `Main.GlobalTimeWrappedHourly` (rainbow bricks, the 620 pulse),
  `Main.timeForVisualEffects` (350), `Main.time`/`dayTime`/`raining` (83),
  `Main.sundialCooldown`/`moondialCooldown` (356/663) and `Main.shimmerDarken`
  (`ApplySurfaceLight`).
- **Paint** вЂ” `flag` in the original means "this lamp's colour came from its frame, so a
  paint coat replaces it". The 93/33/34/100/173 tables set it for their painted arms and
  `739`, `519` and the 70-72/190/348/349/528/578 family set it when painted.
- **Per-tile randomness** вЂ” `Terraria.Utilities.FastRandom`: the scanner keeps one LCG
  state, re-seeds it every frame and derives a per-tile stream with `WithModifier(x, y)`.
  `FastRandom` in `tile_light/palette.rs` reproduces the multiplier/mask, `NextBits`,
  `NextFloat` and both `Next` overloads. Our seed is `world.seed ^ frame * golden` instead
  of `Guid.NewGuid()`, so screenshots at a fixed frame are reproducible.
- **Tables** вЂ” the five largest arms (93, 33, 34, 100/173, 42: 1 535 lines of C#) are
  extracted mechanically by `tools/gen_tile_light_tables.py`, which also resolves the
  stacked `case 7: case 8:` labels and the four dynamic entries each table contains
  (paint, demon torch, shimmer, `0.5/0.9/1.0 + flag`). Re-run it after a source update.

Deliberate deviations, all invisible in the current content set:

- `tile.invisibleBlock()` / `tile.invisibleWall()` are not stored in the packed 12-byte
  tile; an invisible block/wall is treated as visible (the scanner's `_drawInvisibleWalls`
  off path).
- `tile.wallColor()` IS stored (`World::wall_paint`, `world.rs:1247`) and drives the /765
  glowing-wall override — W4-d66 (2026-11-20) re-gated it to the C# `flag` arms only
  (walls 357/175, `TileLightScanner.cs:169/178/214/318`); the old `l != 0` proxy painted
  every glowing wall. The tile paint (`tile.color()`) drives the lamp override.
- The jellyfish-cage animation state machine (`Main.Update`'s `jellyfishCageMode`) is not
  ticked yet; `LightParams::cage_mode` is zeroed, which selects the dim cage colour.
- `new Color(230,230,230,0).MultiplyRGBA(hsl) * 0.4f` (type 620) is reproduced with the
  XNA byte multiply (`>> 8`) and byte truncation, which can differ from XNA by one LSB.
- The `Main.liquidAlpha[13]` blue boost (`TileLightScanner.cs:3160-3166`) stays at 0:
  the W4-e19 aether census found NO C# writer ever raises `liquidAlpha[13]` — the
  `DrawWaters` ramp (`Main.cs:57476-57489`) skips style 14 (`IsLiquidStyleWater`,
  `:57456-57463`) and the capture loop (`:56701-56707`) only writes 0..=10 — so the
  C# arm is dead code and the 0 feed is faithful, not a gap.
- `Main.time` is `f32` here (the original is `double`); the affected comparisons
  (`time > 40500`, `time < 16200`) are exact at these magnitudes.
- `demonTorch`, `DiscoR/G/B` and `mouseTextColor` advance once per *rendered* frame rather
  than per fixed 60 Hz tick, so at other frame rates their phase differs from the original.

Because the flicker inputs change every frame, the D2/D3 light cache now misses on every
frame (`TR_STATS` reports `reused=0%`). That matches the original, which recomputes the
whole light map per frame, but it gives back the "static view costs 0 ms" property the
M1.5 optimisation pass measured; `TR_NOCACHE=1` no longer changes the outcome.

Verified numerically with `TR_LIGHT_AT`: at midnight a `Torch` (`frameY 0`) tile reads
exactly `[1.000, 0.950, 0.800] = TorchID.TorchColor` (base torches are constant; only ids
7/14/23 animate), and surface air at noon reads `[1,1,1]`.

Remaining lighting gaps:

- Sun/moon/star light and the `Lighting.GetColor` shader path for light *behind* tiles are
  not ported.
- The shader has an aberration hook (`Globals::aberration`), but it is disabled for Trippy
  until instances carry a per-sprite flag: shifting full-screen sky quads samples past
  their atlas sheet.
- The real parallax, cloud and underground background layers are ported (see
  "Surface backgrounds" and "Sky and daylight"): the game's own `Background_0.png`
  gradient anchored to `Main.worldSurface`, the `DrawSurfaceBG` layer stack for the four
  generated biomes with its cross-fade, drifting `Cloud_*` sprites, the `Background_1/2`
  underground backdrop, and sun/moon/stars on `DrawSunAndMoon`'s screen-space arc.
- `TileDrawingBase.DrawOwnBlacks`: an exactly-zero-light cell paints opaque black before
  its sprite/wall. Vanilla emits that quad from `TileDrawing.DrawSingleTile` for every
  active tile and from `WallDrawing.DrawWalls` for every walled cell that is not a
  `FullTile`; the renderer folds both cases into one merged black rectangle per row
  (`light_is_zero && (active || wall != 0)`), which is what stops the parallax/underground
  backdrop bleeding through unlit caves. A fully dark tile is solid black either way, so
  skipping its sprite is pixel-identical (glow masks are not implemented yet). Echo walls
  (`WallID.EchoWall`, 318) are skipped entirely — no sprite and no black — exactly like
  `WallDrawing` with invisible walls hidden; **W4-g78**: with Echo sight granted they
  draw WHITE (`WallDrawing.cs:100-103`) and never merge into black coverage, and hidden
  Echo-coated cells (block or wall) paint no black at all (`Main.cs:58006-58007`).
`Main.time` advances with a 15-minute day and 9-minute night (60 ticks/s); the sky colour
and light are quantised to one-second steps so the map/instance caches still hit.

## Liquids

`LiquidRenderer.InternalPrepareDraw` is ported in `tr-core/src/liquid_draw.rs`. For every
visible cell the cache computes:

- `VisibleLiquidLevel` (including seepage into empty cells between two liquid cells), the
  four edge-wall values and the edge flags, `FrameOffset`, the source rectangle and
  `LiquidOffset`, the waterfall-fade `Opacity`, `IsSurfaceLiquid` and the half-brick
  visibility rule. The waterfall pass keeps the original's 10-row lead, so only the bottom
  rows of an extended draw area see the fade;
- `DrawNormalLiquids` then runs twice like `Main.DrawLiquid(bg)`: opaque (`Opacity`, usually
  1.0) before walls/tiles and `DEFAULT_OPACITY` (0.6 / 0.95 / 0.95 / 0.75) after entities,
  so the parallax never shows through the lake and entities standing in water are tinted;
- water uses the biome style sheet (`Main.CalculateWaterStyle` в†’ `Misc/water_0..14`). The
  atlas stores these sheets under their `Misc/` path, so `Lookups` must resolve
  `Misc/water_N`: the old `water_N` key returned `None` and silently skipped every
  `DrawNormalLiquids` quad вЂ” only the `Liquid_*` strips behind blocks were visible;
- the source frame is chosen by `FrameOffset`: interior water uses the plain row
  `(16, 48)`, surface tiles near `worldSurface - 40` snap to the still frame at `Y = 1280`,
  and edge/corner frames use the 3x18 px sheet columns. The old hand-written "always row
  32 + frame*80" pass, the per-column sine offset, the UV ripple flag and the depth tint
  are gone: they produced the repeating white squiggles and dark bands;
- `Lighting.GetCornerColors` is ported as `LightMap::corner4`; the instance format carries
  one tint, so the visible rect is split 3x3 and each cell samples the bilinear corner
  field. This is the original's smooth top-lit water surface.

Solid tiles that stand in liquid also get `DrawTile_LiquidBehindTile`: `LiquidSlope_*`
diagonal masks are drawn behind slopes (and 4 px `Liquid_*` strips behind block edges), so
the open corner of a shore slope shows water. Deviation: the original skips that quad when
water is both above and beside the slope and uses 0.5 opacity below `worldSurface`, which
leaves the known 1 px background gaps at shorelines; we always fill submerged corners and
use full opacity when the cell is under water, as requested. This affects only the
transparent part of shoreline slope/edge frames.

The system is completed by `tr-core/src/liquid.rs`, a port of `Liquid.UpdateLiquid` and
`Liquid.Update`: a 25 000-entry active-cell list (with the 50 000-entry overflow buffer),
per-cell gravity plus the six-neighbour leveling passes (3/4/5/7-cell averages, edge
openness, `Math.Round` banker's rounding), and retirement after eight quiet passes.
Falling water keeps the original's 254в†’255 quirk. Block edits wake the surrounding liquid
cells, so a breach visibly drains.

The pass window matches `Liquid.cs:1069-1106` (S1-A-8, 2026-11-13): every
`Liquid.UpdateLiquid` call advances `Liquid.wetCounter` and walks one
`curMaxLiquid / cycles` = 25 000 / 10 = 2 500-entry stride, and the `numLiquid` clamp
(`:1077-1082`) re-walks the whole list вЂ” retiring its dead entries вЂ” whenever the active
list is shorter than one stride, so a small pool is simulated every call instead of once
per ten. Single-player keeps `curMaxLiquid` at 25 000; the multiplayer scaling by the
active-player count (`:998`) stays out of scope. (The earlier `ceil(len/10)` slice, which
made short pools update ~10Г— too slowly, is gone.) Still not ported: `skipLiquid`
(`Liquid.cs:586-587/1096-1103`) and the `quickFall`/`quickSettle` delay seeding.

Not ported: the `Liquid` wave mask/vertex displacement, the water-style fountains and
shimmer sparkles.
The generator adds a forest lake and lava puddles so the pass is visible in the default
world; loaded `.wld` files expose their own liquids.

### Waterfall overlay

`tr-core/src/waterfall/` ports `Terraria.WaterfallManager`; `world_sim/liquids.rs`
runs it on the 60 Hz clock and `render/tiles.rs` emits the quads between the
non-solid and solid tile passes (`Main.DoDraw_Waterfalls`).

- `FindWaterfalls` keeps the 30-tick cadence (`findWaterfallCount < 30 && !forced`), the
  `waterfallDist = (int)(75 * gfxQuality) + 25` scan rectangle around the view, the
  `qualityMax` cap and the exact spout test: an active `halfBrick()` tile whose tile above
  has `liquid < 16` or is solid, with a neighbour holding `liquid > 160` while the other
  side is dry, non-solid and unsloped. The `196`/`460`/`717` fountain tiles spawn types
  `11`/`22`/`26` one row below when the cell underneath is open. The liquid kind check
  order is `tile2` (above) then `tile4` (right) then `tile3` (left), as in the source.
- Source-detection residuals (W4-g73 falls-adjacent census, code-only): the
  kind probes are PURE header-bit tests — `Tile.lava()/honey()/shimmer()`
  (`Tile.cs:345-382`) never read `liquid`, so a drained tile's stale flag still
  classifies the spout (`any_liquid_kind` dropped its invented `liquid > 0`
  guard). The scan rectangle is `WaterfallManager::scan_view`
  (`WaterfallManager.cs:119-122`): four `(int)` TRUNCATING casts of the raw
  unscaled `screenPosition`/screen size — no zoom divide, no floor/ceil (the
  first port pass's floor/ceil ±1 derivation scanned up to a tile wider).
  The forced flag is `Main.instantBGTransitionCounter == 10`
  (`Main.cs:61841`): the local-player Spawn arms set 10
  (`Player.cs:37569` — the revive path and `spawn_recall`), `DrawBG`
  decrements (`:64039-64041`), and the world-load init stays 2
  (`:66738`). Census note: the C# has NO type-12 SOURCE — 12 is the rain
  arm's background TEXTURE (`:486`); the source types are exactly
  0/1/14/25 (half-brick spout) and 11/22/26 (tiles 196/460/717), all landed.
  Witnesses: `a_stale_liquid_flag_classifies_without_any_liquid_amount`,
  `the_scan_view_truncates_like_the_csharp_int_casts`,
  `the_forced_flag_bypasses_the_thirty_tick_rescan_gate` (written, not run).
- `UpdateFrame` reproduces all five counters (regular 3-tick, slow 7-tick, rain,
  lava-rain and snow) plus `DoUpdate_AnimateDiscoRGB`. The `Main.mouseTextColor` flicker
  that the lava/shimmer light pulses use is owned by `lighting/` (`M1.5-LIGHT-1`) rather
  than duplicated in the manager.
- `DrawWaterfall` is a line-by-line port of the 640-line geometry walk: `stopAtStep`,
  the `num11..num42` state, the slope/half-brick/liquid neighbour rules, the 1 px
  left/right wobble per row, the `num41 = liquid / 16` clipping of the source rectangle,
  `GetAlpha` (0.6 under a wall or below `worldSurface`, 1.0 above it; lava 1.0, honey 0.8,
  shimmer 0.75, both fading over the last 10 steps) and `StylizeColor` (lava floor 190,
  disco RGB for tile 160, white for 262..268).
- Tint is `style.shade(LightMap::get(x, y))` quantised to bytes, matching the byte
  multiplies of `Color` in XNA; the app turns each record into one atlas quad
  (`Lookups::waterfall_uv`).
- Deliberate approximation: `Main.gfxQuality` is fixed at 1.0 (the value a machine holding
  60 FPS converges to), so the scan distance is 100 tiles and the cap 1000 falls вЂ” the
  same as the original at full quality.
- `WaterfallManager.Draw` (`WaterfallManager.cs:1118-1174`) runs one
  `DrawWaterfall(style, liquidAlpha[i])` pass per water style with a non-zero alpha вЂ”
  `liquidAlpha[0]в†’0`, `[2]в†’3`, `[3]в†’4`, `[4]в†’5`, `[5..9]в†’6..10`, `[10]в†’13`, `[12]в†’23`,
  `[13]в†’24` вЂ” so a biome water-style transition cross-fades the falls between the two

- The walk collects `WaterfallManager.AddLight` (`WaterfallManager.cs:1067-1116`) per
  visited cell вЂ” the lava fall's warm flicker, the disco fall, the gemspark falls
  (15-21), the shimmer fall (25) and the fountain (26) вЂ” and the light map seeds it as
  a per-cell maximum before the blur (`LightMap::compute_into_with_lights`). Vanilla
  applies the lights one frame late (the engine keeps the previous frame's `AddLight`

- `WaterfallManager.TrySparkling` (`WaterfallManager.cs:1046-1065`): 50+ steps into a
  lit fall, a 1-in-20000 draw scaled by the brightest light channel spawns a `Dust` 43

  drawing (`Dust` frame 43, scale 0.5) and fade with the generic dust decay

  The Y-distance arm keeps the original's verbatim quirk at `:725-728` (tests

  `honey_frames_ride_the_slow_counter`,
  `honey_alpha_is_flat_point_eight_without_a_glow_floor`,

  replaced, which is why shimmer glows in dark caves) and the sparkle overlay with the
  rainbow `GetShimmerGlitterColor` (`SimpleWhiteNoise` + `GetShimmerFrame`). The tile
  batch is premultiplied in XNA and the glitter colour carries alpha 0 (additive);
  this renderer blends non-premultiplied, so the sparkle encodes the premultiplied
  colour as `rgb/max(r,g,b)` with `alpha = max(r,g,b)` вЂ” the same source contribution
  with a slightly dimmed backdrop under the sparkle. `Main.DrawTileInWater` (the
  tile-518 submerged redraw) is not ported: the generator never places tile 518.

  `TR_NO_WATERFALL=1` skips the walk for A/B screenshots; `TR_SPOUT=x,y` stamps a
  half-brick spout with liquid and a clear drop (`TR_SPOUT_KIND=<0..3>` sets the
  liquid kind) and `TR_POOL=tx,ty,w,h,kind` fills a rectangle with liquid at load, so
  every style, the shimmer pass and the glow are capturable deterministically.

## Wind sway and tree leaves (TILE-DRAW-3)

`tr-core/src/wind.rs` already carried `Main.windSpeedCurrent`'s walk and
`TileDrawing.GetWindCycle` (`TileDrawing.cs:7676-7700`); the app now owns a
`Wind` instance (seeded from the world seed, `world_surface` set at load) and
advances the `TileDrawing.Update` counters per frame вЂ” `_treeWindCounter`
(1/240 + numВ·2/240), `_grassWindCounter` (1/180 + numВ·4/180),
`_sunflowerWindCounter` (1/420 + numВ·5/420) and `_vineWindCounter`
(1/120 + numВ·0.4/120), with `num = GetLerpValue(0.08, 1.2, |wind|)`
(`TileDrawing.cs:367-375`).

- `TileDrawing.DrawGrass` (`TileDrawing.cs:8326-8375`): the `TileID.Sets
  .SwaysInWindBasic` tiles (hand-transcribed into `wind.rs` as
  `SWAYS_IN_WIND_BASIC` вЂ” `TileID.cs:549`; the tiledata generator is due its
  own regeneration pass and was not extended here) draw with the grass cycle:
  position `+= (cycle, |cycle|)`, rotation `cycle * 0.1` about
  `(tileWidth / 2, 16 - tileTop)`, zeroed when the tile's wall does not
  `WallID.Sets.AllowsWind` (hand-transcribed in `wind.rs`, `WallID.cs:95`) or
  `!WorldGen.InAPlaceWithWind(x, y, 1, 1)` (`WorldGen.cs:86858-86879`). The
  row-major tile loop draws them inline instead of deferring them to the
  `WindyGrass` special pass (a documented z-order approximation, like the
  waterfalls); the `WindGrid` gust push (`GetWindGridPush`) is not ported.
  The type-227 frame exceptions of `ShouldSwayInWind` apply.
- `DrawTrees` (`TileDrawing.cs:8137-8245`): every canopy top leans
  `pos += (cycleВ·2, |cycle|В·2)` and rotates `cycle * 0.08` about its trunk
  anchor (the sprite's bottom centre); the frameX-44/66 branches shift
  directionally and rotate `cycle * 0.06` about `(40, 24)` / `(0, 30)`. The
  sway is skipped when the marker tile sits in front of a wall
  (`flag = tile.wall > 0`, line 8073). The renderer gained
  `push_sprite_origin_rot` (a `SpriteBatch.Draw` origin emulation).
- `TileDrawing.EmitTreeLeaves` (`TileDrawing.cs:7779-7891`): every visible
  top/branch rolls `1/leafFrequency` per frame for a leaf
  (`UpdateLeafFrequency`'s |wind| table Г— 7, halved for hallowed trees, Г—3
  for branches, 10000 underground); `WorldGen.GetTreeLeaf`
  (`WorldGen.cs:29384-29598`) resolves the gore id per ground tile (fully
  transcribed, including the gem/vanity/ash overrides and the hallowed
  tables вЂ” unreachable in the generated worlds but data-complete), and the
  spawn offsets follow the branch side and `frameY` variants. The roll uses
  `TileDrawing._rand`'s port вЂ” a per-frame pinned `FastRandom` вЂ” and the
  offsets' `Main.rand` draws fold into the same stream (the original keeps
  two separate streams; the visible distribution is unchanged).
- `Gore_UpdateLeaf` (`Gore.cs:1085-1209`): the leaf falls along a growing
  angle (`velocity.Y += PI/180`; the movement `(в€’sin, |cos|)` plus
  `wind * 4` above `worldSurfaceВ·16`), collides through the port's
  `tile_collision`/`slope_collision` on the 4Г—4 probe (leading the position
  by 4 px, re-anchored by `vector2 = (в€’4, 0)` exactly as the source), rests
  on the ground and drifts `Г—0.94` per tick until the ground frees up or the
  fade completes (`goreTime` 600, then 255 of alpha). The leaves draw from
  the `Gore_910/911` sheets (32 paint columns Г— 8 variant rows; the port
  draws column 0) in the UI range like the rain, keeping the G6 world range

  ported. The G6 `anim` folds the sway counters only while
  `|wind| > 0.08` вЂ” the cycle is zero below that (`GetLerpValue(0.08, 0.18)`),

- Not ported: the `WindGrid` push system (`TileDrawing.cs:8540-8600`), the

## Paint and coatings (TILE-DRAW-4)

`Tile.paint()` (5 bits in `Tile.meta`, E1) already loaded from `.wld` and fed the
map colours and the painted-lamp light; this port adds the RENDER side, the wall
paint and the coatings.

- Storage: `World.extras` вЂ” a sparse `HashMap<u32, u8>` keyed by the tile index вЂ”
  holds the states that do not fit the packed 12-byte `Tile`: `wallColor()`
  (5 bits, `Tile.cs:335-343`) and the Echo/Glow wall coatings
  (`invisibleBlock`/`invisibleWall`/`fullbrightWall`, one bit each;
  `Tile.cs:528-548`, `:718-721`). Tile-side paint stays in `Tile.meta`; the tile
  Glow bit is the existing `FLAG_FULLBRIGHT`. `.wld` reads the wall paint
  (`WorldFile.cs:2589-2592`) and the coating chain (`:2664-2682`) into the map;
  the native `.trwld` persists it as a sorted sparse section (v3; v2 loads with
  no extras).
- Render: the sprite instance gained a `paint` id and the WGSL fragment recolors
  the texel through a `WorldGen.paintColor` table (`WorldGen.cs:43921-44034`)
  before the light tint multiplies it вЂ” the architectural twin of
  `TilePaintSystemV2`'s per-(type, style, paint) baked render targets
  (`TilePaintSystemV2.cs:43-51`), collapsed into a per-instance shader branch.
  Deviation: the vanilla recolor runs as compiled HLSL passes whose source is
  not part of the decompile; this port washes the texel with the paint hue while
  its sRGB luminance carries the texture detail (the `paint_rgb`/dye constants
  decode with the piecewise sRGB EOTF into the samples' linear space вЂ” S1-G-4).
  The basic/deep paint pairs
  (1-12/13-24) therefore shade identically (vanilla deepens saturation), and the
  grass "special group" hue bands are not modelled. Negative paint (30) inverts
  the pixel byte-exactly (`decode(1 - encode(tex))` = `255 - tex_byte`); illuminant
  (31) draws unpainted (the vanilla pass 0) and glows
  through the light path.

### The tint's colour space (S1-G-4, 2026-11-14)

XNA's render formats are plain `Color` вЂ” no sRGB decode anywhere вЂ” so the vanilla
SpriteBatch multiplies the texture's sRGB bytes with the tint bytes in gamma space
and the backbuffer stores that product raw: `display = tex_byte * tint_byte / 255`
(the float pipeline rounds; the CPU-side `Color * Color` operator truncates). The
port's atlas view decodes (`Rgba8UnormSrgb`) and its swapchain re-encodes, so the
fragment carries the product linearised once: `f = srgb_decode(encode(painted) *
tint)` вЂ” `encode(f)` lands back on the product byte exactly. The earlier
`pow(tint, 2.2)` (and even linearising the tint with the piecewise decode) solved
the wrong equation вЂ” `decode(tex) * decode(tint)` в‰  `decode(tex * tint)` вЂ” and
drifted up to 7 LSB per channel. `sprite.rs`'s
`tint_parity_with_the_csharp_byte_multiply` pins the 256Г—256 pair table, and the
A/B screenshots show the corrected output (max 9 LSB over a world frame,
deterministic; the invariants in AGENTS.md "Rendering" describe this as the tint
matching XNA's byte multiplies).

**W4-d67 re-verify (2026-11-20, code-only):** the EOTF helpers are intact in
`sprite.wgsl` (`srgb_decode`/`srgb_encode` + the `_rgb` forms), every consumer
talks to them (the tint's gamma-space product at the fragment tail, the
paint/dye constant decodes, the negative-paint byte inversion), and no other
shader in `tr-render` carries a `pow(x, 2.2)` shortcut (`post.wgsl` and
`water_mask.wgsl` are colour-space-neutral; grep `pow` over `*.wgsl` hits only
the piecewise 2.4 arms and the history comments). The CPU mirror in
`sprite.rs`'s tests matches the WGSL branch-for-branch (0.04045 / 12.92 /
0.0031308 / 1.055 / 2.4). The three pins stand: `srgb_eotf_round_trips_every_byte`,
`tint_parity_with_the_csharp_byte_multiply` (256×256, exact vs the rounded float
product, ≤1 LSB vs the truncating `Color * Color` reading) and
`sprite_wgsl_compiles_headless`. No shader edit was owed. The committed goldens
in `docs/screenshots/` are stale **by design** after the S1-G-12b skyline
repack (all UVs moved); they must be re-taken per `docs/GOLDEN_REPIN.md`
(b4, on `task/W4-b4-atlas-skyline-packer`) in the next build-allowed window —
this branch neither re-takes them nor changes draw code to "fix" a mismatch.
- Coatings: Echo blocks/walls are hidden (`TileDrawing.IsVisible`,
  `TileDrawing.cs:1411-1432`; `WallDrawing.cs:91`) unless Echo sight is granted
  — **W4-g78 (2026-11-21) wired the sight chain** (the Echo Monolith scene
  scan + `Player.CanSeeInvisibleBlocks`, the 4409/5345 grants; ANALYSIS "The
  Echo-coating draw lane"), so the coated state draws with sight and stays

  (`WallDrawing.cs:96-99`); the tile-side Glow bit (`FLAG_FULLBRIGHT`) was

- Light: a painted glowing wall takes the paint colour at the /765 scaling of

### The blend batches (S1-G-3, 2026-11-18)

The vanilla frame runs three `SpriteBatch.Begin` blend configurations the port
now expresses (`Main.cs:27457-27494`, research/41 D-2): the alpha-blend default
(`Main.cs:22193`), `BlendState.Additive` (`:27490`) and the custom
`Main._multiplyBlendState` (`:27462-27470` вЂ” `ReverseSubtract` with
`SourceAlpha`/`One` on both the color and the alpha channels, i.e.
`dst в€’ srcВ·srcAlpha` clamped at 0). `sprite.rs::BlendMode` builds one pipeline
per mode over the same shader вЂ” exactly like XNA, where only the device blend
state changes between `Begin` calls. The per-instance `blend` tag rides the
instance buffer and `draw_blend_runs` splits each range into contiguous
same-mode runs: a run boundary is the C#'s `End()`/`Begin(blendState)` batch
boundary, so push order (and therefore composite order) is preserved; an
all-alpha range stays a single draw, leaving the default path byte-identical.

The only vanilla consumer of the two extra states is `DrawProj_LightsBane`
(`Main.cs:27455-27495`), ported as `projectile.rs::draw_lights_bane`: the
13-row frame slice (the drawer's own `Frame(1, 13, вЂ¦)`, NOT
`Main.projFrames[974]` = 1), the `(0.7, 0.7)В·scale` quads, two
`WhiteВ·0.3В·num` stretched ghosts of row 12 (`(1, 6)` and `(2, 2)` stretches)
plus four `Color.White` copies in the multiply batch, then two `Color.Magenta`
copies in the additive batch. `num = Remap(frame, 0, 3, 0, 1) В· Remap(frame,
4, 12, 1, 0)` (`:27480`). No light tint вЂ” the C# draws raw White/Magenta here.
The aiStyle-188 frame machine (`Projectile.cs:42229-42262`) and the SetDefaults
row (`:9237-9252`) landed with it; the sound cue and the dust streak (with
their `Main.rand` draws) are skipped like `ai_volcano`'s (no sound/dust layer
in the pool). The pool's `timeLeft = 30` kills the slash before the frame
machine's own frame-12 kill at tick 36 вЂ” both gates are ported and tested.

Deviations kept: the alpha-blend default's *premultiplied* convention stays
asserted (XNA's `BlendState.AlphaBlend` definition is not in the decompile вЂ”
research/41 D-2's original note); the additive/multiply equations themselves
are pinned by `blend_equations_land_on_the_csharp_batches` on both an sRGB
target (the port's swapchain) and a plain UNORM target (the vanilla's non-sRGB
backbuffer, where the blend maths runs on the stored bytes directly).

Verification: `blend_states_match_the_csharp_fields`,
`blend_runs_split_only_at_batch_boundaries`, the headless GPU equation test,
and `lights_bane_tests` (4). Screenshots
`docs/screenshots/s1-g-3-lights-bane-{base,blend}.png` (golden.wld, TR_DAY=1,
TR_THROW=974, frame 20): two identical runs SHA256-equal (`61c19b9bвЂ¦`), the
blend frame differs from the base only in the slash's bbox (32 826 px,
`tools/pixel_diff.py`).

The verifier FAILed the first landing on two placement/tint defects; both are

* **D1 вЂ” the anchor/origin convention.** `draw_lights_bane` passed the C#'s

  `push_ui_sprite_blend`, but the helper wants the UNROTATED TOP-LEFT
  (`pos = anchor в€’ origin`) and shifts it by `origin в€’ RВ·origin` itself вЂ”
  every quad landed a full origin away from the anchor, and the two ghosts
  further off still: XNA's `SpriteBatch.Draw(вЂ¦, origin, scale, вЂ¦)` multiplies
  the texture-space origin by the scale vector, so the `(1, 6)`/`(2, 2)`
  stretched ghosts (`:27483-27484`) pivot at `half В· s В· stretch`, not
  `half В· s`. The placement now lives in the pure `lights_bane_quads`
  (`Main.cs:27477-27492`): per quad `origin = half В· s В· stretch`,
  `pos = anchor в€’ origin`, `size = base В· stretch` вЂ” the

  precedent: pos = anchor в€’ origin; `frame_quad`'s tl = anchor в€’ RВ·origin).

  verified CORRECT and is untouched.

  house helper `ui::color::mul` twice + `tint` (the `bars.rs` precedent).
