## The atlas composite order (S1-G-11, 2026-11-20, code-only)

Research/41 D-3/D-11: merging every sheet into one atlas loses the vanilla's
cross-texture composite order. The audit's framing ("XNA's `Deferred` sort")
is corrected by the source: **`SpriteSortMode.Deferred` does not sort** — it
flushes in submission order (only `Texture`/`BackToFront`/`FrontToBack`
reorder, and the Terraria sources use none of them). The vanilla's
composite-order machinery is `TileBatch`'s **layered mode**
(`Graphics/TileBatch.cs`):

- `SetLayer(layer, stack)` arms a one-shot `LayerStack = (layer << 8) | stack`
  (`:235-242`); the first call latches `_layeredSortingEnabled` and throws if
  sprites were already queued (`SetLayerStack`, `:244-255`).
- `GetNextSpriteIndex` (`:421-439`): the armed layer wins; else a draw whose
  texture differs from the current batch's auto-increments the layer by one
  (`:433-436` — this is what lifts glow/flame overlays above the tile
  sprites); the arming is consumed either way (`:437`).
- Draws bucket per `(LayerStack, Texture)` (`SwitchBatch`/`CreateBatch`,
  `:485-536`), push order kept inside a bucket; `End` → `FlushLayered` sorts
  the buckets by `SortKey = (LayerStack << 16) | textureId` (`:49`, `:674`)
  and flushes them in that order (`:672-725`), resetting all pass state
  (`:717-724`). `textureId` is the texture's **first-use ordinal within the
  pass** (`CreateBatch`, `:513-521`).
- `TileDrawing`'s layer constants (`TileDrawing.cs:791-794`):
  LiquidBehindTiles 0, BehindTiles 1, Tiles 2, OverTiles 3.

The port (`crates/tr-render/src/batch.rs` + `sprite.rs`, three commits on
`task/W4-d68-composite-order`):

- `batch.rs` — the pure state machine: `layer_stack`/`sort_key` (the u64
  widening of the C# composition, same lexicographic `(layer, stack,
  texture)` order), `BatchCursor` (`set_layer`/`take_layer` =
  `SetLayerStack`/`GetNextSpriteIndex`'s arming + auto-increment),
  `sorted_draw_order`/`needs_reorder` (the stable bucket flush), and the
  uv0 → sheet reverse lookup `sheet_rect_contains`/`sheet_at` (the atlas
  erased the `Texture2D` reference identity the C# compares at `:428/433`,
  so the source sheet is recovered from the uv — half-texel slack on the low
  edges for the `(x0+sx)/aw` round-trip, exclusive high edges, lowest-id
  wins on overlap).
- `sprite.rs` — `SpriteInstance` gains a CPU-only `sort: [u32; 2]` (the u64
  key's words; stride 84 → 92, the vertex attrs stop at `blend` — the GPU
  skips the trailing 8 bytes). `set_tile_layer`/`end_tile_batch` arm/reset
  the world range's `BatchCursor`; every world push resolves its key through
  `world_sort` (the `sheet_id_at` last-hit cache rides the tile runs).
  `draw_ranges` runs `reorder_layered` before upload: each contiguous
  same-blend run is stably sorted by the key, **never across a blend-run
  boundary** — the C# flushes each `Begin` blend batch before re-beginning
  the next (`Main.cs:27457-27494`, the S1-G-3 batches), so a multiply quad
  can never ride an alpha batch regardless of its layer.

**The frozen default.** No caller arms `set_tile_layer` yet (the tile-pass
wiring — `TileDrawing.cs:456/523-526/879-887/1365-1398/1526-1536`'s
`SetLayer` sites — waits on the per-layer draw passes, S1-G-13's consumers).
Until then every key is 0, `needs_reorder` short-circuits, and the upload is
byte-identical to the pre-S1-G-11 straight copy
(`unlayered_ranges_stay_byte_identical`); a stable sort of the sorted range
is the identity, so the G6-kept world range re-uploads safely. The
`WorldFrameKey` is untouched — the keys are resolved at push time and ride
the cached instances.

**Deviations (batch.rs documents both):**

1. **Texture ids are stable, not first-use.** The vanilla id is the runtime
   first-use ordinal of a `Texture2D` reference — load-order dependent, and
   painted variants go through `TilePaintSystemV2`'s render-target cache.
   The port assigns lexicographic 1-based per-sheet ids
   (`SpriteRenderer::sheet_batch_id`), deterministic across runs and atlas
   repacks. The ordering *between layers* is exact; between two sheets
   inside one layer the port follows its stable id order instead of the
   vanilla load order.
2. **`LayerBatchKey.Equals` ignores `Texture`** (`TileBatch.cs:75-78`) while
   `GetHashCode` includes it (`:80-83`) — same-layer different-texture draws
   merge only on a hash collision, nondeterministic in the vanilla itself.
   The port keys by `(LayerStack, Texture)` always, the collision-free
   reading.

Tests (WRITTEN NOT RUN — code-only mode, no cargo in this pass):
`batch.rs` — the composition pins, the arming/auto-increment sequence
(including the back-to-previous-texture bump: the C# compares against the
CURRENT batch, not a history), the stable within-bucket order, the identity
permutation, the one-ulp low-edge slack + exclusive high edges, the
lowest-id overlap pick under entry-order reversal; `sprite.rs` — the frozen
byte-identity, the in-run stable sort + blend-boundary containment + the
u64 high word + the idempotent re-flush, the stride/attr-span pins updated
to 92.

**Goldens re-pin note.** The frozen default changes no pixels, so the
committed goldens stay valid *until the tile pass arms the layers*. When
that wiring lands, the cross-sheet composite order inside the world range
changes by design (that is the D-3/D-11 fix) — every world-frame golden
(`docs/screenshots/*`, the G6 replay hashes, the S1-G-3 lights-bane pair
included, since the world range rides under the slash) must be re-taken and
re-pinned in that task, with the pixel diff confined to overlapping
translucent cross-sheet regions. The stable sheet ids make the re-pin
deterministic; an atlas repack (S1-G-12b) moves UVs but not ids, so it
re-pins goldens without touching the order.

## Living trees (M5-LIVING-trees)

`crates/tr-core/src/worldgen/living_trees.rs` ports the "Living Trees"
generation pass (`WorldGen.cs:15476-15715`) and `GrowLivingTree`
(`WorldGen.cs:27973-28627`): the anchor/patch placement (outside the spawn
plateau, `Next(4)` patches per side stepping `Next(13, 31)`), the tapering
trunk (`Next(2, 3)` per side, 1/5 single-side widen, patch narrowing, the
`Next(5, 15)` branch cadence and the `1/2` taper until the edges meet), the
side branches (`width * (1 + Next(20, 30) * 0.1)` long with the 2-tile
thickenings as leaf centres), the upper trunk (`Next(width*3, width*5)` rows,
branches `Next(width, width*3)` flagged for round canopies), the roots
(`Next(1, 6)` down-rows then `Next(2, width+1)` diagonal arms of
`Next(width*3.5, width*6)`), the elliptical/round canopy blobs
(`Next(5, 8) * (1 + width*0.05)`, round `Next(6, 12) + width`, the vertical
squash `2.0 - Next(5)*0.1`) with `GrowLivingTree_CanPlaceLeaves`
(`WorldGen.cs:28607-28627`), and the hollow passage (`MakePassage`,
`WorldGen.cs:28865-29133`: 3-wide air, wall 244 lining, the drift every 6 rows,
the shell, the patch tunnels).

- Ground/anchor gates: the ground must be dirt/grass/stone or ore
  (`WorldGen.cs:28004-28010` вЂ” sand is excluded, so beaches reject), the
  anchor cell must be inactive, `j >= 150`, and вЂ” replacing the vanilla's
  `j >= worldSurface в†’ continue` scan gate (`WorldGen.cs:15549`), which does
  not translate to this port's terrain-vs-`world_surface` offset вЂ” the anchor
  cell and its ground must be free of liquid.
- Living wood/leaf rendering is plain-tile: `Tiles_191`'s transparent gaps +
  `tile_hides_wall`'s opacity check let wall 244 show through the bark (the
  `TileID.Sets.DrawsWalls[191]` effect), and the hollow is real geometry (air
  + wall 244). No special draw path exists in the vanilla either
  (`TileDrawing` has no 191/192 case).
- Framing: the generic merge dispatch gains the `WorldGen.cs:82070-82082`
  pairs вЂ” 192's Frametest merge against 191 (the port merges unconditionally;
  the vanilla re-frames the wood neighbour and reads `mergeDown/Up/...`, which
  needs the generic -2 openness tables вЂ” documented) and 191's
  `TileMergeAttempt(-2, 192)` leaf marker + the dirt fold.
- Leaves (192) are walk-through: `WorldGen.cs:15715` sets
  `tileSolid[192] = false` after the pass; the port adds the `kind != 192`
  exception to the collision helpers, the wall-hide check and the column-
  surface scans (the leaves never cut the sun), while
  `TILE_BLOCK_LIGHT[192]` stays true (the canopies self-shadow, matching the
  vanilla dark interiors).
- Not ported: the hollow room's furniture (door style 7, chair style 5, the
  Living Loom, the buried Living Wood Chest вЂ” `TileObjectData`, M1.4-TO), the
  leaf-pile decorations (tiles 187/185 with `PlaceTile` frame tables), the
  passage floor platforms (tile 19 style 23), the horizontal-tunnel doors, the
  secret-seed/remix variants and `PaintTheLivingTrees`.
- Determinism: the pass draws from the worldgen xorshift in the vanilla draw
  order; the unit test `living_trees_generate_for_seed` asserts the 191/192/
  wall-244 counts for seed 1.

## Rain and weather

`rain.rs` ports `Rain.MakeRain`/`Rain.NewRain`/`Rain.Update`/`Main.DrawRain` verbatim
(W4-d130) plus `Main.UpdateWeather`'s intensity ramp: a weather event has a target
(`maxRaining`), `cloudAlpha` moves toward it at `0.0005` per 60 Hz tick, and `MakeRain`
runs `screenWidth / 1920 * 25 * (0.25 + cloudAlpha)` attempts per tick (the C#'s float
`i < num` loop, `Rain.cs:47`), with the `NPC.AnyDanger` 0.05 throttle (`:37-45`). Each
attempt rolls the x-window then the y (`:54-55`), shapes them with the player velocity
and the `windSpeedCurrent * 15 * 40` lead (`:50-57`), clamps to the world edges and
gates on open sky (`!SolidTile && wall <= 0`, `:84`); `NewRain` then budgets the FIRST
inactive slot within `maxRain * cloudAlpha` scaled by gfxQuality (< 0.9), the snow-tile
suppression `(1 - (count/threshold)^2)` — the threshold is the skyblock-aware
`SceneMetrics.SnowTileThreshold` (300 when `WorldGen.Skyblock.lowTiles`, else 1500,
`SceneMetrics.cs:154-163`; the g67 R5 `f8c4b659` fold — `World.skyblock_low_tiles` is
censused at load/gen by `World::scan_skyblock_low_tiles`, `WorldGen.cs:3210-3218`/
`:3238-3265`, and rides `RainInputs.skyblock_low_tiles`) — and `atmo^9` (0 below 0.4)
(`:166-207`), and rolls the
scale (`1 + Next(-20,21)*0.01`) then the `waterStyle*3 + Next(3)` frame. The fall velocity
is the LIVE `(windSpeedCurrent * 18, 14) * scale` (`GetRainFallVelocity`, `:91-94`) — the
old frozen seed-time wind snapshot + sine term is retired. `Rain.Update` (`:96-133`)
moves the drop and kills it on the real `Collision.SolidCollision`/`WetCollision` 2x2
probes or below the view; the impact dust's `Next(100) < gfxQuality*100` roll (`:120`)
fires for ALL THREE kills of the ONE combined `:117` branch — the below-screen kill
included — and NEVER for the `gameMenu`/`remixWorld` kill-only arms (`:103-116`, which
only clear `active`). The `+100f` bottom margin is raw world px, unscaled by zoom.
(W4-d130 reconcile, `docs/research/83-weather-reconcile.md`: the earlier collision-only
reading was wrong; g67's `006bc04d` reading of `Rain.cs:117-131` is the verified truth.)
The pool is the C#'s fixed 750 slots (`Main.cs:66801`) — slot
order IS the draw/update order, never compacted. `DrawRain` (`Main.cs:38800-38826`)
samples the light at `(int)(pos + 4) >> 4` per axis and tints through the XNA byte chain
(`GetColor` → `* 0.85` → shimmer `* (1 - shimmerAlpha)`, alpha included), rotated about
the top-left origin. `SetBackColor`'s `1 - cloudAlpha * 0.9 * atmo` multiplies the sky
colour, which also dims surface sunlight via `ApplyColorOfTheSkiesToTiles`.

Storms add two pieces from `Main.DrawSurfaceBG`/`Main.SpawnStormLightning`: the
`cloudBG` layers (`Background_112/113`, scale 1.65/1.85, parallax 0.09/0.12) fade in with
the C# `cloudBGAlpha` ramp (`Main.cs:59358-59373` — per draw, ±0.0005·dayRate toward 1/0
by the live `cloudBGActive` overcast machine, W4-g69; the earlier intensity-tied
stand-in is retired), and heavy rain (> 0.65) throws a
lightning flash every 5вЂ“15 s. The flash is a 0.38-alpha full-screen white overlay that
decays over ~11 ticks; there is no bolt geometry or thunder audio yet.

The ambient snowfall is `Main.snowing()` (`Main.cs:13032-13116`), ported verbatim as
`crate::snow` (W4-d130) — NOT a rain mode: it spawns `Dust` type 76 into the shared pool
wherever the scene metrics count snow tiles at the surface, storm or no storm. The
intensity is `pow(count/6000, 4 - 3*cloudAlpha)`, the per-screen budget
`(int)(500 * viewWidth/4096) * (1 + 2*cloudAlpha)` (the HiDef `maxScreenW`, see (b)
below), the attempt count `1 + 50*cloudAlpha`,
and the `Main.snowDust` population gates the loop (`:13057`, a BREAK not a skip). The
Deerclops-near fades divide the intensity by 20 and the budget by 3 (`:13047-13052`) and
drop each flake's scale 0.5. The flake recipe branches on `Main.raining`: dry drift is
`wind + Next(-10,10)*0.1 + wind*15`, storm drift is
`sqrt(|wind|)*sign(wind)*(cloudAlpha+0.5)*10 + NextFloat()*0.2 - 0.1` with the fall halved
(`Math.Sign(0) = 0` mirrored). The type-76 AI (`Dust.cs:1745-1763`) plus the shared
second-chain tails (the `*0.99` drag `:2073`, the rotation rebuild `:2081`, the `-0.01`
fade `:2127`) ride the shared `UpdateDust` tick; `Main.snowDust` lands on `DustPool`
(head reset `:428`, `++` per live flake `:1747`). The draw is `DrawDust`'s generic path
(`Main.cs:38836-39023`) with the ±1000/±1050 cull rect + else-kill
(`:38832`/`:38847`/`:39020-39022`, the g67b fix), the 8x8 frame at the `(4,4)` origin and
the full-dark kill. The RNG is the GLOBAL bare-`Main.rand` stand-in
(`NamedRngs::global()`): `:17238` sits in `Main.Update` BEFORE `DoUpdateInWorld`
(`:17280` → the `SwapRandom` wrapper `:17732`), so no swap is live at the call — the
g11 research/83-addendum F1 adjudication (`docs/research/83-weather-reconcile.md` §7);
the earlier private snow splitmix was WRONG for this site and is retired. The old
biome-gated rain-rig flake approximation (per-flake sine sway, `snow_cap`) is retired.

First-pass simplifications, as updated by later tasks: the session-local weather
schedule is **retired** — M1.4-BG-22 landed the vanilla `rainTime`/`maxRaining` pair
and the `UpdateTime` start/stop rolls on the shared 60 Hz world tick (see "dayRate
consumers (M1.4-BG-22)" below); the wind-gusts gap was closed by WEATHER-1 (the
"gusts" ARE vanilla's `extremeWindCounter` tiered re-rolls plus the proportional
easing, already ported). W4-d130 landed the verbatim rain fall/draw core and
`Main.snowing()`. Deliberate deviations (W4-d130): (a) the C# runs `Rain.Update` INSIDE
`DrawRain` per drawn frame (`Main.cs:38819-38822`) and `MakeRain`/`snowing` per
`Main.Update`; the port keeps the drop/snow sim on the 60 Hz accumulator and the spawn
on the frame's scene slot — the recorded cadence fold, same as the rest of the weather
rig. (b) `Main.maxScreenW` in `snow.rs` is the HiDef 4096 (`Main.cs:3709` — the port
runs HiDef; g11 `13a1c48e`'s pin, folded by the final-phase census). The earlier
Reach-1920 pin retired FOR THE SNOW BUDGET ONLY — `sand.rs`'s emit budget keeps its
own recorded 1920 deviation, and `rain.rs`'s spawn rate reads `MaxWorldViewSize.X`
(`Rain.cs:36`), a different static that IS 1920. (c) the impact splash is g67's REAL
`Dust.NewDust(..., dustWater())` lane (weather-rain-splash, `40128e5d`/`006bc04d`),
TRANSPLANTED onto this core by the union-exec (`docs/research/83-weather-reconcile.md`
§3 EXECUTED): d130's verbatim fall/draw core (fixed 750-slot pool, slot order, the remix
kill-only arm, the live-wind velocity, the tint chain) + g67's `spawn_splash` DustPool
recipe, `water_splash_arm` physics and `draw_splashes` draw — g67's compacted-Vec
`update_drops` was NOT taken wholesale (it lacks the remix arm). The `Next(100)` gate is
verbatim for ALL THREE `:117` kills (the reconcile fix — the earlier collision-only
gate was a misreading). See "The rain collision splash (g67, transplanted W4-d130)"
below for the lane's own deviations. (d) `NewRain`'s depth factor (`Rain.cs:174-175`) is computed-and-discarded in
the C# (a bare `Math.Max` statement) — ported as a note, no effect. Still first-pass: no
lightning bolt geometry and no thunder audio — the flash rides WEATHER-1's tiered
thunder chain, not a bolt mesh.

## Biomes

The generator has three surface biomes plus beaches. The forest fills the centre, the snow
biome starts at two thirds of the width, and an inland desert band sits west of spawn
(`desert_center = width/2 - 380`, 340 tiles wide, disabled below 2000 tiles width). The
desert surface is blended toward smooth dunes (`sin(x*0.045)*5` plus low-frequency noise)
before the 1-tile smoothing pass, so it stays slope-friendly. Its strata are 16 px of sand,
14 px of hardened sand (`397`), 16 px of sandstone (`396`) and then stone, with sandstone
walls (`187`) instead of dirt/stone. The tree and plant passes only accept grass/snow, so
the desert stays clear. The background switches to `Background_21` (far, scale 1.25,
parallax 0.37) and `Background_20` (near, scale 1.34, parallax 0.49) when the sampled
surface is sand and the camera is away from the beaches. Two-to-four-tile cacti are placed
on flat sand: tile 80 is flagged important and framed by hand on its 7x3 grid (y=0 top,
18 middle, 36 base) because `WorldGen.CactusFrame`'s arm rules are not ported; cactus
items are collectible but not placeable. Desert structures and loot are not ported.

## Surface backgrounds

`Main.DrawSurfaceBG` is ported for eight of the surface biomes: forest (0), corrupt (1),
desert (2), jungle (3), ocean (4), hallow (6), snow (7), crimson (8) and mushroom (9).
Every layer is gated and tinted by its
`Main.bgAlphaFrontLayer` / `Main.bgAlphaFarBackLayer` entry
(`ColorOfSurfaceBackgroundsBase * alpha`), so two biomes blend while `Main.bgStyle`
cross-fades; a zero alpha skips the layer.

The far pass (`DrawSurfaceBG_BackMountainsStep1`) draws the four forest sets' far hills
(`Main.treeMntBGSet1..4[0]`, style 0 = `Background_7`/`93`/`171`/… per `SetForestBGSet`),
desert `23` (only when `desertBG != 4`) and snow `35` at parallax 0.15, scale 1·2 and top
`magic·1300 + 1090 + scAdj + 30` plus `GetLayerYOffset`. The near pass (`...Step2`) draws
the sets' near hills (style 0 set 1 = `8`), desert `22`, ocean `28` (`Main.oceanBG`,
default style 0) and snow `36` at parallax 0.20, scale 1.15·2 and top
`magic·1400 + 1260 + scAdj + 30`, in the original's index order (0, 1, 3, 4, then the
forest sets 10/11/12). The front pass draws the biome's three layers: the forest sets'
tree lines (style 0 set 1 = `9..11`, style 1 = `50..52`) and snow `37..39` — see the
W4-g70 note below for the forest chain's exact per-id math — resp. snow at
1.25·2/1.31·2/1.34·2, 0.40/0.43/0.49 and `+1350/1600/1850` (no flip); desert `21`/`20`
at 2.5/2.68, 0.37/0.49 and `+1600/+2000`, with no tree line. Everything is laid out in
`Main.screenPosition` space
(camera в€’ screenSize/2, **not** divided by the game zoom, so changing `GameZoomTarget`
moves only the world) and the X phase is
`-IEEERemainder(screenLeftВ·parallax, scaledWidth) в€’ scaledWidth/2` against the screen's
left edge, as in `DrawSurfaceBG`.

The five remaining surface variants ride the same front-layer path: corrupt (1), jungle
(3), hallow (6), crimson (8) and mushroom (9). [`World`] stores one **style byte** per
biome (`corrupt_bg_style`, вЂ¦), and `surface_bg_texture_ids` resolves it to the three
`Background_<id>` ids with `WorldGen.setBG`'s cases 1/2/4/5/8 (`WorldGen.cs:7235-7608`);
`-1` means the row is not drawn. The ids are derived on demand, so a style change needs
no atlas rebuild вЂ” but the world-dependent sheets are packed at load
(`assets::load_world_sheets`), hence a world's session must see one style set.

**Deliberate deviation — the atlas budget guard.** A rolled non-default surface style
can overflow the 8192 px atlas (style-0 baseline 7847 px; non-default styles add
336–1503 px, measured). The C# draws surface bgs through `Main.spriteBatch` under the
sky matrix, OUTSIDE the tile atlas (the S1-G-13 background-target family). Until that
lands, `build_atlas_inner` runs `assets::fit_bg_styles_to_atlas`: on overflow it
reverts the offending biome styles to slot-0 (the classic look) in fixed `setBG` order
1..8 until the set fits (measured via the cheap `Atlas::packed_height`), then rebuilds.
Deterministic, greedy, no RNG; the forest tree sets + underworld are not reverted
(g70/g72 own their draw sides). This trades the rolled look for an in-bounds atlas on
overflowing worlds — recorded here as the interim fix pending S1-G-13. See
`docs/research/218-doc-sweep-bg.md` §2.

Every row goes through `FrontLayer` + `front_layers`, which is a literal port of each
`DrawSurfaceBG_*` row: the caller's `(scale, parallax, magicВ·k + top)` magic numbers,
then `SetBackgroundOffsets` (`Main.cs:60384-60775`) overriding `bgScale`/`bgParallax` and,
for the ids whose `num`/`num2` pair is non-zero, replacing `bgTopY` wholesale. That is why
a style whose id is in the offsets table ignores the caller's row constants. Scale is
doubled by `bgGlobalScaleMultiplier = 2` (`Main.cs:59329`) and every `top` already carries
the front loop's `pushBGTopHack = -150` (`Main.cs:59302/59346/59525`).

The per-row quirks are applied *after* the offsets, exactly like the source: corrupt's
`bgTexIndexes[0] == 56` nudge subtracts 100 from **row 0's id on every row**
(`Main.cs:61128/61154/61199`); jungle subtracts 200/175/150 for `59`/`60`/`61` and adds
`DrawSurfaceBG_GetLayerYOffset` on every row (`:59740`, `:60944-61008`); crimson nudges
row 0 by `+50` for `105` and `-350` for `174`, and row 2's `175` by `-1000` in X, `-400` in
Y plus one extra tile (`:60206-60291`); hallow's first `SkyManager` boundary is
`1.2f / parallax` after the offset override (`:60788`); mushroom closes with
`DrawToDepth(1f)` (`:60186`). (The snow close the earlier port carried was a
deviation — `DrawSurfaceBG_Snow` has **no** trailing `DrawToDepth`, its stratum
waits for the `DrawRemainingDepth` flush like the other biomes; fixed by
W4-g71.) Row 1 of corrupt/jungle/forest is mirrored
(`SpriteEffects.FlipHorizontally`), mushroom's three rows each replace the tint with the
glow colour (`:60001/60065/60127`), clamped at or above the base colour's byte.

The animated sheets (`GetBackgroundRect`, `Main.cs:61220-61262`) sample a 2Г—2 grid: `235`
every 20 ticks, `219/220/221/271/272/273/302/303/305/307/309/311/313/315/317/326/337/338/341`
every 15, `281` every 5, then `Inflate(0, -2)`. `background_frame` halves `w`/`h` because
`Main.backgroundWidth/Height` are already halved for those ids at load (`:59046-59072`).

**Deviation (Mushroom glow RNG).** `DrawSurfaceBG_Mushroom` rolls
`Main.rand.Next(28, 42)` once per row (`:60002/60066/60128`). The port derives that value
from `Main.GameUpdateCount` and the row index through `next_rand` instead of consuming
`Main.rand`, so the draw path never advances the simulation's RNG stream вЂ” a hard
invariant of the port (a draw-time draw would desync world generation against the
original for the same seed). The resulting glow oscillates over the same 28..41 range at
a comparable rate; the two rolls are not bit-identical to the original's.

`Main.GetPreferredBGStyleForPlayer` (`Main.cs:64211-64256`) is ported in full, including
the beach/corrupt-blood-count branches and the glowshroom test; the final
`Main.treeX[]` forest sub-style selection (10/11/12) is ported since W4-g70, and only
the desert evil variants (5/13/14) still collapse to 2 — their style table
(`Main.desertBackgroundSet`) is unported.
`DrawBG_HandleBackgroundTransition`
waits 30 frames before adopting a new style (60 when entering a forest style), then sets
`bgDelay = -60` as a 60-frame cooldown (0 for a forest target);
`UpdateBGVisibility_BackLayer`/`_FrontLayer` move 16 alpha slots at
`backgroundLayerTransitionSpeed = 0.05` per drawn frame, and
`instantBGTransitionCounter = 2` forces the loaded biome on the first two frames. The
timer/alpha maths is unit-tested in `bg_transition_tests`. Layer tops use
`backgroundTopMagicNumber = -(screenTop - 300) / (worldSurface * 16)` plus `ComputeScAdj`,
exactly like the original, and вЂ” like the original вЂ” depend only on the camera's Y, never
on the terrain under the camera; an earlier clamp to the local column's surface made the
skyline jump at every hill and was removed (BUG-018). The background batch keeps the
original's zoom-1 matrix, so the layers hold their screen size at any game zoom. Clouds
are world objects at a fixed altitude above `worldSurface` and drift with the wind; the
storm `cloudBG` banks (`Background_112/113`) fade in with `cloudAlpha`.

Not ported: the desert evil variants 5/13/14 (their style tables need
`Main.desertBackgroundSet`; only the pure desert set is packed), snow's 20-style table
(`Main.snowBG`, style 1 assumed), `DrawSurfaceBG_GoodEvilDesert`, the far-cloud depth
layers (`DrawClouds_Distant/Closer`), the ocean water-line ambience and the
`Background_49` fog.

**The four forest sets (W4-g70).** `World.forest_bg_styles[4]` + `World.tree_x[3]` carry
`WorldGen.treeBG1..4` / `Main.treeX` (the `.wld` flags block owns them now; generated
worlds keep the `WorldGen.Reset` defaults — style 0 everywhere, dividers at `maxTilesX`,
so the classic `Background_9/10/11` tree line and `7/8` hills draw until a loaded world
says otherwise). `World::forest_bg_set` ports `SetForestBGSet` (`WorldGen.cs:7639-7768`)
verbatim — all 19 style arms plus the default. `render/bg.rs::forest_layers` ports
`DrawSurfaceBG_Forest` (`Main.cs:61273-61519`) with the C#'s exact write order, which
differs from the other biomes' shared `front_layers` path in three ways: row 0 calls
`SetBackgroundOffsets` **twice** (`:61302` then `:61307`), the second call landing after
the ×2 with no re-multiply, so a tabled id's scale ends un-multiplied (282 draws at 2.6,
not 5.2); rows 1/2 multiply first and call the offsets once after, and their
unconditional `bgTopY` rewrites (`:61399`, `:61473`) make the table's top pair dead code
for them; and the `ids[0] == 91` row-2 scale/parallax drop lands **after** the row's
`DrawToDepth` (`:61456-61462`), so the depth boundary keeps the pre-drop 0.49 while the X
phase uses 0.42. The `173` tree line swaps its drawn sheet to
`251 + GetBackgroundCounter()/10 % 4` (`:61373`) while every offset read keeps id 173.
The front dispatch walks the C# `l` loop's order — set 1 at `l == 0`, sets 2-4 at
`l == 10/11/12` **after** mushroom — each followed by `DrawSurfaceBG_DrawChangeOverlay`
(`:61098-61107`), the full-screen `Color.Black * flashPower` quad fed by
`world_sim/bg_animation.rs::BackgroundChangeFlash` (`BackgroundChangeFlashInfo.cs`:
latch 1 on a style change at load, 0.05 decay per update at `Main.cs:17218`). The hill
passes draw all four sets' live ids (`App.forest_hills`, stepped by
`DoUpdate_AnimateBackgrounds_UpdateForest` `Main.cs:19658-19735` — the 94/114-116 family
rewrites both hill slots, the 180-183 family only the near one, 6-tick counters, 4-frame
wrap) with the full `GetLayerYOffset` table (`:59740-59797`) and the passes' own
`screenPosition.Y < worldSurface*16 + 16` gates. The world-half atlas packs each set's
ids plus the animated families and the 173 frames, so a style change needs no re-pack
within a session. TRWLD grew a v18 tail (3 i32 dividers + 4 style bytes); pre-v18 files
load the reset defaults.

the eclipse light step (`:63845-63898`), the DontStarve hooks — and the
`ApplyColorOfTheSkiesToTiles` integer 7/10 BEFORE the atmo colour dim
(`:61982-61983` order). `render/sky.rs` carries `DrawSunAndMoon`'s event bodies
(eclipse Sun3, the Sunglasses head==12 Sun2/Extra_280, the Smiley/Pumpkin/Snow
moons), the byte-exact num12/num13 chain with the real `cloudAlpha` (the base used
`cloudBGAlpha`), and `NextHorizonRenderer.DrawSun`'s five flare quads.
`tr-app/star_field.rs` carries the whole `Star.cs` — the live 200..400-slot pool
replacing the static `make_stars`/`StarSprite` stand-in — and the starfall chain
lands end to end (`WorldGen.cs:71828-71856` roll → aiStyle-148 spawner 720 →
natural star 12 → `Star.StarFall`). Deliberate deviations:

- **Star spawn RNG pin.** The C# `SpawnStars` seeds a fresh OS-random `FastRandom`
  per call (`Star.cs:88`); the port pins each call's stream to
  `world.seed ^ counter × 0xA076_1D64_78BD_642F` so screenshots stay deterministic
  (the make_stars deviation, kept).
- **Smiley moon gate.** The C# reads `WorldGen.drunkWorldGen`, which is
  gen-time-only (set `WorldGen.cs:11115`, cleared in the finally `:11097`) — in-game
  it is always false, so the Smiley moon never draws in vanilla after generation.
  The port reads the in-game DRUNK seed flag instead, so a drunk-seed world actually
  shows the Smiley moon. The port's seed flags are the persistent in-game
  representation of the gen-time flags.
- **AFK gate always open.** The starfall target scan's `afkCounter < 10800` gate
  (`Player.cs:57103`) has no port AFK counter, so the gate is always open.
- **Flare blend.** The DrawSun flares draw at colour `(255,255,255,0) × strength` —
  alpha 0. Under the port's premultiplied blend an alpha-0 tint leaves the
  destination alpha untouched while the tinted rgb ADDS, matching vanilla's
  additive glow.
- **Star draw alpha.** The decompile builds the star colour from `default` and
  assigns only R/G/B (`Main.cs:63083-63086`) — a zero alpha would make every star
  invisible under the port's blend, so the port draws them at the computed
  brightness with the byte alpha the `color *=` chain produces.
- **Sound/dust/gore bodies skipped.** The starfall chain's dust/gore BODIES are the
  pool-wide skip (the draws stay on the stream); the `SoundID.Item10` cue is the
  sound skip. The gore types 16/17 carry no SpecialAI (`GoreID.cs:20`).
- **The menu gravity block.** `Star.UpdateStars`' secret-seed menu gravity block
  (`Star.cs:261-316`) needs `gameMenu && generatingWorld` — unreachable in the
  port's frame loop, documented out. The `dayCheck` never-true quirk (the decompile
  only writes `false`, `:245`/`:321`) is kept verbatim: every day tick past 27000
  respawns the hidden slots.

Remainders (research 79 §5): the artificial shimmer star pass (`Main.cs:62203`),
the starGame minigame, the AFK counter, the menu flat-35 night, the AuroraSky tint.

Also not ported: the per-biome **animated screen effects**. In particular the day-time
desert **heat shimmer** вЂ” `SceneState.ApplyVisuals` enables the `HeatDistortion` filter
(`FilterHeatDistortion`, `Images/Misc/noise`, `UseIntensity(4)`, registered in
`ScreenEffectInitializer`) whenever `Main.UseHeatDistortion` and either the camera is on the
desert surface (`TileCenter.Y < Main.worldSurface && ZoneDesert && !ZoneRain &&
!ZoneSandstorm`) or in the underworld (`TileCenter.Y > maxTilesY - 320`) or the Sun Scorch
debuff is active; the shader scrolls the noise so the pixels drift a few pixels side to
side. The `Blizzard`, `Sandstorm`, `Aurora`, `WaterDistortion` and monolith/story filters
from the same block are likewise unimplemented.


The underground backdrop is a port of `Main.DrawBackground_SurfaceTransitionBackground` +
`DrawBackground_DirtBackground`: `Background_1` supplies the one-row transition at
`worldSurface`, `Background_2` tiles as 96x96 blocks from `worldSurface + 1` down, both
scrolled with `Main.caveParallax` (0.9) and covering the whole screen. Every 16x16 cell
takes the light of the world tile it covers, sampled at the un-jittered cell centre on the
*unscaled* grid (`(cellCentre + screenPosition) / 16`, exactly C#'s `num3`/`num4`), so lit
ground stays lit and caves go black at any zoom вЂ” this is the original's screen-wide dirt
backdrop, not a per-column fill. Two deviations from the source: a cell is tinted with one
flat colour from `Lighting.GetColor` rather than the original's four `Lighting.GetCornerColors`
(the tile-batch path, which only smooths the light across a single cell and never moves the
sheet); and the `Background_4` band that closes the clamped dirt sheet at the rock
transition was added with M1.4-BG-10. Anchoring the old gradient per column made every
player-placed row of blocks paint a dark "wall" underneath itself; that artifact is gone.

The rock layer and hell are a port of `Main.DrawBackground_DrawRockLayer`,
`_DrawMagmaTransition`, `_DrawMagmaLayer` and `_DrawUnderworldBlackBox` (`Main.cs:53100`,
`:53344`, `:52856`, `:53382`), driven by the same orchestration order as `Main.DrawBackground`
(`Main.cs:52844-52849`: transition в†’ dirt в†’ black box в†’ rock в†’ magma, all under one
`GlobalBrightness` ramp). `GetRockTransitionPoint` truncates `(int)rockLayer -
(int)worldSurface` per row before the difference and snaps up to the dirt block height
(`Main.cs:53088-53099`); `magmaLayer` truncates the span below the surface to 6-row blocks
(`Main.cs:52812-52813`). `hellBackStyle` lives on `World`, rolled at generation from the
same generator as `moonType` (`WorldGen.cs:8247`; vanilla re-rolls it per session at load вЂ”
it is not a `.wld` field), and picks the animated magma sheet `Background_125..127` (three
96 px frames cycled every 8 ticks, `Main.cs:62218-62224`) plus the hell floor row
`Background_185..187`. Unlike the dirt pass, the rock/magma cells carry the original's skip
chain: a cell is skipped when it is covered by an active tile but fully lit, when it is
dark, or when it has no `wallLight` wall and the parallax is zero (`Main.cs:53152-53159`),
with the hell variant letting rows below `maxTilesY - 300` draw even when dark
(`Main.cs:52907`). The result is faithful to the original's data: natural walls hide the
backdrop (the wall pass draws over it), so the rock bands and magma only show in open
air вЂ” the generated world places `Wall_1/2/187` behind everything underground, which hides
them exactly like vanilla's DirtUnsafe/Cave walls would; the underworld floor row and the
magma transition band draw unconditionally, and the black box fills the gaps above the
hell floor line (`hellBlackBoxBottom` is produced by the previous frame's magma pass).

Deviations kept for the rock/magma passes: the 9-slice/4-slice light smoothing
(`Lighting.GetColor9Slice/4Slice`) is collapsed to the flat per-cell colour, like the dirt
pass; `undergroundBackground` is pinned to the classic set (`Main.cs:53817-53824`) in the
LIVE pass — the style machine itself is now ported UNWIRED (W4-g72 lane 3,
`render/bg_styles.rs`: `DrawBackground_PickUndergroundBackgroundStyle` `Main.cs:54033-54095`,
the full 22-case `UpdateBackgroundStyles` sheet table `:53812-54008` and the
`ugBackTransition` latch/decay step `:52823-52841`, 9 witnesses written not run). Wiring
is blocked on two owned-state gaps: the per-biome sheets overflow the single 8192 px atlas
(the full static+gore set already packs to 7530 px, measured with the `tools/atlas_sim.js`
skyline twin — even one extra biome set overflows), and the style rolls
(`WorldGen.RandomizeCaveBackgrounds`, `WorldGen.cs:8192-8249`) would insert draws into the
worldgen tail and move the frozen `world_hash` pins. The wall-parallax gate IS live and
now carries the full `WallLightAt(i, j, showInvisibleWalls)` (`Main.cs:55169-55181`): an
Echo-coated non-light wall keeps lighting the backdrop while invisible walls are hidden
(the coating is set by `WorldGen.cs:966/970/976` and the `.wld` load `WorldFile.cs:2672` —
the old "never set, table alone decides" shortcut was wrong); the show flag rides the
`TR_SHOW_INVISIBLE` pin until the Echo Monolith / see-invisible accessory lands. XNA clamps out-of-range source rectangles to
the sheet edge (`SamplerState.PointClamp`, `Main.cs:2774`) and the port clamps the cell's
source offset instead вЂ” the quad-UV pipeline cannot smear per pixel, which only affects
the last 16 px column of each 128 px rock block. The draw pad `Main.offScreenRange` (the
padded render target of `WorldSceneLayerTarget`) cancels out of the draw positions in the
port's unpadded viewport and survives only as the dirt sheet's visibility padding.

The hell parallax stack (`Main.DrawUnderworldBackground`/`DrawUnderworldBackgroundLayer`,

three style sets (`WorldGen.cs:7609-7635`); 9 witnesses with exact-f32-derived expectations

`RenderTargetFamily` (≤49 MB for style 1 + one composite pass), NOT atlas pages; the

as d69's `sky_target_active`); `FilterManager.EndCapture` then composites `skyTarget` FIRST

one that captures into `backgroundTarget` (`RenderToTargets` phase 2, `:57290` →
`RenderBackground` `:55200-55218`), composited with the cave-parallax X shift (`:62213`). In
both cases the "target texture" is the DESTINATION — the sheets are still `TextureAssets`
drawn through `Main.spriteBatch`, never the tile atlas. `bg_target.rs` ports the style-specific
seams d69's generic family (`9ba463ae`, `tr_render::targets`) does not own: the

(`WorldSceneLayerTarget.cs:49-57` + the `:52818` `drawOffset`), the `DoDraw` background consume
dispatch (`:62207-62215`, destination math left to d69's `layer_composite_position`), the

(`:53077-53081` et al.), the `DrawCapture` `!CameraSpaceEffects` camera override
(`:56844-56858`, `Utils.Clamp` max-first + `Rectangle.Intersect`) and the
`underworld_layer_plan` → sprite adapter (`:52786-52795`, `None`-safe without the atlas-blocked
sheets). UNWIRED: the frame-path composition is d69's in-flight consumers lane and the sheet

### The cross-fade overlay draws LIVE (W4-g72 closeout)

The `_drawBackground_oldBackTexture` overlays are now WIRED into the same
live chain (`bg.rs::UgOld` resolves the old-style table once per frame —
`Main.DrawBackground_UpdateBackgroundStyles`' second switch run,
`Main.cs:53804-53810` — and every pass draws its overlay while
`ugBackTransition > 0`). The C# census of the seven overlay families:

| Slot / pass | C# overlay seat | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 surface row | `:53768-53797` | SECOND whole loop, re-phased against the OLD sheet's width (`old.Width()-32`), light re-read at the old loop's samples |
| 1 dirt sheet | `:53651-53694` | SECOND whole corner-lit loop (`GetCornerColors(.., ugBackTransition)` scales the corner sum, `Lighting.cs:299`; alpha `(byte)(255*t)`); the per-cell twins (`:53560/:53608/:53625`) live ONLY in the collapsed slice arms — the plain arm (`:53636-53645`) draws none |
| 2 rock band | `:53723-53730` | per-cell twin, single row (no `j` pitch) |
| 3 rock field | `:53249/:53289/:53306/:53327` | per-cell twin in ALL four arms incl. the plain one; row pitch `backgroundHeight[oldBackTexture[3]] * j` |
| 4 magma band | `:53369-53376` | per-cell twin, single row |
| 5 magma FIELD | — | **NO overlay in any arm** (`backTexture[5]` at `:53002/:53033/:53041/:53049` never pairs with `oldBackTexture[5]`) — the animated hell field itself never fades |
| 6 hell floor | `:53075-53082` | per-cell twin, single row |

The per-cell twins route through `push_cave_cell`'s fade arm: the tint is
the base cell's already-lit colour folded through the landed
`bg_target::ug_crossfade_tint` (every channel incl. alpha byte-truncated by
the transition), the row pitch is the OLD sheet's height
(`backgroundHeight[oldBackTexture[slot]] * j` — the port's `UgOld::pitch`,
falling back to the NEW pass's pitch when the old sheet is unresolved),
and the source rect/jitter/sample point stay the NEW pass's. The dirt
corner-lit overlay does NOT route through `ug_crossfade_tint` — its
truncation seat is inside `GetCornerColors`' scaled corner sum
(`Lighting.cs:299`'s `GlobalBrightness * scale * 63.75`), so the port folds
`bg_brightness * transition` into the bilinear corner sample itself (the
same per-vertex→quad-centre approximation `push_wall_lit` documents) and
sets the alpha to `(byte)(255*transition)/255`. Its light gate is `InWorld`
(no 1-margin) + any-channel-nonzero (`:53672-53679`), NOT the base pass's
wall-light gate. DEVIATION (unchanged graceful degradation): a non-classic
old slot resolves `None` and its overlay skips — classic↔classic fades draw
today, the rest close when d35's per-world bg pages land. 1 witness
WRITTEN NOT RUN (the old-table resolution + pitch fallback + degradation).

The sheet is anchored to `Main.worldSurface`, so its value must match `TerrainPass.ApplyPass`:
`worldSurface = (int)(max(surfaceY) + 25.0)` вЂ” the *deepest* column, not the mean вЂ” with
`rockLayer` snapped up to a multiple of 6 above it (BUG-019). An earlier generator used the
mean column height, which floated the dirt sheet ~60 tiles (в‰€1000 px) above the true layer
boundary; the underground now begins where the original's does.

## The TileLightScanner residual census (W4-d66, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

Full 147-arm census of `ApplyTileLight` vs `tile_light/scanner.rs` (scripted label
extraction + f32-exact constant comparison + paired-body reads): arm coverage was
already 147/147; nine in-body/gate residuals were found and fixed. Full evidence
table with verbatim C# cites: `docs/research/10-lighting.md` § W4-d66. Summary:

- Lantern 42 frames 7/9 had been folded onto `TorchColor(7)`; the C# uses its own
  `demonTorch` shifts (`TileLightScanner.cs:2608-2627`). Fixed + witness.
- The /765 wall-paint override ran for every glowing wall; the C# gates it on
  `flag`, set only by walls 357/175 (`:169/178/214/318`). Fixed + witness.
- The modern blur mask had dropped `!tile.inActive()` (`:68`); the legacy mask
  kept it. Fixed + witness (`blur.rs::mask_of`).
- Gemspark 262-268 were muted: `Main.cs:10334-10342` sets `tileLighted` in a
  `for` loop the generator's literal-index regex never saw, so the scanner's
  `Main.tileLighted` gate (`:345`) rejected all seven arms. `tools/GenTileData`
  now replays that loop **for tileLighted only** (its sole consumer is the
  scanner gate); `sets.rs` regenerated, `--check` green. Witness pins the seven
  colours + the dead `case 235` (no `tileLighted[235]` write exists in C#).
- The hell glow was pinned to 0.55; the driver now computes
  `0.55 + sin(GlobalTimeWrappedHourly * 2) * 0.08` (`:3245`, double sin → f32).
- The modern engine had dropped `IsTileNullOrTouchingNull` (`:26-30/43-54`);
  `seed_row_range` now zeroes the 1-tile world border like `ExportTo`. Witness.
- `GetShimmerWave`'s phase subtraction + sin run in double in C#
  (`LiquidRenderer.cs:756`); the all-f32 port drifted ~2.6e-6 at large tick
  counts. Fixed to the f32-pos/f64-phase split; the `14f/15f` endpoint stays
  f32 (`:796`). Witness with reference-evaluated values.
- f32-ULP literal folds restored: `1.2824999f` (campfire frame 6), `1.3499999f`
  (`TorchID.cs:150`), `0.089999996f`/`0.052500002f` (walls 182/33),
  `128f/255f` = 0.50196081 (five lamp arms), and the sundial frame-5 products
  `0.9*0.8`/`0.9*0.2` (folded 0.72/0.18 are one ULP off). The shimmer liquid's
  `n3` keeps its own `/125f` division (`:135`).

## Sky and daylight

`Main.SetBackColor` (day `0..54000`, night `0..32400`) is ported to `color_of_the_skies`:

- Day `< 13500`: sunrise ramp `(230,220,220)В·t + (25,35,35)`.
- Day `13500..37800`: pure white вЂ” this is why vanilla daytime tiles are lit at 100 %.
- Day `> 37800`: the two sunset ramps (orange, then dusk).
- Night: `(5,5,5) + 30В·t`, floored at `minimalLight = 15` (moon-phase dependent in the
  original; we use the full-moon value).

`ApplyColorOfTheSkiesToTiles` pulls each channel 70 % towards its own value
(`(sum + 7В·c) / 10`), which is the colour passed to the surface light seed.

### Sun and moon (`DrawSunAndMoon`)

`crates/tr-core/src/sky.rs` holds the placement maths; `draw_sky` draws the bodies on
the camera's screen-space arc (`Main.cs:62848`):

- `celestial_body` computes the anchor `time/period В· (screenWidth + 2В·texWidth) в€’ texWidth`
  (integer-truncated like the original), the arc `bgTopY + |2В·tв€’1|ВІВ·250 + 180`, the scale
  `1.2 в€’ |2В·tв€’1|ВІВ·0.4` (the day branch multiplies by `1.1`) and the rotation `2В·t в€’ 7.3`;
  `period` is `54000` for the sun and `32400` for the moon.
- `sky_bg_top_y` is the in-game `SceneArea.bgTopY` (`Main.cs:62040`,
  `в€’screenPosition.Y / (worldSurfaceВ·16 в€’ 600) В· 200`), so the bodies ride the camera; they
  only draw while `screenPosition.Y / 16 < worldSurface + 2` (`Main.cs:62090`).
- The sun is drawn twice вЂ” the raw texture, then `sunColor` at alpha `sunColor.B` вЂ” through
  a new rotated background sprite (`push_back_sprite_rot`) so it spins about its centre.
  The moon picks `Images/Moon_0..8` by `Main.moonType` and the 50-px source row by
  `Main.moonPhase`. `sun_color`/`moon_color` port the base (forest) `SetBackColor` branches.
- `World` gained `moon_type`/`moon_phase`: the phase advances one step at each nightв†’day
  rollover (`Main.cs:19982`, wrapping 7в†’0) and `moon_type` is drawn from the generator RNG
  (`Main.cs:10873`). The native save is now `TRWLD` v2 (v1 still loads with 0/0) and the
  `.wld` reader picks up both header fields.

Not ported: the eclipse (`Sun3`), the `head == 12` sun (`Sun2` + `Extra_280`), the event
moons (`Moon_Pumpkin`/`Moon_Snow`/`Moon_Smile`) and the title-screen grab-the-sun
interaction. The first sun pass is always `Color.White` because no eclipse is modelled.

## World generation and native saves

`tr-core/src/worldgen/` is a compact model of the shapes the original generator produces,
not a port of all 45 000 lines. On first launch it builds a 4200Г—1200 forest world from a
seed in ~165 ms:

1. FBM value-noise surface around 30 % of the height, with a flattened spawn plateau and a
   smoothing pass that limits adjacent height differences to one tile.
2. Grass (top), dirt (16вЂ“22 rows), stone, then ash/hellstone for the bottom 170 rows; dirt
   walls above the rock layer, stone walls below.
3. Caves from a large-cavern field plus a worm field, with a 9-tile surface crust.
4. Dirt/stone/ash blobs, then copper/iron/silver/gold blobs by depth and hellstone in ash.
5. Slopes on every one-tile surface transition, a forest lake near spawn (a bowl with a
   raised rim, filled with water), small lava puddles on cave floors, sand ocean beaches at
   both edges and a snow biome in the eastern third (snow surface tiles, winter trees, pine
   background).
6. Common trees (22 px trunk frames, canopy marker, branch markers, base forks) and
   tile-3 grass/flower plants; snow-ground trees use the biome trunk section and `Tree_Tops_4`.

The result is saved as `Documents/My Games/Terrustaria/Worlds/Terrustaria.trwld`
(`tr-core/src/save.rs`): magic/version/seed + header fields + the `frame_important` bitset,
then per-row RLE of the 14-byte tile struct (~3.9 MB for the default world). Loading restores
every field; framing/lighting run afterwards exactly as for a `.wld`. `TR_REGEN=1`
regenerates, `TR_SEED=<n>` selects a seed. The other biomes, structures, the full ocean
biome and hardmode spread are not generated; the original generator remains an M5 milestone.

ids (Wood в†’ 9); consumption is a single index-ordered pass matching

consumes over 58 incl. coin/ammo вЂ” no subset ingredient lives there); a full

The panel (`ui/crafting.rs`) draws available recipes with a 44 px cell grid;
