### Ambience emitters (`tr-app/ambient_sound.rs`, M6-AUDIO-1)

The ambience *audio* of 1.4.5.8 is five emitters; `Main.Ambience` (the waterfall/lavafall
loops, M1.4-BG-20 — the verbatim decision half `liquid_loop_update` landed with the
W4-g73 falls-adjacent census: the (int) casts, the ambientLava Manhattan pick + strength
sum, the 960 pan divisor, the out-of-range keep-last-volume arm and the case-34 −0.2
pitch; see ANALYSIS "Waterfall overlay") and the rain/wind music-pool loops were already
in main, so this task ported the remaining three and verified the fourth:

* **Blizzard loops** (`SceneState.cs:189-253`). The two tracked global loops resume on
  `ZoneRain && ZoneSnow` вЂ” the raw zone pair, not the `UseStormEffects`-gated visual вЂ” and
  cross-fade through `_blizzardSoundVolume` (`MoveTowards В±0.01` per `SceneState.Update`,
  so it lives on the port's `SceneState` beside the other fades, not on a tick) split
  `min(1, cloudAlpha*2) * outsideWeatherEffectIntensity`. `audio.rs::set_ambient_loop` is
  the `ActiveSound.DetermineIntendedVolume` engine half: global в†’ no attenuation,
  `clamp(Style.Volume Г— Volume Г— ambientVolume)`, `SoundID.cs:1598-1599`'s 0.5/1 style
  volumes. The sink is created on the first non-zero volume and then kept (muted at 0) вЂ”
  the C# `SlotId` policy.
* **Thunder strike** (`Main.cs:58747-58766`). The cue plays from the weather tick with the
  C# position math and the `case 43` family (`Thunder_0..5`) from Rain's own stream.
  S1-E-25 closes both documented gaps: the `case 43` re-roll-on-playing loop is modelled вЂ”
  the port tracks a live sink per `SoundInstanceThunder` slot (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:113`,
  `audio.rs::thunder_slots`), `Rain::thunder_step` reads it live through its
  `is_playing` callback and re-rolls like `:456-464`, and the play replaces the picked
  slot's instance (`:466-476`'s Stop + CreateInstance) вЂ” and the pitch jitter is applied:
  `SoundEffectInstance.Pitch` is XNA octaves, so the engine resamples the PCM at a
  `2^pitch` rate (`audio.rs::resample_i16`, frame-aligned, nearest frame вЂ” the legacy
  engine skips/repeats frames).
* **Liquid-change sounds** (`WorldGen.cs:4632-4650`, S1-E-25): the liquid merge pass is
  ported (`tr-core/liquid.rs`'s `LiquidCheck`/`CreateLiquidMergeTile`), so the merge
  queues its `PlayLiquidChangeSound` event (`LiquidSystem::drain_merge_events`,
  `Liquid.cs:1345-1347`'s `!gameMenu && !isGeneratingOrLoadingWorld` gate = the engine's
  `!generating`) and the liquid tick plays it: the `Liquids*` rows ride the trackable
  style path вЂ” the `Style` getter picks the variation per play
  (`LegacySoundStyle.cs:21-28`) вЂ” and the shimmer arm rides case 19
  (`SoundSplash[4]`, the playing guard, the Г—0.75 cut and the `Next(-20, 1)` pitch;
  `WorldGen.cs:4644`'s trailing `4` is the Style argument, not a volume scale).
* **Critter sounds** (`NPC.cs:92244-92340`, S1-E-25): the caller rides the NPC update
  loop at the `NPC.cs:90323` position (after the AI's draws, the same per-NPC stream),
  and the legacy zombie-family cases behind the table's ids are modelled per C#
  (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:1051-1076`/`:1099-1213`: the slot picks, the 110/111-style
  playing guards, the Г—0.2..Г—0.9 volume cuts and the pitch ranges, in the C#'s draw
  order). The port's roster still has no critter NPC kinds (M4-NPC), so the emitter
  stays silent until they land вЂ” the seam, the asset bank (`Sounds/Zombie_*`) and the
  resolution are in place.

Deviations (deliberate):

* The tracked-sound layer is ported (S1-E-23: `tracked_sound.rs`'s
  `SoundPlayer`/`ActiveSound` over `tr_core::slot`'s `SlotVector(4096)`; the
  SceneState blizzard loops ride it verbatim). Two engine seams remain: the
  per-frame **re-pan** is baked at creation (XNA re-pans the live instance
  every `ActiveSound.Update`, `ActiveSound.cs:148` вЂ” a rodio sink cannot; the
  volume leg is live), and `SoundInstanceGarbageCollector` maps to nothing
  (rodio drops its finished sources). The C#'s try/catch around the blizzard
  block permanently disables the emitter when a play fails (`:191-193`'s
  `_disabledBlizzardSound`); the port retries next frame instead.
* The pitch mechanism is a rate resample (`2^pitch`, nearest frame), not XNA's DSP вЂ”
  the audible effect of the small jitter rolls (В±0.07 octaves) is the intended one.
* The engine's two static style streams are `UnifiedRandom` stand-ins seeded 1:
  `audio.rs::style_random` (`LegacySoundStyle.Random`, the variation picks) and
  `audio.rs::sound_style_random` (`SoundStyle._random`, the tracked `GetRandomPitch`
  rolls). The C# seeds both with `Environment.TickCount` (`LegacySoundStyle.cs:9`,
  `SoundStyle.cs:8`) вЂ” unobservable streams. The liquid-change splash pitch rides
  `style_random` too: the C# draws it from `Main.rand` mid liquid-pass
  (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:883`), and the port's liquid engine is pure, so no world
  stream is touched.
* The thunder slot/pitch rolls and the critter rolls come from the owning system's
  stream (the WEATHER-1/WEATHER-2 per-consumer convention), not the shared `Main.rand`
  the C# draws.
* `FocusHelper.UpdateBackgroundThunder`'s unfocused half and `StopAmbientSounds`
  (`Main.cs:11040-11045`) stay as BG-20 pinned them (the port always claims focus).
* The blizzard emitter's menu behaviour is the C#'s: `SceneState.Update` does not run in
  the menu, so the loops hold their last volume (the vanilla instance also keeps playing).

### The item-use sound wave (S1-E-21-itemuse)

`Player.ItemCheck_StartActualUse` (`Player.cs:51681-51698`) plays `sItem.UseSound`
at `base.Center` with `sItem.useSoundPitch`. The port provisions the data through
`tools/GenItemData`: `ItemDef.use_sound` indexes the new generated
`crates/tr-app/src/soundid.rs` (all 506 `SoundID` styles, ctor order), and
`Audio::play_use_sound` ports the faГ§ade (`SoundEngine.cs:93-99`) + the legacy
case-2 maths (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:516-644`, `sound.rs::item_use_case2`) + the
case-42 trackable arm (`:1376-1381`). The use-start seam is
`world_sim/editing.rs::start_swing_extras` (every swing/shot/consume arm calls it);
the `SkipsInitialUseSound` gate `{2350, 4870}` (`ItemID.cs:408`) lives in
`item.rs::initial_use_sound`. RNG contract: the case-2 `Main.rand` draws ride the
caller's `UpdatePlayers` stream (`Player.ItemCheck` under the `Main.cs:17754`
swap) and run ONLY after the attenuation gate passed (the C# order); the
`GetRandomPitch` NextFloat rides the audio-only `sound_style_random` and never
touches a gameplay stream вЂ” pinned by
`s1_e_21a_the_use_sound_draws_ride_the_passed_stream_only_when_audible`.
Deliberate deviations: (1) the multi-variation trackables pin the `_0` asset
(the standing D3 pin вЂ” the variation pick rides `LegacySoundStyle.Random`, an
unobservable stream); (2) the per-style instance stop/re-create pool and the
53/55/159 playing guards are unmodelled (the standing D4 deviation вЂ” repeated
cues stack); (3) the net-sync arm (`Player.cs:51690-51692`, `NetMessage.SendData
152`) has no port (single-player); (4) `Main.musicPitch` (styles 26/35/47, none
named by a `UseSound` row today) reads 0.0. Tile place/break sounds are NOT this
wave (break landed in S1-E-21c; place is a follow-up).

### The recall / mirror teleport (S1-P-i38)

`Player.ItemCheck`'s spawn-recall arms — the mirror family (Magic Mirror 50, Cell
Phone 3124, Ice Mirror 3199, Shellphone 5358, `Player.cs:42976-42999`), Recall
Potion 2350 (`:43107-43140`) and Potion of Return 4870 (`:43141-43172`) — were
entirely missing from the port (only the `SkipsInitialUseSound` gate
`item.rs::initial_use_sound`, the bed check `bed_spawn_valid` and the camera-lerp
seam existed). `crates/tr-app/src/recall_teleport.rs` ports them verbatim-order,
wired into `world_sim/editing.rs::update_editing` at the boss-spawner seam (the
item-use tick, not the cursor/reach path — the mirror fires mid-swing regardless
of where the cursor points).

The three arms differ exactly as the C#:

* **Mirror family** — a per-tick `Main.rand.Next(2)` dust gate (`:42978`, draws
  even when `NewDust` culls), teleport at `itemTime == item.useTime / 2` (90/2 =
  45), 70 type-15 dust at the OLD position + `RemoveAllGrapplingHooks` +
  `Spawn(RecallFromItem)` + 70 at the NEW (`:42988-42997`). **No stack consume, no
  immune save/restore** — the mirror keeps the 60-tick spawn immunity. Its Item6
  `UseSound` plays once at the use START (`:51696`), never at the teleport.
* **Recall 2350** — Item3 + 10 Cyan dust at `ItemTimeIsZero` (`:43109-43117`),
  teleport at the HARDCODED `itemTime == 20` (`:43118`, NOT useTime/2 = 15 — the
  recall is faster than half its useTime), Item6 + 70 Cyan dust OLD, the
  immune/immuneTime SAVE (`:43126-43127`) + Spawn + RESTORE (`:43129-43130`, no net
  i-frames), 70 Cyan dust NEW, `stack--` (`:43135-43138`).
* **Return 4870** — the recall twin, but the spawn leg is
  `DoPotionOfReturnTeleportationAndSetTheComebackPoint` (`:37498-37510`): records
  the use Bottom + the post-spawn home Bottom, saves/restores immune, `stack--`.

All three call `Spawn(RecallFromItem)` — NOT `Player.Teleport` — so there is no
`Main.TeleportEffect` dust/sound for them; the arm's own bursts + `UseSound` are
the whole visual/audio. `spawn_recall` ports the RecallFromItem subset of
`Player.Spawn` (`:37534-37710`): the bed re-validation (`FindSpawn` + `CheckSpawn`,
the port's `check_bed_spawn`), the vanity stop, the lava refill, the dead/immune
reset, the bed-else-world position pick, the wet/velocity/fall reset,
`oldPosition = position + (0,-1)` (`BlehOldPositionFixer` `:3235`), `SetTalkNPC(-1)`,
the 60-tick immunity + `immuneNoBlink` (`:37665-37672`) and the delay-0 camera lerp
(`:37676`, NOT the `Teleport` style-1 potion-recall 10). The position helpers
(`Spawn_IsAreaValidSpawn` `:37937-37985`, `Spawn_ValidSpawnFloor` `:37896-37912`,
`Spawn_DescendFromDefaultSpace`+`_Inner` `:37818-37894`, `Spawn_GetPositionAtSpawn`
`:37723-37804`, `Spawn_SetPosition` `:37987-37991`, `Spawn_ForceClearArea`
`:37914-37935`) are verbatim.

RNG contract: every `Main.rand` draw rides the `UpdatePlayers` stream
(`Player.ItemCheck` under the `Main.cs:17754` swap) in C# order — the mirror's
per-tick `Next(2)` gate, then the six `Dust.NewDust` default-block draws per spawned
dust (`Dust.cs:170-175`, `:190`: `Next(w-4)`, `Next(h-4)`, `Next(-20,21)`×2,
`Next(3)`, `Next(-20,21)`), then the teleport bursts (mirror 70+70; recall 10 start
+ 70+70). The witnesses mirror the cited draws on a CLONED `UnifiedRandom` and
compare the full state (`UnifiedRandom: PartialEq`); the rig mutes audio so the
case-2 legacy sound draws stay off the gameplay stream (S1-E-21 pins those
separately). 13 witness tests WRITTEN NOT RUN (code-only mode, no compiler invoked).

Deliberate deviations / scope:

* The `Player.Teleport`/`Main.TeleportEffect` system is a SEPARATE follow-up: the
  Potion of Return RETURN leg (`DoPotionOfReturnReturnToOriginalUsePosition`
  `:37512-37523`, `Teleport` style 8) and the Shellphone Spawn 5359 arm
  (`:43066-43106`, `Shellphone_Spawn` `:56164-56181`, `Teleport` style 11) are not
  this cluster's to-spawn leg. The two `PotionOfReturn*` comeback fields ARE
  recorded (the 4870 arm needs them; `Player.cs:2480-2482`).
* `Spawn`'s unported state tails are cited-dropped: the head/body/leg position +
  rotation resets (`:37582-37587`, the composite arms recompute per frame),
  `lavaOpacity` (`:37590`), `insideUnbreakableWalls` + `DoUnbreakableWallScan`
  (`:37591-37592`, derived per tick in `scene_scan.rs`), `DamageTracker.Reset`
  (`:37593`), the advanced/social shadows (`:37642-37646`),
  `UpdateBiomesIfMovedEnoughForBlackFade` (`:37677`, M6 cinematics) and the
  `SpawningIntoWorld`/`ReviveFromDeath`-only tails (`:37687-37709`).
* Single-player: the `Main.netMode` arms (`SendData`, the client `73` request) have
  no port; `whoAmI == Main.myPlayer` always holds.
* `Spawn_ForceClearArea`'s `WorldGen.KillTile(i, j)` rides the port's `break_tile`
  (the `CanKillTile` refusal + sounds + drops); the liquid clear's
  `SquareTileFrame` object drops drain through `spawn_item_drop`.
* The start gate uses the port's `prev_mine_released && !prev_mine_down` press edge
  (passed in — `update_editing` overwrites `mine_prev_down` to the current frame at
  its top, the `throw_ready` convention); `CCed`/dead zeroes the animation
  (`:42598-42603`). The port's frozen/HUD gates approximate the C#'s
  `controlUseItem`/`CCed` gates upstream of the seam.

## In-game interface (M7-UI)

The in-game HUD and inventory are immediate-mode in the original (`Main.DrawInterface`,
`Main.DrawInventory`), so the port keeps one Rust function per original function in
`crates/tr-app/src/ui/` with the original's constants and pass order (see `docs/UI.md`).
The deviations below are deliberate and are the places the port is **not** pixel-exact.

### Resources (`ui/resources.rs`, `ClassicPlayerResourcesDisplaySet.cs`)

* `Player.statLifeMax`/`statLifeMax2` are collapsed into a single `Player.max_hp`, so
  the bonus-heart branch (`ClassicPlayerResourcesDisplaySet.cs:112-116`, only reached
  when `statLifeMax2 > statLifeMax > 400`) is unreachable and **not ported**. A fresh
  character has `max_hp = 100`, where the branch cannot trigger; the `Heart2` sheet is
  therefore never drawn.
* `Player.ghost` is modelled now (W4-c46's hardcore lane, `Player.cs:1350`); the
  breath/lava meters gate on it (`Main.cs:43440`/`:43476`). The hearts/mana still
  draw for the dead/ghost player — the C# resource set has no dead/ghost
  early-return (`ClassicPlayerResourcesDisplaySet.Draw`), so that is faithful.
* Breath bubbles: **W4-c46 sweep landed the full
  `Main.DrawInterface_Resources_Breath`** (`Main.cs:43406-43513`) — the dead
  early-return, the lava-suppression flag, the anchor walk (the `+32` row offset,
  the `gfxOffY`, the open-inventory `< 1000` drop / closed `-100` lift, the
  options/fancy-UI re-anchors), the per-bubble `num2` grey **as the alpha**, the
  `breathMax/20` count with the `i > 10` wrap, and the lava **flame** meter
  (`TextureAssets.Flame`, `lavaMax/10` per flame). The old deviations (no `+32`,
  alpha 1.0, fixed 10 bubbles, no lava meter) are resolved. The `UIScale` divide
  (`:43431`) cancels the C#'s `UIScaleMatrix` batch; the port's whole HUD is
  unscaled (the S1-H-3 deviation above), so the anchor stays raw.
* `Main.statLifeMax`-driven heart *count* and the per-heart scale/alpha/`Main.cursorScale`
  pulse are ported exactly.

### Cursor and mouse text (`ui/cursor.rs`, `ui/tooltip.rs`)

* `Main.ThickMouse` / `Main.mouseItem`'s `+34` tooltip offsets (`Main.cs:20162`) are not
  modelled; the tooltip is anchored at the pointer.
* Tooltip stat lines are placeholders (zeros) until `Item.ToolTip`'s data-driven lines
  are ported; the 9-slice box, the rarity colour and the 4-direction
  `DrawColorCodedStringWithPadding` shadow are exact. `rare` values below the ported
  table (`-12`, `-13`, `diff` colours) fall back to white.

### Inventory (`ui/inventory.rs`, `ui/chrome.rs`, `ui/slot.rs`)

* Vanilla keeps one 59-slot `Player.inventory` plus the `armor`/`dye`/`miscEquips`/
  `miscDyes` arrays. The port keeps the 50-slot grid in `App::inventory` (so the saved
  format in `persist.rs` is unchanged) and the rest in `inv::EquipSlots`.
* `Main.invAlpha` pulses `180..=240` at `В±0.2`/frame (`Main.cs:45697-45708`) and tints
  every slot background; the port uses the fixed `220` (`Main.cs:67274`) so screenshots
  stay deterministic. The equipment columns keep the **loadout-1** colours
  (`ItemSlot.LoadoutSlotColors[0]`, `ItemSlot.cs:365-371`) since loadouts 2/3 are not
  modelled.
* The page tabs, defence counter and guide text are drawn but not interactive, and
  `Player.statDefense` is not modelled, so the defence counter always shows `0`.
  `ItemSlot.Handle` over the four equipment columns landed with S1-H-5
  (`clicks.rs::equip_slot_click` + `ui::inventory::equip_cell_at`), so the armour,
  vanity, dye and misc cells now take presses, hover tooltips and the right-click
  ladder.
* The bestiary/emote/achievement shortcut buttons and the NPC-housing page
  (`EquipPage 1`) are not drawn yet.
* `Main.inventoryBack`-tinted labels use white instead of the pulsing
  `Main.mouseTextColor` (`ui/inventory.rs` `LABEL_COLOR`).
* The reforge slot's menu opened with M3-REFORGE-1 — the (50,270) slot, the
  (120,310) button and the cost label ride the text-panel fidelity at the
  vanilla coordinates (`ui/mod.rs` + `clicks.rs`; the Reforge[0]/[1] button
  textures and the coin breakdown stay out). The guide/crafting slots keep
  their empty frames. **S1-P-i45 (2026-11-20)** corrected the hit boxes to the
  C# geometry (the slot `[50, 50+52*0.85] x [270, 270+52*0.85]` inclusive,
  `Main.cs:41673`; the button the strict `(105,135) x (295,325)`,
  `:41639-41641`) and removed the wrong `Main.mH` offset — the reforge block
  draws/clicks at the literal coordinates, only the equipment column's `num20`
  rides `mH` (`:41146`). See "Reforge fidelity (S1-P-i45)" below.
* **Equipment swaps (S1-H-5) вЂ” deviations from `ItemSlot.cs:3283-3650`.**
  RETIRED (S1-P-i48): the two-wings arm of `CanEquipBothAccessories`
  (`:3457-3464`) now reads the port's `Player::wing_slot` table (the i40
  wings census, the same 47 `Item.wingSlot` assignments), including the
  3580 vanity-wings exception. `Player.IsItemSlotUnlockedAndUsable`
  (`Player.cs:12579-12604`) is now the LIVE gate in the swap helpers too
  (S1-P-i48): rows 8/18 open with `extraAccessory` + expert mode exactly like
  the sim's grant loop (`player.rs::is_item_slot_unlocked_and_usable`); rows
  9/19 stay locked (no master difficulty) and the `Main.gameMenu` escape arms
  read false in play.
  The achievement hooks (`AchievementsHelper.NotifyItemPickup`/`HandleOnEquip`),
  the display-doll `NetMessage.SendData` tails and the `AnnounceTransfer` call
  have no port counterpart (single-player, no achievement events from swaps).
  `MouseItemSwap`'s favourite clear rides the port's positional `favorite_slots`
  table instead of a per-`ItemSlot` flag; the equipment arrays are outside that
  key space, so only the grid cell's entry is dropped.

### Closed hotbar and mouse item (`ui/mod.rs`, `ui/slot.rs`)

Both draw through the same `slot::draw_slot` (the `ItemSlot.Draw` port) as the open
grid: the closed hotbar at context 13 (`GUIHotbarDrawInner`, `Main.cs:43600-43639`) and
the cursor stack at context 21 (`DrawInterface_38_MouseCarriedObject`,
`Main.cs:45173-45195`). Remaining deliberate gaps:

* The context-13 **ammo/wand/bait count** (`num22`, `ItemSlot.cs:2577-2691` вЂ” the
  counter that replaces the stack text on bows, wands and fishing poles) is not
  ported; it needs the `useAmmo`/`bait`/`tileWand` inventory scans the item model
  does not have yet. Such items show their plain stack instead.
* `Inventory_Back20` (`ItemSlot.cs:2234-2237`, the white variant for
  `slot == player.selectedItemState.Hotbar`) and the context-36 override slot
  (`Main.cs:43641-43649`) are unreachable without `Player.SelectedItemState`
  overrides, which the port does not model; the selected slot always merges into the
  `Inventory_Back14` branch.
* The `Main.DoGlowingMouseItemDraw` shader pass over the cursor item
  (`Main.cs:45196-45220`) is not ported.
* `hotbarScale` keeps lerping while the inventory is open; vanilla freezes it because
  `GUIHotbarDrawInner` early-returns on `Main.playerInventory`
  (`Main.cs:43588-43591`) and the update lives in that draw pass. The targets
  (1.0 selected / 0.75 rest) and the `В±0.05` rate match (`Main.cs:43604-43611`).

### Crafting panel (`ui/crafting.rs`, `NewCraftingUI.cs`)

The modern crafting panel is ported as draw-only chrome at the source's geometry and
z-order (`docs/UI.md` в†’ "Crafting panel"). The deviations:

* The detail area (craft slot + `Images/UI/Craft` arrow) is drawn without a selected
  recipe; vanilla draws it only inside the
  `recipeEntry = _hoveredEntry ?? SelectedEntry` block (`NewCraftingUI.cs:447-448`,
  the `:448-482` range). With `Recipe.maxRecipes == 0` the port always renders it as
  static chrome.
* The panel ships open with the inventory (`NewCraftingUI.Visible`,
  `Main.cs:41706-41709`); `TR_NOCRAFT=1` hides it and `TR_CRAFT=1` forces it on
  (mirroring `TR_INV`).
* The recipe **filter strip** is live (S1-H-7): `craft_filter.rs` ports the eleven
  `ItemFilters` predicates (`ItemFilters.cs:71-464`), the exclusive tab toggle
  (`UICreativeItemsInfiniteFilteringOptions.cs:80-100`) and
  `EntryFilterer.FitsFilter` (`EntryFilterer.cs:30-55`). Three deviations:
  `Item.tileWand` is not a field on the port's `ItemDef`, so a tile wand is
  classified by its `createTile`/`createWall` alone вЂ” a wand whose tile is
  frame-important falls to `MiscFallback` instead of `BuildingBlock`/`Tools`;
  `MiscFallback`'s per-type `bool?[]` cache (`:410-425`) is omitted because the
  predicate is already a pure function of the item type (so is the grid's
  `_filteredRecipes`, which `FilterBoard::shown` recomputes each call вЂ” the C#
  only re-derives when the count changes, `:624-627`); and `ItemFilters.BySearch`
  (`:16-69`) is not wired to the search box, which has no keyboard text field
  anywhere in the port (the same reason the char/world-name screens use
  stand-ins). The `CreativePowers.Tab*` hover label resolves through
  `Language.GetTextValue`, which the port's `lang::text` already serves.
* No scrollbar interaction: the panel is draw-only for the recipe grid, without
  `ItemSlot.Handle` (out of scope, as documented for the inventory panels above).
* The cancel button is always visible вЂ” `White * 0.4` at rest, `White` on hover.
  Vanilla's `UIImageButton` never hides the icon (`_visibilityInactive = 0.4f`,
  `UIImageButton.cs:13-15`); the port's plan wrongly assumed it hid while the search
  box was empty.
* The `Main.InGuideCraftMenu` variants (guide slot, "Place a material here" label,
  hidden nearby-chests toggle) are ported behind `crafting::draw`'s `guide_mode`
  parameter but never reached: the guide slot cannot be opened in the port yet, so
  the menu is never entered and `guide_mode` stays false.

### Minimap frame and boss bar (P4) (`ui/minimap.rs`, `ui/bars.rs`, `ui/chrome.rs`)

The minimap frame (`MinimapFrame`/`MinimapFrameManager`/`MinimapFrameTemplate`)
and the boss bar (`BigProgressBarHelper.DrawFancyBar`) are ported at the source
geometry (`docs/UI.md` в†’ "Minimap frame" / "Boss bar"). The deviations and
behaviour notes:

* `Main.MapScale` is **live** as of M6-SETTINGS P4 (before that it was pinned to
  the reference `1.0`): the minimap anchor and the whole panel's render scale
  read the `MapScale` config key (load-clamped `0.5..1.0`, `Main.cs:4494`), and
  the port stands in for `Matrix.CreateScale(Main.MapScale)`
  (`Main.cs:55308-55329`, foreground batch at `:55768`) by keeping
  `ui::minimap`'s geometry in the source's transform space вЂ” the origin divided
  by the scale (`:55510-55511`), the pointer too (`:55512-55513`) вЂ” and
  multiplying back inside the two draw passes. The full map keeps
  `Main.mapFullscreenScale` (`Main.cs:55390`, default 4f `:66756`) and the zoom
  axis `Main.mapMinimapScale` (`Main.cs:55515-55522`) is unaffected. The
  Interface slider itself is still a P5 hand-off вЂ” the key is read from
  `config.json` only.
* No UI cue plays: the buttons' hover/click sounds `SoundEngine.PlaySound(12)`
  (`MinimapFrame.cs:167,174`) and the icon row's `PlaySound(10)/(12)`
  (`Main.cs:41100,41109-41119`) are not ported вЂ” no UI cue is loaded
  (`audio.rs:22-31`), consistent with the silent menus. `Main.DoStatefulTickSound`
  (`:41126`) is not ported either.
* `mapStyle == 2` (the overlay style) draws nothing in the minimap branch вЂ”
  but its OWN style-2 arm is landed: the D18 draw arm (compose step 0 re-fold
  of e18 `099beeba5`, research/84 §10.4) draws the overlay tile pass +
  `num37` layer walk + hover tail in `frame/draw.rs`'s style-2 branch
  (`Main.cs:55548-55578`/`:55609`/`:55615-55625`); the old "Uncertainty 7 /
  no Rust counterpart" wording is superseded. The `:55626-55694` icon block
  rides the f29-tip landing.
* The minimap **content** icons are not ported: NPC map icons, player heads,
  revenge/death markers (`TextureAssets.MapDeath`) and map pings
  (`TextureAssets.MapPing`) вЂ” the render entry points of research В§F
  (`geometry-extraction.md`, `Main.cs:55619-55680`, `PingMapLayer.cs:35`).
  The frame chrome draws around the bare tile pass; a future `MapIcons` task
  owns them.
* The shielded 7-arg `DrawFancyBar` overload (`BigProgressBarHelper.cs:72-126`)
  and `DrawBareBonesBar` (`:11-23`) are not ported вЂ” the former has no
  reachable caller in this port, the latter is dead code.
* `BigProgressBarSystem.ShowText` is **live** as of M6-SETTINGS P4 (before that
  it was always on): `boss_bar_text` feeds `ui::bars::draw_fancy_bar`, which
  skips `DrawHealthText` when the flag is off (`BigProgressBarHelper.cs:53-55`)
  вЂ” the bar, the frame and the head icon keep drawing, only the `current / max`
  numbers disappear.
* The map-style icon row draws without the `Main.mapEnabled` gate
  (`:41056`) while its clicks keep the gate (the documented draw/click
  asymmetry in `chrome.rs`/`app/clicks.rs`): the row is visible with the map disabled,
  but only clicks when the map system is enabled. Visible only with
  `MapEnabled=false`.
* The icon-row clicks fire on the press frame; vanilla tests
  `Main.mouseLeft && Main.mouseLeftRelease` (`:41095`), i.e. on the release
  frame. One shot either way (the port's pre-existing press convention).
* Hovering a minimap zoom button suppresses mine/place/attack inputs вЂ” the
  port mirrors `MinimapFrame.Update`'s `mouseInterface = true`
  (`MinimapFrame.cs:164`) through its `minimap_hover` flag. Listed because it
  changes input behaviour; it is faithful, not a gap.

### Determinism hooks

`TR_MOUSE=x,y` (pin the (UI-space) pointer), `TR_PAGE=name` (open a menu screen
directly вЂ” the word aliases `settings|general|interface|video|multiplayer` and the
numeric `menuMode` of every P5 sub-screen: 26, 28, 25, 252, 1125, 111, 2008, 1212,
1213, 1127, 27, 272727, 12, 13, 131, 30, 31, 889), `TR_MENU=1` (keep the menu on
screen), `TR_INV=1` (open the inventory),
`TR_CRAFT=1`/`TR_NOCRAFT=1` (force the crafting panel on/off), `TR_PVP=1`
(open `DrawPVPIcons`'s multiplayer-only draw/click gates),
`TR_EQUIPPAGE=n` (select `Main.EquipPage`), `TR_MAPSTYLE=0|1|2` (select
`Main.mapStyle`; invalid/missing в†’ 1, `Main.cs:66750`), `TR_BOSS` (spawn King
Slime вЂ” the boss bar's input), `TR_NOHUD=1` (hide the HUD, hotbar and minimap),
`TR_NOPLAYER=1`, `TR_NO_BG=1`, `TR_DAY=f`, `TR_SHOT=path`. Screenshots are
byte-identical across runs with `TR_NOPLAYER=1 TR_NO_BG=1 TR_DAY=0.5`.

## Menu sub-screens (P5) (`menu/`, `ui/sliders.rs`)

The seventeen `Main.DrawMenu` settings branches below menuMode 11 (26, 28, 25,
252, 1125, 111, 2008, 1212, 1213, 1127, 27, 272727, 13, 131, 30, 31, 889) and the
multiplayer branch (12) are ported as visual-only pages at the source geometry
(`docs/UI.md` в†’ "Menu sub-screens (P5)"); `IngameOptions.DrawValueBar` and the
HSL colour-slider block live in `ui/sliders.rs`. Deviations and behaviour notes:

* **Config write timing.** Vanilla saves `config.json` when the menu closes;
  the port writes it immediately on every toggle and once per drag on slider
  release (the port's write-per-edit convention from the settings-persistence
  milestone) вЂ” same keys and values, different moments.
* `parallax_scroll` defaults to **60** with a fresh config, not 0: vanilla seeds
  `Main.caveParallax = 0.88f` (`Main.cs:66809`) and `LoadSettings`'s keyless
  `Get("BackgroundParallax", ref bgScroll)` derives `bgScroll = 60` from it
  (`:4405-4408`), so the screen shows "Parallax: 60" and the backdrop applies
  the 0.88 factor вЂ” matching vanilla's out-of-box look.
* **The colour screens** differ in exactly two flags: menuMode 25 clamps
  luminosity to `[0.15, 1]` and hides the alpha bar, 252 uses the full range and
  shows it (`Main.cs:51239-51276`). Each frame the branch copies `selColor` into
  the page's colour (`:50324` / `:50346`) before the sliders seed/drag/recompose
  it, so the stored colour trails the knob by one frame вЂ” the original's order.
  The cursor tint reads the stored colour per frame (`app/frame.rs`, before
  `cursor.update()`), so dragging re-colours the pointer live (`Main.cs:50324` в†’
  `:52490`).
* **Lock-on priority cycles 0 в†’ 1 в†’ 2 в†’ 1**, not back to 0: `CycleUseModes`
  ThreeDSв†’TargetClosest (`LockOnHelper.cs:103-116`) skips `FocusTarget`, which is
  unreachable by cycling (a fresh `LoadSettings` also rewrites 0 to 2,
  `Main.cs:4496-4505`).
* **Multiplayer transitions are cut down to the menu.** Without a character/world
  select (P6): Multiplayer "Join"/"Host & Play" open the input screens directly
  instead of the character select (`Main.cs:50713-50730`); menuMode 131 Accept
  opens the password screen (31) instead of connecting (`OnSubmitServerPort`,
  `:52047-52054`); the password screens' Back rows return to Join Port /
  Multiplayer instead of cancelling the connect / the world select
  (`:51950-51957`, `ExitServerPasswordMenu :52018-52028`); 889 Back returns to
  Multiplayer instead of the world select (`:48804-48806`). The 889 "Allowed
  Users" rows stay blank вЂ” the Steam-only lobby branch (`:48749-48777`) never
  fills them without `SocialAPI.Network`. The port splits the host and join
  password strings where vanilla shares one `Netplay.ServerPassword`. Host keeps
  the vanilla fixed listen port 7777 (`HostAndPlay`, `:52011`); the old custom
  port row is gone (`TR_HOST` still overrides for tests).
* **M6-SETTINGS (config parity, 2026-11-09).** The settings layer now matches
  the source on all four axes:
  - **Defaults.** `Settings::default()` is the `static Main()` set:
    `musicVolume`/`ambientVolume`/`soundVolume` `1f` (`Main.cs:66857-66859`),
    `invasionProgressMode` `2` (`:67080`), `SettingPlayWhenUnfocused` `false`
    (`:66512`), `FrameSkipMode` `Subtle` (`:67204`) вЂ” the port's earlier
    `0.75`/`1`/`true`/`0` were plain parity breaks (the out-of-box screen
    labels and the first-run audio levels differed).
  - **Key names.** `to_json` writes the vanilla `SaveSettings` names вЂ”
    `ShowItemText` (`Main.cs:4135`), `GraphicsQuality` (`:4130`),
    `GoreVisualsAllowed` (`:4101`), `SettingsEnabled_MinersWobble` (`:4153`),
    `SettingsEnabled_TilesSwayInWind` (`:4157`),
    `GamepadDisableInstructionsDisplay` (`:4151`), `InvasionBarMode` (`:4096`),
    `VolumeMusic`/`VolumeSound`/`VolumeAmbient` (`:4105-4107`),
    `PlayWhenUnfocused` (`:4217`), `HidePasswords` (`:4144`) вЂ” and `parse`
    keeps every pre-parity port spelling as an alias, so a port-written config
    from before this pass still restores its values. The earlier
    `"HidePassword"`-singular note is superseded: the port now writes the
    vanilla plural and reads both spellings.
  - **The `LightingMode` ordinal.** The C# enum is
    `{White=0, Retro=1, Trippy=2, Color=3}`
    (`Terraria/Graphics/Light/LightMode.cs:3-9`) while the port's internal
    order is `{Color=0, White=1, Retro=2, Trippy=3}`
    (`tr-core/src/lighting/params.rs:12-17`), so `parse`/`to_json` translate in
    both directions and only the persisted byte is the vanilla ordinal
    (vanilla casts the stored int unchecked, `Main.cs:4398-4403`; an
    out-of-range byte keeps the default instead вЂ” a deliberate robustness
    deviation).
  - **Read-once.** `config.json` is read exactly once (`main.rs` в†’
    `App::new(settings, вЂ¦)` в†’ `Menu::new(settings, вЂ¦)`, the menu holding a
    working clone); the four read sites the research listed (`main.rs`,
    `App::new`, `Menu::new` and `CursorState::default`) collapse to one, and the
    menu-close sync (`close_menu`/`park_menu` в†’ `App.settings` +
    `apply_settings`) still carries the edited values back.
  - **Kept limitation:** a real vanilla `config.json`'s `MouseColor` /
    `MouseBorderColor` dictionaries are multi-line (Newtonsoft
    `Formatting.Indented`, `Preferences.cs:47-53`), which the port's line-based
    parser cannot read; the port writes one-line dicts itself, so its own
    round-trips work and a vanilla file's colours fall back to their defaults.
  - **Kept port-wide behaviour:** a malformed boolean coerces to `false`
    rather than vanilla's `Preferences.Get` keeping the field default
    (`Preferences.cs:176-190`); changing that is a parser-wide change, not a
    settings one, so it is recorded here instead.
* **Stored without consumers yet** (visual-only, spec В§9.1): the volume sliders
  (no audio engine reads the volumes), the six Effects toggles / smart-cursor
  flags / `FlashyEffects*` (no gameplay consumer), `resource_sets` (the HUD
  always renders the Classic set вЂ” the default above) and
  `portrait_preference`. The Interface "Minimap Border" row is the exception вЂ”
  live, see below. `boss_bar_text` and `map_scale` left this list with the
  P4 consumers below.
  Flags whose *system* the port does not have at all stay stored-only, each with
  its own note (never a stand-in consumer вЂ” the P4 rule): a flag is either wired
  to the real system or written down here.
  - **`blood`** (`ChildSafety.Disabled`, key `GoreVisualsAllowed`, `Main.cs:4101`
    Put / `:4349` Get) is vanilla's gore gate вЂ” it also suppresses the dangerous
    dust (`Dust.cs:194`, `:445`) and the player-side blood
    (`Player.cs:38912`), with the gore check itself at `Gore.cs:1334`. The port
    has no gore system (only the ambient leaf gores of `render/foliage.rs`), so
    nothing exists for the flag to turn off: it stays stored-only until the gore
    port lands.
  - **`placement_preview`** (`Main.placementPreview`, key `PlacementPreview`,
    `Main.cs:4100`/`:4348`) drives the placement preview's opacity ramp вЂ”
    `Player.UpdatePlacementPreview` (`Player.cs:43402`) counts the frames the
    player has been moving and `GetPlacementPreviewOpacity`
    (`Player.cs:43389-43399`) remaps that count from full alpha to zero, which
    `TileObject.DrawPreview` draws (`TileDrawing.cs:740`). The port places tiles
    without drawing the tile-object preview, so the flag has no consumer yet.
  - **`mouse_border_color`** (`Main.MouseBorderColor`, key `MouseBorderColor`,
    `Main.cs:4179` Put / `:4462` Get, default `(64,64,64,64)` `:66514`) is the
    cursor's border tint: `Main.ThickMouse` (`Main.cs:2599`) thickens the
    smart-cursor outline with it and shifts the mouse-text block 6 px
    (`Main.cs:20203`; the other reader is `Utils.cs:2789`). The port draws
    neither a cursor border nor a smart-cursor outline, so the colour (like
    `mouse_color`, which the cursor tint does read) has no consumer.
  - **`smart_cursor_toggle`** (`Main.cSmartCursorModeIsToggleAndNotHold`, key
    `SmartCursorToggle`, `Main.cs:4094`/`:4330`, default `true` `:67178`) picks
    toggle vs hold for the smart cursor in `Player.TryToToggleSmartCursor`
    (`Player.cs:28814-28842`). The port has no `SmartCursorHelper` block
    selection, so there is no smart cursor to toggle.
  - **`smart_axe_first`** (`Player.SmartCursorSettings.SmartAxeAfterPickaxe`,
    `Player.cs:331`, key `UseSmartAxeAfterSmartPickaxe`, `Main.cs:4139`/`:4412`,
    default `false`) is the smart-cursor priority order вЂ” axe before pickaxe
    instead of after. Without the ported block selection there is no priority to
    order.
  - **`smart_blocks`** (`Player.SmartCursorSettings.SmartBlocksEnabled`,
    `Player.cs:330`, key `UseSmartCursorForCommonBlocks`, `Main.cs:4138`/`:4411`,
    default `false`) lets the smart cursor bridge to common blocks; it is the
    branch `SmartCursorHelper` takes when scanning for a target. The port has no
    such scan, so the flag is inert.
  All three smart-cursor flags share one missing system:
  `SmartCursorHelper` (`SmartCursorHelper.cs`) and its drawing half
  `Main.DrawSmartCursor` (`Main.cs:46609`) вЂ” the 16x16 outline around
  `Main.SmartCursorX/Y` plus the directional arrows (`:46650-46656`) вЂ” are not
  ported, so no consumer is honest until that task lands.
* **The menuMode 888 destinations stay hints**: the 1127 "Keybindings" row shows
  the not-ported notice because `ManageControlsMenu` is a `UIState` screen, out
  of P5 scope (spec В§9.1) вЂ” the 27/272727 lists below cover the raw bind data.
* **The Video page carries a port-only "Zoom: вЂ¦%" row** the original does not
  have (menuMode 1111 is Resolution, Parallax, Frame Skip, Lighting, Quality,
  Background, Blood and Gore, Miner's Wobble, Windy Environment, Effects, Back вЂ”
  11 rows, `Main.cs:49988-50096`); vanilla persists Zoom to `config.json`
  (`"Zoom"`, `Main.cs:4200`) but no `DrawMenu` row edits it вЂ” drop the row in a
  follow-up (or P6).
* The Settings "Language" row label is vanilla `Lang.menu[103]` and the screen
  it opens here is the 1213 list (`Main.cs:49759-49764`) вЂ” noted for the P6
  phase.

### Task 5 notes (C# facts that override the plan tables)

* `menuMode` 27 (Keybindings) and 272727 (Map Keys) are **unreachable
  upstream**: no `menuMode = 27` / `= 272727` assignment exists anywhere under
  `decompiled/` вЂ” the Settings "Controls" row opens 1127, whose "Keybindings"
  row opens the menuMode 888 `ManageControlsMenu` UIState
  (`Main.cs:50661-50666`, out of scope). Both list screens are ported for
  completeness and are reachable only via `TR_PAGE=27` / `TR_PAGE=272727`; no
  navigation leads to them.
* `Reset Keybindings` (`Main.ResetKeyBindings`, `Main.cs:52459-52475`) is only
  called by the mode-27 Reset row (`Main.cs:50561`); it restores
  `W S A D Space T Escape H J B E LeftShift LeftControl R`
  (`:52461-52474`). The 272727 Reset row inlines the map seeds
  `Tab M Add Subtract PageUp PageDown` (`:50451-50456` = the
  `:67190-67195` defaults). 1127 has no Reset row. The port keeps the binds
  session-only (vanilla saves them in the player file, not `config.json`);
  captured keys store winit debug names (`KeyW`) where XNA would store `W`.
* C# facts that override the plan table (plan arithmetic/reading slips, C# is
  truth):
  - 1127 Back draw y = `250 + 52*3 + 18` = **424**, not the plan's 464.
  - 272727 Back keeps **scale 1.0**: the branch assigns `array7[6] = 0.8f`
    twice (`Main.cs:50439-50440`) and never touches `array7[7]`
    (`:50441-50444`), unlike the mode-27 twin's 0.8 (`:50550`).
  - `SelectionHolder.CycleSelection` (`SelectionHolder.cs:44-58`) activates
    the option **before** the active one, wrapping the first to the last вЂ”
    the Interface selector cycles run *backwards* (Default в†’ Valkyrie в†’ вЂ¦ в†’
    Golden в†’ Default; resource sets: Default в†’ New в†’ NewWithText в†’ вЂ¦ в†’
    Default). The plan's "next-in-order" and its "cycling from Valkyrie lands
    on Default" oracle were both wrong; from Valkyrie the cycle lands on
    Retro.
  - `BigProgressBarSystem.ShowText` defaults **true** (static ctor,
    `BigProgressBarSystem.cs:259`), so `TR_PAGE=interface` shows "Boss Health
    Bar Numbers: On" by default, not the plan's "Off". The flag is live:
    `boss_bar_text` reaches `ui::bars::draw_fancy_bar`, which skips
    `DrawHealthText` when it is off (`BigProgressBarHelper.cs:53-55`).
* `resource_sets` defaults to `"Default"` (label "Classic") while vanilla's
  config default is `"New"` (`PlayerResourceSetsManager.cs:28`) вЂ” the planned
  deviation: the port renders the Classic set, so the row must agree with the
  HUD. A vanilla `config.json` value still round-trips unchanged.
* The Interface "Minimap Border" row is *live* behaviour, not visual-only:
  cycling rewrites `settings.minimap_frame`, which the game loop feeds
  through `ui::minimap::style_index` (`app/clicks.rs`), so the minimap frame
  re-renders immediately. Map Scale is the other live row: `map_scale` feeds
  the minimap's anchor (`52 + (int)(240 * MapScale)`, `Main.cs:55275-55276`) and
  the whole panel's render scale, through the port's stand-in for
  `Matrix.CreateScale(Main.MapScale)` (`Main.cs:55309-55329`): `ui::minimap`
  keeps its geometry in the source's transform space (the origin divided by the
  scale, `Main.cs:55510-55511`, the pointer likewise `:55512-55513`) and the two
  draw passes multiply back. The full map is untouched вЂ” it scales by
  `Main.mapFullscreenScale` (`Main.cs:55390`, default 4f `:66756`) вЂ” and so is
  the `mapMinimapScale` zoom axis (`Main.cs:55515-55522`).

## Front-end screens (P6) (`ui/`, `app/flow.rs`)

The whole-UI P6 front end (character/world select + create, the virtual
keyboard, credits вЂ” commits `02182dc..043e11c`) is ported at the source
geometry; the screens, coordinates and flow are in `docs/UI.md` в†’
"Front-end screens (P6)". The deviations and stand-ins:

* ~~**No `.plr` reader/writer** (spec §9.4).~~ **Closed (S1-J-3/S1-J-5 +
  W4-f22).** The `.plr` reader/writer are live (`player_file.rs`, release 326,
  the full `Serialize`/`Deserialize` walk), the listing reads real files
  (`save_list::list_players`), Create writes one
  (`session.rs::save_created_character`), and the card renames
  read-modify-write it (W4-f22, research/19 M1 —
  `rename_player_file`/`rename_world`, the keyboard tails; see "The card
  renames" below). The session stand-in plus optional `TR_FAKE_CHARS`
  fakes remain alongside the disk cards.
* **World metadata stand-ins.** Favourites are a `<world>.trfav` marker file
  (`Main.LocalFavoriteData` has no port); creation time is the file's mtime;
  the world writer stores no `GameMode`, so every real entry reads Classic
  (`WorldEntry::difficulty`), which is why the Journey rejection (S1-H-10) can
  only fire for a Journey session player today;
  the world card icon is a fixed `IconCrimson` (no evil data to pick the
  sprite); the playtime panel is a fixed `00:00:00` (no play-time tracking).
  Invalid worlds bucket to Small (vanilla shows Unknown вЂ” no Unknown
  bucket); `erase_world` deletes the orphan `.map` (vanilla leaves it,
  plan-ordered); erases delete outright вЂ” no recycle bin
  (`FileUtilities.Delete`).
* **No cloud favourite buttons, `Rename` at card Left 52** вЂ”
  `SocialAPI.Cloud == null` in the port, exactly the branch the original
  takes without a cloud account.
* **No gamepad snap points** (the `SetSnapPoint` sites, e.g.
  `UIWorldListItem.cs:205`, have no port) and **no UI click sounds**: the
  `SoundEngine.PlaySound(10/11/12)` sites вЂ” the confirms' Yes/No included вЂ”

  `char_creation.rs` ports `Click_CopyHex`/`Click_PasteHex`/`GetHexColor`/
  `GetPlayerTemplateValues`/`Click_PastePlayerTemplate` plus `Click_RandomizePlayer`
  and `Click_RandomizeSingleColor`. Two retained deviations: (1) the draft still
  has **no voice fields** (`voiceVariant`/`voicePitchOffset`), so `player_template`
  writes the gender default `voiceStyle = (Male ? 1 : 2)` (`Player.cs:55735`'s
  legacy default) and `voicePitch = 0.0`, and a pasted template's `voiceStyle`/
  `voicePitch` are validated but dropped вЂ” `Click_RandomizePlayer` still *consumes*
  the C# voice draw (`Main.rand.Next(2)`) so the stream stays 1:1; (2)
  `apply_player_template` is lenient where the C# `catch` would abort the whole
  paste on a type cast (a colour value that is not a string is skipped, not
  fatal), and it follows `Player.PrettyPrintProfiles`' no-op-for-a-flat-object
  behaviour rather than the formatting transform.
* **`assign_random_world_name` is a stand-in**: `AssignRandomWorldName`
  (`UIWorldCreation.cs:1002-1025`) composes a name from the
  `RandomWorldName_*` localization tables the port has not loaded; the
  stand-in is `"World {n+1}"` (`UIWorldSelect.cs:113`'s shape). A
  non-numeric world seed likewise hashes the name through the
  `ReLogic.Utilities.Crc32` port (poly 0xEDB88320) instead of `Main.rand` вЂ”
  deterministic per name, so the same draft always creates the same world.
* **`Color` multiplication wraps, not saturates** (`color.rs`'s pinned
  convention, re-pinned by the Task 8b review): `DarkGray * 1.2` =
  `[202, 202, 202, 50]` вЂ” the ghosted Master-difficulty bunny preview.

## UIElement framework — margins, snap points, state stack, layer stack (W4-d87, 2026-11-20)

The three framework gaps research 18 left open are now ported as pure machinery
(code + hand-computed pins; no cargo run on this lane):

* **Margins** — `ui/uistate.rs::resolve_with_margins` ports `Recalculate`'s head
  (`UIElement.cs:293-297`) and `GetDimensionsBasedOnParentDimensions`' inflate
  (`:317-318`) **in C# order**: clamp the content size (`:315-316`), inflate to
  the margin box, align the *inflated* box (`:319-320`), then shrink to
  `_dimensions` (`:293-296`). The inflate/subtract pair is not a no-op under
  `HAlign`/`VAlign != 0` — a centred margin box shifts by half the margin total.
  `resolve`/`resolve_with_max_h`/`resolve_in_list` delegate at `margin = [0; 4]`;
  the `+0.0`/`-0.0` steps are exact for every finite float, so every existing
  caller is bit-identical (pinned by
  `resolve_zero_margins_is_bit_identical_to_the_old_margin_free_pass`).
  Deviation: `resolve_in_list` still substitutes `f32::MAX` for the C#'s
  `float.MaxValue` (`:290`) — pre-existing, unchanged.
* **Snap points** — `ui/snap.rs` ports `SnapPoint.cs` (`Calculate` `:27-31` =
  `Position() + offset + anchor*size` against `GetDimensions()`, the
  margin-shrunk rect; `ThisIsAHackThatChangesTheSnapPointsInfo` `:33-38`) and
  `UIElement.SetSnapPoint`/`GetSnapPoint`/`GetSnapPoints` (`:124-145,271-283`):
  the (0.5, 0.5)/zero defaults, the recalculate-on-read, and the
  self-then-children pre-order walk over the flat table's `parent` links
  (append order preserved, same ruling as `framework.rs`). The gamepad consumer
  (`UILinkPointNavigator`) remains unported — deliberate, Stage 1.
* **State stack** — `ui/state_stack.rs` ports `UserInterface.SetState`/`GoBack`/
  `AddToHistory` (`:276-322`) over screen ids: the same-state early return
  *before* the history append, the MouseOut→Deactivate→ResetState→Activate→
  Recalculate effect order, the 2-deep `GoBack` pop that re-appends via
  `SetState`, and the history **sawtooth** (`>32` drops the first **four**,
  33→29 — not a sliding window). Verified: `UserInterface.GoBack` has zero call
  sites in 1.4.5.8 (all 8 `GoBack()` hits are screens' private helpers, e.g.
  `UIWorldCreation.cs:670-674` → `Main.OpenWorldSelectUI()`); research 18
  deviation 9's "is called from the back-button paths" was wrong and is
  corrected. `app/flow.rs` is **not** rewired — its per-screen back entries are
  what the C# screens actually do.
* **Layer stack** — `ui/layers.rs` ports `InterfaceScaleType` (Game/UI/None),
  `GameInterfaceLayer.Draw`'s matrix selection (`:22-37`), the 43-layer vanilla
  table (`Main.cs:44718-44918`, 16 Game / 27 UI / 0 None — `Mouse Over` is
  world-space while its neighbours are UI) and `DrawInterface`'s stop-on-false
  walk (`:44930-44935`, the stopping layer counts as drawn). Deviation:
  `app/frame.rs` still draws the HUD in fixed code order and applies no
  per-layer zoom — the table is data the wiring follow-up will consume; no
  pixels change in this task.
### The card renames (W4-f22, research/19 M1)

The select screens' Rename buttons now WRITE. `KeyboardTail::Rename` (the
character card) and the new `KeyboardTail::WorldRename` (the world card) run
`OnFinishedSettingName` (`UICharacterListItem.cs:208-214`,
`UIWorldListItem.cs:427-432`) instead of the historical "Renaming is not
ported yet" notice; `KeyboardSession.rename_index` carries the clicked card
(`this._data`), so the submit writes THAT entry, not a name search.

- **Character** — `player_file::rename_player_file` is `PlayerFileData.Rename`
  (`IO/PlayerFileData.cs:207-214`) as a read-modify-write: the vanilla mutates
  the live `Player.name` and re-serializes the whole player; the port models
  only the card state, so it decrypts the `.plr`, replaces ONLY `Serialize`'s
  first field (`Player.cs:54752`, offset 24 = release 4 + FileMetadata 20),
  keeps every other byte (the unmodelled tail is NOT re-defaulted), and
  re-encrypts with the write-side PKCS7 envelope. The `.bak` copy is
  `InternalSavePlayerFile:54730-54733`. The load gate runs first
  (`Player.GetFileData`'s null-skip, `:55862-55881`).
- **World** — `save_list::rename_world` is `WorldGen.RenameWorldCallBack`
  (`WorldGen.cs:6727-6753`: load, `Main.worldName = newName`, save) as the
  `.trwld` header-name splice (`save.rs:230-232`'s u32-length + UTF-8 field at
  offset 20); the tile body and the v7+ side sections ride through unchanged.
  The callback's sound 10 (`GetRenameCallback`, `WorldFileData.cs:473`) plays
  after the submit cue, then the `menuMode = 6` reopen re-lists.
- **Deviations**: (1) the world file keeps its stem — the vanilla
  `GetWorldPathFromName` move belongs to the cloud path (`WorldFileData.cs:433`),
  and `RenameWorldCallBack` itself rewrites the loaded file in place; (2) the
  session stand-in IS the live player, so its rename lands on
  `player_name`/`session_draft` (`PlayerFileData.cs:209-212`'s `Player.name`
  write) and survives the re-list; a `TR_FAKE_CHARS` fake renames in memory
  only and the re-list rebuilds it (the fake-erase shape); (3) a failed write
  keeps the old name and surfaces `front_hint` — the vanilla
  `FancyErrorPrinter` dialog has no port; (4) the `menuMode = 10` saving
  pass-through is synchronous (the port's saves are inline).
- Witnesses (written, not run — code-only): `player_file::tests` (4: the
  rename + `.bak` + untouched-fields round-trip, the byte-splice invariant,
  the garbage refusal, the multibyte 7-bit-length name), `save_list::tests`
  (3: the header rewrite + re-list + full-parse survival, the splice

  rename-click session shape, the submit seam, the world rename click +
  submit end-to-end).

## UIElement framework (M7-UI-1, 2026-11-08)

The framework halves of `UIElement`/`UserInterface` that the screens cannot live
without вЂ” the pointer machine (`ui/pointer.rs`) and the flat hit order
(`ui/framework.rs`, `ui/select_hit.rs`) вЂ” landed on branch `M7-UI-1-uielement`
with the layout pass unchanged in `ui/uistate.rs`. The screen-model ruling stays:
an immediate port, no retained tree, no `UserInterface` object. Card double-click
play is the feature it buys, and it is **routing only**: the port has no per-card
selection state and its play path closes the front flow rather than loading the
entry (spec В§9.4), so a double-click resolves to the same flow a Play button
click does.

Corrected deviations (both were geometry the layout pass would have got right,
and a third was the click gate the geometry feeds):

* **The state-change click lockout never expired (fix-world-select-clicks).**
  `App::enter_front` arms `UserInterface`'s 200 ms post-`SetState` disable
  (`ResetState`, `:178`, ported at `ui/pointer.rs:141`), but the *only* countdown
  site sat inside `frame()`'s `if self.menu.is_none() && self.front.is_none()`
  branch вЂ” the in-game regime вЂ” so `PointerState::tick` never ran while a front
  screen (`Main.menuMode == 888`) was live. `click_disabled_ms` therefore stayed
  at 200.0 and `clicks_disabled()` was permanently true, which dropped every
  press twice: once at `app/loop.rs:422` (no `PointerEvent` produced) and again
  at `handle_front_click` (`UserInterface.cs:214-218`, the gate the click tables
  run behind). **Every** row of **every** front screen вЂ” world select's cards,
  New/Back/Favorite/Rename/Delete, and the character-select twins вЂ” was dead
  until the app was restarted. The C# decrements unconditionally:
  `Main.UpdateUIStates` (`Main.cs:17039`/`:17487-17492`) reaches
  `MenuUI.Update` on every frame, and `UserInterface.cs:203-204` clears the
  countdown before reading the gate. The port now calls
  `App::tick_pointer_clock` from `frame()` on every frame, outside the
  in-game branch, with a citation naming the C# reach. This replaces the older
  note here that the 200 ms disable "is armed on the enter direction only
  (`enter_front`), not on the leave direction the C#'s `SetState(null)` also
  resets" вЂ” neither direction decayed.
  The existing double-click test had masked it by hand-ticking the lockout away
  (`app.pointer.tick(300.0)`); it now advances the real `frame()` seam.
  The screen geometry itself was never implicated: `world_select::card_hit`
  (`ui/world_select.rs:506`), the layout shared with char_select (`:42`, `:185`)
  and the framework's `get_element_at` (`ui/framework.rs:64`) are all 1:1 with

  **Re-landed 2026-11-10 (fix-world-select-clicks-2):** the M6-ACH-2 merge
  (a75dd14) silently reverted this fix - its auto-resolution restored the

* **The bestiary panel was 180 px short.** `bestiary::panel_rect` hand-wrote

## UI scale (S1-H-3, 2026-11-13)

`Main.UIScale` is ported as a value: `settings::ui_scale_max` is the C#
`Main.UIScaleMax` (`Math.Max(1f, Math.Min(h / 600f, w / 800f))`,
`Main.cs:2576-2583`), `Settings::ui_scale` is the persisted **wanted** scale
(`Main._uiScaleWanted`, key `"UIScale"`, `Put` `:4201` / `Get` `:4487`) and
`Settings::applied_ui_scale` is the setter's down-only clamp to the max
(`:2563-2572`). The ingame-options `GameUI.UIScale` bar is live (the C# slider's
0.5..2.0 range, `IngameOptions.cs:571-578`) and the fullscreen-map head icon
takes the applied scale.

Two deliberate deviations remain, recorded here rather than silently:

* **The default is plain `1.0`.** Vanilla's `Get("UIScale", GetScaling())` reads
  the platform DPI scaling and, on a fresh install, `TryPickingDefaultUIScale`
  sets `displayHeight / 1080f * 1.1f` (`:4257-4265`, applied at `:4489`). Neither
  is available at settings-load time in this port (no `IWindowService`, no
  display), so a headless boot starts at 1.0; the user can still set any scale
  from the bar.
* **The scale is applied at the render sites the port has, not to the UI root
  dimensions.** Vanilla divides `UserInterface.GetDimensions()` by `Main.UIScale`
  (`UserInterface.cs:335`) and gives `GameInterfaceLayer` three scale spaces; the
  port's screens derive their rects straight from the swapchain, so scaling the
  whole UI is still open (the M-sized follow-up noted against S1-H-3 in
  `docs/research/18-ui-framework.md`).

## Scroll wheel (S1-H-4, 2026-11-13)

`UserInterface.Update`'s scroll arm (`UserInterface.cs:219-223`) now lives in the
pointer machine: `PointerState::queue_scroll` accumulates
`PlayerInput.ScrollWheelDeltaForUI` and `PointerState::scroll_wheel` dispatches it
to the element under the pointer, zeroing the accumulator **whatever the hit**
(the C# `= 0` runs even when `uIElement` is null, `:222`); `PointerEvent::ScrollWheel`
carries the int delta (`UIScrollWheelEvent.cs:7`). `loop.rs` routes the
achievements/emotes/chest surfaces through the machine and hands the consumed delta
back; the hotbar and the fullscreen-`map` zoom fallbacks stay raw because neither
is a `UserInterface` element in 1.4.5.8.

* **Fidelity note.** The machine's delta is an `i32` (matching C#'s int
  `ScrollWheelDeltaForUI`), so the achievements arm now fires only when the rounded
  delta is non-zero. Previously it scrolled on sub-notch `PixelDelta` values
  (`|d| < 0.5`), which C# cannot produce. W4-d88 completed the arm: the consumed
  int delta passes through as notches (`scroll_achievements(delta)`), each worth
  the raw 120-unit XNA counter (`UIList.cs:112`'s `-=`), and the wheel only
  reaches the list through `GetElementAt` — a point inside the list rect
  (`UIList.cs:16-19`'s `ContainsPoint => true`), never the panel-child scrollbar
  (`UIAchievementsMenu.cs:86`). The former one-row-per-notch stand-in
  (`delta * (ROW_H + 5)`) is gone.

## World select (S1-H-10, 2026-11-13)

`UIWorldListItem.PlayGame` (`UIWorldListItem.cs:360-385`) runs `base._data.IsValid`
then `TryMovingToRejectionMenuIfNeeded` (`:387-413`). The port now reproduces both:
`flow.rs::world_play_click` requires `WorldEntry::valid` and asks
`world_select::rejection_key` whether the world must be refused вЂ” an invalid
`GameModeID` (`GameModeID.cs:19-26`, modes 0..=3), a Journey player on a
non-Journey world, or a non-Journey player on a Journey world. Both the Play
button and `OnLeftDoubleClick`'s `PlayGame` route through it.

* **Rejection surface.** C# sets `Main.statusText` and `menuMode = 1000000`

  cue is kept (`Audio::play("Menu_Open")`).

## UI list clipping and the в€ћ-height parent (S1-H-2, 2026-11-13)

`UIElement.Draw`'s `OverflowHidden` branch (`UIElement.cs:199-238`) and
`GetClippingRectangle` (`:252-269`) are now ported, together with the `UIList`
parent special case in `Recalculate` (`:288-291`).

* **The clip is per-instance, not device state.** The renderer batches the whole
  UI into a single instanced draw (`SpriteRenderer::draw`, one range), so
  `wgpu::RenderPass::set_scissor_rect` would need one pass per clipped list вЂ” and
  nested lists would break the batch entirely. Instead `SpriteInstance` carries a
  `clip: [f32; 4]` rect (vertex attribute `@location(9)`), `sprite.wgsl` passes it
  to the fragment stage and `discard`s when
  `p.x < clip.x || p.y < clip.y || p.x >= clip.x + clip.z || p.y >= clip.y + clip.w`
  вЂ” XNA's rule (`left <= x < right`), so the edge pixels match a real scissor.
  `SpriteRenderer::push_clip`/`pop_clip` maintain a `clip.rs::ClipStack`; a nested
  push **intersects** the parent rect, which is what `GetClippingRectangle` does
  with `_innerDimensions` (`:254`) all the way up.
  The sentinel `NO_CLIP = [f32::MIN/2, f32::MIN/2, f32::MAX, f32::MAX]` makes the
  discard test a no-op for the 99 % of instances that are not clipped, so there is
  no second pipeline and no branch in the push paths. Cost: 16 extra bytes per
  instance (80 total) and one comparison chain per fragment.

* **`Element.viewport` is the hit-side half.** The C# `GetElementAt`
  (`:324-352`) descends only through a child whose `Contains(point)` is true, so a
  list row entirely below the list's inner bottom is *unreachable* even though its
  own rect does not overlap the list at all вЂ” the ancestor rejects the point
  first. The port models this as `Element.viewport: Option<[f32;4]>` (set by
  `Element::row`/`row_child`) and requires `point в€€ own rect && point в€€ viewport`
  in `hit_at`. This is stricter than an "overlap" test and is what the old
  break-gate approximated; two select-screen tests that had encoded the looser
  version were corrected (y 800 now resolves to `(None, None)`; y 777 still hits
  the Back/New row, because those are not list children).

* **`resolve_in_list` sets the в€ћ.** `UIElement.cs:288-291` resolves a child's
  percent height against `float.PositiveInfinity` when the parent is a `UIList`.
  `uistate::resolve_with_max_h` takes that parent height explicitly;
  `resolve_in_list` passes `f32::INFINITY` and `resolve` passes the real parent
  height. The hair grid (`48 * 22` rows) is the first consumer: it now spans the
  list's *content* height, and the list's own viewport is what clips it вЂ” the
  arithmetic the old `break` at `char_creation.rs:1859` was faking.

* **Screenshot proof.** With the scissor the hair screen loses **140 949 px** in
  the box `x 565-1022, y 484-899` (exactly the rows past the list inner bottom at
  482); two identical runs are SHA256-equal. Reverting `push_clip` reproduces the
  old overdraw.

* **W4-d67 (2026-11-20, code-only): the crafting grid joins the scissor
  consumers.** The modern crafting panel's recipe grid rides a `UIList` with
  `OverflowHidden = true` (`UIList.cs:59`, appended at `NewCraftingUI.cs:367-386`),
  but `ui/crafting.rs` drew the cells unclipped from the grid *container's*
  origin — two deviations fixed together:
  (1) `recipe_cell` now derives `startX`/`startY` from `GetGridParameters`
  (`UIDynamicItemCollection.cs:81-97`): the collection fills the inner list
  (`UIList.cs:57-58`), which fills the (padding-0) `UIList`, so the cells start
  at the **list** rect (y 446 at 1600×900, below the separator that owns the
  container's top 7 px), centred — `Center.X − (int)(44·cols·0.5)` gives the
  5 px inset (x 37); `_itemsPerLine` is the C#'s `Width / 44` on the collection
  width (450/44 = 10), not the old `(grid.w − 4)/44` stand-in (same 10 today,
  wrong divisor in principle).
  (2) The draw pass wraps the cell loop in `push_clip(l.list)`/`pop_clip` and
  `hit_test` rejects points outside the list before testing cells — the
  clipped-ancestor rule (`UIElement.cs:327-341`), the same `Element.viewport`
  contract the select screens use. At 1600×900 the 404 px view holds 9 whole
  rows; row 9 (842..882) straddles the 850 bottom and is cut mid-cell, rows ≥ 10
  are unreachable. Pins: `the_recipe_list_clip_rect_bounds_the_grid_content`,
  `clipped_recipe_cells_are_unreachable` (+ the re-based pitch/hit tests).
  The C# `UIDynamicItemCollection.GetGridParameters` also *virtualises* the
  draw range (`startItemIndex`/`endItemIndex` from the view culling area,
  `:89-96`) — an optimisation that skips off-view rows entirely; the port draws
  all rows and lets the fragment scissor cut them (same pixels, no LOD of world
  state; the scroll mechanics themselves stay deferred with `UIScrollbar`).
  The other two `GraphicsDevice.ScissorRectangle` sites (`Main.cs:25403-25424`
  and `:40406-40414`) are the bestiary/dialogue **portrait dummies** — both ride
  the deferred `Main.DrawNPCPortrait` system (`npc_chat.rs`'s module header),
  so they land with it; the map/minimap "clip" is `MapOverlayDrawContext`'s
  centre-point cull (`MapOverlayDrawContext.cs:45-48`), already ported in
  `map_layers.rs`, not a device scissor.

## Architecture refactor (2026-11-01)

The god-file split (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-01-architecture-refactor.md`,
commits `9c84351..028daba`) moved code, gave the moved functions readable Rust
names (overriding the C#-name rule for this pass) and added three C#-shaped
trait seams. Behaviour and RNG streams were pinned unchanged: the worldgen
byte-proof (four FNV-1a state hashes вЂ” at the time an out-of-tree harness;
now in-tree as `worldgen/world_hash.rs`'s pinned constants, M5-GEN-1) and a
post-refactor determinism pair
(SHA256-equal repeat screenshots) both pass; the workspace tests read
399/10/147. The new tree, the "where to look" map and the frame flow live in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; the `PORT_MAP.md` rows are re-pointed. The movements,
compressed:

- **tr-app.** `main.rs` 10 497 в†’ 86 lines (bootstrap only). The `App` split
  into `app/` (`mod.rs` struct + startup, `loop.rs` the winit handler,
  `frame.rs` the `Main.Draw` orchestrator + G6 cache, `flow.rs` the front-end
  state machine + `FrontScreenBehaviours`, `clicks.rs`, `session.rs`,
  `settings_ui.rs`, `netglue.rs`, `saveglue.rs`); the world draw passes into
  `render/` (`sky`, `bg`, `tiles`, `liquids`, `entities`, `foliage`, `debug` вЂ”
  ~4.5 k lines); the fixed-step simulation into `world_sim/` (`step`, `player`,
  `npcs`, `items`, `projectiles`, `editing`, `clock`, `liquids`, `weather`,
  `camera`); leaf types out of the bootstrap into `item.rs` and `biome.rs`.
- **`menu.rs` 4 187 в†’ `menu/`**: `mod.rs` (state, items, slider drag),
  `pages.rs` (the per-screen row tables), `actions.rs` (the `Action`
  semantics the App dispatches).
- **tr-core directories.** `tiledata.rs` regenerated by the fixed
  `tools/GenTileData` and split (`sets`/`emissive`/`merge` + a hand-written
  `mod.rs`); `map.rs` в†’ `map/` (`mod`/`colors`/`option`/`file`); `tile_light.rs`
  в†’ `tile_light/` (`mod`/`palette`/`scanner`); `lighting.rs` в†’ `lighting/`
  (`mod`/`params`/`blur`) with the `LightEngine` trait; `waterfall.rs` в†’
  `waterfall/` (`mod`/`draw`, the `LiquidKindChecks` trait artifact replaced by
  the free function `any_liquid_kind`); `worldgen.rs` в†’ `worldgen/`
  (`mod`/`noise`/`terrain`/`caves`/`liquids`/`surface`); `localization.rs` в†’
  `localization/` (`mod`/`culture`/`format`/`json`); `binio.rs` is the one
  little-endian cursor behind `save`/`wld`/`map` (the app-side `.trwld` header
  probe in `ui/save_list.rs` joined in this docs sweep).
- **Deduplication.** `ui::in_rect`/`in_rect_strict`/`hover_pair`/`push_whole`
  and the `text::border_string`/`draw_border_string`/`large_text_width`
  families replaced their per-screen copies; `ui/cards.rs` shares the select
  screens' card pieces; `world_sim/step.rs`'s `FixedStepper` replaced six
  identical 60 Hz accumulators; the `ReLogic.Utilities.Crc32` port lives once
  in `ui/world_creation.rs`.
- **C# seams** (the only new abstractions): `FrontScreenBehaviours` в‰€
  `UIState` (`app/flow.rs`), `LightEngine` в‰€ `ILightingEngine`
  (`tr-core/src/lighting/mod.rs`), and `render/bg.rs`'s `PassPrologue` в‰€ the
  `bgStartX`/jitter prologue the `Main.DrawBackground*` passes repeat.

Deviations recorded by the refactor and this sweep:

- **`tools/GenTileData`'s `numN` local is approximated, not modelled.** The
  `TileID.Sets.NeedsGrassFramingDirt[num]` argument is a decompiler-renamed
  local (`num11` in the previous decompilation, `num9` in the current one);
  the fixed generator resolves it to the active `case` ids (the grass id
  itself) instead of modelling the local's data flow вЂ” the approximation the
  framer expects grass variants to merge against (`Program.cs:613-621`).
- **`env.rs` landed (2026-11-09, REFACTOR-env).** The ~112 `TR_*` flags
  consolidated into `crates/tr-app/src/env.rs` as named accessors: every pin
  resolves once through a `OnceLock` and keeps its original read semantics
  (`env::var` vs `env::var_os`, the presence/value/parse shape), so no
  screenshot or test behaviour changed. `TR_SUNDIAL`/`TR_MOONDIAL` deliberately
  stay live reads вЂ” they are the only flags a test mutates (`set_var` /
  `remove_var` in the DW-1.6 pair, serialized by `ENV_LOCK`) and a `OnceLock`
  would latch the first test's value into the second's. The tr-core /
  tr-render pins (`TR_NOCACHE`, `TR_PROBE`) stay with their crates вЂ” a
  cross-crate pins module is the follow-up.
- **The P6 stand-ins** this sweep documented (see "Front-end screens (P6)"):
  `GameTipsDisplay` not ported, the Crc32-instead-of-`Main.rand` world-name/
  seed composition and the `assign_random_world_name` stand-in.
- **Risk 7 above is closed**: the generator matches the current
  decompilation again, and `tiledata.rs` is generated from it (the hand
  extraction in `torch.rs` stays as-is).

## GetTileDrawData deviations (TILE-DRAW-1, 2026-11-02)

`TileDrawing.GetTileDrawData` (`TileDrawing.cs:4527`, the type switch at
`:4540-6032`) is ported in full as the static layer of
`crates/tr-core/src/drawdata.rs`: a pure table
`draw_data(kind, x, y, frame_x, frame_y, tile_frame, solid_above) -> TileDrawData`
plus `TileDrawData::apply_world_corrections` for the four world-probing
corrections (below). Every case of the switch has an explicit status вЂ” an arm
carrying its unconditional static part, or a documented deviation вЂ” nothing
falls through silently. `C# ref tileFrameX/Y` rewrites are expressed as
`frame_x_override`/`frame_y_override`; the caller (`render/tiles.rs`) builds
the source rectangle from the final frame (`TileDrawing.cs:1007`).

**Animation state.** `tile_frame` is `Main.tileFrame[kind]`; the animator is
ported in `crates/tr-core/src/drawdata_anim.rs` (S1-F-9 wave B, below) but not
yet wired, so the production call still passes 0 вЂ” exactly the vanilla t=0
state. All `tile_frame * N` formulas are ported verbatim and activate unchanged
when the wiring lands. The default `addFrY = Main.tileFrame[type] * 38`
(`TileDrawing.cs:4533`) is ported as the same formula. `tile_frame = 0` was
verified against the C# per formula (transcription tests in `drawdata.rs`).

### S1-G-1f render wiring — ropes + animator (code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

The wiring wave for the landed-unwired render modules. **Code-only mode: no
compiler invoked; tests WRITTEN NOT RUN** — the gate phase runs them.

**G-1b ropes — WIRED.** `render/tiles.rs::draw_tiles` calls
`ropes::wants_back_rope` + `ropes::draw_back_rope` once per cell, at the exact
C# position: after `DrawSingleTile`'s `!flag` return (`TileDrawing.cs:1014-1017`)
and `IsVisible` (`:983`) — the port's dark-cell merge / `skip_draw` / unframed /
echo-hidden `continue`s — and BEFORE the cell's own sprite, because both C#
dispatch sites draw the rope first: `DrawBasicTile`'s planter/platform gate
(`:1511-1514`) and `DrawTile_MinecartTrack` (`:3792`, before the track sprites).
One gated hook covers both sites (`wants_back_rope` = 380 ∪ 314 ∪ Platforms).
The tint is the RAW `drawData.tileLight` (`:3781`) — the port passes `raw_l`,
never the actuation-ghosted `l`; sheet/paint come from the TOP rope tile
(`:3776-3780`). **G6:** the draw reads only world state (tile kinds/paints),
already covered by `world_revision` — no key change needed. Draw-order
witness: `back_rope_draws_after_the_gates_before_the_cell_sprite`
(source-scan, the S1-B-7 pattern).

**F-9b animator — WIRED (CritterCages still deferred).**
- Tick: `App::animate_tiles_phase` (`app/frame/world.rs`) runs
  `TileAnimator::animate_tiles` on a 60 Hz `FixedStepper` in the pre-gate
  Animate cluster, right after the waterfalls phase — the port's slot for
  `Main.AnimateTiles` (`Main.cs:17150`, after `DoUpdate_AnimateWalls`
  `:17149`). Like the waterfalls it ticks while paused (the C# cluster is
  pre-gate). The 453/456 drift draws + the bob roll ride `NamedRngs::global()`
  (the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in); `generating_or_loading` is false in the
  frame loop (worldgen completes before it starts). World-load reset in
  `enter_loaded_world` (`Main.cs:8393-8394`).
- Draw feed: `draw_tiles` takes `&TileAnimator`; `draw_data` +
  `apply_world_corrections` receive `animation_row(kind)`
  (`Main.tileFrame[typeCache]`, `TileDrawing.cs:4533`), slice B's
  `case_draw_data` receives the row + `tile_frame_counter[kind]`, and
  `CaseInputs::weather_vane_bobframe` rides `weather_vane_bobframe`.
  Out-of-range kinds keep the t=0 row (the `TILE_SOLID` bounds convention).
- **G6 key coverage:** new `WorldFrameKey::tile_anim` =
  `TileAnimator::anim_key()` — FNV-1a over EVERY `tile_frame` +
  `tile_frame_counter` entry + the bobframe (all three are draw inputs), so
  any clock-dependent pixel change invalidates the cached range. Gated on
  an animated kind being active in the view rect
  (`TileAnimator::is_animated_kind`, the waterfall/vine-grid convention):
  animator-free views keep the pre-wiring cache behaviour bit-for-bit.
  Witnesses: `every_touched_kind_is_in_the_gate_set` (diffs both arrays +
  bobframe across 700 ticks × 4 winds against the gate set),
  `anim_key_tracks_state_and_reset`, `tile_animator_state_changes_the_frame_key`.
- Order pins updated: `WORLD_PHASES` gains `animate_tiles` after
  `waterfalls`; the paused-frame and stepper-blocked traces include it
  (pre-gate cluster).
- **Remaining deviation:** the minecart track's `GetFinalLight` pre-pass
