## Torch flames (TILE-DRAW-2)

- `tr-core/src/flame.rs` ports `TileDrawing.GetTileFlameData` (`TileDrawing.cs:1847-2677`)
  and both inline tables of `DrawSingleTile_Flames` (`:2826-3462`); the two C# tables
  disagree in a few places (colour of styles 13/14, discarded offsets for sheet 7) and
  are ported literally, kept separate on purpose.
- The 48-bit LCG behind `Utils.RandomInt` is ported (`tile_frame_seed_for`); C# seeds
  `Main.TileFrameSeed` from `Guid.NewGuid().GetHashCode()` (`Main.cs:66567`) вЂ”
  unobservable randomness. The port starts from a fixed 32-bit constant with the same
  advance schedule (`Main.cs:61716-61721`), so flame jitter is deterministic across
  runs while distribution-identical.
- Not ported: type 85's graveyard flames (`:2724-2750`, needs
  `Main.GraveyardVisualIntensity`/`ZoneGraveyard`, not simulated); the separate
  `Main.tileGlowMask` table (`Main.cs:10024+`, consumed in `DrawSingleTile` at
  `TileDrawing.cs:1178`) is its own wide task.
- **Premultiplied alpha fix (tr-render):** the XNB textures are premultiplied by the
  XNA content pipeline (verified: a=0 texels are rgb=0, semi-alpha texels satisfy
  rgb <= a across Flames/Moon assets). Vanilla `BlendState.AlphaBlend` therefore uses
  factors (One, OneMinusSrcAlpha): a tint with alpha 0 (the tile flames'
  `Color(200,200,200,0)`) is a pure rgb add. The renderer's previous
  (SrcAlpha, OneMinusSrcAlpha) standard blend double-dimmed every semi-alpha texel and
  made a=0 tints invisible; the pipeline now uses XNA's factors and the shader no
  longer multiplies rgb by alpha. Binary-alpha tiles are unchanged; semi-alpha texels
  (panel fades, font edges) render brighter вЂ” the XNA-correct result.
- XNA nuance kept: `TileBatch` blends premultiplied, but the renderer's single
  alpha-blend pipeline cannot express rgb-add at a=0 for partial-alpha tints (the
  furniture/jar colours with a > 0 dim slightly against vanilla's full add). Fully
  a=0 tints (torches) are exact.

## Animations (M2-ANIM-foundation)

The shared primitives live in `crates/tr-core/src/anim.rs` (`FrameCounter` вЂ”
the `frameCounter += speed; while (>= threshold)` idiom of
`Player.cs:36259-36264` and `NPC.FindFrame`, `wrap_row_band`, the useStyle-1
thirds, the UI sine pulse). Deviations and ports:

- **Player draw origin** (`render/player_layers.rs` `gfx_off_y` state field):
  the 40x56 frame rides the
  20x42 hitbox at `(x - 10, y - 10 + gfxOffY)` вЂ” the resolution of
  `PlayerDrawLayers.cs:1150-1153` plus the `LegacyPlayerRenderer.cs:457,468`
  `position + (0, gfxOffY)` call. `gfxOffY` was previously ignored (the step
  ease popped vertically) and is now also part of the G6 player render key.
- **Composite arm cells** follow `PlayerDrawSet.CreateCompositeData`
  (`PlayerDrawSet.cs:1962-2023`): front arm `(X, Y)` per bodyFrame row, back
  arm the same column two rows down. The old front-arm cell hardcoded column
  8 (the composite *back*-arm use column), which mismatched the pose while
  walking and during useStyle-1 swings.
- **Item swing** (`Player.cs:50686-50852` + `PlayerDrawLayers.cs:3043-3215`,
  implemented inside the `render/player_layers.rs` builders that M2-DRAW-1
  introduced вЂ” `held_item_layers` consumes the vanilla `itemRotation` /
  `itemLocation` and the real atlas frame size):
  `itemRotation = (itemAnimation/itemAnimationMax - 0.5) * (-direction) * 3.5
  - direction * 0.3`, `itemLocation` thirds over the held frame's size, pivot
  at the drawn sprite's bottom-left. `SWING_TIME` (0.28 s) still stands in for
  the per-item `useAnimation` вЂ” the real timings remain the M2-ANIM-item-timings
  catalog row. The `UsesBetterMeleeItemLocation` nudge is not applied (no
  ported item belongs to that set).
- **NPC.FindFrame** for the four ported kinds now runs in the fixed 60 Hz sim
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs` state, `npc.rs::find_frame`): slime `NPC.cs:70801-70826`
  (2 frames, counter doubles while moving), King Slime `:73380-73414`
  (grounded 0..=3 with the landing squash 4 shown until the first advance;
  airborne 4 then 5), demon eye `:73994-74057` (2 frames + `rotation =
  atan2(vy, vx)`, `+ 3.14f` when moving left, frozen while `velocity.X == 0`),
  zombie `:76324-76389` (walk band 0,1,2,1 at 8/16/24/32 accumulated px;
  lurch frame 2 while airborne or backpedalling). The old wall-clock
  `anim * N` frame derivation is gone; `render_key` now hashes the rendered
  frame and the eye rotation instead of raw `anim` bits, so the G6 cache
  invalidates exactly when the baked pixels change.
- `aiAction == 4` (attacking) never fires for these kinds вЂ” the third counter
  tick of the slime/King Slime cases stays out until combat AI lands.
- The demon-eye draw rotates the quad about its centre (`Main.DrawNPC`
  origin = frame centre); the mirrored quad's corners are centre-symmetric,
  so the flip does not move them.

## Item use timings (M2-ANIM-item-timings)

The per-item `useTime` / `useAnimation` / `useStyle` / `holdStyle` /
`autoReuse` now live on `registry::ItemDef`, extracted from
`Item.cs SetDefaults1` for all 20 ported kinds (blocks and ores 10/15,
grass seeds 7/15, shuriken 15/15 with `autoReuse` off, coins with
`noMelee`-style zero damage, torch `holdStyle = 1`). Deviations and notes:

- The swing duration is `useAnimation` ticks at the 60 Hz rate
  (`Player.ApplyItemAnimation`, `Player.cs:4449-4451`); the fixed `SWING_TIME`
  stand-in is gone and the render builders consume the remaining *fraction*
  (`itemAnimation / itemAnimationMax`).
- The cadence follows `ItemCheck`: an `autoReuse` kind re-fires while the
  button is held; a non-autoReuse kind waits for a release
  (`Player.cs:42733`, `42819-42822`) вЂ” the shuriken throw is press-edge gated,
  and the release edges refresh every frame like `Player.releaseUseItem`.
  Placement (the RMB path) fires whenever `itemTime` hits zero inside a
  running swing (`Player.cs:39743` + `ApplyItemTime = useTime`,
  `Player.cs:4416-4418`) вЂ” dirt every 10 ticks inside the 15-tick swing,
  walls every 7; the legacy `place_cooldown = 0.12` retired. The LMB mining
  path keeps the port's own `mine_timer`/hardness model paced by the swing
  (`M3-TOOL` owns pick power), a documented deviation.
- A resting `holdStyle == 1` item (the torch) is drawn in the hand вЂ”
  anchor `position.X + width/2 + (frame.W/2 + 2)В·direction`,
  `position.Y + 24`, `itemRotation = 0` (`Player.cs:50275-50460`) вЂ” and pins
  the body to row 3 (`Player.cs:36455-36459`).
- The M2-DRAW-2 `swing_stand_in` (rotated composite front arm during a swing)
  retired for useStyle 1: the original never calls `SetCompositeArmFront` in
  the useStyle-1 branch (`Player.cs:50686-50953` sets only
  `itemRotation`/`itemLocation`), so the arm pose rides the bodyFrame thirds
  and the item swings alone. The stand-in returns for styles 5/9/11 with the
  bow/thrown tasks.
- XNA pivot semantics (`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:3161`): the draw origin
  `(W/2 - W/2В·direction, H)` positions the quad; the `direction < 0` flip
  swaps the UVs inside the quad, not the quad geometry (MonoGame
  `SpriteBatch.DrawInternal`). This also fixed the held-item mirror that
  main's `origin_drawn = width - origin` adjustment got backwards.
- The `itemLocation` thirds run on the DECREASING `itemAnimation`: the
  C# chain's first branch (`itemAnimation < max * 0.333`,
  `Player.cs:50709-50734`, Y+24 / X+10) is the swing END and the last
  (`:50776-50843`, X subtracted) the start вЂ” the port had them swapped since
  the M2-ANIM-foundation pass; corrected here (pre-existing, byte-identical
  visually at rest).
- The shuriken damage now matches `Item.cs:1876` (10, was 15) вЂ” a registry
  data fix spotted during the review; the remaining pre-existing registry
  mismatches (coins' damage/noMelee, Wood's `createTile`) stay with the
  item-data catalog work.

## Tile objects (M1.4-TO)

`tr-core/src/tileobject.rs` ports the `TileObjectData` registry as flat const
data (approach A вЂ” a full-registry generator is the follow-up) and
`tr-core/src/edit.rs` the logic on top of it: `TileObject.CanPlace`/`Place`
(`TileObject.cs:174-853` / `:29-172`), the KillTile destruction cascade through
the six per-type `Check*` routines (`CheckDoorClosed` `WorldGen.cs:86432`,
`CheckDoorOpen` `:86339`, `Check3x2` `:49187`, `Check1x2` `:43335`, `Check2x1`
`:46973`, `CheckChest` `:57923`; the origin reconstruction is generalized
through the registry: `dx = frameX/18 % width`, `dy = frameY/18 % height`, the
open-door hinge via the C# `frameX % 72` switch), and `WorldGen.OpenDoor`/
`CloseDoor` (`:37630-37784` / `:31805-31907`) behind `interact_at` вЂ” the
port's first world-tile interaction hook, embedded in the fixed-step editing
pass at the vanilla `Update` order point (interactions `Player.cs:27430` в†’
`ItemCheck` `:31827`). The registry slice is the wooden set вЂ” closed/open door
(10/11), table (14), chair (15), work bench (18), chest (21); every entry
cites its builder chain. Deviations and seams:

- The registry is a deliberate slice: sub-tiles are not ported (the table's
  styles 13/25, `TileObjectData.cs:3182-3190`) and the gemspark/glow tiles
  stay excluded (research decision вЂ” they are wall/light render work, not
  placement); adding objects is data-only until the generator lands.
- The chest is no longer a pure tile object (flipped 2026-11-07, M3-CHEST-UI):
  the item storage and the open/lock/unlock/rename interaction are ported вЂ”
  `crates/tr-app/src/chest.rs` owns the `Chest.cs` entity semantics and the
  world-chest store, `crates/tr-app/src/ui/chest.rs` the `ChestUI.cs` panel
  (see "Chest UI + world chests (M3-CHEST-UI)" below). The placement-time
  entry hooks (`Chest.FindEmptyChest`/`Chest.AfterPlacement_Hook`,
  `TileObjectData.cs:3464-3465`) stay unhooked вЂ” store entries are created
  lazily on first open instead (empty-entry-equivalent; that section).
- Net placement replication (`apply_edit` kind 1, `world_sim/editing.rs:548`)
  sends style 0 / dir 1: the generic replication path carries no
  style/alternate/direction (vanilla's `NetMessage.SendObjectPlacement`
  does), so a left-facing chair replicates mirrored.
- `CloseDoor`'s `genRand.Next(3)` closed-frame variant is pinned to 0
  (`edit.rs`, `close_door`): the port has no runtime RNG stream to draw from
  and the determinism invariant forbids introducing one; the two skipped
  variants are a closed-frame cosmetic only.
- The interaction hook consumes the click with no same-time fall-through to
  placement вЂ” the research contract is stronger than vanilla's nuance where a
  refused door toggle and a placement can land in one `Update`.
- Door sounds are wired (Door_Opened/Door_Closed cues); the door net message
  (vanilla 19) is NOT wired вЂ” there is no `apply_edit` kind for a toggle yet;
  multiplayer seam.
- The left-facing open door's frames come from the generic `TileObject.Place`
  math (style-row shift в†’ frameY 54) while vanilla's hand-written `OpenDoor`
  uses a different hardcoded left-leaf layout (frameX +36,
  `WorldGen.cs:37695-37698`); both are ported as-is вЂ” a vanilla quirk, not a
  port bug.
- The wooden recipes expand the `RecipeGroups.Wood`/`IronBar` requirement
  groups to concrete ids (Wood в†’ 9, Iron Bar в†’ 22; `Recipe.cs:610-616` /
  `:4738`) вЂ” the subset recipe table carries no group machinery (`craft.rs`).
- LMB breaking of `frame_important` tiles was gated off in
  `world_sim/editing.rs` (the former `:204-210`/`:213` as of the M1.4-TO-5
  claim вЂ” `!important`, cacti exempted; the earlier `:158-165` citation had
  drifted after the M2 merges). Removed 2026-11-04 (M1.4-TO-5): vanilla's
  mining chain has no `tileFrameImportant` check at all (grep over
  `Player.cs` hits only `:40019`/`:40608`, both outside the mining chain вЂ”
  `Player.cs:45656` в†’ `PickTile :53757`), so doors/chests/furniture reach
  `break_tile` through the mining branch with the full KillTile cascade and
  the object drop. Cactus 80 keeps its old path (`check_object`
  `_ => None`, the per-cell drop); the visible remainder is the missing
  `CanKillTile` refusals (next bullet, M1.4-TO-6).
- `CanKillTile` refusals landed 2026-11-06 (M1.4-TO-6): C# `CanKillTile`
  (`WorldGen.cs:62219-62326`) refuses a locked door type 10 (`:62290-62295` вЂ”
  the already-ported `IsLockedDoor` frames, `:69191-69197`), a chest 21/467/88
  holding items (`:62311-62323` вЂ” the app's chest store answers
  `CanDestroyChest`, `Chest.cs:609-623`; the store is populated since
  M3-CHEST-UI, so a stocked chest refuses its break for real) and the tile
  under a container {21,26,72,77,88,467,488}
  (`:62259-62270`); `edit::can_kill_tile` (`edit.rs:1798`) ports the three
  and gates the mining tick (`damage = 0`, `Player.cs:53830-53833`),
  `break_tile`, the replicated break (`apply_edit` kind 0) and the bomb
  explosions. Deviations: the C# `out bool blockDamaged` flavour collapses
  into one bool (the 2-arg overload discards it, `:62213-62217`); the same
  C# function's tree-trunk/palm/cactus anchors (`:62247-62257`,
  `:62271-62281`), the boulder scan (`:62283-62287`) and the teleporter 235
  (`:62297-62310`) stay unported; `kill_tile`'s body and the cascade's
  re-entries are not re-checked (the C# `KillTile` entry duplicates the
  refusals through `CheckTileBreakability` `:62377-62461` вЂ” the port chokes
  the outer break sources instead, one query shared by all of them); the
  per-tick `KillTile(fail: true)` sound/dust of a refused pick
  (`Player.cs:53822-53831`) has no ported path, so the refusal is silent;
  explosion/replication pass `|_, _| false` for the chest store вЂ” the
  M3-CHEST-UI task left this unchanged (the M1.4-TO-6 deviation stands; the
  store is populated now, so the widening is observable and is the PHYS-7
  follow-up).
- The mining break carries no net messages: vanilla syncs the break/fail
  with `SendData` 17/34/125 (`Player.cs:45685-45696`, `:53774-53819`); the
  SP port has no replication for it (the same seam as the door message 19
  above).
- Placement does not run the KillTile cascade: `reframe_area` (and
  `frame_world`) leave `frame_important` tiles alone, so a floating object at
  placement does not pop although vanilla's `PlaceTile` в†’ `SquareTileFrame`
  would kill it; it resolves at the next neighbouring break.
- The object route bypasses the app's legacy single-tile pre-checks
  (neighbour/overlap) вЂ” `TileObject.CanPlace` owns the verdict;
  `BlockPlacementIfOverPlayers` (`Player.cs:41427`) is not ported for the
  wooden set.

## Tile-placement validity/adjacency (S1-P-i32)

Code-only census round (2026-11-20, `task/S1-P-i32-tile-placement`, no
compiler/test run — witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN). The placement machinery
(`Player.PlaceThing_Tiles` → `TileObject.CanPlace`/`Place` for the registry
route, `WorldGen.PlaceTile` for the legacy route) was already largely faithful;
the census isolated four WRONGs in the tile-validity/adjacency layer and fixed
them verbatim, each with its C# cite:

1. **Adjacency predicate** (`world_sim/editing.rs::can_place`). The default arm
   of `BlockPlacementForAssortedThings` (`Player.cs:41247-41261`) accepts a
   cardinal neighbour that is active and (`tileSolid` **OR `TileID.Sets.IsBeam`
   OR `tileRope` OR the minecart track 314**) or carries any wall; failing all
   four, the target cell's **own wall > 0** still accepts (`:41257-41260`). The
   pre-fix port read only `tileSolid` neighbours and never the target's wall, so
   a block could not be placed against a rope/beam/track or onto a walled empty
   cell. Both now read 1:1 (`td::SET_IS_BEAM`/`td::TILE_ROPE` are the generated
   tables).
2. **Platform fallback** (`can_place` tail). `Player.cs:41332-41345`: when the
   default arm refuses a platform-placing item (`TileID.Sets.Platforms`), ANY
   active tile in the 3×3 around the target accepts — diagonals included. The
   pre-fix port had no fallback. Added, gated on the held item's `createTile`.
3. **`Collision.EmptyTile` overlap** (`can_place` head). `Collision.cs:1359-1381`
   blocks **players AND NPCs**; `WorldGen.PlaceTile` consults it only for SOLID
   placements (`WorldGen.cs:59373`: `forced || EmptyTile || !tileSolid[num] || …`).
   The pre-fix port blocked only the player and blocked EVERY kind (a torch could
   not stand inside the player). Now the overlap reads each NPC's `size()` box and
   is gated on the held tile's solidity — a non-solid tile bypasses it, exactly as
   vanilla. The C# `!dead && !ghost` player filters fold to the port's live-player
   check (no hardcore ghosts / PVP deaths).
4. **Lava gate** (`use_tile_item` + `tileobject.rs`). `PlaceThing_Tiles`' OR chain
   (`Player.cs:39743`) refuses an inactive lava target unless the block is
   replaceable or the item is a grass/moss override; `IsBlockedByLava`
   (`:41489-41504`) refuses a solid `createTile` outright, else answers
   `TileObjectData.CheckLiquidPlacement` (`TileObjectData.cs:5039-5042` →
   the def's `LiquidPlace` or the global `LiquidPlace` `:5044-5071`, which reads
   `tileLavaDeath`/`tileWaterDeath`). The pre-fix port had NO lava gate. Added
   `is_blocked_by_lava`, `check_liquid_placement`, `is_replaceable_block`
   (`Player.cs:39753-39760`) and the `TILE_WATER_DEATH` literal table (10 ids,
   `Main.cs:8061-8067`/`:8309`/`:9504`/`:9508` — a literal extraction like
   `torch.rs::NO_ATTACH`, since GenTileData emits `TileID.Sets` only).
5. **Platform case-19 frame** (`edit/place.rs::place_platform`). `WorldGen.PlaceTile`
   case 19 (`WorldGen.cs:60221-60225`) writes `frameY = 18*style`, type 19, and
   `Main.tileFrameImportant[19]` is a boot static (`Main.cs:7654`). The pre-fix
   port fell through to the generic single-tile write (frames `-1/-1`, no
   frame-important mirror), so the re-frame drew the platform as a plain merged
   block. Added the case-19 arm mirroring the existing `place_planter_box`
   (case 380) pattern; tile 19 is registered but `CustomPlace`-false, so it keeps
   the legacy route.

RNG order: unchanged. None of the five fixes draws from any stream — they are
pure predicates/frame writes. The placement sound's `Main.rand.Next(3)` +

## Slime variants and the demon-eye family (M4-NPC-1-slimes-eyes)

- The four hand-tuned NPC stats moved to the `SetDefaults` values: blue slime

  demon eye 30x32 / 60 / 18 / defense 2 / knockBackResist 0.8 (case 2; was

  frames (`Main.cs:67082`) and 300/40/20; it is hardmode-gated in the night
  spawn roll (`NPC.cs:4555-4558`), so the pre-hardmode ambient pass never
  spawns it вЂ” the kind exists for the future M5-HARDFORCE.
- The slime variants are the negative net ids (`Lang.cs:520-533` names,
  `NPC.SetDefaultsFromNetId` stats): green -3, pinky -4, baby -5, black -6,
  purple -7, red -8, yellow -9. The hitbox rides the per-variant size scale,
  the sprite is the 32x26 frame scaled and anchored at the frame centre over
  the hitbox centre (`Main.DrawNPC`'s `origin = frame.Size() / 2`), tinted by
  the per-variant `NPC.color` through the premultiplied pipeline (the alpha
  channel renders the vanilla translucency).
- The ambient selection ports `Spawner.GetBasicSlimeToSpawn`
  (`NPC.cs:5625-5654`): underground 1/5 yellow, else 1/2 blue / red; forest
  surface 1/3 green (or within 200 tiles of spawn), 1/10 purple beyond 400
  tiles, else blue; then `Spawner.SpawnNPC`'s `RollLuck(180)` swap of any blue
  slime for Pinky (`NPC.cs:5238-5246`; the port rolls it un-lucked). Jungle
  tile 60 (-10) and snow 147/161 stay out until those biomes exist; black and
  baby slimes have no ambient roll in the forest branch.
- The loot follows `ItemDropDatabase.cs:1074-1082`: standard slimes (blue
  family) always drop 1-2 Gel, red/purple/black 2-5, green/baby/pinky none
  (Pinky drops 25-50 Pink Gel instead, `:1072`). Gel (23) and Pink Gel (3111)
  are registered as materials (empty `SetDefaults` cases -> `ResetStats`
  defaults: no use timings).
- The death check keeps the vanilla semantics: `life` is not clamped, death
  is `life <= 0` (`NPC.checkDead`).
- The coin drops keep the port's pre-existing denominations (the `value`
  copper amounts are a separate M4-LOOT row).

  `ItemDropResolver.ResolveRule`/`TryDropping`/`ResolveRuleChains`
  (`ItemDropResolver.cs:14-62`), `ItemDropDatabase`

  `DropLocalPerClientAndResetsNPCMoneyTo0` (the `npc.value = 0` side effect

## The Martian Drone (M4-EVENT-4c)

The type-4 sky mob (`NPC.cs:13935-13953`): 40Г—30, dmg 60, def 16, 300
HP, kb 0.4, npcSlots 1.5, noTileCollide + noGravity.
`AI()`'s aiStyle-74 block (`:35218-35500`, the 388 parameter set):
`ai[0] == 0` hovers вЂ” the approach vector points 200 px above the player
at speed 10, damped into the velocity over 30 ticks, gated by the
line-of-sight + the В±ПЂ/8 angle cone (the cone only opens downward вЂ” the
drone dives under the players it cannot see, with the 120-tick argue
override); `ai[0] == 1` charges 30 ticks (the Г—0.95 damp, then the
В±50Г—0.04 jittered vector Г—14); `ai[0] == 2` dashes (the 20-lerp toward
the player, the exit at velocity < 7 or the 100-px-past + 30-tick
window, the solid-collision fold to the explosion); and within 64 px of
the player the machine folds to `ai[0] == 3` вЂ” the 192Г—192 box, the 80
damage, the 3-tick fuse. The loot db registers no 388 rules, so the
explosion drops nothing.

`item_rng` and placed the NPC at the fixed `(px в€’ 600, py в€’ 400)` offset

### The EoC task's loss and re-land (M4-NPC-3n)

The smart-cursor agent's `5075a462` "sync" merge resolved its conflicts by
taking its own branch's wholesale tree, which predated `07c1d4e4` вЂ” main
lost the entire M4-NPC-3m task (the case-4 `find_frame`, the 110x166
frames, the `halfSize` override, the `eoc` hook name and the ROADMAP
row). The AGENTS.md hazard ("another agent's merge reverts a finished
feature вЂ” verify your markers after every merge") caught it in the audit
log (`git show origin/main:... | grep -c`), and the work was cherry-picked
back on this branch. The lesson joins the 2026-11-08 incidents list: a
"sync" merge whose message says it restores dropped work is exactly where
someone else's finished work gets dropped again.

## The draw-anchor overrides (M4-NPC-3n)

`Main.cs:23048`'s switch overrides the per-kind draw anchor in two ways,
and the port now models both:

- `halfSize` (the origin point that lands on the anchor) shifts the frame
  by `override в€’ frame_h / 2`: the EoC/Twins' (55, 107) gives +24/+7, and
  the Plantera head's absolute 77 (over its 86-px row's 43) gives +34.
- `num47`/`num46` are flat pixel nudges: the Plantera head's +26, the
  Brain's `+50 В· scale`, the DD2 group's negative shifts (the
  javelineers' в€’8, the bombers' в€’5, the Wither Beasts' в€’3).

`npc_anchor_nudge` sums them and is applied once after the draw match, so
every generic-anchored kind takes its own value; the towers, the saucer
family and the Deerclops compute their own positions in dedicated
`DrawNPCDirect` arms and are excluded, exactly like the C#. The still
unported arms (626/627's wet dual switch, 692's `num46 = wet ? 10 : 6`,
688/694's direction terms, 469's ai[2]-gated +14, and the DD2 sprite
effects/flip toggles) are the follow-ups.

### W1-5 fix (fix/verifier-w1-golem-plantera, 2026-11-19, code-only)

TR-VERIFY-W1 W1-5 (LOW): the phase-1 sight gate read the POST-integration
position. The C#'s `Collision.CanHit(base.position, …)` (`NPC.cs:31918`)
runs inside AI(), BEFORE `NPC.Update`'s movement integration — the
aim/muzzle (`:31926-31965`) already used the captured pre-move centre,
only the sight gate was off by one tick of motion (≤15 px enraged).
Fixed with the smaller change the fix spec names: capture `(x0, y0)`
before the mid-step integration and feed those to `can_hit` (moving the
integration to the end would force every early `return` to integrate
too). The same-tick spawn requests (spore/hooks/tentacles) are drained
by the sim without a position payload today (kinds 263/264/265 unported,
`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s drain) — when the minion wiring lands it must read
the PRE-move centre (the C# spawns at `base.Center` inside AI()); noted
here as the wiring obligation. Witness:
`npc_ai_plantera.rs::w1_5_the_sight_gate_reads_the_pre_move_position`
(a wall column the tick's motion crosses: pre-move blocked → no seed,
the wall-free control fires). **No compiler invoked** — WRITTEN NOT RUN.

The Martian Madness family's 16 kinds had a `find_frame` arm each and a
draw arm each, but both were the v1's blind `(frame + 1) % count` strip
and a box-sized quad at the hitbox corner. Against the C#:

  (`ai[2] / 12 % 2` вЂ” the work animation), and its walk wraps at 9, not at
  the sheet's 11 rows.

  2) and its slow walk (`|vx| < 0.2`) parks on the idle row only when an

  `spriteDirection = -direction` (`NPC.cs:71746-71753`/`:71795`): the

  when it holds 0). The port folded `direction` into `facing`, so the
  martian kinds now carry the separate `Npc.sprite_dir` field
  (`NPC.cs:6515`'s default -1) that the draws flip on
  (`Main.cs:23124-23128`: `spriteDirection == 1` is the flip) вЂ” without it
  the Scutlix family drew mirrored.
- **The saucer family's rows ride the core's `ai[3]` clock**, which the
  mounts mirror (`:35832`/`:35860`/`:35906`): the core's
  `frameCounter % 66 / 6` (11 rows) double-increments and pins to
  [36, 54) during the [20, 260) attack window (rows 6-8); the shell's

## The Old One's Army's kill worth (S1-E-12)

`tr_core::dd2::monster_points_worth` is `DD2Event.GetMonsterPointsWorth`
(`DD2Event.cs:546-554`) over the three tier bodies (`:1106-1130`,
`:1199-1223`, `:1509-1528`): a kill outside the two family id ranges
(`(uint)(id-551) <= 14` / `(uint)(id-568) <= 10`) scores 0 вЂ” note the
skeletons 566/567 sit between the ranges and score nothing, exactly as
the C#'s casts do. Tier 1's wave 5 freezes the ordinary kills at
`waveKills >= 139` (only the Dark Mages 564/565 score, latching
`_downedDarkMageT1`), tier 2's wave 7 does the same at 219 (only the
Ogres 576/577, `_downedOgreT2`), and tier 3's wave 7 scores Betsy (551)
alone. The latches live in `World::dd2_latches`, reset by
`use_etherian_crystal` (`StartInvasion`'s `:268-275`), and lift their
wave's kill cap in `required_wave_kills`/`required_wave_kills_t2`
(`:993`, `:1181`).

Deliberate reductions: `Main.expertMode` is constants-off (the world
carries no game mode вЂ” the same reduction as `spawner.rs`'s town block
and the nurse's heal cost), so the band's `!expertMode ? 1 : 2`
collapses to 1 and the `waveKills == 138` / `== 218` anti-overshoot rows
(`:1119`, `:1212`) return the same 1 that the classic arm already does.
The latches are not saved: `DD2Event.Save` (`:151-156`) writes only the
three tier flags, so a reload mid-wave starts a fresh invasion's latch
state, as the C#'s statics do.

## The Old One's Army's loss path (S1-E-12a)

**Code-only mode** (user directive, 2026-11-18): this round ran no
cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests вЂ” the 5 core `loss_tests` + 6 sim
`dd2_loss_tests` are written, NOT run; every citation was re-verified by
reading the decompiled source. The victory half is the sibling branch
`dd2_victory.rs` (0ffce2ee) вЂ” untouched here.

The chain, in the C#'s order: the crystal's `checkDead` intercept
(`NPC.cs:78087-78095`: `type == 548 && ai[1] != 1` в†’ `ai[1] = 1`,
`ai[0] = 0`, `life = lifeMax`, no death) в†’ the scene's first-tick arm
(`:40868-40885`: every active portal 549 flips to its fade, then
`DD2Event.ReportLoss`) в†’ `ReportLoss` (`DD2Event.cs:507-515`:
`LostThisRun = true` + the 30-tick spawn hold) в†’ `UpdateTime`'s hold
zero-crossing (`:219-236`) broadcasts `LoseInvasionMessage`
(`:344-347`) in `INFO_FAILURE_INVASION_COLOR` (255,0,0, `:1812`) в†’ the
aiStyle-105 loss arm (`NPC.cs:40862-40967`: the 96-tick rise
`vy = Lerp(0,-1,ai[0]/96)`, the `alpha += 50` fade capped 255, the
600-tick end) в†’ `StopInvasion(win: false)` (`:293-312`: the counters
clear) в†’ `WipeEntities` (`:629-692`): the `IsADD2Turret`
(`ProjectileID.cs:526`, 12 ids) tower kills, the
`BelongsToInvasionOldOnesArmy` (`NPCID.cs:10432`, 30 ids вЂ” the
bartender 550 is OUT) hostile removal via direct `active = false`
(no death chain: no loot, no kill credit, no death sound), and the
open chests' 3822 stacks `TurnToAir`. `CheckProgress`'s `LostThisRun`
refusal (`:364`) gates `dd2_report_kill` for the whole scene.
`StartInvasion`'s reset (`:268-275`), the `LostThisRun` clear (`:271`),
the 300-tick hold (`:288`) and the wipe (`:289`) land in
`use_etherian_crystal` BEFORE the crystal's `NewNPC`, so the wipe
cannot eat the fresh crystal.

Recorded deviations:

- **The batched intercept.** The C# flips the crystal inside
  `StrikeNPC`'s `checkDead` (the player pass); the port resolves it in
  `update_dd2_event` after the AI pass and before the death retain вЂ”
  the same batched-death architecture as the death sounds (S1-E-21c).
  The scene's first-tick arm (portal marks + `ReportLoss`) rides that
  resolve instead of the next AI tick, and the hold decays on the same
  tick: the loss broadcast lands 29 ticks after the killing blow where
  the C#'s `UpdateTime`-before-players order gives 30 (the test pins
  `SPAWN_HOLD_LOSS - 1`). The scene counter starts clean (`ai[0] = 0`)
  and ticks from the next frame.
- **The shield fold.** `dontTakeDamageFromHostiles` folds into the full
  `dont_take_damage` вЂ” the mid-scene player re-kill edge is unmodelled.
- **The scene's RNG draws are unmodelled.** The dust ring
  (`:40941-40952`) spends 12+ `Main.rand.NextFloat()` draws per tick
  and `MoonlordDeathDrama.RequestLight` (`:40887-40891`) lights the
  fade; the port draws nothing and consumes nothing вЂ” the same
  dust-deviation class as the rest of the port. The ported loss path
  itself draws NO RNG, and the fixed-step order is preserved by
  construction: the intercept/broadcast/stop all ride the existing
  `update_dd2_event` slot, no new pass.
- **The scene-end crystal removal rides the retain** (no gore/death
  sound chain) вЂ” the pre-existing win-death shape (M4-EVENT-5p).
- **Single-player chest sweep.** `Chest.GetCurrentlyOpenChests` is the
  multiplayer open-chest list; the port sweeps the local player's one
  open chest (`Player.chest`).
- **The double tower clear folds to one.** `StartInvasion` clears the
  towers at `:276` and again inside `WipeEntities` (`:289`); the port
  wipes once at the `:289` point вЂ” no tower can spawn between the two
  C# calls, so the states agree.

Deferrals (the follow-up slices): the 672 defeat-scene projectile
(`:40883`, aiStyle 132's filters/sound/gore drama) and the
`CrystalDestructionVortex`/`Color` filter activation/deactivation
(`:40959-40961`, `UpdateTime` `:198-200`); the scene dust +

none alive), the Sorcerer 1/9, the Thief 1/5, the Peon 1/3, the Warrior
1/3, else the Archer. The five kinds carry their verbatim `SetDefaults`
rows (18Г—38, the aiStyle-3 walker вЂ” the Sorcerer keeps its caster arm,
the Summoner rides it in hardmode).

The kill credit (`NPC.cs:78236-78279`): the dead goblin's
`GetNPCInvasionGroup` (1) matches the active `invasionType` в†’
`invasionSize -= num9` (the Summoner's 10-point kill, the rest 1) вЂ” the
progress `ReportInvasionProgress` fields land with the UI-bar slice.

The borrow shape: the invasion spawn ride reads the world/player/roster
BEFORE the npc_step split borrows and resolves the spawn AFTER the tick
(the wholesale-app pass) вЂ” the same shape the voodoo sacrifice uses.

Deviations: the town-NPC fallback window (the `maxTilesX/2 В± 5` arm of
`ShouldSpawnInvasionEnemies`) needs the town roster scan вЂ” the follow-up;
the UI progress bar (`DrawInvasionProgress`), the invasion-delay timer's
save persistence and the waves 2-4 (the Frost Legion/Pirates/Martians)
are the follow-ups.

## The lava burn (M1.5-ITEM-lava-burn)

`CheckLavaDeath`'s non-doll arm: the drops touching lava vanish
(`TurnToAirAndSync`) unless `ItemID.Sets.IsLavaImmuneRegardlessOfRarity`
(the 18-row set вЂ” the obsidian family, the Fireblossom, the
Hellstone-bar rows вЂ” rides the port's `LAVA_IMMUNE` const) or the item's
rarity clears the `rare 0/-1` gate. The rare drops keep their loot:
the rarity gate is the whole reason the mid-game items survive the hell
pools. The voodoo arm rides the same lava read; the burn lands inside
the drops pass before the pickup (a drop in lava vanishes the same tick
it would be collected вЂ” the C# runs `CheckLavaDeath` before the pickup
chain too, `WorldItem.cs:405-425`).

## The voodoo sacrifice (M4-BOSS-6c)

The gameplay hardmode gate: the dropped Guide Voodoo Doll (267) touching
lava (`WorldItem.CheckLavaDeath`'s arm вЂ” `lavaWet` в†’ `VoodooDollLavaDeath`)
is consumed and strikes the town NPCs dead вЂ” the Guide FIRST
(`StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999)` в†’ the port kills outright; the death pass
picks the kill credit up), then the stack's remainder across the other
town NPCs (the C# `isLikeATownNPC` list walks a shuffled copy; the port
walks the spawn order). `NPC.SpawnWOF` ports the gates (the depth
`maxTilesY - 205`, one living wall), the 1200-px player-clearance scan
(the spawn x steps 16 px away from the world centre's side while a player
sits within 1200 px), the free-row search (the solid/liquid>=100 blocker,
the В±1000-step expand), the `UnderworldLayer+10..+80` row clamp and the
`Announcement.HasAwoken` broadcast (the literal stands in for the
localization key).

The borrow shape: the items pass (`update_items`) reads the tile under
each drop inside its tick closure and collects the lava-hit doll; the
sacrifice resolves AFTER the tick (the spawn/kill pass takes `app`
wholesale). The doll items never burn silently вЂ” the non-doll lava
consumption (`rare 0/-1` items without the lava-immunity set) is the
follow-up.

## The Wall of Flesh + the Hungry + the Leeches (M4-BOSS-6b)

The aiStyle-27 machine (`npc.rs::update_wof`, the classic path
verbatim over BOSS-6's v1): the off-edge kill, the underworld
draw-band scan (`UnderworldLayer = maxTilesY - 200`; the 15-tile
solid/liquid walks ease the band 1 px per tick with the 160-px clamp),
the Y pinning to the band midpoint, the slide speed by the hp
thresholds (1.5 в†’ 2.75 across the 75/50/25/10% steps вЂ” the direction
locks and never damps), the dead-player abandonment (3 s dead в†’ the
wall kills itself), the tongue phase (`ai[1]` 2700 with the hp bonuses
в†’ the 3-4 phase cycle в†’ the Leech spawns) and the Hungry init (11
minions along the band).
**Re-audited 2026-11-18 (S1-D-3 aiStyle-27 round, code-only mode): the
"verbatim" claim above is FALSE вЂ” the live arm + the sim write-through
are an approximation with a catastrophic every-tick respawn loop; see
"The Wall of Flesh aiStyle-27 re-port (S1-D-3)" below. The faithful
module `npc_ai_style27.rs` is landed UNWIRED; the live `update_wof`
keeps running until the wiring round. Corrections to the paragraph
above: the 160-px clamp was never implemented (only the ease), the
bottom walk never counted liquid, the classic ladder tops out at 3.25
(not 2.75 вЂ” no threshold produces 2.75; the cumulative sums are
1.75/2.15/2.65/3.25), and the abandonment timer rides
`ai[0]`, not the C#'s `localAI[1]`.**

A structural note: the AI arms hold `&World`, so the wall cannot write
the band вЂ” the wall's AI computes the scan targets onto its own
`wof_bottom_target`/`wof_top_target` fields and the world sim eases
`World.wof_draw_top/bottom` toward them, alongside
`wof_present`/`wof_hp_ratio`/`wof_x` (the Hungry's read set). The same
borrow shape carried the spawn requests (`wants_leech` with the
`CountNPCS(117) < 10` gate, `wants_hungry`).

**The Hungry (115)** вЂ” the aiStyle-29 verbatim: the anchor = the wall's
x + the band row at `ai[0]`, the chase toward the player clamped to the
leash (300/500/700 by the wall's hp; the dive cycle Г—1.3 after 100
ticks), the defense/damage tiers (30/60 at <50%, 20/45 at <75%) through
the new `defense_override`/`damage_override` fields (the contact path
prefers the override), the justHit recoil (the hurt cooldown stands in
for the C# flag), the wall's death deactivates the minion.
**Re-audited 2026-11-18 (S1-D-3 aiStyle-29 round): the live arm is an
approximation, not verbatim вЂ” see "The Hungry aiStyle-29 re-port
(S1-D-3)" below; the faithful module `npc_ai_style29.rs` is landed
UNWIRED, the live `update_hungry` keeps running until the wiring round.**

**The Leeches (117/118)** вЂ” the aiStyle-6 worm family: the head rides
the worm engine's chain assembly (the `Next(3, 6)` budget, the AI_006
default tunables, the 14×14/60 HP segments).
**Correction (W-A2-1): the budget is TWO draws — the discarded
`Next(8, 13)` (`NPC.cs:51310`) runs first for every listed head, then
the `Next(3, 6)` override (`:51341`); the crumble `Next(100)` also runs
for the Leech even though the type-117 guard blocks the effect
(`:51590`). Both ledgers are pinned in `worm_tests`.**

Deviations: the eye/mouth mirrors (114, the 100Г—100 8000-HP wall parts)
are the render-machinery follow-up (the vanilla draws them inside the
wall's band); the expert burst block (the hp-scaled spawn odds) and the
`getGoodWorld` spawn are out; the roar timer (`localAI[3]`'s sound 4)
is cosmetic and skipped. The bestiary `card_at` now matches the draw's
centred lattice вЂ” the stale top-left guard dropped cards once the
roster's rows overflowed the panel.
**Correction (S1-D-3 aiStyle-27 round): the roar timer is NOT
cosmetic-only вЂ” it draws `Main.rand.Next(1000)` every tick and
`Next(200)` on each roar (`NPC.cs:25717`/`:25719`), so skipping it
desynchronises the shared RNG stream for every later consumer. The
faithful module keeps both draws.**

### The Hungry aiStyle-29 re-port (S1-D-3, code-only mode)

The 2026-11-18 aiStyle-29 round re-read the whole arm (`NPC.cs:26209-26404`)

in the section above). The arm IS ported, but approximately вЂ” the escape

  (`:26280`, INTEGER half-width); the live arm uses `World.wof_x` alone

  arm's `damage_override = None` at full hp happens to match, but the
  tier write skips `GetAttackDamage_ScaledByDifficulty` (`:26253`,
  `NPC.cs:7036-7039` вЂ” the classic `EnemyDamageMultiplier.Sample(1)` is
  exactly 1: the curve's Journey 0.5в†’0.5 / Master 3в†’3 keys,

  and restores `defDefense` only in the expert block (`:26257`). A Hungry
  that drops from <75% back to full hp keeps def 20 in the C#.
* **f32-ratio vs f64-int ladder** вЂ” the live arm reads the sim's
  precomputed `World.wof_hp_ratio` (f32); the C# compares
  `(double)life < (double)lifeMax * k` (`:26225`/`:26238`) вЂ” boundary

  uses `center()`'s float halves. Identical for the even 30Г—30/20Г—42

  onto the World IN-LOOP right after the wall's update — later slots in

  `Main.wofDrawArea*`/`Main.npc[wofNPCIndex]` reads. The presence mirror
  arms per living wall (the `OnSpawn` type-113 shape, `NPC.cs:8404-8407`)
  and clears on the death tick (`ResetNPCSlotData`, `:8379-8381`).
* **justHit** — `Npc.just_hit` is the strike tick: the three hurt paths
  arm it (`NPC.cs:81274`), the update tail clears it (`:90516`). The
  Hungry's recoil (`ai[1] = 10`, `:26211-26214`) now fires for ONE tick
  per strike, not the whole `hurt_cd` cooldown the v1 stood in with.
* **Deviations (documented)** — `Start` (the C#'s `GetAvailableNPCSlot`
  search seed, `NPC.cs:80796`) is not carried: the port's compacting
  pool appends (the established spawn convention, the Prime-limb/Skeletron
  precedent). `NewNPC`'s direction default is `Entity.direction = 1`
  (`Entity.cs:20`); the children spawn facing 1 with the ctor's
  `spriteDirection = -1` (`NPC.cs:6515`). The getGood demon (type 24)
  has no port kind — getGoodWorld is false so the arm never emits it.
  The `EverLastingTicker` stamp stays 0 (the `update_zombie` stand-in).
  The noTileCollide integration (`NPC.cs:90495-90498`) rides the family
  wrappers (the modules leave the step to the caller).

## The Eye of Cthulhu (M4-BOSS-1)

The first boss lands through the aiStyle-4 block's classic path
(`npc.rs::update_eye_of_cthulhu`; the 841-line C# `if (this.aiStyle == 4)`
in `AI()`). The machine state rides the new `Npc.ai[0..4]` (the phase /
the sub-state / the timer / the dash-servant counter):

- **Phase 0** вЂ” the hover at 200 px above the player (5 speed, 0.04
  accel); `ai[2]` counts to 600 unconditionally and flips into the 3Г—
  dash chain (`ai[1] = 1в†’2` at 6 speed, 150-tick flights, the 0.98 damp
  after 40 ticks); while the eye is above + within 500 px the servant
  counter `ai[3]` reaches 110 and requests the servant spawn (10 px out
  along the aim, the launch velocity inherited вЂ” the
  `wants_servant` в†’ the world-sim resolve).
- **Phases 1/2** вЂ” the spins: the rotation ramps `ai[2]` 0.005в†’0.5
  rad/tick while `ai[1]` counts to 100, then the phase increments (the
  getGood expert servant bursts + `reflectsProjectiles` are out).
- **Phase 3** вЂ” the final: `defense_override = 0` (the new `Npc` field
  the damage path reads), the faster machine (6.8 dashes, 130-tick
  chains).

Deviations: the expert rage arms (`flag2/flag3` at 12%/4% hp, the
`ai[1] = 3/4/5` spread-dash sub-states, the Г—1.5 turn rate) are out with
the port's missing difficulty flags (the skips carry the C# cites);
`EncourageDespawn(10)`'s off-screen counter becomes the distance cull
(the dawn climb `velocity.Y -= 0.04` + the sim's removal above the
player); `SpawnOnPlayer`'s tile scan simplifies to the clamped
600-px-above position (the boss flies to the target from wherever it
appears); `WorldGen.spawnEye` (the natural night spawn) is not modeled вЂ”
the Suspicious Looking Eye (43) is the only summon path.

The summon rides the new boss-spawner arm
(`editing.rs::use_suspicious_looking_eye` вЂ” the night gate, the
`SummonItemCheck` aliveness refusal, the roar cue `("Roar_0", 15)` =
`SoundID.Roar` 15, the consumption + the swing timers) вЂ” hoisted before
the editing fn's `player` borrow (the arm takes `app` wholesale). The
kill sets `World.downed_boss1`, fed into the loot flags (the `Cond::`
gates read it); the boss bar and the `MusicID.Boss1` (5) music extend
the King Slime hooks (the 93-then-5 ladder order kept).

## The full drop database (M4-LOOT-2)

`tools/gen_loot.py` reads the decompiled
`GameContent/ItemDropRules/ItemDropDatabase.cs` `Populate()` and emits
`crates/tr-app/src/loot_db_gen.rs` - `loot_db::database()`, **1421
net-id registrations over the 643 C# register sites** in the C# order.
The C# `RegisterToNPC(type)` expands to the type itself + the negative
net-id family (`PrepareNPCNetIDsByTypeDictionary` over `NPCID.NetIdMap`
- e.g. the type-1 slime family = `-3..-10`); the removal wrappers
(`RemoveFromMultipleNPCs(RegisterToMultipleNPCs(...), ids)`) compute the
net id set minus the removals, keeping the tough-slime gel split. The
negative-id dedupe mirrors `TrimDuplicateRulesForNegativeIDs`.

The engine grew the pieces the registrations need:

- **`LootFlags` + `LootNpc`** - the world/event snapshot the conditions
  read (the downed bosses 1/2/3/any/plantera/plant-boss, the seasons,
  the special seeds, `NPC.waveNumber` + the pumpkin/frost moon formulas
  verbatim, the closest player's zones, the pirate-map/soul depth bands,
  the npc's `value`/`lifeMax`/`damage`/`defense`/`boss`/
  `SpawnedFromStatue`); `spawn_loot` fills it from
  `World.hard_mode`/`day_time` + the scene zones + the dying npc.
- **`Cond`** - the data-driven enum porting ~50 `Conditions.*` gates;
  the yoyo gates and the moon trophy tables carry their exact formulas.
- **`LeadingConditionRule`** (`LeadingConditionRule.cs`: the condition
  rides `CanDrop`, `TryDroppingItem` always `Success`), the free
  functions `chain_on_success`/`chain_on_failed_roll` (the C#
  extension methods; the `self: Box<Self>` receivers do not erase across
  `dyn`), `DropPerPlayerOnThePlayer`, `OneFromRulesRule`, the luck
  variants (`NotScalingWithLuck`/`ScalingWithOnlyBadLuck` flags on
  `CommonDrop`, the OneFromOptions pair), and the
  `Food`/`StatusImmunityItem`/`MasterModeCommonDrop`/
  `MasterModeDropOnAllPlayers`/`BossBagByCondition` factories (all
  compositions of the M4-LOOT-1 rules, exactly as `ItemDropRule.cs`
  composes them).
- **The global entries** - `RegisterToGlobal` (the biome keys, the
  souls, the goodie bags, the kite drops) resolve before every NPC's
  own rules (`GetRulesForNPCID(includeGlobalDrops = true)`).

Findings: `corruption`/`crimson` recipe-style flags do not exist here -
the evil drops gate on `Conditions.IsCorruption/CrimsonAndNotExpert`
which read `WorldGen.crimson` (the WORLD type). The skipped rows
(13, warned): the NamedNPC localization gates, the RedHat legendary
gate, the MechBossSpawners/SlimeBody/StatueMimic/
FromOptionsWithoutRepeats rule classes (each needs its own event state) вЂ”
S1-E-14 has since landed all four classes and both conditions ("Loot rule
classes (S1-E-14, 2026-11-17)" below).
The unknown item ids (the ~20 warn-only OneFromOptions sets) emit and
resolve - the executor drops only registry-known items, so they surface
as the registry scale-up work.

## Loot rule classes (S1-E-14, 2026-11-17)

The four rule classes and two conditions the M4-LOOT-1/-2 build skipped
are ported verbatim in `crates/tr-core/src/loot.rs`:

- **`SlimeBodyItemDropRule`** вЂ” the ai[1] item rain: the stack table's
  seven families + the default 1..1, `Next(min, max+1)`, behind the
  `SlimeCanContainItems` + ai[1] gates.
- **`StatueMimicItemDropRule`** вЂ” `statue_style_to_item`
  (`WorldGen.cs:37928`, 26 cases), stack 1.
- **`MechBossSpawnersDropRule`** вЂ” the three sequential short-circuit
  arms (`!downedMechBossN && player.RollLuck(2500)==0` в†’ 556/544/557)
  behind `npc.value > 0 && hardMode && (!d1||!d2||!d3) &&
  !is_in_simulation`.
- **`FromOptionsWithoutRepeatsDropRule`** вЂ” the temp-list `Next(count)`
  + `RemoveAt` loop.

The conditions: **`NamedNPC`** compares the given name to the localized
key through the `get_text_value` seam, reading `LootNpc.given_name`;
**`RedHatSkeletron`** is a `Cond` variant with the 35/36/32/33 Г—
ai[3]/localAI[3] matrix. The `LootNpc`/`DropAttemptInfo` seam fields
carry all of it; `world_sim/npcs.rs::spawn_loot` fills
`is_in_simulation=false`, `get_text_value`, the real `npc.value()`, the
ai/local_ai zeros, the `given_name` Some-path and the four `downed_mech*`
flags (previously dead, C# 1:1 `MechBossSpawnersDropRule.cs:15`).

**The generator.** `tools/gen_loot.py` retires the four-rule/
two-condition skip rows and splices WHOLE C# methods; `loot_db_gen.rs`
regenerates 1421в†’1445 register calls вЂ” the diff is the 24 new rows only,
the existing rows byte-identical (`gen_loot.py --check` green).

**Deviations.**

- RedHat's 36/32 paths are unreachable at runtime вЂ” the port's `Npc` has
  no `localAI` (the ai[3] paths for 35/33 work); the field port is
  follow-up S1-E-14b. (RESOLVED 2026-11-18 by S1-E-14b, see below.)
- The mech-flags fill is a deliberate hardmode behavior change: mech
  spawner drops become possible.
- The generator splices whole methods вЂ” 24 registrations, not 12;
  half-body emission would drop C# rows.
- NamedNPC's key comparison rides the `get_text_value` seam.

### The eye aiStyle-2 re-port (S1-D-3, code-only mode)

The A-1 audit (`docs/research/54-audit-slime-eye.md` §2, branch
`docs/audit-slime-eye`, seed A1-3) found the LIVE eye family
(`npc.rs::update_eye` `:6733-6772`, seven kinds 2/133/190-194) is a
stand-in with a **FALSE citation**: `FlyerParams::FLOATING_EYE
{accel: 0.12, max_speed: 3.0}` (`npc_ai.rs:59-62`) claims `AI_002`, but
0.12/3.0 appear NOWHERE in `NPC.cs:52274-52731`. The re-port lands
`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_eye.rs` (`floating_eye_ai` + the `EyeEnv`/
`EyeOut` seams + the pure `despawn_discouraged` predicate), UNWIRED —
the live arm keeps running byte-identical until the wiring round (the
caster/style10 precedent). **Code-only mode: no compiler invoked; the
15 witness tests are written, not run.**

The defect catalogue the port corrects (audit §2a-c, verified against
the C# this round):

* **The movement core** — the live normalized-aim `dx/d*0.12` ±3 clamp
  plus the invented `sin(anim*3)*0.4` position bob vs the C#'s
  axis-separated direction-driven steering (`:52639-52708`):
  `num2 = 4f`, `num3 = 1.5f`, both `*= 1f + (1f - scale)`; X −0.1 /
  extra −0.1 over-cap / +0.05 wrong-sign / clamp ±num2; Y −0.04 /
  −0.05 / +0.03 / ±num3. No sqrt, no normalization, no bob.
* **The bounce kicks** (`:52283-52306`) — `oldVelocity × −0.5` (LAST
  tick's velocity, not the current one the live arm reflects), with
  the direction-gated floors: |vx| ≥ 2 away from the wall, |vy| ≥ 1
  both signs. The floors are what keeps eyes off ceilings.
* **The dawn flee** (`:52308-52325` + the predicate `:52752-52763`) —
  day && `position.Y <= worldSurface * 16` && !target-graveyard for
  types 2/133/190-194/317/318 → `EncourageDespawn(10)` (`:7249-7256`,
  the port's `despawn_timer` seam), `directionY = -1`, and the C#'s own
  dead-store quirk (`:52312-52320`: the `vy > 0 → direction = 1` write
  is immediately overwritten by `direction = -1`) ported VERBATIM.
  Else `TargetClosest()` — the live arm's ad-hoc `sign(dx)` facing and
  its aiStyle-13-cited sprite-dir keep are gone (the wiring drops them;
  `npc_target.rs` is the S1-D-3p core).
* **The 133 half-life enrage** (`:52502-52637`) — the f64
  `life < lifeMax * 0.5` compare flips the caps 4/1.5 → 6/4 and the
  accel 0.1/0.04 → 0.1/0.1; the live arm routed 133 through the same
  stand-in, so the enrage never happened.

## Buff slots (M2-BUFF-1)

`crates/tr-app/src/buffs.rs` ports the `Player.buffType[44]`/`buffTime[44]`
engine: the full `AddBuff` chain (`Player.cs:5263-5447`), `DelBuff`/`ClearBuff`/
`FindBuffIndex` (`:5250-5480`), the `UpdateBuffs` timer head (`:9855-9876`) and
the end-of-update immune purge (`:26012-26018`), hooked into the 60 Hz player
step (tick at the top of `Player::update`, purge at the end вЂ” the C# calls
`UpdateBuffs` at `:24535` and purges at `:26012`, so the interleave becomes
meaningful only once per-buff effects land with M2-BUFF-3/4). The verbatim
`Main.debuff`/`lightPet`/`vanityPet`/`meleeBuff`/`pvpBuff` tables are extracted
from `Main.cs:8867-9316`.

Deviations:

- **Multiplayer branch skipped** вЂ” `AddBuff`'s `Main.netMode == 1` remote path
  (`Player.cs:5269-5275`, msg 55 + `Main.pvpBuff`) is unreachable in the
  single-player port; the `pvpBuff` table is kept as data for M6-NET.
- **Difficulty multiplier is expert-only** вЂ” `AddBuff_DetermineBuffTimeToAdd`
  samples `GameDifficultyData.DebuffTimeMultiplier` (Classic 1 в†’ Expert 2 в†’
  Master 2.5, `GameDifficultyData.cs:96-100`); the port has no difficulty modes
  yet, so `expert_mode` applies Г—2 and master waits for M6-CREATIVE/difficulty.
  `resist_cold` and `dead_cells_potion_station` are `BuffSlots` fields defaulted
  `false` вЂ” the rules are ported and unit-tested but have no sources yet.
- **Timer-head effect branches deferred** вЂ” the mount refresh
  (`buffTime = 10`, `:9881-9884`) and the per-buff effect chain (`:9875-12000`)
  land with M2-MOUNT and M2-BUFF-3/4; the tick only decrements today.
- **Quirks preserved verbatim**: `DelBuff`'s compaction runs to `maxBuffs - 1`
  (deleting from a full bar leaves a hole at 42 while slot 43 keeps its buff вЂ”
  `Player.cs:5457`); the pet-removal loops have **no** `i--` rescan while the
  melee loop does (`:5377-5397` vs `:5347-5360`); a bar of 44 debuffs rejects
  new buffs of any kind (the first non-debuff scan finds nothing, `:5331-5334`);
  a debuff added to a mixed bar evicts the first *positive* buff; the immune
  purge does not rescan after `DelBuff`. Each is covered by a unit test naming
  the line.
- **`buffImmune` sizing** вЂ” `BuffID.Count = 401` (`BuffID.cs:997`), so ids are
  valid only below 401; the C# would throw on higher ids and the port panics the
  same way (tests synthesise bars from real ids via a `safe_ids()` helper).

- **Layer order**: the port draws the panel in `draw_hud` right after the
  emote bubbles (layer 1.1) rather than at the C#'s layer 23
  (`DrawInterface_23_NPCSignsDialog`, `Main.cs:45713-45716`) вЂ” the port's
  HUD spine draws the chat input strip early too; the panel sits under the
  inventory/bestiary/options layers, which is the visible-order difference
  that matters.

## The sign keyboard (W4-f22, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

The sign editor end-to-end: `IngameFancyUI.OpenVirtualKeyboard(1)`
(`IngameFancyUI.cs:86-145`) on the existing `ui/keyboard.rs`, the sign domain
in `crates/tr-app/src/signs.rs` (the S1-E-27 net half extended), and the
NPCChatPanel dialog's sign half. **Code-only mode**: no compiler/tests were
invoked; the 14 witnesses are written not run (4 in `ui/keyboard.rs`, 9 in
`signs.rs`, 1 in `ui/npc_chat.rs`), verified by re-reading the C#.

**The 2026-11-21 follow-up round** (code-only, 7 new witnesses in `signs.rs`,
written not run) landed the four hover/break deviations: the signHover
tooltip (`Main.cs:42940-42986`), the SignTileBubble
(`Main.cs:45739-45760` + the `Player.cs:32098-32115` latch), the lazy
kill-on-break (`WorldGen.cs:43686-43689`) and the tombstone epitaph display
census; the IME/clrInput/blockKey skip is final (input-system scope) and the
1200-cap scroll census confirms the source carries no scroll (the dialog's
10-line wrap is the display cap). See the deviation bullets below.

**The sign-TILE placement + style census (W4-f22 retire, 2026-11-21,
code-only)** — the place-arm and the sign-style text-store questions,
answered against the source:

- **The sign item is 171, NOT 177** (`ItemID.cs:2025` Sign = 171; 177 is
  Sapphire `:2037`). The full place-item family (itemdata rows verified):
  171 Sign → tile 55 (`Item.cs:3477-3487`), 321 Tombstone → 85 style 0
  (`:5186-5195`), 1173-1177 Grave Marker/Cross/Headstone/Gravestone/Obelisk
  → 85 styles 1-5 (`:14405-14459`), 3229-3233 Rich Gravestones → 85 styles
  6-10 (`:29791-29805`, `placeStyle = 6 + type - 3229`), 3617 Announcement
  Box → 425 (`:32574-32585`, `mech: true`), 4319/4320 Arrow Sign/Painted
  Arrow Sign → 510/511 (`:36997-37020`), 4710 Tattered Wood Sign → 573
  (`:38711-38721`). There is NO wood/stone/metal sign-item family and NO
  "gold sign" item — the gold variants are the Rich Gravestones (tombstone
  styles 6-10), and the one Sign item places the one tile 55.
- **The place-route is the TileObject registry, complete**: all six kinds
  (55/85/425/573/510/511) carry `UsesCustomCanPlace` defs
  (`TileObjectData.cs:3822-3947`) and route through `TileObject.CanPlace`/
  `Place` (`Player.cs:39771-39773` → the port's `place_item_tile` registry
  arm). The legacy `WorldGen.PlaceSign` (`WorldGen.cs:43781-43861`) is
  reached ONLY from the `PlaceTile` dispatcher (`:60166-60171`) — the
  item-use path never enters it, so the port needs no `PlaceSign` port.
  The base def is 2x2 `Style2x2` (`:3451-3460`: origin (0,1), AnchorBottom
  SolidTile|SolidWithTop|Table|SolidSide ×2) + four mounting alternates
  (alt 1 ceiling/AnchorTop, alt 2 left wall, alt 3 right wall, alt 4
  AnchorWall — `:3824-3844`); tile 85 has NO alternates (floor-only,
  `LavaDeath false`, `DrawYOffset 2`, `:3942-3947`) and tile 511 keeps the
  four (`:3918-3941`). The port's generated `D_55/D_85/D_425/D_510/D_511/
  D_573` defs match field-for-field (witnessed in `tr-core/edit/place.rs`).
- **The frame census — the mount rides frameX, the style rides frameX,
  frameY is always 0/18**: `TileObject.Place` writes `frameX =
  CoordinateFullWidth(36) · CalculatePlacementStyle + 18·col`, `frameY =
  18·row` (`TileObject.cs:60-109`; `CalculatePlacementStyle = style ·
  StyleMultiplier + Style`, `TileObjectData.cs:1990-1998` — the alternates
  carry Style 1-4, the tombstone styles 0-10 ride the base Style 0). So
  `Sign.ReadSign`'s origin decode (`frameX/18 % 2`, `frameY/18`,
  `Sign.cs:26-29`) resolves EVERY mount and EVERY style to the same 2x2
  top-left — the record lookup is mount/style-agnostic by construction.
  The death-drop projectiles pick the tombstone style the same way
  (`Projectile.cs:25339-25350`: 201-205 → styles 1-5, 527-531 → 6-10, the
  43 tombstone → 0; the `DropTombstone` coin gate `Player.cs:39116-39117`:
  >10 gold → `Next(5)+527`, else `Next(6)` with 0 → the 43 plain tombstone).
- **All sign styles read/write the SAME text-store**: `Main.sign[0..31999]`
  keyed by the frame-decoded origin — `Sign.ReadSign`/`TextSign`/`KillSign`
  (`Sign.cs`) never read the style or the mount; the tombstone epitaph
  write (`Projectile.cs:25358-25363`, the d2 sweep), the editor
  (`Main.SubmitSignText`), the hover tooltip and the wiring announcement
  all ride the one store. VERIFIED — no per-style store exists.
- **The announcement box (425) wiring arm** (`Wiring.cs:1177-1233`): the
  2x2 SkipWire, the `-disableannouncementbox` guard, then
  `Sign.ReadSign(num7, num8, CreateIfMissing: false)` — the SAME store,
  printed pink via `NewTextMultiline(…, 460)` (SP) / message 107 (MP), with
  the `-announcementboxrange` distance gate. The port's
  `tr-core/wiring.rs` 425 arm carried a 2x2-BOX record scan instead of
  ReadSign's EXACT-origin match — the retire census fixed it to the exact
  (x, y) lookup + the `!tileSign` origin kill arm (`Sign.cs:30-34`), with
  the off-origin-record and stale-origin witnesses.
- **The `tileSign` set is exactly {55, 85, 425, 573}** (`Main.cs:10081-
  10084`) — the arrow signs 510/511 place through the same registry route
  but are NOT sign kinds (no record, no right-click editor, no hover). The
  port's two `is_sign_tile` copies carried wrong tile NAMES in their doc
  comments (85 "Tattered Wood Sign", 425 "Illuminant Hanging Sign", 573
  "Sunplate Sign") — corrected to Tombstones/Announcement Box/Tattered
  Wood Sign; the sets themselves were already right.
- **The CheckSign break cascade** (`WorldGen.cs:43548-43779`, dispatch
  `:85761-85768` — 55/85/395/425/510/511/573): the destroy tail's
  `Sign.KillSign` (`:43686-43689`) is the lazy sweep already landed; the
  drop arms (`:43690-43764`) map 85 → 321/1173+style-1/3229+style-6 by the
  frameX style (`num12`), 425 → 3617, 573 → 4710, 511 → 4320, 510 → 4319,
  default → 171, plus the 85 ghost roll (`genRand.Next(8/4/2)`, NPC 316,
  `:43708-43742`). The port's `check_object` has no CheckSign arm (the
  pre-existing lazy-sweep deviation) — the per-cell drops are suppressed
  by `KILL_TILE_NO_CELL_DROP` (all six kinds true), so a broken sign
  currently drops NO item; the cascade + drops stay the break-lane's
  follow-up (recorded, not ported here).

**The census pin: the sign text cap is 1200, NOT 500.** `IngameFancyUI.cs:145`
passes `allowEmpty: false, 1200` to the `UIVirtualKeyboard` ctor (the ctor
default `maxLength` is 20, `:159`); pinned as `signs::SIGN_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH`
and witnessed by `the_sign_keyboard_opens_with_the_1200_cap` (a 1300-char
write trims to 1200 through `SetTextMaxLength`, `:428`).

## Town housing (S1-E-11a, 2026-11-14)

`WorldGen.ScoreRoom` (`WorldGen.cs:5858-5992`) landed in `tr-core::housing`:
the room's **score** and its **best home spot** (`WorldGen.bestX/bestY`).

- **The base**: 50 minus the evil count over the tested area (the room's
  bounds grown by 5/3 + 40 and clipped, `:5994-6020`); the evil count is
  `GetTileTypeCountByCategory(counts, TotalGoodEvil)` (`:5845-5856`) over the
  active tiles' kinds (`:5831-5843`). A room scoring в€’250 or worse is
  rejected outright (`:5889-5892`).
- **The candidates**: the room's own area (`:5897-5899`); each needs an active
  solid tile, a home spot (the tile 379 never is, `:6021-6029`), solid
  neighbours left and right and no solid tile in the box below (`:5901-5904`).
- **The furniture**: the 5Г—4 block above each candidate scores +5 for a
  non-solid tile and в€’5 for a solid one, в€’20 for a door (10/388) or an open
  door anchor (389), the ninth column в€’15 each and a chest в€’30 each
  (`:5910-5951`); the tile kinds of `TileID.Sets.IgnoredInHouseScore` and the
  `BasicChest` set are the C#'s (`TileID.cs:620`/`:570`).
- **The room membership**: the three cells above the spot must be in the
  room's mask (`WorldGen.roomTiles`, `:5953-5972`) and the room must hold the
  spot itself.

`town.rs::scan_spot` now returns the scored spot instead of the scan's
centre, so `quick_find_home` picks the room's best home (the C#'s
`QuickFindHome` в†’ `RoomNeeds` в†’ `ScoreRoom` в†’ `hiScore > 0` chain,
`WorldGen.cs:5732-5795`).

S1-E-11b added the occupancy: `town.rs::room_occupancy` ports
`ScoreRoom_IsThisRoomOccupiedBySomeone` (`WorldGen.cs:5814-5829`) вЂ” a housed
town NPC whose home (and the cell above it) is in the room refuses the home
(the C#'s `hiScore = -1`), and the asking NPC is skipped through the
`ignoreNPC` argument. The C#'s `CanNPCsLiveWithEachOther`
(`TownRoomManager.cs:144-156`) compares the two `housingCategory` fields;
the port's town kinds all carry the vanilla default category 0 (the
category-1 kinds 637/638 are not ported), so a housed NPC always conflicts
and the shared-room arm (`WorldGen.sharedRoomX`, `:5936-5939`) is
unreachable вЂ” the score takes the shared room as an argument. (S1-E-11c
below replaced that shortcut with the real `housingCategory` comparison.)

Deviations: the relocation (`MoveTownNPC`/`moveRoom`, `WorldGen.cs:4685`/
`:4843`), `GetHouseholdStatus` and the `lookForHomeTimeout` gate were still
out at 11b.

## Town housing (S1-E-11c, 2026-11-16)

The relocation machinery, the `housingCategory` data and the household status.

- **`housingCategory`** (`ID/HousingCategoryID.cs:3-8`: `CommonNPCs = 0`,
  `PetNPCs = 1`) is `town.rs::housing_category`, keyed by the vanilla net id вЂ”
  0 for every town NPC (`NPC.cs:8518`) and 1 for TownCat/TownDog 637/638
  (`:17224`), TownBunny 656 (`:17308`), TownSlimeBlue 670 (`:17494`) and the
  678-684 slime band (`:17607`). `CanNPCsLiveWithEachOther`
  (`TownRoomManager.cs:144-156`) is `can_npcs_live_with_each_other`, so
  `room_occupancy` now compares them the way `ScoreRoom_IsThisRoomOccupiedBySomeone`
  (`WorldGen.cs:5821-5825`) does: a same-category occupant refuses the room,
  a different-category one only sets `sharedRoomX` and the loop keeps going.
  `quick_find_home`/`scan_spot` take the asking NPC's net id for it.
- **`lookForHomeTimeout`** (`NPC.cs:6547`): `Npc::look_for_home_timeout`,
  decaying one per tick at the `NPC.UpdateNPC` tail (`NPC.cs:90324-90327`).
  `kickOut` arms it to `KICK_OUT_LOOK_FOR_HOME_TIMEOUT` = 3600
  (`NPC.cs:95267`) and `moveRoom` clears it (`WorldGen.cs:4852`); both home
  scans skip a non-zero timer (`WorldGen.cs:5621`, `:71635`).
- **`GetHouseholdStatus`** (`TownRoomManager.cs:130-142`) is
  `TownRooms::household_status`: 1 homeless, else 2 when `HasRoomQuick`, else
  0. `TownRooms::occupants_at` ports `AddOccupantsToList` (`:22-31`).
- **The relocation arm**: `town::kick_out`/`town::move_room` port
  `WorldGen.kickOut` (`:4869-4879`) and `WorldGen.moveRoom` (`:4843-4855`),
  and the arrival path now prefers a live homeless NPC of the kind over a
  second spawn (`FindNPCLookingForHomeThatCanMoveIn` `:5428` в†’
  `:5453-5463`).

Reachability note: the shared-room arm is now **live in the predicate** but
still unreachable in gameplay, because the port's `NpcKind` roster carries no
category-1 pet kind (637/638/656/670/678-684 are unported, they have no AI
and no bestiary row). The data and the predicate land 1:1 so that the arm
turns on with the pets rather than needing a second pass. The remaining
`S1-E-11` items are `MoveTownNPC`'s failure-reason feedback text
(`:4694-4828`, the housing query UI reads it), which needs the housing-query
`Main.mouseNPC` model (`ui/housing.rs:12-14`).

### Stinkbug flags (S1-E-11b, 2026-11-18)

`RoomScan.has_stinkbug`/`has_echo_stinkbug` are added by this change and
set by `check_tile` from the active tiles 630/631
(`CheckRoom`, `WorldGen.cs:6189-6198`) вЂ” the cages are not solid, so the fill
keeps running and only the flags are written; `check_room` clears both per
scan (`StartRoomCheck:6047-6048`). The consumers landed with the relocation
round below (`MoveTownNPC`'s pet-exempt rejection `:4777-4799`); the arrival
gate (`:5431`) still rides the arrival path. No RNG draws in any
ported block (`Main.rand` untouched; the flags are pure tile reads).

## Town housing (S1-E-11d, 2026-11-18)

`MoveTownNPC`'s failure-reason feedback and the `Main.mouseNPC` housing-query

- **`MoveTownNPC`** (`WorldGen.cs:4685-4841`) is `town::move_town_npc`: the

- **The support seams** in `tr-core::housing`: `score_room_report` returns
  `ScoreRoom`'s globals (`hiScore`, `bestX/bestY`, `roomOccupied`, `roomEvil`,

  thin wrapper; `room_needs_flags` returns the four `RoomNeeds` flags
  (`:4292-4298`); `check_special_town_npc_spawning_conditions` ports the
  Truffle's mushroom gate (`:4970-4998`, `MushroomTileThreshold = 100`,

- **The query/relocation UI**: `Main.mouseNPCIndex/mouseNPCType`
  (`Main.cs:751-753`) ride the App; the housing page's cell click arms them

  `ui::housing::draw_carried` (`DrawInterface_38:45214-45216`) and suppresses
  the hover text (`MouseTextInner:20192`), the world click runs
  `town::perform_housing_check` (`Main.cs:45162-45170`) or

  the right release / a carried item / a closed inventory / a dead NPC drop

Deviations:
- **The `RichRoomCheckFeedback` particle pass is not ported**
  (`Main.cs:45165`, `DataStructures/RichRoomCheckFeedback.cs`). Its

  runs the chain twice on identical inputs (identical state) and proves a

## Mid-game housing relocation (W4-d119, 2026-11-21, code-only — tests written NOT run)

The mid-game relocation driver — a town NPC re-homes when its house is lost,
is evicted, or a free room appears near the player. Stacked on W4-d118's
`QuickFindHome`/occupancy seams (`task/W4-d118-housing-scoreroom`); relocation
only — the NEW-NPC homeless arrival/departure pair is out of scope.

- **Home loss** (`Main.UpdateTime_SpawnTownNPCs`, `Main.cs:65607-65614`): at the
  7200-tick check, every housed resident that is not the Travelling Merchant
  (368) / Old Man (37) / Skeleton Merchant (453) and not already homeless runs
  `WorldGen.QuickFindHome(k)` around its own home tile. A destroyed room
  re-scans: `QuickFindHome` either re-homes at a new scored spot or sets
  `homeless = true` (`WorldGen.cs:5785`/`:5790`). Wired in
  `world_sim/npcs.rs`'s arrival block on the same `check_for_spawns + 1 >= 7200`
  boundary the party roll predicts. The port's `home: Option` models homeless
  as `None`, so a failed scan clears it. **The outer-guard quirk is kept**:
  `QuickFindHome`'s `homeTileX > 10 && … && homeTileY < maxTilesY` guard
  (`:5736`) makes an out-of-range home a NO-OP — the NPC keeps its home, it does
  NOT go homeless; only an in-range home whose scan fails unhouses. Each
  re-home fires NO_HOBO (8, `:5780`).
- **The prioritized type** (`WorldGen.UpdatePrioritizedTownNPC`,
  `WorldGen.cs:71627-71641` → `town_rehome::update_prioritized_town_npc`): the
  first live homeless town NPC with `lookForHomeTimeout == 0` and a type other
  than 368/160 becomes `WorldGen.prioritizedTownNPCType` (the port parks the
  kind on `ArrivalState::prioritized`). The Old-Man (37) early return is
  vacuous — no ported kind. RNG-free.
- **The house probe** (`WorldGen.CheckForHousesNearAPlayer`,
  `WorldGen.cs:71643-71674` → `town_rehome::check_for_houses_near_a_player`):
  the view rectangle around the player's centre tile (`ToTileCoordinates` is
  `(int)x >> 4`, an arithmetic shift — `Utils.cs:1809`), inflated by
  `MaxWorldViewSize / 32` = (60, 37) (`Main.cs:66714`), clamped to
  `[10, max − 10]` (`WorldUtils.ClampToWorld`, `WorldBuilding/WorldUtils.cs:9-14`),
  then 300 random picks. The first house-wall pick runs the relocation-only
  `SpawnTownNPC(x, y, canSpawnNewTownNPC: false)` (`:5409-5463`): the room
  check + furniture + stinkbug + score gates, then
  `FindNPCLookingForHomeThatCanMoveIn` moves an existing homeless NPC of the
  prioritized type into the scored spot (`:5453-5463`), registers the room and
  zeroes the prioritized slot. With `canSpawnNewTownNPC: false` the new-spawn
  tail (`:5468-5611`) is unreachable — this arm NEVER spawns a new NPC. Wired
  in `world_sim/growth.rs`'s `UpdateWorld` head (after the liquid pass, before
  the growth loops), on the `UpdateWorldGen` stream; each relocation fires
  NO_HOBO (8) once the borrow releases.
- **The eviction predicate** (`WorldGen.IsNPCEvictable`,
  `WorldGen.cs:4857-4867` → `town_rehome::is_npc_evictable`): the local
  player's hitbox inflated by half the max world view size (±960/±600) must
  intersect the NPC's 16×16 home tile; a negative index / missing player /
  missing home is never evictable. RNG-free. **The predicate has NO caller in
  this decompile** (grep of the whole tree finds only the definition); the
  real eviction triggers are the house-banner right-click (`Main.cs:40827`),
  the controller path (`UILinksInitializer.cs:908`) and net message 60
  (`MessageBuffer.cs:2723`/`:2732`), all of which call the already-ported
  `town::kick_out` (`WorldGen.cs:4869-4879`: homeless + 3600-tick
  `lookForHomeTimeout` + `TownManager.KickOut`). The banner-draw surface
  (`DrawNPCHousesInWorld`, `Main.cs:40711-40832`) is unported, so the predicate
  lands as the faithful gate for when it arrives; the kick-out primitive and
  the timeout decay (`NPC.cs:90324-90327`) are already live.

## Deterministic screenshots: the OS pointer (M1.5-LIQUID-2-det-fix)

The follow-up flagged by the M4-LOOT-3 work ("the waterfall sparkle pass breaks
pure-world screenshot determinism, `TR_NO_WATERFALL=1` restores SHA256
equality") did **not** reproduce as a waterfall bug. The investigation:

- Two `TR_SHOT` runs of the same command differed by exactly 290 px at the
  forest lake вЂ” and *both* the `TR_NO_WATERFALL=1` and `TR_NO_WEATHER=1` pairs
  differed the same way. The diff was a small blue arrow (the in-game
  `Main.DrawCursor` sprite) at a different screen position per run: the **OS
  mouse pointer**. `App.mouse_pos` starts at `Vec2::ZERO` and follows real
  `CursorMoved` events, so the desktop pointer's position at capture time is
  run-to-run harness noise.
- An important false lead on the way: without a pristine world copy each run,
  the default `Terrustaria.trwld` is **rewritten by the autosave**, so run N+1
  loads run N's settled liquids and the comparison is meaningless. Deterministic
  pairs must `cp` a pristine `.trwld` per run (or use `TR_SPOUT`, which builds
  its fall by edits after load).
- The waterfall walk itself was audited and is deterministic: all state runs on
  fixed steppers (`waterfall_step`, `liquid_step`), `find_waterfalls` rescans on
  a 30-tick gate, and `TrySparkling`'s single randomness (`WaterfallManager.cs:
  1046-1065`) is pinned to a frame-derived `FastRandom` seed
  (`frame_count * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 ^ world.seed`). New unit tests pin this:
  `the_draw_walk_is_deterministic_for_the_same_seed_chain` (two managers, 600
  seeded frames, equal quads/lights/sparkles every frame) and
  `try_sparkling_grants_deterministically_for_a_seed` in `draw.rs` (the grant is
  a pure function of the seed; dark falls never roll).

Fix (harness semantics, a deliberate deviation from the C#): during a `TR_SHOT`
capture without an explicit `TR_MOUSE`, the logical pointer is parked offscreen
(`-64,-64`) and `CursorMoved` is ignored вЂ” `deterministic_pointer_park()`
(`app/mod.rs`). The pointer is harness *input*, not scene content; the original's
`Main.DrawCursor` still draws wherever the player's pointer is when `TR_MOUSE`
pins it (cursor/tooltip screenshots keep working).

Verified byte-identical SHA256 pairs (pristine world copy per run):
- forest lake, waterfalls on, no `TR_MOUSE` вЂ” before the fix this pair differed;
- `TR_SPOUT=2240,160` with the fall live in view for 1200 frames, no `TR_MOUSE`;
- the same `TR_SPOUT` scene with `TR_MOUSE=200,200` (explicit pin still wins).

## Regeneration engines (M2-BUFF-2)

`crates/tr-app/src/regen.rs` ports the life and mana regen accumulators:
`UpdateLifeRegen` (`Player.cs:18942-19391`) вЂ” the DoT clamps, the ramp tiers at
300/600/900/1200/1500/1800/2400/3000, the 3600 cap, moving Г—0.5 vs standing
Г—1.25, the final `(int)Math.Round(num3 * (statLifeMax2/400В·0.85 + 0.15))` add
(banker's, via the shared `tr_core::damage::round_bankers`, now `pub`), the
В±120 chunk counters and the generic в€’120 drain (в‰¤4 hp per examined chunk) вЂ”
and `UpdateManaRegen` / `ApplyManaRegenerationDelay` (`:19380-19562`) вЂ” the
delay curve `((1в€’mana/max)В·240+45)В·0.7`, the standing/grappling/buff double
decrement, the `maxMana/3 + 1` base with the still/grapple double-add, the

behind an `hp > 0` gate; `Hurt` resets `lifeRegenTime` (`:38395`) while the

- **Death from a DoT drain clamps at 0 hp** вЂ” resolved by M2-BUFF-3: the

## DoT debuffs (M2-BUFF-3)

The DoT set (poison/fire/blood; ichor is *not* a DoT in 1.4.5.8 вЂ” it is the
armor-penetration debuff and stays with M2-BUFF-4) landed on top of the
M2-BUFF-1/2 engines:

- **Player side** вЂ” `player.rs` derives the DoT deltas as a pure
  `derive_dot_inputs(&self, expert) -> DotDerivation` in the exact C# branch
  order (`Player.cs:18949в†’19095`: poisoned в€’4, venom/chlorophyte spore в€’30,
  the fire family в€’8/в€’16/в€’24/в€’60 each doubled while dripping slime (buff
  137) is held, suffocation в€’40, electrified в€’8 plus в€’32 more while
  running, tongued в€’100 expert-only; bleeding (30) only zeroes the ramp
  time, `:19178-19181`; honey (48) softens a negative sum by 4 clamped at
  0, `:19096-19103`) and feeds the five `RegenInputs.dot_*` fields.
  `regen.rs` runs the drain: the fast lane (burned || suffocating ||
  tongued && expert, `:19313`) chunks в€’600 в†’ 5 dmg with an early return
  (`:19313-19335`), the generic lane keeps the в‰¤4 hp per в€’120 chunk; both
  return a `DotDeath` (`ByOther` 7/8/9/10/12/22/23 вЂ” the priority chains
  7в†’12в†’8 and 22в†’9в†’10в†’23в†’8 are precomputed by the caller,
  `:19321-19331`/`:19362-19385`) that `death.rs::death_text_for` renders.
  `update_survival` hosts the demo inflictions/cures: lava contact в†’
  `add_buff(24, 420)` (`:27710-27711`), water deletes OnFire/OnFire3
  (24/323, `:27750-27761`), Wet 103 re-grants the fire immunities every
  frame (`:11740-11751`), and the expired-buff sweep (`:25608-25616`) +
  per-frame `buff_immune` reset (`:25561-25565`) ride `Player::update` in
  the C# frame order (reset в†’ tick в†’ sweep в†’ вЂ¦ в†’ immune purge,
  `Player.cs:25555в†’26016`).
- **NPC side** вЂ” `npc_buffs.rs` ports the NPC chain as its own module (the
  C# keeps the Player and NPC `AddBuff` chains separate, so the port does
  too): the 20-slot `NpcBuffs` (`buffType`/`buffTime` `NPC.cs:6193-6197`,
  `NPC.maxBuffs = 20` `:95189`, `lifeRegenCount` `:6249`), the verbatim
  `NPC.AddBuff` chain (`:89926-89983`: immune guard в†’ same-id extend в†’
  evict the first non-debuff в†’ reject at 20 debuffs), the `UpdateNPC` buff
  block ticked from the head of `Npc::update` at the C# position
  (`:90373-90377`: set flags в†’ clear expired в†’ apply DOTs) with the
  `DOTTally` sum (`NPC.cs:59-141`, `:91594-91774` вЂ” Oiled (204) adds a
  flat +50 in combination with a fire debuff, AcceleratePoisons (398)
  doubles the boostable half via `SupportAcceleration`) and
  `GetHurtByDebuff`'s direct `life -=` drain that bypasses
  `StrikeNPC`/i-frames/knockback (`:91864-91888`). Immunities are the
  roster's slice of `NPCID.Sets.DebuffImmunitySets` (slime 20, King Slime
  20+31, demon eye/zombie/wandering eye none вЂ” `NPCID.cs:6079-6086`,
  `:6386-6392`, `:6905`) plus the derived rules of `NPC.cs:17818-17838`
  (immune 20 в‡’ 30 + 375, immune 69 в‡’ 36).

Deviations:

- **Honey does not extinguish fire** вЂ” the C# curing loop is driven by
  `WetCollision`, whose tile scan sets `Collision.honey` as readily as
  `Collision.wet` (`Collision.cs:1608-1618`), so standing in honey *would*
  douse OnFire in the original. The plan assumed the cure required actual
  water; checked against the source it was wrong in the C#'s favour of
  honey, and the port takes the plan fallback (DW-2.2): the cure is
  conditioned on a water probe distinct from honey
  (`in_water && !in_honey && !in_lava`).
- **The NPC DoT drain stops at hp в‰¤ 0** вЂ” the C# `GetHurtByDebuff` clamps
  `life = 1` and finishes the kill with `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999)`
  (`NPC.cs:91880-91887`); the port instead breaks the drain loop at
  `hp <= 0` and lets the existing hp в‰¤ 0 collect (`world_sim/npcs.rs:38`)
  run the normal death path (coins/gel drop exactly once).
- **The player-side DoT drain stops at the first hp в‰¤ 0 crossing** вЂ” the C#
  while-loops keep chunking a dead player until the counter empties (fast
  lane `:19315-19334`, generic `:19357-19385`); the port returns one death
  per tick and clamps at 0 (`regen.rs:236-241` fast lane, `:251-255`
  generic) вЂ” death lands the same tick, only the transient negative
  `statLife` differs.
- **The `dontTakeDamage` gate is omitted** вЂ” `UpdateNPC_BuffApplyDOTs` is
  wrapped in `if (!this.dontTakeDamage)` (`NPC.cs:91596`); the flag has no
  Rust counterpart yet, so the port always applies DOTs.
- **The last tick of an expiring debuff does not drain** вЂ” the C# keeps the
  boolean flags (`poisoned`, `onFire`, вЂ¦) set until the end of the frame,
  so `UpdateLifeRegen` (`:25977`) still drains on the tick a buff expires;
  the port re-derives the flags by scanning the slots *after* the
  expired-buff sweep, so a debuff whose timer hit 0 this tick contributes
  nothing. One tick of drain lost per expiry; the sweep itself is verbatim.
- **Wet self-deletion runs one tick early** вЂ” the C# branch tests the
  previous frame's `lavaWet` (`:11741-11744`); the port tests the current
  `in_lava` probe, so Wet is deleted one tick sooner and OnFire from lava
  is granted immediately while Wet is held (the C# rejects it through the
  immune guard for one frame).
- **Pre-existing gaps made visible by the DoT path**: the lava contact hit
  is 30 dmg vs the C#'s 80 (`Player.cs:27687`), and `Player::respawn` does
  not wipe buffs while the C# `Spawn` clears every non-persistent buff
  (`Player.cs:16995-17002`) вЂ” both predate this task and stay open.
- **Death texts are EN stand-ins** вЂ” `death_text_for` hardcodes one English
  string per `DotDeath` after the `DeathText.*` keys of `Lang.cs`'s
  `CreateDeathMessage` switch (`:1073-1126`, e.g. `DeathText.Suffocated_*`);
  the localization pass replaces them.
- **Deferred pieces**: the starving lane and the honey regen aura
  (M2-BUFF-7/M2-BUFF-5), the Daybreak/Dryad's Bane spear sources, the
  `ApplyDOTs`-only flags (javelined/eelwhip/celled/вЂ¦), `SuperNatural`
  lifeRegen, `TryAddingRepeatedBuff`, `vampireSeed` (nothing grants buff 22
  or sets the vampire-slime `ai[1] = 9` in the roster), ichor в†’ M2-BUFF-4,
  and the presentation half вЂ” combat text, dust and the buff-bar HUD icons.
