## Named RNG streams (`Main.SwapRandom`, S1-A-2)

`crates/tr-app/src/app/rng.rs` ports `Main._rngs` (`Main.cs:1294-1295`) and
`Main.SwapRandom` (`:3204-3215`) as `NamedRngs` + `RngKey`. The 17 keys are the exact
strings the decompiled source passes to `SwapRandom`: the 13 nested stage wrappers of
`DoUpdateInWorld_Inner` (`:17749-17809`) plus `DoUpdateInWorld` (`:17732`), `SpawnNPC`,
`UpdateLiquid` and `UpdateWorldGen`. Each stream is created lazily as
`new UnifiedRandom(Main.ActiveWorldFileData.Seed)` (`:3210-3212`) вЂ” i.e. every key starts
from the *same* integer and the streams diverge only by how many draws each stage has
consumed. The C# dictionary is created **once per process** in `Main.Initialize()`
(`Main.cs:6465`) and no world-load hook clears it вЂ” the stage streams persist across
worlds within a session (the S1-A-2 note claimed a per-world reset; the decompile says
otherwise). The port rebuilds `NamedRngs` per world load (`App::swap_world`): a recorded
deviation вЂ” deterministic, and identical for the single-world sessions the port models
(see "The S1-A-11 runtime migration" under S1-A-10 below).

The C# swaps the stage's stream into `Main.rand` for the duration of a `using` block.
The port has no global `Main.rand`, so a stage asks the registry for its key and passes
the `&mut UnifiedRandom` down: the isolation is the same, and the "no shared stream
consumed in a different order" contract is expressible per stage instead of relying on
the call stack.

Seeding rule (S1-A-2 deleted the ad-hoc constants; S1-A-11 then deleted the bridge
fields themselves): every App stream is seeded from the world seed. The bridge fields
`npc_rng`/`item_rng`/`prefix_rng`/`ambience_rng`/`growth_rng` no longer exist вЂ” the
stage bodies draw their named `UnifiedRandom` streams directly (S1-A-11 below).
`craft_rng` keeps a world-seeded splitmix stream until S1-L-11e (the crafting stream is
its own convention, `craft.rs::next_rand3`), and `light_rng_seed` keeps `world_seed | 1`
because it seeds the tile-light `FastRandom` (`TileLightScanner._random`), not a
`SwapRandom` key.

Wired consumer: `clock_rng` is **gone**; the clock's dawn/dusk rolls now draw from
`_rngs["UpdateTime"]` *inside* the boundary branch (`world_sim/clock.rs`). This also
fixes a determinism bug: previously one `roll01` was drawn every frame and only used at
a boundary, so the event roll depended on the frame count. The port keeps its
uniform-threshold approximation of the C#'s `Next(n) == 0` rolls (the exact
`Next` chain for the invasion cluster is deferred with the event-roll task).

Bridge streams (S1-A-11, **landed 2026-11-13**): the stage bodies for items/loot,
NPCs/spawns, ambience, growth and the prefix rolls now draw from their named
`UnifiedRandom` streams in the C# order вЂ” the deviations this introduced are recorded
under S1-A-10 ("The S1-A-11 runtime migration"); `docs/research/35-rng-utils.md` tracks
the matrix.

## The RNG-order contract (S1-A-10)

Determinism is a hard invariant of the port (AGENTS.md: "RNG streams, the G6
`WorldFrameKey` contents and the fixed-step order must not change"). Every random
draw in the C# comes from one of four kinds of source, and **the order in which a
stream is consumed is itself observable behaviour**: the same seed with a different
draw order is a different world, a different loot table and a different set of pixels
(`docs/research/35-rng-utils.md` в†’ Responsibility).

| # | C# source | C# anchor | Port counterpart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the global `Main.rand` (`UnifiedRandom`) | `Main.cs:1291-1292` | `app/rng.rs` `NamedRngs::global()` вЂ” the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in (S1-A-11); worldgen keeps its own `Streams` contract rng |
| 2 | a **named** `Main.SwapRandom(key)` stream (`Main._rngs[key] = new UnifiedRandom(worldSeed)`) | `Main.cs:1294-1295`, `:3204-3215`; stage wrappers `:17749-17809` | `app/rng.rs` `NamedRngs`/`RngKey` (S1-A-2); `clock_rng` в†’ `_rngs["UpdateTime"]` |
| 3 | a `FastRandom` (48-bit LCG) вЂ” `WithModifier(x, y)` per tile/position, or a fresh `CreateWithRandomSeed` | `FastRandom.cs:7-11, 27-51, 85-88` | `tile_light/palette.rs` `FastRandom` (exact); the runtime growth draws ride `stream(UpdateWorldGen)` (S1-A-11 вЂ” `WorldGen.genRand` is a `Main.rand` alias) |
| 4 | a per-call **re-seed** of one of the above вЂ” `Main._drawRand.SetSeed(proj.localAI[0])`, `Main.TileFrameSeed` | `Main.cs:35795`, `:66567`, `:61721` | folded/synthetic seeds (documented deviations) |

`WorldGen.genRand` is an **alias** of `Main.rand` (`WorldGen.cs:4445`; `Item.Prefix`
reads it during generation, `Item.cs:506-508, :528`), so the worldgen and the gameplay
draws interleave on **one** stream. The port does not model that single stream
(`research/35` deviation 4); worldgen uses its own `Streams` contract rng.

### The contract

Any task that adds, moves or touches a random draw must state вЂ” in the task row and in
the code,

1. **which stream** it consumes (`Main.rand` / the named key / which `FastRandom` /
   the worldgen `Streams` contract rng), and
2. **in which order** the draws happen on that stream: the call sequence relative to
   the other draws on the same stream (per AI sub-step, per tile, per frame), and the
   guards that skip a draw.

A draw whose **count** or **order** depends on a value that is not itself
deterministic вЂ” the frame rate, the wall clock, a memory address, a `HashMap`'s
iteration order вЂ” breaks the contract even when the stream identity is right.

### Review checklist (apply to every RNG-touching task)

- [ ] The task names its stream(s) and cites the C# draw site (`file.cs:line`), not
      only the Rust file.
- [ ] The **draw count per unit of simulation** matches the C#: a draw inside a
      `while`/`for` AI sub-step is not the same as one per update, and a draw inside a
      boundary branch is not the same as one per frame.
- [ ] The **draw order** relative to the other draws on the same stream is preserved:
      a `SwapRandom` stage's body draws in the C# sequence and a shared stream is not
      reordered.
- [ ] No `HashMap`/`HashSet` iteration, `f32`/pointer, or wall-clock value feeds an RNG
      seed or a draw guard; seeds come from the world seed or a frozen, documented
      constant.
- [ ] A change of **stream identity** (splitmix в†’ `UnifiedRandom`, a re-key, merging
      two streams) is recorded as a deliberate deviation here and in
      `research/35-rng-utils.md`, with a before/after determinism pair.
- [ ] The reproducibility tests and `TR_STATS`/`TR_BENCH` still hold; any pinned
      constant that must move is re-pinned in the same commit and explained.

A stream is **not** "frozen" by pinning the port's own output as if it were the C#'s
(`world_hash.rs`'s constants, `research/35` deviation 6): a self-consistency pin cannot
detect a C#-divergent stream. Pin against a `dotnet` oracle (S1-A-1/S1-A-5) or an
original `.wld` where one exists.

### The S1-A-11 runtime migration (2026-11-13)

S1-A-11 moved every runtime stage body off the splitmix bridges onto its named
`UnifiedRandom` stream. Each stream's **identity** and per-site **draw shape** match the
C#; the deviations below are the deliberate divergences, grouped:

- **`_rngs` lifetime.** The C# creates `Main._rngs` once per process in
  `Main.Initialize()` (`Main.cs:6465`) and never clears it вЂ” stage streams persist
  across world loads within a session. The port rebuilds `NamedRngs` per world load
  (`App::swap_world`): deterministic, and identical for the single-world sessions the
  port models. (`NamedRngs::reset` keeps the C#'s lazy per-key creation, `:3210-3212`.)
- **Bare-`Main.rand` seeding.** Vanilla seeds the bare stream from the wall clock вЂ”
  `new UnifiedRandom((int)DateTime.Now.Ticks)` (`Main.cs:6462-6464`) вЂ” so two vanilla
  sessions never replay each other. The port seeds `NamedRngs::global()` with the world
  seed instead: the determinism contract (this section) outranks the wall-clock seeding,
  and no `dotnet`-pinned vector can observe the choice.
- **Within-stream order across the tick.** The C# spends the weather/town/angler-swap
  rolls inside the single `Main.UpdateTime` block (the wrapper at `Main.cs:17795`), in
  its statement order. The port's consumers run in `update_world_tick`'s subsystem
  order (weather в†’ town pass в†’ angler), so two draws that share the `UpdateTime` stream
  sit at their subsystem positions, not the C#'s statement positions вЂ” same stream,
  same draw shapes, a reordering recorded here. The wiring rolls stay on their own
  seeded stream, **not** `UpdateWorldGen` (S1-L-6c unchanged; the actuation-drop spawn
  rides `Wiring::rand_mut()`) вЂ” vanilla's `Wiring.cs` rolls `Main.rand` under whatever
  swap is live (`:811-812`, `:1393`, `:1849`), which the port still does not reproduce.
- **DD2 gate stream.** `DD2Event.SpawnMonsterFromGate` is called from the lane gate's AI
  (`NPC.cs:41001`, under the `UpdateNPCs` swap, `Main.cs:17767`). The core's
  `tr_core::dd2::lane_spawn_roll_*` take `Fn` rolls, so the port rides a `RefCell` over
  `stream(UpdateNpcs)` (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) and the closure draws live: the old
  32-draw pre-buffer (a splitmix-share workaround) is dissolved and each pick spends
  exactly the vanilla draw count.
- **Per-site decisions confirmed in build (P2-P5).** The extractinator's chain runs on
  `stream(UpdatePlayers)` (`world_sim/extract.rs`; `ExtractinatorHelper.cs:5-525` called
  from `Player.cs:39591`/`:41665` under the `UpdatePlayers` swap, `Main.cs:17754`).
  A shimmered WorldItem's `StartSlimeRain` duration draw runs on
  `stream(UpdateItems)` (`shimmer.rs`; `WorldItem.UpdateItem` under the `UpdateItems`
  swap, `Main.cs:18024`), while the weather pass's own slime-rain check draws
  `stream(UpdateTime)` (`weather.rs`). Reforge and the other bare-`Main.rand`
  consumers (chat, ambience, char randomize) share `NamedRngs::global()`.
- **Recorded, not fixed (pre-existing modelling, follow-up rows).** The saucer's
  grouped emitter shares one roll where the C# draws per emitter; the port-side
  stand-in draws (ring dust, rubble scatter, salvo spread) keep the stream census
  without a visual consumer; the sky-spawn `Next(200)`'s `-4` arm is folded; the
  angler reward's money Г—1.5 (`Player.cs:56545`) is missing (a loot-VALUE bug, its own
  row). The deerclops/meteor-night crossing arms are dead in `update_world_tick`'s
  order (their C# `Main.cs:65123`/`:65230` gate cannot fire where the port calls it) вЂ”
  recorded as a follow-up, not re-homed here.

## Magic staves (M4-PROJ-6)

The port's caster families land in `crates/tr-app/src/projectile.rs` beside
the arrow/boomerang/bomb arms. The slot state the machines need
(`localAI`/`alpha`/`scale`) and the row defaults the spawn applies ride the
C# `SetDefaults` reset group; the dispatch arms 8/9/18/22/24/28/29/47/48/50/
129 plus the aiStyle-1 rider gate sit at `ProjectilePool::update`'s
`match data.ai_style`.

Deliberate deviations and skips (all one-line-cited in the code):
- **Dust and sound are skipped in every arm** вЂ” the pool has no dust layer
  and no sound sink; the `Main.rand`/`SoundEngine` calls inside the C# AI
  blocks are recorded per arm. The frame animations (`frameCounter`/`frame`)
  are skipped the same way: no frame fields on the slot and no frame slicing
  in the projectile draw. Both are the render/Audio follow-up.
- **The Magnet Sphere's candidate pick is the first in `Main.npc` order** вЂ”
  the C#'s `Main.rand.Next(num)` pick has no pool RNG (the determinism rule);
  identical to the vanilla for the single-candidate case the spawn usually
  sees. The rider damage/penetrate bumps (the lasers' `rand.Next` rolls) are
  skipped for the same reason.
- **AllGems2's seven-bolt branch is ported but unreachable in this
  decompilation** вЂ” only `AllGems` (the Bejeweled Staff 6171) has a writer in
  `Player.cs`, so bit 9 is never set; the initial `NextFromList` draw the
  branch's loop overwrites is therefore not consumed.
- **Wind physics runs only for the new arms** (styles 8/24/28/29, the C#'s
  `ShouldUseWindPhysics` `:22101-22124`, applied after the AI sub-steps). The
  ported arrow/bomb arms keep their pre-existing no-wind behaviour вЂ” the fix
  is behaviour-affecting and belongs to a follow-up row. `Main.windPhysics`
  is false in this decompile, so the pool's `wind_speed` defaults to inert
  and the faithful behaviour is "no wind" either way. The C#'s
  `MathHelper.Clamp` on the tail line discards its return (a no-op in the
  source) вЂ” ported as written.
- **The PVE hit test is `Damage_GetHitbox()`'s rectangle** (S1-C-8): the normal
  walk (`damage_pve`) intersects `damage_hitbox` вЂ” `Damage_GetHitbox()`
  (`Projectile.cs:14959-15023`, every kind/state inflate arm, the 301/383/262
  `localAI[0]` consume included) вЂ” with `npc.getRect()` (`:12654`), the same
  rectangle `Damage()` computes once (`:12499`). `Colliding`'s per-type overlay
  arms (the gem-staff `oldPos` sweep, types 698/973/985/1115/1116/554/301/вЂ¦, and
  the `Collision.CanHit` line tests) stay unported: those kinds read the plain
  overlap (`Colliding`'s own fallback). The resized death bursts (the gem bolts'
  AoE, the bombs' `PrepareBombToBlow`) keep the `damage_pve_boxed` walk over the
  raw resized box вЂ” against a 160 px burst the `Damage_GetHitbox` inflations are
  в‰¤ 4 px.
- **The channel reads a one-tick-old aim**: the frame runs
  `update_projectiles` before `update_editing`, so the aim the spell reads
  was written on the previous tick вЂ” the same net state as the C#, where
  `ItemCheck` precedes `UpdateWorld_Projectiles` and the owner block reads
  the previous tick's player state too.
- **The Bejeweled Staff 6171 rides `registry::ITEM_CORRECTIONS`** вЂ” the
  GenItemData placeholder band (3263-3989) still emits the zero row for it
  (the generator misses its case); the id-keyed correction is the `place_tile`
  3813 precedent. The band's other in-scope staves (3377/3779/3787) were
  fixed by the M6-SAVE-1 `itemdata.rs` regen and now ride the generated rows.
- The style-22 owner tile writes (the Ice Rod's `PlaceTile`/`KillTile`) run
  at the owner branch through `tr_core::edit`; the frozen block variant of
  the hostile 291 style-50 branch stays out (no ported row).

The batch review's three spell-arm findings (the missing
`MathHelper.Lerp(0f, 0.2f, вЂ¦)` wrap on the aim blend, the 800f target-search
default and the retarget's closest-wins loop) were fixed forward against the

## The early magic staves (S1-P-i20, 2026-11-19, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode**: written without invoking any compiler (no

(`magic_ai_tests`' `s1_p_i20_*` block) are WRITTEN, NOT RUN — each expected
value was verified by re-reading the cited C# and hand arithmetic. A
follow-up build must run `cargo test -p tr-app s1_p_i20` before merging.

**Census** — `Player.ItemCheck_Shoot` (`Player.cs:47056+`, the decompile's
name for the task's "ManageShoot magic arm") vs the port's generic shoot in
`world_sim/editing.rs`, for the nine listed early staves:

| Item | Shoot | C# arm | Port verdict |

**The channel-id fix (the WRONG):** the aiStyle-9 owner block holds the aim
only while `player.channel && player.HeldItem.shoot == this.type`
(`Projectile.cs:43241`) — the held item's **projectile** id vs the spell's own
kind. The pre-fix port stored the held **item** id in `channel_item` and
compared it to the projectile kind (`p.channel_item == self.kind`), so for the
Magic Missile (item 113, proj 16) and Flamelash (item 218, proj 34) the compare
was `113 == 16` / `218 == 34` — always false, the channel hold never fired in
the real use path (the unit fixture masked it by setting `channel_item` to the
proj id). The fix adds `Player.channel_shoot` (the held item's `shoot`, written
by the channel block in `update_editing`) and compares THAT in
`ai_magic_missile`; `channel_item` stays the item id for the Last Prism
holder's `registry::item(channel_item)` keep-alive (`Projectile.cs:66540`).

- **The Band of Starpower is an accessory**, not a staff — the task's list
  includes it, but `Item.cs:2692-2699` gives it no shoot/damage/mana, so the
  use path never fires it (`registry::is_weapon` is false). No ManageShoot arm
  exists to port; the witness pins that it fires nothing.

**The ItemTimeIsZero volley tick (the i01 census item, 2026-11-20):** the
pre-fix port fired every non-ammo shooter ONCE per swing — the spawn chain ran
only in the use-start block. The C# fires the shot from the `itemAnimation > 0
&& ItemTimeIsZero` gate (`Player.cs:43544-43570`) on EVERY tick the action timer
hits zero mid-swing, and `ItemCheck_Shoot`'s `ApplyItemTime` (`:47185-47194` →
`SetItemTime(useTime)`, `:4416-4419`) re-arms `itemTime = useTime` after EACH
shot. A `useTime < useAnimation` staff therefore fires its whole volley inside
one swing: the **Aqua Scepter** (`useTime 8 < useAnimation 16`,
`Item.cs:3252-3268`) fires 2 shots/swing (press tick + 8 ticks later), not 1.

The fix extracts the non-ammo spawn chain into a shared nested helper
`fire_non_ammo_shot` (called from the use-start block AND a new mid-swing volley
gate that mirrors the ammo fire block's tick semantics — integer counts off the
60 Hz-rounded timers via `ticks_of`, never a raw float compare). The helper
re-borrows `p = app.player.as_ref()` inside (read-only) rather than taking it as
a parameter: the chain touches only `app` fields disjoint from `app.player`
(projectiles/rngs/inventory/world/local_id), so the split borrow compiles where
a passed-in `&Player` alongside `&mut App` would be E0502. It returns whether the
aim was non-zero (the port's `dir != ZERO` gate) so the caller keeps the swing
tail gated; the swing tail (`ApplyItemAnimation`, `:51680`) stays on the
use-start path only — a mid-swing volley shot must NOT restart the swing. The
press path re-arms `item_time = useTime` after the first shot (`ApplyItemTime`);
the volley gate re-arms after each subsequent shot. Mana is paid ONCE per swing
(`ItemCheck_TryStartUse` / `ActuallyPayMana`, `:52021-52040`/`:52638`), NOT per
volley shot — the pay stays in the start block.

The volley gate carries the C# `flag`/`flag4` exclusions verbatim:
- **Coins** (`sItem.IsACoin` → `canShoot = false`, `:47103-47106`): never fire.
- **`shootsEveryUse`** (`:43560-43562`, `flag4 = ItemAnimationJustStarted`): the
  set {190, 273, 368, 674, 675, 757, 1226, 1826, 5382} fires once per use. All
  have `useTime == useAnimation`, so the exclusion is belt-and-suspenders.
- **Channel items** (the drills/chainsaws, the aimed spells, the Last Prism):
  fire once per use, then the channel holds the projectile; the C# keeps their
  `itemTime` armed via the channel/mining cadence (`toolTime`, `:43576-43587`),
  so they never reach a mid-swing re-fire. The port skips them (`d.channel`).
  None of the nine listed staves is a channel item, so this excludes no target.
- **The animation-window limits** (`:43491`/`:43502`/`:43506`/`:43514`): the
  Zenith 4956 / True Copper 5669 fire inside `useTime*3` (their `useTime =
  useAnimation/3`, so the window spans the whole swing — all 3 shots fire); the
  Fairy Queen magic 4952 / Book Staff 3852 / Daybloom 6152 inside `useTime*4`.
  The 4953 limit is the ammo path's.

**Blast radius:** among the ported `useTime < useAnimation` non-ammo shooters,
the general gate gives the Leaf Blower 1178 (5<15) and Sky Fracture 3787 (4<12)
faithful volleys they lacked. The existing Leaf Blower witnesses are all
single-tick (`fire_once`), so they are unaffected; no Sky Fracture volley test
existed. The drills/chainsaws are channel items (excluded). The gem staves,
whips and Last Prism have `useTime == useAnimation` (no mid-swing re-fire).

**The Flamelash wet gate (`Player.cs:52112-52115`):** a wet (non-lava) player
refuses the fire spells `{85, 15, 34, 1122}` — the Flamelash (shoot 34) among the
listed staves. `base.wet` is `WetCollision` (ANY liquid, `Collision.cs:1605-1645`
returns true for water/honey/shimmer); the port splits the kinds
(`player.rs:4315-4358`), so the gate reads the water/honey/shimmer union
`(p.wet || p.honey_wet || p.shimmer_wet) && !p.lava_wet`. It sits at the USE START
(`ItemCheck_CheckCanUse_Inner` via `TryStartUse`, `:52023`), after the silence
check — the mid-swing shot gate (`:43544`) does NOT re-check wet, so a player who
enters water mid-swing keeps firing until the swing ends (faithful). The refusal
returns before the mana pay and the swing start: no shot, no mana, no swing.

**The Aqua Scepter aiStyle-12 RNG-order fixes (2026-11-20):** two defects in the
new arm were corrected against `Projectile.cs:24501-24635`:
1. The scale-death early `return` was removed — the C# `Kill()` (`:24594`) does
   NOT return from `AI()`; the gravity arm (`:24596-24634`) still runs on the
   dying sub-step and its dust gates still draw. The port marks the slot dead
   and falls through (the `kill_step` movement tail runs regardless — C#
   `HandleMovement` has no `active` guard, `:17015`).
2. The lava-bounce taken branch now draws the gore-type roll `Next(61, 64)`
   (`:24583`) after the `Next(3) == 0` gate (`:24581`) — the house
   gore-type-roll convention (`ai_freaking_pirates`' `Next(580,583)`). The
   pre-fix port drew only the gate, dropping the taken branch's draw.

**Volley witnesses (WRITTEN NOT RUN):** `s1_p_i20_the_aqua_scepter_fires_a_two_shot_volley_per_swing`
(2 shots at swing ticks 16/8, one mana pay), `s1_p_i20_the_aqua_volley_rolls_crit_and_seed_per_shot`
(per-shot crit `Next(1,101)` + LCG seed `Next(0,20000)`, draw-exact stream),
`s1_p_i20_the_wet_flamelash_refuses_the_use` (water/honey/shimmer each: no shot,
no mana, no swing), `s1_p_i20_the_lava_wet_flamelash_still_fires` (the `!lavaWet`
exclusion), `s1_p_i20_the_dry_flamelash_fires_and_channels` (the control).
## The hardmode staves' use census (S1-P-i21, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

**Gate-merge reconciliation (V2, 2026-11-20):** i20's generic non-ammo
`ItemTimeIsZero` volley gate (the C#-true cadence with the coins/shootsEveryUse/
channel exclusions and the animation-window limits) supersedes i21's
HARDMODE_MAGIC_STAVES-scoped re-fire block; i21's four dedicated staff arms
(Razorpine/Blizzard/Nimbus/Bat) live inside i20's shared `fire_non_ammo_shot`
chain, so both the first shot and every mid-swing re-fire run them. The i21
volley witnesses ride the generic gate unchanged. HARDMODE_MAGIC_STAVES stays
as the census record (anchors row).

cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/dotnet/graphify). The witness tests in

NOT RUN — each expected value was verified by re-reading the cited C# and hand
arithmetic. A follow-up build must run `cargo test -p tr-app` before merging.

The six MISSING staves shared one root cause: their projectile kinds had no
`proj_data` row, so `spawn_with_data_ai` returned `None` and the staff fired
nothing. The fix lands the eight `SetDefaults` rows (the six kinds plus the
Nimbus chain's raining cloud 238 and rain drop 239), the four dedicated shoot
arms, and the projectile AIs the rows dispatch to.

Deliberate deviations (the pool-wide conventions, same as M4-PROJ-6):
- **Dust/sound skipped with their draws** — the Golden Shower's three-dust
  trail + `Next(8)` sparkle (`Projectile.cs:24522-24540`), the Blizzard's
  `Next(2)` dust (`:56949`), the bat's frame dust, the cloud's rain dust. The
  arms keep the state markers (alpha/scale/frame) so the tick order stays
  observable; the RNG streams are preserved BY CONSTRUCTION (no draw consumed
  for a skipped cosmetic).
- **The wet/shimmer gates fold dry** — the bat's wet kill (`:27294`), the rain
  drop's shimmer bounce (`:28088`), the NPC `wet` chase gate (`:27377`): the
  port carries no liquid-wet/shimmer state on the slot or the NPC, so these
  read their dry default (the M4-PROJ-6 convention).
- **The Shadowbeam's per-hit ×0.9 decay** (`:13411`) lands in `damage_pve`'s
  landed block AFTER the strike (the moon-lord 0.96 precedent): the C# switch
  runs before `StrikeNPC` but the strike reads the local `dmg` computed at
  `:12938` from the pre-decay store, so this hit keeps full damage and the next
  hit reads the decayed value — behaviour-identical.
- **The Nimbus cloud cap** (`:28058-28082`) ages out the oldest of >2 living
  raining clouds (`ai[1] = 18000`); the `netUpdate` flag is the MP bookkeeping
  the single-player port drops.
- **The bat's homing** picks the tightest-Manhattan candidate (the C#'s
  `num281 < num277` closest-wins loop, `:27382`), not the magnet sphere's
  first-candidate stand-in — the bat's C# has no RNG pick, so it is faithful.

### The i01 non-ammo volley `ItemTimeIsZero` tick (the retry round)

The census above fixed the SPAWN half (the six row-less kinds). The second
half — the fire CADENCE — was still WRONG for the non-ammo path: it fired once
per swing (`attack_cd <= 0`) and never armed `item_time`, while the C# fires
`ItemCheck_Shoot` at EVERY `itemAnimation > 0 && ItemTimeIsZero` tick
(`Player.cs:43544`'s `flag4` → `:43568-43570`), `ApplyItemTime` re-arming
`itemTime = useTime` after each shot (`:47185-47194` → `SetItemTime(useTime)`,
`:4416-4418`). A `useTime < useAnimation` staff therefore volleys inside ONE
swing; the ammo shooters already had this seam (`held_use_ammo > 0`,
`editing.rs`'s `ItemTimeIsZero` block), the non-ammo half was missing.

Of the 12 staves only TWO have `useTime < useAnimation` (the rest pace
`useTime == useAnimation`, one shot per swing, already correct):
- **GoldenShower 1336**: `useTime 6 < useAnimation 18` (`Item.cs:16545-16546`)
  → THREE streams per swing (ticks 1, 7, 13).
- **BlizzardStaff 1931**: `useTime 5 < useAnimation 10` (`Item.cs:20976-20977`)
  → TWO icicle pairs per swing (four icicles, ticks 1 and 6).

The fix (`world_sim/editing.rs`): the first-shot block now arms
`app.item_time = shooter_use_time_secs(...)` after the swing start (the
`ApplyItemTime` tail), and a new mid-swing re-fire block — gated on
`HARDMODE_MAGIC_STAVES.contains(&held.kind) && ticks_of(app.swing) > 0 &&
ticks_of(app.item_time) <= 0` — re-runs the SAME per-staff spawn chain (the
Razorpine volley, the Blizzard sky icicles, the Nimbus cursor cloud, the Bat
flock, the generic/Crystal-Storm tail) and re-arms `item_time`. The block pays
NO mana: the C# pays ONCE per swing at `ItemCheck_TryStartUse`
(`Player.cs:52026` → `ActuallyPayMana` `:52638`); the mid-swing `flag4` re-fire
calls `ItemCheck_Shoot` directly with no mana gate, so the whole volley is free
after the one pay. The crit rolls per shot on the `UpdatePlayers` stream and
the multi-shot spreads re-roll in the C#'s argument order (the re-fire is the
same `ItemCheck_Shoot` body, not a cached first shot).

Scope discipline: the re-fire is gated to the 12-staff list, so the melee
weapons, the gem staves, the Spirit Flame / Sky Fracture / Nebula Blaze and the
`useTime == useAnimation` staves keep their one-shot-per-swing cadence
unchanged (their `item_time` re-arm equals `useAnimation`, so the block never
fires mid-swing). Witnesses `s1_p_i21_the_golden_shower_volleys_three_streams_per_swing`,
`s1_p_i21_the_blizzard_volleys_two_icicle_pairs_per_swing`,
`s1_p_i21_the_crystal_storm_stays_one_shard_per_swing`,
`s1_p_i21_the_razorpine_volley_draw_order_is_per_shot` (WRITTEN NOT RUN).
## The channel machinery (S1-P-i23)

**Code-only mode**: this task was written without invoking any compiler (no
cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/dotnet/graphify). The 25 `s1_p_i23_*` witness tests
are WRITTEN, NOT RUN — each expected value was verified by re-reading the
cited C# and hand arithmetic. A follow-up build must run
`cargo test -p tr-app s1_p_i23` (plus the repointed `test_dw_4b_*`,
`test_dw_5_2_*` and `prism_rig` fixtures) before merging.

The census found the port's `Player.channel` was a per-tick button re-derive,
not the C#'s latch, and the cancel-key machinery was absent entirely. The
fixes (all RNG-neutral — no draw added, removed or reordered):

- **The channel is a LATCH** (`Player.cs:52952-52981`). Armed at the use
  start AFTER the mana pay (`StartChanneling(sItem)` inside
  `ItemCheck_StartActualUse` `:51677`); cleared on the button release
  (`ItemCheck` `:42804-42807`'s `if (!flag5) channel = false`), the buffered
  item switch (`:42800-42803` — even a switch to ANOTHER channel item drops
  it; the new item re-arms at its own use start), a CC (`:42598-42603`,
  `CCed` = frozen || webbed || stoned `:3377-3387` — the port's `cced()`
  reads buff 156 for stoned), the tracked shot's death (`TryCancelChannel`
  `:52975-52981`, the pool's `Kill` head) and the dead tick (`UpdateDead`
  `:17017`). The port hoists the release/switch/inventory clear to the
  tick head (ahead of the cursor/reach early-returns — the C# `ItemCheck`
  clears every tick regardless of cursor position); the channel block
  only REFRESHES the aim while the latch survives; the yoyo/flail
  snapshots (`world_sim/projectiles.rs`) read the latched `p.channel`, so
  a kill-cancel can drop the channel mid-hold.
- **`ChannelCancelKey`** (`Player.cs:115-141`) ported as two Player fields:
  `channel_proj_expected` (the held item's `shoot`, seeded by
  `StartChanneling(Item)` `:52963-52966`) and `channel_index_expected` (the
  pool slot of the LAST spawn of the expected type). The C# struct's index
  defaults to 0 — NOT an Option — so an untracked cache matches slot 0;
  the port keeps the same 0 default verbatim.
- **The intent-queue convention**: `NewProjectile`'s tail
  (`Projectile.cs:11097-11100`) calls `TryUpdateChannel` on every
  local-owner spawn, but the pool's slot loop cannot borrow the player.
  Both spawn seams (`spawn_with_data_ai_owned` and the raw `spawn`) push
  `(kind, slot)` onto `pending_channel_tracks`; the use-path tail
  (`world_sim/editing.rs`, same-tick tracking) and the projectile-pass tail
  (`world_sim/projectiles.rs`, the AI-side spawns) drain them through
  `apply_channel_tracks` — the `drain_mark_spawns` convention. The last
  spawn of the expected type wins (`TryTracking` `:134-140`).
- **The kill-cancel** (`Projectile.Kill`'s head `:70651-70659`):
  `try_cancel_channel` runs at the pool's per-slot death hook — the
  `owner == Main.myPlayer` gate, the `DontCancelChannelOnKill` {190}
  exemption (`ProjectileID.cs:524`, the Piranha Gun's piranha) and the
  `Matches` arms (`Player.cs:121-132`: the aiStyle-99 `ai[0] == -3`
  Magic-String ghost cancels regardless of the key; otherwise type+index).
  The out-of-world guard's direct deactivate (`Projectile.cs:16696` —
  `active = false` + `return`, NO `Kill()` call) never cancels; the port
  flags that death path (`died_out_of_world`) to keep the distinction.
- **The aiStyle-9 hold gate** (`Projectile.cs:43241`): the C# compares
  `player.HeldItem.shoot == this.type` — the held ITEM's shoot projectile
  vs the spell's kind. `channel_item` stores the held item's kind, so the
  arm resolves `registry::projectile(p.channel_item)` before the compare
  (the pre-i23 code compared the item id against the projectile id — an
  item id is never a projectile id, so the hold NEVER ran in game).
- **The homing blend** (`:43297`): `t = base.Distance(vector.Value)` is the
  projectile CENTRE to the target (`Entity.cs:195-198`), not the velocity's
  length. (The ramp itself is a C# dead-ramp quirk kept verbatim: the outer
  `GetLerpValue(200f, 20f, x)` reads x in [0,1], always below the 20f `to`,
  so the descending range returns 1 and the blend amount is the constant
  0.2 — the witness pins the exact `Lerp((4,0),(32,0),0.2) = (9.6,0)`.)
- **The idle rotation** (`:43358`): `rotation.AngleLerp(0f, 0.2f)`
  (`Utils.cs:2033-2051`) — the shortest-way 20% ANGULAR lerp, not a 0.2*pi
  max-step turn (`angle_towards`). The port's `angle_lerp` helper carries
  the XNA `WrapAngle` form.
- **The Last Prism interval pay** (`:66612-66613` -> `CheckMana(mana, pay:
  true)` `Player.cs:52576-52586`): the pay scales `(int)(item.mana *
  manaCost)` — the armor/accessory multiplier the use path already folds.
  Folds (no port fields): the `manaFlower` quick-mana retry (`:52588-52609`)
  and the `DebugOptions.ManaV2` cast-at-zero arms (`:52602-52615`) — the
  plain `statMana >= num` compare stands; the prism gate's `!player.noItems`
  term (`:66614`) has no port field either (the flail kill gate's same fold,
  `:43727`).
- **`LimitPointToPlayerReachableArea`** (`Player.cs:45447-45473`) rewritten
  verbatim: `Utils.CenteredRectangle(Center, MaxWorldViewSize)`
  (`Utils.cs:947-950` — the `(int)` corner truncation, the size stays
  1920x1200) clamped by `WorldUtils.ClampToWorldBorders`
  (`WorldBuilding/WorldUtils.cs:24-31` -> `Utils.Clamp(Rectangle, Rectangle)`
  `Utils.cs:236-239`): the TOP-LEFT slides inside the 640-px-inset play
  area (`GetWorldPlayArea` `:16-22`) while the box KEEPS its size — on a
  world smaller than the view the clamp's max < min and `Utils.Clamp<T>`
  (`:223-234`, max FIRST) returns the max, so the box hangs off the far
  edge exactly as the C#'s does. The centre is XNA's int `X + Width/2`.
  The pre-i23 helper shrank the box to the world and centred on floats.
- **The yoyo release** (`Projectile.cs:67920-67925`): `!channel || CCed`
  drops the aim to -1 — the CCed arm rides the new `YoyoInputs.player_cced`
  snapshot (the pre-i23 port stubbed it false). The flail kill gate's CCed
  term (`:43727`) already rode `FlailInputs.player_cced`.
- **The toolTime hold guard** (`Player.cs:43576-43587`): the port's
  swing-hold stand-in for the projectile-less channel items now requires
  the LATCHED `p.channel` — the per-tick button re-derive would resurrect
  a kill-cancelled channel.

Deliberate folds (recorded, all cited in the code):
- **The projectile-less channel items keep a per-tick arm**: the mounts'
  `StartChanneling()` parameterless overload (`Player.cs:52941`, no cancel
  key) fires from the mount-use path the port has not ported; the port's
  use path only arms the WEAPON channel at the shot start, so the
  `!held_weapon` family (the mounts, the fairy bell — the items with no
  `projectile` row) keeps its pre-i23 per-tick arm in the third else-if of
  the channel block. The latch's clear paths (release/CC/switch/death)
  still apply to it.
- **The aim is a one-tick-old snapshot** (the M4-PROJ-6 deviation above,
  unchanged): the use start seeds `channel_target` with the clamped cursor
  so the spawn tick already carries it; the refresh block re-clamps on the
  following ticks.
- **The `Matches` ghost arm reads `proj_data(kind).ai_style == 99`**: the
  C# reads the live `projectile.aiStyle`; the port's row table is the same
  value for every rowed kind (the yoyo family). A rowless aiStyle-99 kind
  cannot spawn through the data seam, so the read is equivalent.
- **Census note (out of scope)**: the port's `channel` item flags match the
  C# (`itemdata.rs` vs `Item.cs` — RainbowRod 495 shoot 79 channel;
  VortexBeater 3475 shoot 615 channel (`Item.cs:31175`); LaserMachinegun
  2795 shoot 439 mana 6 channel; 726 FrostStaff / NimbusRod / MagnetSphere /
  Shadowbeam NOT channel). The AI_075 channel kinds 439/445/460/595/735/927
  etc. are rowless in the port (their per-stave spawn params belong to the
  i20-i22 rows); the machinery here serves every kind once rowed.
- **Census fold (ammo shooters)**: the C# `ItemCheck_StartActualUse` calls
  `StartChanneling(sItem)` for EVERY item (`:51677`), including the
  `useAmmo` guns; the port's use-start arm rides the generic (non-ammo)
  shoot path only, so the channel guns (Vortex Beater 3475, Phantasm 3540,
  Celeb2 3930, DD2 Phoenix Bow 3854) do not arm the latch through the
  separate ammo-shooter arm. Their gunProj rockets (615/630/705/714) carry
  aiStyle 75, which the port's dispatch currently routes through the
  `ai_last_prism` stand-in (the per-gun AI_075 arms are unported — the
  i20-i22 rows); that stand-in reads `p.channel`, so the guns' channel
  behaviour is already coupled to the prism stand-in, not to a faithful
  gun arm. Wiring `StartChanneling` into the shared shooter arm and the
  real per-gun AI_075 arms belong to those rows, not this machinery slice.

## .trwld v6 вЂ” the world flags, wires and tile entities (M6-SAVE-1) (re-landed)

Re-landed: the `M5-CHEST-gen-flag-extras` merge (`07d786ab`) dropped this work from
main with its merge resolution. The section and its code are restored verbatim here;
the v7 chest section builds on it.

The native `.trwld` (`crates/tr-core/src/save.rs`) grew these sections after the v5
bed-spawn byte. They landed as the v6 tail (`VERSION` 5 в†’ 6), but a later merge
dropped them and claimed the v6 slot for the secret-seed flags; the re-landed
sections therefore ride the v7 gate (`VERSION` 7 вЂ” the seeds u16 at v6, then the
flags block, the wires and the tile entities at v7, the chests behind them).
Before them the three state groups were simply dropped by the save: the recorded gaps were the wires
("Persistence in `.trwld`/`.map` is pending", the "Wiring engine (M7-WIRE-1)"
deviations), the tile entities ("Persistence in `.trwld`/`.map` is pending
(M6-SAVE-1)", the "Tile entities (M7-TE-1)" deviations) and the `SaveWorldFlags`
progression fields вЂ” the world's `downed_*`/invasion/hardmode state only ever
survived until the next reload, and `unlocked_slime_rainbow_spawn` had no save
slot at all (the "Shimmer transforms (M7-SHIMMER-1)" note). Each group rides its
own version gate, so a v5 (or older) file still loads, with the `World::new`
defaults standing in exactly as they do for the v3/v4/v5 tails.

**1. The world flags block** вЂ” `save.rs::write_flags_v6`/`read_flags_v6`: a fixed
**108 bytes** = two 16-byte bool groups + 14 i32s + 2 f64s + 1 f32 (the second
group's last byte is a reserved 0 that keeps both groups 16 bytes; a back-compat
test truncates exactly `V6_FLAGS_LEN` bytes). It carries the port's `World`
fields that the C# `SaveWorldFlags` persists (`WorldFile.cs:1238-1430`), grouped
with the C#'s own line citations:

- bool group A (16): `_tempBloodMoon`/`_tempEclipse` (`:1277-1278`), the
  downed-boss ladder (`:1282-1294` вЂ” Boss1/2/3, QueenBee, MechBoss1/2/3,
  PlantBoss, GolemBoss, SlimeKing, savedGoblin; the port has no
  MechBossAny/savedWizard/savedMech state, so those slots are not written),
  `downedGoblins`/`downedFrost`/`downedPirates` (`:1296-1299`).
- bool group B (15 + the reserved byte): `shadowOrbSmashed`/`spawnMeteor`/
  `hardMode` (`:1300-1304`), the DD2 event flags (`DD2Event.Save`,
  `DD2Event.cs:151-156`), `downedMoonlord` (`:1346`), `TowerActive*`
  (`:1357-1360`) and `downedTower*` (`:1352-1355`).
- the i32 block: `shadowOrbCount`/`altarCount` (`:1302-1303`), the invasion state
  (`invasionDelay`/`invasionSize`/`invasionType` `:1306-1309` +
  `invasionSizeStart` `:1339`), the four tower shields,
  `lunar_shield_power_normal`, and the port-only slime-rain/DD2 counters; the
  two f64s `invasionX` and `slimeRainTime` (`:1309-1310`) and the f32
  `dd2_wave_kills`.

**2. The wire side table** вЂ” `World.wires` (`wiring.rs::WireState::write`/`read`):
per colour вЂ” the `WireColor` declaration order Red/Blue/Green/Yellow, which is
also `TripWire`'s four sequential pass order (`Wiring.cs:525`) вЂ” a u32 cell count
then the (i32, i32) pairs **sorted by (x, y)** (`HashSet` order is unstable, the
file bytes must not be). The C# has no wire section at all: the four colours ride
per-tile `sTileHeader` bits packed into the tile stream (`Tile.cs:623-657`) and
the port's 12-byte `Tile` has no header space, so the side table needs its own
section вЂ” a port-native shape, recorded as a deviation.

**3. The tile entities** вЂ” `World.tile_entities`
(`tile_entities.rs::{TileEntity::write/read, TeData::write/read(r, kind),
TileEntities::write_all/read_all(r, world)}`): a u32 count, then per record a
u8 kind, a u32 id, an i16 x/y pair and the per-kind payload вЂ” `TileEntity.Write`/
`Read` (`TileEntity.cs:173-207`, the `WriteInner` half of the save path: the id
rides, the network send omits it) plus the world-file section
`SaveTileEntities`/`LoadTileEntities` (`WorldFile.cs:3302-3357`), including the
load-side re-validation: a record whose cell left the world (`WorldGen.InWorld`,
`:3334`) or whose `CheckValidTile` frame test fails (`:3338`) is dropped, the
payload emptied. `TeData::write`/`read(r, kind)` mirror `WriteExtraData`/
`ReadExtraData` per kind вЂ” the item triple `short type, byte prefix, short stack`
behind the port's presence byte (`TEItemFrame.cs:47-56`), the HatRack
presence-bitsByte (`TEHatRack.cs:59-80`), the dummy's `npc`
(`TETrainingDummy.cs:119-126`) and the sensor's `logicCheck`/`On`
(`TELogicSensor.cs:380-396`).

Deviations and notes:

- **The format is the port's own, not the C#'s 11-section pointer table.** The
  `.wld` writer emits an `i16 sectionCount` + `i32 sectionPointers[]` index that
  the reader then walks; `.trwld` appends each new group in order behind its
  version gate, so a format bump is one new tail and old files keep loading. All
  three groups are port-native sections even where the C# folds them into another
  stream вЂ” the flags into a flat `BinaryWriter` walk with no section markers at
  all, the wires into the per-tile header bits.
- **Port-only persisted state**: the slime-rain flag and kill counter
  (`slime_rain`/`slime_rain_kills` вЂ” the C# writes only `slimeRainTime` and
  derives the rest on load), the DD2 wave counters (`dd2_wave`, `dd2_spawn_hold`,
  `dd2_wave_kills`), and the tower shields (`tower_shield_*`,
  `lunar_shield_power_normal`) as live values вЂ” the C# restores the four tower
  shields from `ShieldStrengthTowerMax` on the load side
  (`WorldFile.cs:2237-2249`), so saving and restoring the numbers is a different
  contract rather than a port of it.
- **Deliberate widenings on the TE record**: the dummy's npc int16 в†’ i32 (the
  port keeps the tie as the NPC slot) and the logic sensor's `counted` grace
  (`CountedData`, runtime-only in the C#) is persisted so a load restores the LED
  state exactly.
- **The port keeps the stored TE ids** instead of reassigning them on load (the
  C# does `tileEntity.ID = num2++` and then sets `TileEntitiesNextID`,
  `WorldFile.cs:3323`/`:3330`), so a save round-trips them and `next_id` runs to
  `max(id) + 1`; a duplicated cell keeps the `place`/`place_unchecked` insert
  semantics (the last record is the one the position book reaches) and a repeated
  id in a hand-written file keeps the first record and drops the rest.
- **The runtime-only fields stay out**: the WoF/Golem/boss write-through anchors
  (`wof_*`, `golem_*`, `skeletron_*`, `brain_*`, `prime_*` вЂ” live boss-encounter
  state the C# rebuilds on spawn), `travel_shop`, and the App-side weather block
  (`_tempRaining`/`_tempRainTime`/`_tempMaxRain`, `:1312-1314`), which stays in
  the app layer until the load-side weather block is ported. The C# seed-flavour
  pair (`vampireSeed`/`infectedSeed` and the `Main.*Seed` family) and the saved
  NPC/bought-pet writes have no port fields either.
- **Verification**: `save.rs`'s `dw_2_1_the_v6_flags_wires_and_tes_round_trip`
  (one flag from every group + the counters + the four wire colours + the
  dummy/frame/sensor/pylon payloads), `dw_2_1_a_v5_payload_loads_defaults` (the
  old file keeps the defaults), `dw_2_1_a_truncated_v6_tail_bails` and
  `dw_2_1_the_wire_and_te_sections_are_deterministic` (byte-identical re-writes),
  plus the updated version-gate tests. `tile_entities.rs` adds 5 (the round-trip
  with the `write_all` layout pin, the invalid-cell drops, the unknown-kind
  refusal, the duplicate-cell semantics); `wiring.rs` adds 3 (the round-trip over
  every colour, determinism, the truncated read). Full suite: 2327 passed /
  0 failed (`cargo test --workspace -- --skip migrates_version_2_kinds_to_item_ids`).

Out:

- the **chests** вЂ” the App-side `App.world_chests` store is re-rolled at load by
  `chest_gen` (the `M5-CHEST-gen` row's documented conflict: the generator and the
  saved contents disagree), so the section needs both a save path and a load gate;
- the **signs** вЂ” the port has no sign store at all;
- the **NPCs/homes/names** вЂ” the NPCs live App-side (`App.npcs`) with `Npc.home`
  in memory (the `M4-TOWN-1` recorded note), so the section follows the NPC
  persistence;
- the **bestiary kill pairs** вЂ” today they ride the `.trplayer` sidecar v5
  (`bestiary.rs::KillTracker`), while vanilla keeps them in the world file
  (section 11), so moving them means a world-side field;
- the **banner counts** вЂ” `banners.rs` is a runtime tally with no save;
- **SavedOreTiers** вЂ” the worldgen-local `ores.rs` struct needs a `World` field
  first (the "OresAndShinies fidelity (M5-ORES-1)" note records the gap), and the
  vanilla quartet has no port representation yet;
- the **angler quest state** вЂ” `Main.anglerQuest`/`anglerWhoFinishedToday` have no
  port fields (`fishing.rs` carries the mechanics only);
- the **TownManager rooms** вЂ” the room store follows the housing/persistence work;
- the **weighted pressure plates** вЂ” no port store for the pressed-plate state;
- the **creative powers/research** вЂ” `M6-CREATIVE-1/2`'s per-player state has no
  persistence yet.

Each is its own scope; none is implied by this tail.

## .trwld v7 вЂ” the world chests (M6-SAVE-1b)

The chest section rides the store's data as neutral records (`tr_core::save::ChestItem` /
`ChestRecord` вЂ” the crate cannot see `App`): a `u32` count, then per chest `i32 x`,
`i32 y`, the name (`u32` length + UTF-8 вЂ” the file's own string convention) and a
`u32` slot count, then per slot `i32 stack` and, while the stack is non-zero, `u16
kind` + `u8 prefix`. The C# shape is `SaveChests` (`WorldFile.cs:1606-1676`) / `LoadChests`
(`:2723-2805`).

- **The deviations.** The vanilla always writes `maxItems` slots (40) and a 7-bit
  length string, and its load re-assigns ids; the port keeps its implicit-air
  compressed vec (a `stack == 0` entry is an empty slot, trailing airs dropped вЂ” the
  store materializes the 40 on open), its own string encoding, and the record's
  anchor is the identity. The stack is `i32` where the C# writes `int16` (the vanilla
  9999 cap fits, the port's `u32` counts saturate on write). The 8000 cap is not
  written: the port's store already refuses past `MAX_CHESTS` (`chest.rs:40`).
- **The app wiring.** `save_world` serializes `App.world_chests` вЂ” removed entries
  skipped, the effective name from `chest::chest_name` (the rename or the derived
  default), the slots mapped through `registry::name`. `App::new` takes the records,
  `chest_gen::store_from_records` culls the stale anchors (the vanilla's pre-count
  validity sweep) and maps the slots, and the records seed `merge_store` ahead of the
  `TR_CHEST` fixture вЂ” **the saved contents win over the chest-gen re-roll**, so a
  player's stock survives the reload; the names ride `chest_names` by the post-merge
  index (`find_chest` on the anchor). The autosave (10 s), F9 and quit write the
  section; the MP world transfer does not carry chests (the tile sections do).
- **The recorded gap, fixed 2026-11-09 (`fix-chest-frame-important`).**
  `boot_statics` had never set the chest family's bits while the vanilla does
  (`Main.cs:7655-7659`: the sapling 20, the chest 21, the 467/441/468 container kinds),
  so `frame_world` re-framed every chest tile through its object def вЂ” the 2x2 anchor
  frames were lost and the anchor scans missed every chest in a loaded world (the roll
  only fired in a freshly generated, unframed one). The bits now ride the boot statics
  beside the other family groups; the test pins the survival with a control arm (the
  same world with the bit cleared loses the anchor).
- Tests: `dw_2_2_the_chests_round_trip_in_v7` (names, interior airs, the prefixes),
  `dw_2_2_a_v6_payload_loads_no_chests`, `dw_2_2_a_truncated_chest_section_bails`,
  `dw_2_2_the_chest_section_is_deterministic`, and the app pair
  `dw_2_2_a_saved_chest_round_trips_through_the_app` (contents/prefix/name survive,
  the no-roll-overwrite control) / `dw_2_2_a_record_with_a_missing_anchor_is_dropped`
  (the cull). Suite 2409 / 0.

Out: the remaining C# sections вЂ” signs (no port store), the NPC block (names/homes/
homeless, App-side `App.npcs`), the bestiary kill pairs (today the `.trplayer` sidecar
v5; moving them into the world file), the banner counts, `SavedOreTiers`
(worldgen-local вЂ” needs a `World` field), the angler quest state (no port fields),
the TownManager rooms, the weighted pressure plates (no port store) and the creative
powers/research вЂ” each needs its own scope.

## The achievements menu + the 137-row registry (M6-ACH-2)

- **The registry is one initializer, three passes.** `AchievementInitializer.Load`
  (`:13-441`) constructs 137 `Achievement` objects (`Achievement.Id` is the
  construction counter), then `RegisterIconIndex` (`:445-582`) assigns the icon
  frame each row draws from `Images/UI/Achievements` and
  `RegisterAchievementCategory` (`:584-736`) the filter category. The port keeps
  all three as one `Row` table (`achievements_data.rs`) so the icon order and the
  `Id` order can never drift (they differ: `BENCHED` is constructed 2nd but
  carries icon 88).
- **One condition can list many ids.** `NPCKilledCondition.Create(13, 14, 15)`
  is a *single* condition named `NPC_KILLED_13` that completes on **any** of the
  three (`NPCKilledCondition.cs:20-30`, the `_listeners` fan-out). The port's
  `CondKind` therefore splits into the single-id event variants and the `вЂ¦Any`
  multi-id stored variants, with `matches_kind` doing the membership test. The
  pre-M6-ACH-2 registry modelled these as one condition per id (all-of), which
  is not the vanilla behaviour.
- **`ItemCraftCondition` reuses the `ITEM_PICKUP_` name prefix**
  (`ItemCraftCondition.cs:8`), so a craft condition and a pickup condition in the
  same achievement would collide on `Achievement._conditions`' dictionary key.
  No shipped row does (each row's first ids differ), which the
  `every_row_carries_a_distinct_condition_key` test pins.
- **`CreateMany` rows are now 1:1 (S1-E-18).** The four lossy rows are expanded
  to the full 180 conditions (`NPCKilledCondition.CreateMany` в†’ one condition per
  id, `NPCKilledCondition.cs:70-79`): `STAR_DESTROYER` 4, `BUCKETS_OF_BOLTS` 3,
  `GELATIN_WORLD_TOUR` 24, `SLAYER_OF_WORLDS` 15 (preserving folded groups where
  the C# does). `STAR_DESTROYER` is therefore no longer vacuously complete.
- **The category filter cannot name the `None` row.** Vanilla's `FilterList`
  indexes `_categoryButtons[(int)achievement.Category]`, and
  `GAIN_TORCH_GODS_FAVOR` is the one row `RegisterAchievementCategory` never
  touches (`AchievementCategory.None = -1`) вЂ” the C# would throw an
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` on a filter click. The port keeps the secret row
  visible in every filtered view instead of crashing (documented deviation).
- **Save path and persistence (S1-E-18).** The port still uses its own
  `achievements.trdat` text format (not the vanilla Rijndael-CBC+BSON
  `"RELOGIC-TERRARIA"` blob) вЂ” writing the vanilla format would touch a real
  install's `achievements.dat`. The path is bound at bootstrap / world swap
  (`App::bind_achievements_save_path`, `app/saveglue.rs`) so headless test apps
  never write a real file; `save()` fires on achievement completion and from
  `save_world`. `load_pairs` resets `Condition.frac` to 0 because the text
  format stores only the whole `value` (a `CustomFloat` sub-unit fraction is
  in-memory only until saved). `notify` persists on completion and returns only
  the last completed achievement name (the caller-facing shape), but since
  S1-E-26 wave A **every** completing row fires: `notify_with` queues each one
  into `AchievementManager.completed_events` (Save + event per row,
  `AchievementManager.cs:180-187`), and `App::drain_achievement_completions`
  consumes the queue once per frame.
- **Notify sites (S1-E-18, partial).** `notify_with` applies the C# `Value`-setter
  semantics (clamp `[0,max]`, complete at `max`) with wrappers for progression,
  custom flag/int/float. Wired sites: progression 1/3/5/6/8/9/16, altar smash
  (break + `SmashAltar` + BEGONE_EVIL, `Player.cs:45665-45704` /
  `WorldGen.cs:49107-49108`), town arrival (`WorldGen.cs:5576`), WoF
  (`WorldGen.cs:31701-31712`, guarded by `!hard_mode`), King Slime slime-rain
  stop (`NPC.cs:79405-79410`), angler `Finish` flag+int (`Main.cs:40260`,
  `AchievementsHelper.cs:411-418`), acorn plant `Do` (`Player.cs:40139`), Shadow
  chest `Peek` (`Player.cs:33243-33246`), grounded running `Move`
  (`Player.cs:28233-28236`). `StopSlimeRain` sets the negative cooldown clock
  (`Main.cs:64787-64820`). **Blocked/unported (2026-11-12 snapshot; the W4-c36
  re-probe reconciles it in research/30):** progression 29 BOOK_WORM's hook
  FIRES (S1-E-18p29) and the S1-F-15 denominator bug is FIXED — the residual
  gate is the town/critter provider fold (c37); nurse `Pay`
  (`Main.cs:40110`) landed via S1-E-18-nurse-pay; IT_CAN_TALK 18 (no Truffle
  kind 160 ON THIS BASE — the NOTIFY-SYNC update: the kind IS on d120
  `4b17a2cf1`, the arrival notify hunk published in research/30),
  REAL_ESTATE_AGENT 17 partial (missing 178/229/209/160 on this base — 107 and
  550 ARE ported; NOTIFY-SYNC: all four now on d120/d37 tips, the roster
  activates at their merge), DUNGEON_HEIST 19 / BIG_BOOTY 20 landed via
  S1-E-18b-chest-progress; most other progression/CustomFlag rows lack
  owning systems. `tile_drop` returns `None` for altar 26 (C# empty drop group)
  to avoid leaking the Journey altar item. **NOTIFY-SYNC (W4-c36, second
  pass 2026-11-21):** TRAINING_DAY 40 + NEW_DIGS 43 are WIRED LIVE on
  g90b `b3b82d071` / f47 `a2561d6d9` — c36's owed rows retired (the
  keep-one contracts + the published b3/d20b/d120 hunks live in
  research/30 NOTIFY-SYNC (1)-(4)). **RETIRE FINAL (W4-c36, 2026-11-21):**
  EXTRA_LIFE 35 joins the retired rows — c46 `2802ed5b9` wires it live
  (`death.rs:527`); the FINAL no-path census is 17 rows (research/30

- **Notify sites, first batch (W4-c36, 2026-11-21).** The row-targeted
  `AchievementManager::complete_condition(row, cond)` primitive ports
  `GetCondition(row, conditionName).Complete()` (`AchievementManager.cs:220-227`,

## The achievement unlock popup (S1-E-26 wave A)

The completion в†’ toast chain is ported: `AchievementManager.AchievementCompleted`
(`AchievementManager.cs:180-187`) в†’ `OnAchievementCompleted` в†’
`InGameNotificationsTracker.AddCompleted` (`UI/InGameNotificationsTracker.cs:75-81`,
the `netMode != 2` gate) в†’ `AchievementUnlockedPopup` (`UI/InGamePopups.cs:13-148`).
The port's event seam is `AchievementManager.completed_events` (one entry per
completing row, registry order вЂ” the old "only the last completion" divergence is
fixed); `App::drain_achievement_completions` (`app/mod.rs`) runs the two
subscribers once per frame after the update branch:

- the popup (`ui/notifications.rs`): the 300-tick timer (`Update`, `:80-87`),
  the `Scale`/`Opacity` curves (`:39-66` вЂ” the timer counts DOWN, so the
  `> 285` arm is the 15-tick fade-in and `< 30` the 30-tick fade-out), the
  `(MeasureString + (58, 10)) * Scale * 1.1` plate (`:100-102`), the icon +
  border at `num * 0.3` scale with the `(0, 32)` / `(4, h/2)` origins
  (`:106-108`), the `mouseTextColor` title at anchor `(1, 0.4)` (`:109`) and
  the `50 * Opacity` anchor push (`:89-93`). The tracker walk
  (`DrawInGame`, `InGameNotificationsTracker.cs:38-55`) starts at
  `(screenWidth/2, screenHeight - 40)` and breaks below `-100`.
- the chat + sound subscriber (`AchievementInitializer.cs:728-735`): the
  `Achievements.Completed` line with the `[a:NAME]` tag
  (`AchievementTagHandler.GenerateTag`) through `Main.NewText` (white +
  `PlaySound(12)`), then the tracked `SoundID.AchievementComplete`
  (`SoundID.cs:1597`, cue `achievement_complete`) behind the
  `FindActiveSound == null` guard.

The popup click (`OnMouseOver`, `:117-142`) consumes the left-release edge
(`App.ui_left_release`), opens the achievements overlay and scrolls to the row
(`IngameFancyUI.OpenAchievementsAndGoto` в†’ `UIList.Goto`'s
`ViewPosition = item.Top.Pixels`, `App::open_achievements_and_goto`). The
update tick rides `frame()` before the world branch (`Main.cs:17045` вЂ” menus
included, capture-frozen); the draw rides after the achievements overlay
(`DrawInterface_13`, `Main.cs:44779-44783`); `SaveAndQuit` clears the tracker
(`WorldGen.cs:6714`).

**Deviations:** the join-request popup (`PlayerWantsToJoinGamePopup`) and the
notifications-area draw (`DrawInIngameOptions`) are unported (no social join
flow); the gamepad anchor drop (`-25f`) and the `IgnoreMouseInterface` /
`mouseInterface` gates have no port counterpart (the buff-bar hover's
documented gap); an expired popup stays in the list at opacity 0 until
`Clear` вЂ” the vanilla quirk (`ShouldBeRemoved` only rides the click, `:141`),
kept 1:1; the menu-twin draw site (`Main.cs:48457`) is unreachable in the port
because the drain runs on the world branch and `SaveAndQuit` clears the list;
the chat line prints the raw `[a:NAME]` tag (the port's chat carries no
snippet markup yet, `chat.rs`); the popup's `gameMenu && menuMode == 0` click
gate is moot for the same reason.

The emote UI was already ported end-to-end before this wave (M6-EMOTE-1,

against `EmoteBubble.cs`, `UIEmotesMenu.cs`, `EmoteButton.cs`,

  (`EmoteBubble.cs:204-205`): `lifeTime < 6 || lifeTimeStart - lifeTime < 6`
  draws the closed shell (column 0) only; otherwise column 1. Over the

  `emote*2%8 + frame`, row `1 + emote/4`. The sheet is 8 columns Г—
  `SHEET_ROWS = 2 + (151-1)/4 = 39` rows (`:1071`, `EmoteID.Count = 151`
  `EmoteID.cs:317`); `Utils.Frame` integer division gives 34Г—28 frames on
  the 272Г—1092 `Extra_48` sheet.
- `bubble_unflips` вЂ” the 87/89 confused/sleep un-flip (`:220-224`): only
  those two ids clear the horizontal flip and shift 4 px right, applied to
  the emote sprite after the shell drew with the original flip.

  ticks the lifetimes in `world_sim/npcs.rs` (`app.emotes.update_all()`):

  `GameViewMatrix.ZoomMatrix`) + the `UIEmotesMenu` state ride

  bottom-centre origin (`:206`), floor (`:203`), camera/zoom transform.
- **input** вЂ” the wheel opens from `DrawEmoteBubblesButton`'s click

## The pillar worms (M4-EVENT-14)

The Crawltipede (412/413/414) is the Solar tower's worm: the head
`ai[3] = whoAmI` + `realLife = whoAmI` (`:51369-51392`), `num34 = 30`
segments, `num36 = 413` swapped to `414` at index 29, each segment
linking forward (`ai[0]`) and back (`ai[1]`), `CopyInterrelations` from
its predecessor. The port's worm pass carries the same shape (`worm_id`,
`seg_index`, `worm_left`), so the chain rides it with the crawltipede's
30-segment budget and the 10/0.3 steering pair. The death guards kill a
segment whose link died (`!Main.npc[ai[1]].active || aiStyle mismatch` в†’
`life = 0; HitEffect(); checkDead()`), and the body/tail don't count for
the enemy cap (`dontCountMe`) while the tail takes Г—10 damage
(`takenDamageMultiplier = 10`, consumed in `StrikeNPC_Inner`).

The StardustWormHead (402) is a lone mega-worm (no segments in this
build вЂ” 403/404 have no `SetDefaults` rows) whose aiStyle-6 arm
(`:51030-51073`) runs the 600-tick cycle: `ai[2]++`, the
`Remap(ai[2], 285, 570, 1, 0.5)` deceleration while `ai[2] <= 570`, the
mark fire at 570 (`SpawnStardustMark_StardustWorm`) with the velocity
re-normalised to 6, and the reset at 600. Its own movement pair is
`num45 = 9` / `num46 = 0.3` (`:51740-51743`).

`SpawnStardustMark_StardustWorm` (`:43909-43993`) picks from the list
405/402/407 (capped at 2 / 3 / 1 alive) and throws the 540 marker
projectile with `ai[0] = -num5 * 10f` and `ai[1] = 0.5..1.0f` which
spawns the chosen NPC on its way; the port folds the hop into the sim's
resolve (`wants_stardust_mark`) because the 540 projectile AI is not
ported.

Deviations: the dust arms, the ground-avoidance tile scan
(`:51784-51798`) and the same-type repulsion of the crawltipede are
unmodelled (the port's worm pass has its own steering), the 540
projectile hop and the mark's 3-5 chain-length roll are unmodelled.

## Minions & sentries (M4-PROJ-8)

The summon system's harness: the per-player slot budget (`maxMinions`/`numMinions`/
`slotsMinions`, `Player.cs:1260-1264`), the keep-alive buff arms, `AI_062`'s
follow/target/return machine and the sentry cap/lifetime/targeting.

### The minion summon use-path (S1-P-i25, code-only 2026-11-20)

The summon-staff USE machinery (`Player.ItemCheck_Shoot`'s minion arms + the
budget/sacrifice/buff chain), audited distrust-verbatim against the C# and
gap-filled. Verdicts + cites:

- **The summon spawn arm was MISSING** — summon staves fell through to the generic
  `Item.shoot` flight (player-centre spawn, aim velocity, class-multiplied damage).
  The C# spawns minions via `SpawnMinionOnCursor` (`Player.cs:49573-49603`): the
  CURSOR point clamped by `LimitPointToPlayerReachableArea` (`:45447-45473`), ZERO
  velocity, the UNSCALED `sItem.damage` as both `Damage` and `originalDamage`
  (`:49600-49601` — the pool applies `minionDamage` at `Projectile.cs:16707`), and
  `GetWeaponKnockback`'s `minionKB` add (`:47151`/`:53348-53351`). Now ported as the
  first branch of `update_editing`'s spawn chain (`world_sim/editing.rs`), gated
  `def.summon && proj_data(proj).minion`. The per-item arms: Pygmy 1157
  (`Next(191,195)` pick + ai1=60 + `localAI[0]=30`, `:48436-48440`/`:49584`), Optic
  2535 (both twins 387+388, zero `RotatedBy` velocity, ai1=1, `:48468-48474`),
  Spider 2551 (`nextCycledSpiderMinionType` mod-3 cycle 390/391/392, `:48476-48481`,
  the field never reset — `Player.cs:1280`), Pirate 2584 (`Next(3)` offset,
  `:48483-48486`), Foxsparks 5664/6149 (`localAI[0]=30`, `:48452-48456`), the ai1=1
  seed for 2364/2365/2621/2749/3474 and ai0=45 for 6164 (`:49587-49596`). The
  Stardust Dragon 3531 chain spawn (`:48498-48554`) stays deferred with the
  aiStyle-121 chain (the 625-628 rows book slots, the chain AI is a follow-up).
- **`FreeUpPetsAndMinions` was WRONG on three counts** (`Player.cs:51701-51851`),
  fixed in `projectile.rs::free_up_pets_and_minions`: (1) the sacrifice sort is
  ASCENDING `minionSlots` (the C# insertion at `:51736-51747` inserts before the
  first strictly-larger entry), not descending — the kill walk eats the SMALLEST
  slots first; (2) the sacrificable arm `return`s at `:51830`, so the same-kind
  outright-kill tail (`:51832-51850`) NEVER runs for a sacrificable staff (it is
  the sentry/pet refresh); (3) the tail's 5131 special keys on `sItem.type`
  (`:51845`), not `shoot` — the fn now takes `staff_item`. The list also includes
  ALL owned minions (no per-kind filter, `:51731`) and `num` counts the dragon
  kinds the removal pass drops.
- **The free-up call gate was WRONG** — the port called it for every `shoot > 0`;
  the C# gates on `LightPet[shoot] || Main.projPet[shoot]` (`Player.cs:42778`). The
  sentry staves' shoot kinds are in NEITHER set, so the C# never frees for them.
  Added `PROJ_PET` (`Main.cs:8728-8852`) + `LIGHT_PET_PROJ` (`ProjectileID.cs:523`)
  verbatim tables and the gate.
- **The slot block excluded the wrong dragon kinds** — `Projectile.cs:16709` is
  `type != 625 && type != 628` (the HEAD/TAIL carry no slot block); the port
  excluded 626/627 (the BODY segments, 0.5 slots each) — the inverse. Fixed in
  `summon_tick_block`; the bodies now book, the head/tail never double-book.
- **The minion-buff PERSISTENCE grant was MISSING** — the port granted only the
  `:42880` `item.buffTime` (0 for the staves, a ghost). The C#'s
  `ItemCheck_ApplyPetBuffs` (`Player.cs:42766` → `:53190-53281`) grants
  `AddBuff(sItem.buffType, 3600)` at the use-start for the 28 summon-staff item
  types; THAT 3600 buff is what the keep-alive arm's 18000 refresh pins while the
  minion lives. Added `MINION_STAFF_PET_BUFF_ITEMS` + the grant. (This SUPERSEDES
  the "0-time grant is a ghost" note below for the summon staves — the ghost was
  the missing 3600 grant, not an inherent C# behaviour.)
- **The maxMinions cap set-bonuses were MISSING** — `HallowedSummoner`
  (`ArmorSetBonuses.cs:225-229`, `maxMinions += 2`, the 8 cartesian triples of
  4873/4899 × 551/4900 × 552/4901) and `ChlorophyteSummon` (`:134-139`,
  `maxMinions += 2`, the 5524/1004/1005 triple) added to `tr_core::armor_sets`
  `SET_STATS`. The per-piece rows (`grant_summon_caps`, `Player.cs:13254-13948`/
  `:15324-15329`) and the buff cap effects (110/150, `:10173-10180`) were already
  faithful.
- **The missing minion `proj_data` rows** — the slot-counting needs every summon
  staff's minion kind to carry its `SetDefaults` slice; 191-194/317/390-392/755/
  831/864/946/951/970/1022/1093/1094/1112/1113/1118/1119/625-628 were absent (the
  staves' spawns declined). Added verbatim (`Projectile.cs` cites in `data.rs`);
  the AI machines stay the documented dispatch no-ops (aiStyle 26/54/156/164/169/
  206). The `is_summon_shot` flag now books for minion/sentry spawns (the whip
  `CanRunHitEffects` gate).
- **RNG**: the only draws the summon arm spends are the Pygmy `Next(191,195)` and
  Pirate `Next(3)` kind picks, on the `UpdatePlayers` stream at the spawn site (the C#
  `ItemCheck_Shoot` runs under `UpdatePlayers`, `Main.cs:17754`). The spider cycle and
  the ai seeds draw nothing. **Round 2 removed the summon crit draw**: the C# has NO
  spawn-time crit roll — `Projectile.Damage` rolls at HIT and only for the
  melee/ranged/magic flags (`Projectile.cs:12890-12901`); the minion/sentry rows carry
  none, and `DefaultToWhip` (`:10704-10718`) sets none either (the whip's crit rides its
  tag effect's hit roll, `WhipTagEffect.cs:69`). The port rolls crit at throw time for
  the three classes (its documented stand-in); the summon arm now SKIPS that draw
  (`crit = false`, no roll) so the stream is faithful — a plain minion staff's use
  leaves `UpdatePlayers` untouched, the Pygmy spends exactly its kind pick. No existing
  stream pin covers a summon shot (leaf=3, blaze=4, prism=1, bow=1/2 all non-summon), so
  the skip breaks no pin. Witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN (`use_loop_tests::i25_*`,
  `test_DW_6_1/6_2` corrected to the ascending order); no compiler invoked.

#### Round 2 (2026-11-20, same branch): the sentry arm, the Clay Pot, centring, kb wiring

A second distrust-verbatim pass over the use path found four more defects, all fixed
in `world_sim/editing.rs` (witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN, no compiler invoked):

- **The sentry spawn arm was MISSING** — the sentry staves (1572/2366/3571/3569/5119/
  5463) fell through to the generic flight. The C# arm (`Player.cs:48189-48211`) calls
  `PickSentryLandingSpot` (`:49525-49543` — the cursor column + its two neighbours
  scanned down to the first `WorldGen.SolidTile2` row, one above, at `row*16-24`; the
  3571/3569/5463 staves SKIP the scan), drops the shot at `vy=15` (the 5463 barnacle
  lands at the cursor's exact world Y, `vy=0`, `:48203-48206`), seeds `ai0=60` for the
  1572 Frost Hydra / `90` for the 5119 Houndius / `0` else (`:48195-48207`), spawns the
  SCALED `Damage` and overrides `originalDamage = damage` (UNSCALED, `:48209`), then runs
  `UpdateMaxTurrets` (`:48210`). The helpers `pick_sentry_landing_spot`/`sentry_solid_tile2`
  were already ported (round 1) but never called; the arm now wires them, gated
  `def.summon && proj_data(proj).sentry`. The shared tail's `update_max_turrets` sweep
  (already present) covers the cap. The `AI_053` init latch overwrites `ai0→120` on the
  first tick (`projectile.rs`), so the spawn seed is passed verbatim but transient.
- **The Clay Pot (6161) was in the WRONG arm** — round 1 gave it a `SpawnMinionOnCursor`
  cursor spawn, but the C# has NO such arm for 6161: it rides the generic tail
  (`Player.cs:49437` — player-centre spawn, aim velocity, SCALED `Damage`) and only
  overrides `originalDamage = damage` (`:49442-49444`). Removed the cursor arm; the
  override now rides the generic spawn. (6161's shoot 1118 is a minion row, so the
  generic spawn's `original_damage` init already books the SCALED value — the override
  corrects it to UNSCALED for the pool's `minionDamage` recompute.)
- **The cursor spawns missed the half-box subtraction** — `NewProjectile` takes the
  CENTRE and subtracts `width/2, height/2` (`Projectile.cs:10876-10877`); the port's
  `spawn_with_data_ai*` seam takes the TOP-LEFT. The minion cursor spawns (and the new
  sentry spawn) now subtract the per-kind half-box (the inferno-blast precedent,
  `projectile.rs`). The GENERIC spawn sites keep their existing centre-ish convention
  (a port-wide stand-in; changing them would break the pinned leaf/blaze/prism tests).
- **`GetWeaponKnockback` was only wired into the minion arm** — the C# runs it ONCE at
  `:47151` for EVERY shoot (after the ammo fuse / gunProj reset). Now folded into the
  shared throw block (`fx_kb`) and the ammo path (`knock_back`), so the gem/spirit/sky/
  blaze/generic/whip shots all carry the glove/Titan/stealth scales. Behaviour-neutral
  today: the only live `minion_kb` writer is the sky-stone accessory (+0.5) and the
  kb-glove; `kb_buff`/`shroomite_stealth` have NO live writers (the DebuffEffects/
  MiscEffects tables never reach the Player), and the gunProj four are Ranged with no
  stealth armed (the DW-4.2 raw-knockback pins hold). The whip (`summon=true`) takes the
  `minionKB` add faithfully.
- **The summon crit draw was removed** (see the RNG bullet above): the C# never
  spawn-crits a summon shot; the port's throw-time roll now skips `def.summon`.

Deviations and notes:

- **The 0-time `item.buffTime` grant is a ghost — but the 3600 `ApplyPetBuffs` grant
  is NOT.** The summon staves' `Item.buffTime` rows are 0 (itemdata, the C#

  grants `AddBuff(buffType, 3600)` at the use-start for the 28 summon-staff types
  (`MINION_STAFF_PET_BUFF_ITEMS`), and the keep-alive arm's 18000 refresh pins THAT buff
  while the minion lives. (Round 1 added the 3600 grant; the earlier "the minion buff is
  swept one tick later" reading was the MISSING-grant bug, not a C# behaviour — the
  regression tests now assert the 3600 grant survives and refreshes to 18000.)
- **The port's arms run after the player tick's expiry sweep** (the Phase-2 seam): the C#
  runs them inside `UpdateBuffs` between the reset and the sweep. The consequence is the

- **The Stardust Dragon chain (625-628) is excluded** вЂ” the relink arms in the kill-oldest
  and the free-up are stubbed; the kinds carry rows only where the summon slice needs them.
- **DD2 persistence** (S1-P-i26 update): the sentry-summon path now reads the world's

- **Dust, sound, light and frame machines unported**: `AI_062`'s dust spawns and their

### The Flame Burst Tower slice (S1-D-4b-9, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode**: this task ran without a compiler вЂ” no `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt`,
no test run, no graphify. The port was verified by re-reading the C# line by line;
the tests below are written as code, NOT executed. The sibling branch
`task/S1-D-4b-3` owns aiStyle 123 and the shots 642/644; this slice touches neither.

S1-D-4b-9 ported aiStyle **130** (Flame Burst Tower, `AI_130_FlameBurstTower`,
`Projectile.cs:68107-68360`) + its target pick (`AI_130_FlameBurstTower_FindTarget`,
`:68362-68407`) and the aiStyle-**131** shot (`AI_131_FlameBurstShot`, `:68456-68508`,
the 664/666/668 rows `:7153-7162` вЂ” 16x16, alpha 255, local-immunity в€’1), plus the
Apprentice T2/T3 set flags (`ArmorSetBonuses.cs:74-78`/`:99-104`, the triples
`:485`/`:489`) and the towers' `proj_frames` 7/9/9 (`Main.cs:8458-8460`).

- **The arm mirrors the 134 Ballista inline precedent** (the per-kind constants, the
  muzzle captured BEFORE the backpack reposition вЂ” Bottom + (direction*6, в€’40/в€’44/в€’46),
  the 300-wrap `localAI[0]`, the init latch, the backpack branch, the reload/target
  state, the fire state at `ai[1] == 12` with the frame `1 + ai[1]/4`, the cycle wrap
  `num6*num7` into the 80/70/60-tick reload, the gravity tail + `dd2_sentry_step`).
  The Apprentice T2 buffs (`:68275-68280`) tighten the angle cone to 0.1 and multiply
  the range Г—1.5 / the speed Г—1.4. The fire-state scan passes
  `canChangeDirection: false` (rejects targets behind the facing).
- **The cone differs from the Ballista's**: `|dir.X| < |dir.Y| * angleRatioMax`
  rejects steep targets BOTH above and below (`:68378`/`:68400` have NO `dir.Y > 0`
  clause, unlike `AI_134_Ballista_FindTarget`'s dead-bottom cone). The reload-state
  facing flip reads `Math.Sign(DirectionTo(npc.Center).X)` from the tower's CENTRE
  (`Entity.cs:205-208`), not the muzzle.
- **The shot spawn has NO В±16 clamp**: aiStyle 131 в‰  1, so `NewProjectile`'s
  aiStyle-1 velocity decay (`:10895-10902`) does not run вЂ” the 12/15/18-px shots
  (16.8/21/25.2 with Apprentice T2) fly at full speed from the centred muzzle
  (`x в€’ 8, y в€’ 8`).
- **RNG order preserved by construction** (unlike the 137 skip-and-document
  precedent, this task draws the gates): per tick the 130 arm draws the type-270
  dust gate `Next(2)` (`:68138`/`:68190`/`:68242`, only while `ai[2] != 1` вЂ” the
  flag is captured BEFORE the pickup latch, `:68119`); on a 0 the two
  UNCONDITIONAL `NextFloat`s follow (`fadeIn` `:68141`, `velocity.X` `:68146` вЂ”
  they draw even when `NewDustDirect` returns the culled dummy slot 6000); then
  the smoke gates `Next(5)` Г— 1/2/3 per tier (`:68158`/`:68210`/`:68262`). The
  131 shot draws `Next(2)` Г— 1/2/3 per tier (`:68495`) and, on a non-zero, the
  always-0-but-consuming `Next(1)` (`:68500`). The targeting, the fire, the shot
  spawn and the alpha fade draw nothing. Tests
  `s1_d_4b_9_the_tower_dust_gates_draw_in_the_csharp_order` /
  `s1_d_4b_9_the_shot_dust_gates_draw_in_the_csharp_order` replay the exact draw
  sequence against a reference `FastRandom` stream.
- **Skipped layers**: the dust BODIES and `Dust.NewDust`'s pool-occupancy-dependent

### The sentry-summon use machinery (S1-P-i26, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode**: no `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt`, no test run, no graphify. The port
was verified by re-reading the C# line by line; the witnesses below are written as
code, NOT executed.

The census found the sentry **AI bodies** already ported (S1-D-4b-2/-3/-9: aiStyle
53/123/130/134/137/138/139/197, the `proj_data` rows, the cap sweep
`update_max_turrets`, the targeting) but the **use path** — the two `ItemCheck_Shoot`
sentry arms and their placement/gate helpers — was MISSING: a sentry staff fell
through to the generic `Item.shoot` firing (spawn at the player centre + 10 px
toward the cursor, aim-normalized velocity, a throw-time crit draw), not the C#'s
cursor/tile placement. S1-P-i26 ports the use machinery verbatim.

- **Arm A — the placeable staff sentries** (`Player.cs:48189-48212`): items 1572
  (Frost Hydra → 308), 2366 (Queen Spider → 377), 3571 (Rainbow Crystal → 643),
  3569 (Moon Lord Turret → 641), 5119 (Houndius Shootius → 966), 5463 (Dead Cells
  Barnacle → 1025). `PickSentryLandingSpot` (`:49525-49543`) picks the spot: the
  hover kinds (3571/3569/5463) skip the ground scan, the rest scan the cursor column
  + its two neighbours down to the first `SolidTile2` row then step one row up;
  `spawnX` is the RAW cursor X, `spawnY = row*16 − 24`. The spawn drops at `(0, 15)`
  (the barnacle at `(0, 0)` on the raw cursor Y), `ai0` = 60/90 for the 1572/5119,
  `originalDamage = sItem.damage` (the UNSCALED prefixed item damage, `:47060` /
  `:48209` — NOT the class-multiplied `weaponDamage`), then `UpdateMaxTurrets`.
- **Arm B — the DD2 tower poppers** (`:49057-49094`): items 3818-3820 (Flameburst →
  663/665/667), 3824-3826 (Ballista → 677/678/679), 3829-3831 (Lightning Aura →
  688/689/690), 3832-3834 (Explosive Trap → 691/692/693). `PayDD2CrystalsBeforeUse`
  (`:42367-42374`) consumes 10 Eternia crystals (3822) in reverse slot order
  (`ConsumeItem` `:9269-9308`, ammo → coins → grid; a drained cell turns to air),
  `FindSentryRestingSpot` (`:53015-53059`) picks the ground spot (the cursor pulled
  into the reachable area, `worldX = col*16 + 8` with the per-kind facing/X offsets,
  `pushYUp = 41` + the per-kind offsets − 14, `worldY = firstSolidRow*16`), the
  per-tier payload rides the spawn (`ai0/ai1` = 1/80, 1/70, 1/60 for the Flameburst
  T1/T2/T3; `ai1 = GetBallistraShotDelay` for the Ballista; `localAI[0] =
  GetExplosiveTrapCooldown` for the Trap), `originalDamage = sItem.damage`, then
  `UpdateMaxTurrets`.
- **The use gates** (`ItemCheck_CheckCanUse_Inner`, `:52079-52111`) run BEFORE the
  use starts: the crystal-payment lock (`CheckDD2CrystalPaymentLock` `:42376-42384`
  — free outside the event, the full 10 required during it), the
  `downedDD2EventAnyDifficulty || Ongoing` gate (`:52083-52086` — the port reads the
  world's three monotonic tier flags, the C# player field is their per-tick latch
  `:24450-24453` / `DD2Event.cs:89-99`), the `WouldSpotOverlapWithSentry` overlap
  refusal (`:52983-53013` — the three probe points against every active sentry's
  hitbox, the aura kinds inflate ±8, the rest recentre to a 30-px width) and the
  solid-tile refusal (`:52095-52111` — the aura kinds test a 3-tall `SolidTiles`
  column, the rest a single `SolidTile`).
- **The DD2 lifetime hold** (`Projectile.cs:17197-17200`): while `DD2Event.Ongoing`
  holds, an `IsADD2Turret` sentry's `timeLeft++` cancels the per-tick decrement, so
  its lifetime never drains during the event. The port's lifetime block gained this
  arm; the `Ongoing` read is the world's live `dd2_event_ongoing` flag, not the
  `event_ongoing()` stub (which still reports false for the wave machinery). The two
  `update_max_turrets` call sites (the spawn sweep `editing.rs` + the cap-change
  sweep `world_sim/player.rs`) likewise read the world flag, so the O'A towers
  genuinely persist through the sweep during the event (`TurretShouldPersist`
  `Projectile.cs:670-690`).
- **RNG order preserved by construction**: NONE of the placement/gate/payment
  helpers draws `Main.rand` — the scans, the overlap test, the crystal consume and
  the spawn payload are pure arithmetic. The C# `ItemCheck_Shoot` makes NO crit draw
  for the sentry arms (`Projectile.Damage`'s crit block `Projectile.cs:12890-12901`
  gates on the melee/ranged/magic flags, which no sentry row sets — the summon class
  has no crit), so the port's sentry arms SKIP the generic throw-time crit roll,
  keeping the `UpdatePlayers` stream's draw count 1:1. The witness
  (`sentry_use_tests::the_sentry_use_draws_no_crit_on_the_updateplayers_stream`)
  isolates the crit by mirroring the stream: one `next_range(1, 101)` on a clone of
  the sentry's post-use stream lands on the non-sentry summon's, proving the only
  delta is the single crit draw the sentry skips. The knockback takes
  `GetWeaponKnockback`'s summon arm (`:53348-53351` `+= minionKB`, then `kbBuff`
  ×1.5 `:53356-53359`).
- **Skips / deviations**: the aiStyle-53 sentry-backpack branch
