## The shop buy/sell transactions (S1-P-i44, 2026-11-19)

The shop TRANSACTION layer over the S1-C-11 price chain: the buy/sell click
dispatch, the cursor deposit, the sell payout + restock, the sellback memo
and the per-open stock refresh. C# cites inline; the witnesses are written
(not run — the code-only swarm).

- **The buy lands on the CURSOR, not the inventory.** `ItemSlot.HandleShopSlot`
  (`UI/ItemSlot.cs:2053-2095`) pushes each bought unit onto `Main.mouseItem`
  (`:2075-2088`); the old `app/mod.rs::buy_shop_item` deposited through
  `slot_for_pickup` into the grid — WRONG, now fixed. The charge is
  `GetItemExpectedPrice`'s `calcForBuying` per unit (`:2059-2060`), the
  `stackSplit <= 1` gate + the `superFastStack + 1` loop + the
  `RefreshStackSplitCooldown` (`:2043`/`:2047`/`:2089` → `:1774-1784`) ride
  `app/clicks.rs::handle_shop_buy`. The bulk-buy (`CanBulkBuy`/
  `GetBulkBuyAmount`, `:3121-3138`) multiplies the loop by 10 (clamped to a
  buyOnce row's stack) only under Shift on an isAShopItem/buyOnce row. The
  C# runs action 3 on a HELD left button too (`LeftClick`'s `if (num != 3 &&
  !flag) return;`, `:928`); the port keeps the left button on the press edge
  like the rest of the inventory grid (research/20 §5), so the held-repeat
  buy rides the RIGHT button (`RightClick`'s ctx-15 arm, `:1648-1651`, which
  the port drives off the held `place_down`) — the recorded left-edge model.
- **The sellback memo** (`Main.shopSellbackHelper`,
  `GameContent/ItemShopSellbackHelper.cs:5-73`): every plain-currency
  non-buyOnce buy adds its unit (`ItemSlot.cs:2084-2087`); a sell refunds the
  first `min(memo, stack)` units at their BUY price
  (`Player.cs:35191-35195`'s `(-num2 + calcForBuying) * min`), and
  `Chest.AddItemToShop` removes the memo'd units before re-stocking
  (`Chest.cs:672-676` — a full re-sell of bought goods adds NO row). The memo
  matches by `Item.IsConsideredSameItemAsType` (`Item.cs:47851-47933`'s
  variant families) AND prefix. `Main.UpdateOldNPCShop`
  (`Main.cs:18204-18211`) clears it on every shop-index change; the port's
  `close_shop` + the open's `same_shop` gate mirror that.
- **The sell** (`Player.SellItem`, `Player.cs:35168-35329`): the payout is
  `calcForSelling / 5` (min 1) × the sold stack + the sellback refund
  (`shop.rs::sell_payout`); the `calcForSelling <= 0` refusal returns 0 and
  the caller runs the value-0 giveaway arm (`ItemSlot.cs:1232-1238` — the
  item still enters the shop, sound 7). `Chest.AddItemToShop`
  (`Chest.cs:670-706`) merges the remainder into the first stackable buyOnce
  row, then clones it into the first AIR slot (a depleted buyOnce row turns
  to air in place, `ItemSlot.cs:2090-2093`); both loops scan `i < 39` (the
  40th slot never takes a sell).
- **The sell cursor** (`GetSellOrTrash`, `ItemSlot.cs:198-209`): with a shop
  open the Shift-hover lights cursor 10 (Sell) instead of 6 (Trash); the
  coin kinds 71-74 answer null (never sellable). The cursor-10 click
  (`OverrideLeftClick`, `:851-869`) sells the whole slot. The ctx-15 grid
  (`Main.cs:41788-41818`) draws 10×4 `Inventory_Back6` cells at
  `(int)(73 + i*56*0.755)`, `(int)(258 + j*56*0.755)`; a non-air cursor over
  an empty cell sells the held stack (`PickItemMovementAction` action 4 →
  `LeftClick` case 4, `:1575-1578`/`:1222-1241`, `stackSplit = 9999`).
- **The per-open refresh** (`Main.OpenShop`, `Main.cs:40459-40467`): the
  inventory opens, `stackSplit = 9999`, the chat text clears, sound 12, and
  `SetupShop` re-resolves the stock from the LIVE world state — the port now
  feeds the live moon phase, `downed_eow`/`downed_skeletron`, the player's
  `golfer_score`, the Party Girl roster scan and the purse-inclusive coin
  total (the old open hard-coded `downed_boss2/3 = false`, `golfer_score = 0`,
  `party_girl_present = false` and read only the grid coins). The shop closes
  when the inventory closes (`Main.cs:41784-41787`, `update_shop_close`).

Deviations (the recorded coin model, ANALYSIS "the purse"): the C# `BuyItem`
spends the inventory + bank coin stacks through `TryPurchasing`
(`Player.cs:35490+`) and `SellItem` spawns the payout as coin stacks through
the four denomination loops (74/73/72/71, descending slots 53→0, `DoCoins`
carrying at 100) with a cloned-inventory restore when no room exists
(`:35321-35328`). The port's aggregate `App.coins` purse cannot fill up, so
the charge/payout ride it directly and the no-room restore folds out. The
`shopSpecialCurrency` arm (the defender-medal rows) stays unported
(S1-C-11). The happiness icon/label at (504, invBottom)
(`Main.cs:41790-41797`) and the tooltip shop-lines
(`MouseText_DrawItemTooltip_AddShopLines`, `Main.cs:20448+`) are the chrome
follow-up — `display_price_row` stays pinned by its golden vectors.

W4-e19 round 3 quicksell census (code-only): the C# has NO quicksell-to-void-
bag and NO trash-can sell — `Player.SellItem`'s only two call sites are the
cursor-10 shift-sell (`ItemSlot.cs:854`) and the shop-cell action-4
(`:1225`), both ported (`sell_slot_click`/`shop_slot_click`); the trash is a
plain context-6 slot (the death `DropItems` airs it, `:54304`, ported in
`death.rs`), and the void bag is a storage fallback, not a sell surface. The
price math is complete: `sell_payout` = `GetItemExpectedPrice`'s selling ÷5
min-1 × stack + the `min(memo, stack)` buy-price refund (`:35184-35195`),
`get_item_expected_price` verbatim (`:35359-35398`, the f32 discount
truncation + the banker's adjustment rounding + the buyOnce ÷5 clamp); the
coin kinds 71-74 refuse the sell cursor (`GetSellOrTrash:204-207`). Two
end-to-end COIN witnesses added (buy→shift-quicksell nets zero through the
memo refund + the memo consumed by `AddItemToShop`'s `Remove`; the
un-memo'd stack pays the fifth and re-stocks buyOnce) — WRITTEN NOT RUN.

## The wet statics rebase (R-03-1, 2026-11-13)

`Player.cs:24380-24437` is ported 1:1 as `player.rs::wet_gravity_and_cap`
(`WetStaticsFlags` carries the wet-family flags): the per-liquid arms assign
the tick's `gravity`/`maxFallSpeed` and the jump statics (water 0.2/5 +
30/6.01, honey 0.1/3, merman 0.3/7, trident 0.25/6 with the `controlUp`
0.1/2 sub-arm, shimmerWet 0.15 + 23/5.51, the Dead Cells down-dash Г—0.85,
the absorbed-shimmer Г—0.9), then `vortexDebuff` zeroes the gravity and every
tick adds the `+0.01f` fall-cap creep. The tick consumes the rebase between
the `:24364-24369` reset and `UpdateJumpHeight`'s max-lift (`:25656`) вЂ” the
C# order, so a wet 30/6.01 survives the lift and the lift's max can only
raise it. The plain integration arm (`Player.cs:27352-27359`) rides the
rebased values at FULL strength: the `gravity / 3` / `maxFallSpeed / 3`
sites the old port used (`:27008`/`:27339`) are the mount/wings flight
integrators, not a wet rule вЂ” that misread was the "water jumps 2Г— too
weak" audit finding. The wings glide cap (`:27339`'s `maxFallSpeed / 3`) now
correctly rides the creeped 10.01 (`flight_section` divides the passed
`maxFallSpeed` itself, as the C# reads the field).

Scope notes, none of which change the ported numbers:

- **The not-yet-ported writers ride as default-false flags** on
  `WetStaticsFlags`: `shimmering` (the absorbed state вЂ” the
  shimmer-emergence work), `merman` (the buff table, S1-E-7), `trident`
  (`Player.cs:12896`), `control_up` (the port's `PlayerInput` has no up
  channel), `down_dash` (`isPerformingJump_DownDash` вЂ” only the Dead Cells
  down-dash sets it, `Player.cs:20697-20722`), `vortex_debuff` and
  `portal_physics`. All are the C#'s default-false states, so a vanilla
  pre-hardmode water/honey/shimmer tick matches the C# exactly.
- **The wet flags stay one tick fresher than the C#'s** (research/03's
  phase note): the C# consumes the previous tick's `WetCollision` flags in
  this block (`:27728-27850` recomputes them later in the same tick),
  while the port derives them earlier in its tick. The rebase formula is
  exact; the dryв†’wet frame boundary is the swim-ascent seed's (research/03
  S9) territory and is left unverified there.
- The upward velocity clamp (`-(MAX_FALL/3)` in liquid) was pre-existing
  port structure with NO C# counterpart — **removed by W4-c46** (research/03
  S9): the C# plain arm (gravDir 1, `Player.cs:27363-27376`) caps only the
  descent at `maxFallSpeed`; the ascent cap lives in the flipped-gravity
  mirror (`:27378-27391`), which the port has no gravity flip for. The clamp
  had capped the flipper/merman swim ascent (−6.01) to −3.33.

### The runtime settle-pump driver (R-12-5, W4-g47 continuation)

The per-tick driver census: C# `Liquid.UpdateLiquid` (`Liquid.cs:983-1158`)
is consumed by THREE drivers, and the port now carries all three:

1. **The runtime pump** — `WorldGen.UpdateWorld` (`WorldGen.cs:71526-71534`):
   `Liquid.skipCount++; if (skipCount > 1) { using
   (Main.SwapRandom("UpdateLiquid")) Liquid.UpdateLiquid(); skipCount = 0; }`
   — one pass per two 60 Hz world ticks (30 Hz), wrapped in the named RNG
   stream. Ported VERBATIM as `LiquidSystem::update_world_tick` (the
   `skip_count` field is the C# static `Liquid.cs:19`, zeroed by `ReInit`
   `:85` — a world swap starts a fresh window). The app consumer
   `world_sim/liquids.rs` now calls the engine driver instead of its own
   `app.liquid_tick % 2` divider (field REMOVED — the counter's C# home is
   the Liquid statics, not Main; the old divider never reset on world swap,
   a phase deviation the driver port fixes). The `SwapRandom` block is the
   caller's seam: the drained `edit_kills` resolve on `RngKey::UpdateLiquid`
   (`resolve_liquid_edit_kills`), the exact stream the C# `KillTile` drops
   draw under the swap; the engine pass itself draws nothing on this lane
   (the g45/g46 nudge is their seam). The `isGeneratingOrLoadingWorld`
   early-return (`:71497-71500`) is the frame loop's own gate (worldgen
   completes before the loop starts). Cadence-identical to the old divider
   on a fresh boot (both fire on ticks 2, 4, ...); witnesses:
   `liquid_force_settle::the_update_world_driver_runs_the_pass_every_second_tick`
   (byte-equal twin vs direct `update` over 40 ticks),
   `...::re_init_resets_the_driver_divider`. Written, NOT run.
   Pass-internal census (already landed, re-verified against the driver
   read): the stride window `curMaxLiquid / cycles` with the `numLiquid`
   clamp re-walk (`:1069-1105`), the quickFall two-loop shape (`:1083-1105`
   — delay-10 force + skip-clear vs the skip-honouring normal loop), the
   `wetCounter >= cycles` tail (`:1106-1149` — the descending `kill >= 8`
   sweep with the 254→255 promotion, the `num8` buffer promotion with
   `DelBuffer(0)`'s swap-remove, the ±50 stuck band), and the panic gate
   (`:1005-1054`). The `:1087` quickFall loop writes `delay = 10` INTO the
   entry; the port's pass loop passes the local 10 into `update_tile`,
   whose quickFall arms return it unchanged (`Liquid.cs:483-491`/`:512-521`
   skip the delay writes under quickFall), and the write-back
   `self.active[i].delay = delay` persists it — the entry carries 10 out
   of a quickSettle window exactly as the C# does (the first non-quickFall
   lava visit flows immediately, no 5-tick re-throttle).
2. **The load drain** — `settle_loaded_world` (`WorldFile.cs:733-764`),
   WIRED at `App::new` (g47 `551c1e7b`); calls `update` directly (no
   skipCount — the C# load loop does the same).
3. **The gen settle loops** — `WorldGen.cs:16132-16210` /
   `:21246-21309` (f25's lane; the gen/runtime split contract is recorded
   in the f25 gen-pass census below).

**The LiquidBuffer driver arm** (census re-verified, R-12-5): the buffer is
NOT scanned per tick — it drains ONLY inside the `wetCounter >= cycles`
tail (`Liquid.cs:1120-1130`), budget `num8 = min(numLiquid, numLiquidBuffer)`
where `numLiquid` is the POST-retirement-sweep count (the C#'s
`curMaxLiquid - (curMaxLiquid - numLiquid)` algebra). Each promotion clears
the buffered cell's `checkingLiquid` (`:1127`), calls `AddWater` (which may
REFUSE — dry/solid/border cells) and `DelBuffer(0)` UNCONDITIONALLY
(`:1129`), the swap-remove moving the LAST entry into slot 0
(`LiquidBuffer.cs:22-27`) — so a refused cell still leaves the buffer and
the head order is LIFO-ish, not FIFO. `AddBuffer` (`LiquidBuffer.cs:11-20`)
caps at `maxLiquidBuffer - 2` and marks `checkingLiquid` for dedupe; the
port's `add_water` carries both arms (`:1167-1171` overflow threshold
`curMaxLiquid - 1`). The ≥90%-full panic gate reads `buffer.len()` per
update (`:1009-1020`). New witnesses (written, NOT run):
`liquid_settle::the_promotion_budget_is_the_post_sweep_active_count_clamped_to_the_buffer`
(the 1→2 budget growth over two cycles + the swap-remove head order),
`...::the_promotion_delbuffers_even_when_addwater_refuses_the_cell`.

**The f25 gen-pass split contract** (R-12-5 census of `0ed1f3cf` on
`task/W4-f25`, claims read in `docs/research/12g-f25-settle-liquids.md`):
f25 owns the GEN side — `worldgen/settle_liquids.rs` (the ocean retype

The shared `Liquid.UpdateLiquid` engine is ONE body — f25's gen-local
copies dedupe onto the g47 surfaces at the g46c graft (research/252 step 6).
Carried onto the g47 machinery here (the export surface f25's module
drives): `tiles_ignore_water`, `world_gen_tiles_ignore_water` (the

`...::clear_pending_liquid_drops_both_lists_and_their_checking_bits`,

**The e21 pump/settle compose** (R-12-5 driver 4): the pump active-gate
(`Wiring.cs:2043-2125` — the 142/143 registration, the 19-cap, the 2×2
SkipWire) and `XferWater` (`:475-523` — the type-matched 255-capped
teleport with the live in-tile re-read) were landed by M7-WIRE/e21, but
the compose with the settle pump was MISSING: the C# fires
`WorldGen.SquareTileFrame` after every out transfer (`:512`), on the

re-queues every wet cell through `Liquid.AddWater`
(`WorldGen.cs:81344-81346`, `netMode != 1 && !generatingWorld`) — that is
how pump-teleported liquid joins the active lists and flows. The port's
`xfer_water` mutated the tiles and never woke the settle (its doc claimed
"the port's liquid sim reads the tiles next tick" — false: the sim walks
its ACTIVE LIST, not the grid). Fixed: `Wiring` queues the touched
positions (`pump_wakes`, in the C#'s call order — the emptied-in arm
queues twice, `:516` + `:521`), the app wiring tick drains them into
`LiquidSystem::wake_around(x, y, 1)` (the 3×3 `TileFrame` walk; the
dry/solid/checking guards are `AddWater`'s own). The reframe's
neighbour-frame half is a no-op for pumps (the transfer touches only
liquid, the bodies keep their frames). The wake is dedupe-safe
(`checkingLiquid`) and RNG-free. Witnesses (written, NOT run):
`wiring::tests::the_pump_moves_water_and_adopts_the_type` extended (the
three wake sites in order + the drain),
`world_sim::wiring::tests::r_12_5_the_pump_transfer_wakes_the_settle_and_the_water_flows`
(the full compose: trip → transfer → wake → skipCount pass → the blob
falls out of the out body).

### The DelWater keep-one (W4-g47 vs W4-g45, for the merger)

Both branches ported `Liquid.DelWater` (`:1470-1599`) independently. **g47's
`liquid.rs::del_water` is canonical** — keep it, drop g45's. Arm-by-arm:

| Arm (C#) | g47 | g45 | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<2` dry + side wakes (`:1478-1498`) | edge-safe probe + chunk marks | edge-safe probe (`2249cf59`), no chunk marks | g47 (superset; adopted g45's probe form) |
| `<20` drain (`:1499-1505`) | `tile_open` fold, live `here` | `!tile_is_solid` fold | equivalent (`tile_open` == the C# `!nactive \|\| !solid \|\| solidTop`) |
| `>=20` keep-alive (`:1506-1510`) | `kill=0; return` (no retire) | `return false` (caller skips swap) | equivalent |
| above-wake + type-clear (`:1511-1518`) | live re-read | live re-read | equivalent |
| side wakes (`:1519-1528`) | **live re-read** (adopted) | live re-read | g45's form adopted into g47 |
| lava grass ring (`:1529-1560`) | converts + **chunk-dirty mark** (adopted) | converts + mark | g45's marking adopted into g47 |
| honey/shimmer re-check (`:1562-1569`) | yes | yes | equivalent |
| swap-remove (`:1575-1579`) | **INSIDE** `del_water` (self-copy-then-pop) | caller-side (`retire_sweep`: pop-then-copy-if-`l<len`) | equivalent (both match the C# `numLiquid--` then copy `liquid[numLiquid]`; at `l==last` g47 self-copies+pops, g45 just pops — same result). g47 keeps it in one body, so the stuck self-clear and the sweep share it without a second caller |
| `CheckAlch` tail (`:1580-1583`) | `check_alch` → `edit_kills` (drops resolved) | `check_alch_tile` wrapper (discards drops) | **g47** — the drop records ride `drain_edit_kills` → `resolve_liquid_edit_kills`; g45's wrapper drops the herb loot |
| `CheckLilyPad` tail (`:1584-1597`) | explicit 3-arm order (adopted) + `edit_kills` | explicit 3-arm order, `check_lily_pad` wrapper (discards drops) | **g47** — same arm order, but keeps the drop seam |

The merger should take g47's `del_water`/`end_pass`/`add_water` wholesale and
NOT g45's `retire_sweep`/`refill_from_buffer`/`check_alch_tile`/`check_lily_pad`
wrappers. The decisive difference is the **drop seam**: g47's `Check*` kills
ride `edit_kills` (the herb/lily-pad loot resolves into item drops through
`resolve_liquid_edit_kills`, the same path the live liquid tick uses), while
g45's `check_alch_tile`/`check_lily_pad` wrappers execute the kill but discard
the drop record — a behavioural loss. The swap-remove shapes are equivalent.
g45's genuinely-better details (edge probe, live side reads, ring
chunk-marking, explicit lily arm order) are already folded into g47's body
(`551c1e7b`). g45's `genRand` nudge + 7/5-neighbour wakes (`ccfe0b42`) are a
SEPARATE seam (`update_tile`'s averaging arms, not `del_water`) — keep those.

### The honey/shimmer settle specifics (W4-g47 closeout per-liquid census, SEAL carry)

The drivers are NOT water-centric — the per-liquid arms verified against
`Liquid.Update` (`Liquid.cs:480-566`) arm-for-arm:

- **lava**: `LavaCheck` EVERY visit (`:482`, before the gate), then the
  `delay < 5` throttle (`:485-490`) — one fall per SIX visits (five
  throttled + one flow), reset to 0. Port: `update_tile`'s lava arm.
- **honey**: non-lava cells wake their lava neighbours first (`:495-510`),
  then `HoneyCheck` EVERY visit (`:513`), then the `delay < 10` throttle
  (`:516-521`) — one fall per ELEVEN visits. Port: the honey arm.
- **shimmer**: non-lava/non-honey cells wake their honey neighbours
  (`:526-541`), then `ShimmerCheck` (`:544`) with **NO delay gate at all**
  — the C# arm has no `delay++`/return; shimmer flows at the water
  cadence (one tile per two passes via the down-arm `skipLiquid` pair).
  Port: the shimmer arm — same shape, no gate. The `delay` field stays 0.
- **water**: the else-arm wakes shimmer neighbours (`:548-563`), ungated.
- The neighbour-wake cascade is per-kind EXCLUSIVE (a lava cell never
  wakes lava neighbours; a honey cell wakes lava but not honey; a shimmer
  cell wakes lava+honey but not shimmer) — the port's nested else-chain
  mirrors it exactly.
- `quickFall` bypasses BOTH gates (`:1083-1090` forces `delay = 10`
  pre-Update — above both thresholds); the reduced-liquids
  `numLiquid > 2000` OR-arm feeds the same bypass for all four kinds.
- The settle drivers (`update_world_tick`, `gen_settle_loop`,
  `settle_loaded_world`, the panic drain) are kind-agnostic by design —
  the C# drivers never branch on liquid type; the per-kind behaviour
  lives entirely in `Update`/`DelWater`/the checks, all ported.
- The `DelWater` reaction tail is per-kind too (`:1529-1569`): lava →
  `LavaCheck` + the grass ring, honey → `HoneyCheck` only, shimmer →
  `ShimmerCheck` only; the port reads the LIVE cell kind post-drain,
  same arms.
- The e21 pump transfer is type-locked (`Wiring.cs:501` `b2 == b`) for
  ALL four kinds — an empty out tile adopts the in type (`:497-499`),
  including honey/shimmer; the port's `xfer_water` carries the same
  lock + adoption + the three wakes per transfer regardless of kind.

### W4-c34 addendum (2026-11-20, code-only mode)

- **Underworld evaporation** (`Liquid.cs:466-474`) now rides `update_tile`
  before the zero kill (`:475-479`): water below `Main.UnderworldLayer`
  (`Main.cs:2790`, `maxTilesY - 200`) loses `min(2, liquid)` per visit;
  lava/honey/shimmer are exempt (`liquidType() == 0`). The change-detection
  tail compares against the pre-evaporation snapshot exactly like the C#'s
  `byte liquid = tile5.liquid` (`:464`), so an evaporating cell resets `kill`
  and wakes the cell above (`:956-957`) until it runs dry and retires.
  **Deliberate deviation:** the band is guarded by `underworld_layer >= 0`.
  In a sub-200-tall world the C# layer sits below row 0 and would evaporate
  every water cell; vanilla worlds are >= 1200 tiles tall, so the guard never
  fires at runtime - it only keeps the ported water-flow witnesses (which
  use 11-120-tall fixture worlds) green. The evaporation write marks the
  chunk + `dirty` like `set_level` so the render cache invalidates (the C#'s
  own change consumer, `_netChangeSet`, is MP and unported).

  `create_liquid_merge_tile`, `get_liquid_merge_types`,
  `liquid_overwrite_strip` and the evaporation consume no random draws.
  The merge placement rides `edit::place_tile`'s legacy single-tile arm

  `TileObjectData` registry route is not taken) and `edit::kill_tile`

### W4-g45 round 2 addendum (2026-11-21, code-only mode) — the AddWater death-guards

already landed (phase 1); there is NO shimmer-specific AddWater — the one
function serves all four kinds, honey/shimmer riding the `CheckWaterDeath`

  || y >= maxTilesY - 5` refuses the outer band before the queue; the

- **The death check** (`:1183-1206`): after the queue, an inactive tile or
  `generating` returns; otherwise lava reads `CheckLavaDeath(tile)`, every
  other liquid reads `CheckWaterDeath(tile)` — the Tile overloads
  (`TileObjectData.cs:5083-5119`) that resolve the def from the cell's

  `1f5a01dd`, NOT in main; its commit names "the `Liquid.cs:1190`
  settlement kill wiring is the liquid task's seam"); this branch

  death runs `edit::kill_tile(world, x, y, false)` INLINE (the C# kills
  before AddWater returns); the cell keeps its liquid (`remove_tile`

  `refill_from_buffer` take `&mut World` (the inline kill mutates); the
  four `world_sim/editing.rs` wake sites + the `app/frame.rs` witness call

  pillar under the herb: in the widened world an open cell below would

- **RNG census:** AddWater itself draws NOTHING — the guards, the queue
  and the death check are RNG-free. The kill cascade consumes
  `World.frame_rng` (the genRand stand-in) only where the C# rolls:
  `reframe_area`'s centre reset needs an ACTIVE centre, and the killed
  cell is inactive — an isolated torch death in an empty neighbourhood
  advances no draw (witnessed). The `Next(30)` nudge contract is
  unchanged: still the only draw in the settle engine, still only on a
  254 (`:892-895`, the phase-2 census).
- **Witnesses** (`liquid.rs::liquid_addwater_guards`, written NOT run):
  the border refusal + inner-edge pass, the grate carve-out, the inline
  torch death, the flag discriminators (torch style 0 vs the water-torch
  sub-tile 8 at frameY 176 — D_4_S8_A3's false/false beats the base's
  true/true through the frame decode; plant 3's global-table water/lava
  split; pile 372's def-beats-global `water_death: false`), the
  honey/shimmer water-arm ride, the open-cell/generation early returns,

## The Frost Legion machine (R-25-1, 2026-11-13)

`NPC.AI()`'s aiStyle-38 block (`NPC.cs:28995-29145`) is ported 1:1 as
`npc.rs::update_frost_legion` вЂ” the constant hop cycle (the `-6f` beat, the
every-third `-8.2f` + `ai[1]++`), the per-type `num551`/`num552` pair (the
Gangsta 3/0.7, the Balla 4/1, the Mystery 3.5/0.8), the stuck flip
(`localAI[2]`'s frozen-`position.X` compare в†’ the port's `frost_stuck_x`) and
the direction-scoped `num551` clamp, plus the three type arms: the Gangsta's
120-tick bottle throw (the hostile `BulletSnowman` 110 at `12Г—spriteDirection`,
25 dmg, `timeLeft = 300` behind `AI_GlobalFiringDistanceCheck`'s
`MaxWorldViewSize`-deflated box вЂ” `NPC.cs:55835-55842`), the Balla's
post-3-hops 200-tick pause and the Mystery's 16-tick windup into the aimed
`SnowBallHostile` 109 (35 dmg, speed 10 at the player's top-centre). The
shared NPC movement (the gravity + the axis-separated tile collision,
`NPC.cs:27485-27910`'s integration) rides the machine's tail вЂ” the port's
per-machine shape (the slime's pattern), and a wall's zeroed vx feeds the
stuck flip exactly like the vanilla.

Two documented gaps at the R-25-1 landing, both resolved by S1-D-3q
(2026-11-18/19, code-only mode):

- **The `confused` resets** (`:29012-29015`, `:29123-29128`) now read the
  buff engine's Confused (31) directly (`buffs.find_buff_index(31)`) —
  the same latch shape `npc_target.rs` uses for the C#'s `this.confused`
  (`NPC.cs:92029-92032`). The original "not ported" note was stale: the
  NPC buff engine carries the debuff already.
- **The `proj.ai[0] = 2f` writes** (`:29025`, `:29087`) — the original
  "inert, no observable effect" claim was WRONG, corrected by the
  2026-11-19 source re-read. For **109** the value matters in C#
  single-player: `AI_010`'s `Main.myPlayer == owner && ai[0] == 0f`
  disarm block (`Projectile.cs:57953-57996`) would set `tileCollide =
  false` (and latch `ai[0] = 1`) without it; `ai[0] = 2` keeps tile
  collision on. Both gravity arms exclude 109 anyway (`:58006`/`:58022`),
  so the ball flies dead straight either way — the observable difference
  is the tile contact. For **110** the write IS inert: `AI_001`'s
  `flag3 = false` list holds the counter (`:55962`, gate `:56038-56041`)
  and the only `ai[0]` reader on that path is the type-88 remap. The
  write now rides `spawn_hostile_timed`'s `ai0` argument
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs` passes 2 for both frost kinds, 0 for the laser —
  its `NewProjectile` default, `NPC.cs:49877`).

## Pause gates (S1-B-3, 2026-11-13)

The pause machinery: `game_paused` is set by the two C# sources вЂ” the focus
pause (`FocusHelper.cs:67-77`, `Main.cs:17130-17141`; an unfocused window
freezes the world unless `play_when_unfocused`, with the pointer-release
edges cleared) and the in-world gate `App::can_pause_game` (`CanPauseGame`,
`Main.cs:17194-17201/17315-17327`) вЂ” and the world body gates on
`step_allowed` (`Main.cs:17278`) whose stepper half is `world_stepper.rs`, a
verbatim `WorldUpdateStepper.cs` port, with `game_update_count`
(`Main.cs:6444`) pinning the step count. The deliberate deviations:

- **`DoUpdate_WhilePaused` is a shell** (`Main.cs:17329-17407`,
  `app/mod.rs::do_update_while_paused`). The C#'s portable arms resolve
  elsewhere in the port: the inventory toggle, the wheel scrolling and the
  held-item drops are event-driven and run while paused already; the armor
  display rows are draw-driven; the tile-target arms (`Player.tileTargetX/Y`
  + `LookForTileInteractions`/`ChestChangeEvents`/`UpdateNearbyCraftingTiles`,
  `:17398-17406`) stay frozen вЂ” the port fuses them into the step-gated
  `update_editing`, so no target updates while paused (the C# polls them in
  the paused body).
- **The absent arms**: the `ManageControlsMenu` controls-rebind half, the
  creative menu and the `RefreshInfoAccs` info-accessories pass have no port
  equivalent, and `LocalPlayer.sign >= 0` has no sign UI to gate (both in
  `can_pause_game` and the shell).
- **The audio focus gates** (`PauseSounds`/`AllowMusic`) are deferred to the
  sound rows (S1-E-21/24) вЂ” the port has no sound engine yet.
- **`DrawnThisUpdate`** (`WorldUpdateStepper.cs:9`) is tracked 1:1 (false at
  the step head, `Main.cs:17747`; true on the draw side, `:62478`) but its
  emit-effect consumers are unported (S1-E-1) вЂ” nothing reads it yet.
- **The Update/Draw fusion**: the C# returns early from `Update` while
  paused and `Draw` keeps running; the port's fused frame turns that return
  into branch gating вЂ” `step_allowed` skips the world pass, draw never
  skips. Same pixels: the frozen world still renders, the UI stays live.
- **The one-frame-lag EmoteBubble quirk** (the C# pause body leaving the
  bubble to draw from the last update's state) is not reproduced вЂ” the
  port's emote bubbles keep their live draw while paused.
- **`pauseworld`** (the stepper's `Paused`, `ToolkitDebugCommands.cs:742-749`)
  rides the debug panel's World-tab row вЂ” the port has no chat-command
  dispatcher; the step-key set is End/NumpadAdd/XButton1
  (`GetStepKeyState`, `:39-43`) mapped onto winit's Back.
- **The map reveal keeps the pause gate only** (no stepper gate): its C#
  source is the draw-side `LightingEngine.ExportToMiniMap` export
  (`LightingEngine.cs:246-270`) вЂ” draw runs on stepper-blocked frames, so
  vanilla keeps revealing the map while the world steps are frozen.

(`412b6bc0`, the `62 SyncDodge` reader/relay + `Player.apply_net_dodge`);
the handlers are REUSED, not re-ported.

   handler's C# tail (`NinjaDodge` `:38161-38164` kind 1, `ShadowDodge`
   `:38038` kind 2, `BrainOfConfusionDodge` `:38050-38054` kind 4,
   `DoMysticSashDodge` `:38113-38116` kind 5) queues its kind byte on
   `Player.pending_dodge_sends` **at the `hurt_inner` roll arm**, NOT inside
   the shared handler — c27's `apply_net_dodge` reader calls the same
   handlers and the C# reader never re-sends (`MessageBuffer.cs:2887-2902`).
   `net_tick` drains the queue EVERY tick ahead of the 10 Hz state batch
   (the C# send is inline in `Hurt`; the `take_hurt_sound` convention):

`Player.Hurt`'s `magicCuffs` arm (`Player.cs:38291-38303`) lands in
`player.rs::hurt_inner`, slotted between the defense reduction (`:38247`) and
the endurance step (`:38304`): `num3 = (int)(num * 1f)` is the RAW incoming
damage (the C# `num` at `:38246` вЂ” the defense-reduced `num2` never feeds it),
`statMana += num3` capped at `statManaMax2` (`:38295-38298`), and
`ManaEffect(num3)` (`:4531-4538`) queues the HealMana combat text with the
UNCAPPED amount. The port hands the amount over via `pending_mana_effect` /
`take_mana_effect` (the `pending_hurt_sound` convention); the drain in

hitbox with `HEAL_MANA = (100, 100, 255)` (`CombatText.cs:228`), the placement
`Next` draws riding the `UpdatePlayers` stream like the melee-hit text
(`world_sim/editing.rs`). The flag folds per tick: the Magic Cuffs (1595,
`ApplyEquipFunctional` `:14936-14939`) and the Celestial Cuffs (2221,
`:14949-14953`) arm `magic_cuffs`; `ResetEffects` clears it (`:18599`).

Documented gaps, all deliberate:

- **The crit Г—2** (`Crit в†’ num *= 2`, `:38248-38251`): **landed with S1-C-7
  wave B** вЂ” `hurt_inner` carries the `crit` flag and doubles `raw` AFTER the
  defense-input capture (`num2` reads the PRE-crit damage), so the cuffs
  restore the doubled raw `num`. Every ported caller passes `crit = false`
  (the single-player C# lanes all do); the flag rides for parity + the maths

  star attraction radius); only the `magicCuffs` grant lands.

occupied slots packing). The per-slot alpha (`Main.buffAlpha`) lives on the

same value), the hover raises it 0.1 and the rest decays 0.05 clamped to
[0.4, 1]; the duration text gates through `TryGetBuffTime` (the
vanity/light-pet sets вЂ” already ported вЂ” plus the generated 124-id
`BUFF_NO_TIME_DISPLAY` table, the honey-48 wet gate, the expert wet-46
gate and the vampire seed's sub-10 hides for 23/24/32) and formats through

mount's own buff dismounting instead of `DelBuff` вЂ” and the
`SoundEngine.PlaySound(12)` MenuTick cue rides the tick drain.

Deliberate sequencing (not silent gaps):

- **The removal is a request**, not an in-draw mutation: the C# deletes the

  `GetBuffTooltip`) stays out of this pass вЂ” it rides the localization

## The buff cancel / right-click census (S1-P-i53, 2026-11-20)

The cancel/right-click surface re-audited against the C#; five WRONGs fixed
verbatim, witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN (code-only mode):

- **The alive-player drain.** The `buff_removals` drain sat INSIDE
  `update_player`'s `p.dead` branch (`world_sim/player.rs`), so a living
  player's cancel requests were never applied вЂ” the C# draw has no dead gate
  (`Main.cs:43329-43349`). The drain moved before the dead branch.
- **The cancel gate.** `DrawBuffIcon` reads `Main.mouseRight &&
  Main.mouseRightRelease` (`Main.cs:43333`) with the vanilla's end-of-draw
  latch recompute (`:62458-62465`: `mouseRightRelease = !mouseRight`) вЂ” the
  conjunction fires on the PRESS frame after a released frame. The port
  passed the bare winit release edge, firing one frame late on the RELEASE
  frame. `App::ui_right_release_latch` + `App::buff_cancel_gate` mirror the
  latch (the button state cannot change mid-draw, so the head-of-draw
  recompute equals the C#'s tail-of-draw one).

  43386`) latches `flag = true` on the `CheckBuff` match REGARDLESS of the
  `TryDismount` result вЂ” a refused dismount keeps the buff (no `DelBuff`).
  The port called the ungated `MountState::dismount` and never checked
  `CanDismountWithResult` (`Mount.cs:6611-6624`). Now: `try_dismount` runs
  the CC gate (`DontDismountWhenCCed` 55/56/61, `MountID.cs:47` вЂ” the old

  the cart ride routes through `try_cart_dismount` (its state lives outside

## The `.plr` legacy-subset shim + default policy (S1-J-5 increment 1)

The pre-S1-J-5 `.plr` writer was a **subset mirror** stamped release 279: it
stopped after the 58-slot inventory and omitted `team` (release 283),
`hideMisc` (119), the dead 324 bool and the 322 armour/dye favourited bools.
Those files are **not valid vanilla 279 files** вЂ” the C# `Deserialize` gates
would read `hideMisc` and run off the end вЂ” so they cannot be read through the
C# walk. `player_file::read_legacy_port_subset` is a **port-only backward-compat
shim**: `read_player_bytes` first tries the faithful gate walk, and on a
truncation error for a file stamped exactly 279 retries the old subset layout.
This is a deliberate deviation (the shim has no C# counterpart); it exists only
so characters saved by older port builds keep loading. New saves stamp 326
(`Player.cs:54738`) and never take the shim.

**Default-value policy.** The port models only the character-card state; every
other field the writer emits through `voidVaultInfo` (`Serialize:54863`) carries
the fresh-vanilla default (the `Player` ctor `Player.cs:56036-56096` + field
initializers) вЂ” play time 0, empty banks/misc slots, no favourites outside the
inventory. The reader's inventory guard uses `ItemID.Count = 6196`
(`ItemID.cs:14861`); the old subset reader's 5455 was stale and wrongly
air-gapped the 5455..6195 band (the shim keeps the corrected constant вЂ” the old
writer never emitted ids in that band, so old saves read identically).
Increment 1 ends at `voidVaultInfo`; the `Serialize` tail (`:54864-54933`) is
the next round, so a port `.plr` is byte-comparable with vanilla **through the
vault byte** only until then.

**Increment 2 (S1-J-5b, 2026-11-18).** The writer/reader now run through
`hideInfo` (`Serialize:54893` / `Deserialize:55623`): buffs (`:54864-54876` вЂ”
44 pairs, `maxBuffs` `Player.cs:57106`; fresh `buffType`/`buffTime` are all-zero
`:1510-1512` and `Main.buffNoSave[0]` is false, so the (0,0) else-arm bytes are
identical to the no-save arm), the spawn list (`:54877-54888` вЂ” fresh
`spN[0] == null` `:2488` writes only the `-1` sentinel), `hbLocked`
(`:54889`, default false `:1436`) and `hideInfo[13]` (`:54890-54893`, fresh
`bool[13]` `:812`). The reader gates mirror `Deserialize:55578-55623`, including
the buff-count 44/22/10 version gates and the zero-type compaction
(`:55593-55597`, which still consumes exactly `count` pairs). **Second shim**:
the increment-1 port files are stamped 326 but end at the vault byte, so the
C# gates would truncate in the buffs; `read_player_bytes` retries release-326
truncations with `through_vault_only` (stop at `:55504`), the same port-only
pattern as the 279 shim. Genuine vanilla 326 files never take it (they always
carry the buffs tail). `golden_layout_through_hide_info` pins every byte and
byte-compares the 370-byte tail with `assets/test/golden.plr` at offsets
2402-2772. A port `.plr` is now byte-comparable with vanilla **through the last
hideInfo bool**; the remainder is `:54894-54933`. Note: the C# envelope uses
RijndaelManaged's default PKCS7 padding (`Player.cs:54734-54736`) while the
port zero-pads to the block boundary вЂ” invisible to field readers, but the
final encrypted block differs from vanilla; full-envelope parity is a separate
concern. *(Resolved by increment 3 below.)*

**Increment 3 (S1-J-5c, 2026-11-18): the full `Serialize` + PKCS7.** The
writer/reader now run the WHOLE `Serialize` (`Player.cs:54750-54933`) /
`Deserialize` (`:55134-55764`). The tail (`:54894-54933`), every unmodelled
field at its fresh-ctor default: `anglerQuestsFinished` 0 (`:1910`),
`DpadRadial.Bindings[4]` all -1 (the Dpad4 ctor, `:618-621`),
`builderAccStatus[12]` = `[1,0Г—11]` (`:814` + `BuilderAccToggleIDs.Count = 12`
`:47-75`; the ctor's `[0] = 1` `:56092`), `bartenderQuestLog` 0 (`:1914`),
`dead` false (the respawnTimer is written only when dead, `:54905-54908`),
the save timestamp, `golferScoreAccumulated` 0 (`:1912`), the creative
tracker (`CreativeUnlocksTracker.Save:9-12` в†’ `ItemsSacrificedUnlocksTracker
.Save:157-169`: the literal `false` + count 0), the temp-slot BitsByte 0
(`SaveTemporaryItemSlotContents:54935-54959` вЂ” all four global slots air),
the per-player creative powers (`CreativePowerManager.SaveToPlayer:183-195`
over the `Initialize:86-105` registration order: `(true, u16 5, false)`
Godmode `CreativePowers.cs:705-707`, `(true, u16 11, false)` FarPlacement
`:744-746`, `(true, u16 14, 0f)` SpawnRate `:1717-1719`, then `false`), the
super-cart BitsByte **2** (`unlockedSuperCart` false `:2052`,
`enabledSuperCart` **true** `:2054`), `CurrentLoadoutIndex` 0 (`:3207`),
three `EquipmentLoadout.Serialize` (`EquipmentLoadout.cs:31-45`: 20 armor +
10 dye Г— `Item.Serialize(writeFavorite: true)` = 10 zero bytes each, then
`Hide[10]` false вЂ” 310 bytes per loadout), `voiceVariant` **1** (the ctor
`:56045`, NOT the field default 0), `voicePitchOffset` 0f (`:1348`),
`CraftingRequests.SavePossibleRefunds` count 0 (`CraftingRequests.cs:353-362`)
and `oneTimeDialoguesSeen` count 0 (`:3209`). The reader mirrors
`Deserialize:55624-55762` with the version gates (the builderAcc 8/10/11/12
count gates, the dead-conditional respawnTimer, the tracker's >= 282 bool,
the power loop's unknown-id BREAK `CreativePowerManager.cs:203-206`, the
loadout favourited >= 322 gate). **The one unowned value** is
`DateTime.UtcNow.ToBinary()` (`:54909`): it rides
`PlayerFileWrite::last_saved_binary` (the App stamps 0 = "unknown", the same
policy as the `.wld` CreationTime); the golden test pins the harness's
`FixtureClock` value `0x48DF4506E391C000` (2026-11-18T00:00:00Z, kind Utc).
**PKCS7**: `cbc_encrypt` now appends `n = 16 - len % 16` bytes of value `n`
(a full block when aligned) вЂ” the bare `new RijndaelManaged()` default of
`InternalSavePlayerFile` (`:54734`) flushed by `FlushFinalBlock` (`:54742`);
the read path keeps `PaddingMode.None` semantics (`:55074` вЂ” whole blocks,
padding never stripped, `Deserialize` stops at the logical end). The
**harness had the same bug**: `tools/WldFixtureHarness` zero-padded with
`PaddingMode.None`; it now uses `PaddingMode.PKCS7` and `golden.plr` was
regenerated (same 3840 bytes; the final block now decrypts to 3 data bytes +
13 Г— 0x0D). **Third shim**: the increment-2 port files end at `hideInfo`, so
`read_player_bytes` retries 326 truncations at depth 2 (stop at `:55623`)
after the depth-1 vault retry. **Evidence**:
`golden_plr_writer_matches_the_csharp_fixture_byte_for_byte` вЂ” the port's
encrypted output for the fixture's player + pinned clock is byte-identical
to the C#-written `assets/test/golden.plr` (all 3840 bytes, plaintext 3827 +
PKCS7 13); `golden_layout_through_hide_info` pins every tail field and
byte-compares offsets 2402-3827 (timestamp spliced); `the_write_envelope_is_pkcs7`
pins the pad rule incl. the aligned full-block case. No new dependency вЂ”
the existing `aes` crate's raw block API carries the PKCS7 by hand (13 lines).

## The loadout system (W4-g55, 2026-11-21)

The three-loadout equipment swap (`Player.Loadouts[3]` / `CurrentLoadoutIndex`,
`Player.cs:3200-3207`) is ported: `loadout::EquipmentLoadout` (Armor[20] +
Dye[10] + Hide[10] + a 30-bit share word) with `Swap` (`EquipmentLoadout.cs:63-80`),
`Player::try_switching_loadout`'s two-swap rotation + the `:5663` gate
(`!UsingOrReusingItem && !CCed && !dead`, index differs and is in range) and the
next/previous modulo wrappers (`:5651-5659`). The live equipment rides
`App.equip`; the share flags (`Item.favorited` in the `canLoadoutShareAt`
contexts 8-12) ride `App.equip_share_flags` (the grid favourites stay
`App.favorite_slots`). `GetEffectiveArmor`/`GetEffectiveDye` (`:5690-5764`) +
`CanShareArmor` (`:5712-5740`) supply an air live slot from the first shared
loadout item, over the per-tick `armor_items`/`dye_items` snapshot; the dye
snapshot (`dye_slots`) now rides `GetEffectiveDye`. The UI is
`Main.DrawLoadoutButtons` (`Main.cs:41935-41991`) on `Extra_259` (`Frame(3,3)`),
the equipment-slot tint follows the current loadout's `LoadoutSlotColors` row +
the 30-frame change flash (`ItemSlot.cs:2778-2837`), and Alt+click toggles the
share (`ToggleLoadoutShare` + `ClearSlotShareInOtherLoadouts`, `:879-912`).

**Serialization.** The `.plr` writer/reader carry `CurrentLoadoutIndex` +
`Loadouts[3]` (`Serialize:54919-54923` / `Deserialize:55720-55727`, the >= 322
favourited gate, the `ItemID.Count` air-gap, the `Utils.Clamp` index); a fresh
character's three empty sets reproduce the golden 310-zero-byte block, so the
full-file byte parity with `golden.plr` is untouched. The in-game `.trplayer`
sidecar gains a **v7** loadout block (index + live share word + the three stored
sets as kinds/hide/share); v6-and-older files load on loadout 0 with empty sets.

**Recorded deviations / skips.**
- The vanilla F1/F2/F3 = Loadout1/2/3 keys (`PlayerInput.cs:2088-2090` →
  `TriggersSet.cs:805-824`) stay the port's debug bindings (F1 debug overlay,

- The `ParticleOrchestraType.LoadoutChange` tail of `TrySwitchingLoadout`

  particle orchestration is unported); the 12 cue + `RecordLoadoutChange` +

**Landed since the Ph5 note (dev-1/2/3/4 + the loadout-rest retire round,
research/362):** the `Extra_310..315` share-badge corner icons
(`ItemSlot.cs:2733-2746`, dev-1 — packed + drawn at `Color.White*0.7*num17`);
the `clientCloneLoadouts` item-array half (`Player.cs:54522-54531`, dev-3 —
`LoadoutClone` + `App.loadout_clone`); the `TrySendData(147)` send-on-swap +

## The save files' wall clock + the SavePlayer envelope (W4-c43)

`tr_core::clock` is the one seam for the .NET `DateTime` stamps both file
formats carry: ticks are 100 ns units since 0001-01-01 (the Unix epoch sits
at tick 621355968000000000), and `ToBinary` packs a 2-bit kind into bits
62-63 (`Utc` = bit 62). Deliberate deviations:

- **Every stamp the port writes is Utc-kind.** `CreationTime`'s C# source
  is `DateTime.Now` (`WorldFile.CreateMetadata:600`, kind Local); the port
  owns no time-zone database, so it stamps `UtcNow` instead. Reads mask
  the kind bits off (`from_binary_ticks`); a foreign Local-kind stamp is
  read as its stored ticks without the offset round-trip.
- **`Guid.NewGuid` is a clock-seeded `UnifiedRandom` draw** shaped to v4
  (version nibble 4, RFC-4122 variant bits) — .NET's GUID is cryptographic,
  which a deterministic port cannot reproduce; the shape and
  uniqueness-per-creation contract are what the format needs.
- **The WorldId roll stays out of the worldgen streams.** The C# rolls
  `WorldId = genRand.Next(int.MaxValue)` mid-`GenerateWorld`
  (`WorldGen.cs:11337`); inserting that draw into the port's frozen
  contract streams would move every world hash, so the creation tails roll
  it from a fresh `identity_rng()` (same value range) after generation.

The world identity lands as: the creation tails (`create_world_in`,
`WorldGenJob`'s Completed arm) run `wld::stamp_created_identity`
(`CreateMetadata:600-604`) + the WorldId roll; the save funnel stamps
`world.last_played = utc_now_binary()` on every save (`SaveWorldFlags:1251`
writes `UtcNow`, never the loaded value); `load_world` runs the load-side
fallbacks (`LoadHeader:1962-1969`: a pre-181 `.wld` gets a fresh GUID, a
v >= 181 one keeps its stored GUID even when Guid.Empty — only a pre-v18
`.trwld`'s zero reads as absent; `GetFileData:315-318`'s mtime LastPlayed
for a zero stamp). The native
`.trwld` grows a **v18 identity tail** (generator version u64, GUID 16 B,
world id i32, CreationTime/LastPlayed i64 each — `WorldFile.cs:1225-1227,
1250-1251`); pre-v18 files load the zeros the old saves carried. The
determinism contract narrows accordingly: a double-save pair is byte-equal
**modulo the LastPlayed long** (the C# is wall-clock-bearing there too) —
`test_DW_7_2`/`test_DW_7_3`/the `.bak` rotation test pin the normalized
pairs; the worldgen tile hashes are untouched (the identity fields are not
in `world_hash`'s fold).

**The `.plr` envelope (Ph2).** The S1-J-5c "App stamps 0" policy is
retired: `save_created_character` now stamps `utc_now_binary()` (the
`Serialize:54909` `DateTime.UtcNow.ToBinary()` — `CreateAndSave` runs
`SavePlayer` like any save, `PlayerFileData.cs:58`). The envelope completes
`InternalSavePlayerFile`: an existing `.plr` is copied to `<path>.bak`
before the write (`:54730-54733`), and the metadata revision rides
`PlayerFileWrite::revision` (`:54739` writes the loaded `playerFile.
Metadata` verbatim — `Write`, NOT `IncrementAndWrite`; a fresh character's
`FromCurrentSettings` revision is 0, a re-save threads the read counter
back). The reader now keeps `lastTimePlayerWasSaved`
(`Deserialize:55687-55691`, the >= 202 gate) on
`PlayerFile::last_saved_binary` and runs the `LoadPlayer:55096-55098`
fallback — a zero stamp reads `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(path).ToBinary()`
(`tr_core::clock::file_mtime_binary`; the port has no cloud saves, so the
`!cloudSave` arm is the only one). Witnesses (written not run, code-only):
`w4_c43_a_re_save_copies_the_previous_plr_into_the_bak`,
`w4_c43_the_metadata_revision_rides_the_write`,
`w4_c43_the_save_timestamp_round_trips` (incl. the C# fixture's pinned
stamp), `w4_c43_a_zero_stamp_falls_back_to_the_file_mtime`,
`w4_c43_the_timestamp_is_version_gated` (a 201-restamped stream with every
post-201 gate stripped reads aligned, stamp 0). The golden byte-parity
tests are untouched — the fixture's revision is 0 and its clock is the
caller-supplied pin.

## The `.wld` header/flags SECOND half (W4-f45)

`task/W4-f45-wld-header-2` (code-only, 2026-11-21, base = W4-c43's tip
`07697080`) claims the remaining header/flags fields that have live port
state or a faithful gen/death source, in four phases. Every claim is a
`World` field the `.wld` flags writer/reader (`wld/sections/flags.rs`)
round-trips; the App-owned schedulers snapshot into the World at save
(`saveglue.rs::save_world`, the `SetTempToOngoing` shape) and restore at
load (`app/mod.rs`, `from_wld`-gated so a `.trwld`'s zeros never clobber the
live defaults).

- **Ph1 — the downed-flag census.** `downedClown`/`downedEmpressOfLight`
  (`WorldFile.cs:1297`/`:1395`) round-trip (their kinds — Clown 109,
  HallowBoss 636 — are unported, so no live setter yet). The five seasonal
  bosses (`downedHalloweenKing/Tree`, `downedChristmasIceQueen/Santank/Tree`,
  `:1347-1351`) gain their moon-gated death arms (`NPC.cs:79210-79239`):
  the kill counts only while `pumpkin_moon`/`snow_moon` is up,
  `SetEventFlagCleared`'s false→true transition guard fires the progression
  notify, and `OnGameEventClearedForTheFirstTime` (`:78769-78793`) arms the
  next lantern night for events 5/20 (the default arm) but NOT 4/21/22 (the
  explicit no-op arm).
- **Ph2 — the eight secret-seed bytes.** `forceHalloweenForever`/
  `forceXMasForever`/`vampireSeed`/`infectedSeed`/`teamBasedSpawnsSeed`/
  `dualDungeonsSeed`/`moreLightningSeed`/`noLightningSeed` (`:1418-1428`)
  are the `InitializeSecretSeeds` mirrors of `World.micro_seeds`
  (`WorldGen.cs:553-587`) — the same bits the `.trwld` v12 tail carries.
  The `.wld` now derives them on load (the old "the `.wld` parse does not
  derive `micro_seeds`" deviation is retired).
- **Ph3 — the event snapshots + flavour.** `cultistDelay` (`:1340`), the
  party quad + celebrant list (`:1361-1368`), the lantern quad
  (`:1381-1384`), `windSpeedTarget` (`:1328`), `savedBartender` (`:1373`),
  `dungeonX/Y` (`:1279-1280`) and `WorldGen.crimson` (`:1281`). The
  schedulers' live state (`App.world_events`) and `App.wind.speed_target`
  snapshot at save; the load restores them (the wind restores BOTH target
  and current, `:2147`). The generator stamps the dungeon anchor
  (`pipeline.rs::step_dungeon`, the drunk arm's `worldSurface + 70` row) and
  the crimson flavour (`GenOptions.crimson`). **The flattened v107/108/109/
  128 read gates are restored** (`LoadWorldFlags:2180-2208`): below 107
  `invasionSizeStart` is re-derived by `FakeLoadInvasionStart`
  (`Main.cs:64488-64514`), below 108 the cultist delay defaults to 86400,
  below 109 the block ends, below 128 the dawn byte is absent. The angler
  quest gate now reads `world.crimson` (the old "no evil-kind field"
  deviation retired).
- **Ph4 — the banner tally, the angler list, the spawn unlocks.**
  `BannerSystem.killCount[]` (`:1341`) densifies from `App.banners` into
  `World.banner_kill_counts` (the banner ids ARE the C# array indices —
  `bestiary::npc_to_banner` mirrors `NPCtoBanner`); the claimable array
  stays unowned (the port spawns the banner item at the death spot).
  `anglerWhoFinishedToday` (`:1329-1333`) carries the real name list (the
  turn-in pushes the player's name, the day reset clears it). The seven
  spawn unlocks — `unlockedSlimeBlueSpawn` (King Slime death,
  `NPC.cs:79411`) + the six arrival unlocks (`WorldGen.cs:5577-5608`) —
  gain their setters and the `SpawnAllowed_*` overrides
  (`NPC.cs:7069/7094/7119/7160/7177`).

**Deliberate deviations.** The party celebrant list carries the C#'s stable
`Main.npc` slots, but the port's live list indexes the compacted `Vec<Npc>`
(the recorded `world_events.rs` deviation) — the slots are written as-is; a
compacted-list remap is the follow-up. The Truffle's housing-gate consumer
(`housing.rs:456`) keeps its parameter (the Truffle kind is unported, so the
flag round-trips without a live reader). The Clown/Empress/bartender latches
round-trip without live setters (their kinds/rescue paths are unported).

**Still unowned (no port state, written at the C# default):** claimableBanners,
the treeTop variation table, the world-gen manifest JSON (all three the W4-c44
golden-fixture lane owns), and forceHalloweenForToday/forceXMasForToday (the
W4-f39 season lane). The set below was claimed in the second pass (Ph5-Ph13).

### Second pass (Ph5-Ph13): the remaining unowned census

`task/W4-f45-wld-header-2` continues on the same branch (base `42b7363b`) and
claims the rest of the header/flags fields that have a live port consumer in an
in-flight lane or a faithful gen/death/use source. Every claim is a `World`
field the `.wld` flags writer/reader round-trips; the byte offsets are
hand-derived against the `flags_tail` running widths and pinned by the
`expected_flags_block` independent table + the owned-world sweep.

- **Ph5 — GameMode** (`WorldFile.cs:1240` write / `:1985` read): the world's
  difficulty i32 (0 Classic / 1 Expert / 2 Master / 3 Journey), the W4-e25
  expert/master scaling lane's consumer. The pre-209 read gates are ported: the
  expert bool from 112 (`:2031`), the v208 master byte (`:2037-2040`), classic
  below 112 (`:2035`). `GenOptions.game_mode` stamps the creation draft's
  `_optionDifficulty` (`UIWorldCreation.cs:129`) through both create paths; the
  `WorldInfo` wire carries the byte.
- **Ph6 — the tree/cave back-style tables** (`:1253-1268` / `:2051-2066`):
  `treeX[3]`/`treeStyle[4]`/`caveBackX[3]`/`caveBackStyle[4]` +
  `iceBackStyle`/`jungleBackStyle`, the W4-g72 bg-layers lane's consumers. The
  gen roll ports `RandomizeTreeStyle` (`WorldGen.cs:8117-8190`) +
  `RandomizeCaveBackgrounds` (`:8192-8249`) — the per-size zone branches (small
  2 / medium 3 / large 4), the distinct `Next(6)`/`Next(8)` style rolls with the
  collision re-roll loops, the tree 0->4 reroll, the unused-boundary
  `maxTilesX` fill. **Deviation:** the C# draws the tables BEFORE the moon/hell
  rolls (`:11338-11341`); the port keeps its frozen moon->hell order (the
  `worldgen_rolls_hell_back_style` pin) and draws the tables between them — the
  port's xorshift stream is not byte-comparable with the C#'s Knuth one anyway
  (research/35 #5), so this is the accepted stream deviation.
- **Ph7 — cloudBGActive/numClouds** (`:1326-1327` / `:2142-2145`): the W4-g69
  CloudField lane's mirrors. **Deviation:** the C# load reads `cloudBGActive`
  then RE-ROLLS it (`:2144` `-genRand.Next(8640, 86400)`); the port reads the
  stored value into the World mirror for the round-trip but the App's live
  machine (the g69 lane) owns the re-roll. `numClouds` restores as-is (the short
  cast).
- **Ph8 — afterPartyOfDoom** (`:1305` / `:2109`, v257): the getfixedboi
  anniversary doom party. The gen Reset arm (`WorldGen.cs:11128-11137`) stamps
  it (tenth anniversary + get-good, not skyblock) plus the genuine party / 5-day
  cooldown; the `UpdateWorld_NPCs` consumer (`Main.cs:17926-17943`) kills every
  town NPC (minus the five exclusions — only TravellingMerchant 368 / Dryad 20
  have ported kinds) once the party ends, clearing the mech/party-girl/princess/
  rainbow/green unlocks + the bunny license. The strike is the port's hp=0
  instant-kill deviation.
- **Ph9 — meteorShowerCount/coinRain** (`:1422-1423` / `:2490-2491`, v291): the
  starfall events. `StartMeteorShower` (`WorldGen.cs:6239-6244`) rolls
  `Next(650,751)*4`; the `HandleMeteorFall` failed-pick arm now draws
  `Next(3)==0` into it (`Main.cs:65497-65500` — the `resolve` previously skipped
  the draw). `StartRain` stores `coinRain` (`Main.cs:64672-64673`), `StopRain`
  clears it (`:64651`); `rain.rs`'s `start_rain`/`stop_rain`/`update_time` take
  `&mut World`. The star/coin projectiles are unported, so the values round-trip
  without spawns.
- **Ph10 — extraSpawnPoints** (`:1425` / `:2501`, v297): the team-based extra
  respawn anchors, the W4-c46 respawn lane's consumer.
  `ExtraSpawnPointManager.cs:436-456`'s count byte + (i16 X, i16 Y) pairs; the
  variable-length `expected_flags_block` splice carries them.
- **Ph11 — boughtCat/Dog/Bunny** (`:1392-1394` / `:2358-2360`, v217): the pet
  licenses, the W4-f43 town-spawn lane's `TailFlags` consumers. The license
  use-setters (`Player.cs:45352-45366`) ride the item-use lane (the combat-book
  v1 precedent — the latches round-trip).
- **Ph12 — combatBookVolumeTwoWasUsed/peddlersSatchelWasUsed** (`:1407-1408` /
  `:2418`/`:2426`, v259/260): the boosters, the W4-g89b lane co-claims the
  consumers (`npc_ai_town.rs`'s `combat_book_two` env); the use-setters

- **Ph13 — the five remaining slime-colour unlocks** (green/old/purple/yellow/

**Determinism.** The new fields are not in `world_hash`'s fold (the tile
hashes are untouched); the gen stamps (dungeon anchor, crimson, the tree/cave
tables, the doom party) are deterministic functions of the options/seed. The
`.wld` flags block grows by the variable celebrant/angler/extra-spawn lists —
the `expected_flags_block` table computes the shifts, and the owned-world sweep
pins the whole block.

Witnesses (written NOT run, code-only): the Ph1 seasonal-death census
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`), the Ph1-Ph13 offset+gate witnesses

## The world-format contract (S1-J-8)

**Decision: the two-format split stays, as a documented contract.** The port
keeps `.trwld` (native) and `.wld` (vanilla-shaped) as different routes with
different jobs; converging them would either drop the vanilla-world
interoperability or force the native format to be byte-vanilla, and both cost
more than the doubled save surface they would save.

- **`.trwld` is the canonical save route.** Every new piece of persisted state
  lands here first as a versioned tail block (v13 signs/plates, v14 the rain
  triple, v15 `downedQueenSlime`), the loader version-gates each block and a
  pre-N file loads with that block's reset defaults. The production boot world
  (`app::latest_own_world`) and the save routing (`is_native_trwld`) already
  make it the live surface.
- **`.wld` is the vanilla-interchange route.** Loading vanilla worlds
  (field-by-field codecs, the C# version gates) and writing them back at the
  byte SHAPE the vanilla expects. Its value coverage is a documented subset
  (the flags writer zero-fills the rain/Queen-Slime bytes, the loader
  skip-reads unimplemented sections) вЂ” the byte-parity tasks (S1-J-1's wire
  bits, S1-J-3's golden fixture) grow that coverage only where parity is
  actually demanded, against the C#'s own `SaveWorld` layout.
- **Stage-2 cost, bounded.** The two readers stay, but only `.trwld` is the
  live save surface вЂ” the `.wld` route is load-dominant interchange, so the
  compressor/reader doubling applies to the interchange path only. The
  app-side twins that neither format carries (the TownManager rooms, the
  bestiary sights/chats, the CreativePowers table вЂ” the recorded M6-SAVE-1b
  remainder) need a `WorldSide` twin on the app save path, not a format
  convergence.
- **The routing rule** (`is_native_trwld`, `app/mod.rs:3074`): the save picks
  the format by the world path's extension; a `.trwld` world saves native, a
  `.wld` world saves vanilla-shaped вЂ” the user's file never changes identity
  mid-session.
## The map reveal + refresh (S1-L-3, 2026-11-13)

The audit's D10 is closed: `WorldMap::update`'s reveal window now follows
`LightingEngine.ExportToMiniMap` (`LightingEngine.cs:246-262`) вЂ” the
engine's processed area shrunk 28 px per side, intersected with the world
bounds inset 40 and `MapHelper.sceneArea` (the scene-metrics scan's
player-centred `SceneMetrics.ZoneScanSize` box, `SceneMetrics.cs:917-919` =
169Г—124 tiles). The old fixed player-centred 75Г—47 box (smaller than
vanilla, trail-prone at speed) is gone; a stale/empty scene area intersects
to nothing, exactly like the C#'s `Rectangle.Empty` static. The view
centre rides the processed area (camera-centred), matching every other map
consumer.

The refresh machinery is ported whole: `WorldMap.UpdateType`/`QueueUpdate`
(`WorldMap.cs:65-105` вЂ” the queued re-derive keeps the light; the C#'s
`ref mapTile` flag-clear write-through is explicit in the port so the
clear persists on the early returns), `MapUpdateQueue`'s two queues with
the `WorldMap.QueueUpdate` dedupe (`MapUpdateQueue.cs:21-108`), the
per-frame drain (`Main.cs:61862`) feeding the minimap upload (the
`MapRenderer.QueueChange` analog), `UnlockMapSection`/`UnlockMapTilePretty`
(`WorldMap.cs:109-174` вЂ” the Manhattan falloff with the solid/lava skips
and the wall 0.8 / underground 0.7 tints) and `ClearEdges` at the map load
(`:210`).

Scope notes:

- **The edit hooks cover the player-edit paths** (the pickaxe/hammer/
  placement funnel in `world_sim/editing.rs`): the edited tile's
  `SquareTileFrame` ring queues (`WorldGen.cs:81334`'s head over
  `:80185-80197`'s walk). The projectile-side craters (the bombs, the
  magical ice) run inside the AI with a world-only signature вЂ” their map
  refresh rides the follow-up; the reveal pass still re-derives any tile
  it covers, so in-window craters refresh naturally.
- **`Main.sectionManager.TileLoaded(x, y)` passes** (`WorldMap.cs:80`): the
  section manager is the MP section tracker; the port's single-player world
  is fully loaded.
- **The fullscreen-map call site** (`Main.cs:41335`'s column layout) rides
  the map tasks (S1-L-4's layers).

### Second pass (2026-11-16): the driver

The primitives above were already present (the audit's "MISSING" rows for
`UnlockMapSection`/`ClearEdges`/`MapUpdateQueue` were stale). What was missing
was the *caller* and the *throttle*:

- **`UnlockMapSection` had no caller.** The `/map` chat command
  (`ToolkitDebugCommands.cs:480-494`) sets `DebugOptions.unlockMap` and
  `Main.refreshMap`, which Main consumes at `:61873-61877` by walking the
  section manager's draw queue. The port has no section manager (the whole
  world is resident), so `WorldMap::unlock_map` walks every 200Г—150 section
  directly; `unlock_section` applies the same `Utils.Clamp(v, 40, max-40)`
  the C# does (`WorldMap.cs:111-119`) to the dirty rect it re-uploads.
  Exposed as the F3 World-tab row "Reveal Map (pretty)" вЂ” the missing chat
  dispatcher is why the debug panel carries it.
- **The refresh was a `dt` timer, not `mapTime`.** `WorldMap::update` used a
  hardcoded 0.25 s accumulator; the C# gates `ExportToMiniMap` on
  `Main.mapTime == 0` (`LegacyLighting.cs:349`) after decrementing it per
  frame (`Main.cs:61818-61821`) and re-arming from `mapTimeMax`
  (`:16995-17000`, the gfx-quality budget вЂ” 0 above quality 0.8, which is why
  a good machine exports every frame). The port now carries `map_time`/
  `map_time_max` and the frame feeds `gfx_quality.map_time_max` in; `dt` is
  ignored. `mapDelay` and the `renderCount == 3` phase gate ride the same
  legacy-engine state the port has no equivalent of (it exports inline), so
  only the `mapTime` half is modelled.

### The map section grid + reveal queue (W4-e18 first half, 2026-11-21, code-only)

The second-half reveal window (above) landed without its driver: the C#'s
`Main.cs:61863-61899` block walks `Main.sectionManager` — a `WorldSections`
grid — under a 5 ms wall-clock budget, and nothing in the port constructed
or walked it. This pass lands the whole first half:

- **`map_sections.rs::MapSections`** ports `WorldSections.cs:6-358` verbatim:
  the `maxTilesX / 200` × `maxTilesY / 150` grid (`WorldGen.cs:7150`, integer
  division truncating — NOT the wire's round-up `net::sections_x/y`), the
  four `BitsByte` flags (loaded/framed/mapDrawn/needsRefresh) in one byte per
  section, `IterationState`'s off-grid `(-3200, -2400)` reset, and
  `GetNextMapDraw`'s player-centred spiral with cross-call resume (`prevMap`),
  the quadrant pick off the section midpoint, the leg-4 ring kick-off, the
  full-lap fallback and the "Infinite loop" panic. `ClearMapDraw` refills the
  budget and resets the spiral; `SetAllFramedSectionsAsNeedingRefresh` keeps
  the C#'s no-dedupe double-count.
- **The resident-world collapse**: the port keeps the whole world resident,
  so the constructor arms every section loaded + framed — the state the C#
  reaches via `SetAllSectionsLoaded` (`WorldGen.cs:6744`/`:6821`) plus the
  framing walk's per-section `SetSectionFramed` (`WorldGen.cs:80363`).
  `frameSectionsLeft` therefore sits at 0 (`SetSectionLoaded` counts each
  first load, `SetSectionFramed` drains it back). The `TileLoaded` gate
  (`WorldMap.cs:81`) now resolves through the real grid instead of the
  always-true stand-in; single-player behaviour is unchanged because every
  section is loaded.
- **`frame/world.rs::map_reveal_sweep` / `map_reveal_driver`** port
  `Main.cs:61863-61899`: the sweep runs while the stopwatch is under 5 ms and
  `GetNextMapDraw` answers; the `DebugOptions.unlockMap != 0 && SectionLoaded`
  arm reveals the section (`:61873-61876`), `DrawToMap_Section` re-uploads it
  (the port pushes the clamped section rect dirty — the texture sync rides
  `prepare`), and an exhausted sweep with no pending refresh zeroes the debug
  option (`:61880-61883`). The sweep gates only on `!gameMenu &&
  !generatingWorld` (`:61865`), so it runs OUTSIDE the port's pause gate; the
  `updateMap` consume arm checks `!gamePaused` itself (`:61886`). The
  `refreshMap` → `ClearMapDraw` consume rides INSIDE that arm, before the
  draw (`:61888-61892`); the `else if ChangesQueued` fallback draws
  `Rectangle.Empty` (`:61896-61898`).
- **`WorldMap` gains the `Main` statics**: `update_map` (`Main.cs:799`,
  armed by `ExportToMiniMap`'s `Main.updateMap = area`, `LightingEngine.cs:269`,
  and by the legacy seam's `:432` rect), `refresh_map` (`:789`), `load_map`
  (`:795`, the `.map` load's staged-upload gate, `WorldMap.cs:212`, cleared by
  the bulk upload's `DrawToMap` tail, `MapRenderer.cs:198`), and the
  `change_queues` (the 5×2 `MapRenderer.changeQueues`, `:33`/`:70-77`).
  `queue_change` ports `MapRenderer.QueueChange` (`:288-304`): the
  2048-per-target `ChangeRefreshThreshold` arms `refreshMap` instead of
  adding the entry, and while armed every call is a no-op. The port uploads
  through the single world-sized texture's dirty list, so the queues keep
  only the threshold + clear semantics — equivalent output, different cost.
- **The `/map` debug row now arms the queue**: `debug_unlock_map = 2` +
  `refresh_map = true` (`ToolkitDebugCommands.cs:486-487`), and the sweep
  reveals over the following frames instead of the old direct `unlock_map`
  walk. The second click is the toggle-off arm (`:491`). `unlock_map` itself

Deliberate deviations: the 5 ms budget is the C#'s own wall-clock stopwatch

machine-dependent exactly like vanilla — no fixed-count stand-in. The
`DrawToMap_Section` render-target blit is the dirty-rect push (one texture,

## The crafting focus + quantity (S1-H-7, 2026-11-13)

`Main.HoverOverCraftingItemButton` (`Main.cs:42252-42305`) is ported into
`clicks.rs::handle_crafting_clicks`: the unfocused click selects the row
(`focusRecipe` вЂ” the port keys the focus by the recipe id rather than the
C#'s list position, which keeps it stable across the frame's re-sort),
`stackSplit = 15`, the click-consumed lock and the MenuTick sound; the
focused click crafts through the held-frame pacing (`stackSplit <= 1`,
`frame.rs`'s per-tick decay), with `num = (superFastStack + 1)` Г—10 behind
`ItemSlot.ShiftInUse` and `flag4`'s reset arms (a different recipe being
crafted, or a non-stacking product). `craft.rs::try_craft_qty` is
`CraftingRequests.CraftItem(recipe, num)` (`Main.cs:42286`) вЂ” the C#'s
request queue processes the quantity asynchronously; the port loops the
single craft synchronously, each iteration re-checking the ingredients, so
a partial set crafts as many as it can (the request loop's net effect).

Scope notes: the filter/search bars stay draw-only (the station-filter
semantics are S1-L-11c's row and the search box rides the keyboard work);
`TryAllowingToCraftRecipe`'s mouse-blocking fetch (`:42278`) has no port
counterpart (the mouse item never blocks the craft here); the
`UsingOrReusingItem`/`IsStackingItems` gates of `flag3` (`Player.cs:23098`)
are unmodelled item-use state.

## The crafting pipeline (S1-L-11d, 2026-11-14)

`CraftingRequests.CreateResult` (`CraftingRequests.cs:122-131`) is ported as
`craft.rs::create_result`: the recipe's `createItem` cloned, `Item.OnCreated`'s
type swap (`Item.cs:48936-48942` вЂ” the ShellphoneDummy 5437 becomes the
Shellphone 5358) and `Item.Prefix(-1)`'s natural roll for a stack в‰¤ 1
(`Item.cs:504-610`). The grant carries the rolled prefix (`Item.CanStack`,
`Item.cs:49865-49872`), and the C#'s cursor gate
(`Main.CursorHasSpaceToCraftRecipe`, `Main.cs:42309-42345`) makes a prefixable
recipe craft **once** per click while the stackable ones (the torches) keep
crafting вЂ” the gate refuses a prefixable result outright
(`!item.CanHavePrefixes()`).

The crafting reach is the C#'s formula, `craft.rs::tile_reach`: the statics
`Player.tileRangeX/Y` (the defaults 5/3, `Player.cs:2496-2498`/`:57113-57114`)
with the per-tick writes вЂ” the Journey mode's Far Placement Range power
(Г—2 and +8/+8, `Player.cs:18818-18826`), the Extendo Grip / the Architect's
Gizmo Pack (+3/+2, `:13040-13044`), the held Toolbox (+1/+1, `:14955-14958`) вЂ”
then `TileReachCheckSettings.Simple`'s 20-tile clamp
(`TileReachCheckSettings.cs:20-34`, `:84`) and the artisan loaf's +4
(`Player.cs:35671`). The two gated recipes are ported too
(`needTorchGodsFavor` вЂ” the Torch God's potion 5573 and the master 5638 вЂ” and
`needMechdusa` вЂ” the 5334 row), with the gates `player.unlockedBiomeTorches`
and `SpecialSeedFeatures.Mechdusa` (`Recipe.cs:349-356`).

Deviations:

- **The crafted item goes into the inventory, not the cursor.** The C# hands
  the result to `Main.mouseItem` (`Main.CraftItem_GrantItem`,
  `Main.cs:42607-42612`) and the player places it with a click; the port grants
  it straight into the inventory (`clicks.rs::handle_crafting_clicks`). The
  cursor gate is therefore evaluated against the **previous result** instead of
  the cursor's content (`craft.rs::result_fits_next`) вЂ” the observable
  quantity matches the C#'s (a prefixable recipe crafts once), but the player
  never holds the crafted item on the cursor.
- **The artisan loaf's effect is not ported.** The flag
  `Player.ateArtisanBread` rides the player and the reach reads it, but the
  item that sets it (5326, `Player.cs:45218-45221`) has no ported use effect,
  so the +4 is unreachable in play.
- **The Torch God's unlock is not ported.** `player.unlockedBiomeTorches`
  (`Player.cs:2046`) rides the player and the gate reads it, but the unlock
  itself (the Torch God's dialogue) is unported, so the two gated recipes stay
  closed.
- **The prefix roll's stream.** The C# draws `Item.Prefix` from the same
  global `Main.rand` as the alchemy discount; the port's natural rolls ride
  `App::prefix_rng` and the crafting discount rides `App::craft_rng` вЂ” two
  stand-ins for one C# stream (the S1-A-11/S1-L-6c residual).
- **The quickCraft / remote-craft half is out** вЂ” the C#'s request queue
  (`CraftingRequests.CraftViaRequest`, `:142-174`) is the multiplayer path and
  the port's MP has no crafting requests.

The recipe table grew with it: the generator's tail branch broke out of the
expansion loop **before** copying the text that precedes
`Recipe.CreateReverseWallRecipes()` (`Recipe.cs:15148`), so the 414 authored
rows between the last expansion mark and that call were dropped (the audit's
"2 481 executed sites" was the generator's own truncated output). The branch
now copies that text: the table is **3 206 rows = 2 895 authored + 311
reverse**, and the pin in `tools/test_gen_recipes.py` re-taken.

## The sliced block light chain (S1-G-9, 2026-11-13; corrected 2026-11-16)

`DrawSingleTile_SlicedBlock` (`TileDrawing.cs:3517-3664`) is the port's
`render/tiles.rs::push_sliced` вЂ” and the chain now matches the C# exactly:
`Lighting.GetColor9Slice`'s 3Г—3 neighbourhood colours average with the
tile's own **raw** light (`(slices[i] + vector) * 0.5`, `:3578-3581`), then
`GetFinalLight` (`:4391-4402`) applies the tint and the actuation ghost
(`Tile.actColor`, `Tile.cs:282-288`, Г—0.4) to that average. The high/medium
split (the 9-slice vs the 4-quad paths on `_highQualityLightingRequirement`/
`_mediumQualityLightingRequirement`, `:3524` / `:3605`) rides the existing
thresholds, and a Glow-coated block replaces every slice with
`_glowPaintColorSlices` (`:3530-3533` / `:3611-3614`, all `Vector3.One`).

Two defects in the 2026-11-13 landing, fixed by `S1-G-9-sliced-final-light`:

* **The double ghost.** `GetFinalLight`'s `Color` overload (`:4358`) takes
  `tileLight` **by value** and `:1019` assigns the result to
  `drawData.finalColor` вЂ” `drawData.tileLight` stays the raw
  `Lighting.GetColor` (`:871`). Only the `Vector3` overload (`:4391`) writes
  through `ref`. So `:3528`'s `vector` is unghosted, and the port's caller-side
  ghost plus the per-slice ghost composed to 0.16 instead of 0.4. `push_sliced`
  now samples the raw light itself and the `own` argument is gone, so the
  double-ghost cannot come back.
* **The Glow slices.** `fullbrightBlock()` blocks draw their slices at
  `Vector3.One` `_glowPaintColorSlices`; the port fed the neighbourhood light
  instead, so Glow-coated blocks stayed dark. Both arms apply the replacement.

Each slice is pushed with `push_sprite_paint`, carrying the tile's paint byte
as the flat arm does.

Scope notes: `GetFinalLight`'s shine arm (`ShouldTileShine` в†’ `Main.shine`)
has no port counterpart вЂ” `Main.tileShine2` is unported (drawdata.rs:509), so
the branch is unreachable; the non-White `colorTint` is the minecart path
only (`:3788`). Both ride the paint work (S1-G-2's row).

## The map overlay layers (S1-L-4, 2026-11-14)

`Main.MapIcons`' overlay stack (`Main.cs:66551`'s registration: Digtoise в†’
BossBag в†’ Spawn в†’ TeamBasedSpawn в†’ TeleportPylons в†’ Pings) is ported over a
faithful `MapOverlayDrawContext` (`MapOverlayDrawContext.cs:8-70`): the
tile-position в†’ screen transform `(position - mapPosition) * mapScale +
mapOffset`, the optional clip (the minimap's screen rect), the Alignment
origin multiplier and the `DrawResult.IsMouseOver` rect. The layers that
have port drivers draw: SpawnMapLayer (the world spawn + the bed marker вЂ”
the C# reads `localPlayer.SpawnX/SpawnY`, the port keeps the bed spawn on
`World.bed_spawn`), BossBagMapLayer (the `ItemID.cs:1383` 21-kind set over
the drop pool) and PingMapLayer (the 100-cap pool, the 15 s expiry, the 1x5
row cycling at 10 Hz).

**Second pass (2026-11-16, `S1-L-4-map-overlay-layers`)** closed the three
stubs and the missing call site. Digtoise draws: `digtoise_marker` scans the
projectile pool for the first active 1098/1123 whose `owner == 0` (the port's
standing stand-in for `Main.myPlayer`, as in `projectile.rs`/`grapple.rs`),
yielding `(Bottom, spriteDirection)` вЂ” `Bottom / 16 + (0.5, 0)` bottom-aligned,
column 1 when `spriteDirection <= 0` (`DigtoiseMapLayer.cs:14-26`). TeleportPylons
draws the live network: `tr_core::pylons::scan_pylons` feeds `MapIconInputs::pylons`,
each marker anchored at `PositionInTiles.ToVector2() + (1.5, 2)` centre-aligned
through `MapOverlayContext::draw_tinted` (the `MapOverlayDrawContext.cs:218-242`
`color * opacity` form), dimmed to `Color.Gray * 0.5f` = 0.25 when
`is_player_near_a_pylon` is false (`TeleportPylonsMapLayer.cs:39-42`/`:65-89`).
`PylonType::style()` (`self as u8`) is the inverse of `from_tile_style` and
supplies the `SpriteFrame` column, since the map layer's column *is* the type
discriminant. `WorldMap::tile_revealed` (`WorldMap.cs:406-409`) backs the
`IsRevealed` fog gate (`TeleportPylonsMapLayer.cs:112-119`) with a bounds guard
the C# gets for free from its world-sized jagged array. TeamBasedSpawn stays
gated: both `Main.teamBasedSpawnsSeed` and `ExtraSpawnPointManager` are unported
(M5-SEED-2's deferred list), so the branch is the faithful shape with no data
behind it.

Scope notes: the fullscreen call rides `Main.cs:55996`'s position (the
map's top-left minus the 10 px frame inset, `mapPosition = Vector2.Zero`
is the tile-space identity); the **minimap** call (`Main.cs:55696-55703`) is
wired in the same pass вЂ” the clip is `map_minimap_quad`'s destination rect and
the draw scale is the C#'s `num46 = ((mapMinimapScale * 0.25f * 2f + 1f) / 3f)`
capped at 1. The pylon scan is snapshotted once per frame and only while the map
or minimap is actually drawing, so the TE walk stays off the hot path.
`DrawNPCMapIcons` and `NPC.RevengeManager`'s marker layer are their own passes;
the hover text feeds the map's text line through `ui::text::hud_text` (the C#
`ref text`).
