## Dust & gore (module 15) (S1-E-1, 2026-11-14; S1-E-3, 2026-11-17)

`crates/tr-core/src/particles.rs` is the `Main.dust` analog: the C# keeps the pool as the static `Main.dust[6001]` array plus the three static pressure counters (`Dust.dCount`, `lavaBubbles`, `SandStormCount`, `Dust.cs:12-16`), and the port carries the same global-pool semantics вЂ” one pool the App owns, spawns addressed by slot, slot 6000 the refuse sentinel `NewDust` returns and never scans (`Main.cs:66985`, `Dust.cs:79`/`:103`). The spawn path is a 1:1 transcription of `Dust.cs:10-407`: the guard chain (`:77-101`), the off-screen cull with the `400*(1-dCount)` margin (`:89-97`), the first-inactive-slot scan and the five pressure bands (`:103-152`), the default block with the per-100 frame shift (`:153-193`), the `ChildSafety` re-type arm (`:194-213`, `ChildSafety.cs:33`) and the per-type tweak chain (`:214-252`). The pool draws from the caller-passed stream (the `DustRng` seam, the C# `Next`/`NextFloat` conversions `UnifiedRandom.cs:120-141`), so per-consumer streams are preserved: the pool's band rolls are the only added draws on the clients' streams. The sand spawn site additionally regained the C# `NewDust` velocity/scale rolls the stand-in had skipped (`Sandstorm.cs:226`; the final 0.9 scale pin unchanged), and `Settings::blood` arms `pool.child_safety` at spawn вЂ” blood on is the vanilla default (the gate skipped), blood off sets `ChildSafety.Disabled` false and the re-type fires.

The migration retired one stand-in cap: the wheel sparks' `MAX_SPARKS` = 500 (the `minecart::Sparks` pool, pinned to no pressure) вЂ” the cart's queued requests now spawn type 213 through the shared pool with the cart's own stream. The flying sand's emit budget is not a stand-in and did not retire: it is the C#'s own line, `num7 = 1000*screenW/maxScreenW` with `gfxQuality` pinned to its no-pressure value 1.0 (`Sandstorm.cs:161`, ported at `sand.rs:106` over `MAX_SCREEN_W = 1920`); the migration only switched its subtrahend to the shared pool's live type-268 count вЂ” the budget stands, its pressure is now the pool's.

Scope notes and documented drops, each recorded at its site: the `shader`/`customData` record fields (no draw-shader chain; the `customData` followers live in `UpdateDust`, S1-E-3), the `Main.rand == null` re-seed and `Main.netMode == 2` server guards and the dead `Main.NoPooling` realloc arm (`Main.cs:67208` sets it false), and the `DANGEROUS` set = the 8 listed ids (5, 227, 273, 237, 248, 249, 250, 251 вЂ” `SetFactory.cs:97-107`; research/15's earlier inverted reading of that set is corrected). tr-app injects the wet probe through the seam (`player::wet_collision`, the `Dust.cs:248` probe). The child-safety sync runs `sync_child_safety` once per frame, so a settings toggle lands one tick late; `max_dust_to_draw`'s first frame reads the seed 0 (unreachable in production вЂ” the frame loop sets it before any spawn); the 268 draw keeps the stand-in's 10-px cell until E-3 ports the real draw, and the `NewDust` `Next(1)` gate draw is absent in both the stand-in and the port (pre-existing).

**The shared update loop (S1-E-3, 2026-11-17).** `UpdateCtx` + `DustPool::update_dust` transcribe the whole `Dust.cs:420-2423` skeleton verbatim: the head resets (`lava_bubbles`/`SandStormCount` вЂ” `snow_dust` is a `Main` static `Main.cs:621` and is not carried, the omission cited at the site), the `i < maxDustToDraw` split with the `else` kill (`:2393-2395`), `d_count++` (`:440`), the scale>10 kill with fall-through (`:447-449`), the `ChildSafety` firstFrame re-type (`:445-466`), `position += velocity` (`:477`), the per-type hook, the gravity tail (`:2335-2342`, 304 exempt and fadeIn-gated), the screen-bottom kill (`:2343-2346`), the `==` dCount nibbles (`:2347-2366`), the num86 ladder (`:2367-2391`), the scale-floor kill and the post-loop recompute (`:2398-2422`).

**Two dead arms, ported DEAD.** Both keep their C# citations because neither can fire in the C# either: `num` never increments (only the recompute's `else { dCount = 0 }` is reachable), and the `==` dCount nibbles never match вЂ” the C# compares the rounded-down byte-width drawing count against an integral `dCount`.

**The clients fold to one pass.** `minecart::tick` (frame.rs's dust phase вЂ” `Main.cs:18045-18047`'s single ported pass) runs `update_dust` ONCE per frame, dispatching the type-213 arm (its own body) and type 268 (`sand::type_268_arm`, world/player_vy/sandstorm-visuals as captured inputs). `scene_scan.rs`'s separate sand tick call is deleted (its emit stays, `Main.cs:17247`), the duplicated generic tails are deleted, and the per-tick `dust_index` pin is deleted вЂ” `Main.cs:18062-18066` is the crash-recovery re-init in `UpdateWorld_Dust`'s catch, not a per-tick reset.

**The corrected chain reading.** The 213/268 arms are standalone statements of the C# FIRST ladder (`Dust.cs:2119-2127`, `:2127`): the burn-out `else if (type != 304)` closes that ladder and the fresh `if (dust.type >= 130 ...)` chain head follows. They therefore do NOT exclude the second chain's final `else if (type != 304 && noGravity)` tail (`:2335`) вЂ” the hooks return false, and the weightless-213 test re-pins the Г—0.92 damp and the fadeIn-gated в€’0.04 on top of the folded pass.

**Stream-draw enumeration.** The loop draws nothing new: the `ChildSafety` firstFrame re-type's `Next` reads ride the client streams through the pool's `DustRng` seam exactly as at spawn (S1-E-1), and the 213/268 arms draw none вЂ” they read only captured inputs. 15 `s1_e_3_*` tests pin the skeleton, the dead arms, the fold and the chain reading.

**Review path and its deviations.** Independent review round 1 PASSED the tr-core skeleton (`0d1cb0e9`); the tr-app fold's round 1 FAILED and produced the two defects fixed forward in `c361d656` вЂ” the double head-run per frame and the wrong either/or reading of the arms vs the gravity tail. The round-2 review agent was quota-cut three times before it could land verdicts (an infrastructure deviation, recorded); the fix was instead verified in-session вЂ” the single call-site grep, the one-move/damp pins and the 4094/0 test counts.

What remains: E-2 (the per-type table + `GetAlpha`/`GetColor` вЂ” the `Dust.cs:467-2334` if-chain arms and light arms that E-3's skeleton skips), E-4 (gore: `NewGore`/`GoreID.Sets`/`Gore.Update` + the leaves, incl. the foliage leaf tail), the `rain.rs` re-point and the NPC/Projectile/player call sites вЂ” the caller-coverage table in `docs/research/15-dust-gore.md` stays authoritative.


What remains: E-2's if-chain arms and light arms (`Dust.cs:467-2334`) and the `customData` follower arms, E-4's remaining `Gore.NewGore*` drop sites and the gore draw pass, the `rain.rs` re-point and the NPC/Projectile/player call sites вЂ” the caller-coverage table in `docs/research/15-dust-gore.md` stays authoritative; the band's neighbours landed alongside (S1-E-2's colour table and S1-E-4's gore pool/update вЂ” their own sections below), so only the parts named here stay outstanding.


## Dust colour table (S1-E-2, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-core/src/dust_table.rs` is the colour/fade half of the per-type table: `Dust.GetAlpha` (`Dust.cs:2425-2727`), `Dust.GetColor` (`:2729-2772`) and the two visual accessors (`:2774-2790`), transcribed arm for arm in source order so the fall-through chain reads like the C#. The XNA colour algebra the arms use is three private helpers at the top of the file вЂ” `Color * float` (every channel scales, then the ctor truncates), `Color.Lerp` (per-channel `MathHelper.Lerp`, truncating cast) and the `ToVector3`/`ToVector4` product (normalised channels, so `a*b/255`) вЂ” because the port has no `Microsoft.Xna.Framework` and inventing a full colour type for three operators would be more code than the operators.

The record stays byte-based (`particles::Color`, sRGB bytes, the `Dust.color` carrier), so every `new Color(int, вЂ¦)` argument takes the C# `(byte)` cast the ctor performs: truncate, wrap past 255. The 213 draw already relied on that wrap before this task (`minecart.rs`, `int num2 = (int)(scale / 2.5f * 255f)`); it now calls the shared table instead of keeping its own copy of the arm.

Two arms read `Main` globals: type 157 (`Main.mouseTextColor`, `Dust.cs:2627-2651`) and type 327 (`Main.rand` + `Main.DiscoR/G/B` + `Main.dayTime`, `:2658-2676`). Originally documented drops (S1-E-2), they are PORTED since the W4-d54 gap-closure (research/131 §7.2 G3/G4) at `dust_table::get_alpha_with_globals(d, new_color, &DustDrawGlobals, rng)`: a small copy struct carries the three statics (`mouse_text_color: u8`, `day_time: bool`, `disco_rgb: [i32; 3]` — the waterfall lane's g75 `set_disco_rgb` latch is the feed precedent), and `rng` is the DRAW-pass `Main.rand` (the 327 draws happen in `GetAlpha`, not `UpdateDust`). The pure two-argument `get_alpha` keeps its shape for global-free callers (the minecart 213 draw); 157/327 fall through to the default formula there. The 327 arm carries a verbatim C# quirk: `(int)(sum) * 255` truncates BEFORE the multiply — the sum (`NextFloat * 0.04 + 0.1 + Disco/800`) is always `< 1`, so each channel computes 0, the `> newColor` lifts never fire and the colour passes through unchanged, but the THREE `NextFloat` draws still advance the draw stream (ported structurally, pinned by `w4_d54_g4_get_alpha_327_night_draws_and_zero_quirk`). The 157 alpha is f32-floor sensitive: `mouseTextColor` 255 → `num7 = 0.94999993f` → alpha 94, not 95 (`w4_d54_g3_get_alpha_157_mouse_text_pulse`). Type 327 IS spawned port-wide: the tile-718 (StarCloud) break ladder maps to dust 327 (`WorldGen.cs:68516-68518`, ported at `worldgen_dust_tile.rs:1013-1015` on this branch), so the night-gate arm is reachable from worldgen tile breaks; type 157 spawns from NPC/Projectile/PlayerDrawSet sites on the other lanes.

The rowвЂ™s other columns are deliberately not in this file. Gravity / `noGravity` / velocity scaling has two halves: the spawn-time chain is already verbatim in `particles.rs::new_dust` (`Dust.cs:214-252`, S1-E-1) and the per-tick gravity tail (`:1819-1828`) belongs to the update walk that S1-E-3 sequences. The light column is the ~70 `Lighting.AddLight` arms spread from `Dust.cs:485` to `:2050`, which cannot be ported without the entity-light seam (S1-E-5) вЂ” and they are not a table anyway, they are code interleaved with the per-type update arms. The `DustID` names already live at `tr-app::id_tables::DUST_ID` (S1-F-6, 196 named constants + `DustID.Count = 332`), so no second copy exists here.

Verification: five tests (`s1_e_2_*`) assert every constant arm against its C# literal (the table rows, the grey families, the `noLight`/`alpha == 255`/`noGravity` gates), the formula arms against hand-computed values (`306 * num`, `263`вЂ™s integer halving, `213`вЂ™s `scale/2.5*255`, the three lerp fractions, the two Vector products), the default tailвЂ™s `(num+3)/4` and `(num+9)/10` divisors, and the accessors. The arm id-sets (`:2494`, `:2584`, `:2681`) were additionally diffed mechanically against the C# conditions, and the constant-arm colours were extracted from the C# and compared row by row.

## Gore: the pool, the spawn family and the update walk (S1-E-4, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-core/src/gore.rs` carries `Main.gore[601]` (`Main.cs:66990`) as
[`GorePool`]: 600 live slots plus the sentinel 600 that `NewGore` returns for a
refused spawn and never scans (`Gore.cs:1308-1320`). The record is
`Gore.cs:14-42` field for field; `sticky = true`, `timeLeft = goreTime` and
`Frame = new SpriteFrame(1, 1)` are the struct initialiser, and `goreTime` is
the pool-level static (`:1507-1510`, 600).

The RNG contract, resolved against `Gore.cs:1327-1328` verbatim (an earlier
checkpoint summary misread it as `Next(2)` в†’ X в†’ Y): one `Next(10, 31)` on
`velocity.Y` **first**, then one `Next(-20, 21)` on `velocity.X`. Nothing else
in `NewGore` rolls except the two ChildSafety draws (`Next(11, 14)` then
`NextFloat()`, `:1336-1338`, only when the gate is armed and the type is
dangerous) and the two type-1225 draws (`:1375-1382`). The per-type arms
(`:1355-1456`) are pure writes.

`crates/tr-core/src/gore_id.rs` is `GoreID.Sets` (`GoreID.cs:20-23`) built the
way `SetFactory` builds it (`SetFactory.cs:97-130`): a default for the whole
array plus the listed `(id, value)` pairs. `special_ai` (default 0),
`disappear_speed` (default **1**), `disappear_speed_alpha` (default **1**) and
`is_drip` (default false) replace the earlier fabricated range table
(`219..=331`, `943..=1242`) that shipped with the draft вЂ” the defaults matter:
a zero `disappear_speed` would have frozen every timer.

The update walk is `Gore.Update` (`Gore.cs:308-1083`) split into the driver(`update`, `Main.UpdateWorld_Gores` `Main.cs:17971-17996`), `update_slot` (the
main chain) and the twelve helpers the C# factors out: the four cloud/spark
rows (`:110-260`), the drip animation (`:378-529`), the drip collision pass
(`:915-977`), the sticky rest (`:978-1019`), the chum bucket and its floating
chunk plus `ChumFloatingChunk_GetWaterLine` (`:552-671`, `:262-290`), the
`SpecialAI == 2` smoke row (`:767-843`), the 411-430 pages (`:844-912`),
`Gore_UpdateLeaf` (`:1085-1209`) and `Gore_UpdateSail` (`:1211-1271`).

Documented drops, each at its site: the texture-gated arms are the port's
`TextureAssets.Gore[...].IsLoaded == false` path throughout (`Gore::width`/
`height`/`aabb_rectangle` return the C#'s own 1/1 fallbacks, and the size
probes keep `32f` вЂ” `4f` for the ogre-spit rows вЂ” so the collision boxes are
exactly the C#'s unloaded-texture sizes); the entity lights (`Lighting.AddLight`
at `:258`, `:940`, `:1076`) wait for S1-E-5; the 716/1383 shimmer tint
(`:917-941`) needs `LiquidRenderer.GetShimmerBaseColor`; the `SoundEngine` hits
and the water-shader ripple (`:953`, `:965`, `:967`) need the audio and shader
seams; and the player-rect/dust-burst arms (`:794-841`, `:850-864`, `:883-910`,
`:1119-1122`) need the entity and dust pools on the core side. None of those
draws a random number, so the stream order is untouched вЂ” which is the property
the port actually needs from them.

`tr-core` cannot depend on `tr-app`'s collision ports, so the walk takes a
[`GoreCollision`] seam (`tile_collision` = `Collision.cs:2292`, `wet_collision`
= `:1572`, `slope_collision` = `:1791`), the same injection pattern the dust
pool uses for its wet probe (`particles.rs:197-202`). The App implements it in
`crates/tr-app/src/gore_seam.rs` over `collision::tile_collision`,
`player::wet_collision` and `collision::slope_collision`. The C#
`SlopeCollision` declares a `gravity` parameter (`Collision.cs:1791`) and never
reads it, so the port's `slope_collision` without it is exact, not a
simplification.

The App owns the pool as `App.gore` (`Main.gore`), ticks it in the `gores`
phase of the fixed step вЂ” between `npcs` and `projectiles`, the C# order at
`Main.cs:17767-17775` вЂ” on the stage's own named stream
(`Main.SwapRandom("UpdateGores")`, `RngKey::UpdateGores`), and feeds it
`Main.WindForVisuals` = `Wind::speed_current` (`Main.cs:2823`). The blood
toggle drives the same `ChildSafety.Disabled` static for both pools
(`ChildSafety.cs:15` вЂ” one static in the C#, so `sync_child_safety` sets both).
The draw pass stays unported, which is why no gore is visible yet.
(`ChildSafety.cs:15` — one static in the C#, so `sync_child_safety` sets both).
The front draw pass landed with S1-E-4b (below); `DrawGoreBehind` stays
unported.

Tested (`cargo test -p tr-core gore --lib`, 14 passing): the spawn order and
velocity, the drip sheet, the `SpecialAI` 1/2/3/4-6 arms, the balloon rows, and
the three lifecycle tests (sticky countdown в†’ alpha fade в†’ deactivate; the free
gore's double-speed fade `:1020-1023`; the floor cloud's wind drift and expiry
`:112-136`). The seam has its own forward test (`gore_seam::tests`), and the
App's phase-order golden test now pins `gores` between `npcs` and
`projectiles`.

## The gore draw pass (S1-E-4b, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/gore.rs` ports `Main.DrawGore`
(`Main.cs:21873-21907`) read-only over `App.gore`: the 600-slot walk, the
inactive/`type <= 0` skip (`:21879-21882`), the drip gate (`:21883-21887` —
`GoreID.Sets.IsDrip` rows outside frames 7..=9 belong to `DrawGoreBehind`
and latch `Main.drawBackGore`), the framed/unframed source split
(`:21889`/`:21900`) and the `SpriteBatch.Draw` call's integer-half origins,
the framed path's `- 2f` Y lift and the type-1217 `+ 4f` nudge
(`:21892-21898`). The seam sits between the rain and the dust draws in
`app/frame/draw.rs` — the C# order `DrawRain` (`Main.cs:62279`) → `DrawGore`
(`:62282`) → `DrawDust` (`:62293`) — in the same world-effect (fx) range the
rain/sand/leaf draws use. No kill-at-draw arm exists in `DrawGore` (unlike
`DrawDust`'s black-death), and none was added: the pool update is untouched.

The tint is `Gore.GetAlpha` (`Gore.cs:1464-1505`) verbatim — the 16/17,
716/1383, 570-572 (`b/2` integer), 331 and 1225 (float ctor) arms, the
default path's `(int)(byte * num)` truncating multiplies, the alpha clamp
(`:1491-1499`) and the 1202-1204 cap at 20. The light input is
`Lighting.GetColor(int, int)` (`Lighting.cs:216-242`) through the active
`LightStyle::shade` (the wires-pass convention), byte-truncated at 255 with
alpha 255. The source cell is `SpriteFrame.GetSourceRectangle`
(`SpriteFrame.cs:72-77`): `texture / count` integer cells, the 2 px padding
subtracted only on multi-cell axes. The light-sample tile keeps both C#
cast orders (`Main.cs:21897`/`:21902`): X casts the sum before the integer
`/ 16`, Y divides before the cast. The rotation emulation is the
`push_sprite_origin_rot` top-left shift with `origin · scale · zoom`, in the
fx range (no world-range cache key change — the fx range rebuilds per frame
like the rain).

Asset loading: `LoadGore` (`Main.cs:59100-59106`) is a lazy texture request;
the port packs every `Images/Gore_<id>.xnb` up front beside the item/buff
icons (`assets.rs::load_static_sheets`, `enumerate_gore_sheet_ids` — the
same file-scan shape, ~1 400 small sheets, ~0.7 MB compressed), exposed as
`Lookups.gore_sheets` keyed by the parsed id. The leaf gores 910/911 keep
their existing `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` slot (the enumeration excludes them so
nothing double-packs) and appear in both maps.

Atlas packing (**re-sync 2026-11-19**): this branch originally carried its own
first-fit decreasing-height shelf experiment in `tr-render/src/atlas.rs`; the
M8 merge wave SKIP-blocked the branch on the atlas bound (first-fit measured
8 305 px > 8 192 with the gore sheets) and the experiment was reverted —
`atlas.rs` on this branch now equals **main's P4 best-fit decreasing-height
shelves** (`2795277e`, the frost-wave fix, 8 416 → 8 121 px on main's set).
The overflow was re-measured on the synced branch in code-only mode: a JS
simulation (`Temp/opencode/e4b-atlas-sim.js` — the LZX/XNB header decode
translated from `tr-content/src/lzx.rs`/`xnb.rs`, the sheet enumeration
mirroring `assets.rs::tests::content_lookups` with `World::new` 8×8 and empty
tile/wall sets, and the packer translated arm-for-arm from main's `build_ref`)
reads every sheet's real dimensions from the retail `.xnb` headers:

* main's set (no gore): **7 779 sheets, 42 shelves, 8 117 px** (the ~4 px
  delta to the recorded 8 121 is the 5 file-less `Minecart*`/`Mount_*` names
  in `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` whose retail files carry different names — they
  never decode at startup either);
* with the branch's **1 402 gore sheets** (1 404 files minus the 910/911
  leaf gores that keep their `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` slot): **9 181 sheets,
  49 shelves, 8 489 px — 297 px over the 8 192 strict-GPU bound**;
* the gore band's ideal area is only ~374 px of shelf height

## The carrier's life pool (S1-D-6, 2026-11-14)

`NPC.realLife` (`NPC.cs:6161`) is the C#'s carrier link: an NPC index that
points at the NPC whose life the linked NPC shares. `AI_006_Worms` gives the
head `ai[3] = whoAmI` + `realLife = whoAmI` and hands the link to every
child (`NPC.cs:51305-51363`); `AI_037_Destroyer` does the same for the
Destroyer (`:49836-49853`) and the crawltipede's own arm for its chain
(`:51369-51392`). The Eater of Worlds is the one exception вЂ” C# forces
`realLife = -1` for types 13-15 (`:51129-51132`), so every EoW segment owns
its own life.

The three consequences the port now carries:

* **One pool.** `StrikeNPC_Inner`'s `realLife` arm (`:81374-81378`) puts the
  damage on the carrier's `life` and copies the carrier's `life`/`lifeMax`
  back onto the struck segment. The pool's size is the carrier's `lifeMax`:
  the Devourer 100 (`:8771`), the Giant Worm 30 (`:8858`), the Leech 60
  (`:10413`), the solar crawltipede 10000 (`:15273`), the Destroyer **80000**
  (`:10667` вЂ” the port carried the per-segment 8000, so the whole worm was
  eight times too tanky).
* **A carrier-bound death.** `checkDead` returns early for a link whose
  carrier is not itself (`:78040-78042`), so a segment never runs the death
  events: no loot, no coins, no bestiary credit, no banner, no invasion
  kill credit. Only the carrier's death carries them.
* **A chain without orphans.** A classic family's link dies with its leader
  (`:51425-51433`); the `Transform(13)`/`Transform(15)` split is the Eater
  of Worlds' rule only (`:51498-51519`). The port used to split the
  Devourer's and the Giant Worm's bodies into new heads вЂ” a segment that
  outlived its chain.

Port notes:

* **The carrier link is a stable identity, not an index.** The vanilla's
  `realLife` is an NPC index, but `App::npcs` compacts every frame (the
  death retain in `world_sim/npcs.rs`), so an index would not survive the
  frame. The port's chain identity (`worm_id` + `seg_index`) stands in: the
  carrier is the link with `seg_index == 0` (`Npc::carrier_index`).
* **The mirror is continuous.** C# copies the carrier's `life` onto the
  segment when the segment is struck; the port's worm pass mirrors it every
  frame, so a segment never shows a stale life. The observable result is the
  same: the pool empties the whole chain at once, and the DoT on a segment
  (which C# also loses вЂ” it writes the segment's stale `life`) cannot kill a
  link.
* **The two strikes without the NPC list defer.** The EoC shield-dash and
  the thorns reflect (`Npc::contact`) have no access to the NPC list, so
  their damage is parked in `pending_pool_damage` and the worm pass pays it
  to the carrier in the same frame. The melee, the projectile and the net
  paths resolve the carrier directly (`Npc::strike_melee` /
  `Npc::strike_projectile`).
* **The net mode carries no chains.** The net snapshot rebuilds `App::npcs`
  from the wire (kind/position/life), so the links have no `worm_id` there
  and a remote strike lands on the segment itself. The host owns the
  simulation, as in the vanilla.
* **The tail's damage multiplier.** `NPC.takenDamageMultiplier`
  (`:81244-81246`) multiplies the strike before it lands; the solar
  crawltipede's tail (414) carries 10 (`:15316`) вЂ” the tail is the softest
  point of the chain by a factor of ten.
* **Still open.** The worm families' boss health bar (`Main.cs:45979`'s
  `DrawInterface_Healthbar_Worm`, the carrier's life on the bar) and the
  Moon Lord carrier + the DD2 anchors (the port's kind-search pre-passes
  instead of the C#'s explicit index links) are the S1-D-6b row.

over 16). The row is therefore split into S1-D-4b-1..8 by family вЂ” the
same precedent S1-D-4c set for the vortex styles вЂ” and the contract
stays "arm them, never remove the rows": every style keeps its
`proj_data` row and gains its dispatch arm.

S1-D-4b-1 ports the four self-contained styles:

Deviations (each deliberate, each with its C# citation in the arm):

* **The dust and gore of the explosion are SKIPPED**
  (`:42305-42369`) вЂ” the port has no dust or gore layer (S1-E-1 /
  S1-E-4 are in flight). With them the arm's `Main.rand` draws go too

  (`:42507-42515`) and the explosion cue (`:42266-42269`): the pool has

  untouched, as in the C#'s other arms with no sound layer.
* **`Projectile.Opacity` (`:540`) is a state-only field**: the port has
  no projectile draw pass yet, so the aiStyle-133 ramp writes the slot
  and nothing reads it yet. The field defaults to the C#'s `1f`.
* **The Flairon Bubble's target is an NPC-slot index** in the C#

  than the C#'s slot did; the port keeps the index shape (the Nebula
  Arcanum's `ai[1] = index + 1` precedent) and reads it with
  `npcs.get`, so a vanished target steers nowhere instead of at the
  C#'s stale slot.
* **Four `proj_data` rows were wrong and are now faithful**: the
  Flairon Bubble (405, `:4864`), the Dark Mage marker (673, `:7213`),
  the Insanity shadow (965, `:9121`) and the Cascade Explosion (1125,

  all of it (the `RESET_STATE` alpha 0), so the arms would have started
  from the wrong alpha вЂ” the aiStyle-70 fade arm floors the alpha at 50,
  which would have *raised* a 0 to 50 on the first fade tick.

## The composite arm poses (S1-G-16, 2026-11-14)

`Player.compositeFrontArm`/`compositeBackArm` (`Player.cs:1906/:4347-4365`)
were never ported: the renderer used a `swing_stand_in` stand-in that
enabled the front arm for three use styles (2/11/13), never the back arm,
and read the stretch ladders off a normalised swing instead of the C#'s
`itemAnimation` вЂ” so the arms posed wrong in most item animations (the
style 11 ladder was inverted, the style 13 stretch was inverted, the style 2
pose never reached its relaxed row). The sim now owns the state:

* `AnimatePlayerAndGetItemFrame` (`Player.cs:43372-43386`) resets both arms
  to DISABLED per frame and dispatches: `itemAnimation > 0` в†’
  `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle`, otherwise в†’ `ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`.
* `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle`'s composite assignments (`:50885-51375`) are
  ported per use style вЂ” 2 (both arms `-PI/2 * dir`, the `num10` quarters),
  8 (the wind-up/swing-arc phases), 9 (the `num7 в†’ num8` arc), 11 (the
  `num12` two-cycle + the back arm Full at `-PI/16`), 12 (the `num30`
  two-cycle + `num31 = cos(num30 * PI) * 0.2`), 13 (the `num20` thirds +
  `itemRotation * Directions.Y - PI/2 * dir`), 14 (the back arm Full at
  `-3*PI/4 * dir`) and 15 (both arms at `-2*PI/5 * dir`).
* `ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`'s composite assignments (`:50520-50582`) are
  ported per hold style вЂ” 4 (the umbrella: the front Full + the back
  ThreeQuarters around `num9 В± num8`), 5 (the back Quarter at `-PI/4 * dir`
  + the front Full at `-0.39269912 * dir`), 6 (the back ThreeQuarters at
  `-3*PI/5 * dir`) and 8 (both arms at `-2*PI/5 * dir`).
* The draw consumes the live state: `PlayerDrawSet.UpdateCompositeArm`
  (`PlayerDrawSet.cs:2246-2275`) picks the front column 7 / the back
  column 8 at the stretch row (Full 0 / ThreeQuarters 1 / Quarter 2 /
  None 3) and the rotation pivots the arm around the composite pivot
  (`render/player_layers.rs::update_composite_arm`).

The shooting styles' `itemRotation` (`Player.cs:47371-47378`) is now the
C#'s `atan2(aimY * direction, aimX * direction) - fullRotation`: the port
keeps the aim as an angle, so the mirrored `atan2` is the aim + PI when
the player faces left (`item_rotation_for_aim`). The old stand-in used
`aim * direction` вЂ” the negated angle, not the mirrored vector вЂ” so the
useStyle 5 body rows (`num21 = itemRotation * direction`, `:36423`) and the
useStyle 13 composite arm were off by PI when facing left.

Deviations (deliberate, bounded):

* The useStyle 8 overshoot branch (`itemAnimation > useAnimation`,
  `:51226-51244`) is unreachable вЂ” the port's swing counter never exceeds
  `itemAnimationMax`.
* The useStyle 13 stretch base is `itemAnimationMax`, where the C# uses
  `itemTimeMax` when it is non-zero (`:51176-51184`) вЂ” the port has no
  per-item use time.
* The useStyle 9 branch also moves `itemLocation` through
  `GetFrontHandPosition` (`:50901-50905`); the port draws the held item
  from its own item-row chain (the held-item positions are the
  M2-DRAW item-row work).
* `AnimatePlayerAndGetItemFrame` reads `lastVisualizedSelectedItem` while
  the animation runs (`:43374`); the port uses the currently selected item.
* The petting composite arms (`ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle`'s `isPetting`
  block, `:50242-50269`) and the football arm (`:36139-36143`) stay
  unported (no petting/football systems).
* `Player.Directions.Y` (the gravity direction, `:3849`) is 1 in the port
  (no gravity flip).

Tests: `s1_player_composite_tests` вЂ” the eat style's quarters, the mow
style's two-cycle + the back arm's constant pose, the rapier's stretch
thirds + its item-rotation arm, the shoot style's back arm, the hold
styles' arms and the aim mirror. All seven are mutation-checked (RED on
the pre-fix code).


## The saucer projectile arms (S1-D-4b-4, 2026-11-14)

The ROADMAP's S1-D-4b-4 slice (the aiStyle-79 deathray and the aiStyle-80
missile вЂ” the Martian Saucer's two shots, `Projectile.cs:30791-31000`) is
the second half of the S1-D-4b-1 split (the row was split into S1-D-4b-1..8
because the 19 styles span ~5 300 C# lines of arms plus the two
mega-families).

**aiStyle 79 вЂ” the Saucer deathray (447)**. The ray is a beam that hangs
from the NPC that spawned it: the C#'s spawn passes `ai0 = base.whoAmI + 1`
(`NPC.cs:35917` for the shell, `:36437` for the core) and the arm reads that
slot. The arm's gates are the owner's state вЂ” the shell's `ai[0]` must name a
live core (`:30805-30813`), the core's phase must be `ai[3] % 120 >= 60` with
`ai[0] == 2` (`:30829-30832`), and the owner's own `ai[0]` must not be one of
the three "no target" states (`:30833-30835`). Then the geometry: the beam's
top is the owner's centre + 46, its column is the owner's centre, and its
height is the scan down to the first solid row at or below the player's feet
(the 150-row cap), trimmed by the last row's `num601 % 16 - 2`.

**aiStyle 80 вЂ” the Saucer missile (448)**. The spawn passes `ai1 = 20f`
(`NPC.cs:35845`) and the arm counts it down (the arming delay); on the
arming tick the arm picks the target (`Player.FindClosest` вЂ” the port's
local player is the only one) and speeds the flight up by 4 px. The flight
turns toward the target for its first 30 ticks at 0.2 rad/tick, dies at the
180-tick life end, and dies on a living player within 42 px.

Deviations (each deliberate, each with its C# citation in the arm):

* **The dust is SKIPPED** (the deathray's `:30863-30878`, the missile's
  `:30920-30929`/`:30946-30956`/`:30963-30971`) вЂ” the port has no dust layer
  (S1-E-1 is in flight). With it the arms' `Main.rand` draws go too (every
  one of them belongs to a dust block), so the arms keep the gem-staff
  arm's zero-RNG invariant (`Projectile.cs:37643-38001`).
* **The owner is an NPC-slot index** in the C# (`Main.npc[(int)ai[0] - 1]`,
  `:30794`). The port's NPC vec drops the dead every tick, so a stored index
  can name a different NPC than the C#'s fixed slot did; the port keeps the
  index shape (the Nebula Arcanum's `ai[1] = index + 1` precedent) and
  re-checks the owner's kind (the C#'s own `type` gate), so a stale index
  kills the ray instead of aiming it at a stranger.
* **The shell's core link is by kind**: the C#'s shell holds the core's slot
  in its `ai[0]` (`:35895-35907`), while the port's saucer family links
  through the carrier write-through (the position link, the port's
  link-by-kind convention for the boss families). The arm therefore looks
  the core up by its kind.
* **The target is the local player**: the C#'s beam reads the owner's
  `NPC.target` (the core's, when the owner is the shell) and the missile
  uses `Player.FindClosest`; the port's NPCs carry no target field and the
  local player is the only one (the MP roster is its own row).
* **The spawn-site `ai0`/`ai1` payload rides the sim's shot drain**: the
  request tuple (`Npc::wants_hostile_shot`) carries no ai slots yet, so the
  drain fills the two values the saucer pair needs (the deathray's owner
  slot + 1 вЂ” the drain knows each requester's index вЂ” and the missile's
  `ai1 = 20f`) and hands them to the pool's `spawn_hostile_ai`. The
  per-shot ai payload the shadow-hand spawn needs
  (`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`, `Projectile.cs:42408-42493`)
  is the follow-up that widens the request tuple.
## The held item's placement (S1-G-17, 2026-11-14)

`ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle` (`Player.cs:50686-51375`) and
`ItemCheck_ApplyHoldStyle` (`:50275-50584`) set the held item's
`itemLocation` + `itemRotation` per use/hold style вЂ” the C# computes them
in the sim, the port computed them in the draw with a single generic arm.
Three real defects came out of that:

* The useStyle-1 swing's **middle third took the X sign from the swing
  start** (`itemLocation.X = position.X + width*0.5 - (frame.W*0.5 - num) *
  direction`, `Player.cs:50829`) вЂ” the C# only subtracts in the *start*
  third; the end (`:50742`) and the middle (`:50773`) add. The item jumped
  to the other side of the body in the middle of every swing.
* The useStyle 5 item's rotation was the raw mouse angle, not the C#'s
  `Player.itemRotation` (`atan2(aimY * direction, aimX * direction) -
  fullRotation`, `:47371-47378`) вЂ” off by PI when facing left (the same
  mirror the S1-G-16 composite arm needed).
* The rest anchor was the holdStyle-1 one for *every* hold style, and the
  use styles 2/6/7/9/11/12/14/15 rode the useStyle-1 arc.

The port now places the item per style (`render/player_layers.rs`'s
`use_item_placement` / `hold_item_placement`):

* the use styles 1 (the thirds + `item_rotation`), 2 (the `num11` table
  over the composite stretch), 3 (the thrust), 4 (the hold-up), 5 (the
  aim), 6/7 (the drinks), 9 (the bow вЂ” through the ported
  `GetFrontHandPosition`, `:50617-50647`), 11 (the `num13` table over the
  composite stretch), 12 (the guitar), 14 and 15;
* the hold styles 1, 2, 3, 4 (the umbrella), 5, 6 and 8.

The port's frame: `pos_x`/`pos_y` are `base.position`, `center_x` is
`base.Center.X`, `mounted_y` is `MountedCenter.Y` (`position.Y + height/2`
= `position.Y + 21`) and `headgear` is `Main.OffsetsPlayerHeadgear`
(`Main.cs:66638-66662`). The `gfxOffY` ease rides the anchor
(`PlayerDrawSet.cs:368`).

Deviations (deliberate, bounded):

* The useStyle 8 (the throw) keeps the useStyle-1 arc: the C#'s three
  phases compare the raw `itemAnimation` counter with the item's
  `useAnimation` (`:51199/:51226`) and the port's draw only carries the
  normalised fraction.
* The useStyle 13 (the rapier) keeps the useStyle-1 arc: the C# leaves
  `itemLocation` at the hold-style value (the branch sets no location,
  `:51174-51196`).
* The per-item nudges (the style-1 types 2330/2320/2341/671, the hold
  styles' torch/fishing-pole/staff specials, the biome torches) are not
  ported; the generic arms carry them.
* `mountOffset` is 0 and `gravDir` is 1 (the port has no mount offset and
  no gravity flip).

Tests: `render::player_layers::tests`'s four `s1_g_17_*` cases (the swing
thirds' X sign, the shoot style's item rotation, the hold styles' anchors
and the eat style's stretch table) вЂ” all mutation-checked (RED on the
pre-fix code).

**S1-P-i04 update (2026-11-19):** the useStyle-1 arm now routes through
`melee_swing.rs` - the per-item nudges deviation above is CLOSED for the
swing (the Bladed Glove claw, the fishing-hammer/Keybrand nudges and the
Breaker Blade's `UsesBetterMeleeItemLocation` offset are ported), the thirds
compare the RAW tick counters in double like the C# (`(double)itemAnimation
< (double)itemAnimationMax * 0.333`), and the draw carries `sItem.type`
(`PlayerCompositeState.item_type`). The `mountOffset`/`gravDir` deviation
stands for the DRAW only (the module carries both for the sim-side hitbox).
See "The broadsword melee swing (S1-P-i04)" below.


## The throw and rapier item placement (S1-G-18, 2026-11-14)

Two more `ItemCheck_ApplyUseStyle` arms and one real bug from the
S1-G-16 composite work:

* The useStyle 8 (the throw) branch (`:51197-51273`) has three phases вЂ” the
  wind-up (the first ticks, while `itemAnimation` is at the item's
  `useAnimation`), the overshoot (`itemAnimation > useAnimation`, which the
  port's swing counter never reaches) and the swing arc
  (`num26 = 1 - itemAnimation/itemAnimationMax`). The item's anchor follows
  the phase (`MountedCenter + (num22 + PI/2).ToRotationVector2() * -2` for
  the wind-up, `... * (-5 * (1 - num26))` for the arc) and the draw rotates
  it a quarter turn (`PlayerDrawLayers.cs:3181-3189`). The port now carries
  the raw animation counters into the draw (`swing_anim_ticks`/
  `swing_max_ticks` вЂ” the port's swing timer runs in seconds, the C#'s
  `itemAnimation` in ticks) and places the item per phase.
* The useStyle 13 (the rapier) branch (`:51174-51196`) sets no location: the
  item keeps the hold-style anchor and is turned by the aim
  (`Player.itemRotation`). The port now does the same instead of riding the
  useStyle-1 arc.
* **The bug:** the umbrella's (and the throw's) `itemRotation` is
  `new Vector2(10 * direction, 10f).ToRotation() + PI/4` (`:50524`,
  `:51201`) вЂ” the XNA `ToRotation` is `atan2(Y, X)`, but the S1-G-16 port
  used `hypot`, i.e. the vector's *length* (14.14) instead of its angle. The
  umbrella's and the throw's poses were therefore rotated by a nonsense
  angle. Fixed to `atan2(10, 10 * direction)` in both the sim's composite
  arms and the draw.

Tests: `s1_g_18_the_throw_style_rides_its_wind_up_and_arc`,
`s1_g_18_the_rapier_keeps_the_hold_anchor` and
`s1_g_18_the_umbrella_rotation_is_the_vector_rotation` вЂ” all
mutation-checked (RED on the pre-fix code; the left-facing cases pin the
mirrored `atan2`, which is where the `hypot` slip showed).

## The shortsword stab (S1-P-i05, 2026-11-20)

The useStyle-3 (Thrust) audit — the stab arm's `itemLocation` maths, the
melee hitbox during the stab and the direction lock, C#-verified against
`Player.cs`. **Scope note:** in 1.4.5.8 the ONLY useStyle-3 items are the
Umbrella (946, `Item.cs:12320-12332`) and the Tragic Umbrella (4707,
`:38683-38695`); the Iron Shortsword (6) is useStyle **13** (the rapier)
since the 1.4 rework (`Item.cs:1455-1471`: `useStyle = 13`, `shoot = 940`,
`noMelee = true`) — its lunge is a projectile, not this arm. The task's
"shortsword stab" is therefore the Thrust style itself.

**The census verdicts:**

* **WRONG — the render's thrust placement**
  (`render/player_layers.rs::use_item_placement`'s style-3 arm vs
  `Player.cs:51031-51063`): (a) the wind-up gate was `remaining > 2/3`
  instead of the C#'s `0.666` literal (`:51033` — the double compare
  `(double)itemAnimation > (double)itemAnimationMax * 0.666`); (b) the
  `num14` extension dropped the `GetAdjustedItemScale(sItem)` factor
  (`:51043`); (c) the clamps were a `clamp(-8, 8)` BOUND instead of the
  C#'s one-sided SNAPS (`:51044-51051`: `num14 > -4 && dir == -1` → -8,
  `num14 < 4 && dir == 1` → 8 — a value between -4 and 4 snaps OUT to ±8,
  it is not bounded IN); (d) the 946/4707 `itemLocation.X -= 6 * direction`
  nudge (`:51054-51057`) was missing. Fixed by delegating to the shared
  verbatim port `player.rs::thrust_item_placement`.
* **MISSING — the stab hitbox** (`ItemCheck_GetMeleeHitbox`'s style-3 arm,
  `Player.cs:45164-45189`): the port had no sim-side `itemLocation` and no
  melee-hitbox port at all — the umbrella pair could not damage anything
  (the cursor melee arm's `held_weapon` gate is `projectile.is_some()`,
  the shooter definition; the umbrellas have no projectile). Ported
  verbatim as `player.rs::thrust_melee_hitbox`: the wind-up `dontAttack`
  (`:45168-45172`), the int-truncated `(int)itemLocation` anchor + the
  `GetAdjustedItemScale`-sized frame (`:45102-45130`), the direction /
  gravDir corner flips (`:45131-45138`), the stab shape (the left 1.4-shift
  reads the PRE-growth Width, `Width *= 1.4`, `Y += Height * 0.6` reads the
  PRE-shrink Height, `Height *= 0.6`, `:45173-45179`) and the umbrella
  `+14 Height / -10 Width / +10 X when left` pair (`:45180-45188`). The
  5094-5097 pre-shrink switch (`:45107-45125`) never meets a style-3 item
  (those four are useStyle 1) — omitted with the cite.
* **MISSING — the per-tick stab sweep** (`ItemCheck`'s melee block,
  `Player.cs:43644-43686`): the C# runs `ItemCheck_GetMeleeHitbox` +
  `ItemCheck_MeleeHitNPCs` EVERY tick while `itemAnimation > 0` — the stab
  rect moves with the extension, so the hit lands when the rect first
  intersects, not on the press. Ported as
  `world_sim/editing.rs::thrust_stab_tick`: the press edge starts the use
  (`ItemCheck_StartActualUse` `:51657-51698` — `attackCD = 0`,
  `ResetMeleeHitCooldowns`, `ApplyItemAnimation`), then every animation
  tick the rect scans the NPC pool in slot order through
  `resolve_melee_strike` — the cursor arm's strike resolution extracted
  VERBATIM (the class multiplier → crit roll → `DamageVar` → the
  Flymeal/cane arms → the penetration sum → `StrikeNPC` → the
  combat-text/net/sound tails; the `UpdatePlayers` draw order is
  byte-identical to the pre-extract inline code). The one-hit-per-swing
  lock is `Player.meleeNPCHitCooldown` (`:3180`), ported as a uid-keyed map
  (the C# indexes stable NPC slots; the port's pool compacts — the
  established `Npc.uid` identity): cleared at the use's start (`:44216`),
  decremented once per non-`dontAttack` damage tick (`:43664`, the
  `:43651` gate skips the wind-up ticks), re-armed to the CURRENT
  `itemAnimation` on a landed hit (`:44414`), gated `<= 0` in the scan
  (`:44246`); `ApplyAttackCooldown` (`:44428-44431`) sets
  `attackCD = max(1, (int)(itemAnimationMax * 0.33))` after each landed
  hit. The sweep runs BEFORE the cursor HUD guard (the C#'s melee block is
  cursor-independent; only the use-START reads `controlUseItem`), so an
  in-flight stab completes with the pointer over the hotbar.
* **WRONG — the direction lock** (`Player.HorizontalMovement`
  `Player.cs:19834-19846`): the port's run-key turn had no `flag3` gate —
  the C# turns only when `(itemAnimation == 0 || useTurn) &&
  mount.AllowDirectionChange && !sandStorm` (`:19837`). A mid-stab player
  turned freely; now the facing locks for the whole animation (the
  umbrellas are `useTurn: false`). `FrameInputs.use_turn` carries the held
  row, `MountState::allow_direction_change` ports `Mount.cs:630-639` (the
  Scutlix 9's `abilityCooldown < row/2` gate; every other mount true), and
  `!sand_storm` joins (the dash owns its 4-tick turn cadence,
  `:36301-36304`).
* **CORRECT — the body rows** (`PlayerFrame` `Player.cs:36377-36387`):
  BOTH branches set row 3 (the vanilla quirk — the `:36385` else is dead);
  the port already did this. The citation was wrong (`:36363-36372`, the
  DrinkLong arm) — re-cited.
* **CORRECT — the composite arms**: the style-3 arm sets NO composite
  arms (`Player.cs:51031-51063` has no `SetCompositeArm*` call — the
  per-frame reset at `:43376-43377` leaves them disabled, the body-row
  cells carry the pose); the port's `apply_item_composite_arms` has no
  style-3 arm either. No change.

**Deviations (deliberate):**

* `GetAdjustedItemScale` (`Player.cs:42566-42582`) folds to the prefixed
  `Item.scale` — the `meleeScaleGlove` ×1.1 arm has no port granter (the
  Titan Glove's scale half is the documented S1-C-12 skip). The prefix
  rides the held tuple into the draw and the `hand_key` (the G6 rule: a
  reforge changes the held item's pixels).
* The held frame is the atlas icon quad — the established
  `Item.GetDrawHitbox` stand-in the renderer already uses (the umbrellas'
  44×44 stock frame matches their icon).
* The `CanHit` wall check (`:44287`) and the `nPC.immune[whoAmI] == 0`
  gate (`:44246`) ride the port's established `strike_melee` `hurt_cd`
  stand-in (the cursor melee arm's convention).
* The cursor arm keeps its full-swing `attack_cd` overwrite after
  `resolve_melee_strike` (the established start-arm stand-in); the stab
  sweep keeps the C#'s `ApplyAttackCooldown` value. The extraction added
  the `:44414`/`:44419` tail to the shared helper — for the cursor arm the
  cooldown insert is inert (its next press re-starts the swing) and the
  `attack_cd` write is overwritten by the caller's start arm, so the
  cursor path's behaviour and RNG draws are unchanged.
* `mountOffset` (`HeightOffsetHitboxCenter`) stands at 0 and `gravDir` at
  1 — the port's established folds (no mount height offsets, no gravity
  flip).

**RNG:** zero new draws. The sweep's landed hits ride the SAME
`UpdatePlayers` resolution the cursor arm uses (crit → `DamageVar` → the
probe/combat-text/hit-sound tails, in that order); the use-start's
`UseSound` rides `start_swing_extras` like every other swing. The
non-landed ticks draw nothing (the C#'s `ItemCheck_GetMeleeHitbox` +
scan are pure).

**Witnesses (WRITTEN NOT RUN — code-only mode):**
`player.rs::s1_p_i05_thrust_tests` (4: the 0.666 boundary incl. the
0.6661/0.6665 pair that discriminates the 2/3 gate, the extension / snap /

## The draw phase order (S1-B-7, 2026-11-14)

`Main.DoDraw` (`Main.cs:61707-62507`) draws the world in a fixed
sequence; the port had one draw branch with no order assertion, and the
dropped items were drawn **before** the NPCs and the player вЂ” the C# draws
them last of the entity group (`Main.cs:62278`):

```
projectiles в†’ the players (`:62256`) в†’ the NPCs over the players (`:62263`)
в†’ the items (`:62278`) в†’ the rain (`:62279`) в†’ the gore/dust (`:62282`/`:62293`)
в†’ the waters (`:62300`) в†’ the wires (`:62303`) в†’ the projectiles over the
wires UI (`:62315`)
```

The port now draws the dropped items after the players and the NPCs
(`render/tiles.rs`: the items' pass moved behind the player passes), and
the draw passes carry a phase marker (`frame.rs`'s `draw_phase`,
`render/tiles.rs`'s `draw_phase`) so the order is assertable:
`the_draw_passes_run_in_the_csharp_order` pins the marker order вЂ” the
world pass's `npcs_behind_tiles в†’ npcs в†’ player в†’ items` and the frame's
`sky в†’ world в†’ rain в†’ wires в†’ projectiles`. The markers move with the
passes, so a future reorder fails the test (mutation-checked: RED on the
pre-fix code).

Scope notes (the remaining divergences, all deliberate):

* The C# splits the NPCs into two buckets вЂ” `DoDraw_DrawNPCsOverTiles`
  (`:63301`, before the players) and `DrawCachedNPCs(DrawCacheNPCsOver-
  Players)` (`:62263`, after them). The port has one NPC bucket, at the
  "over the tiles" slot, so the NPCs that vanilla draws over the player
  are drawn under it.
* The C# splits the projectiles into four buckets (`CacheProjDraws`:
  behind the projectiles, over the players, over the NPCs, over the wires
  UI). The port has one bucket, at the "over the wires UI" slot, so the
  projectiles are drawn over the player.
* The C#'s leaves ride the particle system (`ParticleSystem_World_Over-
  Players`, `:62259`); the port draws them with the dust cluster
  (`frame.rs`'s leaf pass) вЂ” the same neighbourhood as the rain/sand.
* The gore pass (`Main.cs:62282`) is unported (the gore pool is empty).

## The Deerclops' projectile family (S1-D-4b-5, 2026-11-14)

The ROADMAP's S1-D-4b-5 slice covers the Deerclops' two projectile
families: the aiStyle-157 ice spike (`Projectile.cs:51358-51477`) and the
Insanity Shadow's spawn (`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`,
`Projectile.cs:42408-42493`) вЂ” the spawn that feeds the aiStyle-187 arm
landed with S1-D-4b-1.

**The aiStyle-157 arm** (the 961; the 1041 rides the same style and has no
ported row). The arm's parameter row for the 961 (`:51376-51389`) is the
fade-in window 10, the fade-out from the 10th tick and the kill at the
20th; the first tick takes the rotation from the velocity and rolls one of
the sheet's five frames (`Main.rand.Next(5)`, `:51439`).

**The `Opacity` property** (`Projectile.cs:540-549`) is a view over
`alpha`, not a field of its own: the getter is `1 - alpha / 255` and the
setter writes `alpha = (int)Clamp((1 - value) * 255, 0, 255)`. The port
models it with the `opacity_of`/`alpha_of` helpers. The S1-D-4b-1 arm (the
aiStyle-133 Dark Mage marker) had carried the opacity as a separate slot
field; that field is gone and the arm writes the alpha, exactly as the
C#'s property does вЂ” the marker's alpha now runs 255 в†’ 242 в†’ 0 в†’ 127 в†’ 255
(the dying tick) instead of the separate opacity value.

**The shadow hand's spawn** now rides the C#'s pick
(`Projectile.RandomizeInsanityShadowFor`): the four cases are the arm's
four variations (`Projectile.cs:42592-42634`), each handing the arm the
variation's start age (0 / 180 / 300 / 390) and the angle, plus the
position and the velocity. The port's old spawn (a made-up ring of six
hands with a stand-in velocity) had no `ai` payload, so every shadow ran
the arm's variation 0 (the drift) вЂ” the arm's other three variations were
dead code.

**The spawn-site `ai0`/`ai1` payload** (`NewProjectile`'s trailing
arguments, `Projectile.cs:10862-10863`) rides the new
`Npc::wants_hostile_shot_ai` request list (`HostileShotAi`): the shots
whose call site passes a non-zero `ai0`/`ai1`. The list joins the plain
`wants_hostile_shot` one (whose call sites pass zero). The S1-D-4b-4
slicer's per-kind table in the sim's drain is retired: the Saucer deathray
now carries its owner slot from the spawn site (`ai0 = whoAmI + 1`, the
C#'s own value вЂ” the port's `Npc::slot` is the sim's current index) and
the missile its `ai1 = 20f`.

Two more Deerclops divergences fell out of the port:

* **The rubble is the 962, not the 961** (`NPC.cs:44463`: the chunk, the
  aiStyle-1 flight, `ai1 = 6 + Next(6)`), and the port now has the 962's
  row (`:9199-9206`). The port's rubble shot the 961 (the forward spike)
  instead.
* **The "blizzard" state spawns no projectile** (`NPC.cs:44285-44320`):
  it chills the player (the buff 32, 720 ticks, inside 800 px). The port
  fired a damage-0 spike at the Deerclops instead вЂ” a stand-in with no
  vanilla counterpart, now gone. The buff itself is the buff row
  (S1-E-7).

Deviations:

* **The dust and the sound are SKIPPED** (the arm's `:51431-51464` and
  `:51453-51461`) вЂ” no dust/sound layer. The frame roll is kept: it is
  the visible state.
* **The C#'s rejection loop never rejects in the port**
  (`Projectile.cs:42476-42493`): the only player IS the target, and the
  C# skips the target in that check, so the pick runs once.
* **The C#'s spike cadence and tile scan are the port's stand-in**: the
  forward/both-sides rows (`MakeSpikesForward`/`MakeSpikesBothSides`,
  `NPC.cs:44466-44534`) and `FindBestY` (`:44586-44640`) pick the spike's
  tile row from the ground scan; the port fires its own rows at the
  Deerclops' feet (the `ai1` scale factor is the C#'s). The rubble's
  `ShootRubbleUp` tile scan and up-bias (`:44448-44465`) are the same
  stand-in. The follow-up row is the cadence row.

## The invasion surface band (S1-F-18, 2026-11-14)

`Spawner.ShouldSpawnInvasionEnemies` (`NPC.cs:442-463`) compares
`position.Y < Main.worldSurface * 16.0 + NPC.sHeight` вЂ” and `NPC.sHeight` is
**1200** (`NPC.cs:6769`), not the 200 the port used. The invasion's
above-surface band was therefore ~6Г— too narrow; it now reads
`crate::spawner::S_HEIGHT` (the port's constant already carried the
vanilla's 1200) and the window test pins both edges (3000 px below the
surface spawns, 3200 px does not вЂ” the test world's surface is row 120 =
px 1920). The В±3000 px window around `invasionX` and the town-NPC fallback
stay as they were (the latter rides the town roster).

## The drop-rate report (S1-E-15, 2026-11-14)

`IItemDropRule.ReportDroprates` and its data (`DropRateInfo`,
`DropRateInfoChainFeed`) are ported into `tr_core::loot`: the trait gains
`report_droprates` (the default reports nothing, so the rule classes that
S1-E-14 still has to port compile unchanged), and the port's rule classes
report with the C#'s formulas вЂ” `CommonDrop`'s
`(numerator / denominator) * the parent's rate`, `CommonDropWithRerolls`'s
`1 - (1 - numerator/denominator)^rerolls`, `OneFromOptionsDrop`'s shared
per-option rate, the nested rules' (expert/master/extra-gel) pairs, and
`DropOneByOne`'s chunk-scaled stack range. `Chains.ReportDroprates`
scales per chain kind (`Chains.cs:24-30`: `TryIfFailedRandomRoll` feeds
`1 - the parent's own rate`; `:50-56`/`:76-82`: `TryIfSucceeded` and
`TryIfDoesntFillConditions` feed the parent's rate itself вЂ” corrected
2026-11-18 with S1-E-14a, the earlier port scaled every kind by `1 - rate`).
`LeadingConditionRule` reports its chains at rate 1
(`LeadingConditionRule.cs:22-26`, S1-E-14a). `ItemDropDatabase::report_droprates` is
`BestiaryDatabase.ExtractDropsForNPC` (`BestiaryDatabase.cs:70-88`): the
NPC's rules report their rows with a fresh feed (the rate 1.0) and the
globals stay out.

The bestiary's "Drops:" list now prints those rows instead of the 4-row
hand-written table (`ui/bestiary.rs`) вЂ” the stack range + the rate, in
`UIBestiaryInfoItemLine.GetDropInfo`'s format (`UIBestiaryInfoItemLine.cs:78-104`)
with `Utils.PrettifyPercentDisplay`'s trimmed percentage
(`Utils.cs:1105-1109`).

Scope notes: the C#'s condition lists (`DropRateInfo.conditions`) and the
chains' `hideLootReport` flag are not modelled by the port, so the rows
carry no condition text and the chained rows always print; the town-NPC and
critter providers, the search filters, the sorting, the flavour and the MP
kill-sync ride the town/MP subsystems. `MasterModeDropOnAllPlayers` sites
pass `this._masterModeDropRng` (`ItemDropDatabase.cs:15` = 4) but the
generated rows carry the factory default 1 (pre-existing since M4-LOOT-2,
kept for row stability вЂ” S1-E-14a leaves it unchanged; the per-player
master-drop chance is 1/1 instead of 1/4 until a dedicated fix).

## The hurting-tile family (S1-E-13a, 2026-11-14)

`crates/tr-app/src/touch_damage.rs` now carries the vanilla's tile-contact
hazards in full. `Collision.CanTileHurt` (`Collision.cs:3206-3225`) reads the
four `TileID.Sets` tables (`TileID.cs:605-609` вЂ” `TouchDamageDestroyTile`,
`Suffocate`, `TouchDamageHot`, `TouchDamageBleeding` and the
`TouchDamageImmediate` value table), all of which the S1-F-8 generator already
emits into `tr-core/src/tiledata/sets.rs`: the hand-written nine-row
immediate table is gone, and the generated bitsets replace the "no ported
members yet" note the module used to carry. `Collision.HurtTiles`
(`Collision.cs:3115-3204`) adds the suffocate shrink (`num6 = 2`,
`:3155-3163`) вЂ” the sands pull the box in by two pixels on every side, and a
sloped suffocating tile is skipped outright (`:3164-3169`).

`Player.ApplyTouchDamage` (`Player.cs:28977-29019`) is ported arm by arm:
the rolled immediate damage (`Main.DamageVar(num, -luck)`), the burning
(buff 67 for 20 ticks) and bleeding (buff 30 for 600-1200 ticks) buffs that
fire only when the hit was *not* swallowed вЂ” the C#'s `flag` is set when
`Hurt` returns 0, so an immune player does not burn or bleed вЂ” the
`suffocateDelay` counter (five ticks in the sand, the sixth suffocates with
buff 68) and the destroy-on-touch `WorldGen.KillTile` for the four thorn
tiles. The counter is the C#'s `byte` field (`Player.cs:2318`) and keeps the
source's quirk: it only resets when another hurt tile is touched, not when
the player walks out of the sand.

Deliberate deviations:

1. `Player.fireWalk` (the Obsidian Skull) has no ported accessor, so the hot
   arm always fires вЂ” the C#'s `player == null || !player.fireWalk`
   (`:3220`) with a player that cannot walk on fire.
2. `Player.shimmering` (the C#'s gate around the whole pass,
   `Player.cs:27608`) has no ported player state, so the pass always runs.
3. `Player.TouchedTiles` (the movement-traced fallback in `GetHurtTile`)
   is still not modelled вЂ” the port's box scan covers the same area with the
   source's own В±1 margin.
4. ~~`ImmunityCooldownID.TileContactDamage` collapses into the port's single
   `hurt_cd`~~ **CLOSED by the W4-d115 wiring round (M4-HAZARD-1)**: the
   lane rides its own `Player.hurt_cooldowns` slot — the C#'s per-source
   array is ported (see "W4-d115 wiring round addendum").
5. The bleeding duration's roll rides the port's `item_rng` stream (the C#'s
   `Main.rand`), the same stream the damage roll already used.

Out (the rest of S1-E-13): `HitTiles`/`HitTilesInACircle`, `StickyTiles` +
`Player.StickyMovement`, `SwitchTiles`, `BuildTileContacts`,
`noSlopeCollision`, `AdvancedTileCollision` and `DrownCollision`/
`GetWaterLine`.
## The goblin family's ids (S1-D-3d, 2026-11-14)

The port's four goblin kinds carried **each other's** vanilla `NPCID`: the
kind named `GoblinThief` sat on the type 26 (the vanilla's **peon**), the
`GoblinWarrior` on the 27 (the **thief**), the `GoblinArcher` on the 28
(the **warrior**) and the `GoblinPeon` on the 111 (the **archer**) вЂ” the
peon/thief/warrior/archer cycle rotated by one.

The C#'s rows (`ID/NPCID.cs:10729-10733`/`:10899`, the `SetDefaults` arms
`NPC.cs:15644-15730`):

| kind | type | HP | damage | defense | kb resist | value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the peon | 26 | 60 | 12 | 4 | 0.8 | 100 |
| the thief | 27 | 80 | 20 | 6 | 0.7 | 200 |
| the warrior | 28 | 110 | 25 | 8 | 0.5 | 150 |
| the archer | 111 | 80 | 20 | 6 | 0.7 | 200 |

The port's stats rows followed the **ids** (the thief carried the peon's
60 HP, the warrior and the peon the thief's 80, the archer the warrior's
110), and the bestiary's `net_id` вЂ” the C#'s `NPC.type` вЂ” carried the
same rotation. The loot tables key on that net id, so a "Goblin Thief"
dropped the peon's loot and credited the peon's bestiary entry.

The fix moves the ids and the stats back onto the names: the bestiary's
four `net_id`s follow the C# (`cs_id` reads them through the S1-F-3
fallback), and the stats rows carry the C#'s values per name. The port's
`docs/NPC_AI_TAXONOMY.md` had the C#'s mapping all along ("26/27/28 |
Goblin Peon/Thief/Warrior | 60/80/110 | 12/20/25 | 4/6/8") вЂ” the code
had drifted from the doc.

Two duplicate match arms died with the fix: the stats functions carried a
second, by-name set of goblin rows *after* the by-id set, so the correct
values were unreachable (`unreachable pattern` warnings). The dead rows
are gone and the effective rows carry the C#'s values.

The port's own wire ids (the `NpcKind` u16 roster: 57/58/59/60) and the
sprite sheets (`NPC_27`/`NPC_28`/`NPC_111`/`NPC_26`) were already keyed by
name and are untouched вЂ” the kinds, their art and their ids now agree.

## The aiStyle-3 walk-speed table (S1-D-3c, 2026-11-14)

`AI_003_Fighters` (`NPC.cs:55856-59800`) is the vanilla's ground-fighter
machine: the per-type walk groups, the shooters' stop-and-fire cycle and
the boss riders. The port ran every kind that rides its walker step at one
speed вЂ” the skeleton's 0.8 for the cave walkers, the pirates and the
martians, the zombie's own 0.6, the shooters' 5.0 вЂ” while the C#'s arm
carries a per-type velocity cap per group:

| group | cap | kinds (the C#'s rows) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the `num107` default (`:58322-58374`) | 1f | the zombie (3), the undead miner (44), the goblin warrior (28) |
| the `num83` group (`:57606-57691`) | 1.5f | the skeleton (21), the goblin peon (26); the gray grunt 1.8, the giga zapper 2.25, the vortex rifleman 6, the vortex soldier 4 |
| the cap-2 group (`:57554-57578`) | 2f | the goblin thief (27), the pirate deckhand (212) |
| the cap-3 group (`:57520-57552`) | 3f | the pirate captain's mate (213) |
| the shooters' group (`:59717-59750`) | 1f | the pirate captain (216), the martian officer (383); the pirate archer 2, the corsair 1.5, the scrambler/ray gunner 2, the stardust spider/soldier 2, the vortex hunter 4, the martian walker 4 |
| the Martian engineer's own arm (`:58032-58069`) | 1.5f | the martian engineer (386) |

`NpcKind::ai3_walk_speed` is the port's table; the zombie, the cave
walkers (the skeleton, the undead miner, the pirate deckhand, the pirate
captain's mate), the goblins and the shooters read it instead of their
hard-coded speed. The kinds whose arm is bespoke (the pillar mobs, the
vortex family, the Goblin Archer) keep their own speed and are not in the
table.

Deviations:

* **The C#'s acceleration model is not ported**: the vanilla ramps the
  velocity toward the cap at 0.07/tick (0.09/0.08/0.5/1.0 for the shooter
  rows) and decays it Г—0.8 past the cap; the port's walker step sets the
  velocity to the cap directly. The cap itself вЂ” the value the C#'s
  acceleration converges to вЂ” is the port's table.
* **The C#'s scale factor on the `num107` group** (`num107 *= 1f + (1f -
  this.scale)`, `:58374-58376`) rides the kind's `scale` (the vanilla's
  humanoid scales are 0.9-1.1); the port's scale is 1 for these kinds, so
  the factor is 1 вЂ” except for the kinds whose scale the port does not
  carry (the goblins' 0.9/0.95/1.1), which the group does not scale
  anyway.

## The drowning family (S1-E-13b, 2026-11-14)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs` ports `Collision.DrownCollision`
(`Collision.cs:1383-1432`) and the two water-line helpers
(`GetWaterLine` `:1498-1544`, `GetWaterLineIterate` `:1551-1570`). The
drown probe is the C#'s: the 10x12 box at the entity's head (the centre
column, `Position.Y + height/2 - 6` for the vanilla gravity, `:1385-1400`),
the liquid's surface offset (`(256 - liquid) / 32 * 2`, `:1421-1423`), the
lava and shimmer exclusion (the honey drowns, `:1416`) and the solid-floor
row (the gravity-side row of the scan, `:1409`/`:1416`) вЂ” the `includeSlopes`
mode lifts that exclusion for the sloped and half-brick blocks, exactly like
the C#'s `blockType() != 0` arm.

`Player::check_drowning` (`Player.cs:23191-23281`) replaces the port's
"the player is in water" stand-in with that probe: the breath meter now
drains only while the **head** is under the surface, and refills with the
C#'s 3 ticks per tick (`breathCD`/`breathCDMax` kept). Before this row the
port's breath drained whenever the wet flags said "somewhere in water", so
wading through a shallow pool cost air.

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s accessory arms (the Merman armour 250/4275, the breathing reed,
   the gills, the shimmering and the mount 4) have no ported counterparts вЂ”
   the port has no accessory system for them, so the probe's own flag
   decides.
2. The C#'s drowning bubbles and the drowning death sound (23) ride the
   effect and audio systems, which are out of scope here.
3. `Utils.Clamp(value, 0, Main.maxTilesY - 40)` folds a negative bound back
   onto itself for the small test worlds; the port clamps the bound at zero
   instead (the scan then runs empty either way).
4. The port runs the breath drain inside `update_survival` (the merged
   life-regen step); the C#'s `CheckDrowning` sits later in `Player.Update`
   (`:27655`, after `StickyMovement`).

Out (the rest of S1-E-13): `HitTiles`/`HitTilesInACircle`, `SwitchTiles`,
`BuildTileContacts`, `noSlopeCollision` and `AdvancedTileCollision`.
## The sticky-surface family (S1-E-13c, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs::sticky_tiles` ports `Collision.StickyTiles`
(`Collision.cs:3362-3435`): the В±1-tile scan window clamped to
`Main.maxTilesY - 40` (`:3369-3384`), the cobweb (51) arm with its zero margin
and `16.01` tall box (`:3396-3406`), and the honey-block (229) arm gated on
`slope() == 0` (`:3410`) with the 1 px margin plus the half brick's `+8` / `-8`
shrunken box (`:3414-3423`). The source's inline `Main.rand.Next(30)` type-30
web puff (`:3401`, `:3425`) is drawn **inside** the probe, at the source's
position relative to the return, and handed back as a flag: the caller owns
`Main.dust`, so `Player::sticky_movement` queues it. The 229 arm's copy of that
`if` tests `Main.tile[i, j].type == 51`, which is always false there and
short-circuits before the `Next(30)`, so the port passes `false` вЂ” drawing it
would add a stream step the C# never takes.

`Player::sticky_movement` (`Player.cs:22910-23087`) keeps the source's order:
the `Next(20,100)` / `Next(80,300)` break roll for `stickyBreak`
(`:22938-22954`) вЂ” the C#'s bitwise `|` means the draw happens even when the
`flag` cart test short-circuits the assignment вЂ” then the cart-above-5-px
early return (`:22956-22958`), `fallStart` (`:22960`), the honey's jump
exemption (`:22961-22964`), the gel/slime mount's halving with its `0.0025`
floor (`:22965-22972`), the `В±1` X cap with the `0.85`/`0.6` damp and the
`В±1`/`-5` Y cap with the `0.96`/`0.3` damp (`:22975-23028`), and the type-153
honey puffs on the hit row plus the two rows below (`:23030-23081`) with their
`Next(0,6)` scale / `velocity *= 0.1` / `noGravity` tail. The tick only has
`&World`, so the tile kill (`WorldGen.KillTile`, `:22949`) and the puffs are
queued and drained in `world_sim/player.rs` вЂ” the same `pending_sparks`
pattern the minecart uses; the drain runs `DustPool::new_dust` on the
`UpdatePlayers` stream, so the pool's own rolls stay interleaved exactly as the
C# interleaves `Main.rand`.

Call site: `Player::update_with_grapple` invokes it between the grapple block
and `check_drowning`, matching `Player.cs:27653-27655`
(`GrappleMovement` в†’ `StickyMovement` в†’ `CheckDrowning`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. **No shimmer gate.** `Player.shimmering` (`:22912-22915`) has no port
   counterpart yet (the shimmer absorption pass is unported), so the early
   return is absent rather than always-false.
2. **No gravity flip.** The C# mirrors the Y drag on `gravDir` (`:22991`,
   `:23010`); the port has no gravity flip, so only the `gravDir == 1` arm
   (`:23012-23027`) runs, matching the vanilla's default `1f` (`Player.cs:1956`).
3. **Hook multi-player gates folded.** `whoAmI == Main.myPlayer` (`:22936`)
   collapses (the port is single-player) and the `Main.netMode == 1` break
   replication (`:22950-22953`) is net-only.
4. **`stickyBreak` survives a respawn.** The C# writes the counter at exactly
   four sites, all inside `StickyMovement` (`:22938`, `:22948`, `:23085`);
   `Player.Spawn` never clears it, so the port's revive path does not either.
## The remaining collision family (S1-E-13d, 2026-11-16)

`crates/tr-app/src/collision.rs` gains the five functions S1-E-13's parent row
still listed after the 13a/13b/13c splits.

* `no_slope_collision` (`Collision.cs:2033-2133`) is `tile_collision` with the
  slope gates removed (`:2059`'s solid conjunct has no `slope()` arm at all).
  The up arm keeps its `+ 0.01f` (`:2124`); the down arm has no `gravDir` term
  (`:2088` is bare `vector4.Y - (vector3.Y + Height)`), unlike
  `TileCollision`'s caller-supplied `gravDir`.
* `advanced_tile_collision` (`:4422-4566`) keeps the slope gates but adds the
  `forcedIgnoredTiles` conjunct (`:4449`), the neighbour-slope exemptions on the
  two side arms (`:4514-4518` skips a slope 2/4 tile to the left,
  `:4534-4538` a slope 1/3 tile to the right) and the `gravDir`-dependent
  nudges вЂ” `-0.01f` on the down arm when `gravDir == -1` (`:4507`), `+0.01f` on
  the up arm when `gravDir == 1` (`:4557`).
* `hit_tiles` / `hit_tiles_in_a_circle` (`:3063-3108`, `:3016-3061`) share one
  scan. Its box test is **inclusive** on all four edges (`:3101`), unlike
  `TileCollision`'s strict comparisons, and the horizontal clamp stops at
  `Main.maxTilesX`, not `maxTilesX - 1` (`:3027`). The circle arm adds the
  centre-distance gate `(centre - (tile + (8, 8))).Length() < (Width + Height) / 4`
  (`:3054`).
* `build_tile_contacts` (`:2135-2290`) enumerates `TileContact`s: the position
  truncates to whole pixels first (`:2137`), the window is `(x - 1) / 16 - 1 ..
  (x + 1 + w) / 16 + 1` and `(y - 1) / 16 - 1 .. (y + 3 + h) / 16 + 1`
  (`:2140-2143`), the Left/Right arms exclude slopes 3/1 and 4/2 respectively
  (`:2177`/`:2181`), and the Top/Bottom arms switch on the slope with the
  slope-3/4 inset variants (`:2232-2257`) and a diagonal `BottomLeft`/
  `BottomRight` fallback when the box only grazes a corner (`:2260-2287`).
  Overlaps are `(int)Math.Max(Math.Min(...) - Math.Max(...) + 0.5f, 1f)`.

`tile_dust_amount` ports `WorldGen.KillTile_GetTileDustAmount`
(`WorldGen.cs:66597-66685`) so the hit scan's effect half is expressible.

Deliberate deviations:

1. **`HitTiles` never destroys a tile, because the source does not either.**
   Both call sites answer a hit with `WorldGen.KillTile(i, j, fail: true,
   effectOnly: true)`; that overload runs `CheckTileBreakability`, the
   item/furniture-rack drops and the dust loop, then **returns** at
   `WorldGen.cs:63704-63707` before any removal, framing or item spawn. The
   port therefore returns the hit cells and `tile_dust_amount` gives the counts
   the C# would spawn. `tr_core::edit::kill_tile` is the *destructive*
   `KillTile` and must not be called here: doing so would break tiles the
   vanilla only shakes.
2. **The dust and the shake sound are not spawned.** The port has no tile-dust
   layer (the same gap the failing mine tick records at
   `world_sim/editing.rs:1350`) and no `SoundEngine` handle in
   `collision.rs`. `tile_dust_amount` is the seam a dust layer would call;
   until it exists the scan is a pure geometry query.
3. **`advanced_tile_collision` and `no_slope_collision` are unexercised.**
   Their only callers are `NPC.Collision_MoveSandshark` (`NPC.cs:92732`) and
   `NPC.Collision_MoveSnailOnSlopes` (`:92782`); the sandshark and snail NPC
   families are unported, so both are marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` with the
   missing caller named in place rather than inventing one. They are covered
   by unit tests, not by gameplay. `build_tile_contacts` is not among them: it
   landed with its caller in S1-E-13e (`ApplyConveyorBeltMovementToVelocity`),
   and that branch's copy is the one in the tree.
4. **The `Main.tile[i В± 1, j] == null в†’ new Tile()` allocations**
   (`:4514-4517`, `:4534-4537`, `:63533-63536`) fold out: the port's tile array
   is dense, so a missing neighbour reads as an empty tile through
   `world.tile()`'s `Option`, which is what the allocation would have produced.

## The Brain of Cthulhu's machine (S1-D-3e, 2026-11-14)

`AI_054` (`NPC.cs:32370-32656`) is the Brain of Cthulhu's family machine:
the creeper swarm's shield, the blink machine (the Brain teleports around
the player, fading out and in), the retreat when its swarm dies and the
despawn ramp when the player leaves the Crimson zone. The port ran a
stand-in вЂ” a 60-tick drift toward the player plus a 9-px dash.

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the normal phase** (`:32522-32527`): the velocity points at the player
  at 1 px/tick (the getGood world's 3);
* **the blink** (`:32532-32599`): the `localAI[1]` timer (120 + `Next(300)`
  ticks, re-rolled every tick) picks a tile 12-40 tiles from the player
  (the signs are random, the player's velocity leads the pick, the tile
  must be free of solid blocks and вЂ” after the 75th try вЂ” in line of sight
  of the player), the fade-in (alpha + 5/tick to 255) teleports the Brain
  onto it and the fade-out (alpha в€’ 5/tick) returns to the normal phase;
* **the retreat** (`:32401-32518`): with no Creeper left the Brain switches
  to `ai[0] = -1` and drifts at 8 px through the 50/51 blend; its timer
  (60 + `Next(120)` ticks) picks a tile 10-12 tiles out (no sight gate) and
  the `-2`/`-3` states fade the Brain in on it and back out;
* **the despawn ramp** (`:32619-32636`): a dead player or a player out of
  the Crimson zone sinks the Brain (`velocity.Y += (localAI[3] - 60) * 0.25`)
  and fades it out.

The creeper swarm's spawn and the shield stay in the sim's pass
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`: the 20 Creepers + `dont_take_damage` while one
lives); the arm's "no Creeper left" test needs the live count, so the sim
writes it into `Npc::brain_local[2]` (the C#'s `num818`).

Deviations:

* **The gore/dust burst is SKIPPED** (`:32401-32419`) вЂ” no dust/gore layer.
* **The MP-only branches use the single-player values** (`Main.netMode !=
  0`): the port has no multiplayer arm, so the blink's period, the fade
  rates and the "crimson boss" bookkeeping are the single-player ones.
* **`justHit` rides the port's `hurt_cd`** (the hit cooldown) вЂ” the C#'s
  flag is a single tick, the port's window is the timer the other arms
  use for the same purpose (the port's convention, documented in the
  Goblin Archer's arm).
* **The sound cues are SKIPPED** (the retreat's roar `SoundID 3`/`15`,
  `:32408`/`:32418`, and the teleport's `Item8`, `:32505`/`:32622`) вЂ”
  the arm carries no audio seam (the port's convention for the boss
  machines; the S1-D-3e audit, 2026-11-18).
* **The `getGoodWorld` arms fold to the classic values** вЂ” the normal
  drift's 3-px speed (`:32538-32541`), the 40-Creeper swarm
  (`GetBrainOfCthuluCreepersCount`, `:50936-50943`) and the
  `brainOfGravity` write (`:32402-32405`) are the for-the-worthy
  branches; the port's boss arms run constants-off (no difficulty
  flags), so the classic 1-px drift and the 20-Creeper swarm stand.

**Audit (2026-11-18, `task/S1-D-3-aistyle54`, code-only mode).** A
line-by-line re-read of the whole `AI_054` block against `update_brain`
confirmed the machine (the swarm init/shield/count seam, the 50/51
retreat blend, the `60 + Next(120)` / `120 + Next(300)` timers re-rolled
every tick, the 10-12 / 12-40 tile picks with the sign rolls, the
velocity lead, the try-101 acceptance and the sight gate after the 75th
try, the В±25 / В±5 fades, the despawn ramp). Two real defects were fixed
surgically:

1. **The 6000-px Manhattan despawn gate was missing** (`:32387-32399`:
   `Math.Abs(center.X - player.Center.X) + Math.Abs(center.Y -
   player.Center.Y) > 6000f` в†’ `active = false`, `life = 0`). The arm
   now deactivates (`hp = 0`) before any machine tick; the boundary is
   the C#'s strict `>` (exactly 6000 lives). The generic `tick_despawn`
   pass does not cover it вЂ” its only writer is the aiStyle-4 arm.
2. **The normal drift's f32 order** (`:32549-32551`): the C# computes
   the reciprocal first (`num816 = num817 / num816`) and then multiplies
   (`delta * num816`); the port ran `dx / d * speed`, which rounds one
   ulp away on some inputs. Witness: dx = 100, dy = 72 в†’ the
   reciprocal-first product is `0.8115344`, the divide-first
   `0.81153435`. The arm now scales by the reciprocal.

Witness tests WRITTEN, NOT RUN (code-only mode вЂ” no compiler invoked):
`s1_d_3e_tests::{s1_d_3e_audit_the_brain_despawns_beyond_6000_manhattan_px,
s1_d_3e_audit_the_normal_drift_scales_by_the_reciprocal}`. The RNG
argument: the fixes add no draws (the despawn gate returns before any
roll; the reciprocal reorders arithmetic only), so the `UpdateNpcs`
stream order is unchanged вЂ” the per-tick draw sequence stays
`Next(300)` в†’ (on fire) the pick's `Next(12,41)`Г—2 + `Next(2)`Г—2 per
try, and the retreat's optional `Next(5)` в†’ `Next(120)` в†’ the pick's
`Next(10,13)`Г—2 + `Next(2)`Г—2.

## The Skeletron head's machine (S1-D-3f, 2026-11-14)

`AI_011` (`NPC.cs:21919-22298`) is the Skeletron head's family machine:
the two hands' spawn, the spin state, the charge, the enraged day-time
state and the despawn. The port ran an EoC-shaped v1 вЂ” a 480-tick hover
into an 8-px dash вЂ” and the head never spawned its hands (the hand's own
arm was ported but nothing created the hands).

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the spin state (`ai[1] == 0`, `:22019-22117`)**: the `ai[2]` timer
  (800 ticks в†’ the charge), the rotation (`velocity.X / 15`) and the hover
  acceleration вЂ” the 250-px band above/below the player, the 0.02/0.05
  accelerations and the 2/8 caps (the expert's 0.03/0.07 and 4/9.5);
* **the charge (`ai[1] == 1`, `:22118-22244`)**: the defense drops by 10,
  the timer (400 ticks в†’ the spin) and the 1.5-px rush (the expert's 3.5
  with the per-distance ramp and the hand-count share);
* **the enraged state (`ai[1] == 2`, `:22245-22259`)**: the day-time (or
  the type-68) turns the head invulnerable вЂ” the damage and the defense
  9999 вЂ” and it rushes at 8 px;
* **the despawn (`ai[1] == 3`, `:22260-22270`)**: a dead player or one
  2000 px away sinks the head and damps it;
* **the expert's spin shot** (`:21978-22018`): every 80 ticks (40 with no
  hand left) the head fires a **Skull (270)** вЂ” the projectile's row is
  new (`Projectile.cs:3558-3566`: 26x26, the aiStyle-1 flight, penetrate
  3, alpha 255, hostile).

The hands' spawn rides the sim's pass (the C#'s `ai[0] == 0` init,
`:21924-21941`): the lower hand (`ai[0] = -1`) and the upper hand
(`ai[0] = 1`, `ai[3] = 150`). The live hand count — the C#'s LOCAL
`num168` — rides `World.skeletron_hands_alive` (B-1: it used to ride the
head's `ai[3]`, which collided with the red-hat latch — see "Loot rule
classes" above).

Deviations:

* **The dust is SKIPPED** (`:22280-22296`) вЂ” no dust layer.
* **The sounds are SKIPPED** (the spawn cue, the spin cue and the charge
  cue) вЂ” no sound layer.
* **The red-hat adjustments** (`RedHatSkeletronAdjustmentsEnabled`, the
  `flag21` rows) are the world-seed flags the port does not carry; the
  getGood world's rows (the 40-creeper count, the 0.8 spin period) ride
  the classic values.
* **The MP-only branches** (`Main.netMode != 0`) use the single-player
  values.

  expert). The expert rows now ride an `expert` seam parameter (the
