## The King Slime's machine (S1-D-3g, 2026-11-14)

`AI_015_KingSlime` (`NPC.cs:43121-43414`) is the King Slime's family
machine: the hop cycle, the shrink/grow teleport, the hp-scaled body and
the minion batches. The port ran a simplified arm вЂ” a hop on a timer, a
stand-in teleport next to the player, a fixed body вЂ” and it spawned **a
minion on every landing**, while the C#'s batches come every 5 % of the
hp (1-3 slimes, `Next(1, 4)`).

The arm now carries the C#'s machine:

* **the hop cycle** (`:43285-43326`): the grounded timer runs at 2/tick
  plus the hp-scaled additions (the 0.8/0.6/0.4/0.2/0.1 life bands), the
  hop itself is the -8/-6/-13 jump with the 4/4.5/3.5 push, and the air
  control is the 0.2 push (or the 0.93 damping) toward the facing;
* **the teleport** (`:43177-43211`, `:43219-43284`): the player out of
  sight for 300 ticks shrinks the King Slime (the scale ramp over 60
  ticks), it blinks onto the picked spot and grows back (30 ticks). The
  spot comes from `AI_015_KingSlime_FindTeleportSpot` (`:43087-43119`):
  a solid (or platform) tile with clear air below and a sight line to the
  player, in the 10/7 ring around the player and then the 6/2 one; the
  anti-cheese case (out of sight for 360 ticks or the player 2000 px away)
  lands on the player instead;
* **the hp-scaled body** (`:43340-43356`): `num9 = life / lifeMax * 0.5 +
  0.75` drives both the draw scale and the 98x92 box вЂ” the port's new
  `Npc::size_override` carries the per-NPC box (the C#'s `base.width`/
  `base.height`);
* **the minion batches** (`:43357-43395`): every 5 % of the hp the King
  Slime spawns 1-3 slimes (the `ai[3]` hp latch).

Deviations:

* **The dust and the gore are SKIPPED** (`:43249-43254`, `:43276-43281`,
  `:43365-43367`, the death gore `:43233`/`:85684`) — no dust/gore layer.
* **The MP-only branches use the single-player values.**
* **The getGood world's rows** (the shrinking scale factor `num2`, the 6-px
  air control) are the classic values — the port carries no world-seed flag.
* **The expert minion kind roll** (`Next(4) == 0` → SpikedSlime 535,
  `:43399-43401`) is constants-off: the port runs the classic solo env
  (`Main.expertMode` has no runtime flag, the `spawn_loot` `is_expert: false`
  precedent), so every minion is the Blue Slime (1) and the per-minion census
  is 5 draws (no expert `Next(4)`).
* **The minions' `ai[0] = -1000 * Next(3)` / `ai[1] = -1`** (`:43407-43408`)
  are SEEDED by the drain but the port's stand-in slime machine
  (`update_slime`) reads `hop_timer`, not `ai[0]` — the jump-delay seed is
  carried as data until the A1-4 whole-arm `AI_001_Slimes` port consumes it.
* **`NPC.hide`** (the teleport-tick draw-skip, `:43283`) has no port field —
  the invulnerability half rides `dont_take_damage`; the King still draws on
  the blink tick.
* **The despawn-refresh is not ported**: the C#'s `CheckActive` resets
  `timeLeft = activeTime` while a player is near (`NPC.cs:77930-77938`), so a
  fleeing-then-returning player keeps the boss alive. The port's
  `despawn_timer` is terminal across ALL bosses (no near-player refresh), so
  an `EncourageDespawn(10)` runs to zero even if the player returns within the
  window. Port-wide deviation, not King-Slime-specific.
* **The King Slime sprite does not scale with `n.scale`** in the draw
  (`render/entities.rs`'s King Slime arm uses a fixed 174x120 frame) — the
  hitbox shrinks with hp but the sprite does not. Pre-existing DISPLAY
  deviation (the M4-NPC-3q display task), out of the AI audit's scope.

### A-1 audit fixes (fix/kingslime-audit-defects, 2026-11-19, code-only)

The 54-audit (`docs/research/54-audit-slime-eye.md`, KingSlime §4) flagged
three WRONG defects (K-1..K-3) plus the K-4 minor folds. All are fixed in
place; the rest of the arm was re-verified against `AI_015_KingSlime`
(`NPC.cs:43121-43414`) line-by-line and confirmed faithful (the teleport
cadence 300/360, the shrink 60 / grow 30 ramps, the hop ladder's five hp
tiers, the air steer 3/0.2/0.93, the `num9` scale + bottom-anchor recentre,
the 5 % batch gate).

* **K-1 — the boss-escape exploit (WRONG → fixed).** The far-player state
  write was UNCONDITIONAL every tick; the C# gates it `Main.netMode != 1 &&
  this.ai[1] != 5f` (`:43164`). Without the guard the shrink timer `ai[0]`
  was re-zeroed each tick, so `ai[0] >= 60` never fired and the corner
  teleport never happened — the King Slime never despawned when the player
  fled. Fix: the `ai[1] != 5.0` guard at the C# position, plus
  `EncourageDespawn(10)` (`:43155`), the away-facing write (`:43156-43163`)
  and the re-aim (`:43152`). The `timeLeft > 10` teleport gate (`:43175`) and
  the `timeLeft < 10` state-clear (`:43214-43220`) now ride `despawn_timer`
  (the -1 sentinel reads as the idle 750 window).
* **K-2 — the minion drain (WRONG → fixed).** The old drain dropped all 5
  per-minion RNG draws, invented an 8-minion cap (the C# has NONE —
  `NewNPC` takes any free slot, `:43394-43413`), and placed the minions in a
  row OUTSIDE the body. Fix: `king_slime_minion_batch`
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) ports the spawn loop — position `Next(width-32)` /
  `Next(height-32)` inside the body (bottom-anchored per `NewNPC` `:80770`),
  velocity `Next(-15,16)*0.1` / `Next(-30,1)*0.1`, `ai[0] = -1000*Next(3)`,
  `ai[1] = -1`. The cap is removed. **RNG census (S1-A-10):** the AI tick
  draws the ONE batch count `Next(1,4)` (`:43393`); the drain draws 5 per
  minion in the C# order (x, y, vx, vy, ai[0]) on the same `UpdateNPCs`
  stream — `1 + 5*count` draws per burst. The expert `Next(4)` is
  constants-off (above). Stream-parity witnesses written (not run):
  `king_slime_audit_tests::k2_*` (`world_sim/npcs.rs`).
* **K-3 — the teleport finder (WRONG → fixed).** Three gates were missing /
  invented: (a) the LAVA gate `!tile.lava()` (`:43066`) — the port let the
  King teleport onto lava-covered platforms; (b) the 50-entry cache cap
  `kingSlimePointCacheSizeMax = 50` (`:95273`, checked `:43063`) — the port's
  unbounded Vec changed the `Next(0, size)` draw range past 50 candidates
  (strict-bounds class); (c) the sight-line origin hardcoded `-46` where the
  C# uses `j*16 - base.height/2` (`:43065`) — height is `92*scale` and shrinks
  with hp, so 46 was only correct at full scale. Fix: the lava gate, the
  50-cap (short-circuiting the gate chain like the C# `&&`), the height
  parameter, and the `below_solid` probe now matches `WorldGen.SolidTile`
  (`WorldGen.cs:69957-69974`: active, solid, not solid-top, not half-brick,
  no slope). The pick uses `Next(0, size)` (`:43099`/`:43108`). Witness:
  `k3_the_finder_rejects_lava_covered_candidates`.
* **K-4 — the minor folds (fixed).** The three `TargetClosest` sites (init
  `:43145`, hop-launch `:43317`, grow-end `:43268`, plus the despawn re-aim
  `:43152` and the teleport `faceTarget:false` `:43182`) now route through
  `npc_target::target_closest` (the zombie precedent) — the King re-aims
  every hop instead of keeping its spawn facing. `dontTakeDamage = flag3`
  (`:43283`), the `life <= 0` early return before the scale write
  (`:43368-43371`), the `(int)(98*scale)`/`(int)(92*scale)` truncation
  (`:43378-43379`), the one-shot `flag` (vs the sticky `localAI[3]`), the
  `aiAction` writes (`:43133`/`:43224`/`:43260`/`:43342`) and the raw-hp
  life-band comparisons (`:43294-43313`) are all ported. `boss = true` on
  spawn (`SetDefaults` case 50 `:9389`).

**Verification: code-only mode — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/dotnet/graphify
invoked.** Evidence = file reads + git. The stream-parity witnesses are
WRITTEN, NOT RUN (the S1-A-10 contract for a code-only wave).

## The wiring-tools census and fixes (S1-P-i34, 2026-11-20)

A code-only census of `Player.ItemCheck_UseWiringTools` (`Player.cs:46749-46944`)
and the `WorldGen` place/kill helpers against the port found three WRONGs and
three MISSING behaviours; all six are fixed, ported verbatim with cites. The
wire signal machinery itself (S1-L-6b2/b3) is untouched — this wave is the
TOOLS use only.

**WRONG 1 — the cutter skipped its first arm.** The C#'s cutter runs
`KillActuator` FIRST (`Player.cs:46857`), then yellow → green → blue → red
(`:46862-46880`). The v1 port started at the yellow wire, so a tile carrying
both an actuator and a wire lost the wire and kept the actuator. The new arm
calls `edit::kill_actuator` and drops **item 849** (`Item.NewItem(..., 849)`,
`WorldGen.KillActuator`, `WorldGen.cs:58030`) — the drop rides the
`UpdatePlayers` stream like the wire drops (the cutter runs in
`Player.ItemCheck`).

**WRONG 2 — the Actuator (849) DOES consume one.** The placement branch
(`Player.cs:46883-46886`) decrements nothing itself, which is where the v1
"consumes no stack" claim came from — but the Actuator is `consumable`
(`Item.cs:11331`), `ApplyItemTime` (`:46885`) sets `itemTime == itemTimeMax`,
`CanConsumeConsumableItem` is true (`Player.cs:5496`), there is no
`ForceConsumption` override (`ID/ItemID.cs:413`), and the item is neither
ranged nor coin — so the generic consumable block (`Player.cs:43280-43325`,
same tick, after `ItemCheck_OwnerOnlyCode`) burns one and empties the slot to
air at zero (`:43321-43324`). The port now decrements the held stack and
empties the slot, matching the block.

**WRONG 3 — the rod lock is per HOLD, not per tick.** `ResetEffects` clears
`ActuationRodLock` only while `releaseUseItem` rides
(`Player.cs:18802-18804`); the v1 port cleared it unconditionally every tick,
letting a held rod re-flip each tick. The clear now runs at the
`update_player` seam gated on `app.mine_released` (the port's release latch),
so a held button keeps the lock and a fresh press re-arms it. Frame order
verified: `update_player` → `update_wiring` → `update_editing`
(`app/frame/world.rs:107/371/496`).

**MISSING 1 — wire visibility.** `WiresUI.Settings.DrawWires`
(`WiresUI.cs:27-45`) gates the whole overlay: a held mech tool draws it;
otherwise the Mechanical Lens (3619) / Wire Kite (3611)
(`InfoAccMechShowWires`, `Player.cs:12801-12804`) draw it while
`builderAccStatus[8] == 0`; the no-traps seed hides it until Skeletron falls
(`:31-34`). `HideWires` (`:47-57`, the Actuation Rod 3620 in hand) suppresses
the wire colours and halves the actuator plate (`Main.cs:58224-58229`). The
`builderAccStatus` channels (`Main.cs:58235-58243`) pick each colour's tint:
0 = White, 1 = light colour, 2 = ×0.5, 3 = Transparent. Ported as

## The wire DRAW overlay census and fixes (S1-W4-g81, 2026-11-21)

A verbatim re-read of `Main.DrawWires` (`Main.cs:58218-58675`) against
`render/wires.rs` (the M7-WIRE-3 draw + the S1-P-i34 visibility gate). The
visibility half (i34) verified FAITHFUL — `wire_view` keeps the held-mech /
lens-toggle / no-traps gates and the `builderAccStatus` channel picks
(`:58224-58243`). The DRAW half carried four WRONGs and one MISSING; all
fixed in the same file, byte-maths first. Scope: the overlay DRAW only —
the wiring arms (tool use, `HitWireSingle`, `Wiring`'s trip scan) belong to
the sibling lanes (c42/e20/e21/f11) and are untouched.

**WRONG 1 — float tints instead of XNA bytes.** The C# tint chain is
`Lighting.GetColor(j, i)` (`Lighting.cs:216-242`: `(int)(light *
GlobalBrightness * 255)` per channel, clamp 255, alpha 255) → the channel
switch (`Main.cs:58318-58329`: White / `color *= 0.5f` / Transparent) →
`color * (1f / num7)` (`:58405`). XNA's `Color * float` is
`(int)(byte * scale)` on EVERY channel INCLUDING alpha — the faded channel
draws at alpha 127 and the overlap dim at `255/num7` truncated (127, not
127.5). The v1 port ran `style.shade` floats and divided by `num7` in
float space, losing every truncation and the alpha entirely. Now
`light_color_bytes`/`channel_tint`/`scale_color` carry the byte chain; the
per-mode `LightStyle::shade` transforms (White/Retro/Trippy) do NOT apply —
the C# draws the raw `GetColor` bytes in every light mode (the legacy
engine's own colour already rides the light map). `GlobalBrightness` rides
`style.brightness` (the blind drop 1.2 → 1.0 is applied at the frame seam).

**WRONG 2 — the overlap strips rode the dim.** `:58405` draws the main
quad at `color2 * (1f / num7)` but `:58410` draws the 6 px strip at plain
`color2` — the channel-tinted colour BEFORE the dim. The v1 port passed
the already-dimmed colour to both. `wire_tint` now returns the pair.

**WRONG 3 — the strip table indexed the wrong sides.** The v1 strip array
was ordered up/down/right/left but indexed `sides[k]`/`claimed[k]`
directly on `[up, right, down, left]` — the down strip checked the RIGHT
claim and vice versa. The `STRIPS` table now carries the side index
explicitly, in the C#'s draw order (`flag8` up, `flag9` down, `flag7`
right, `flag6` left — `:58406-58437`), with the source rects
`(18, Y, 16, 6)` / `(72, Y+10, 16, 6)` at +10y / `(46, Y, 6, 16)` at +10x /
`(144, Y, 6, 16)`.

**WRONG 4 — the actuator gate + the guard scope.** The plate's draw gate
is `Lighting.Brightness(j, i) > 0f` (`:58643`) — the RAW light mean ×
GlobalBrightness (`Lighting.cs:118-122`), not the v1's per-channel any-positive
on the shaded colour. And the C#'s `flag && CanShowWireStuffHere` guard
(`:58266`) wraps ONLY the four wire colours: the actuator plate (`:58643`)
and the 423 collection (`:58660`) sit outside it and draw inside the
pre-Golem temple and under `HideWires`. The v1 `continue`d the whole tile.
The plate's `color5 * num` (`:58658`) is a byte scale too (the rod's ×0.5
halves the alpha). A Transparent actuator channel draws an alpha-0 quad in
the C# (premultiplied blend: no-op); the port skips it — pixel-identical.

**MISSING — the tile-423 range rectangle.** `DrawWiresSpecialTiles`
(`:58223`/`:58660-58672`): every active 423 with `frameY == 36` collects
during the walk; after the loop each draws `Utils.DrawRectangle` from
`(j*16-33, i*16-161)` to `(j*16+49, i*16+1)` in `Color.LightSeaGreen`
(32, 178, 170, 255), width 2. `Utils.DrawRectangle` (`Utils.cs:2619-2625`)
is four `DrawLine` calls (left, top, bottom, right); `DrawLine`
(`:2689-2702`) draws `min(5, (int)distance)` segments — collapsed to ONE
when `colorStart == colorEnd` (the 423 case) — each a `BlackTile` quad
scaled `(num/num2/16, width/16)`, rotated `(end-start).ToRotation()` about
the origin `(0, 8)` (source px — the destination anchor is `(0, width/2)`,
the left-middle). Ported as `special_tile_rect`/`line_segments`/
`draw_line`/`draw_rectangle` through the solid-white pixel block (no
`BlackTile` sheet — the `ui/crafting.rs` precedent). The port has no
placeable 423 yet, but `.wld` worlds carry the sensor (`tile_entities.rs`).

**Kept deviations (documented, unchanged):** the unified `claimed` walk
(the C# red claims its sides unconditionally, the later colours only on
draw — unreachable in practice: the UI cycle wraps at 3 so Transparent is
never selected, `Main.cs:47551-47555`); the `dualDungeonsSeed` temple-wall
style check in `CanShowWireStuffHere` (`Player.cs:46955`) has no ported
seed; the screen-range walk keeps the port's ±1-tile margin form.

**RNG:** the draw pass draws no random numbers — no stream touched.

**Verification: code-only mode — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/graphify
invoked.** 13 witnesses in `render/wires.rs::tests` WRITTEN, NOT RUN: the
four i34 visibility tests kept, plus the GetColor byte truncation/clamp,
the channel switch's alpha truncation (255 → 127, 101 → 50), the overlap
dim's byte truncation (255/2 = 127, 255/3 = 85), the strip-colour escape
from the dim (main 76 vs strip 153 at ×0.5 on 0.5 light), the raw
brightness mean, the 424/445 junction offsets, the temple guard's scope
(the 423 collects behind wall 87), the strip side mapping, the 82×162 rect
corners, and the DrawLine single-segment collapse + gradient plan.


## The Deerclops' ice-spike rows (S1-D-4b-5b, 2026-11-14)

`AI_123_Deerclops_MakeSpikesForward`/`MakeSpikesBothSides` +
`TryMakingSpike` + `TryMakingSpike_FindBestY` (`NPC.cs:44466-44534`,
`:44575-44640`) are the Deerclops' signature attack: the spikes rain down
on the ground near the player, in volleys.

The port fired a stand-in вЂ” all twenty spikes at once, from the Deerclops'
feet, straight up. The arm now carries the C#'s shape:

* **the forward row** (state 1, `:44466-44500`): from the 36th tick, every
  fourth tick makes four spikes (the row's spread is 20 tiles);
* **the both-sides row** (state 4, `:44502-44532`): from the 56th tick,
  every second tick makes the row's spikes on both sides (the spread is 15
  tiles);
* **the spike's landing row** (`:44586-44640`): `FindBestY` walks the
  column toward the player's feet and keeps the walkable row closest to
  them, then walks up through the solid tiles and down to the first
  walkable one;
* **the spike's flight** (`:44582`): the `(0, -1)` vector rotated by
  `whichOne * dir * 0.7 * (PI / 4 / howMany)` and the `ai1` scale factor
  (`0.1 + rand * 0.1 + xOffset * 1.1 / howMany`).

The two tile probes the C#'s helper uses ride with it:
`WorldGen.ActiveAndWalkableTile` (`WorldGen.cs:70300-70318` вЂ” the tile is
active, solid and not framed off) and `WorldGen.SolidTile`
(`:70111-70132` вЂ” the full solid block, no slope and no top-only tile).

The rubble's own tile scan (`AI_123_Deerclops_ShootRubbleUp`,
`:44448-44465`) is still the port's stand-in вЂ” the follow-up row.

## The debug god mode (S1-E-34, 2026-11-16)

No new damage-path code. `Player.creative_god_mode` вЂ” the journey Godmode power вЂ”
already gates every way a player can take damage: `Hurt` returns before the
iframes, the defense reduction and the knockback
(`Player.cs:38203-38206`), `KillMe` refuses the death (`:38809-38812`),
`Update_NPCCollision` returns before the whole contact pass (`:31321-31324`) and
`Main.UpdateWorld_Players` refills life/mana/breath (`Main.cs:17869-17873`).

What the task actually adds is the **debug surface**: a twelfth row on the F3
panel's World tab (`God Mode: ON/OFF`) that flips a new
`Player::debug_god_mode`.

Deliberate deviation (one-line-cited at the site): the tick ORs
`debug_god_mode` into `creative_god_mode` instead of writing it directly,
because `Player.ResetEffects` re-derives `creative_god_mode` from the journey
power **every tick** (`:18789` clears it, `:25493-25497` re-reads it), so a
direct toggle would last exactly one tick. Keeping a separate field also keeps
the two independent: the journey power's own toggle is untouched, and the debug
flag cannot silently turn the power on. CheatSheet's `GodMode.cs:56-67` and
HEROsMod's `GeneralMessages.cs:182-190` are mod sources that are not part of
`decompiled/`, so this row implements the *behaviour* the ROADMAP row describes
("damage is swallowed while on") on top of the existing vanilla gate rather
than porting either mod.

## The Eye Fire / Flames Trap and the Baby Bird (S1-D-4b-5c, 2026-11-16)

Two leftover styles ride the Eye and Moon Lord chains: **23** and **158**.

* **Style 23 is two types.** `aiStyle = 23` covers the Eye Fire (**101**,
  `ProjectileID.EyeFire`) and the Flames Trap (**188**,
  `ProjectileID.FlameTrap`). They share the whole arm; only the trap arms the
  launch-counter floor (`if (ai[0] < 8) ai[0] = 8;`, `Projectile.cs:25863-25868`)
  and the 60-tick life cap (`:25871-25874`). Both count launches in
  `localAI[0]` (`:25869`, `:25892`), which `Damage_CanDealDamage` (`:12448`)
  reads to refuse the shot while the counter is still below 7 вЂ” so the counter
  is load-bearing state, not decoration.
* **Style 158 is one type**, the Baby Bird pet (**759**): `projFrames[759] = 5`
  (`Main.cs:8506`). The arm keeps the pet alive while the `babyBird` buff flag
  is set (`timeLeft = 2`, `:48760-48769`), walks its five frames at six ticks
  per frame wrapping at `projFrames - 1` (`:48770-48777`), and snaps onto the
  owner's home spot on the **last** frame when inside the
  `8 + |player.velocity|` band (`:48919-48927`) вЂ” the walk never reaches the
  last frame itself, which is why the perch frame is only visible while
  sitting. The target scan is `Minion_FindTargetInRange` (`:48990-49027`) with
  the four reach helpers `CanHitWithOwnBody` / `CanHitWithOwnMeleeWeapon`
  (`:12400-12444`).

Deliberate deviations and skips (all one-line-cited in the code):

* **Dust, gore and sound are skipped** in both arms вЂ” the pool has no
  `Main.dust` layer and no sound sink, matching the `ai_volcano` /
  `ai_sharp_tears` precedent above. The `Dust.NewDust` calls in the C# blocks
  are recorded at the site, not ported.
* **The two separation loops and the group index are computed pool-side.**
  `AI_158` walks `Main.projectile` twice to find its sibling birds and its own
  index among them (`:51895-51911`); a slot arm cannot see its siblings, so
  `ProjectilePool::baby_bird_group` pre-computes the group index and both
  separation vectors and hands them to `ai_baby_bird`. The arithmetic is the
  C#'s verbatim; only the *where* moved.
* **`gravDir = 1` and `mounted_center == center` are folded.** The port has no
  gravity flip and no mount pivot offset, so `AI_158`'s
  `RotatedRelativePoint(MountedCenter)` chain reduces to
  `Center + gfxOffY - (0, 21) + (0, headgear - 2)`. `Player::`
  `apply_head_offset_from_mount` and `rotated_relative_point` are ported
  faithfully anyway (the mount ids that do move the head are live), so the fold
  is one call site, not a missing function.
* **`correctSlopeCollision` is `projPet`, so `pet_movement` skips the slope
  pass.** `Projectile.cs:707` sets `correctSlopeCollision = projPet`;
  `AI_158`'s pet movement therefore runs `Collision.TileCollision` with
  `fallThrough = fall2 = true` and no `correctSlopeCollision` pass. The port
  calls `collision::tile_collision(..., fall_through = true, fall2 = true)` and
  omits the slope correction вЂ” faithful to the C# for this flag combination.
* **`NPC.boss` has no port field.** The arm's boss bypass
  (`if (npc.boss) ...`) reads `crate::revenge::BOSS_KINDS` instead; the set is
  derived from the C# `npc.boss` assignments, so the predicate is the same.

## The Eye of Cthulhu's machine (S1-D-3k, 2026-11-14)

`AI_004` (`NPC.cs:19960-20801`) is the Eye's whole family machine вЂ” the
hover phase (0), the two spin phases (1, 2) and the final dash phase (3) вЂ”
plus the servant bursts. The port's `update_eye_of_cthulhu` already carried
the phase-1 hover, the dash chain and the final phase's shape; three deltas
remained, and the servant (the Eye's minion, type 5) ran on the *shared*
hover archetype instead of the C#'s own `AI_005` branch.

**The spin hand-off (the inverted reset).** The C#'s spin block
(`:20287-20301`) ramps `ai[2]` (the spin speed) to 0.5 in phase 1 and decays
it in phase 2; the phase hand-off (`:20356-20361`) resets `ai[2]` **only**
when the phase reaches 3 (`if (this.ai[0] == 3f) this.ai[2] = 0f;`). The
port had the test inverted (`if self.ai[0] != 3.0`), so the phase-1 в†’ 2
hand-off zeroed the spin speed: the Eye's third phase stood still instead
of decaying from 0.5, and the phase-2 в†’ 3 hand-off kept a stale speed. The
fix restores the C#'s hand-off: the phase-2 spin now decays from 0.5 to 0
over its 100 ticks, and the final phase starts with the spin stopped.

**The final phase's damage.** The C#'s final phase writes
`this.damage = GetAttackDamage_LerpBetweenFinalValues(23, 18)`
(`:20392-20408`) вЂ” the classic difficulty remaps onto the first value, so
the contact damage rises from the `SetDefaults` 15 to **23** in the final
phase. The port kept the 15 for the whole fight; the arm now carries the
override (`damage_override = Some(23)`). The defense drop (`this.defense = 0`,
the same block) was already there.

**The servant's spawn point.** `NPC.NewNPC` takes the spawn point as the
NPC's **bottom centre** (`NPC.cs:80770` вЂ” `nPC.Bottom = new Vector2(X, Y)`,
whose setter writes `position = (X - width/2, Y - height)`, `Entity.cs:122-132`)
and the call site truncates it to whole pixels (`NPC.cs:20180`:
`(int)vector2.X, (int)vector2.Y`). The port placed the servant at
`(X - 10, Y - 10)` вЂ” 10 px too low and un-truncated. The spawn helper now
writes the bottom-centre convention and the truncation.

**The servant's own machine.** The Servant of Cthulhu (type 5) runs
`AI_005_EaterOfSouls` вЂ” the C#'s type-5 branch (`:50379-50383`: the speed 5,
the accel 0.03) plus the shared fly core (`:50418-50579`) and the type-5
rotation (`:50652-50655`). The port ran it through the shared hover
archetype, which misses two things the C# does:

* the aim is quantised to the **8-px grid** вЂ” the target's centre and the
  servant's own centre both floor to 8 px (`:50421-50424`) and the aim is
  the difference of the snapped values;
* the approach's **double-add on a sign reversal** is gated by `flag5`
  (`:50447`), which is *true* for type 5.

The servant's own arm (`update_servant_of_cthulhu`) now carries the C#'s
branch: the snapped aim, the 5-speed / 0.03-accel approach with the
double-add, the dead-target flee vector (`num4 = direction * num/2`,
`num5 = -num/2`, `:50480-50484`) and the velocity tilt
(`rotation = atan2(velocity.Y, velocity.X) - 1.57`). Its `noGravity` +
`noTileCollide` (`SetDefaults` case 5) make the step a raw integration вЂ”
no tile collision (the shared archetype bounced the servant off tiles).

The residuals of the S1-D-1 hover section (the 8-px floor and the `flag5`
gate) therefore remain only for the kinds that still ride the archetype вЂ”
the Eater of Souls (6), the Hornet (42) and the Meteor Head (23) вЂ” where
`flag5` is false for the first two: the shared `hover_step` still
over-adds for them. That is the S1-D-3l follow-up.

Deviations:

* **The dust and the gore** (the 1-in-5 dust at `:20062-20067`, the
  spin-phase gore at `:20365-20375`) are skipped вЂ” the port has no dust or
  gore layer.
* **The expert / `getGoodWorld` branches** (the rage sub-states `ai[1] =
  3/4/5`, the expert servant bursts, the phase-3 dash speed bonuses) are
  constants-off: the port has no difficulty flag, so the classic path runs
  verbatim and the skipped arms carry their C# cites.
* **The day-time `EncourageDespawn(10)`** (`:20071-20073`) rides the sim's
  day cull (the Eye rises out of the player's view and is removed).

## The NPC hit and death sounds (S1-E-21a, 2026-11-14)

The first wave of the sound bank (S1-E-21) landed with S1-E-21a: the NPCs
now play their **own** hit and death cues.

`NpcKind::hit_sound` / `NpcKind::death_sound` (`crates/tr-app/src/npc.rs`)
carry the C#'s per-kind table вЂ” `NPC.HitSound` / `NPC.DeathSound`
(`NPC.cs:6475-6477`, the `SetDefaults` assignments). The C#'s `null` guard
(`NPC.cs:8537`) is kept: the kinds with no row in `SetDefaults` (the Brain
Scrambler 381 and the Ray Gunner 382) play nothing. The cue names are the
legacy asset names вЂ” the sound id 3 family is `NPC_Hit_N` and the sound id 4
family is `NPC_Killed_N` (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:646`/`:676`).

The two call sites are the C#'s: the melee strike plays the kind's hit cue
at the NPC's position (`NPC.StrikeNPC`, `:81544-81553`) and the death plays
the kind's death cue at its centre (`NPC.checkDead`, `:91852`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s trackable styles pick a random variation
   (`LegacySoundStyle.Style`, `LegacySoundStyle.cs:33-38`); the port plays
   the first file of the family (the `_0` asset) вЂ” the same asset family, a

2. ~~The legacy per-sound pitch and the per-family instance reuse (the C#'s
   `SoundNpcHit[n]` pool) stay unported~~ вЂ” **closed by wave C below**
   (2026-11-18): the case-3/4 maths, the pitch draws and the slot pools are

3. The C#'s special hit cues for the newest NPCs (the Turkey/Undead/Vampire
   hurts, `NPC.cs:81535-81545`) have no ported kinds.

  draw (`:651-654`), 57 Г—0.6 (`:655-658`), 55/56 Г—0.5 (`:659-662`), one
  `Main.rand.Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` pitch draw (`:670`).
- `sound.rs::npc_killed_case4` ports case 4 (`:673-695`): styles 23..57 Г—0.5
  (`:674-677`), 61/62 Г—0.6 (`:678-685`), the 10 playing guard (`:686-689`),
  one `Next(-10, 11) * 0.01` pitch draw (`:693`).
- `audio.rs::play_npc_hit_sound` / `play_npc_death_sound` run the faГ§ade
  (`SoundEngine.cs:93-99`): the `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat on the audio-only
  `sound_style_random` (variance 0 for every NPC style вЂ” the draw still
  happens), the attenuation gate (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436`) BEFORE any
  gameplay draw, then the case maths. The final
  `Clamp(pitch + pitchOffset, -1, 1)` is `:1410`. The style row comes from
  the generated `soundid.rs` table through `npc_sound_style` (the asset name
  в†’ `NPCHitN`/`NPCDeathN`, the trackable `_0` pins в†’ their style, so the
  Deerclops' hit rides its 0.3 style volume).
- The instance pools: `npc_hit_slots[59]` (`SoundNpcHit` is
  `new Asset<SoundEffect>[59]`, `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:74`) stops + re-creates
  the slot's sink (`:663-667`); `npc_killed_slots` (a map over
  `SoundID.NPCDeathCount = 69`, `SoundID.cs:1383`) overwrites WITHOUT a Stop
  (`:690` вЂ” the old sink detaches and plays out), exactly the two cases'
  different semantics. Headless nothing plays, so the guards never trip вЂ”
  the engine's fresh-instance-table behaviour.

The call sites and their named streams (`Main.SwapRandom`,
`Main.cs:17749-17809`):

| Site | C# | Port | Stream |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Melee strike | `NPC.StrikeNPC` `NPC.cs:81544-81553` via `Player.ItemCheck_MeleeHitNPCs` | `world_sim/editing.rs` (the landed strike) | `UpdatePlayers` (`Main.cs:17754`) |
| Projectile strike | `Projectile.Damage` в†’ `StrikeNPC` (`Projectile.cs:13649`) | `projectile.rs::damage_pve`/`damage_pve_boxed` queue в†’ `world_sim/projectiles.rs` drain | `UpdateProjectiles` (`Main.cs:17775`) |
| Death | `NPC.checkDead` `NPC.cs:78186-78194` (**`base.position`** вЂ” the old port played at the centre citing `:91852`, which is actually the eel-whip DoT's `HitSound` site) | `world_sim/npcs.rs` death retain | `UpdateNPCs` (`Main.cs:17767`) вЂ” see deviation 2 |
| Net client strike | `MessageBuffer.cs:1797` runs the full `StrikeNPC_Inner` on the client | `app/netglue.rs` `S2c::NpcStrike` | the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in (`Main.Update` `Main.cs:16895` в†’ `Netplay.UpdateInMainThread` runs outside every swap) |

The host's own strike path plays nothing: the C#'s `netMode == 2` guard
(`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:386`) вЂ” the port's listener carries `server: true` on
the Host role (S1-E-24).

Deliberate deviations (wave C):

1. **Death-stream placement.** The C# runs `checkDead` inside `StrikeNPC`,
   so the death pitch draw rides the *striking* stage's stream
   (`UpdatePlayers`/`UpdateProjectiles`). The port batches deaths into the
   NPC pass's retain, so the draw rides `UpdateNPCs` instead. One draw per
   death, same window; the stream assignment differs (the port's death
   batching predates this wave вЂ” M4-NPC).
2. **Projectile draw position.** The C# draws the hit pitch mid-damage-walk
   (between the strike and the loot/immunity rolls); the port's pool cannot
   reach the audio, so the strikes queue `(cue, x, y)` intents
   (`drain_npc_hit_sounds`, the `take_cart_sounds` precedent) and the pass
   tail plays them вЂ” the draws land after the walk's other rolls instead of
   interleaved. Same count, same window, same stream; the interleave differs.
3. The trackable `_0` variation pin (deviation 1 of S1-E-21a above) and the
   unported pet-hurt switch arm (`NPC.cs:81490-81549`, the type-1
   `ai[1]` cases вЂ” the port ships no pet kinds) stay.
4. The 229 shimmer-variant death override (`NPC.cs:78187-78190`,
   `NPCDeath6`) has no ported kind вЂ” the invasion Pirate 229 is unported.

Tests: `s1_e_21c_npc_hit_case3_tweaks_the_volume_and_guards_57`,

## The tile-break sound table (S1-E-21c, 2026-11-16)

`WorldGen.KillTile_PlaySounds` (`WorldGen.cs:66427-66575`, called from
`KillTile` `:63558`) is the biggest single missing cue table: ~200 tile types
resolve to one of 13 asset families. It is a pure per-type switch вЂ” no state,
no draw except the 147/224 roll вЂ” so it ports as a table.

`tr-core/src/edit.rs::kill_tile_sound(kind, frame_x, fail)` returns
`KillSounds { primary, extra, shatter }`; the app maps each `(sound id, style)`
through `world_sim/editing.rs::kill_cue` to a pinned asset and the case's
volume scale (`LegacySoundPlayer.PlaySound`, `:360-1100`). `break_tile` plays
the hit cell's cues **once**, before the loot, and the pot events now play
their real `CheckPot` cues (4/6/13 в†’ `NPC_Killed_1`/`Grass`/`Shatter`) rather
than the `Dig_1` stand-in.

Deliberate deviations:

1. **Variation families are pinned** (research D3): `Dig_0..2`, `Tink_0..2`
   and `Item48`/`Item49` are a per-play `Main.rand`/`genRand` pick in the C#;
   the port plays one fixed member (`Dig_1`, `Tink_1`, `Item_48`). Audio-only:
   no state depends on the pick.
2. **The per-play pitch jitter is not applied at the call site**: the
   `LegacySoundPlayer` cases roll `Main.rand.Next(-10,11)*0.01` (and the
   item/dig windows) per play. `sound.rs` already carries the roll machinery
   (`legacy_family_pitch`, S1-E-22) with `Playback.pitch`; the headless
   `Audio::play_at` path plays without a resampler, so the roll is not wired
   here. Recorded as an audio-output gap, not a behaviour one.
3. **The per-family instance pools are not modelled**: the C# stops and
   recreates `SoundInstanceDig[n]`/`SoundTink[n]`/`SoundItem[n]` per play. The
   port's `play_at` opens a fresh `rodio` stream per call; the audible result is
   the same single-shot cue (the tracked-sound layer, S1-E-23, is for the
   looping/ambient families).
4. **The per-drop sound is gone**: the port used to play `Dig_1` once per
   dropped item in `break_tile`. The C# plays the break cue once, at the hit
   cell, from `KillTile_PlaySounds` вЂ” `Item.NewItem` plays nothing. The
   per-drop cue was an invention and is removed.
5. **The failure-tick callers stay unported**: `Player.cs:39880` and
   `Projectile.cs:70219` play the table with `fail: true` while a pickaxe
   chips an unbreakable tile / a drill bit bites. The port has no per-tick chip
   path (it refuses the break outright), so only `fail: false` is wired; the
   table itself carries the `fail` arms (the glass pop and the shatter tail).

## The hover family's residuals (S1-D-3l, 2026-11-14)

`AI_005_EaterOfSouls` (`NPC.cs:50244-50760`) is the shared fly core of the
hover family. The port's `npc_ai::hover_step` had the shape вЂ” the target
vector scaled to the kind's `num`, the `num2` approach, the type-42 scale
factor and its surface-gated damping вЂ” but five things of the source were
missing, and the frame clock ran twice.

**The 8-px aim floor** (`:50421-50424`). The C# floors the target's centre
and the NPC's own centre to the 8-px grid and takes the aim as the
difference of the snapped values:
`num4 = (int)(num4 / 8f) * 8; vector.X = (int)(vector.X / 8f) * 8;`. The
port aimed at the exact centre. The floor is now in `hover_step` (and in
the Servant of Cthulhu's own arm, S1-D-3k).

**The `flag5` gate** (`:50447`). The approach's extra add on a sign
reversal is gated:
`flag5 = type в€‰ {6, 42, 94, 139, 173, 619} в€§ type в€‰ [231, 235]`. The port
applied it to every hover kind, so the Eater of Souls (6) and the Hornet
(42) over-added on every reversal. `HoverParams` now carries `double_add`
and the table sets it per kind.

**The dead-target flee vector** (`:50299`/`:50480-50484`). A dead player
replaces the aim with `num4 = direction * num/2; num5 = -num/2` вЂ” the NPC
flies off along its facing. `HoverTarget` now carries the dead flag.

**The per-kind rotation arms** (`:50580-50655`). The C# ends the core with
one of four shapes, and the port had none of them:

| kind | arm | the port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6/94/173/619 | `rotation = atan2(num5, num4) - 1.57` (the aim tilt) | вЂ” |
| 23 | the sprite-aim arm: the sprite direction follows the aim's x sign, `rotation = atan2(num5, num4)` (+ПЂ to the left) | вЂ” |
| 42/176/205/231-235 | the sprite direction follows the velocity's x sign, `rotation = velocity.X * 0.1` | вЂ” |
| the rest | `rotation = atan2(velocity.Y, velocity.X) - 1.57` | вЂ” |

`HoverParams::rotation` now selects the arm (`HoverRotation`).

**The tile collision** (`:50656-50688`). The C#'s bounce arm covers the
kinds that collide with the tiles: `velocity.X = oldVelocity.X * -num14`
(`num14` = 0.7, 0.4 for the types 6/173) plus the small-velocity clamps
(`|v| < 2` в†’ В±2 on the x, `|v| < 1.5` в†’ В±2 on the y). The port bounced
every hover kind with a flat Г—0.5 вЂ” and it bounced the kinds that
`SetDefaults` gives `noTileCollide` (the Eater of Souls and the Meteor
Head), which in the source fly straight through the tiles. `HoverParams` now
carries `no_tile_collide` and `bounce`.

**The frame clock ran twice.** `update_hover` advanced the frame counter
*and* `find_frame` advanced it again (the C#'s `NPC.FindFrame` is the only
owner), so the hovers' flap advanced at half the stride. The frame handling
now lives in `find_frame` alone вЂ” and the Hornet gets the C#'s four-phase
flap (`:74907-74934`: two ticks a phase over the rows 0/1/2/1) instead of
the port's 8-tick stride over three rows.

Deviations:

* **The tile collision** is the port's rectangle probe
  (`crate::player::collides_rect`) instead of the C#'s tile sweep with
  `oldVelocity`; the bounce's factor and the clamps are the source's.
* **The dust and the wet arms** (`:50695-50730`) are skipped вЂ” the port has
  no dust layer and no wet flag on the hovers.
* **The per-difficulty / secret-seed overrides** (`:50308-50316` the remix
  values for type 6, `:50345-50348` type 231's 3/0.017) are constants-off.
* **The `facing` write** at the end of the step is the port's convention
  (the C#'s `base.direction` is not written by `AI_005`); the render uses
  `spriteDirection`, which the rotation arms now own.
## The player voice cues (S1-E-21b, 2026-11-14)

The second wave of the sound bank: the player's own hurt and death cues.

`Player.Hurt`'s tail plays the hurt cue (`Player.cs:38525` в†’
`PlayHurtSound`, `:38569-38712`) and `Player.KillMe` plays the death cue
(`:38868` в†’ `PlayDeathSound`, `:38715-38744`). The port queues the cue on
the Player (the `take_hurt_sound`/`take_death_sound` handoff вЂ” the Player
has no audio device) and the fixed step drains it.

Two behaviour changes ride the wave:

1. The hurt sound now rides the **damage path** instead of the frame's
   hp-drop heuristic (`app/frame.rs`'s `last_hp` compare) вЂ” the C#'s
   `PlayHurtSound` is called from `Hurt`, so the damage-over-time ticks
   (the poison, the burning) no longer play a hurt sound.
2. The death sound is new: the legacy "Player Killed" id 5
   (`Player.cs:38737`, the default arm of `PlayDeathSound`).

Deliberate deviations:

1. The C#'s voice system (`Player.voiceOverride`/`voiceVariant`/`Male`,
   `Player.cs:1346`/`38581-38710`) is not ported вЂ” the default voice
   variant 1 (`Player.cs:56045`, the legacy "Player Hit" id 1) stands in.
2. The C#'s hurt cue picks a random variation (`Main.rand.Next(3)`,
   `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:505`); the port plays "Player_Hit_0".
3. The C#'s death cue switches to the remastered hurt cues in the Don't
   Starve and 10th-anniversary worlds (`Player.cs:38737-38740`); the port
   plays the legacy cue everywhere.
4. The C#'s local-player hurt sound plays non-positionally
   (`Player.cs:38572`); the port's drain plays it without a position вњ“.

## The explicit carrier links (S1-D-6b, 2026-11-14)

The C#'s boss-part links are index links into `Main.npc` вЂ” `NPC.ai[3]`
points at the carrier (`NPC.cs:6161`), `AI_077`'s `localAI[0..2]` point at
the Moon Lord's three parts (`NPC.cs:41229-41232`), and `AI_082`'s leech
blob holds its head's index + 1 (`NPC.cs:36630-36640`). The port's
`App::npcs` compacts every frame (the death retain), so a Vec index does
not survive the frame; the port used to re-derive the links by KIND search
every tick ("the first alive Moon Lord core").

**The stable identity.** `Npc.uid` (`NPC.whoAmI`, `NPC.cs:6145`) is the
port's stand-in: the sim hands every NPC its id once (`App::next_npc_uid`)
and never reuses it. The links now ride the ids:

* the Moon Lord's hands and head carry the core's id in `carrier_uid` (the
  C#'s `ai[3]`) and the core keeps the parts' ids in `moon_parts` (the
  C#'s `localAI[0..2]`) вЂ” set at the spawn, exactly like the vanilla;
* the leech blob's anchor is the head's id;
* the core's part check (`NPC.cs:41250-41269`) resolves the ids each tick
  (`moon_parts_lost`), because the core's own AI has no NPC list.

A part whose carrier died falls with it (`Main.npc[ai[3]]` inactive), and a
second Moon Lord never steals the first one's parts вЂ” with the kind search
it did.

**Per-carrier resolution (re-verified 2026-11-18).** Each carrier family now
has its own resolution test: `the_moon_lord_parts_keep_their_own_core` (the
hands/head в†” core, `NPC.cs:41229-41232`/`:41579-41583`),
`the_leech_blob_keeps_its_own_head` (the clot в†” head, `AI_082`'s anchor
`NPC.cs:36630-36640` вЂ” two families on the field, the clot mirrors ITS
head's centre and falls with it while the other head lives) and
`the_true_eye_keeps_its_own_core` (the True Eye в†” core, `AI_081`'s anchor
`NPC.cs:42466-42470`, the link handed out by `MoonLord_SpawnTrueEyeOfCthulhu`
`:41154` вЂ” the eye survives the OTHER core's death and falls with its own).

**Deliberate deviation вЂ” the unlinked-part fallback.** The C# resolves
`Main.npc[(int)ai[3]]` unconditionally: a part whose `ai[3]` was never set
points at slot 0 and dies when slot 0 is inactive or the wrong type
(`NPC.cs:41579-41583`). The port's pre-pass instead falls back to a KIND
search for the first alive core/head of the family when `carrier_uid == 0`
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s carrier pre-pass) вЂ” a part spawned outside the Moon
Lord's spawn arm (the debug spawn, a save load) still finds its family.
Once the link is handed out it is explicit and never re-searched, so the
two-family isolation above holds. The True Eye's spawn site
(`MoonLord_SpawnTrueEyeOfCthulhu`, `NPC.cs:41134-41155` вЂ” the head-loop
phase maths over `CountNPCS(400)`) is not ported; the eyes reach the field
through the debug/net spawns and the pre-pass resolves their links the same
way.

**The Old One's Army's wave-7 anchor.** `DD2Event`'s tier-3 budget reads
the Betsy's own life (`NPC.FindFirstNPC(551)`, `DD2Event.cs:1487-1494`):
`currentKillCount = 100 - life/lifeMax*100` and the budget is 100; with no
Betsy on the field the C#'s `-1` arm takes the budget of 1. The port had
the anchor stubbed (`betsy_hp_ratio` was a hard 0.0, so the wave always
showed 100). The app now resolves the Betsy (`dd2_betsy_hp_ratio`) and the
tier's table reads it.

**The tiered wave budget.** `CheckProgress` (`DD2Event.cs:367-392`) takes
the budget and the kill worth from the ongoing difficulty
(`GetInvasionStatus` в†’ `Difficulty_N_GetRequiredWaveKills`,
`GetMonsterPointsWorth` at `:546-554`), and the wave's roster from the
same tier (`GetEnemiesForWave`). The port's kill report used the tier-1
table for every tier; it now picks the tier's roster, budget and worth.
The per-monster exceptions inside the C#'s worth rows (the Dark Mage /
Ogre / Wither Beast zero-point kills at the wave cap, `DD2Event.cs:1106`/
`:1199`/`:1509`) are still the port's flat per-tier worth вЂ” a follow-up.

**Still open (S1-D-6c).** The Moon Lord core's vulnerable phase: the C#'s
`flag2` check (`NPC.cs:41270-41285`) hands the core its vulnerable state
(`ai[0] = 1`, `dontTakeDamage = false`) once all three parts are in their
death state. The port's core stays in its `ai[0] == 0` phase with
`dont_take_damage = true`, so the melee cannot touch it and only the
projectile path (which lacks the C#'s `dontTakeDamage` gate,
`Projectile.cs:12662-12666`) can land a hit. Both halves belong together:
the gate alone would make the Moon Lord unkillable.

## The Moon Lord core's phases (S1-D-6c, 2026-11-14)

`AI_077_MoonLordCore` (`NPC.cs:41157-41575`) runs the core through four
phases, and the port's state machine had lost two of them:

| phase | the C# | the port (before) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| init | `localAI[3] == 0` в†’ 1, `ai[0] = -1` (`:41163-41168`) | `ai[0] == 0` в†’ -1, **every tick** |
| spawn-in | `ai[0] == -1`, 60 ticks, then the hands + the head (`:41193-41235`) | the same, but the phase re-armed |
| waiting | `ai[0] == 0`: the hover + the part bookkeeping (`:41236-41291`) | unreachable вЂ” the init re-armed the phase |
| vulnerable | `ai[0] == 1`: the hover, `dontTakeDamage = false` (`:41294-41310`) | unreachable |
| death | `ai[0] == 2` (`:41307-41445`) | the same |

**The init latch.** The C#'s latch is `localAI[3]` (0 в†’ 1) вЂ” a one-shot.
The port tested `ai[0] == 0` instead, so every return to the zero state
re-armed the spawn phase: the core asked for its parts again every 60
ticks and a second pair of hands + a second head rode out behind the
first. `moon_spawn_latch` is the port's `localAI[3]`.

**The vulnerable phase.** The C#'s `flag2` check (`:41270-41285`) hands
the core `ai[0] = 1` and `dontTakeDamage = false` once all three parts
are in their death state. The port had no such transition: the core stayed
shielded and only the projectile path (which lacked the C#'s
`dontTakeDamage` gate) could land a hit. `moon_parts_dead` is the sim's
resolution of the C#'s check (the core's own AI has no NPC list вЂ” the
same shape as the carrier mirrors).

**The projectile's shield gate.** `Damage_PVE`'s outer walk skips the
shielded NPC (`Projectile.cs:12583`: `!nPC.dontTakeDamage`). The port's
`damage_pve` had no such gate, so the shots went through the Moon Lord's
shield and the Brain's Creeper shield. The box walk (`Damage()`,
`:14087-14119`) has no gate in the C# вЂ” the port keeps it that way.

**The C#'s `flag` arm.** `NPC.cs:41251-41269` takes the core down when a
slot points at no living part. In the C# a dead part stays `active`
through its death animation, so the arm only fires for a part that
vanished; the port removes the dead parts at once, so "the part is gone"
is the normal death and the arm would kill the core on the first part's
fall. The port implements the `flag2` arm only вЂ” the `flag` arm's
counterpart does not exist in the port's immediate-death model.

## The town-NPC melee swing (S1-D-3n, 2026-11-15)

`NPC.AI_007_TownEntities` carries the town-NPC family (the `aiStyle 7` arm,
`NPC.cs:52965-55561`). Its melee state (`ai[0] == 15`, `NPC.cs:54995-55114`)
reads four per-type numbers: `num78` (the swing damage, scaled by
`NPC.GetAttackDamage_ForTownNPC`), `num79` (the swing knockback) and
`num80`/`num81` (the swing item width and height, taken by
`NPC.GetSwingStats`). The C# rows live at `NPC.cs:55018-55054`:

| NPC | type | damage | knockback | item |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dye Trader | 207 | 11 | 4.25 | 32x32 |
| Tax Collector | 441 | 9 | 3.5 | 28x28 |
| Stylist | 353 | 10 | 5 | 32x32 |
| town pets | - | 10 | 3 | 32x32 |

**The port.** `crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai.rs::TownWeaponParams` carries those
four numbers as the `DYE_TRADER`, `TAX_COLLECTOR`, `STYLIST` and `TOWN_PET`
rows, with the C# line cites; the table test
`s1_d_3n_tests::the_town_weapon_presets_match_the_csharp_table` pins them.

**The deliberate gap.** The swing machine itself is not ported: it needs
`NPC.GetSwingStats` (`NPC.cs:66485`), `NPC.StrikeNPCNoInteraction` and
`GameDifficultyData.TownNPCDamageMultiplier` (`NPC.cs:7062-7065`), and the
port has no swing-stats helper, no NPC-to-NPC strike path and no difficulty
multiplier for the town-NPC damage. Porting the machine is a follow-up under
S1-D-3; the preset table lands first so the numbers have one home. `num77`
and `maxValue4` are not read by the swing code and stay unported.

## The moon-event wave machinery + the roster ladders (S1-F-13, 2026-11-15)

The a-slice landed on `S1-F-13-moon-wave-machinery` (phases: the machinery
`882bf20e`, the ladders `9455e325`). The rate/pacing half was already on
`SpawnContext`'s `moon_event` flag (`get_spawn_rate`'s `:396` arm вЂ” the C#
`:771-774` moon override, folded next to the invaders override); the wave
machinery and the two roster ladders are new:

- **State** (`World`): `wave_number` (i32, starts 1), `wave_kills`,
  `total_invasion_points` вЂ” runtime-only (the C#'s moon-event state rides
  `Main` statics and is saved only inside the invasion-progress's own save
  section the port's format does not mirror вЂ” the persistence deviation).
- **Walk**: `CheckProgressFrostMoon`/`CheckProgressPumpkinMoon`
  (`NPC.cs:78445-78600`/`:78588-78719`) as `World` methods, called on the
  death site beside `report_invasion_kill` (`world_sim/npcs.rs`) вЂ” the
  per-kind points tables (snow `:78518-78549`; pumpkin `:78658+`), the 1Г—
  scalar (single-mode: the C#'s master 2.5 / expert 2 arms collapse),
  `wave_kills >= requirement(&& != 0)` в†’ `wave_kills = 0`, `wave_number++`.
  The waves key on the vanilla `NPC.type` u16 (all 30 wave kinds are
  unported until S1-F-13b/c, so the tests drive them directly);
  `MOON_WAVE_REQUIREMENTS.get()` saturates out-of-range waves to the
  terminal 0 (the C# array would throw; waves only reach 0..=20).
- **Start/stop**: `start_pumpkin_moon`/`start_snow_moon`
  (`Main.cs:10979-11017` вЂ” the flags, the mutual clear, the resets,

## The Dark Mage's machine (S1-D-3o, 2026-11-16)

`AI_109_DarkMage` (`NPC.cs:65791-66186`) carries the Old One's Army's
casters (types 564/565). The whole arm is ported in
`crates/tr-app/src/npc.rs::update_dark_mage`, in the C# statement order:

- the per-kind block (`:65813-65829`: the rotation = `vx * 0.04`,
  `spriteDirection`, the tunables вЂ” `num3` 2, `num4` 0.05, `num5` 0.2,
  `num6` -0.05, `num7` -0.4, `num8` 0.5, `num9` 0.1, `num10` 0.5,
  `num11` 0.02; note `flag5 = false`, so the upward probe at
  `:66058-66078` never runs);
- the materialize (`:65928-65962`): `localAI[3]` (the port's
  `caster_counter`) ramps 0 в†’ 60, `alpha = 255` on the first tick, then
  `alpha -= 5` clamped at 0;
- the cast cycle (`:65834-65881`) behind `flag6`/`num12 = 0.9`, whose
  tail (`:66024-66028`) returns before the gravity/steer block: the summon
  673 at `ai[0] == 64` (`ai[1] == 2`), the shadowflame 675 at 32
  (`ai[1] == 0`, `direction` re-aimed from the shot vector), the heal 674
  at 40/48/56 (`ai[1] == 1`), and the `ai[0] <= 0` re-roll (-20 after the
  shadowflame, -120 otherwise);
- the re-arm (`:65882-65927`): `ai[0] == 0 && localAI[3] >= 60` picks the
  97/127/183 window per `ai[1]`, gated by `flag9` (`:65905-65909` вЂ” the
  shadowflame round needs the target within 1000 px and in line of sight);
- the walk-anchor stuck detector (`:65968-66019`) and the
  `TargetClosestOldOnesInvasion` retarget / `FaceTarget` write of
  `direction`+`directionY` (`:66009-66012`, inside the detector's
  `localAI[2] >= 0` branch);
- the probe columns (`:66020-66072`), the float gravity (`:66079-66097`),
  the `collideX`/`collideY` bounces off `oldVelocity` (`:66098-66121`) and
  the four steer blocks (`:66122-66185`).

`Npc` gained `direction_y`, `collide_x`, `collide_y`, `old_vx`, `old_vy`
and `dark_mage_local[3]` (the C#'s `directionY`, `collideX`, `collideY`,
`oldVelocity.X/Y` and `localAI[0..2]`).

**The deliberate gaps.** `DD2Event.RaiseGoblins` (`DD2Event.cs:716-...)`
needs `_deadGoblinSpots`, the DD2 event's dead-goblin coordinate list, which

in the 1200x400 box, `:65884-65896`) needs the NPC list the AI method cannot
see, and the `OnlyCrystal` half of `TargetClosestOldOnesInvasion`'s search
(`NPCUtils.cs:268`, the 548 crystal) needs it too вЂ” the player arm of the
search is modelled. `GetAttackDamage_ScaledByDifficulty` runs
classic (the port has no difficulty-scaled NPC damage for this kind). The
three tracked sounds (`DD2_EtherianPortalSpawnEnemy` at `localAI[3] == 30`,
`DD2_DarkMageSummonSkeleton` at `ai[0] == 80`, `DD2_DarkMageCastHeal` at

## The F3 developer workbench (S1-E-29, 2026-11-16)

The F3 cheat-sheet panel is **project-specific**: vanilla Terraria 1.4.5.8 binds F3
to `Loadout3` (`PlayerInput.cs:2090,2203,2315,2427` РІвЂ вЂ™ `TriggersSet.cs:813-816` РІвЂ вЂ™
`Player.TrySwitchingLoadout(2)`) and ships no debug overlay, so there is no vanilla
panel to be 1:1 with. The port's panel is therefore a dev tool, and the deviations
below are recorded rather than resolved:

* **The crate seam.** The panel lives in `tr-debug` (state, layout, hit-testing,
  `Event` intents) with `tr-app` supplying the rows, the drawing and the action
  application. The direction is forced: `tr-app` is a binary crate (`[[bin]]`, no
  `[lib]`), so it cannot be a dependency of `tr-debug`. The gameplay consequence is
  nil РІР‚вЂќ the actions are the unchanged code; only the hit-testing moved.
* **The Cargo feature.** `debug` (default OFF) gates the module, the `App` field,
  its two initialisers and the six call sites, so a release build without it
  contains no panel. `TR_DEBUG`/`TR_STATS`/`render/debug.rs` are **not** gated: they
  are the separate F1 stats overlay and the deterministic-screenshot workflow needs
  `TR_DEBUG=0`.
* **Recipes tab.** Gives `craft::RECIPES[i].create` straight into the inventory with
  no station, ingredient or crafting-hour check. That is deliberate for a debug give
  and is *not* a claim about `Recipe`'s availability rules (`Recipe.cs:15162-15191`
  etc. stay unported).
* **Action semantics.** The World rows now call the real C# entries (S1-E-37, landed
  2026-11-16) instead of flipping flags вЂ” `WorldGen.StartHardmode`
  (`WorldGen.cs:31701-31719`, the runner half *and* the `Lang.misc[15]` broadcast plus
  progression 9), `Main.StartInvasion` (`Main.cs:64435-64486`), `Main.StartSlimeRain`/
  `StopSlimeRain` (`:64742-64820`) and the blood-moon hit body (`:65344-65346`). The
  goblin row's old `80` and the slime row's `43200` were both wrong and are gone. The
  panel cannot switch hardmode back off: the C# `StartHardmode` returns early when
  `hardMode` is set (`:31703`), and the port's `start_hardmode` does the same, so the
  old toggle-off revert is gone. The **kill-all row stays project-specific**: no
  `KillAll`/`KillAllNPCs` exists in the decompilation, so its `hp = 0` sweep is the
  port's own dev shortcut and is not claimed as a port. The pause row *is* exact
  (`WorldUpdateStepper.cs:45-49`) and its test pins it. `main.remixWorld`/
  `isThereAWorldSurface`/the announcement and `netMode` arms of the invasion and slime
  functions fold out вЂ” the port is single-player and none of those flags exist.
* **Upstream reference only.** The feature set takes *behaviour* references from
  CheatSheet (no licence file, credits Gameiki) and HEROsMod (GPLv3); no code, data
  or art is copied or adapted, so nothing of theirs ships.

## S1-L-1 - scene metrics: ScanOnScreenTiles / ScanNPCPositions / the ore finder (2026-11-16)

The scan now runs the whole `SceneMetrics.Scan` body (`SceneMetrics.cs:326-351`) in
source order: `ScanTiles`, `ScanOnScreenTiles`, `ScanNPCPositions`,
`AggregateTileCounts`, `CalculateZones`. Readings behind deliberate deviations:

* **The visual rect.** `Main.cs:62536-62537` is `Main.GetAreaToLight()` then
  `.Inflate(28, 28)`; `GetAreaToLight` (`:63926-63936`) is the *scaled* camera rect,
  `floor(pos/16) - 1` to `floor((pos+size)/16) + 2`. The port has no
  `GameViewMatrix`, and its `camera` + `screen / zoom` is exactly the world-space
  view the tile pass already draws (`render/tiles.rs:312-318`), so the rect is
  derived the same way. Zoom is the only divergence: vanilla's scaled camera differs
  from ours by the view matrix translation, which the port does not model. The rect
  only gates the music box / clock / fountain / monolith reads, all of which are
  single-tile proximity probes - a one-tile difference shifts a fountain colour by at
  most one tile of the view, never the pixel output of an unrelated pass.
* **`ScanNPCPositions` is gated on `npcs` being passed**, not on the C#
  `settings.ScanNPCPositions` bool (`Main.cs:62541` always sets it; `Player.cs:16683`
  also always sets it). `scan_scene_at` (the unit-test entry) passes none, so the
  array stays zeroed there - the C# would clear it in `Reset` regardless (`:786`).
* **`nPC.active` is approximated by `hp > 0`.** The port reaps dead NPCs at the end of
  the NPC tick (`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s `retain(|n| n.hp > 0)`), so a slot in
  `app.npcs` with `hp <= 0` is the transient state between the kill and the retain -
  which the C# would also skip via `active == false`.
* **`NPCBannerBuff` indexing** keeps the port's `vec![false; 320]`; the C# is
  `BannerSystem.MaxBannerTypes = 293` (`BannerSystem.cs:1453`). Only ids < 293 are
  ever written by `banner_num_from_frame`, so the wider vec is inert.
* **Not ported (no reader in the port):** `PartyMonolithCount` (the party monolith
  tile is not in the port's tile set), `MoonLordMonolith` (tile 623's state only
  feeds `ManageSpecialBiomeVisuals("MoonLord", ...)`, unported), `CanPlayCreditsRoll`
  (`ActiveMusicBox == 85` only gates the credits roll, which the port does not have),
  and the `AddPlayerEffects` arms for held items 148/3117/5322 plus
  `player.musicBox`/`musicBoxSilence`/`happyFunTorchTime` (`:747-774`) - the player
  struct has none of those fields. `shimmerWet` is the one `AddPlayerEffects` input
  the port does carry and it is wired (it was already).
* **`ActiveFountainColor`'s consumer — SUPERSEDED by the W4-g73 retire
  phase.** This note recorded the gap (`Main.CalculateWaterStyle`
  `Main.cs:57388-57393` returns the colour when `>= 0`, the port derived
  the style from the camera alone); the head arm is now PORTED as
  `biome::calculate_water_style_with_fountain` with the draw/rain consumers
  wired — see ANALYSIS "The fountain head arm (W4-g73 RETIRE phase)".
* **`TownNPCCount` is now real.** It feeds `MusicEnv.town_npcs` (the `>= 3` town
  music gate, `Main.cs:12199`) and `SpawnContext.town_npcs` (the spawn-pressure
  tiers, `NPC.cs:604-621`), both of which were hardcoded to `0` with an "M4-TOWN"
  comment. The port does spawn town NPCs (`NpcKind::is_town_npc`), so this was a
  real behavioural gap, not a placeholder.

### S1-E-37's remaining deviations

Three, all forced by the port's shape:

* **The bare RNG stream.** The C# debug console is a chat-command dispatcher
  (`ToolkitDebugCommands`) running outside every `Main.SwapRandom` block, so the
  `Main.rand` it touches is the bare stream. The port has no chat-command layer
  (S1-E-29's deviation) and models it with `NamedRngs::global()` (the `key: None`
  arm of `start_invasion_in` and the slime rows' draws), seeded from the world seed
  rather than `DateTime.Now.Ticks` вЂ” the S1-A-10 deviation, unchanged here.
* **`StartHardmode` runs inline.** `WorldGen.StartHardmode` (`WorldGen.cs:31701-31719`)
  defers the strip walk to a background thread
  (`TransformWorldOnBackgroundThread`, `:31721-31742`) and queues the chat/achievement
  follow-up back to the main thread. The port's `start_hardmode` transforms inline

## The Slime Rain event (W4-f39, 2026-11-21, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode.** No `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt`/test run was invoked. The port was
verified by re-reading the C# source in ≤100-line windows (`Main.cs:64742-64961`,
`:65166-65176`, `:65504-65522`, `:48216-48219`, `:52242-52244`; `NPC.cs:5892-5955`,
`:77902-77924`, `:79080-79096`, `:79405-79410`, `:7022-7029`; `Collision.cs:3455-3488`)
and by hand-arithmetic on the witness tests (written, not run). The witnesses are the
`weather_w4_f39.rs` / `npcs_w4_f39.rs` / `npcs_w4_f39_spawns.rs` / `saveglue_w4_f39.rs`
`#[cfg(test)]` modules (the d129 `#[path]` convention).

S1-E-37 landed the `StartSlimeRain`/`StopSlimeRain` entry points and the morning roll's
draw shape. W4-f39 re-ports the **UpdateTime slots** and the **sky-fall spawn** to the
C# statement order, fixing the deviations the census found:

* **The `:64846` surface gate wraps the whole block.** `isThereAWorldSurface` is
  `worldSurface > 50.0` (`Main.cs:2788`), EXCLUSIVE — the pre-fix port gated the slime
  clock/roll on nothing (the clock decayed in a surface-less world). The gate now wraps
  the clock, the rain section and the roll; `start_slime_rain`'s own `:64744` refusal
  moves from `<= 0.0` to `<= 50.0` and gains the `remixWorld` arm (the port HAS the seed
  flag now, `SeedFlags::REMIX`).
* **The clock decays BEFORE the rain section** (`:64848-64863` ahead of `:64864`). The
  pre-fix port ran the slime clock AFTER `Rain::update_time`; the expiry's
  `StopSlimeRain` draw now precedes the rain section's draws on `UpdateTime`.
* **The `:64864`/`:64890` ladder samples its arm ONCE.** The C# reads `Main.raining` at
  the branch entry; a rain that expires INSIDE `Rain::update_time` (`:64880`) leaves the
  tick in the raining arm — the start arms and the slime roll (`:64925`, inside the
  else-if) stay closed until the next tick. The port now samples `was_raining` /
  `slime_rain` / `lanterns_up` / `next_night_lanterns` at the entry (the lantern statics
  are read BEFORE `LanternNight.UpdateTime` at `:64965` can move them).
* **The lantern arms.** `:64868-64871`'s `LanternsUp → StopRain()` (no drain, no strength
  roll) and `:64890`'s `!slimeRain && !LanternsUp && !NextNightIsLanternNight` gate on the
  start arms — the pre-fix `Rain::update_time` folded all three to false.
* **The kill counter's per-death gate** (`NPC.cs:79082`). `DoDeathEvents_AdvanceSlimeRain`
  re-checks `slimeRain && slimeRainNPC[type] && !AnyNPCs(50)` for EACH death; the pre-fix
  port checked `!AnyNPCs(50)` once before the loop, so a King spawned by an earlier death
  in the same tick did not close the gate for later deaths. The check now lives inside
  the loop. The `slimeRainNPC[1]` filter (`Main.cs:8864`) is the port's `Slime` kind —
  every colour variant shares vanilla type 1.
* **The sky-fall spawn** (`Spawner.SlimeRainSpawns`, `NPC.cs:5892-5955`) is re-ported
  whole: the `position.Y` (TOP, not centre) depth gate, the `nearbyActiveNPCs` slot sum
  with the 0.65 `slimeRainNPCSlots` discount (`Main.cs:66803`, `NPC.cs:77916-77918`), the
  `45 + (int)(450f * (nearby/15))` truncated denominator, the `maxTilesX + 10` upper bound
  (was `-10`), `Collision.SolidTiles(xt-3, xt+3, yt-5, yt+2)` + the `Main.wallHouse`
  refusal (was folded), and the full four-arm kind chain — `Next(200)==0` → Pinky(-4),
  `Next(10)==0` → Purple(-7), `Next(5)<2` → Green(-3), else Blue (the pre-fix port folded
  the Pinky arm and mapped the `Next(10)` arm to Yellow).
* **The menu-return stop** (`Main.cs:48216-48219`, `DrawMenu`'s `menuMode <= 1 &&
  slimeRain → StopSlimeRain`). The port's `save_and_quit` is the in-world → menuMode-0
  transition; the stop runs AFTER the save (the C# saves the live event, then the menu
  frame stops it), on the bare `Main.rand` stand-in.

**Documented folds (single-difficulty / port-absent systems):** the expert `×0.85`
denominator and the `Next(7)`/`Next(3)` kind arms (`NPC.cs:5902-5905`/`:5935-5945`), the
journey spawn-rate slider (`:5906-5913`), the `WorldGen.Skyblock.lowTiles` `/5` roll arm
(`Main.cs:64931-64934` — `lowTiles` is skyblock-only, `WorldGen.cs:3215`), the
`FreezeRainPower` gates, and the `netMode`/`SkyManager` arms. The King's `SpawnOnPlayer`
tile-scan placement stays the S1-D-3g deviation (the port spawns at the player's column
+12, the C# scans a 500×50 off-screen area). The death-path loop split (the counter pass
ahead of the boss-death `checkDead` pass) means a slime dying in the SAME tick as the King
still counts — the C# interleaves per-NPC; recorded, not re-homed.

**RNG argument:** the clock walk is RNG-free; the expiry's `StopSlimeRain` draws one
`Next(3024, 6048)` on `UpdateTime` (the King-death caller draws `UpdateNpcs`, the
menu-return caller the bare global); the morning roll draws one `Next(num3)` +
`StartSlimeRain`'s `Next(32400, 54000)`; the sky-fall arm draws `Next(num2)` + the two
window `Next(min, max)` + the kind chain (`Next(200)`, [`Next(10)`], [`Next(5)`]) on
`SpawnNPC`. Every witness mirrors the sequence on a cloned `UnifiedRandom` and compares
the full stream state.

## The season/date gates (W4-f39 Phase B, 2026-11-21, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode.** No `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt`/test run was invoked. Verified by re-reading
the C# in ≤100-line windows (`Main.cs:13118-13172`, `:10901-10937`, `:65389-65392`,
`:65334-65337`, `:64664-64667`, `:65945-65948`; `WorldFile.cs:651-652`, `:1347-1351`,
`:1386-1387`, `:2334-2340`; `NPC.cs:79210-79238`, `:6371-6379`; `Chest.cs:1558`/`:1655`/
`:1903`/`:1966`/`:2027`/`:2249`/`:2667`/`:3436-3468`; `AmbienceServer.cs:130-137`;
`Item.cs:49668-49714`) and hand-arithmetic on the witnesses (written, not run).

**The user-flagged gap.** The port had NO calendar: `Main.halloween`/`Main.xMas` were stood
in by the endless micro seeds alone, so the Oct/Dec windows never opened. Phase B ports the
date decisions and wires every constants-off season consumer to the resolved flags.

* **The pure date module** (`tr-core/src/season.rs`): `is_halloween_date` (Oct 10-31 + Nov 1,
  `Main.cs:13141-13155`, both edges inclusive), `is_xmas_date` (Dec 15-31, `:13123`),
  `check_xmas`/`check_halloween` (date OR force-today OR force-forever, `:13118-13172`), and
  `moon_event_temporary_seasons` (`CheckForMoonEventsStartingTemporarySeasons`,
  `:10901-10937` — wave >= 15 raises the today-flag, the forever seed suppresses its own).
  Every decision takes a caller-pinned `(month, day)` — the **FixtureClock seam**
  (`tools/WldFixtureHarness/Shims/FixtureClock.cs` precedent): the wall clock is injected,
  never read inside the decision. `now_month_day()` is the ONLY runtime read (UTC
  `SystemTime` → Hinnant `civil_from_days`, the `ui/world_select.rs` conversion). All
  draw-free — the C# checks compare integers, they consume no `Main.rand`.
* **The resolved statics** (`World.xmas`/`halloween`/`force_xmas_for_today`/
  `force_halloween_for_today`): re-derived at every dawn by `World::refresh_seasons`
  (`Main.cs:65389-65391`, BEFORE `stopMoonEvent` at `:65392` clears the moon state the
  temporary-season check reads) and at world load (`enter_loaded_world`,
  `WorldFile.cs:651-652`). The `*Forever` flags are the endless micro seeds
  (`WorldGen.cs:572-578`). Runtime-only — the C# does not save the resolved flags (they
  re-derive from the date + the saved force flags).
* **The dawn seam** (`world_sim/clock.rs::advance_time` gains a `date: (u32, u32)` param):
  the runtime caller (`advance_time_with_events`) passes `season::now_month_day()`; the
  witnesses pin any date. The season trio runs in the dawn branch ahead of `stop_moon_event`.
* **The five seasonal moon-boss downeds** (`World.downed_halloween_king`/`_tree`,
  `downed_christmas_tree`/`_ice_queen`/`_santank`, `NPC.cs:6371-6379`): the `DoDeathEvents`
  cases 325/327/344/345/346 (`NPC.cs:79210-79238`) raise them under the RUNNING event's own
  flag. Persisted: the `.trwld` v18 tail (5 bytes) + the C# `.wld` flags block

## The boss sprite direction and roll audit (S1-G-19, 2026-11-16)

Every sprite flip in the renderer comes from one field вЂ” `Npc::sprite_dir`
(`render/entities.rs:2603`) вЂ” because that is what the C# does: `Main.cs:23124-23128`
draws mirrored iff `spriteDirection == 1`. Two failure modes follow, and both were
present:

* **A sign slip mirrors the whole sprite.** `AI()`'s boss arms write
  `direction = spriteDirection = (Center.X < target.Center.X) ? 1 : -1`, i.e. **+1
  when the player is to the right**. The port had four of Betsy's written as
  `if pcx < cx { 1 } else { -1 }` (`:61899`, `:61902`, `:61999`, `:62053`), so the
  dragon faced away from the player for half of every phase. Fixed to `cx < pcx`.
* **A kind absent from the rotation whitelist never rolls.** The renderer opts each
  kind into the generic `Main.cs:26632` rotation draw by an explicit list
  (`render/entities.rs:2611-2660`), because most NPC kinds leave `rotation` at zero
  and would be rotated by garbage. `NpcKind::DD2Betsy` was missing from it while
  `update_betsy` was already writing `npc.rotation` вЂ” the whole `AngleTowards` tail
  (`:62256-62301`) was dead. The kind is now listed and the tail ported: the
  per-phase `num40` aim / `num41` turn rate (phases 2 and 5 write `num41 = 0` and so
  keep the phase's own aim; 3 starts at 0.01 and switches to 0.05 with a
  `В±ПЂ/12` lean once `ai[1] >= 40`; 4 aims at `ПЂ` or `2ПЂ`; 6 at 0.02), then the
  unconditional `spriteDirection == -1` ПЂ fold before `angle_towards`.

The Wall of Flesh's eye was the mirror-image bug in a literal sense: the port had
invented its own aim logic for the eye, while `AI()`'s aiStyle-28 arm
(`:26066-26068`) simply copies the parent вЂ” `position.X = wof.X - width/2`,
`direction = spriteDirection = wof.direction`, `position.Y -= height/2` вЂ” so the eye
always looks the way the mouth does. The parent's direction is now carried on the
world (`World::wof_dir`) because the eye's update has no access to the body NPC, and
`update_wof_eye` mirrors it.

Two structural traps met in the same pass, both of which had produced *silently*
wrong port code rather than a visible mirror flip:

* `AI_045_Golem`'s charge block is gated on the literal `velocity.Y == 0f`
  (`:19640`), this repo's `Npc::on_ground` is the tile-contact flag written by the
  integration step. They agree for a settled body and disagree for a body whose
  velocity was just zeroed by a wall or a test fixture; the C# spelling is the one
  that was ported.
* The golem's flight `vy` sink (`:19727-19730`) is applied only while
  `Bottom.Y < player.position.Y` **and** the horizontal span test passes вЂ” the span
  test compares both edges (`position.X < player.position.X && position.X + width >
  player.position.X + player.width`), not the centres.

Not ported, and now filed as **S1-D-3p**: `NPC.TargetClosest` `:77652-77781`
including `TryTrackingTarget`/`SetTargetTrackingValues`, `targetRect`,
`npcTypeNoAggro`, `tankPet` gating, `confused`, `oldTarget` and `DirectionY`. The
port has no such method; each machine writes `facing`/`sprite_dir` itself, and
`npc_ai.rs::walker_step`'s `aggro_x`/`aggro_y` window (80Г—40 tiles at the call sites)
is an invention with no C# counterpart. Retrofitting it changes which NPC targets
which for every aiStyle-3 kind, so it needs its own branch and its own test pass.
**The helper landed with S1-D-3p (2026-11-18)** вЂ” see "The shared target selection
(S1-D-3p)" below; the caller migration is the documented remainder.

Deliberate deviations (the wiring remainder):

* **Wiring deferred.** The sim's Destroyer still rides the aiStyle-6 worm
  pass (`npc.rs`'s `NpcKind::TheDestroyer => {}` arm +
  `world_sim/npcs.rs::update_worms_in`'s 80-budget same-kind chain). The
  machine is not called from `Npc::update_rng`'s style axis yet вЂ” the port

  body/tail branches activate unchanged when those kinds land.

  (`:49929`), `SoundEngine.PlaySound(15)` (`:50093`), `HitEffect`/`checkDead`

  the caller resolves them (the port's pool has no `active` field and
  compacts every frame).

  (S1-D-3j), no getGoodWorld вЂ” the same constants-off convention as the
  other difficulty-gated machines. `soundDelay`/`justHit` have no `Npc`
  fields; the ctx carries them (the wiring's `justHit` stand-in is
  `hurt_cd > 0.0`, the port's recoil convention).

  (`Main.cs:66989`); the port's Vec compacts. A missing `ai[1]` slot reads
  as the C#'s `try/catch` outcome (`:49999-50007`: keep the snapped player
  aim); the orphan check treats it as a dead parent (the C# would throw вЂ”
  the port's chain never carries dangling links because the worm pass
  kills them, `:51425-51433`).
* **RNG argument.** The machine's only draws are the body laser's: per
  tick `Next(4)` (`UnifiedRandom.cs:134-141` в†’ `next_max(4)`) then
  `Next(1400, 26000)` (`:120-132` в†’ `next_range`), and on a firing tick
  four `Next(-20, 21)` in the order aim-X, aim-Y, spread-X, spread-Y. All
  take the caller's `UnifiedRandom` (the exact `Main.rand` stream) вЂ” the
  witness tests clone the stream and replay the draws in source order, so
  any reordering or extra draw fails the equality. No other stream is
  touched; the head's machine is draw-free.

  (`DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged`, `NPC.cs:57336`,
  `:60300-60330` вЂ” for type 3 only the non-eclipse-day-above-surface terms
  can fire) and drops the invented 80Г—40-tile aggro window. The other ~29
  `walker_step` callers and every ad-hoc-facing AI keep their current
  writes until the migration; `walker_step`'s `aggro_x`/`aggro_y` params
  stay for them (the C# has no such window вЂ” the chase is gated by the
  despawn-discouragement arm, not a distance box).
* **Stock player inputs.** `Player.aggro`, `npcTypeNoAggro` and `tankPet`
  have no port fields (the stealth armour / tank pets are unported
  systems); the wiring passes 0/false/None, the C# stock values. The
  `:60300-60330` — for type 3 only the non-eclipse-day-above-surface terms
  can fire) and drops the invented 80×40-tile aggro window. The 2026-11-19
  walker migration batch 1 (`walker_step_fighter`, below) wires 10 more
  fighter callers on the FULL gate. The remaining walker callers and
  every ad-hoc-facing AI keep their current writes until the next batch;
  `walker_step`'s `aggro_x`/`aggro_y` params stay for them (the C# has no
  such window — the chase is gated by the despawn-discouragement arm, not
  a distance box).
* **Stock player inputs — the fields landed with batch 1.** `Player.aggro`
  (`Player.cs:1446`), `npcTypeNoAggro[NPCID.Count]` (`Player.cs:2994`,
  `NPCID.Count = 697`, `NPCID.cs:12581`) and `tankPet` (`Player.cs:870`,

  `session_candidate_for(player, kind)` resolves the per-type

* **The zombie's velocity write stays direct** (`facing * 1f`): the C#'s

* **The `old_*` latches** (`NPC.cs:90393-90395`, `UpdateNPC`'s head) are

* **`targetSetFrame` stamps 0** from the zombie wiring: the

  `SetDefaults` boss rows land with the caller migration; the gate's

11 parity tests (`npc_target::tests`): the aggro metric, the no-aggro
penalty + facing suppression, the rect truncation + int-centre ties, the
aiStyle-3 bottom-edge arm, the oldTarget inheritance (swing/fresh/boss
breaks), the confused flip, the tank steal + its LOS wall, the dead/absent

## The walker migration batch 1 (S1-D-3p, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

`task/S1-D-3p-walker-migration` — the first coherent batch of the
`walker_step` caller migration: **10 aiStyle-3 fighter callers** now run
the shared selection at the C# position through
`npc_ai.rs::walker_step_fighter`. No compiler invoked (code-only mode):
the equivalence argument is below, the A/B tests are tests-as-code
(written, NOT run).

### The C# shape (re-read, cited)

`AI_003_Fighters` (`NPC.cs:55856+`) runs its target core at `:57336`:

```
if (this.ai[3] < (float)num57 && NPC.DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged(...))
{
    ... sound rolls (:57340-57367, the unported audio layer) ...
    this.TargetClosest();                                   // :57369
    if (this.directionY > 0 && Main.player[this.target].Center.Y <= base.Bottom.Y)
        this.directionY = -1;                               // :57370-57373
}
else if (...) { ... the wander/despawn arm (:57375-57401) ... }
```

`num57` is 60 (`:57035`), 180 for type 120 (`:57036-57038` — no batch kind
is 120, the fold keeps the gate verbatim). The velocity ladder
(`npc_ai3_speeds.rs`, S1-D-3) runs AFTER the core (`:57403-58401`), then
the position integration. `walker_step_fighter` reproduces exactly this
order: gate → `target_closest` (the `npc_target.rs` helper, slot-0 session
candidate, aiStyle 3, ticker 0) → `sprite_dir = facing` (the BUG-07
lockstep, the zombie convention) → the `:57370-57373` directionY re-check
→ `run_ai3_ladder` with the direct `facing * speed` fallback → the
unchanged `walker_integrate`. The discouraged arm keeps the port's
`vx *= 0.9` decay (the zombie convention; the C# wander-flip arm is the
full AI_003 migration's job).

The gate itself — `DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged`
(`NPC.cs:60300-60330`) — is ported whole as `fighters_not_discouraged`:
the day-above-surface `&&` chain (eclipse / `IsItDay` / statue / surface /
graveyard / snowMoon / invasionType 1+3+4 / dontStarve / the ~50-type
exclusion list / the 411 ai[1] window) and the switch (409/415/419/425/
427/428/429/508/524-527/580/582 + 528-532 stay encouraged; the default
returns `NPCID.Sets.CritterThatCanTurnOnPlayers`, `NPCID.cs:10436`). When
ANY chain term fails (night, underground, ...) the method returns true —
every fighter chases. Stock stand-ins: `ZoneGraveyard` and
`Main.dontStarveWorld` have no port fields (false — their terms pass);
`Main.remixWorld`'s `IsItDay` half (`Main.cs:62825-62832`) is unported.
