`CaptureSettings.cs`, `CaptureBiome.cs`). Deliberate deviations:

- **The "smoothing" is a verbatim copy in 1.4.5.8.** `DrawSelf` assigns
  `_visualOverallProgress = _targetOverallProgress` (and the current pair)
  directly (`UIGenProgressBar.cs:68-69`) вЂ” no lerp exists in this version.
  The port keeps both field pairs and pins the copy in a test so a later
  smoothing lerp cannot land silently.
- **Wired (round 2).** `FrontScreen::WorldLoad` is the sixth front screen;
  `finish_creating_world` (`app/session.rs`) starts the generation job and
  opens the screen (`WorldGen.CreateNewWorld`, `WorldGen.cs:6607-6625`);
  `update_world_load` polls the result and hops to the world select
  (`worldGenCallback`'s `menuMode = 6`, `:6599-6602` в†’ `Main.cs:49468-49472`).
  The generation runs on a worker thread (`app/worldgen_job.rs`, the C#'s
  `Task.Factory.StartNew`) through the `GenProgressHook` seam
  (`tr_core::worldgen::pipeline`); the progress/controller pair is the
  `WorldGenerator.CurrentGenerationProgress`/`CurrentController` statics
  (`WorldGenerator.cs:398-400`). The bar's four `Outer_*` textures load
  (`assets.rs`, `UIGenProgressBar.cs:34-37`). The Inventory trigger queues
  the abort (`UIWorldLoad.cs:54-58`); the abort arm skips the save
  (`WorldGen.cs:6595-6598`).
- **The drunk-world `Main.rand` arms are deferred.** The evil-texture
  flicker (`UIGenProgressBar.cs:63-67`) and the random-digit message
  (`UIWorldLoad.cs:93-103`) draw from `Main.rand`; wiring them would perturb
  that stream's call order (the RNG-order invariant). The ported
  `draw_frame` takes the evil flags as inputs.
- **`placingTraps` stays false.** It is a pass-runtime static
  (`WorldGen.cs:18662`) the port's compact pipeline never sets; the
  get-good message reversal's `noTraps && placingTraps` gate
  (`UIWorldLoad.cs:108`) therefore always takes the reversal arm on a
  For-the-Worthy world.
- **`GetStatusText`'s `0.0%` formatting rides the shared
  `tr_core::generation_progress::format_percent`** (`(v*1000).round()/10`,
  half-away-from-zero вЂ” .NET's `"0.0%"` custom specifier). An earlier round
  used Rust's `{:.1}` (half-to-even) and claimed the tie input was not
  binary-representable; that claim was false вЂ” e.g. `0.0625` scales to
  exactly `6.25`, where .NET prints `6.3%` and `{:.1}` prints `6.2%`. Both
  the status text and the `Message` `{0:0.0%}` substitution now use the one
  formatter, pinned by the `0.0625 в†’ "6.3%"` test.
- **The get-good message reversal walks Unicode scalars, not UTF-16 code
  units.** The C# reverses via `Text.Substring(num, 1)` per UTF-16 unit
  (`UIWorldLoad.cs:110-115`); the port's `chars().rev()` reverses whole
  scalars. The two differ only for surrogate-pair characters (emoji, rare
  CJK extensions), which the `Lang.gen`/`WorldGeneration.*` messages never
  contain вЂ” ASCII and the localized messages are identical in practice.
- **`worldGenCallback` plays sound 10 twice; the port plays the completion
  one only.** The C# plays `SoundEngine.PlaySound(10)` at entry AND exit
  (`WorldGen.cs:6592`/`:6603`); the port plays `Menu_Open` on the completion
  poll (`app/session.rs::update_world_load`, `:6603`). The entry cue is
  deferred: the worker thread has no audio seam, and playing it on the
  frame thread at job start would shift the cue's frame relative to the
  C# task-start ordering вЂ” a documented deviation, not a silent drop.
- **`CreateNewWorld` reseeds `Main.rand`; the port does not.** The C#
  assigns `Main.rand = new UnifiedRandom(Main.ActiveWorldFileData.Seed)`
  (`WorldGen.cs:6612`) before the task starts. The port keeps its `Main.rand`
  stream untouched (the RNG-order invariant): reseeding at world creation
  would change every subsequent menu/gameplay roll's provenance. Documented
  deviation; revisit with the faithful `UnifiedRandom` port.
- `Main.gameTips` (`UIWorldLoad.cs:117-118`) is research/19 M3
  (`GameTipsDisplay`), out of scope; the gamepad squiggle (`:122-127`) and
  F5 `UIWorldGenDebug` (`:50-53`) are desktop/debug pieces, unported.
- **W4-d86 re-verification (research/18c, f22 conflict 5).** The research/18
  PARTIAL row ("folded into world_select/save_list") was stale: the screen
  is a first-class `FrontScreen::WorldLoad` state and nothing was folded.
  Verdict PORTED with the deferrals above. The F5 arm's scope-out is now
  explicit: `UIWorldGenDebug` (1 702 ln) opens only via
  `DebugOptions.enableDebugCommands && F5` (`UIWorldLoad.cs:50-52`) or the
  worldgen debug hook (`WorldGenerator.cs:477`) and is excluded with
  `Testing/**`; `OnActivate`'s `ChangePoint(3000)` (`:37-44`) joins the
  squiggle in the Stage-1 gamepad exclusion. The note rides
  `world_load.rs`'s module header so the code carries the record too.
- **The `TR_UI=worldload` preset latches a fixed snapshot.** The screenshot
  preset (`settings_ui.rs`) parks a mid-generation progress (42.5% overall /
  60% current, the `LegacyWorldGen.11` "Generating jungle" label) with no
  worker thread, so the shot is SHA256-stable; `update_world_load` only
  re-latches the snapshot while a job is live (a job-less frame keeps the
  preset's). Baseline `docs/screenshots/s1-e-17-worldload.png`,
  `TR_SHOT` + `TR_UI=worldload` + `TR_NAME=ShotPin` + `TR_DEBUG=0` +
  `TR_DAY=1.0`, two runs SHA256-equal
  (`8f308c82c27b29ad523dfd2baa48dedb5887f55d6514ce1967e6c0e316496b9a`).

### The capture mode (S1-E-17)

`crates/tr-app/src/capture.rs` ports the capture family's state machines
1:1: the `CaptureManager` facade (`CaptureManager.cs:8-114`), the
`CaptureInterface` selection state machine (the three modes вЂ” edge selection, drag
bounds, change settings вЂ” the toolbar, the camera countdown,
`CaptureInterface.cs:15-1607`), the `CaptureCamera` chunk queue / scaling /
blit / finish machine (`CaptureCamera.cs:17-425`), `CaptureSettings`
(`CaptureSettings.cs:6-28`) and `CaptureBiome`'s style table + biome pick
(`CaptureBiome.cs:3-246`). The App owns the one `CaptureManager.Instance`
(`App.capture`); `app/capture_driver.rs` pumps it per frame at the C# call
sites (`Update` at `Main.cs:46187`/`:62166`, `DrawTick` at `:61729`). The
capture freeze has TWO halves, both ported: (1) the `DoUpdate` gate
(`Main.cs:16886-16890`, `if (IsCapturing) { FocusHelper.UpdateFocus; return; }`)
вЂ” while a capture renders the ENTIRE world update skips: `Sandstorm.EmitDust`
(`:17247`, it consumes the dust RNG), `SceneState.Update` (`:17816`) and the
whole sim sit AFTER that return. Ported in `frame.rs`: `update_world_frame`
is gated on `!is_capturing()` (the capture interface itself still updates вЂ”
it rides the interface pass, not DoUpdate's world branch). (2) The
`UpdateSceneMetrics` gate (`Main.cs:62518-62521`) вЂ” the DRAW-SIDE guard for
the lighting engines' ExportMetrics callers (`LightingEngine.cs:93`,
`LegacyLighting.cs:722`): `update_scene` reads `is_capturing()` and keeps the
parked metrics (no rescan) for any draw-side caller that still runs.
Deviations:

- **The selection UI has no sprite draw yet вЂ” state only.** The
  `CaptureInterface` state machine (modes, toolbar actions, countdown) is
  ported and live, but `capture.rs` has no sprite-draw function: the
  selection rectangle, the toolbar buttons and the countdown digits do
  not render on screen. The UI draw lands with the S1-G-13 render-target
  seam (the GPU chunk render needs the same targets); until then capture
  mode is driven blind (F6 toggle + the state machine). Earlier
  ROADMAP/PORT_MAP wording calling the selection UI "live" meant the
  state machine only вЂ” corrected.

- **The GPU render half is the S1-G-13 seam.** `Main.DrawCapture`
  (`Main.cs:56673-57066`) renders each chunk into the 2048ВІ framebuffer
  through the layer targets; the render-target FAMILY now exists
  (`tr_render::RenderTargetFamily`, `App.targets` вЂ” S1-G-13, ANALYSIS
  "The render-target family (S1-G-13)"), but the chunk render through it
  is not wired: the port's `CaptureRenderer` trait is still a no-op
  stub, so a started capture drains its queue without producing pixels.
  The selection state machine, the countdown and the `IsCapturing`
  metrics gate are live (the selection UI's sprite draw is NOT вЂ” see the
  bullet above); the write-out waits on the per-layer render callbacks +
  `DrawCapture`.
- **The capture toggle rides F6, not F4.** The vanilla binds
  `ToggleCameraMode` to F4 (`PlayerInput.cs:2091`); the port's F4 is the
  debug-overlay toggle (`loop.rs:652`), so the capture toggle uses F6.
- **The fullscreen-map selection arm is a gap.** `GetMapCoords`
  (`CaptureInterface.cs:1318-1458`) needs the map renderer's texture
  geometry; the port's selection modes run the world arm only.
- **`Player.ghost`/`gravDir` and `Main.treeX` are unported**, so the
  capture input's ghost/gravity gates read false and `GetPurityForPlayer`
  takes the no-treeX fall-through (`CaptureBiome.cs:206-222`).
- **`Utils.OpenFolder` is a no-op** (the port has no folder-open seam);
  the toolbar's open-folder button plays its cue only.

## The render-target family (S1-G-13, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-render/src/targets.rs` ports the render-target FAMILY
infrastructure вЂ” the seam `Main.DrawCapture` and the per-layer offscreen
caching wait on. What landed, 1:1:

- **`InitTargets`' size math** (`Main.cs:58167-58181`,
  `init_target_layout`): `val = MaxWorldViewSize.X` (1920, `:677-681` /
  `:66714`) clamps BOTH axes (`:58173-58174` вЂ” the C# uses `.X` for the
  height clamp too); `SupportWideScreen && HiDef` raises it to 4096
  (`:58169-58172`); `offScreenRange` starts at 192 and shrinks to
  `(_renderTargetMaxSize - num) / 2` (C# int division) when the padded
  width would overflow (`:58176-58179`). `_renderTargetMaxSize` is 4096
  HiDef / 2048 Reach (`SetGraphicsProfileInternal`, `:3708-3718`).
- **All ten targets in creation order** (`:58187-58196`,
  `RenderTargetFamily::init`): the seven world-space
  `WorldSceneLayerTarget`s (water, backWater, tile, tile2, wall,
  background, backgroundSwap вЂ” `Main.cs:765-777`) at the padded size,
  then skyTarget / screenTarget / screenTargetSwap at the raw backbuffer
  size (`:781-785`). `ReleaseTargets` (`:58093-58150`) is Rust `Drop`;
  `EnsureRenderTargetContent` (`:58152-58158`) is
  `RenderTargetFamily::ensure` вЂ” called at the draw head
  (`frame/draw.rs`, the `Main.Draw` wrapper's first step, `:61644`).
- **`WorldSceneLayerTarget`** (`Graphics/WorldSceneLayerTarget.cs:7-70`):
  `UpdateContent` (`:43-64`) computes the camera override (screen size =
  target в€’ 2В·offScreenRange, position = `Utils.Round(center в€’ size/2)` вЂ”
  banker's rounding, `Utils.cs:112-115` вЂ” zoom = 1), clears the target
  transparent and records `_position = screenPosition в€’ (osr, osr)`
  (`:57`); `IsPartiallyOffscreen` (`:17-34`) with the zero-position quirk
  (a never-rendered layer counts as offscreen) and the strict `>`
  margin test on both axes.
- **`RenderToTargets` scheduling** (`Main.cs:57277-57327`,
  `render_to_targets_plan`): the `renderCount` phase arms (1 в†’ water;
  2 в†’ backWater + backgroundSwap + the pending flag; 3 в†’ wall + tile +
  tile2; the count is driven by the lighting engine,
  `LightingEngine.cs:90-103`), then the fixed partial-offscreen re-render
  order tile в†’ tile2 в†’ backWater в†’ background (apply the pending swap,
  RE-CHECK, then maybe re-render вЂ” `:57311-57318`) в†’ wall в†’ water. The
  unreachable `renderNow` arms of the else-if chain are ported verbatim.
- **`ApplyPendingBackgroundTargetSwap`** (`:58047-58054`): the
  `Utils.Swap` + flag clear; the phase-2 arm sets the flag (`:57291`).
- **The skyTarget gate** (`:62021-62027`, `sky_target_active`):
  `(CanCapture || ForegroundSunlightEffects) && !drawToScreen &&
  !mapFullscreen && !onlyDrawFancyUI && Lighting.NotRetro`.
- **The `drawToScreen`/`targetSet` transition** (`:61751-61766`,
  `target_transition`): Release on leaving the target path, Init on
  entering, Keep otherwise.

Deviations / scope (deliberate):

- **No draw pass consumes the layers yet.** The frame path is unchanged:
  the port keeps its single G6-cached world range + the
  `render_world_fx` screen ping-pong (`sprite.rs`), and the family is
  allocated but not rendered into by the world passes. The per-layer
  render callbacks (`RenderTiles`/`RenderWallsAndBlacks`/`RenderWater`/
  `RenderBackground*`, `Main.cs:57329-58091`), the skyTarget bind in the
  sky pass (`:62025`) and the composite draws (`:63333`, `:62213`,
  `:62196`, `:62308`) are the follow-up half of S1-G-13 вЂ” moving the
  existing passes onto the layers is a draw-pass-order change and needs
  its own A/B (the draw-pass order is frozen this round). The G6
  `WorldFrameKey` is untouched.
- **`IsContentLost` has no wgpu equivalent** вЂ” device loss recreates
  everything; `ensure` re-inits on absence or backbuffer-size change
  (the null-check half of `:58154`).
- **The `InitTargets` catch arm** (`:58203-58215`: fall back to Retro
  lighting + map off on allocation failure) is not ported вЂ” wgpu texture
  creation aborts the process on failure instead of throwing.
- **`Lighting.UpdateEveryFrame`** (`Lighting.cs:77-86`) is not yet a
  live input: the port always runs the cached path, so
  `target_transition` is ported + tested but the frame only ever takes
  the Init/Keep arms. The Retro/UpdateEveryFrame drawToScreen branch
  stays the research/02 deviation.
- **The capture seam stays a stub** (`app/capture_driver.rs`'s
  `PendingCaptureRenderer`): the family exists, but `Main.DrawCapture`
  (`:56673-57066`) rendering chunks through it is the consumer half вЂ”
  documented in "The loading screen + capture mode" above.

Tests: 17 in `targets.rs` вЂ” the layout math (1080p HiDef/Reach, small
window, the X-cap-on-both-axes clamp, wide-HiDef), `IsPartiallyOffscreen`
(zero position, strict boundary, per-axis), the banker's camera override,
the phase arms + offscreen order + swap-cancel, the sky gate's six
inputs, the transition arms, and four headless-GPU tests (family sizes,
update_content position/clear readback, the background swap exchange,
ensure's size-change re-init).

## S1-F-7 wave A - the generated TileObjectData registry (2026-11-18)

`tools/GenTileObjectData/gen.py` interprets `TileObjectData.Initialize`
(`TileObjectData.cs:2110-5014`) statement-by-statement and emits all 389
registered tiles (604 defs) into `crates/tr-core/src/tileobject/registry.rs`,
retiring the 33 hand-written defs. The generator reproduces the copy-on-write
builder chain (module sharing via `CopyFrom`, the `_hasOwn*` no-op-compare
setters, `Calculate`'s liquid-death fold, `LinkedAlternates` propagation,
`addTile`/`addSubTile`/`addAlternate`/`addBaseTile` cursor resets) and two C#
bugs verbatim:

* **`FullCopyFrom` empties the sub-tiles** (`TileObjectData.cs:1722-1741` +
  `TileObjectSubTilesModule.cs:17-27`): the copy ctor loops `i < this.data.Count`
  over the FRESH list (Count 0, capacity != count), so tiles 83/84
  (`FullCopyFrom(82)`/`(83)`, :4785-4788) and 389 (`FullCopyFrom(388)`, :2323)
  resolve NO sub-tiles in vanilla. The hand defs wrongly carried 82's sub-tiles
  into 83/84; the generated table reproduces the bug.
* **`AnchorAlternateTiles` compares against `tileInvalid`** (:449) вЂ” a no-op
  write when the alternate list equals the INVALID list (a C# typo, reproduced).

The shared-reference alternates/sub-tile cycles (C# heap references; `CopyFrom`
shares the lists, then `addAlternate`/`addSubTile` appends) emit acyclic:
top-level defs AND sub-tile nodes keep their OWN alternates lists verbatim вЂ”
`GetTileData` (`TileObjectData.cs:5148-5157`) does `alternate--` then indexes the
RESOLVED sub-tile's Alternates, so dropping them refused placements the C#
accepts (S1-F-7a: chair style 16 right-facing, torch sub8 wall-anchor; 69
sub-tiles carry non-empty alternates). Alternate NODES are leaves (scalar
fields + empty nested lists): their deeper nested lists are the cycle depth no
consumer reads вЂ” `GetTileData` resolves only one level past the sub-tile and
`can_place`/`custom_place` read the base's lists plus one resolution level.
Verified over the interpreted graph: every sub-tile alternate target is a pure
leaf (never a top/sub-tile object, no self-references), so top -> sub ->
alternate-leaf emission is acyclic (the DFS test in `test_gen.py`). Sub-tiles'
nested sub-tile lists are likewise not emitted (the deeper C# cycles; no
consumer resolves a sub-tile's sub-tiles).

### Consumer switch (minimal, behaviour-preserving)

* `edit::place_item_tile` gates on `tileobject::routes_through_tile_object`
  (`CustomPlace(type, style)` + the 82/227/4 exclusions, `Player.cs:39771-39772`),
  NOT mere registration вЂ” the natural objects (pots 28, small piles 185,
  platforms 19, plants, torches 4, dye plants 227) keep the legacy
  `WorldGen.PlaceTile` route. The large piles 186/187 ARE `CustomPlace`-true and
  ride the TileObject route.
* `editing::legacy_precheck_applies` mirrors that gate; alch seeds (82/83/84)
  bypass the neighbour pre-check because `BlockPlacementForAssortedThings`
  forces `canPlace = true` for them (`Player.cs:41294-41296`).
* `editing::cell_drops` reads the generated `KILL_TILE_NO_CELL_DROP` table (the
  `KillTile_GetItemDrops` empty case group, `WorldGen.cs:63988-66090`) instead of
  `def_for_tile(...).is_some()` вЂ” the full registry registers torches/platforms/
  orbs/plants that DO drop per-cell, so the old proxy would swallow their drops.

### Wave B (S1-F-7b, 2026-11-18): the RandomStyleRange runtime hook

The `Main.rand` random-style path (`TileObject.cs:761-825`) is now ported and
wired; the rest of wave B stays documented callbacks.

* `tileobject::can_place` takes `rand: &mut UnifiedRandom` (the `Main.rand`
  stand-in) and `random_cache: Option<RandomCache>`. The draws are verbatim:
  `Main.rand.Next(RandomStyleRange)` (:787) is spent EVEN when `forcedRandom`
  overwrites it (:788-791) or the cache sticks (:792); `SpecificRandomStyles`
  draws a second `Next(len)` (:819) with the same overwrite/stickiness rules
  (:820-824) and its result replaces `num37`. Draw order: range first, list
  second вЂ” pinned by `s1_f_7b_specific_random_styles_rand_path_and_draw_order`.
* `RandomCache` ports the read side of `TileObjectPreviewData.randomCache`
  (`Type`/`Coordinates`/`ObjectStart`/`Random`, TileObject.cs:769-774/:801-806);
  the staleness compare is `Coordinates + ObjectStart` vs `click - Origin`
  (:773-780). A fresh cache is ZERO-initialised (`Random = 0`), not `Reset()`'s
  -1 вЂ” `Reset` is never called on the random cache.
* **Deliberate deviation (documented)**: the `randomCache` WRITEBACK happens
  only inside `onlyCheck` (`TileObject.cs:826-837`, verified: no other writer
  in the tree), and the port does not run the preview вЂ” so
  `World::tile_object_random_cache` stays `None` in production and every
  `CanPlace` draws fresh. The stickiness branch is ported and tested with an
  injected cache (`s1_f_7b_random_cache_stickiness_still_draws`); it goes live
  with the smart-cursor preview task.
* **Stream choice (documented)**: vanilla shares one `Main.rand`; the port
  keeps per-consumer streams (the house pattern вЂ” `craft_rng`, `frame_rng`,
  S1-A-11). `World::place_rng` is the placement family's dedicated
  `UnifiedRandom`, seeded from the world seed beside `frame_rng` in
  `seed_frame_rng`. Its draws never interleave with the framing rolls; the
  worldgen contract streams are untouched (`place_buried_chest`'s chest 21
  has `RandomStyleRange = 0`, so the temple pass draws nothing вЂ” pinned by
  the frozen world-hash tests staying green).
* `SpecificRandomStyles` is null in every generated def (`Initialize` never
  assigns it); the branch is ported for synthetic defs and future data.
* Consumers wired: `edit::place_item_tile` (the `Player.cs:39773` route) and
  `worldgen::temple::place_buried_chest` (`WorldGen.cs:57820`) pass
  `world.place_rng` + `world.tile_object_random_cache`.
* RNG-order proof: `s1_f_7b_random_style_range_rng_order` replays a witness
  `UnifiedRandom` (`next_max(3)` per sunflower placement, 6 seeds x 5 spots)
  and asserts FULL stream-state equality (seed array + cursor) after every
  call, plus the placed `frameX = 36 * draw`;
  `s1_f_7b_place_item_tile_rides_the_world_place_rng` pins the consumer wiring
  (one draw per placement, twin worlds byte-equal, non-random defs draw
  nothing, `frame_rng` untouched).

**Wave B GetStyleOverride resolution DONE (W4-d112, 2026-11-20, code-only)**:
`tileobject::resolve_tile_def` ports the tile-based `GetTileData(Tile)`
overload (`TileObjectData.cs:5196-5261`) 1:1 — the frameX/frameY cell decode
(:5212-5213), the wrap-0→1 fold (:5214-5218), the horizontal/vertical style
layout (:5219), the multiplier split (:5220-5221), the `GetStyleOverride`
short-circuit (:5222-5226 → `apply_style_override`, the three `GetStyle_*`
bodies :5294-5327 with their exact thresholds 36/18/36-72-90), the
`StyleLineSkip` re-decode (:5227-5240), the null-padded sub-tile lookup
(:5241-5248) and the FIRST-match `[Style, Style+RandomStyleRange]` alternate
window scan with INCLUSIVE upper bound (:5249-5259). Documented deviations:
the null-Tile arm is the caller's `world.tile()` `None`; the out-of-range-type

index the sub-tile pair slice positionally (the three override kinds' lists

:4999/:5005/:5011). No consumer is re-wired: `object_tiles_at` and the kill
cascade keep their base-def frame math (their C# counterparts are the
`WorldGen.Check*` loops, not this overload); the framing/liquid-death
consumers wire in with their own tasks. Witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN (task
constraint): `tests/tileobject_resolve_witness_d112.rs` (10 tests — the three
override thresholds incl. boundaries, chair multiplier + sub-tile-own
alternates, door line-skip re-decode + style-19 sub-tile, lamp zero-wrap
line-skip, sunflower overlapping range windows, torch sub-tile→alternate
walk, the 3-kind override tag census). Registry NOT regenerated (wave A
frozen).

Still wave B (documented callbacks): the runtime hook bodies
(`Chest.FindEmptyChest`, `WorldGen.PlantCheck_CanPlaceHook`, the `TE*`
tile-entity hooks). The generated defs carry the C# method NAME in
`PlacementHook::callback` with `hook: None`.

### W4-e11 (2026-11-20): the tile-based GetTileData(Tile) frameY resolution

The d111-researched "open half" of wave B — `TileObjectData.cs:5196-5261` —
is ported as `tileobject::get_tile_data_for_tile` (+ the private
`resolve_from_frames` body split, so synthetic defs can pin branches the
generated table never combines):

* The frame decode (:5212-5221): `num = frameX / CoordinateFullWidth`,
  `num2 = frameY / CoordinateFullHeight`, wrap-0 → 1, horizontal vs vertical
  index, `style = num4 / StyleMultiplier`, `remainder = num4 % StyleMultiplier`.
* The `GetStyleOverride` short-circuit (:5222-5226) with the three arms:
  `GetStyle_Detritus` (:5294-5301, frameY ≥ 36 → SubTiles[0], kind 233),
  `GetStyle_SmallPiles` (:5303-5310, frameY ≥ 18 → SubTiles[0], kind 185),
  `GetStyle_Stalactite` (:5312-5327, frameY ≥ 90/72/36 → SubTiles[2/1/0],
  kind 165). A null sub-tile slot answers None (the C# returns the null
  element); every generated override def carries its slots.
* `StyleLineSkip > 1` re-decodes (:5227-5240); `SubTiles[style]` narrows
  (:5241-5248, null slot keeps the def); the resolved def's alternates answer
  on the inclusive band `[Style, Style + RandomStyleRange]` (:5249-5258).
* Direct consumers ported beside it: `TryGetTileBounds` (:5163-5194 →
  `try_get_tile_bounds` + `TileBounds`) and the tile-based
  `CheckWaterDeath`/`CheckLavaDeath` (:5083-5119 → `check_water_death`/
  `check_lava_death`, resolved-def flags vs the `Main.tile*Death` globals).
  The `Liquid.cs:1190` settlement-kill wiring stays the liquid task's seam;
  `object_tiles_at` keeps its wooden-slice `frame/18 % width` derivation
  (the `WorldGen.Check*` per-type loops it cites — a different C# body).
* **Derived quirk (1:1, not a deviation)**: with `StyleMultiplier = 1` the
  remainder is always 0, so multiplier-1 alternates with `Style > 0`
  (sunflower 20's 3..30 bands, lightbulb 149's 6/12/18) are unreachable from
  frames — they are placement-time only (`TileObject.cs:761-825`, wave B).
  Pinned by the sunflower/lightbulb witnesses.
* Witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN (code-only mode):
  `tests/tileobject_frame_resolution_witness.rs` (10 integration tests over
  real registry defs — stalactite/piles/detritus bands, torch multiplier-6
  sub+alternate walk, closed/open door line-skip, boulder wrap-16, bounds

  (`test_w4_e11_*`: horizontal line-skip — no generated def combines

### W4-d113 (2026-11-20): the TryGetTileBounds coordinate walk

`tileobject::try_get_tile_bounds` ports `TileObjectData.TryGetTileBounds`

  quality particle pass (consume duplicate furniture cells; centre the
  room-check icon). Unported (housing lane); the walk is the ready seam.

### W4-e12 (2026-11-20): the GetTileData(int,int,int) alternate-tail correction

The lane's original scope (the `GetTileData(Tile)` frameY resolution
:5196-5261 + `TryGetTileBounds` :5163-5194) was claimed on the sibling
branches before this one resumed — d112 `resolve_tile_def`, d113 the bounds
walk (resolver-parameterised), e11 `get_tile_data_for_tile` +
`try_get_tile_bounds` + the tile-based death twins, d114 the hook-invocation
consumers (`CallPostPlacementPlayerHook`/`OriginToTopLeft` + the style-indexed
death checks). The duplicate draft in this worktree was deleted (the d113
precedent); the UNCLAIMED remainder is the placement-side int overload's
alternate tail, where the port diverged from the source:

* `TileObjectData.GetTileData(type, style, alternate)` (:5126-5161): C#
  replaces the resolved def ONLY with a non-null in-range alternate entry
  (:5152-5158); a null slot or an index past `Alternates.Count` KEEPS the
  current def (:5159). The port's `get_tile_data` answered `None` on an
  out-of-range index (`alternates.get(alt)?`) — and a unit test pinned that
  wrong answer. Fixed 1:1 (`if let Some(a) = ... { resolved = a; }`); the
  sub-tile narrowing (:5141-5148) still runs FIRST, so an overflow on a
  sub-tile style keeps the SUB-TILE, not the base.
* Reachability: the `CanPlace` alternate loop only passes
  `0..=AlternatesCount` (`TileObject.cs:203-208`), so the divergence never
  bit the placement gates; the exposed consumers are `TileObject.Place`
  (:31, arbitrary `toBePlaced.alternate`) and `DrawPreview` (:859) — an
  overflow alternate previously refused the placement before any world
  write, now it places with the resolved def exactly as C#. No generated
  def combines a base alternate list longer than its sub-tiles' lists
  (census: 0 hits across the 604 defs), so the in-registry behaviour change
  is confined to overflow indices; no RNG, no frame-cache, no determinism
  surface touched.
* Witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN (code-only): the corrected
  `test_get_tile_data_resolution` (overflow keeps the base; a sub-tile with
  no alternates keeps the SUB-TILE) + `test_w4_e12_alternate_overflow_keeps_the_resolved_def`
  (real registry 15/14: in-range replacement pointer identity, overflow
  `2/7/i32::MAX`, negatives/0 skip the list, empty-list table) +
  `test_w4_e12_place_rides_the_alternate_overflow` (chair placement with
  `alternate = 5` runs and is tile-byte-equal to the alternate-0 placement).

## The legacy lighting engine (S1-E-19 wave A, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-core/src/lighting/legacy.rs` ports `Terraria.Graphics.Light.LegacyLighting`
(LegacyLighting.cs, 1442 lines) - the pre-1.2 engine the White/Retro/Trippy modes
select (`Lighting.Mode` setter, `Lighting.cs:45-56`). The port is ADDITIVE: the
modern Color engine (`lighting/mod.rs` + `blur.rs`) is byte-identical - its maths,
RNG draws and the S1-G-10 `NON_VISIBLE_PADDING = 18` are untouched, and
`presenting_legacy_then_modern_recompute_is_byte_identical` proves a LightMap that
served a legacy present recomputes the exact modern result afterwards.

Ported paths (citations in place):
- `ProcessArea` (`:302-369`): the renderCount cycle - pre-render at
  `count > RenderPhases`, swipe passes at counts 0/1/2, the publish at count 2,
  the camera shift + sky reseed at counts 3..phases. `RenderPhases` reads the
  S1-B-6 `GfxQuality::render_phases` field (`Main.cs:17085-17101`).
- `PreRenderPhase` (`:648-849`): working-set clear, the scanner export over the
  expanded rect clamped to `[5, maxTiles-1]`, the mask flags, the lit-cell bound,
  the AddLight dictionary merge, the area snapshots, `renderCount = 0`.
- `DoColors` (`:851-1085`): the blue wave (`0.97..1.0` by `0.0001`), the White
  factors (`neg 0.9 / neg2 0.54 / neg3 0.8`, `wet_r = 0.95*neg*wave`), the
  Retro/Trippy subtractive factors (`0.04/0.16/0.08` + the buff deltas), the
  nightVision/blind/blackout/headcovered arms, and the four swipe-pass bounds.
- The swipes: White `doColors_Mode1_Swipe` (`:1192-1271`, multiplicative carry,
  the `0.0185` cutoff, the neighbour gate, R2-only - no colour bleed), Retro
  `Mode2` (`:1273-1329`, subtractive, no neighbour gate), Trippy `Mode3`
  (`:1331-1435`, per-channel subtractive with the `<= 0` done gate; the
  StopLight subtraction is additive to the channel decay and the B channel has
  no wet arm - both C# quirks kept).
- `CopyFullyProcessedDataOver` (`:538-621`) incl. the inner-guard quirk (the
  condition reads the x delta, the subtraction the y delta, `:583/608`),
  `ShiftUnProcessedDataOver` (`:473-536`, the +/-5-tile jump guard),
  `UpdateLightToSkyColor` (`:435-471`, the unconditional-R quirk at `:459`),
  `Clear` (`:623-646`), `AddLight` (`:258-300`, the 2000 cap, the non-RGB mean
  collapse), `GetColor` (`:211-219`).
- The legacy seed gate is the GLOBAL `(int)Main.worldSurface`
  (`TileLightScanner.cs:92`) and `UnderworldLayer = maxTilesY - 200`
  (`Main.cs:2790`); the legacy mask keeps the C# `!tile.inActive()` conjunct
  (`TileLightScanner.cs:68`) the modern blur mask does not have - an actuated
  block is air to the legacy swipes. The per-type arms reuse the shared
  `tile_light` port.

RNG streams (order exact, seeds pinned - the S1-A-6 precedent):
- `_swipeRandom`: `NextSeed()` after EVERY swipe pass (`:1082`), wet cells draw
  `WithModifier((ulong)(i*1000+j)).Next(98,100)*0.01f` (`:1250-1251`). Vanilla
  seeds it `CreateWithRandomSeed()` (`:1440`, session-nondeterministic); the
  port pins seed 0.
- The legacy engine's own `TileLightScanner._random` advances once per
  PreRenderPhase (`Update()`, `:723`), NOT once per frame like the modern path;
  seeded from the frame's `LightParams.rng_seed` on first use.

Deliberate deviations:
- `FastParallel.For` chunks run as ONE sequential chunk per pass. The C# swipes
  wrap their body in `try/catch` (`:1091/1196/1277/1335`), so an out-of-bounds
  inner index aborts the rest of that thread's chunk; writes never cross outer
  indices, so chunking cannot change cell values - only the abort extent, which
  the single chunk reproduces for the sequential case.
- The minimap light export (`TryUpdatingMapWithLight`, `:371-433`) was not
  ported in wave A - it is the map system's own lighting pass
  (`Main.Map.UpdateLighting`), gated on `mapEnabled && renderCount == 3`.
  **Ported in wave B** (see "The legacy minimap light export (S1-E-19 wave B)"
  below), including the netplay `mapTime = 1` poke (`:341-344`).
- The Wall-of-Flesh `gross` light block (`:678-717`) needs `Main.wofNPCIndex` +
  `Player.gross`, neither ported; the gate is false in the port.
- Mode 0 (`doColors_Mode0_Swipe`, `:1087-1190`) is unreachable through the mode
  selector (Color selects the NEW engine, `Lighting.cs:40-44`); only the Mode
  1/2/3 swipes are ported. The Mode-0 water/honey decay table (`:874-929`) is
  kept in the factor block for completeness.
- `Player.nightVision/blackout/headcovered` are not ported fields; the driver
  passes `false` (the `blind` flag is wired). The factor arms are code-complete.
- The G6 `WorldFrameKey`'s `anim` slot carries `anim_time` in the legacy modes
  (the engine re-publishes every frame); the key's contents are unchanged.

Tests: 12 in `legacy.rs` - the Retro falloff table (hand-derived 0.04 steps +
the 0.16 solid gate), White's multiplicative carry / no-bleed / 0.0185 cutoff /
wet RNG draw, per-mode engine goldens on a fixed 96x96 torch world, cycle
determinism, mode-switch no-leak (`set_mode` + `clear`), the modern-recompute
byte-equality, the AddLight cap/mean-collapse, the actuated-block mask gate,
lava/water decay.

Observations (cave scene, the torch ring right of the centre torch, screen
row at torch height; mean-of-RGB per tile step): Retro's subtractive carry
(в€’0.04/air) out-reaches White's Г—0.9 at distance вЂ” 5..8 tiles out Retro reads
130/101/54/43 vs White 87/47/19/15 and Color 113/56/24/18; Trippy's
per-channel subtraction kills B first (8 tiles out: (36,19,0) вЂ” the RGB
fringe), matching `doColors_Mode3_Swipe`'s independent `<= 0` gates
(`:1331-1435`). White's LIGHT field is grey (the `white_engine_golden`'s
every-cell-grey assertion); the warm cast on lit dirt is the texture's own
colour under grey light вЂ” the no-bleed property is the light, not the tint.
The surface scene shows the engines' different reach: Color leaves the
sealed caves below the surface black, while the legacy engines light cave
pockets through the shafts вЂ” their `OffScreenTiles = 35` working area
(`Lighting.cs:45-56`) vs the modern engine's 28/18 padding carries sunlight
further down; both shapes are the C#'s. No engine defect found вЂ” the modes
render distinctly and match the C# expectations.

**The wave-B harness defect (fixed, not an engine change).** The first shot
matrix came out Color-identical for all four modes: `App::new` seeds
`light_mode` from `TR_LIGHT_MODE` (`mod.rs:3361`), but the boot
`apply_settings()` (`main.rs:199`) then re-read `settings.light_mode`
(the config's Color) and clobbered the pin. Fix: `apply_settings` re-reads
`env::light_mode()` first (the `TR_ZOOM`/`zoom_pinned` precedent), and
`env::light_mode` became a live read (the `TR_SUNDIAL` precedent) so the
settings-screen close path cannot drop a live pin either. Test
`s1_e_19b_light_mode_pin_survives_apply_settings` (settings_ui.rs) pins the
boot order, the repeat-apply and the no-pin config fallback.

**Post-merge re-pin (MERGER-L6, 2026-11-19).** After the sync over main's
S1-G-1 waves (vines/ropes/cracks/pylons), one shot pair per mode was re-taken
on the merged state (Г—2 SHA256-equal each; the recipe above, pristine
`Terrustaria.trwld` copy per run via `TR_WORLD`). The color-surface baseline
stayed byte-equal; the other seven shifted (2.7k-21.7k px). Investigated, not
silent: an A/B build at the pre-vine base `8ab0ede3` reproduces every old
baseline byte-exactly, and the shift bisects to the vine-strip pass
(`934e8242`, S1-G-1 wave A): `draw_tiles` now routes `VineThreads` cells to
the deferred `DrawVines` strip pass (`TileDrawing.cs:429`, `:536-545`), which
lights every segment with its OWN `Lighting.GetColor(x, i)` (`:9081`) - the
old inline draw tinted vine cells through the generic tile path (dimmer,
pre-strip approximation). The bright strips in the new shots are the C#'s
per-segment lighting; the engine behaviour is the landed, cited correction,
so the baselines are re-pinned to the merged state (the SHAs above).
MERGER-L7 re-verified one pair (white surface+cave) after the further sync
over main 5d1bd25c (E-7a/F-7b/F-9c waves): x2 SHA256-equal runs, byte-equal
to the committed baselines and the re-pinned SHAs above вЂ” no further scene
shift from those landings.

## The bestiary cursor and portrait (fix/bestiary-cursor-and-icon, 2026-11-18)

Two bugs: no mouse cursor over the bestiary, and the entity icon showed the
whole animation sheet squashed into one frame-sized box (or spilled the cell).

Cursor: the `bestiary_open` branch of `ui::draw_hud` returned before the
global `cursor::draw` tail. The C# bestiary is a fancy-UI state:
`DrawInterface_12_IngameFancyUI` (`Main.cs:46148-46158`) returns false for
it, stopping the layer loop before layer 36's cursor; `IngameFancyUI.Draw`
draws the cursor itself after the state (`IngameFancyUI.cs:220-223`,
`Main.DrawCursor(Main.DrawThickCursor())`). The fix draws the cursor inside
the bestiary branch before the early return - the same structure.

Icon: `draw_portrait` passed `(frames_x=1, frames_y=1, frame=0)` to
`draw_sheet_frame`, sampling the entire NPC animation strip as one rect.
`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.Draw` (`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.cs:194-207`) draws
`DrawNPCDirect` with the NPC's single `npc.frame`; frame geometry from
`FindFrame`/`SetFrameSize` (`:100-109`, `:185`; the division itself
`NPC.cs:66666`/`:66694` - `frame.Height = tex.Height /
Main.npcFrameCount[type]`, integer data). The fix slices frame 0 of
`frames_y = sheet_h / frame_h` rows (the `.round()` is an inverse
derivation of the integer row count, not a `Math.Round` port) and applies
the 8 px bottom inset / floater centring from `UpdatePosition` (`:112-123`).

The interim `portrait_fit` uniform scale-down stand-in is GONE
(fix/bestiary-per-npc-scale, 2026-11-18): the per-NPC
`NPCID.Sets.NPCBestiaryDrawOffset` table landed as a generated static table
(`tools/gen_bestiary_draw_offsets.py` -> `ui/bestiary_draw_offsets.rs`, 666
rows; sources `NPCID.cs:393-412` merge order + `GetRedigitEntries`
`:414-770`, `GetGroxEntries` `:772-786`, `GetLeinforsEntries` `:788-...`,
struct defaults `:15-42`). `portrait_layout` applies
Scale/PortraitScale/Position/PortraitPositionX-YOverride/Frame per
`UnlockableNPCEntryIcon.cs:52-82` + `UpdatePosition` `:112-123` (floor
included); the 68 px inner box clips via `SpriteRenderer::push_clip`
(`UIBestiaryEntryButton.cs:30-38` `OverflowHidden`, the info-page card the
same per `UIBestiaryNPCEntryPortrait.cs:20-28` with `isPortrait: true`
`:56`). `CustomTexturePath` portraits (`UI/Bestiary/NPCs/NPC_*`, 25 ids)
are packed in `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` and drawn centred per `:197-201`.
`Rotation` rides `push_ui_sprite_rot` about the frame centre
(`DrawNPCDirect`'s centre-origin draw). Remaining approximation: the
`Direction`/`SpriteDirection` horizontal flip (`Main.cs:23123-23127`,
default -1) is not modelled вЂ” the UI pipeline has no flip seam yet; the
`Velocity`-driven hover animation is likewise still frame 0 at rest
(faithful for the idle icon, `Velocity` rows animate only while hovered).

## Save & Exit was a no-op (fix/settings-menu-layout, 2026-11-18)

The Settings menu's Save & Exit row armed `pending = Some(SaveAndExit)` then
called `close()`, which clears `pending` (`ingame_options.rs`); no caller
ever drained it, so the button only closed the window. The C# row
(`IngameOptions.cs:296-305`) does `Close()` + `menuMode = 10` +
`gameMenu = true` + `WorldGen.SaveAndQuit()`; `SaveAndQuit`
(`WorldGen.cs:6701-6719`) plays sound 11, resets the invasion bar
(`:6705-6708`) and queues `SaveAndQuitCallBack` (:6664-6687`:
`Player.SavePlayer` + `WorldFile.SaveWorld` on the `netMode == 0` arm,
sound 10, fast-forward flags cleared, `menuMode = 0`).

The fix wires the row to `App::save_and_quit` (`saveglue.rs`): sound 11 ->
invasion reset -> the existing `save_world` funnel (world + player sidecar +
map + achievements) -> sound 10 -> fast-forward flags -> reopen the main menu
(the `net_disconnect` shape). Deliberate deviation: the C# mode-10 "saving"
screen exists only to cover the ThreadPool async save; the port's synchronous
single-player save has no window to cover, so mode 10 is skipped (documented
in the fn's doc comment, alongside the unmodelled `StopTrackedSounds` /
`ResetFocus` halves covered by the `game_menu` audio listener). The
multiplayer `netMode == 0` gate + force-disconnect arm is out of scope until
the MP pause-menu flow lands. The Settings panel layout deviations remain a
follow-up round.

## The Settings menu layout + dead buttons (fix/settings-menu-layout, round 2)

The window's geometry and several rows were still the port's own invention
after M7-UI-4/4b. This round ports them to the C# constants
(`IngameOptions.cs` unless noted) and wires every row whose backing feature
the port already has.

**Layout corrections (the misplaced panel contents):**

1. **Left pitch** вЂ” `vector5.Y = (480 - 100) / (num7 + 1) = 380 / 8 = 47.5`
   (`:181`, `num7 = 7` without the social invite row). The port divided by
   `LEFT_SLOTS + 1 = 9` (42.2 px), compressing the column and lifting every
   row off its vanilla position. Fixed: `left_pitch() = 380 / LEFT_SLOTS`.
2. **Left hit boxes** вЂ” `DrawLeftSide` hit-tests the *measured string box
   centred on the anchor* (`:1470`); the port's rect started **at** the
   anchor and extended 120 px right, so the left half of every label was
   unclickable and the right half of the column swallowed clicks that
   belong to no row. Fixed: `left_row_rect` measures the DeathText label at
   the row's scale and centres it, with the C#'s int truncations.
3. **Left column font** вЂ” `DrawBorderStringBig` draws **DeathText** with the
   3x3 black ring (`Utils.cs:2520-2536`); the port drew the MouseText font
   with no border. Fixed (`centred_big_text`).
4. **Right labels** вЂ” `DrawBorderStringMeasured` carries ChatManager's
   four-way shadow at `spread = 1.5f` (`Utils.cs:2506`); the port drew flat
   text. The per-row scale multipliers are now ported: zoom 0.85 (`:519`),
   UI scale 0.75 (`:561`), map scale 0.85 (`:766`), lock-on/smart rows 0.9
   (`:1372-1399`).
5. **Value bars** вЂ” the window draws every `DrawValueBar` at `scale = 0.75f`
   (`:116`), not the menu screens' 1.0; the track is 133x12 (int-truncated
   178x16 * 0.75) and its centre is the row anchor's Y **minus 3**
   (`valuePosition.Y -= 3f`, `:417`). The port drew full-size bars centred
   on the raw anchor. Fixed: `sliders::value_bar_rects_at` /
   `draw_value_bar_at` carry the scale; `bar_center_y` the -3.
6. **Hover/lock state machine** вЂ” the C# steps the scales off the *previous*
   frame's hover, keeps the **selected** category's left row at the plateau
   (`(leftHover == j) | flag6`, `:194`), re-arms `rightLock` from the hover
   at the end of every Draw (`:1409-1412`) and gates the bar write on
   `!notBar` (a label/band hover must not drag the bar, `:409-412`). The
   port now models `notBar`, the selected-row plateau, the wide hover band
   (`:427-434`) and the end-of-draw lock re-arm; the bar's value write moved
   from the click to the held-drag tick (`:422-425`), so a click on a bar
   label no longer zeroes the value.
7. **Settings apply** вЂ” the options clicks wrote `App.settings` but never
   ran `apply_settings`, so zoom/lighting/quality changes did not reach the
   renderer (`App.zoom`/`App.light_mode`). Every mutating click and the bar
   drag now apply, like the menu's close does.
8. **The bar drag's held-button source** вЂ” `frame_head` fed
   `pointer.left_held()` (the front-end pointer machine, which only tracks
   the 888 screens' presses) into the window's drag, so in-world the button
   never read as held and the bars could not be dragged at all. The C# reads
   `Main.mouseLeft` вЂ” the physical button, the port's `mine_down`
   (`app/frame.rs`).

**Test-harness fix:** the process-global `LanguageManager` was mutated and
read by tests without a consistent `test_lock` discipline, so a culture
reload in one test could land between another test's registration and its
assertions (bare keys mid-reload) вЂ” the source of the flaky
`s1_e_20_the_hover_name_carries_the_affix_and_the_stack` and options-label
failures. `lang::test_register_source` now loads the shipped sources first
when the manager is empty (a partial fragment could become the *only*
registered file, since `lang::init` early-returns on a non-empty source list)
and documents that the **caller holds `test_lock`** for the whole test (the
lock is not reentrant); the tooltip/buff-tooltip registration tests and
`npc_chat::init_lang` now take the guard.

**Follow-up (fix/ingame-options-culture-flake):** five more
`ui/ingame_options.rs` tests still read the culture without the guard вЂ”
`the_value_bar_geometry_is_the_c_sharp_scaled_track` (the 1045-vs-979 flake:
`color_bar_right_x` shifts 60 px in English but 126 in the long cultures,
`IngameOptions.cs:1071`), `refresh_button_latches_the_hover_and_the_layout`
(`measure_button` reads `Lang.inter[62]`),
`save_and_exit_click_saves_the_world_and_returns_to_the_menu`,
`the_keybinds_row_opens_the_in_game_keybinding_screen` (culture-shifted
`left_row_rect`) and `a_toggle_click_applies_the_setting_to_the_app`
(`right_row_rect`). Under parallel load a sibling's `lang::init`/
`set_language` flipped the culture between their geometry reads and their
assertions. Each now takes the same house guard вЂ” `crate::lang::test_lock()`
acquired **once** at the top of the test (never twice: the mutex is
non-reentrant and a double acquire self-deadlocks the whole gate) plus
`lang::init(GameCulture::English)` to pin the culture for the test's whole
run. The six previously-guarded tests that used a bare
`lang::set_language(English)` were switched to `lang::init(English)` under
the same single guard: on an empty manager `set_language` marks the culture
active **without loading any sources**, and every later `init` then
early-returns in its trailing `set_language` (culture unchanged,
`localization/mod.rs:196-200`), leaving all texts as bare keys for the rest
of the process вЂ” the second half of the flake (only the tests asserting
real key resolution failed; bare-key-vs-bare-key comparisons passed
vacuously, and `--test-threads=1` passed because an `init` test happened to
run first). No game logic or value-bar maths changed вЂ” test synchronization
only.

**Verification.** 11 new unit tests: the left anchors/pitch (47.5) and the

geometry (133x12, the -3 centre, the 60 px colour offset), the per-row draw
scales, the Interface/Controls wiring, the map-scale round trip, the colour
bars' HSL round trips + floors, the new cycles' ladders, the Keybinds
clickв†’screen mapping and the toggle clickв†’`apply_settings` path; the stale
pitch/label expectations were corrected to the C# values.

## The C#-written golden fixture (S1-J-3)

`assets/test/golden.wld` (3666 bytes) and `assets/test/golden.plr` (3840 bytes)
are written by the **real decompiled save path** through
`tools/WldFixtureHarness`: `extract.ps1` slices the save-path method bodies
verbatim out of `decompiled/` (`WorldFile.SetTempToOngoing` +
`SaveWorld_Version2` and every section writer, `WorldFile.cs:1040-1758`;
`Player.Serialize`, `Player.cs:54750+`; `Tile`, `TileEntity.Write` + the
per-kind `WriteExtraData`, the bestiary/creative/town/banner/DD2/spawn/treetops
`Save` bodies, `Item.Serialize`), and `Program.cs` builds the smallest real
world вЂ” a fixed 40x30 tile array, every value a literal, no genRand вЂ” plus a
fresh player. The shims (`Shims/*.cs`) carry only the global statics the bodies
read, at the C# types/defaults; no serialization logic is reimplemented.

**The one substitution:** `DateTime.UtcNow` -> `FixtureClock.UtcNow` (pinned
2026-11-18T00:00:00Z). The vanilla writers stamp the wall clock
(`SaveWorldFlags:1251`, `Player.Serialize:54909`); a reproducible fixture
cannot carry it. Everything else is byte-for-byte the decompiled body. The
importance bitmap is parsed from the real `Main.cs` at runtime (direct
assignments + for-loop ranges + `AddEchoFurnitureTile`), not transcribed.
Regen: `powershell -File tools/WldFixtureHarness/extract.ps1` then
`dotnet run --project tools/WldFixtureHarness -- assets/test`; two runs are
byte-identical.

**Byte-compare result** (`s1_j_3_*` in `wld/mod.rs`, `player_file.rs`):
- The port decodes every section of the fixture (all eleven pointers land
  exactly; the app-side fix-ups keep 2 signs, 11 tile entities, 2 plates).
- Re-write is **byte-identical for sections 2..10** (tiles, chests, signs,
  NPCs, tile entities, pressure plates, town rooms, bestiary, creative powers)
  **and the footer**; the prologue framing + importance bitmap match with the
  pointer table zeroed.
- The header/flags block diverges in **exactly four unowned spots**, pinned
  field-by-field (`s1_j_3_the_header_flags_divergences_are_exactly_the_unowned_fields`):
  the banner kill/claimable counts (`killCount[1]`/`claimable[1]`, no `.wld`
  store), the tree-top variations (`treeTop[0]`, no store) and the world-gen
  manifest JSON (`manifest`, the port writes the empty string). These are
  documented divergences, not faked parity. **S1-J-3b closed the rest** (see
  the next subsection): `CreationTime`, the file-faithful `spawnTileY`, the
  seven ore tiers, the saved-NPC flags, the angler quest index, the
  cultist/Moon Lord/Queen Slime kills, the tower downeds/actives + apocalypse
  phase (with the load-time shield restore) and the party-girl/princess
  spawn unlocks.
- The `.plr` fixture exposed a real reader bug: `FILE_TYPE_PLAYER` was 1
  (`Map`) where `FileType.cs:8` says `Player = 3` вЂ” every real vanilla
  character was rejected with `WrongFileType`. Fixed (read parity); the `.plr`
  writer's own byte parity stays S1-J-5's.
- **S1-J-5c envelope fix**: the harness itself zero-padded the `.plr` with
  `PaddingMode.None` (mirroring the *read* path's `Player.cs:55074`); the
  vanilla *write* path uses the bare `RijndaelManaged`'s default **PKCS7**
  (`:54734-54742`). The harness now encrypts with `PaddingMode.PKCS7` and
  `golden.plr` was regenerated вЂ” same 3840 bytes, the last block now
  decrypts to 3 data bytes + 13 Г— 0x0D. `golden.wld` is unchanged
  (byte-identical regen). The port's writer is byte-identical to the
  regenerated fixture end-to-end (see "The `.plr` legacy-subset shim +
  default policy", increment 3).

## The worldgen parity proof (S1-A-7)

`ROADMAP` S1-A-7 asks for a comparison against a **C#-generated world**, not the
self-consistency replay (`generation_is_reproducible_for_a_seed`). The obstacle is
the deliberate stream divergence (research/35 #5): the port's worldgen draws
**xorshift64** per-pass streams (`Rng(seed ^ fnv(pass_name))`) where vanilla draws
one **Knuth subtractive `UnifiedRandom`** (`WorldGen.genRand => Main.rand`,
`WorldGen.cs:4445`, re-seeded `new UnifiedRandom(worldSeed)` per pass,
`WorldGenerator.cs:497`). A full generated world is therefore **not** byte-comparable
with a C# one by design вЂ” comparing them would only re-prove the known divergence.

**What is provable is the algorithm.** `tools/WorldGenParityHarness` extracts the
verbatim C# `WorldGen.TileRunner` (`WorldGen.cs:76770-77142`) + `PlaceWall`
(`:75125`) + `CanBeClearedDuringGeneration` (`:80168`) with **zero** substitutions
(`extract.py`), shims only the global statics, and runs them in two modes:

- **DIFF** вЂ” `genRand` replays the **port's** xorshift64 stream (state passed in).
  The verbatim C# walker then draws the same sequence as the port's `tile_runner`,
  so the two tile arrays are comparable. The Rust test
  `s1_a_7_the_tile_runner_matches_the_csharp_differential`
  (`worldgen/tile_runner.rs`) replays the same 6-call scenario on a 200Г—400
  all-stone world (ore placement over a protection zoo, a single-step ore disc,
  kind-59 mud with the stone draw + liquid clear, type -2 liquid fill, type -1
  carve, and the mud-wall lining) and compares **all 80 000 tiles field-by-field**
  (kind, wall, liquid, active, slope, half-brick, lava/honey/shimmer) **plus the
  final stream state** against the C# dump (`assets/test/parity_tiles.bin`). The
  initial state is pinned to `Xorshift64::from_seed(42).0` and the final state to
  the harness's `portState`, so a draw-order or algorithm divergence trips the test.
- **REAL** вЂ” `genRand` is the real Knuth `UnifiedRandom(42)`. The `.wld` it writes
  (`assets/test/parity_real.wld`) is a **genuine C#-generated world**. The test
  `s1_a_7_the_csharp_generated_world_decodes_and_rewrites_tiles` (`wld/mod.rs`)
  proves the port decodes every section and re-writes the **tile section
  byte-identical** (the tile codec is stream-independent вЂ” S1-J-3 proved the same
  for the golden fixture).

**Scope / divergences (documented, not faked):**
- The scenario uses only branches the port has ported. Excluded (the port's
  unported arms, `tile_runner.rs` module doc): the 367/368 shell wall placements
  (`WorldGen.cs:76914-76921`), the `case 53` underground-desert containment
  (`GenVars.UndergroundDesertLocation`, `:76934`), and the remix `oceanDepths` lava
  split (`:76899-76905`). The shim's empty `UndergroundDesertLocation` and
  `oceanDepths => false` match the port's deferral exactly.
- `SquareWallFrame` (`:80198`) is a **no-op on both sides** вЂ” a visual wall-framing
  pass the port defers (`place_wall` doc); wall frames are runtime-only and never
  serialized, so the comparison stays on saved fields.
- The **stream** divergence (xorshift64 vs Knuth) is factored out by the DIFF mode
  so the algorithm can be proven; the REAL world is the genuine C# output and is
  **not** claimed byte-equal to the port's generator. Full-world byte parity stays
  open and is A1-gated (it requires moving the passes onto the single Knuth
  `genRand` stream вЂ” S1-K-1's interleave half).

Regen: `python tools/WorldGenParityHarness/extract.py` then
`dotnet run --project tools/WorldGenParityHarness -- assets/test diff 13679457532755275413`
(the DIFF state) and `... real 42` (the REAL world). See the harness README.

## The tile-place sound wave (S1-E-21 wave B, 2026-11-18)

`tr_core::edit::place_tile_sound` ports `WorldGen.PlaceTile`'s tail sound
switch (`WorldGen.cs:60263-60282`): 127 (Actuator) -> SoundID.Item30
(`SoundID.cs:1413`), 314 (minecart track) -> SoundID.Item52 (`:1435`),
330-333 (coin piles) -> the legacy id 18 (Coins), default -> the legacy
id 0 (Dig). None of the special kinds is a `CustomPlace` registration, so
the switch covers the `TileObject` route too (whose C# plays the plain 0:
`Player.PlaceThing_Tiles_PlaceIt` `Player.cs:40124`, `WorldGen.PlaceObject`
`:51441`). `WorldGen.PlaceWall` (`:75141`) plays the 0 as well вЂ”
`place_wall_item` now rides the same faithful play instead of the pinned
`Dig_0`. `Audio::play_place_sound` plays the cue: the Item arms delegate to
wave A's `play_use_sound` (the `SoundEngine.cs:93-99` faГ§ade вЂ” the
`GetRandomPitch` NextFloat on the audio-only `sound_style_random`, the
case-2 `Main.rand.Next(-6,7)*0.01` pitch after the gate, style 52's Г—0.35
volume `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:567-569`); the int arms (`SoundEngine.cs:102`
вЂ” no `GetRandomPitch` draw) play Coins with no draws (case 18 `:865-869`)
or the case-0 Dig (`:440-452`): `Main.rand.Next(3)` picks Dig_0/1/2, then
`Next(-10,11)*0.01` sets the pitch вЂ” both draws ride the caller's
`UpdatePlayers` stream (placement runs from `Player.ItemCheck` under the
`Main.cs:17754` swap, the `break_tile` precedent) and only AFTER the
attenuation gate passed. `Item_30` joins the bank. Deviations: the
`SoundInstanceDig` stop/re-create pool is the standing D4 (fresh source per
play); the wire/actuator placement feedback (`wire_placed_feedback`,
`WorldGen.PlaceWire*` `:58115` etc.) keeps its pinned `Dig_1` вЂ” the wiring
wave is a follow-up. Tests `s1_e_21b_the_placement_cue_follows_the_tile_type`,
`s1_e_21b_the_dig_variation_draws_ride_the_passed_stream`.


## The pylon/trophy/void-lens passes (S1-G-1 wave D, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/pylons.rs` ports three of
`TileDrawing.PostDrawTiles(solidLayer: false)`'s deferred families
(`TileDrawing.cs:414-434`, draw order `:423-425`): `DrawTeleportationPylons`
(`:8639-8706`), `DrawMasterTrophies` (`:8597-8637`) and `DrawVoidLenses`
(`:8708-8736` + `VoidLensHelper.cs:11-105`). The collectors take the special
point's tile coords (the classification switch's gates, `:695-712`: pylon 597
`frameX % 54 == 0 && frameY == 0`, trophy 617 `frameX % 54 == 0 && frameY % 72
== 0`, lens 491 `frameX == 18 && frameY == 18`) and produce world-pixel sprite
records; the hook scans the view rect row-major and pushes them into the
always-rebuilt world-effect range. The colour math is XNA `Color` semantics вЂ”
every `Lerp`/`operator*` step truncates to bytes (`scale_bytes`/`lerp_bytes`),
including the alpha (`value3 * 0.7f` scales A 255 -> 178); the tests pin the
per-step truncation (`s1_g_1d_the_byte_math_truncates_per_step`). The lens's
`Lighting.AddLight(position, 0.4, 0.2, 0.9)` (`VoidLensHelper.cs:36`) lands in
the shared `EntityLights` pair behind `!Main.gamePaused`
(`TileDrawing.cs:8717-8720`), so the engine reads it one frame late like the
item/NPC feeds.

Deliberate deviations:

* **Z-order + range.** In the vanilla the three passes draw between the
  non-solid and solid tile layers (`Main.cs:63374` -> `PostDrawTiles`), inside
  the tile render targets. The port's fused tile pass has no layer seam, so
  the sprites ride the screen-space fx range (like the leaf gores) after the
  cached world range вЂ” the same documented z-order approximation the inline
  grass sway uses (`tiles.rs`). This keeps the G6 `WorldFrameKey` and the
  cached range untouched; the sprites animate per frame in the always-rebuilt
  range instead.
* **Dust rolls skipped.** `TeleportPylonsSystem.SpawnInWorldDust`
  (`TileDrawing.cs:8669-8673`, two `_rand.Next` draws) and
  `VoidLensHelper.SpawnVoidLensDust` (`VoidLensHelper.cs:40-75`, `Main.rand`)
  belong to the unported particle pass. Skipping them wholesale leaves both
  RNG streams untouched (the `entity_lights.rs` rule).
* **Frame counters.** `Main.tileFrameCounter[597]` wraps at 64 and `[491]` at
  40 (`Main.cs:19284-19287`/`:19227-19230`, `AnimateTiles`); the animator is
  unported (`drawdata.rs`'s `tile_frame в‰Ў 0`), so the pass stands them in with
  `game_update_count % 64` / `% 40` вЂ” same cadence and wrap, phase anchored at
  world load.
* **Smart cursor.** The selection-glow arms are ported
  (`Colors.GetSelectionGlowColor`, `Colors.cs:89-92`, integer halves/thirds;
  the pylon's column-2 mask and the lens's `Extra_93`), but
  `Main.InSmartCursorHighlightArea` is unported вЂ” the hook feeds
  `selection_mode = 0`.
* **Registry.** The `_specialPositions` deferred registry is not ported; the
  hook re-scans the view rect (the collection order is row-major, matching
  `Draw`'s loop). The pylon/trophy visibility gate reads the bottom-right cell
  `(x+1, y+1)` through `IsVisible` (`:1411-1432`) exactly, including the
  Echo-coating flag (`World::invisible_block`) and `TR_SHOW_INVISIBLE`.

Sheets: `Extra_181` (pylon, 14x8 frames), `Extra_198` (trophy, 1x28),
`Extra_93` (lens selection mask) join `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES`; `Projectile_734`
(the lens sprite, 1x8) is packed outside `spawnable_kinds`
(`VoidLensHelper.cs:79-80` loads it directly). Tests: 8 `s1_g_1d_*` per-pass
tests in `render/pylons.rs` (gates, bob/ring geometry, byte colours, flip,
lens frame cadence, light anchor, selection tints).

## The tile-crack overlay (S1-G-1 wave C, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/tile_cracks.rs` ports `Main.DrawTileCracks`
(`Main.cs:61533-61626`) 1:1: the book-type filter + the `<20` damage floor
(`:61543-61551`), `WorldGen.InWorld` fluff-0 (`WorldGen.cs:9688-9695`), the
active-block/wall visibility arms (`:61558-61566`), the door/solid/solid-top/
tree/glowing-mushroom shape classification (`:61571-61598`, the 22 px tree
frame windows verbatim), the slope/half-brick skip (`:61599`), the
20/40/60/80 damage ladder (`:61601-61617`), the `crackStyle*18` /
`(4+crackStyle/2)*18` source rects on the 18 px grid (`:61618-61622`) and the
`Lighting.GetColor` tint at `x*16-(int)screenPosition.X` (`:61623`). The draw
sites are `TileDrawing.cs:732-733` (`hitReplace` then `hitTile`, crack type 1)
and `WallDrawing.cs:203-204` (crack type 2). The `TileCracks` sheet joins the
static atlas loads (`assets.rs`, the `WiresNew`/`Actuator` seam) вЂ” one atlas,
one pipeline, unchanged.

Deviations (deliberate):
- **Single-accumulator projection.** The C# keeps 500-entry `hitTile` /
  `hitReplace` books with per-hit `AddDamage` steps and 60-tick TTL decay
  (`HitTile.cs`). The port's mining is one `mine_target` + `mine_timer`
  accumulator (`world_sim/editing.rs`); `mining_crack_record` maps it linearly
  onto the C# 0..100 damage (`mine_timer / mine_hardness * 100`, truncated
  like the int accumulator). At most one crack draws at a time; `hitReplace`
  draws nothing until replacement mining lands. The wall arm already emits
  `CRACK_WALL` records when the mined cell has no active block.
- **World-seeded crack style.** `HitTileObject.Clear` rolls
  `rand.Next(4)` re-rolled against the static `lastCrack` (`HitTile.cs:40-45`)
  from a `DateTime.Now.Ticks`-seeded stream. The port keeps the roll + the
  no-repeat loop verbatim but seeds `App.mine_crack_rng` with the world seed
  (the determinism rule, same deviation class as `NamedRngs::global`). The
  roll fires once per dig target (the C# rolls on slot reuse).
- **Invisible-block conjuncts vacuous.** `ShouldShowInvisibleBlocksAndWalls`
  (`Main.cs:58023-58030`) reads the echo monolith / `CanSeeInvisibleBlocks`;
  neither exists in the port and `Tile` carries no invisible bits, so the
  `(flag || !invisibleвЂ¦)` conjuncts are always true.
- **Draw site.** The C# draws inside the solid tile layer; the port hooks the
  per-frame world range right after the cached tile pass (`frame/draw.rs`) вЂ”
  the damage timer advances every frame, so the crack cannot ride the
  G6-cached range. The `WorldFrameKey` is untouched; the existing tile draw
  order and framing are unchanged.
- The C#'s `type == 72` arm (`:61591`) is kept verbatim but unreachable: 72 is
  in `TileID.Sets.IsATreeTrunk` (bits 71-77), so the tree arm claims it first.

Tests: `s1_g_1c_*` (7) вЂ” the damage ladder, the 18 px rects + tree column
shift, the shape classification (incl. every tree exclusion window), the
no-repeat style roll + seed determinism, the timerв†’damage projection, the
full per-record draw-gate walk (`crack_draw_plan`) and the hook's one-record
projection.

## The combat accessory dedupe/wiring (S1-C-12 wave E, 2026-11-19, code-only)

Wave B landed `accessory_combat.rs` UNWIRED while wave A's
`apply_equip_functional` carried verbatim INLINE arms for ten of the family's
kinds — naively calling the hook would DOUBLE-GRANT. Wave E dedupes to a
single grant path per row (code-only mode — no compiler invoked; tests
written, not run):

1. **Per-slot family**: `apply_equip_functional` now calls
   `accessory_combat::apply_combat_accessory(kind, self)` FIRST and returns
   when it claims the kind; the ten inline arms (489/490/491/2998/935/897/
   936/1343/1301/3015) are DELETED from the match. The C# rows are
   independent per-type `if`s (`Player.cs:14368-15450`), and the family
   kinds are disjoint from every remaining match arm, so claiming before
   the match is order-identical. The family gains what the inline arms
   missed: `kbGlove = true` on 897/936/1343 (`:15301/:15371/:15308`) and
   the two previously-absent kinds 3992 (Berserker's Glove, `:14411-14417`)
   and 3016 (Flesh Knuckles, aggro-only, `:14647-14650`).
2. **Wave-B parity fix found by the wave-E re-read**: the module's
   Berserker's Glove arm copied the Mechanical Glove's `meleeDamage +=
   0.12f` — the C# switch arm `:14411-14417` has NO meleeDamage row
   (kbGlove/autoReuseGlove/meleeScaleGlove/meleeSpeed/aggro only). Removed;
   the module test now pins `melee_damage == 1.0` for 3992.
3. **Sky-stone bundle**: the inline flag scan + stat fold in `player.rs`
   are replaced by `accessory_combat::set_sky_stone_flag` /
   `apply_sky_stone_effects` (ONE path). The fold now includes the C#
   `minionKB += 0.5f` (`:13002`) the inline copy omitted; its `lifeRegen
   += 2` half (`:12991`) keeps riding the existing `accessory_life_regen`
   fold. Flag timing is unchanged (scan before `update_equips`, fold at
   the same site).
4. **Per-tick clears the wired grants need** (without them the new rows
   would accumulate/stick): `minion_kb = 0.0` (`ResetEffects`
   `Player.cs:18347`) and `kb_glove = false` (`:18709`) added beside the
   crit-base resets in `player.rs`. `minion_kb` had NO reset before
   (only spawn-zeroed); no live producer existed until this wave — the
   field's consumer is the summon tooltip's knockback line
   (`ui/tooltip.rs:344`, `Main.cs:20749-20798`); `buff_effects_misc.rs`'s
   minion_kb is its own effect struct, not this field.
   `autoReuseGlove`/`meleeScaleGlove` (`:18710-18711`) still have no port
   fields.
5. **Naming fix**: the `player.rs` test comment calling 1301 "Necromantic
   Scroll" is corrected — 1301 is `ItemID.DestroyerEmblem`
   (`ItemID.cs:4285`); the Necromantic Scroll is 1845 (`:5373`).

Dedupe proof (tests-as-code): `player.rs::
each_combat_accessory_grants_exactly_once_through_the_wired_seam` pins the
FULL row set (4 damage classes, 3 crits, melee-speed bonus, kbGlove) for
each of the 12 family kinds through a real `Player::update` tick, re-ticks
(a second grant path would drift tick 2), unequips (the per-tick clears
end the grant) and stacks two slots of the same emblem (1.30 = per-slot,
not double). `the_sky_stone_bundle_grants_once_including_minion_knockback`
pins the bundle once per tick incl. `minion_kb == 0.5`, stone+emblem
together, and the unequip decay. The module's 10 wave-B tests stay green
with the 3992 correction. Deliberate deltas vs the pre-wave-E port: 3992
no longer grants +12% melee (C# parity fix), the gloves now arm `kbGlove`
(the tooltip's melee-knockback line, `ui/tooltip.rs:330`), the bundle adds
`minion_kb 0.5` — all three are moves TOWARD the C#, not deviations. The
standing documented-skipped halves are unchanged (aggro/autoReuseGlove/
meleeScaleGlove/magmaStone; the minion emblems' `minionKB += 2f`
`:15317/:15322` still has no live consumer and stays with the inline
1167/1864 arms, outside the combat family). No RNG rides any arm; the
fixed-step order is untouched.

## The vine strip pass (S1-G-1 wave A, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/render/vines.rs` ports `TileDrawing.DrawVines` /
`DrawVineStrip` (`TileDrawing.cs:8890-8901`, `:9034-9132`) plus the root crawl
`CrawlToTopOfVineAndAddSpecialPoint` (`:744-762`) and its attachment probe
`WorldGen.BottomEdgeCanBeAttachedTo` (`WorldGen.cs:70440-70458`, now
`tr_core::torch::bottom_edge_can_be_attached_to` - note the C# bottom edge has
NO half-brick check, unlike the top edge). The vine cells (52/62/115/205/382/
528/636/638, `TileID.Sets.VineThreads` `TileID.cs:544`) are skipped inline in
the row-major pass exactly like the C# draw-area switch (`:536-545`); the
roots are collected in draw-area row-major order, deduplicated like
`_vineRootsPositions`, and the strips draw right after the foliage pass - the
C# `PostDrawTiles` order `DrawTrees` -> `DrawVines` (`:428-429`). The strip
maths is term-for-term: the unclamped `Lerp(0.2, 1, |wind|/1.2)` factor, the
`-0.08*num3` rotation ladder (+0.0025 at num2>=2, +0.0075*num3 at num2>=5,
the wall probe incrementing num2 BEFORE the rotation), the remix-flipped
surface gate, the `GetWindGridPush(x, i, 20, 0.01)` subtract/-0.78-bounce
accumulator, the `(rot + PI/2).ToRotationVector2()*16` anchor walk, the
`(tileWidth/2, halfBrickHeight - tileTop)` origin and the case-638
`GlowMask[327]` glowmask (`Color.Lerp(White, tileLight, 0.75)`, `:6080-6084`,
sheet now packed). `_vineWindCounter` (`:375`) rides the sunflower's 60 Hz
step. The G6 key mixes the vine counter into the existing windy-anim slot and
adds the `WindGrid` clock ONLY when a vine thread is in the view rect (the
push decays on the grid clock even in calm air; vine-free worlds keep the
old cache behaviour bit-for-bit).

Deliberate deviations:
- The `NextNatureRenderer` LitNature dawn/dusk shader
  (`NextNatureRenderer.cs:71-145`) is not ported - segments draw plain, like
  its `DrawWithoutShader` arm (`:111-119`); the `seam_bottom` flag is computed
  and carried for that future port. Same standing deviation as the tree
  canopies' nature draw.
- The `biomeSight` recolour + its `Dust.NewDust` roll (`:9089-9115`) are
  skipped: the port has no biome sight, and adding the roll would change the
  draw RNG stream order.
- The strip applies NO `GetFinalLight` actuation ghost (the C# reads
  `Lighting.GetColor` raw, `:9081`); fullbright -> White is ported (`:9084`).
- The reverse-vine (549, `DrawRisingVineStrip` `:9134-9193`) pass landed with
  W4-g83 and is WIRED into the fused pass (below, the wiring phase); the
  multi-tile vine (`DrawMultiTileVines` `:8829-8888`) pass is the furniture
  lane (d57) and stays out — its cells keep the old inline draw.
- The dark-cell merge still covers unlit vine cells (the port's black-quad
  coverage shape); the C# `DrawBlackHelper` runs inside `DrawSingleTile`,
  which the vine cells never reach - a documented z-order/coverage
  approximation of the fused pass, unchanged by this wave.

Tests: `s1_g_1a_*` (10, `render/vines.rs`) - the root crawl + dedup, the
platform/no-attach/bottom-slope/half-brick attachment gates, the calm straight
hang, the sway ladder + anchor walk, the blocking-wall freeze, the remix

(`e2dc1fcf`, `:11406-12012`), d73 (`7cf886f9`, `:10328-10485` + `:9935-9946`)
and d74 (`dc654c62`, `:10318-10808`) claims (the full table + per-piece
live-owner evidence: `docs/research/28f-wave-f-claim.md`). Per the
"genuinely unclaimed" rule this wave re-ports NO arm id; it ports the
**`UpdateBuffs` FRAME** — the statements around the arm chain no wave's
range includes — as `crates/tr-app/src/buff_effects_frame.rs`
(`run_buff_frame` → `FrameEffects` + `FrameState`), the wave-B seam
pattern. Deliberate deviations:

- **Wiring deferred**: the module is test-only until the waves' merge

  change, no RNG or fixed-step-order change. `player.rs` untouched.
- **The loop preamble is witness-only**: the slot skip + the
  `TimeLeftDoesNotDecrease` decrement (`:9865-9874`) is already live
  (`buffs.rs::update_buffs_tick`); the `s1_e_7f_preamble_*` test pins it,
  no second copy.
- **The hunger ladder is keep-one**: `potions.rs::update_hunger_buffs`
  (the drink path's helper) split into the slot-level
  `update_hunger_buffs_slots` — the frame's per-tick call site
  (`:12046`, the missing half: hunger tiers never expired on their own)
  runs the SAME ladder, no second copy of the expiry logic. The
  emote/sound halves the potions port deferred are REQUESTS here
  (`emotes: Vec<i32>` 146/147/148 in C# order, `hungry_sounds` count for

## The vine draw residuals (W4-g83, 2026-11-21)

The four unclaimed vine-family residual groups left after the S1-G-1a hanging
strip + the d56 animated-tile draw gate: the **vine-tip variants** (the rising
seaweed strip + its tip-frame columns), the **jungle thorns** (the underground
grow arm + the down-merge frame), the **glowing mushroom vines** (the 528
conversion/grow arms) and the **grow-tops** (the overground vine grow chain).
All UNWIRED code-only — the natural seams are contested by in-flight siblings
(`tiles.rs`/`draw.rs` d56-d60, `framing.rs` d109/d110/g48, `growth.rs`
d102/d106/g42, `drawdata.rs` d62/g34/g79); the ports land in unclaimed modules
and the wiring is the family's merge step. No RNG stream, frame-cache key or
fixed-step order changes until wired.

### Phase 1 — the rising-vine draw pass (`render/vines.rs`)

`draw_reverse_vines` / `rising_vine_strip_segments` / `collect_reverse_vine_root`
port `DrawReverseVines` (`TileDrawing.cs:8903-8914`), `DrawRisingVineStrip`
(`:9134-9193`) and `CrawlToBottomOfReverseVineAndAddSpecialPoint` (`:764-782`).
Verbatim differences from the hanging strip, each pinned by a witness:
- the anchor starts `(x*16+8, startY*16+16+2)` (`:9138`, +16+2 not -2) and
  walks UP along `(rot - PI/2)` (`:9190`, not `+ PI/2`);
- the walk runs `num7 > 10` descending (`:9144`, not `< maxTilesY-10`);
- the exposure gate has NO remix arm — always `num7 < worldSurface` (`:9163`);
- the grid push is `GetWindGridPush(x, num7, 40, -0.004)` (`:9167`, the
  40-window / negative force, not 20 / 0.01);
- the rotation negates the ladder: `num2 * (0 - num4) * cycle` (`:9179`);
- the origin pivots at the sprite's BOTTOM-centre
  `(tileWidth/2, halfBrickHeight - tileTop + tileHeight)` (`:9188`);
- NO glowmask: `:9173` discards the glow out-params (`out var _`).
The reverse crawl starts AT `j` (`:767`, not `j-1`) and roots at `k-1` (the row
ABOVE the attachable floor); `torch::top_edge_can_be_attached_to` is lifted to
`pub` (identical to g28/g30 — keep-one at merge). The `ReverseVineThreads` set
is `{549}` alone (`TileID.cs:545`). 10 `w4_g83_*` witnesses written not run.

### Phase 2 — the vine lifecycle checks (`tr-core::vine_checks`)

`check_vines` ports `WorldGen.CheckVines` (`WorldGen.cs:84858-84960`): the
eight-family LAST-write-wins type-conversion ladder (ash 638, mushroom 528,
hallow 115, jungle 62, corrupt 636, crimson 205, plain 52 [excluded for 382],
flower 382 — `:84883-84914`) reads the `nactive && !bottomSlope` support above;
a mismatch converts the cell + `SquareTileFrame`, otherwise the per-type
support gates kill an unsupported vine (`:84921-84958`). The glowing-mushroom
arm (70/528 → 528) is the `num4` flag. `can_underwater_plant_grow_here`
(`:58542-58576`) + `check_underwater_plant` (`:58578-58627`) port the seaweed
validity (50-border, three full-water cells, sand/same-type support, the
0/63-69/80-81 wall whitelist) and the TIP-FRAME variants — `frameX` column 0
(lone), 1-7 (a 549 above, `Next(1,8)*18`) or 7-12 (a 549 below,
`Next(7,13)*18`), `frameY = 0`. These columns are the rising strip's
per-segment source frames (`DrawRisingVineStrip` `:9173`). 16 witnesses.

### Phase 3 — the grow-tops + jungle thorns (`tr-core::vine_growth`)

`grow_overground_vines` ports `UpdateWorld_OvergroundTile`'s vine chain
(`WorldGen.cs:72506-72802`): the plain/flower 2/52/382/192 arm (the wall
68/65/66/63 + below-wall + remix `Next(5)` flower pick, `:72516-72535`; the
`num24` budget `:72508-72512` is dead in the C# and not carried), then the
jungle 60/62/384/226 (the `TooManyJungleVinesNearby` gate on 226), mushroom
70/528, hallow 109/115, corrupt 23/661/636, crimson 199/662/205 and ash
633/638 arms — each behind the free-below gate, the 10-row grass look-up and
`grow_more_vines`' density (`:45586-45621`, the 60 budget ÷5 on a 528 source,
the LOS-weighted `(j-y)*2`/`*20` accumulation). `too_many_jungle_vines_nearby`
(`:73189-73212`) is the ±9×±5 clamped box counting active 62, true strictly
above the cap (default 6). `grow_underground_jungle_thorn` (`:73658-73661`)
is the underground dispatcher's 69 arm — `GrowSpike(69, 60)` with NO roll; the
port's overground 69 arm (`growth.rs:843`) sits inside `grass_pass`, which 69
is not a member of, so it never fires — the genuine arm is the underground
one. `thorn_down_merge_frame` (`:82043-82066`) ports the thorn down-merge:
cases 32/352/69/655 fold a matching grass neighbour BELOW into the thorn
(`down = num`) before the generic block frameset — these are direct `down=num`
assignments, NOT `TileMergeAttempt` calls, so `tools/GenTileData`'s merge

BEFORE the merge (`:81632-81700` precedes `:82043`), so a sloped grass-below
cell does not merge. The generic frameset (`framing.rs::RULES`) is re-ported
verbatim (the table is private to the contested `framing.rs`). 16 witnesses.

`NetMessage.SendData`/`SendTileSquare` sides are MP scope; `SquareTileFrame`
rides `edit::square_tile_frame_default`; `CopyPaintAndCoating` copies `meta` +

biomeSight dust stay the standing S1-G-1a deviations. The multi-tile vine
(`DrawMultiTileVines(:InWind)`) is the furniture lane (d57), out of scope.

The MANA-POTION / ARMOR-SET tier block (`Player.cs:10318-10461`, 20 ids:

`:10486-10972` — disjoint by C# line). Shape: the simple arms (94, 396) fold

wave-B seam); the set-tier arms read AND write the whole buff bar, so they
ride the slot-ordered `update_potion_set_buff_arms` driver over
`&mut BuffSlots` + the accumulator with the C# `DelBuff(j); j--` rescan (the
`update_summon_buff_arms` convention). Deliberate notes:

* **Code-only, test-only until the merge**: no `player.rs` code, no live-tick
  wiring. The wiring step copies `latest_mana_potion_*` into
  `PotionEffectContext`, runs the driver AFTER `update_buffs_tick` (the driver
  does not decrement — the `:9871-9874` tick already ran), then folds the
  accumulator: `mana_heat +=`, the stat adds `+=`, the orb/shield/level fields

  (`:10320-10323`) is constants-off, same as the potions module.

  accumulator records it as `mana_potion_duration_floored` for the wiring.
* **The double-delete path is unreachable in retail play** (the downgrade
  branch AND the set-flag-off branch on one slot would drive the C# `j`

  set flag is on, the two beetle flags are mutually exclusive (one
  chestpiece), and the off-family buff is purged on the first tick after an

  `base..=base+num-1`, and `buffType[j] == base+num-1`): after the walk the

## The NPC aiStyle dispatch axis (S1-D-2, 2026-11-18)

The C# dispatches NPC AI on `aiStyle` first (`NPC.AI`, `NPC.cs:19819-41132`:
the `if (this.aiStyle == N)` chain of 128 arms), then on `this.type` inside
the family arm. The port dispatched on `NpcKind` alone (research/25 finding
9, research/39 rank 9) - a style could not be ported once for all its kinds.

**The seam.** `NpcKind::ai_style()` (`npc.rs`) is the first axis: a 199-row
table mapping every ported kind to its vanilla `SetDefaults` aiStyle, each
group cited to the `this.aiStyle = N;` lines (extracted mechanically from
the decompile - the compound `this.type` conditions evaluated per id, not
copied from the doc comments). `update_rng` now runs
`match self.kind.ai_style()`: a claimed style enters its family arm, every
other style falls through to `update_kind_ai` - the pre-axis `match
self.kind`, moved verbatim (no arm reordering, no body edits). The buff
block, `find_frame` and `contact` keep their exact positions around the
dispatch, so the fixed-step order and every RNG draw are unchanged.

**The first migrated family: aiStyle 5** (`AI_005_EaterOfSouls`,
`NPC.cs:20802-20806` -> `:50244-50700`). `ai_005_hover_family` carries the
four ported style-5 kinds - the Eater of Souls (6), the Hornet (42), the
Meteor Head (23) and the Servant of Cthulhu (5, its own type-5 branch from
S1-D-3k) - calling the same `update_hover`/servant machines with the same
params as the old kind arms. The old kind-match arms for these four are
`unreachable!` markers (the axis claims style 5 first); D-3 rounds shrink
`update_kind_ai` the same way, one family per round. No new arms ported.

**Proof.** `s1_d_2_tests::s1_d_2_the_style_axis_keeps_the_hover_behaviour`
runs all four kinds 300 ticks through the axis vs the verbatim pre-axis
arm bodies on cloned state with identical RNG seeds and asserts bit-equal
x/y/vx/vy/frame/frame_counter/rotation/sprite_dir/facing/on_ground and
player hp every tick.
`s1_d_2_the_ai_style_table_matches_the_csharp_set_defaults` pins 86
representative rows against the C# (the full 199-row table is cited
in-place). The world-hash pins and the existing NPC AI tests pass
unchanged (`cargo test --workspace -- --skip migrates_version_2_kinds_to_item_ids`).

**Known doc-vs-C# drift surfaced by the extraction** (the table follows the
C#, not the comments): the Retinazer's SetDefaults row is aiStyle 30
(`NPC.cs:10526`) and the Spazmatism's 31 (`:10543`) - the S1-D-3i work
labelled them 57/3; the port's machines are unchanged this round (behaviour
frozen), the style ids now carry the C#'s rows. Same for the Golem family
(the body 45 `:12167`, the attached head 46 `:12184`, the fists 47
`:12198`, the free head 48 `:12212`), the Wall of Flesh (27,
`:10347`) and the Moon Lord core/head (77/79, `:14127`/`:14089`).
