## The Plantera hook-centroid anchor (S1-D-3-plantera-minions, rescoped, code-only mode, 2026-11-18)

**Rescope (Lead coordination note):** the three minion machines were
already ported by sibling branches while this task ran вЂ” kind 263
PlanterasHook (aiStyle 52) in `npc_ai_style52.rs` (commit 61e1bd5c,
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle52`), kind 264 PlanterasTentacle (aiStyle 53) in
`npc_ai_style53.rs` (89a9b808, `task/S1-D-3-aistyle53`), kind 265 Spore
(+261 FungiSpore, aiStyle 50) in `npc_ai_style50.rs` (613aac92,
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle50`). The duplicated machines written here were
REMOVED; the only remaining gap was the boss's leash-anchor
computation вЂ” none of the four modules computes it (the boss core
`npc_ai_plantera.rs`, ba8159fc `task/S1-D-3-plantera-audit`, only
RECEIVES `hook_anchor: (f32, f32)`; its sim currently passes Plantera's
own centre). This task delivers exactly that seam.

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_plantera_anchor.rs` ports `NPC.cs:31743-31762`
(the anchor block inside the aiStyle-51 boss arm) as pure fns over the
NPC pool:

- `hook_centroid(npcs, type_of) -> Option<(f32, f32)>` вЂ” walk the slots
  in order (`:31747`), take the first three live aiStyle-52 hooks
  (`:31749`, the `num745 > 2` break `:31755-31758`), sum their
  `Npc::center()`s as f32 in slot order (`:31751-31752`), divide by the
  count (`:31761-31762`). aiStyle 52 has ONE member вЂ” 263
  (`ID/NPCID.cs:11203`, `SetDefaults :12402`) вЂ” so the filter rides the
  caller's `type_of` closure, the SAME convention `npc_ai_style52.rs`
  uses for its `:32129` same-type scan.
- `hook_anchor(npcs, type_of, boss) -> (f32, f32)` вЂ” the merge-union
  call site: the centroid when hooks live, the boss centre otherwise.

Faithful details: `Center` is `Entity.Center`'s FLOAT width/2
(`Entity.cs:50-55`, the port's `Npc::center()`) вЂ” NOT the tentacle
anchor's integer-width centre (`:32301-32302`); the sums accumulate in
slot order before the divide; `array2` (`:31743`/`:31753`) is a DEAD
store (written, never read anywhere in the arm вЂ” verified) and is not
ported; the block draws NO RNG.

Deliberate deviations:

- **`NPC.active` в†’ `hp > 0`** вЂ” the pool's live-slot convention, the
  same reading `npc_ai_style52.rs` uses for the boss slot
  (`:32080-32085`); absent slots do not exist in the dense pool.
- **Zero hooks в†’ `None` + boss-centre fallback**: the C# divides by a
  zero count в†’ NaN (`:31761-31762`) and the leash reads NaN; the port
  returns `None` and `hook_anchor` falls back to Plantera's own centre
  вЂ” the sibling boss module's documented stand-in until hooks spawn.
- **WIRED at the union (2026-11-19, merger P5)**: the sim's pre-pass
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs`, before the tick closure вЂ” the carrier pre-pass
  precedent) computes `hook_centroid(&app.npcs, type_of)` per live
  Plantera and stores it on the new `Npc::plantera_hook_anchor:
  Option<(f32, f32)>` field; `update_plantera` consumes it with
  `unwrap_or_else(|| self.center())`. `type_of` reads `kind.to_u16()`
  (no NpcKind maps to 263 yet), so the centroid stays `None` вЂ” the
  wiring is live, the boss-centre stand-in persists until the hook
  kind lands with `npc_ai_style52`. The module-level
  `#![allow(dead_code)]` is removed (`hook_centroid` is live; the
  `hook_anchor` convenience wrapper keeps a fn-level allow вЂ” the sim
  stores the Option, the fallback lives in `update_plantera`). The
  pre-pass scans the pool once per tick vs the C#'s inside-the-AI scan:
  same tick's positions either way (the boss's own movement integrates
  after the AI), recorded as the port's pre-pass convention.

**THE MERGE UNION (four modules, no file overlap).** At merge, the
sim's kind-262 dispatch replaces the centre fallback with
`hook_anchor(&app.npcs, type_of, boss)` and passes the result into
`npc_ai_plantera::step`'s `hook_anchor` parameter. No edit to any of the
four sibling modules (`npc_ai_plantera.rs`, `npc_ai_style52.rs`,
`npc_ai_style53.rs`, `npc_ai_style50.rs`) is needed вЂ” this module is
new and disjoint. The sibling branches are NOT merged to main yet
(verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for all four); the union rides
their merge order, and this branch touches none of their files.

## The Golem head's aiStyle-46 machine (S1-D-3, UNWIRED, code-only mode, 2026-11-18)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style46.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s aiStyle-46 arm
(`NPC.cs:31129-31346`) вЂ” the attached Golem head (246), the arm's only user

cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests); the 13 witness tests are written, not run.

**UNWIRED** (the aiStyle-42 / `8ac80b4e` precedent): the live head still rides
the stand-in inside `update_golem`'s `NpcKind::GolemHead` arm (`npc.rs`). The
sibling aiStyle-45/47/48 rounds are rewriting that same function and the
findframe rounds FindFrame case 246, so this round touches neither. The merge
step: (1) the kind arm calls `golem_head_step` (or the axis claims `46 =>` and
the kind arm becomes unreachable, the `ef07892e` shape), (2) FindFrame case
246 reads `local_ai[0]` instead of re-deriving the mouth window, (3)
GOLEM_EYE_BEAM joins the `timeLeft = 300` list at the shot drain
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`, `NPC.cs:31307`/`:31333` вЂ” the style-48 free head's
`:31568` beams share the row).

The stand-in's defects the port fixes (all witnessed):

- **Tether**: the stand-in accelerates toward the dock and clamps В±7; the C#
  writes velocity DIRECTLY вЂ” inside 100 the raw delta (a snap, rotation 0),
  outside normalized to exactly 100 with `rotation = velocity.X * 0.1f`
  (`:31146-31164`). The dock is body Centre + (-3, -57) * scale вЂ” NO
  `golem_vx` term (that is the fists' aiStyle-47 tether only).
- **Balance/enrage**: missing entirely. `GetMyBalance()` solo 1f
  (`:18485-18488`), ftw +3 (`:31134`), Г—2 when the target is out of BOTH the
  temple and the jungle OR above `worldSurface * 16.0` (a DOUBLE compare,
  `:31136`). The factor scales both fireball window adds and the phase-1
  `num688 = (balance + 3) / 4` cadence.
- **Fireballs**: the stand-in pushes the raw delta; the C# normalizes to
  speed 8 (`:31196-31198`/`:31251-31253`), aims at the player CENTRE from
  Centre + (0, 10*scale) (phase 1 adds the В±40*scale side muzzle), dmg 18
  phase 0 / 24 phase 1, `TargetClosest` on every fire tick (and every phase-1
  tick) вЂ” all absent from the stand-in.
- **Beam gate RNG**: the stand-in folds `60 + Main.rand.Next(600)` (`:31278`)
  to a flat 300. The port restores the real draw вЂ” exactly ONE `Next(600)`
  per phase-1 tick (the C# evaluates the comparison's right-hand side
  unconditionally), ZERO in phase 0. Witness:
  `s1_d_3_s46_the_arm_draws_one_next_600_per_phase1_tick`.
- **Beam life tiers**: `life < lifeMax / 3` / `/4` / `/5` are INTEGER
  divisions (`:31262-31272`); the stand-in used f32 `/3.0` for the first
  tier. The fireball tiers (`:31227-31233`) are DOUBLE `* 0.4` / `* 0.2`
  compares вЂ” the port keeps both kinds distinct. The tail phase gate
  `life < lifeMax / 2` (`:31338`) is INTEGER too.
- **Mouth flag**: `localAI[0]` is an AI write on the first/last 20 of the 300
  cadence (`:31181`/`:31186`, `:31238`/`:31242`); the stand-in folded it into
  FindFrame. The port writes the flag; the FindFrame read swap is the merge
  step.

Host-path folds (the module header carries the same list):

- `GetMyBalance` multiplayer scaling is unported (one session player в†’ 1f).
- `Main.getGoodWorld` / the player zone flags have no runtime fields вЂ” the
  `Style46Flags` struct keeps the gate complete; the wiring passes
  false/false/false until those systems land.
- `noTileCollide = true` (`:31140`) folds to the raw `position += velocity`
  tail integration (`integrate_no_tile_collide` shape) + the port's
  below-world despawn guard.
- `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999, 0f, 0)` on `golemBoss < 0` (`:31141-31145`)
  folds to `hp = 0` + return before any write (the sim's body-gone precedent).
- `Main.netMode != 1` and `GetSpawnSource_ForProjectile()` fold to the
  standing `wants_hostile_shot` convention (always request, no source).
- The beams' `timeLeft = 300` rides the sim's timed-spawn list at the merge

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style49.rs` ports `NPC.AI()`'s

which case the CURRENT velocity is the aim (`:31597-31601`). Each axis

## The legacy minimap light export (S1-E-19 wave B, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

**Code-only mode**: this wave was finished under a user directive of file
reads/writes + git only - NO cargo/rustc/rustfmt/test runs, no dotnet, no
graphify. The tests below are **tests-as-code: written, NOT run**; the wave-A
legacy goldens and the full-suite verification are deferred to the next
build-capable pass. No compiler was invoked.

`crates/tr-core/src/lighting/legacy.rs` gains `try_updating_map_with_light`
(`TryUpdatingMapWithLight`, `LegacyLighting.cs:371-433`) and the `ProcessArea`
gate block (`:341-358`) runs INLINE in `process_area` - before `PreRenderPhase`
resets the count, so the `renderCount == 3` gate sees the C# value. The export
is split along the C#'s own seam:

- `MapLightExport<'a>` borrows the `Main.Map` tile array (`WorldMap._tiles`),
  the `Main.mapTime` counter (`Main.cs:803`), `mapTimeMax` (`Main.cs:801`) and
  the `Main.mapEnabled` gate (`Main.cs:813`). The app's `WorldMap` hands it out
  through `legacy_light_export` (`tr-app/src/map.rs`); the frame driver
  (`app/frame/draw.rs`) attaches it only while a legacy mode is active and
  pushes the returned `changed` list into the map texture's dirty queue
  (`push_dirty`, the `MapRenderer.QueueChange` analog).
- The gate order is verbatim (`:340-358`): `ShiftUnProcessedDataOver` -> the
  `Netplay.Connection.StatusMax > 0` poke `mapTime = 1` (`:341-344`, wired
  from `App.net_status_max`) -> the `mapDelay` countdown (`:345-348`) -> the
  `mapTime == 0 && mapEnabled && renderCount == 3` gate (`:349`). `mapDelay`
  lives ON THE ENGINE (`Main.mapDelay`, `Main.cs:229`, static ctor `= 2` at
  `:66504`, world-load re-arm `WorldGen.cs:6947`); `enter_loaded_world` calls
  `reset_map_delay` (`app/mod.rs`).
- The export body (`:373-432`): the re-arm `mapTime = mapTimeMax` happens
  FIRST (`:373`); the window is the camera's SCALED view
  (`Camera.ScaledPosition/ScaledSize`, `Camera.cs:12-14` - the
  `GameViewMatrix.Translation` offset, `SpriteViewMatrix.cs:149-153`'s
  `Utils.Round` banker's rounding, computed in the driver from `world_zoom`)
  intersected with the requested rect, both clamped with the C#'s max-first
  `Utils.Clamp` (`Utils.cs:223-234`, the shared `wind::cs_clamp`). The walk is
  x-outer/y-inner over the PRESENTED `R/G/B`: max channel, White's 1.5x
  brighten (`IsColorOrWhiteMode`, `Mode < 2`, `:204`/`:416-419`), the
  `(byte)Math.Min(255f, num4 * 255f)` truncation (`:420`), the sky-air 22
  ambient (`:421-424`), the revealed-floor 22 (`:425-428`), then
  `Main.Map.UpdateLighting` (the shared `crate::map::update_map_lighting`,
  `WorldMap.cs:49-63`). `Main.updateMap` (`:432`) rides the seam's
  `update_map` field.
- The C# `try/catch` (`:351-357`) becomes abort-on-out-of-bounds early
  returns: the re-arm at `:373` happens first either way, tiles written
  before the abort persist and `updateMap` stays untouched. The state COLUMN
  is bounds-checked once per `i` BEFORE the inner loop (`:398` reads
  `_states[...]` before the `j` loop) - an out-of-range column aborts even
  when the y range is empty.

Map-side split (`tr-app`): while a legacy mode is active the frame's map
phase runs only the per-frame `Main.mapTime` countdown
(`WorldMap::tick_map_time`, `Main.cs:61818-61821`); the modern
`ExportToMiniMap` countdown/reveal stays inside `WorldMap::update` for Color
mode. The legacy engine owns the export itself - exactly the C# split
(`LightingEngine.ExportToMiniMap` vs `LegacyLighting.TryUpdatingMapWithLight`).

**RNG streams are untouched by construction**: `TryUpdatingMapWithLight`
draws NO random numbers (the whole `:371-433` body is reads, clamps, byte
maths and map writes). The swipe stream keeps its exact order - `NextSeed()`
after every swipe pass (`:1082`), `WithModifier((ulong)(i*1000+j))` +
`Next(98,100)` per wet decay draw (`:1250-1251`) - and the scanner stream
keeps its one `NextSeed()` per `PreRenderPhase` (`:723`). The export runs
between the shift and the sky reseed inside `process_area`, adding no draws
before, between or after them. The witness test
`map_export_keeps_the_rng_streams` drives 20 frames with wet cells beside
the torch (real swipe draws) and asserts byte-identical presented light plus
identical `swipe_rng`/`scanner_rng` seeds against a seam-less run.

Deliberate deviations / deferred callers:
- `Main.updateMap`'s CONSUMER (`Main.cs:61886-61894`, `MapRenderer.DrawToMap`
  of the rect) is not separately ported: the port's texture upload rides the
  per-tile dirty list (`push_dirty` -> `prepare`), which covers the same
  changed tiles. The rect itself is carried on the seam for parity.
- `BlackFadeCameraTeleport`'s `mapTime < 5 -> 5` poke (`Main.cs:62552-62555`)

  borrow is where it will land.
- The `gameMenu` re-arm `mapTime = mapTimeMax` (`Main.cs:61822-61825`) is a
  menu-state concern outside this wave; the in-game countdown is exact.

Tests-as-code (written, NOT run - code-only mode): 7 new
`legacy::tests::map_export_*` (the RNG-stream witness, the delay/count/
renderCount gate schedule, the disabled gate, the netplay pin, White's
1.5x + floor-22 + byte truncation + changed-list order, Retro's raw byte,
the sky-air 22 arm with a wet-cell counterexample) + 1 `tr-app`
`s1_e_19b_the_legacy_light_export_seam_borrows_tiles_and_counter` (the seam

12 wave-A goldens are untouched and must stay green when later run.
## The Creeper family (S1-D-3 aiStyle-55, 2026-11-18, code-only mode)

`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style55.rs` ports `NPC.AI`'s whole

velocity machine. **Family identity verified from the C#**: the only
`this.aiStyle = 55;` row in `SetDefaults` is the **Creeper**, type 267
(`NPC.cs:12456-12469`, `NPCID.cs:11211`). The Brain of Cthulhu (266) is
aiStyle **54** (`:12443`) вЂ” style 55 is not a Brain phase-2 arm; it is the
orbiting swarm's own machine, reading the Brain's centre through the static
`NPC.crimsonBoss` slot (set at `:32372` by the Brain's AI head, cleared
at `:8397`/`:95176`). The port's `npc/data.rs` style table already
carried the correct row (`Creeper => 55`, `:1567`).

The arm carries every branch: the brainless despawn (`:32659-32664`),
the orbit state's `ai[1]` reset, the strict `> 90f` ring with the
8-px homeward drift through the 15/16 blend and its early return, the
strict `< 8f` Manhattan amplify (Y then X), the lunge roll
(`:32686`), the `TargetClosest` + reciprocal-first unguarded 8-px aim
(`:32688-32694`), the expert homing steer (the unguarded `Normalize`,
the ftw 12f/49-50 row and the expert 9f/99-100 row, `:32700-32714`), the

recoil with the `knockBackResist == 0f` six-hit counter (`ai[1] > 5f`,
`:32724-32739`).

**RNG by construction** (the `npc_ai_style16` precedent): the arm's only
draws are the lunge roll at `:32686`,
`Main.netMode != 1 && ((Main.expertMode && Main.rand.Next(100) == 0) || Main.rand.Next(200) == 0)`.
Classic: the `&&` short-circuits before `Next(100)` (never drawn);
`Next(200)` is drawn EVERY in-ring state-0 tick, even when the roll
fails. Expert: `Next(100)` every in-ring tick; `Next(200)` only when
the first roll is non-zero (the `||` short-circuits on a zero вЂ” one
draw, not two). The far-orbit return and the whole state-1 tail draw
nothing. The witnesses mirror the cited draws on a cloned
`UnifiedRandom` and compare the full stream state (`PartialEq`),
including a ten-tick replay; a drifted draw count/order fails by
construction once executed.

**Code-only mode**: no cargo/rustc/tests were run on this branch вЂ” the 14
witness tests in the module are WRITTEN, NOT RUN.

**WIRED (S1-D-3 W-2, 2026-11-19, code-only mode вЂ” no compiler invoked):**
the aiStyle axis claims `55 =>` (`npc.rs::ai_055_creeper_family` ->
`ai_055_step`) and the `update_creeper` stand-in is RETIRED (the kind arm
is the axis-unreachable marker, the style-5/9 precedent). The seam feeds
`Ai55Ctx`: `brain_anchor` over the sim's `world.brain_*` write-through,
`npc_target::session_candidate` as the slot-0 candidate,
`player.buffs.expert_mode` (the retaliate convention,
`world_sim/npcs.rs`), `SeedFlags::FOR_THE_WORTHY` for `getGoodWorld` (the
`npc_ai_bat` convention), and the new one-tick `Npc::just_hit` field
(`NPC.cs:6453`) вЂ” armed by the strike paths (`hurt`,
`hurt_from_projectile`, `strike_pooled` вЂ” `strike_melee`/
`strike_projectile` delegate there; `NPC.cs:81274`), read by the arm,
cleared once per `update_rng` after the AI (`NPC.cs:90516`; the clear
sits BEFORE the port's folded-in `contact` pass so a thorns reflect
survives to the next tick's AI like the C#'s player-update strike).
`ticker` stays 0 (the zombie's `target_closest` precedent). The
`Ai55Effects::deactivate` request drains via `EncourageDespawn(0)` вЂ” the
same-tick pool removal (`world_sim/npcs.rs`'s `despawn_expired` retain),
the port's `active = false` shape without the death effects `hp = 0`
would trigger; the sim's `update_brain_state` retain
(`world_sim/npcs.rs:1040`) is the backstop.

**RNG parity of the swap (classic worlds):** the stand-in drew exactly
one `Next(200)` per in-ring state-0 tick and nothing elsewhere; the
faithful arm draws the identical census вЂ” the expert `Next(100)` half
short-circuits BEFORE drawing on classic (`ctx.expert_mode == false`),
the far-orbit return precedes the roll, the state-1 tail draws nothing,
and `TargetClosest`/the aim/`netUpdate` writes are RNG-free. The shared
`UpdateNpcs` stream therefore stays in step on classic worlds (witness
`s1_d_3_w2_the_wired_classic_draw_census_matches_the_mirror`). Expert
worlds gain the C#'s real draw shape (a faithful fix, not a regression).

The wiring witnesses (`npc.rs`, WRITTEN NOT RUN): the repointed
`the_creeper_orbits_brain_and_lunges` (now through the axis arm, plus the
one-tick-flag lifecycle: strike-tick recoil, update-tail clear, the
cooldown tail no longer recoils),
`s1_d_3_w2_the_700_leash_is_live_through_the_axis`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_lunge_retargets_and_syncs_through_the_axis`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_wired_classic_draw_census_matches_the_mirror`,
`s1_d_3_w2_the_brainless_creeper_despawns_same_tick`.

The line-by-line audit of the stand-in against the C# block (the W66
defect classes) found these real deviations, all fixed in the module
(and now LIVE via the wiring):
- **Missing 700-px leash** (`:32715-32721`): the stand-in's lunging
  Creepers never drop back to the orbit on distance вЂ” they lunge forever.
- **Missing `TargetClosest`** (`:32688`): the stand-in aims at the
  session player directly, never updating `target`/`targetRect`/
  `direction`/`directionY`/`targetSetFrame`.
- **Invented `.max(1.0)` distance floor**: the C#'s `8f / sqrt` at
  `:32692` is unguarded (a coincident centre gives `inf`/`NaN`);
  the stand-in floors the distance at 1.
- **f32 operation order**: the stand-in computes `dx / d * 8.0`
  (divide-then-multiply); the C# computes `num829 = 8f / d` then
  `dx * num829` (reciprocal-first) вЂ” different rounding (the (15, 20)
  witness fixture discriminates them: 4.7999997 vs 4.8000002).
- **`hurt_cd` vs `justHit`**: the stand-in reads the ~11-tick damage
  cooldown as the recoil gate; the C# reads the ONE-TICK `justHit`
  flag, so a struck Creeper should recoil on the strike tick only.
- **Missing gates/branches**: the `netUpdate` writes (`:32662`,
  `:32696`), the expert/ftw homing steer (`:32700-32714`) and the
  `knockBackResist == 0f` six-hit counter (`:32728-32735`, dead for
  the vanilla Creeper's 0.8f row but part of the arm).

Deliberate folds, all cited in the module:
- `Main.netMode != 1` в†’ true (single-player port) вЂ” on a client the C#
  draws nothing at the roll.
- `NPC.crimsonBoss` в†’ `Ai55Ctx::crimson_boss_center` (`None` = the
  `< 0` despawn), fed by `brain_anchor` over the sim's
  `world.brain_present`/`brain_x`/`brain_y` anchor
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs:993-995`).
- `active = false` leaves as `Ai55Effects::deactivate` (the port's
  `Npc` has no `active` field; the sim's pass retains the Creepers
  away when the Brain dies).
- `NPC.justHit` в†’ the port's `Npc::just_hit` one-tick field (the W-2
  wiring landed it: armed `NPC.cs:81274`, cleared `:90516`; the
  `Ai55Ctx::just_hit` seam carries it into the pure arm вЂ” the
  `Ai16Ctx::just_hit` precedent).
- `Math.Sqrt` keeps the C#'s f32-sum в†’ f64-root в†’ f32-cast shape
  (provably bit-identical to a direct f32 sqrt for this input shape, but
  transcribed literally); `Vector2.Normalize()` is XNA's
  reciprocal-multiply, unguarded.
- Position integration stays OUT of the arm (the C# AI ends before
  `UpdateCollision`).

## The Martian Saucer core audit (S1-D-3 aiStyle-76, code-only)

`NPC.AI()`'s `else if (this.aiStyle == 76)` arm (`NPC.cs:36071-36519`)
was ALREADY ported on main — `npc.rs::update_saucer_core` (M4-EVENT-4e,
2026-11-08), the sole kind being the MartianSaucerCore 395 (the census of
`this.aiStyle = 76;` across `NPC.cs` returns exactly one hit, `:14052`,
the `type == 395` SetDefaults row `:14045-14062`). No new module was
created (the no-parallel-implementations rule); this round is the
distrust-verbatim audit of the live arm against the whole C# block, with
surgical fixes. CODE-ONLY MODE: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; the
11 witness tests (`npc.rs::s1_d_3_s76_audit_tests`) are WRITTEN NOT RUN,
verified by C# re-reading + hand-arithmetic.

The defects found and fixed (each cited to the C# line):

- **The despawn ride was nested under the far gate.** The C#'s
  `if (ai[0] == -1 || ai[0] == -2)` (`:36130`) is its OWN if/else-if
  chain — a core that entered -1/-2 while the player was far keeps
  climbing after the player returns inside the 5600-px window. The v1
  ran the ride only while `far`, freezing the negative phases near the
  player. Fixed: the ride chains off the phase, not the distance.
- **The living-player restore reset -1 to 0.** The C# restores only
  -2 → 2 (`:36137-36140`); the `if (ai[0] == 0) ai[0] = 0;` at
  `:36141-36144` is DEAD code (the phase is -1 or -2 there). The v1's
  `if -2 { 2 } else { 0 }` killed the -1 climb on the first restore
  tick. Fixed: -1 stays -1, the counters still zero (`:36145-36147`).
- **The despawn timers were missing.** `EncourageDespawn(10)`
  (`:36133`, the only-lowering `:7249-7256` write) and the DIRECT
  `timeLeft = 300` (`:36136`, not an EncourageDespawn) now run; the
  dead-player branch takes neither (the `!player19.dead` gate).
- **The vulnerable wobble never dropped the shield.** The C# sets
  `dontTakeDamage = false` at `:36383` (the SetDefaults `true` row
  `:14060` holds until then). The port now models the SetDefaults
  shield at construction (`Npc::new`) and drops it in the wobble —
  the core is unkillable by damage until the crew-dead bridge hands
  it the vulnerable phase (the bridge itself stays the documented
  M4-EVENT-4f follow-up).
- **The gun's 447 dropped its owner payload.** `NewProjectile(..., 447,
  80, 0f, myPlayer, whoAmI + 1)` (`:36437`) — the deathray arm
  (`Projectile.cs:30818`) reads `ai0 - 1` to find its owner. The v1
  pushed the plain shot tuple; the shot now rides
  `wants_hostile_shot_ai` with `ai0 = slot + 1` (the shell's entry
  shot already did, `update_saucer_mount`).
- **The side picks used Rust `signum`.** The band-0 approach's -600
  offset (`:36229`) and the band-2 approach's +300 (`:36285`) multiply
  `Math.Sign`, which returns **0 on the exact tie** — Rust's
  `f32::signum` returns +1 on +0.0, sending the core 600 px the wrong
  way when it sits exactly above the player. The new `math_sign`
  helper carries the C# tie. The band-CHANGE writes (`:36217`,
  `:36433`) use the `Sign(...) == 1 ? 1 : -1` ternary instead — the
  tie folds to -1 there; both forms are pinned by witnesses.
- **The clearance probe dropped `!tileSolidTop`.** The C# predicate is
  `nactive() && tileSolid[type] && !tileSolidTop[type]`
  (`:36247`/`:36256` and the three replicas) — platforms do NOT stop
  the scan. `ground_clearance` now carries the term (the Dutchman's
  `:38908`/`:38917` probe shares the helper, same predicate), and the
  row-0 landing keeps the C#'s literal `count--` shape (the v1 clamped
  it to 0). The probe columns are the C#'s cast-then-divide
  (`(int)Center.X / 16`, `(int)(position.Y + height) / 16`,
  `:36244-36245`), not divide-then-cast.
- **The dive/park/dash Y targets were inverted at low clearance.** The
  C# eases toward -4 but caps the steepness at the clearance
  (`0f - num1111 > num1110` → `-clearance`, `:36266-36270`,
  `:36347-36351`, `:36481-36485`): a 0-px clearance eases toward 0,
  not -4. The v1's `-(clear.max(-4.0))` ran -0/-4 backwards. Fixed in
  all three arms.
- **The wobble rotation ran f32 cos of 6.283.** `RotatedBy` takes a
  DOUBLE and computes `(float)Math.Cos(radians)` (`Utils.cs:1675-1684`)
  on the promoted f32 angle; the angle literal is
  `(float)Math.PI * 2f` = TAU, not 6.283. The three cosine bands now
  promote to f64 and use TAU; the 120+ raw-angle band uses TAU too.
- **The gun chase had an invented zero guard.** The C#'s
  `vector154.Normalize()` (`:36454`) has NO `.max(0.001)` floor — the
  port's guard is gone (the approach arms' <50/<70 gates make their
  zero vectors unreachable; the chase's exact-coincidence NaN is the
  C#'s own behaviour, carried verbatim).
- **The netUpdate writes were missing** (`:36116`, `:36128`, `:36148`,
  `:36223`, `:36392`, `:36441`, `:36449`, `:36517`) — all landed.

RNG by construction: the whole arm draws NO `Main.rand` — no
`Next`/`NextFloat` anywhere in `:36071-36519`; `NewNPC`'s only draw is
the getGoodWorld gate (`:80752`, constants-off in the port);
`TargetClosest` (`:77652-77781`) is the deterministic Manhattan scan
(now riding `npc_target::target_closest`, style 76, the S1-D-3p
helper); `EncourageDespawn` and the 9999 instant-kill
`StrikeNPCNoInteraction` path (`:81237`'s `Damage >= 9999 &&
owner == 255` flag — no loot/dust/combat-text draws) draw nothing. The
`rng` parameter stays for the dispatch signature, untouched; the
witness `s1_d_3_s76_audit_the_arm_draws_no_rng` pins a `UnifiedRandom`
state across all six scan bands, the wobble, the gun and both rides.

Documented folds (unchanged from M4-EVENT-4e): the off-world
`active = false` (`:36516`) folds to hp=0 through the death pass; the
classic-only constants (no expert difficulty flags in the arm itself —
the 80 damage is the literal `num1126`); the crew spawn's
`localAI[0..3]` sibling slots ride the pre-pass write-through (the
port's link model). The shell's missile battery + the classic/expert
phase bridge remain the M4-EVENT-4f follow-ups — with the shield now
modelled, the core is damage-immune until that bridge lands (the C#
behaviour; the v1 let the player kill the shielded core outright).

the style axis (`npc.rs::ai_009_sphere_family`) through the new
`crates/tr-app/src/npc_ai_style9.rs`. The ported kinds are the three
caster spheres вЂ” Burning Sphere 25 (`SetDefaults` `:9093-9107`), Chaos
Ball 30 + its Tim clone 665 (`:15699-15713`, `:17403-17417`, folded into

  else arm's `Lighting.AddLight` `:21561`) вЂ” the S1-D-3e/f precedent; the

### Faithfulness traps kept (the W66/W94 catalogue)

- **Draw-before-early-return**: `spriteDirection = -(int)this.ai[0]`
  (the TRUNCATED int negation) is the FIRST write in all three arms
  (`:28247/:28524/:28759`), BEFORE the head-gone despawn gate вЂ” the
  port writes `sprite_dir` first too (witness tests pin it on the
  despawn tick).
- **Two different centres**: the band comparisons use INTEGER
  half-widths (`(float)(width / 2)` on both entities) while the
  dock/aim vectors use the FLOAT centre (`width * 0.5f`) вЂ” kept
  distinct (`half_w` vs `dock_vector`).
- **f64-on-f32**: `Math.Sqrt`/`Math.Atan2` are DOUBLE calls on f32
  operands вЂ” the port computes `((x*x + y*y) as f64).sqrt() as f32`
  and `(y as f64).atan2(x as f64) as f32` (`cs_sqrt`/`cs_atan2`);
  the sums/products stay f32 and the `speed / (float)Math.Sqrt(...)`
  divisions are f32 divides of an f64-rounded sqrt. The literal
  `1.57f`, not FRAC_PI_2.
- **Strict bounds**: the hysteresis >800/<400, the snap |vx|+|vy|<2,
  the rise gate y<head.Yв€’280, the В±500 centre gate, the state-5
  playerCentreв€’100 condition, and ALL four shot cadences (>140, >40,
  >200, >80 вЂ” the ++ runs first, so equality holds) are STRICT, pinned
  by boundary witness tests.
- **Dead stores annotated**: the vice's `num516` (`:28432`),
  `num519`'s first value (`:28444`, the name is reused for the dash
  scale at `:28460`), `num522`'s first value (`:28487`, reused at
  `:28502`), and the cannon's `num531` head-Y read (`:28693`,
  overwritten at `:28694`) вЂ” kept verbatim, no observable effect. The
  cannon's `num525`/`num532` and the laser's `num539`/`num546`
  ARE read (the shot normalisers) вЂ” not dead.
- **No epsilon floor**: the normalisers divide by the distance
  verbatim вЂ” a zero distance yields the C#'s NaN/Inf (the live arm
  floors at 0.001; the port does not). The cannon's reversed vector is
  `(0f в€’ num) * scale` verbatim (`-0.0` preserved).
- **No integration**: all three are noTileCollide, so `UpdateNPC`
  integrates `position += velocity` after `AI()`
  (`NPC.cs:90498`); the step fns do not move the limb.
- **Despawn fall-through = early return**: `ai[2] += 10` per tick,
  `> 50 || netMode != 2` kills (single-player dies on the first
  tick); after the kill `ai[2]` is 10 or в‰Ґ60 so no state branch
  matches вЂ” the port's early return is observationally identical. The
  `life = -1; HitEffect(); active = false` rides the hp-0 convention.
- `EncourageDespawn(10)` rides `Npc::encourage_despawn`
  (`NPC.cs:7249-7256` вЂ” only ever lowers the window).

### RNG by construction

The vice arm draws NO `Main.rand` вЂ” every counter is deterministic;
`style34_step` takes no RNG parameter and the dispatcher witness
pins the stream bit-identical after a vice tick. The cannon and laser
each draw exactly TWO `Main.rand.Next(-40, 41)` values (X then Y) per
FIRED shot вЂ” the reversed-dock bomb `:28669-28670`, the player bomb
`:28748-28749`, the hover volley `:28904-28905`, the flank volley
`:28982-28983` вЂ” and nothing else. Both draws sit INSIDE
`Main.netMode != 1` AND the STRICT `localAI[0] >` threshold, so a
client or a non-firing tick draws ZERO; `UnifiedRandom::next_range`
is the exact `Next(min, maxExclusive)` stream
(`Utilities/UnifiedRandom.cs:120-132`). The stream-clone witness
tests pin the exact draw count and order per firing tick and the
zero-draw gates. The despawn's `HitEffect()` reaches the
type-128..131 gore arm (`NPC.cs:89433-89469`) whose four
`Main.rand.Next(61, 64)` picks (`:89452/:89456/:89460/:89464`) are
COSMETIC gore вЂ” the dust/gore skip precedent (S1-D-3e/f/g and the saw
sibling), so the despawn draws nothing. `npc_target::target_closest`
is RNG-free. The shots ride `Npc::wants_hostile_shot` (the style-28
seam); the C#'s knockback `0f` and `Main.myPlayer` owner are the
tuple's documented non-carried fields.

### The head seam

`PrimeLimbContext` names every head field the arms read:
`active`/`aiStyle` (must be 32 вЂ” any other style in the head slot
despawns the limb), `position`, `width` (INT вЂ” the half-width is
integer division), `velocity` (ONLY the vice's rise/fly blends read
it, `:28446/:28489`), `ai[1]` (the head's phase: 0 hover, 1 charge,
2 rage, 3 despawn), plus `net_mode` and the `EverLastingTicker`
stamp. Same shape as the sibling's `Style33Context` plus the
velocity pair вЂ” the port's `World.prime_*` write-through carries
only the position today, so the wiring round must extend it (or read
the head's NPC slot directly) before claiming the dispatch.

## The atlas skyline packer (S1-G-12b, 2026-11-19, code-only)

**The bound.** The renderer draws ONE atlas through one instanced sprite
pipeline (AGENTS.md rendering invariant; research/41 D-3 вЂ” the C# itself is
per-texture, `TileBatch.cs:485-536`, so the packing algorithm is
port-infrastructure, not game logic). The atlas is 8192 px wide and must stay
в‰¤ 8192 px tall (the strict-GPU max 2D dimension). The landed best-fit
decreasing-height shelf packer (S1-F-13c slice B) held the main sheet set at
~8121 px вЂ” 71 px of headroom. Two branches were SKIP-blocked on it:
`task/S1-E-4b-gore-draw` adds ~1400 `Gore_<id>` sheets
(`AssetInitializer.cs:135-137`, the `Main.DrawGore` source
`Main.cs:21873-21907`) and `task/S1-L-8b-mount-data` adds 25
`STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` rows (the Drill glow strips, the mount GlowMasks
283/284/285/370, the corrected minecart file names, the S1-L-9 land-mount
sheets).

**Measured heights** (`tools/atlas_sim.js` вЂ” reads the REAL sheet dims out
of the retail `.xnb` files through an LZX decoder ported from
`crates/tr-content/src/lzx.rs`, mirrors the `assets.rs` enumeration
including `proj_data`'s range arms and the two branches' additions; no
compiler invoked). The sim's best-fit shelf height on the main set is
8117 px vs the recorded 8121 вЂ” a 4 px census residual (a handful of sheets
whose decode the sim skips), immaterial to the bound decision:

| sheet set | best-fit shelves (main) | first-fit shelves (E-4b) | skyline waste | skyline span | maxrects BAF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (test world, 7826 sheets) | 8117 | 8117 | **7289** | 7251 | 7070 |
| main + gore (9228 sheets) | 8493 OVERFLOW | 8493 OVERFLOW | **7680** | 7643 | 7462 |
| main + gore + mount + font (9254 sheets) | 8664 OVERFLOW | 8664 OVERFLOW | **7932** | 8091 | 7601 |

**The choice: skyline bottom-left, waste tie-break** (option 1 of the task
brief). Each rect tries every skyline node's left edge; the placement y is
the max skyline height over the span; the winner minimises `(y, waste, x)`
вЂ” bottom-left first, then the least area buried under the rect, then
leftmost. All keys are integers and the scan order is fixed, so the layout
is a pure function of the input list (the world-swap `build_ref` contract).
The skyline backfills the width tails the shelf pass strands per row вЂ” the
exact failure mode the ~1400 same-band gore sheets exposed. The span
tie-break was evaluated and rejected: it wins on the smaller sets but packs
the critical combined set at 8091 px (only 101 px headroom) vs the waste
tie-break's 7932 px (260 px headroom). Maxrects best-area-fit packs tighter
still (7601 px) but is more code (free-rect split + containment prune) for
headroom the port does not need yet; it stays the documented next step if a
future sheet wave eats the 260 px. A two-atlas split (option 4) was not
needed and would break the one-atlas/one-pipeline invariant.

**Name dedup** (option 3): the census found 41 duplicate decodes in the full
set вЂ” 48 `Projectile_*` names ride both `STATIC_SHEET_NAMES` and the
`proj_data` loop (minus the ones whose file is absent). The `sheets`
HashMap keeps one rect per name, so the later copy's pixels were dead weight.
`build_ref` now keeps the FIRST occurrence of each name вЂ” UV-neutral for
every lookup (they already resolved to one rect), and it removes the dead
pixels. No sheet a draw references was removed.

**Implementation.** `crates/tr-render/src/atlas.rs`: `skyline_pack`
(the pure packer over PAD-inflated rects in a `max_width - PAD` bin) +
`build_ref`'s dedup/sort/skyline pass. The PAD geometry is unchanged:
every sheet keeps the 2 px border and в‰Ґ 2 px separation (the rects are
inflated by PAD before packing and offset by PAD after). `build` delegates
to `build_ref` exactly as before, so the owned and borrowed paths stay
bit-identical. `font_atlas.rs`'s independent shelf packer is untouched.

**Tests (WRITTEN, NOT RUN вЂ” code-only mode, no compiler invoked).**
`tr-render/src/atlas.rs`: `skyline_layout_is_deterministic_across_runs`
(two runs, identical pixels + rects), `skyline_copies_every_sheet_to_its_rect`
(UV correctness: every sheet's pixels at its rect, rect in-bounds with the
PAD border), `skyline_sheets_never_overlap_including_padding` (pairwise
on the inflated rects), `skyline_backfills_the_tall_sheets_tail`
(hand-computed 3-sheet witness, height 84 vs the shelf pass's 96),
`duplicate_names_pack_once_first_wins`, `skyline_fits_the_gore_shaped_stress_set`
(1400 small sheets + a tall band under 8192). The pre-existing
`build_ref_matches_build_bit_for_bit` still pins the owned/borrowed
contract. `tr-app/src/assets.rs`:
`the_full_gore_and_mount_sheet_set_fits_the_strict_gpu_bound` decodes the
real content, appends the simulated E-4b gore enumeration (910/911 excluded)
and the L-8b additions, and asserts height в‰¤ 8192 + every sampled gore sheet
addressable.

**Consequence for the goldens.** Like the E-4b branch's own packer change,
the skyline moves every sheet's atlas position: all UVs shift, so the golden
screenshot SHA256s change by construction and must be re-taken when a build
is next allowed (no pixel-behaviour change вЂ” the same texels, new addresses).
The E-4b and L-8b branches can now un-skip: their sheet sets fit.

**W4-b4 re-verify + re-pin procedure (2026-11-20, code-only).** The packer
landed intact (`548fc335` via merge `4791ae7f`; the scout's "unmerged branch"
note was stale — the branch was merged, then deleted in the wave-2 purge).
E-4b's gore enumeration landed on main afterwards (`b45c70fc`), so the
`the_full_gore_and_mount_sheet_set_fits_the_strict_gpu_bound` witness's
"simulated E-4b additions" now double-enumerate the gore set — the name dedup
makes the second copy a no-op (first wins, identical pixels), the test stays

backfills at (42,22) — y=22 beats y=82; height 82+2=84). UV-pin audit: no

was repaired for the purge: the L-8b branch ref is gone, so the sim falls

The golden re-pin procedure (which goldens, the harness commands, twin-run +

next build-allowed window. Unblocks: N16 wyvern sheets, S1-L-8b mounts, gore
draw refinements (each lane re-takes the goldens it touches at its merge).

**Fresh measurement (2026-11-20, `node tools/atlas_sim.js`, real `.xnb` dims,
no compiler).** The sheet set GREW since the 2026-11-19 measurement (E-4b's

| sheet set (2026-11-20 census) | best-fit shelves | skyline waste | skyline span | maxrects BAF |

The 7932 px figure above is the 2026-11-19 census; today's full set packs in

## The vines keep their background walls (fix/vines-destroy-walls)

**User report.** Spawned vines destroy background-wall tiles: in mini-caves
with a destructible `dirt_wall`, the wall disappears and a vine stands in
its place.

**Root cause вЂ” the worldgen Vines pass, not the growth tick or the draw.**
`worldgen/biome_detail.rs::pass_vines` planted each vine segment by
REPLACING the whole `Tile` struct:

```rust
world.tiles[i] = Tile { kind: vine, frame_x: 0, ..Default::default() };
world.tiles[i].flags |= FLAG_ACTIVE;
```

`Tile::default()` zeroes `wall`, `wall_frame`, `liquid`, `meta` (paint) вЂ”
so every generated vine erased the cell's background wall. The C# Vines
pass writes fields only (`WorldGen.cs:20210-20216` for the 52 arm,
`:20246-20251` for the jungle 62 arm, `:20390-20395` for the corrupt 636
arm): `active(true)`, `type = <vine>`, `ClearSlope()` вЂ” `tile.wall` and
`wallFrame` are never touched. Jungle-grass overhangs above mini-cave
pockets carrying the natural dirt wall grew vines straight through the
wall field, which is exactly the reported symptom.

The two other suspects were re-verified faithful and left unchanged:

- The runtime growth arm (`growth.rs::grow_vine_arm`,
  `WorldGen.cs:73311-73341` + the four sibling families `:73343-73499`)
  writes `kind`/`flags`/`liquid` only; `wall` is a separate `Tile` field
  (`tile.rs:19`) it never touches. (Its `SquareTileFrame` /
  `CopyPaintAndCoating` calls remain the documented M7-GROWTH omissions.)
- The draw layer: walls draw in their own pass BEFORE tiles
  (`render/tiles.rs`, `Main.DrawWalls` shape), gated only by
  `wall_visible` + `tile_hides_wall` вЂ” the frame-opacity proxy for
  `WallDrawing.FullTile` (`WallDrawing.cs:91`, `:241-442`), which returns
  false for every non-solid kind. Vine frames are transparent, so the
  wall draws under vine cells; the deferred `DrawVines` strip pass
  (`render/vines.rs`, S1-G-1) draws only vine sprites and never touches
  the wall layer.

**Fix.** `pass_vines` now writes the C#'s fields in place: `FLAG_ACTIVE`,
`kind = vine`, `set_slope(0)` + clear `FLAG_HALF_BRICK`
(`Tile.ClearSlope`, `Tile.cs:130-134`), `frame_x = 0` (the port's existing
framing convention for vine segments). Wall, wall frame, liquid and paint
survive. The RNG draw order is unchanged вЂ” the write itself draws nothing
вЂ” so `generation_is_reproducible_for_a_seed` (a == b) stays green; the two

## The aiStyle-48 census (S1-D-3, docs-only, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

**Census.** A whole-tree `aiStyle = 48` grep finds **exactly one NPC kind**:
GolemHeadFree 249 (`SetDefaults` case 249, `NPC.cs:12207-12220` вЂ” `noGravity`,
70x70, dmg 80, def 32, lifeMax 16000, kbResist 0, `dontTakeDamage = true`
`:12219`). The five `Projectile.cs` hits (`:3382`/`:3445`/`:3797`/`:3842`/
`:5041`) are projectile-aiStyle machines, out of NPC scope. The arm is
`NPC.AI()`'s inline `else if (this.aiStyle == 48)` block (`NPC.cs:31351-31586`,
no `AI_048_*` method).

**Coverage: LANDED + WIRED.** The sibling `task/S1-D-3-golem-audit` (merge
`c7fe175d`, the 4-arm rewrite) already ports style 48: the kind-gated arm
`npc.rs::update_golem_rng`'s `NpcKind::GolemHeadFree` block (`npc.rs:14467-14558`)
over the pure cores in `npc_ai_golem.rs` (`free_head_hover_velocity` `:232`,
`free_head_fireball_step` `:276`, `free_head_barrage_step` `:300`,
`free_head_beam_tier` `:340`, `free_head_barrage_trigger` `:482`,
`free_head_blocked_lead` `:490`, `enrage_balance` `:35`). The earlier
TR-D3s48 partial (`npc_ai_style48.rs` + an `npc.rs` style-axis claim) was a
competing duplicate вЂ” DISCARDED per the coordination note; this round is the
distrust-verbatim census audit of the landed arm. No golem-module edit.

**Verified faithful (line-by-line vs `NPC.cs:31351-31586`).**

- *The enrage gate* (`:31354-31362`): solo `GetMyBalance` 1, +3 getGood
  (parked false), x2 on `(!temple && !jungle) || Center.Y < worldSurface*16` вЂ”
  `enrage_balance(false, 3.0, ...)` at `npc.rs:14027-14035`, the shared
  four-arm gate.
- *The hover* (`:31378-31417`): the 7-speed aim at `player.Center - (0, 300)`,
  the 0.05 per-axis converge with the sign-cross DOUBLE add, the post-increment
  sign test вЂ” `free_head_hover_velocity` matches the structure and the order
  (X then Y), no invented clamp.
- *The fireball salvo* (`:31418-31465`): `(num+4)/5` base + the four BODY-hp
  tier adds; the mouth window `ai[1] < 20 || > 280` written to `localAI[0]`
  BEFORE the flag53 pin `ai[1] = 20` (`:31437-31448` вЂ” the port keeps this
  order); the `>= 300` reset + the normalized 8-speed 258 fireball at dmg 20
  from `(cx, cy - 10)` (`:31449-31465`, the `10f*scale` folds at scale 1).
- *The barrage ladder's mixed DOUBLE/INTEGER tiers* (`:31467-31505`): base
  `num`, `+num` at the DOUBLE `lifeMax/1.25` and `/1.5`, then the INTEGER
  `/2`/`/3`/`/4`/`/5`/`/6` вЂ” `free_head_barrage_step` splits them correctly
  (f32 divisions for the first two, raw `i32` divisions for the last five);
  the World carries the raw `golem_hp`/`golem_max_hp` ints
  (`world_sim/npcs.rs:2861-2862`/`:3794-3795`), so the integer tiers are
  reproducible (a ratio could not). flag54 (the BODY's blocked line,
  `:31497-31501`, via `world.golem_x/y` = the body's centre) adds `num*10`.
- *The restored RNG triggers*: `ai[2] > 100 + Main.rand.Next(4800)`
  (`:31506`) вЂ” ONE draw per tick, every tick, strict `>`; the blocked-line
  lead `NextFloat()` X THEN Y, two draws PER BEAM, only while flag54
  (`:31555-31556`) вЂ” `free_head_blocked_lead` keeps the order; the tier
  escalation `(int)(dmg*1.5)` / `speed*2.5` (`:31553-31554`).
- *The beams* (`:31509-31569`): two at `+-14` from `cy - 50`, base 24 dmg /
  11 speed, +1/+0.25 at each BODY 50/40/30/20/10 % tier (`:31521-31548`),
  the normalized aim, the 3-tick spawn lead (`:31563-31564`), the
  `timeLeft = 300` override in the shot drain (`world_sim/npcs.rs:3897-3900`,
  `:31568`).
- *The shield*: `dontTakeDamage = true` from `SetDefaults` (`:12219`) never
  clears вЂ” the sim's spawn writes it (`world_sim/npcs.rs:3434`); the
  `golemBoss < 0` orphan guard (`:31372-31376`) rides `!world.golem_present`
  -> `hp = 0` (the family's documented direct-write stand-in for
  `StrikeNPCNoInteraction(9999, 0f, 0)` вЂ” the C#'s `owner == 255` +
  `Damage >= 9999` bypass flag `:81237` pierces the shield, so the kill
  itself is behaviourally right; the death-chain gore/sound fold with it).
- *The `TargetClosest` calls* (`:31377`, `:31451`) fold into the port's
  single-player target seam (the family-wide documented fold).

**Gaps found (for the follow-up вЂ” NOT fixed this round, the golem module is
the sibling's).**

- **G1 вЂ” the `noTileCollide` phase machine is UNPORTED** (`:31363-31371`).
  The C# free head defaults `noTileCollide = false` (case 249 sets no such
  line) and PHASES it per tick: its own blocked line sets it true (with
  flag53), and `noTileCollide && Collision.SolidTiles(position, w, h)`
  re-collides it. The port's arm integrates RAW every tick
  (`npc.rs:14556-14557`, `x += vx; y += vy`) вЂ” the head flies through temple
  walls even on clear-line ticks where the C# collides. `local_ai[0]` is
  taken by the mouth flag; the discarded TR-D3s48 partial had added a
  dedicated `Npc::no_tile_collide` field for exactly this. The fix needs the
  field (or a free local slot) + the two-probe phase + the seam's
  `player::collides_rect` pass gated on it. Behavioural, the largest gap.
- **G2 вЂ” the f32-vs-DOUBLE tier boundaries + the accumulation order** (the
  f1701eb0 catalogue class). The C# casts `(double)life < (double)lifeMax *
  0.8` etc. (`:31420`/`:31424`/`:31428`/`:31432`, `:31469`/`:31473`,
  `:31524-31544`); `free_head_fireball_step`/`free_head_beam_tier` compare in
  f32 (`npc_ai_golem.rs:279-291`/`:343-349`). At non-exact products the
  boundary flips: e.g. lifeMax 21000 at the 30 % beam tier вЂ”
  `21000.0f32 * 0.3f32` rounds ABOVE 6300.0, so `life == 6300` takes the tier
  in the port but not in the C# (`6300 < 6300.0` is false in double). The
  sibling's OWN attached-head core uses f64 for the same class
  (`head_fireball_step`, `npc_ai_golem.rs:367-371`) вЂ” the free-head cores
  should match. Second residual: the C# adds each tier to `ai[1]`/`ai[2]`
  SEQUENTIALLY (five/eight rounded f32 adds, `:31419-31434`/`:31468-31504`);
  the port pre-sums the ladder in f32 and does ONE `+=` (`npc.rs:14489`/
  `:14522`) вЂ” a different rounding path that can drift the 300-cadence /
  the trigger crossing by a tick over long fights. Both are ulp-class;
  fix = f64 compares + per-tier sequential adds (or a stream-witnessed
  proof of equivalence, which does not hold in general).
- **G3 вЂ” the facing write is a stand-in**: the port writes
  `facing`/`sprite_dir` from the velocity sign (`npc.rs:14554-14555`); the
  C# arm writes NO direction вЂ” it rides `TargetClosest`'s
  `SetTargetTrackingValues` target-face (`:77744-77755`). Diverges while the
  head drifts away from the player; folds with the family's TargetClosest
  seam but was not cited there.
- **G4 вЂ” the dust tail's stream offset, quantified**: the skipped 228-dust
  tail (`:31572-31585`, the standing cosmetic-skip) draws **SEVEN**
  `Main.rand` values EVERY tick while the head lives вЂ” `Next(2)` `:31575`,
  `NextFloatDirection()` + `NextFloat()` `:31576`, `NextFloatDirection()` +
  `NextFloat()` + `NextFloat()` `:31579`, `NextFloat()` `:31581`. Unlike the
  event-gated dust skips elsewhere in the family, this is a CONSTANT 7-draw
  per-tick offset on the shared `UpdateNpcs` stream вЂ” every downstream
  vanilla-synced roll drifts while the free head is alive. The gameplay
  draws (the trigger + the leads) are restored in the C#'s order, so the
  port's own stream is self-consistent; the offset matters only for
  vanilla-stream parity (the standing deviation, now counted).
- **G5 вЂ” FindFrame reads the POST-pin cadence**: the C# case 249
  (`:72963-72976`) reads `localAI[0] == 1` вЂ” the PRE-pin mouth flag; the port
  RECOMPUTES `ai[1] < 20 || > 280` (`npc.rs:6296`) AFTER the flag53 pin
  `ai[1] = 20`. On a blocked-line tick whose pre-pin `ai[1]` was in the
  window (e.g. 285 -> flag53 pins 20), the C# shows the mouth OPEN (the
  stored flag 1) and the port shows it CLOSED (20 fails both tests). Fix =
  read `local_ai[0]` (the arm already stores it). The dropped
  `frameCounter` 16-wrap (`:72972-72975`) is cited dead (no reader for this
  type) вЂ” accepted.

**Verdict.** Style 48 is COVERED by the landed golem-audit arm вЂ” the census
finds no missing kind and no competing port needed. The cores are faithful
in structure, constants, tier SPLIT (DOUBLE vs INTEGER) and RNG order; the
five gaps above (G1 behavioural, G2 ulp-class x2, G3/G5 small, G4 the
quantified standing skip) are the follow-up's scope. The three-way reconcile
is already recorded (ANALYSIS "The Golem family (S1-D-3)" вЂ” axis 47
delegates, style46/47 stay unwired references); the discarded TR-D3s48
partial adds nothing the landed arm lacks except the G1 field sketch.

### Deviations (deliberate, documented)

* sounds skipped (their RNG consumed); `TargetClosest` counted, not run (the
  fishron precedent - the caller's env rides unchanged); `netMode != 1` is the
  single-player constant true, `NetMessage.SendData` skipped; HitEffect/
  `active = false` ride the despawn/kill flags (`life = 0` convention);
* the HasNaNs dead-store Vector2 constructions (`:64862-64865`,
  `:64931-64934`, `:65067-65070`) and the `new List<int>().Add` dead store
  (`:64571`) annotated, not ported (pure, no RNG, result unused in the C#);
* the f32/double seams kept literal: Length/Distance = f32 sum under the double
  sqrt cast back; Normalize = the XNA reciprocal-first unguarded shape (the
  style55 precedent); RotatedBy = float cos/sin of the double angle; the ring
  angles all-f32 (the `(float)Math.PI * 2f` casts), widened at the call;
* the clone view is caller-supplied (ascending slot order) - the C# scans
  `Main.npc[0..maxNPCs]` five times per tick; the port folds the scans into
  one slice (same order, same membership predicate `active && type == 440 &&
  ai[3] == whoAmI`); a clone killed mid-step stays in the slice with
  `active = false` - the purge/despawn arms are the only mid-step kills and

## The Pufferfish puff-flag fix (W4-c4 follow-up, 2026-11-21, code-only)

The puff state machine (`NPC.cs:23498-23571`) was already ported verbatim
in `npc_ai_style16.rs` (the justHit latch ai[2]=1/localAI[0]=180, the
countdown deflate/re-arm at 120, the 0.98 damp + water-line hover + the
early return that skips the rotation tail) and the `num46 += 10` anchor
(`Main.cs:23115-23117`) landed in `render/entities.rs`. The DEFECT was the
wiring seam: `update_swimmer` fed `Ai16Ctx.just_hit` the **`hurt_cd > 0`
cooldown stand-in** (the S1-D-3 reconcile's note "the port has no one-tick
flag"). The one-tick `Npc::just_hit` flag NOW exists (armed by `hurt` at
`NPC.cs:81274`, cleared at the update tail `:90516` — the Hungry/Creeper
wiring). The cooldown (~11 ticks) outlives the flag, so at the deflate
boundary (`:23518-23521`, `if (this.justHit) ai[2]=1`) the stand-in
**re-puffed the Pufferfish through the whole cooldown tail** — the W95
Creeper defect class.

**Fix:** `update_swimmer` now passes `just_hit: self.just_hit` (the

**The arm.** `NPC.AI`'s inline `else if (this.aiStyle == 64)` block,
`NPC.cs:34019-34248` (no `AI_064_*` method). Ported 1:1 in the module,

**Faithfulness traps kept (each has a witness):**
- The 677 TOP-margin clamp writes `base.velocity.Y = 3f` (`:34098`),
  NOT the aim `num959` — the aim keeps its unclamped value while the
  velocity is pinned; the pin feeds the `:34189` blend. The other three
  margins clamp the aim.
- `ToTileCoordinates` (`:34073`, margins) is `(int)X >> 4` — an
  arithmetic shift (`Utils.cs:1807-1810`); the glow tail's
  `(int)Center.X / 16` (`:34156-34157`) TRUNCATES toward zero. They
  differ below coordinate 0 (witnessed with a negative-centre fly).
- The down-scan's `velocity.Y *= 0.9f` is INSIDE the 4-tile loop
  (`:34200-34203`) — up to four damps per tick, one per blocking tile
  (solid OR `liquid > 0`); the up-scan's 30-tile walk counts solid only
  and damps ONCE after the scan (`:34220-34227`).
- `num963 -= Main.rand.Next(100, 251)` (`:34050`) is a CONDITIONAL draw
  (only when `position.Y > player.Y - 100f`) — the stream length shifts
  with the geometry; the far speed ladder draws the base `Next(50,151)`
  AND the band replacement (`:34037-34045` — both draws happen, the
  second wins).
- The far/near normalize is f64 `Math.Sqrt` over an INT sum, cast to f32
  BEFORE the divide (`:34052`/`:34062`); NO zero guard — the C# NaN/Inf
  passes through into `ai[0]`/`ai[1]`. Kept.
- `Entity.DirectionFrom` (`Entity.cs:210-213`) is XNA `Normalize(Center
  - Source)` — a zero vector yields NaN, carried by the f32 threat sum
  (slot order matters). The flee's `SafeNormalize(Vector2.Zero)`
  (`Utils.cs:1837-1844`) folds zero/NaN to (0,0), so a NaN velocity
  zeroes at the 8-cap. Kept.
- `Hitbox.Distance(Center)` is `Utils.cs:1507-1542`'s rect-to-point
  distance over the INT-truncated Hitbox (`Entity.cs:171-183`): the
  `FloatIntersect` touching-edge overlap (`Utils.cs:982-989`), the axis
  bands, the corner `Vector2.Distance`. The threat scan reads ONLY
  `active` for players (`:34132` — dead/ghost players still scare).
- `Main.tileSolid[type]` is the RUNTIME table — 192 (living-tree leaves)
  cleared after generation (`WorldGen.cs:15714`, the
  `collision.rs::solid_kind` precedent). Platforms (`tileSolidTop`) do
  NOT bounce; liquid bounces on the down-scan only.

**RNG by construction.** The arm's only `Main.rand` draws, in C# order:
the scale latch `Next(75,111)` (`:34028`, once, before the rearm check);
on rearm — `TargetClosest()` (`:34032`, draws nothing) THEN
`Next(60,180)` (`:34033`), then either the FAR sequence
(`Next(50,151)` [+ `Next(150,201)`/`Next(100,151)` band replacement],
`Next(100,251)` direction-scaled X, `Next(-50,51)`, the CONDITIONAL
`Next(100,251)` Y-bias) or the NEAR quad (`Next(5,151)`,
`Next(-100,101)` x2); then the non-677 idle else `Next(30,180)` +
the CONDITIONAL `Next(10,30)` (`:34181-34185`, night OR
`(double)(Y/16f) > worldSurface + 10.0` — the f64 compare). Rearm and
idle can share a tick; the rearm's draws precede. Everything else (the
margins, the flee scan, the blend, the bounces, the rotation) is pure
maths. The witnesses mirror the cited `Next` calls on a CLONED
`UnifiedRandom` and assert stream-state equality (`PartialEq`) — a
drifted order or a skipped draw fails by construction.

**Deliberate folds (all cited in the module):** `Main.netMode != 1` →
true (single-player); `Lighting.AddLight` → `Ai64Effects::light` (the
colours pre-scaled by `scale`, coords truncated here — the wiring feeds

**Fidelity notes (the quirks kept 1:1).**

  quirk; Y uses the FULL old height. `size_override` carries

  roll tick never resizes (the witness pins it).

  (`SpawnedFromStatue`), else all three types `Transform(677 Shimmerfly)`
  (`NPCID.cs:10470`'s `359,677`/`360,677`/`655,677` rows, `NPCID.cs:12031`).
  The 677 kind is unported, so both arms ride `SnailEvents` intents; the
  early return writes no `noGravity` (`None`). The `liquid > 30` gate is
  strict (30 does not shimmer).
- The fall roll `Next(7200)` rides the RIGHT `&&` operand (`:34411`):
  drawn only while `ai[2] == 0`, a gate-FAIL draw is still consumed.
- The fall block's ground probe is
  `(int)(Center.X + width/2 * -direction) / 16` — integer half-width,
  cast AFTER the add (`:34446-34453`); a non-topSlope tile + collideY
  decrements the timer, a bottomSlope ahead flips direction.
- The flag70 wall latch (`:34458-34464`) skips the whole rotation ease;
  the stuck detector (`:34465-34482`) forces direction +1 after 11 ticks
  at the same X (`localAI[2] > 10`).
- The rotation ease captures the target, restores the current rotation
  (`:34577-34578`), wraps at the strict `> 6.28` / `< 0` with the
  `(double)` compare kept as an f64 promotion, then runs TWO separate
  `if`s (not else-if) with the `> 3.14` long-way branch and the
  clamp-to-target.
- `Collision_MoveSnailOnSlopes` (`:92704-92721`, dispatched at
  `:92568-92571` in place of the normal slope pass) keeps the vanilla
  `direction *= -direction` quirk (`:92711`) — for ±1 that is always −1.
  The C#'s `NPC.gravity` argument to `Collision.SlopeCollision` is UNUSED
  in the body (`Collision.cs:1791-2031`; only `WalkDownSlope` reads it,
  `:1688`), so the port's gravity-free `slope_collision` signature is
  faithful.
- `snail_find_frame` is the pure twin
  `(vx, vy, frame, counter) -> (frame, counter)` (the
  `npc_ai_style49.rs::nimbus_find_frame` convention —
  `Npc::frame_counter` is private to `npc.rs`); the wiring drives both
  fields from `find_frame`. Fall rows 4/5 at the 6-tick phase (reset at
  `6*2-1 = 11`), walk rows 0/1/2/3/2/1 at the 10-tick phases (reset at
  `10*6-1 = 59`), zero velocity freezes both (`:72258-72261`).

**RNG by construction.** Exactly TWO `Main.rand` sites in the arm, in
source order, both on the caller's `UnifiedRandom` (the exact `Main.rand`
stream):
1. `Next(80, 111)` (`:34381`) — type 359 ONLY, once, when `ai[3] == 0`
   AND `netMode != 1`; zero draws once `ai[3]` is set (the resize never
   re-rolls).
2. `Next(7200)` (`:34411`) — when `ai[2] == 0` AND `netMode != 1`,
   gate-fail draw consumed; zero draws once the fall timer is armed.
Nothing else draws: the lights, speed split, tile probes, state machine,
rotation ease and velocity tail are RNG-free; `TargetClosest`
(`NPC.cs:77652-77781`) and `SlopeCollision` (`Collision.cs:1791-2031`)
were re-read — no `Main.rand` in either body. The witness tests replay
the stream draw-for-draw against a clone (`assert_eq!(rng, witness)`);
the client path (`netMode == 1`) draws nothing at all.

**Seams.** `SnailEvents::no_gravity` (the arm's `noGravity` writes, last
write wins — `Npc` carries no gravity flag), `SnailEvents::light`
(`(tile_x, tile_y, [r,g,b])` for the `EntityLights` feed,
`npc_lights.rs`'s vocabulary), `shimmer_statue_despawn` /
`shimmer_transform` (the `GetShimmered` intents).

**Documented skips (outside the AI arm).**

### The RNG argument

Every gameplay draw rides the C#'s named stream at the site's own
position in the update order:

- The player-tick queues (hurt/death/jump/Fart/splash/drown/flap) drain
  at the `update_player` pass tail on `UpdatePlayers` — `Player.Update`
  runs under the `Main.cs:17754` swap, and `GrabItems` (`:27428`) runs
  INSIDE it, so the world-pickup chime's C# stream is `UpdatePlayers`
  even though the port's pickup lives in the items pass (the drain
  point differs, the named stream is the source's — the E21h
  queue→drain precedent).
- The revenge ping draws on `UpdateItems` (`WorldItem.UpdateItem` under
  the `Main.cs:17779` swap), right after the share draws in the same
  arm — the draw ORDER inside the arm is the source's.
- The chest transfers run from the click handlers OUTSIDE every swap —
  the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in (`rngs.global()`, the wave-C net-strike
  precedent), snapshotted across the field borrows.
- The grapple fire runs in the player pass before `Player.Update` —
  `UpdatePlayers`, after the gate.
- The attenuation gate precedes EVERY gameplay draw
  (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436` before the switch); a muted or
  out-of-range play consumes nothing. The style façade's GetRandomPitch
  NextFloat rides the audio-only `sound_style_random` (never a gameplay
  stream). The int overload (`SoundEngine.cs:102-108`) draws NO
  GetRandomPitch — the wave's int-id plays consume only their case
  draws.

### The worm sim-pass RNG + placement (W-A2-1, code-only mode)

Audit `docs/research/55-audit-worms.md` (branch `origin/docs/audit-worms`)
finding W-A2-1 — the shared `AI_006_Worms` mechanics in
`world_sim/npcs.rs` (`update_worms_in` + `worm_head_step`), fixed in
place on `fix/worm-rng-placement`. The C# was re-read whole at every
cited window before each edit.

**The fixes (per audit finding):**

- **T1c budget draws (`NPC.cs:51303-51342`).** Every head in the
  `:51303` list rolls `ai[2] = Next(8, 13)` FIRST (`:51310`); type 10
  (GiantWorm) rolls again `Next(4, 7)` (`:51313`), type 117 (Leech)
  again `Next(3, 6)` (`:51341`), type 13 (EoW) overrides with
  `GetEaterOfWorldsSegmentsCount()` (`:51317`) but the first draw was
  still consumed. The pre-fix port drew once per family — a stream
  shift for every later `UpdateNpcs` consumer on every worm spawn.
  Now: draw-then-override, the discarded result kept advancing the
  stream. The Destroyer (`AI_037`'s own roll) and the crawltipede
  (the fixed 30-link spawn, `:51369-51392`) are OUTSIDE the list and
  draw nothing — their spawn routing stays byte-identical (R55 boundary).
- **T1g flag3 scan (`NPC.cs:51525-51597`).** The margins are
  `(int)(x/16)-1 .. (int)((x+w)/16)+2` exclusive-high, clamped; a tile
  counts when `nactive && (tileSolid || (tileSolidTop && frameY==0))`
  OR `liquid > 64` (liquid on INACTIVE tiles too), and only when its
  16-px box actually overlaps the NPC rect (`:51586`). Each
  overlapping tile draws `Main.rand.Next(100)` (`:51590`) — the draw
  sits BEFORE the `type != 117 && nactive && tileSolid` guards in the
  C# `&&` chain, so Leech heads and liquid-only tiles consume it too;
  on 0 the effect-only `KillTile(fail:true, effectOnly:true)` fires
  (dust only — the dust effect rides the unwired dust seam, the DRAW
  cannot be skipped). The pre-fix scan had no margins, no overlap
  test, no solidTop arm, liquid gated on active, and no draw at all —
  a per-digging-tick stream divergence. The always-fly presets
  (`:51548-51567`) skip the scan entirely (`!flag3 | flag2` is false);
  of the ported kinds only the crawltipede 412-414 (`:51560-51563`) —
  ported so its stream stays draw-free.
- **T1a head rotation (`NPC.cs:52201`).** `rotation = Atan2(vy, vx) +
  Math.PI/2` at the tail of the no-leader `else` — every head, every
  tick. The pre-fix `worm_head_step` never wrote rotation (heads drew
  frame-up while digging sideways). The heads use PI/2
  (`FRAC_PI_2`), the followers keep the `1.57f` literal (`:51878`) —
  the two constants stay distinct.
- **T2b child placement (`NPC.cs:51347` + `NewNPC:80770` +
  `Entity.cs:128-131`).** `NewNPC` sets `Bottom = (X, Y)`:
  `child.pos = (X - width/2, Y - height)` with
  `X = (int)(pos.X + (float)(width/2))` — the width is an INT, so
  `width/2` is integer division — and `Y = (int)(pos.Y + height)`.
  The child's BOTTOM sits at the parent's bottom; the pre-fix port
  put the child's TOP there, one child-height low per link, and did
  not int-truncate. Fixed.
- **T2c pass order.** C# runs `AI_006` inside each NPC's `Update` in
  slot order; `NewNPC`'s `Start = whoAmI` gives every child a higher
  slot, so the head moves first and each follower snaps to the
  leader's SAME-TICK centre. The pre-fix pass ran followers before
  heads — a one-tick lag along the chain. Now heads first, then the
  follower trail in ascending slot order (= ascending `seg_index`).
- **T1d surface gate (`NPC.cs:51110-51148`).** `flag = true` for
  types 10/39/95/117/510 (ported: GiantWorm, Leech); target dead OR
  (flag && player above `worldSurface*16`) → `EncourageDespawn(300)`
  (the existing `despawn_timer` seam) + `velocity.Y += 0.2` while
  gated. The dead-target arm runs for every segment (family-wide).
  The `TargetClosest()` retarget has no single-player seam (the
  target IS the one player) — documented. The 513/510/621 rows ride
  their kind waves.
- **T1e corruption escape (`NPC.cs:52004-52050`).** INSIDE the dig
  branch after the aim scale: Devourer/EoW whose target is outside
  Corrupt/Crimson or dead → flag6; no living player in ZoneCorrupt
  (flag7 — Corrupt only, NOT Crimson) → below
  `(rockLayer + maxTilesY)/2` the head deactivates and walks the
  `ai[0]` chain dead (the port kills the head + every DOWNSTREAM
  `seg_index` of its `worm_id` — an EoW split fragment ahead keeps
  its own life, as the C# walk never reaches it), and the aim
  overrides to straight down (`num48 = 0, num49 = num45`).
- **T1f 1000-px override (`NPC.cs:51598-51615`).** A listed head
  (ported: Devourer/GiantWorm/EoW/Leech) with no player inside the
  ±1000-px box around its rect forces flag3 (one rectangle test,
  strict inequalities, int-truncated positions).

**The RNG argument (stream-position parity).** `UnifiedRandom` is the
exact .NET subtractive stream (`next_range`/`next_max` = one
`Sample()` each). Per head kind, at chain start: Devourer 1 draw

### Structure decisions

- The four aiStyle-1 kinds ride the slice-A/B module shape
  (`projectile_ai_frostmoon::step` + `finish_flight`, the verbatim
  `ai_style1_flight` tail replication) — the C# block order preserved:
  hook group → flag3 counter → below-counter hooks → the gravity else-if
  chain → the shared tail. 345 counts (not on the flag3 list) and pins at
  50 in its own arm; 348/349/350 rest (`:55985-55987`) so the generic
  `ai[0] >= 15` gravity never opens for them — they fly straight (the
  349's +0.2 is its own hook's, applied every tick).
- The aiStyle-14 pair are HEADS only: the dispatch runs `ornament` /
  `spike_pulse` and then the SAME generic `ai_spear` tail — no parallel
  flight copy. The 346 burst's five spawns ride back to the pool
  (`ShrapnelSpawn`, the nebula request shape) and drain through
  `spawn_with_data_ai_owned` with the ornament's owner, Damage 40 / KB 0
  (`:24894`), `ai1 = ornament.ai[1]` (the frame payload), the box centred
  (`NewProjectile` `:10876-10877` — the spawn site subtracts the 6x6
  half-box). The spawned shrapnel is flipped `friendly = false` (the
  `spawn_hostile` convention — the row's stock friendly is false, the
  pool's slot default true).
- The style-58 arm is inline in the module (`present`) and gated to 351
  in the dispatch — the style's only rowed kind, so no other kind's
  behaviour changes. The C#'s two consecutive `if`s (`:28913`/`:28926`)
  are kept: the tick that flips ai[0] to 1 runs BOTH blocks (frame 1, the
  second +0.1, the drag) in the same tick — the witness pins it.
- The 346 burst's `owner == Main.myPlayer` gate (`:24883`) folds to the
  pool's `simulated` gate: the port models hostile shots as owner 255
  (`spawn_hostile`) while the C# spawns with `Owner: Main.myPlayer`
  (`NPC.cs:32885`); the arm only runs on locally-simulated slots
  (`projectile.rs:12961-12965`), which IS the owner test in the
  single-player port (the saucer precedent).

### RNG by construction

- **Zero-draw arms**: 345 (`:57116-57128` — the latch is sound-only), 348
  (`:56246-56273` — sound-only latch), 349 (`:56221-56245`), 352
  (`:24848-24866`), 351 (`:28906-28937`) contain no `Main.rand` call at
  all. Their ports cannot drift any stream.
- **350's dust window** (`:55138-55157`): `Next(3)` (+ inner `Next(10)`),
  `Next(4)` (+ inner `Next(5)`) — every draw feeds `Main.dust` alone, no
  observable state. The window is SKIPPED whole with its draws (the
  aiStyle-1 pool's zero-RNG convention, the slice-A/B precedent — the
  same documented stream-position deviation those slices carry). No
  trajectory can change; the deviation is the convention, recorded here.
- **346's burst** (`:24885-24894`): the draws FEED observable state (the
  five shrapnel velocities) and are KEPT on the pass's threaded stream in
  the C#'s exact order — per fragment `Next(-20,21)` → `Next(-20,0)` →
  `Next(-30,31)` (SpeedX's jitter, named-argument evaluation order) →
  `Next(-30,31)` (SpeedY's). The Y draw's range tops at −1, so the
  `10/sqrt(dx²+dy²)` normalise never divides by zero. The recording-stream
  witness (`the_ornament_bursts_five_shrapnel_in_draw_order`) pins the
  20-draw sequence. The burst fires once per ornament (timeLeft == 1),
  so the stream cost is deterministic per spawn.
- The spawn-site draws (`NPC.cs:32838`'s `Next(0,31)` ai0 payload,
  `:32885`'s `Next(2)` frame pick, `:33607`'s `Next(5)`, the velocity
  jitters) belong to the NPC-side machines (the S1-F-13c frost-boss
  slices own them — `npc_ai_frost_boss.rs`/`_b.rs` already carry them);
  this round adds no spawn site, so no UpdateNPCs-stream position moves.

### Deliberate skips

Dust (350's window, 346/349's Kill bursts `:74171-74181`/`:74236-74249`,
345's Kill burst `:74020-74028` — all dust/sound-only), light (346's
per-frame `AddLight` `:24877`/`:24881`, 350's `:55137`), sound (345 Item1,
346 Item1, 348 Item8, 350 Item42), `netUpdate`, `coldDamage` (348/349 —
damage-side, no consumer). The `Kill()` dust arms need no port: the pool's
death path carries no per-kind Kill hooks for these kinds and the C#
blocks roll nothing observable.

blocks is dust-only — its result feeds nothing but a dust count/velocity/
scale, never state: the 638 proximity burst `Next(15,31)` (`:55889`), the
640 dust gates `Next(extraUpdates)`/`Next(2|6)`/`Next(2)`/`NextDouble`/
`Next(10)` (`:55453-55470`) and the numUpdates==1 trail dust
(`:55473-55481`), the Kill() dust counts `Next(5,10)` (`:73433`) and
`Next(2,5)` (`:76123`). Skipping them with the dust layer therefore keeps
every state-bearing decision identical (the ai001_a/b dust-skip
convention). The ported arms draw nothing, so the pass's UpdateProjectiles
stream is untouched for every OTHER kind — byte-identical by construction.
The `damage_pve` decay is pure arithmetic (no variance draw added).

### The stream argument (why the drain is safe)

`Main.UpdateProjectiles` runs under the `Main.rand` swap
(`Main.cs:17775-17777`): every `PlaySound` inside the projectile walk —
the AI arms AND the `Kill()` tail — draws its case-2 pitch from the
`UpdateProjectiles` stream. The port queues each play as a
`(id, style, x, y, pitchOffset)` intent (`Projectile.wants_sound`, the
`wants_mark_spawn` pattern; the pool forwards it into
`pending_proj_sounds` right after the dispatch) and drains at the pass
tail in `world_sim/projectiles.rs` — AFTER the wave-C NPC-hit drain, on
the same named stream. `Audio::play_proj_sound` gates attenuation BEFORE
any draw (`LegacySoundPlayer.cs:369-436` precedes the case switch), the
E21e precedent; the `GetRandomPitch` NextFloat rides the audio-only
`sound_style_random`. The C# plays mid-walk; the port's batch drain moves
the draw to the pass tail — the same recorded deviation as wave C's
strike plays (relative order among the tick's sound draws is preserved;
the interleaving with gameplay draws is not). The witness tests pin the
contract: muted/out-of-range plays draw NOTHING, an audible play draws
exactly one `Next(-6, 7)` on `UpdateProjectiles`, every other stage
stream stays pristine.

  `Volume *= 0.15f * ai[0]` on the returned instance) is DEFERRED — the

  (Center) and −1 latch are ported.

  Gated to the five kinds `explode_bomb` accepts.

  ported row — deferred; the generic 8-tick arm covers the ported

  either way (the drain runs at the pass tail), so one helper keeps the

### B-6d-1 — the apocalypse slot table (FIXED)

`WorldGen.UpdateLunarApocalypse` (`WorldGen.cs:86693-86748`) sets one
flag per tower TYPE (517 solar / 422 vortex / 507 nebula / 493 stardust,
`:86708-86725`). The port's match had `NebulaTower => 2` AND
`NebulaTower => 3` — the second arm unreachable, slot 2 (vortex) never
set, so `tower_active_vortex` cleared on the first update after any
tower death and `:86744`'s all-four doom gate could fire with the Vortex
pillar standing. Fixed to `VortexTower => 2` / `NebulaTower => 3` — the
slot order keeps the flag writes (`lunar.rs:147-150`) consistent (the
audit's alternative "VortexTower => 3" would have crossed the

### B-6d-4 — the DD2 lane fade window (AUDIT FALSE POSITIVE, no change)

Audit 53 §4.1 defect 1 claimed `npc.rs:10769` ramps 500→550 while C#
ramps 500→600, and that the port's scale at death is 0.05 vs C#'s 0.525.
Re-verified against source — the claim miscomputes its own cite:
- C# `NPC.cs:41028`: `scale = Lerp(1, 0.05, GetLerpValue(500, 600,
  ai[0], clamped: true))`.
- `Utils.GetLerpValue` (`Utils.cs:315-343`) with clamped=true returns
  0 below 500, 1 above 600, else `(t - from) / (to - from)` =
  `(ai[0] - 500) / (600 - 500)` = `(ai[0] - 500) / 100`.
- The port: `let t = ((self.ai[0] - 500.0) / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  self.scale = 1.0 + (0.05 - 1.0) * t;` — algebraically IDENTICAL.
- At the death tick `ai[0] == 550` (`NPC.cs:41038`): t = 0.5, scale =
  1 − 0.95·0.5 = 0.525 in BOTH. The gate dies mid-fade in vanilla too;
  the 600 endpoint is never reached. The audit's "port finishes at 550"
  reading treated the `/100` divisor as a 100-tick window ending at the
  death tick — but the divisor is the C#'s own `to - from`.
No code change (the golden rule forbids "fixing" faithful code). A
witness test pins the window at 500 (scale 1), 525 (0.7625) and the 550
death (0.525, hp 0, unshielded) so no future pass narrows it.

## The pillar shield loop (B-6b, 2026-11-19, code-only mode)

Audit research/53 (`docs/audit-pillars-dd2lanes`, rows 1c/2b) found the
pillar shield STATE faithful but unwired: `tower_shield_absorb` /
`update_tower_shields` had test-only callers, the towers never read
`tower_shield_*`, and no live code spawned the 629 TowerDamageBolt —
pillars were killable by direct damage from tick 1 and no mob kill ever
chipped a shield. This round wires the loop
(`task/S1-D-3-pillar-shield-loop`).

**The C# machine (read whole).**

- **Spawn sites** — `NPC.cs:79279-79320`, inside `checkDead`'s
  pre-death type switch: solar mobs 412-419+518 spawn a 629 while
  `ShieldStrengthTowerSolar > 0` with `ai0 = FindFirstNPC(517)`;
  vortex 425/426/427/429 → host 422; nebula 420/421/423/424 → host 507;
  stardust 402/405/407/409/411 → host 493. Each call is
  `NewProjectile(source, Center.X, Center.Y, 0f, 0f, 629, 0, 0f,
  Main.myPlayer, FindFirstNPC(host))` — damage 0, velocity 0, knockback
  0. `FindFirstNPC` (`NPC.cs:89885-89895`) returns the first active
  slot of the type, **-1** on miss. NOT in the sets: 428
  (VortexHeadcrab), 406 (StardustCellSmall), 410 (StardustSpiderSmall).
  The `checkDead` carrier guard (`NPC.cs:78042`: `realLife >= 0 &&
  realLife != whoAmI`) skips linked segments — the crawltipede
  bodies/tails ride the carrier's death events.
- **The spend** — `Projectile.cs:72944-72979` (the 629's `Kill` arm,
  `netMode != 1`): switch on `Main.npc[(int)ai[0]].type` (the HOST
  NPC's type — `ai[0]` is an NPC index, not a tower ordinal); if the
  matching shield `!= 0` set the host's `ai[3] = 1` (the flash
  trigger), then `Shield = (int)MathHelper.Clamp(Shield - 1, 0,
  ShieldStrengthTowerMax)` — **−1 per bolt regardless of damage**.
- **The gate** — `NPC.cs:39101-39115` (aiStyle 94, every tick):
  `dontTakeDamage = ShieldStrengthTower<Kind> != 0` per type. While
  the shield stands the tower refuses every hit; the shield falls ONLY
  through 629 contacts. `downedTower*`/`TowerActive*` are written by
  the tower's DEATH (`NPC.cs:79321-79345`), never by shield
  exhaustion. The ai[3] flash cycle (`:39069-39100`: NPCDeath58 on
  the shield-state flip, NPCDeath3 at ai[3]==1, the 120-wrap) reads the
  trigger the spend writes.

**The wiring (Rust).**

| C# | Rust | position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NPC.cs:79279-79320` spawn cases | `world_sim/npcs.rs::spawn_tower_damage_bolts` | `update_npcs` death path, BEFORE the tower death arms (the C# switch's mob cases precede the pillar cases) |
| `NPC.cs:89885-89895` FindFirstNPC | the `app.npcs.iter().position(kind && hp>0)` scan, -1.0 on miss | inside the spawn loop; the port's compacted vec index is the sim's current whoAmI (the saucer-deathray seam precedent) |
| `NPC.cs:39101-39115` dontTakeDamage gate | `world_sim/npcs.rs::apply_tower_shield_gates` | `update_npcs` death-path tail (after the death arms, so cultist-spawned towers are gated the same tick) |
| `Projectile.cs:72953` etc. −1 spend | `world_sim/npcs.rs::tower_shield_absorb` (RESHAPED: −1 clamp 0..max, returns the pre-spend `!= 0`) | the fn seam; the live 629 arm call site is R71's |
| `NPC.cs:95247-95251` all-dead reset | `world_sim/npcs.rs::update_tower_shields` (was test-only) | `update_npcs` death-path tail |
| the hurt/strike/PVE refusals | pre-existing gates: `npc.rs` hurt's `dont_take_damage` check, the strike gate, `projectile.rs` PVE walk's `!nPC.dontTakeDamage` (`Projectile.cs:12583`) | unchanged — the gate pass now feeds them live |

The spawn rides `spawn_hostile_ai` (the `HostileShotAi` seam): kind
629, the mob's CENTRE (the port's seam carries centres; the C#
`NewProjectile` subtracts half the extent at `Projectile.cs:10876-

**The absorb reshape (audit §2.2's fix spec).** The old
`tower_shield_absorb(world, tower, dmg)` drained `dmg` per hit and
flipped `downed_tower_*`/`tower_active_*` at zero — both wrong

(`the_absorb_drains_and_flags_the_down`) is repointed to the faithful
model (`the_absorb_chips_one_per_bolt_and_never_downs`).

**RNG argument (by construction).** The spawn loop draws NOTHING: the
C# cases contain no `Main.rand` call, and `NewProjectile` for type
629 draws nothing either — aiStyle 122 is not the aiStyle-1 velocity
damp (`Projectile.cs:10895-10902`), 629 is absent from the owner-rand
spawn arms (`:10907-10919`: 206/335/358/406), the golf-ball and
CD-copy sets (`ProjectileID.cs:191`), the timeLeft overrides and
`FinalizeProjectile`'s 93/113/gem arms (`:22043-22061`). The gate
pass and the reset are pure state writes. The all-streams census
witness (`the_spawn_loop_draws_nothing`) pins every named stream
byte-identical across a two-kill loop.

**Boundaries / deliberate folds.**

- **The 629 arm's spend call site** (`projectile.rs:13502-13521`:
  drains `slot.damage`, selects by `ai[0] as usize` ordinal, never
  sets ai[3]) is **R71** (`fix/lunar-dd2-small-wrongs`) — this branch

- **The pillar AI machine re-port is B-6a (queued)** — the stand-in
  `update_ancient_cultist`'s 180-tick self-kill (ai[2] misused as a
  timer; the C# ai[2] is the dissolve FLAG set by `checkDead`

- **Gate/reset position fold**: the C# runs the gate inside the pillar

- **R71 handoff resolutions** (LEAD-R71-HANDOFF, consumed): (1) the
