## The small-kinds wiring wave (S1-D-3-wire-smallkinds, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

Four landed-UNWIRED NPC-AI modules from the entity-ai-census §2b worklist
are now WIRED: the Blazing Wheel (aiStyle 21, type 72), the Angry Nimbus
(aiStyle 49, type 250), the Dungeon Spirit (aiStyle 56, type 288) and the
Force Bubble (aiStyle 72, type 384). Each was a pure module with no
`NpcKind`, no dispatch arm, no anchors/PORT_MAP row on main. This wave
adds the four kinds + their `SetDefaults` rows + the dispatch claims +
the minimal Ctx seams, retiring the stand-in routing with `unreachable!`
markers (the aiStyle-5/9 precedent). The modules' own witness tests stay
as the audit cross-check; three new wiring tests per kind are WRITTEN,
NOT RUN — **no compiler invoked**.

**The kinds + protocol ids.** `NpcKind::{BlazingWheel, AngryNimbus,
DungeonSpirit, ForceBubble}` (`npc.rs`). The protocol ids (`to_u16` /
`from_u16`, `npc/data.rs`): AngryNimbus 250, DungeonSpirit 288,
ForceBubble 384 keep their vanilla ids (all free); BlazingWheel takes the
port-local **353** because the vanilla 72 slot is the MartianWalker's
(`to_u16`'s bijection guard). `cs_id()` returns the vanilla `NPC.type`
(72/250/288/384) for the AI arms' type gates. Every exhaustive `NpcKind`
match gained arms (scripted scan): `to_u16`, `ai_style`, `size`,
`max_hp`, `contact_damage`, `defense`, `value`, `render_key`,
`update_kind_ai`, `find_frame`, `debuff_immune_ids`, the netglue
`npc_seed`, the bestiary portrait table, the draw match. The `SetDefaults`
rows are verbatim (`NPC.cs:9714-9731` / `:12221-12233` / `:12738-12752` /
`:13882-13894`): the wheel's alpha 100 / behindTiles / dontTakeDamage /
scale 1.2 land in `Npc::new`; the bubble's kb 1 (the head default,
`:8533`) and dmg 0 (`:8563`) are explicit rows.

**The dispatch split (the Ctx seams).** `Npc::update_rng`'s aiStyle axis
(`npc.rs`) claims 21/49/56/72:
- **21 (BlazingWheel)** — the arm runs inline: `ai_style21` (the

`NPC.cs:56222-56251`) is wired through `Npc::martian_officer_bubble`
(called after the officer's walker step in `update_kind_ai`): the spawn
gate (`carrier_uid == 0 && local_ai[0] == 0`) raises `wants_force_bubble`
+ the `localAI[0] = -1` latch; a living linked bubble sets
`dont_take_damage = true`; a dropped link starts the 180-tick re-spawn
cooldown. The world-sim drain spawns the ForceBubble at the officer's
centre (`NewNPC`'s `Bottom` placement, `NPC.cs:80770`, the `(int)Center`
truncation), stamps `timeLeft = (int)(activeTime * 1.25)` = 937
(`:80772`, `activeTime = 750` `:95186`), and links the pair through the
stable uid (`carrier_uid`, the Moon Lord parts' convention — the C#'s
`ai[2] = slot + 1` / the bubble's `ai[0] = whoAmI` hold slot indices the
compacting list cannot keep). The rider pre-pass resolves the uid to the
current slot each tick and writes `ai[0]` before the module call.

**Order deviation (documented).** The C# runs the bubble's aiStyle-72
arm at the bubble's own slot turn; the port runs it in a pre-pass at
tick start (the sibling-slot read needs the whole list borrowed
immutably before the per-NPC `&mut` loop). The snap therefore reads the
officer's PREVIOUS-tick centre when the officer's slot is later — the
one-tick lag the carrier write-through family (WoF / Moon Lord /
Scutlix) already carries. The arm is RNG-free, so the placement does not
move any stream. The DungeonSpirit's arm DOES run at its slot turn (the
dust draws keep their slot order).

**RNG census (preserved).** The wheel (21) and the bubble (72) draw NO
`Main.rand` by construction (the modules' headers pin this). The
nimbus (49) draws exactly one `Next(14)` per fired shot. The spirit
(56) draws the six cited `NewDust` rolls (the pressure-band gate + pos
X/Y + vel X/Y + frame row + scale) per tick through the pool. The
officer's spawn/shield block draws nothing. No new stream is introduced;
the `UpdateNPCs` stream's draw order is unchanged for every pre-existing
kind (the four new kinds only add their own draws at their own slots).

**Atlas headroom (verified, no compiler).** The four kinds draw their
own sheets (`NPC_72` 34×144, `NPC_250` 48×168, `NPC_288` 28×102,
`NPC_384` 48×52 — decoded via the prebuilt `tr-content` `dims` example,
not a fresh compile). A best-fit-decreasing shelf simulation over all
737 static sheets (the `Atlas::build_ref` algorithm, `max_width` 8192,
PAD 2) shows the four sheets backfill existing shelves: the static
atlas grows 5318 → 5322 px (**+4 px**), far inside the 71 px headroom
under the 8192 strict-GPU bound. The `item_icon_uvs_are_normalized_and_atlas_fits`
test (`atlas.height <= 8192`) stays green. The bestiary sheet table
(`BESTIARY_NPC_SHEET_IDS`, 175 → 179) and the portrait arms gained the
four rows; the `npc_sheets` map keys them by vanilla net id.

**Deliberate skips (unchanged from the modules).** The nimbus's
netMode gate folds to the host path; the dust/thunder sound layers and
the wet/slope collision halves are unported engine work; the 264 rain
projectile's own aiStyle-45 arm is M4-PROJ work. The bubble's HitEffect
dust arm (`NPC.cs:84342-84361`, dust 226, no gore) is the count-only
visual skip (`bubble_hit_dust_plan`). The spirit's zero-distance NaN is
the C#'s own (no invented clamp). The wheel's `dontTakeDamage` makes it

## The saucer wiring (S1-D-3-wire-saucer, code-only)

`task/S1-D-3-wire-saucer` wires R34's faithful `npc_ai_style75.rs` module
into the live sim, closing the **P0 event-progression blocker** the R58b
audit flagged as M3: the live `update_saucer_mount` had NO phase bridge,
so killing the Martian saucer crew (392 shell / 393 turrets / 394 cannons)
NEVER opened the core 395 and the invasion fight could not progress. The
old witness `the_dead_crew_opening_the_core_kills_it` asserted
`core.is_some() || invasion_type == 0` — a tautology that admitted the gap.

**Base.** The work is based on R34's module branch
`task/S1-D-3-aistyle75` (tip `ac1f45a2`), merged onto `origin/main`
(`c7fe175d`) in the `TR-wire16` worktree — the chain lands both the module
and the wiring. CODE-ONLY MODE: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; the
new witnesses are written, not run.

**What the wiring does.**
- **Axis claim.** `npc.rs::update_rng`'s aiStyle axis gains
  `75 => self.update_rng_style75_solo(...)`; the six kinds' kind-match arms
  (`ScutlixRider`, `MartianSaucer`/`Turret`/`Cannon`, `FlyingDutchmanCannon`,
  `SolarDrakomireRider`) become `unreachable!` markers and the three
  stand-in functions are deleted. The duplicate dead saucer arm
  (`npc.rs:4036-4038` in the audit) is marked unreachable too.
- **Pooled sim path.** The family machine is a POOL step (the host/crew
  slot links read `App::npcs` live), so `world_sim/npcs.rs`'s tick closure
  runs `style75_step(npcs, i, ...)` in slot order on the `UpdateNPCs`
  stream for every aiStyle-75 NPC — ahead of the solo `update_rng` axis
  (which only sees a one-slot pool). The shared `NPC.Update` preamble is
  extracted to `Npc::update_preamble`; the pooled arm runs
  preamble → `style75_step` → `find_frame` → `contact`, matching
  `update_rng`. The solo wrapper (`update_rng_style75_solo`) keeps bare
  `update_rng` test callers faithful over a one-slot pool.
- **Slot-aligned links.** `carrier_link_pre_pass` (+ its linear A/B twin)
  now writes the slot-aligned `ai[0]` host link (the module's
  `npcs[ai[0]]` read) and the 392 shell's `local_ai[0..3]` crew slots (the
  C#'s `localAI` links, `NPC.cs:36095-36102`), adds the 416 DrakomireRider,
  and NO LONGER kills orphaned mounts — the module owns the orphan-death
  (`:36064-36069`) and the riders' `Transform(382/518)` fallbacks
  (`:36056-36063`). A hostless mount gets `ai[0] = -1`.
- **Seam drains.** `Style75Out.shots` → `wants_hostile_shot` /
  `wants_hostile_shot_ai` (the sim's shot drain resolves them);
  `spawn_carrier` → `wants_mount_carrier` (a resolve pass spawns the 391/415
  Bottom-placed, `NPC.cs:80770`, `timeLeft = 750`); `transform` →
  `wants_transform` (a resolve pass runs `Npc::transform_to_kind`, the
  `NPC.Transform` maths `:81084-81114`); `sounds` → `Audio::play_use_sound`
  drained at the C# call position on the `UpdateNPCs` stream (the case-2
  `Next(-6,7)` pitch draw, `LegacySoundPlayer.cs:632`); `died` → hp already
  0, the death pass owns HitEffect + deactivation. Dust spawns through the
  REAL `DustPool::new_dust` on `app.dust` with `app.spawn_ctx()`.

**M1–M4 resolution (the audit's mount defects).**
- **M1 (seats unrotated/unscaled)** — RESOLVED by activation: the module's
  ride offsets do `offset *= core.scale` THEN `RotatedBy(core.rotation)`
  (`NPC.cs:35547-35551` shell, `:35623-35627` turret, `:35637-35641`
  cannon, `:35652-35656` Dutchman), exactly the C# order. The wiring feeds
  the live core's `scale`/`rotation` through the slot-aligned pool.
- **M2 (grouped one-emitter battery)** — RESOLVED by activation: the module
  draws ONE `Next(maxValue4/5)` gate per LIVE-flag emitter in the order
  turret-left, turret-right, cannon-left, cannon-right, each hit drawing
  its own NextDouble/NextDouble/Next/Next chain (`NPC.cs:35978-36025`).
  The wiring runs that exact code on the `UpdateNPCs` stream.
- **M3 (phase bridge absent)** — RESOLVED: the module's 392 arm implements
  the bridge (`NPC.cs:35552-35613`, read whole): flag80 = core in [0,1) AND
  no crew lives; the %200 crew netUpdate marks; crew all dead → core
  `ai[0] = 3` (classic) / `1` (expert) + zero ai[1..3] + netUpdate. The
  wiring drains it through the sim (the module writes the core slot
  directly in the pooled step). The tautology witness is replaced by
  `the_dead_crew_open_the_core_and_the_fight_progresses`: live crew blocks
  the bridge, dead crew opens the core (ai[0]=3, ai[1..3]=0), the core's
  death ride (`NPC.cs:36104-36107`) kills it next tick.
- **M4 (despawn-ride restore inverted)** — the −1→0 / −2→2 restore lives in
  the CORE's aiStyle-76 machine (`update_saucer_core`, `NPC.cs:36130-36149`),
  which is R35's branch territory (89b65c54, in-place fixes). This wiring
  does NOT touch `update_saucer_core`; the bridge writes core `ai[0]` only.
  The module's mount-side M4 concern (the riders' despawn mirrors) is
  carried by `DiscourageDespawn(60)` + the `timeLeft` mirrors.

**RNG argument.** The wiring adds NO draws of its own: the sim calls the
SAME `style75_step` on the SAME `UpdateNPCs` stream the module's 16
witnesses pin (per-slot battery gates + hit chains + dust gates, the real
`DustPool::new_dust` internals, the sentinel velocity writes). The only
new stream consumers are the Item12/Item39 sound drains, which the module
already accounts for via `Style75Out::sounds` (the audio seam owns the one
`Next(-6,7)` pitch draw per audible play, at the C# call position). The
carrier-spawn/Transform resolves draw nothing (`NewNPC`/`Transform`/
`TargetClosest` are RNG-free). The `the_wired_style75_path_is_rng_parity_deterministic`
witness pins two identical apps to byte-identical NPC state + the
`UpdateNPCs` stream at the same position.

**Boundary.** Core 395 rides aiStyle 76 = R35's branch (`89b65c54`,
in-place fixes). `update_saucer_core` is UNTOUCHED; the bridge writes the
core's `ai[0]` (and zeroes ai[1..3]) only, exactly as the C# shell arm does.

**Verification.** Code-only: every seam call site checked against the
actual signatures by read/grep (`style75_step`'s 8-arg shape,
`Style75Ctx`/`Style75Out` fields, `play_use_sound`'s 6-arg shape,

and Transform (`:81084-81148`) and NewNPC Bottom placement (`:80755-80784`)
were re-read whole. The progression/retirement/RNG-parity witnesses are

## The zombie fighter audit (S1-D-3z, code-only mode, 2026-11-19)

Branch `fix/zombie-fighter-audit-defects` on the chain base `aab09419`
(S1-D-3p walker migration batch 1). Scope: distrust-verbatim audit of the
port's zombie fighter (`npc.rs::update_zombie`, the `AI_003_Fighters`
family, `NPC.cs:55856-60339`) + the missing small zombie variant kinds.
**Code-only mode — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked; every test below
is WRITTEN, NOT RUN.**

### The three verified defects (fixed)

**A — the invented daylight burn.** The port accumulated `burn += 1/60`
in daylight and dealt `hp -= 6` per second ("the vanilla burn", the old
M4-first-pass note at ANALYSIS "NPCs and combat" — now corrected in
place). The C# `AI_003_Fighters` has NO daylight damage anywhere in
`:55856-60339`: the discouraged arm's daytime block is
`if (Main.IsItDay() && (double)(position.Y / 16f) < Main.worldSurface
&& type != 624 && type != 631) EncourageDespawn(10)` (`NPC.cs:57377-57380`)
— a 10-tick `timeLeft` flee-despawn window (`EncourageDespawn`
`:7249-7256`, the per-tick decrement + cull `:77986-77996`, mirrored by
the port's `despawn_timer`/`tick_despawn` in `world_sim/npcs.rs`). Fix:
the burn block is removed; the discouraged arm now calls
`encourage_despawn(10)` under the C#'s gate. NOTE the two boundaries are
different compares: the despawn gate is `<` on the TILE coordinate
(`position.Y / 16 < worldSurface`), the chase-discouragement gate is `>`
on PIXELS (`position.Y > worldSurface * 16`, `:60302`). The `burn` field
stays in `Npc` for struct-layout stability but is RETIRED — no machine
reads or writes it. The old test
`zombie_walks_to_the_player_and_burns_at_dawn` is repointed to
`zombie_walks_to_the_player_and_despawns_at_dawn` (no hp loss + the
10-tick window armed + expired).

**B — the blocked-path jump constant.** The port jumped `-6.2` at a
blocked path; `-6.2` exists NOWHERE in the C# arm. The one-tile-wall
step-up arm is `base.velocity.Y = -6f` (`NPC.cs:60125`, inside the
obstacle scan's `SolidTileNoPlatforms(num198, num199 - 1)` branch
`:60111-60128`; the taller walls jump `-8f`/`-7f` `:60102`/`:60107`, the
slope arm `-5f` `:60131`). Fix: `update_zombie`'s jump → `-6.0`;
`npc_ai.rs::WalkerParams::ZOMBIE`/`WANDER` jump → `-6.0` and the false
`-6.2` cite corrected to `NPC.cs:60125`. The port keeps its
collision-jump STAND-IN (jump whenever the horizontal move is blocked
and grounded) — the full door-bash / step-up scan (`:59831-60088`) is
the documented remainder below.

**C — the chase gate's missing idle term.** C# `NPC.cs:57336` is
`if (this.ai[3] < (float)num57 && NPC.DespawnEncouragement_AIStyle3_Fighters_NotDiscouraged(...))`;
`num57` is 60 for the zombie family (the 180 override is the type-120
row, `:57035-57038`, unreachable for these kinds). The port's inline
fold tested only `!discouraged`, so a zombie whose idle counter reached
60 kept chasing instead of wandering. Fix: `self.ai[3] < 60.0 &&
!discouraged`. `ai[3]` is the fighter idle counter that
`world_sim/npcs.rs` ticks via `ambient_sound::fighter_idle_counter`
(`NPC.cs:57034-57149`) BEFORE `update_rng` (the S1-E-21 wave E wiring —
unchanged by this task). The batch-1 `walker_step_fighter`
(`npc_ai.rs`) already carried this term; the zombie's own fold had
dropped it. The discouraged arm itself was also wrong (`vx *= 0.9`
decay): it now ports the C#'s else-if body (`NPC.cs:57375-57401`) — for
the zombie family `CanBeBusyWithAction` is false (none of the listed
types, `:60332-60339`), so the arm always runs when the gate fails: the
daytime despawn (defect A), then the wander-flip (grounded + stopped →
`ai[0]++`, flip `direction`/`spriteDirection` every 2 ticks; any
horizontal motion resets `ai[0]`; `:57381-57397`), then the zero-direction
snap to +1 (`:57398-57401`).

### The audited-CORRECT rows (no changes)

### The obstacle scan (the remainder, now ported)

`npc_ai_fighter_scan.rs::fighter_obstacle_scan` ports `AI_003_Fighters`'
obstacle-scan tail (`NPC.cs:59831-60284`) verbatim for the zombie family,
called from `update_zombie` at the C#'s position — after the chase /
discouraged arms and the num107 ladder, BEFORE the gravity + collision
integration (`AI_003_Fighters` ends `:60298`; `UpdateCollision`
integrates afterwards). The four blocks:

- **The flag5 ground probe** (`:59831-59867`): while `vy == 0` (the hop
  `flag` is false for every zombie kind — it is set only by the
  scarecrow 305-309 arm, `npc_ai3_speeds`' `fx.hop_flag`, dropped by
  `run_ai3_ladder`), probe the floor row `(bottom + 7)/16` and the head
  row `(top - 9)/16` across the body's column span; a solid head cell
  kills flag5, a solid floor cell sets it, a null cell inside the span
  arms the `flag23` early-return (`:59863-59866` — the C# returns from
  `AI_003_Fighters` itself; the port returns `true` and the caller still
  integrates, as `UpdateCollision` runs after `AI()` regardless). No
  floor + rising cancels the jump (`:59859-59862`).
- **The 1-tile step-up assist** (`:59872-59948`): while falling or level,
  probe the NEXT-x column `centre + (width/2 + 1) * sign(vx)` at the
  body's bottom row; a 1-tile ledge with clear head/body room lifts
  `position.Y` onto it (the `gfxOffY` record + `stepSpeed` 1/2 by the
  lift's <9px threshold), the 16.1px reach. This is the block that makes
  1-tile climbing WORK — the jump ladder alone does not handle 1-tile
  ledges (the unicorn machine's inline copy, `npc_ai_unicorn.rs:328-387`,
  is the shape precedent). The `gfxOffY`/`stepSpeed` writes land on the
  NPC fields; the render pass does not read `gfx_off_y` yet and the decay
  helper (`npc_ai_unicorn_b.rs:285`) is unwired — the lift itself is
  live, the visual offset is the documented remainder.
- **The door bash** (`:59949-60088`): a closed door (tile 10) / tall gate
  (388) in the ahead probe column ticks `ai[2]` each scan; at 60 the bash
  fires — `vx = 0.5 * -direction`, `ai[1] += 5` (door) / `+2` (gate),
  `ai[2]` resets, and at `ai[1] >= 10` the open arms. The boolean algebra
  is ported VERBATIM (not simplified): `flag24` = the type list
  (`:59996`, 35 types — 489 is NOT in it), `flag25` = the graveyard
  `Next(60)` roll, `flag26` = the target inside unbreakable walls,
  `flag27 = ((!bloodMoon || getGoodWorld) && !flag25) & flag24` (the
  non-blood-moon reset gate). On a normal night a flag24 type resets
  `ai[1]` to 0 before the +5 (never opens); on a blood moon flag27 is
  false for EVERY type, so `ai[1]` accumulates and the door opens. The
  world mutation (`WorldGen.OpenDoor`) rides the `Npc::wants_door_bash`
  request drained in `world_sim/npcs.rs` (the `wants_sphere` borrow-safe
  shape — `update_zombie` holds `&World` immutable); the drain plays the
  `KillTile(fail: true)` thud on every bash and, when open, calls
  `edit::open_door` (a refusal sets `ai[3] = num57`, `:60064`) + the
  `Door_Opened` cue, all on the `UpdateNPCs` stream.
- **The probe jump ladder** (`:60089-60203`): while moving WITH the
  facing (`spriteDirection` matches the velocity sign, `:60096`), the
  ahead column `centre + 15 * direction` at row `bottom - 15`: a 3-tile
  wall jumps -8, a 2-tile wall -7, a 1-tile wall -6 (`:60125`), a sunken
  floor -5 (`:60131`), a gap (directionY < 0, no bottom-slope support)
  leaps -8 with `vx *= 1.5` (`:60134-60139`); no obstacle resets the bash
  counters (`:60140-60144`). The parked re-hop (`flag6 && ai[3] == 1`,
  `:60145-60148`) is carried; the expert-mode / type-586 hop
  (`:60149-60203`) is skipped (no expertMode flag, 586 not a zombie kind).
  The else-flag8 reset (`:60280-60284`) clears the bash counters when no
  floor is under the body.

The collision-jump stand-in survives ONLY as the fallback for cells the
15px-ahead probe misses (a wall the probe did not name): blocked +
grounded + `vy >= 0` → -6. The `vy >= 0` gate keeps the scan's own jump
(still negative after the +GRAVITY) from being overwritten on the tick
it fires. The repointed `the_blocked_path_jump_is_minus_six` witness
stands the zombie flush against a TWO-tile wall so the scan's -6 tier
fires deterministically (a 1-tile wall is now stepped, not jumped).

TR-VERIFY-W1's findings against this family, fixed on the branch

- **W1-2 (MED) — the free head's noTileCollide toggle was dropped.**
  The C# (`NPC.cs:31363-31371`) toggles `noTileCollide` per tick: a
  BLOCKED `CanHit` line head→player sets it (and flag53); a CLEAR line
  while the flag rides AND `SolidTiles(position, width, height)`
  releases it. `SetDefaults` 249 (`:12207-12220`) sets `noGravity` but
  NOT `noTileCollide` — the free head normally tile-collides. The port
  raw-integrated through walls unconditionally. Fixed: the flag rides
  `local_ai[1]` (249 uses no localAI slot — the body/fist mapping
  convention); the toggle runs at the arm top (the C#'s position,
  BEFORE the hover/cadence machine), and the tail free-integrates only
  while the flag rides, otherwise running the fists' axis-separated
  collision pass (velocity zeroes on impact, collideX/Y latch).
  `SolidTiles`' tile scan rides the house `collides_rect` stand-in.
  Witness: `npc.rs::w1_2_the_free_head_toggles_tile_collide_on_the_blocked_line`
  (blocked→set+pin, clear+air→keeps, clear+solids→release, impact→
  zero+latch). The per-tick `TargetClosest()` (`:31377`) stays folded:
  solo impact is facing only, the tail's vx-sign facing stands in
  (the documented solo convention — the G2 census claim below).
- **W1-6 (LOW) — the invented `.max(0.001)` normalize guards dropped.**
  The C# divides by the RAW `(float)Math.Sqrt` at every one of the six
  sites (`:31196`, `:31251`, `:31299`/`:31325`, `:19321`, `:19382`,
  `:31459`, `:31560`) — coincident centres produce NaN/inf velocity in
  vanilla (NaN pass-through, NOT a SafeNormalize zero-fold: the source
  is a bare division, no guard). The guards were port inventions;
  removed for strict fidelity (behaviour differs only in the degenerate
  coincident case). The fist follow's `num3 / d` division is never
  reached at d == 0 anyway (the `d < 12 + num3` gate takes the contact
  arm first). The unwired `npc_ai_style47` reference keeps its guard —

damage row 9999, the contact 9999, `flag2` forced true (the expert cadences +
the +5 timer shave apply even in classic). The one-shot kill IS the 9999
damage — no special kill code exists.

### RNG by construction

Every `Main.rand` draw is consumed in C# order (each draw = one
`InternalSample`, `UnifiedRandom.cs:62-88`); the stream-clone witnesses
replay the draws against a clone (the style-52 pattern):

* `DoMagicEffect` (`:45832-45923`): per dust, the `NewDustPerfect` ARGUMENTS
  evaluate first — `NextVector2CircularEdge` (1, `Utils.cs:1271-1274` →
  `NextVector2Unit` `:1261-1264`), the velocity `NextFloat` (1), the colour
  `NextFloat` (1), the scale `NextFloat` (1) — then `Dust.NewDust`'s own 6
  (`Dust.cs:170-175`/`:190`: `Next(w-4)`, `Next(h-4)` with w/h clamped ≥ 5,
  `Next(-20,21)` ×2, `Next(3)`, `Next(-20,21)`). Effect 5 with 0 < progress
  draws `Next(86,92)` ONCE (`:45869`) even when progress ≥ 1 zeroes the
  count; progress == 0 draws NOTHING (the `customData` branch `:45902-45909`
  is dead code).
* case 0 trail (`:46040-46058`): per dust 6 (`NewDust`, w/h = 100) + 2
  (`NextVector2Circular`, `Utils.cs:1266-1269`) + 1 (velocity) + 1 (fadeIn)
  + 6 (`CloneDust` → `NewDust`, `Dust.cs:263-281`) = 16 ×2 = 32/tick, ticks
  11..149 (139 ticks × 32 = 4448 draws over the materialize).
* case 13 trail (`:46880-46898`): 1 (colour) + 6 (w/h = 200) + 2 + 1
  (velocity) + 1 (scale) + 1 (fadeIn) + 6 = 18 ×5 = 90/tick.
* gameplay: case 2 `NextFloatDirection` (`:46291`, +`NextFloat` `:46294`
  when phase-2 expert — BOTH consumed), case 5 `NextFloat` (`:46473`),
  case 7 the DISCARDED `NextFloat` (`:46553`).

**Dust-pool assumption (documented deviation)**: the pool is below the 50 %
`maxDustToDraw` threshold (the FIRST skip tier, `Dust.cs:139-143`) and
on-screen, so `Dust.NewDust`'s skip draws and early-outs (`Dust.cs:77-101`)
never fire; `ChildSafety.Disabled` is true by default
(`GameContent/ChildSafety.cs:33`) so its branch (`Dust.cs:194-213`) never
draws. Dust type 267 is in NONE of the extra-draw type lists
(`Dust.cs:214-253`), so exactly 6 draws per `NewDust`.

### Documented deviations / skips

* the dust VISUALS, the sounds (`SoundID.Item160-165`), the
  `Lighting.AddLight` tail (`:46941`) and `GetSpawnSource_ForProjectile` are
  skipped — the dust RNG is still consumed (above);
* `TargetClosest` is a REQUEST (the S1-D-3p `npc_target.rs` helper when
  wired); the caller's target rides unchanged within the tick;
* single-player assumed (`Main.netMode != 1`): every `NewProjectile` fires
  and the `Boss_CanShootExtraAt` scans (`:46962-46982`) run over the caller's
  ascending-slot player slice;
* the remix scan (`:45933-45941`) takes THIS boss as the first live 636 (the
  single-Empress invariant);
* `Vector2.Normalize` of an exactly-zero vector yields NaN in XNA; the port
  guards to zero (the Fishron precedent) — only differs on exact overlap;
* the 874/873/872/919/923 projectiles have no port AI yet — the spawns are
  REQUESTS carrying the C# `ai[0]`/`ai[1]` arguments verbatim.

Remainder 4: the BossNoCheese immunity group. **The census correction**:
there is NO `NPCID.Sets.BossNoCheese` — the group is the
`ImmunityCooldownID.BossNoCheese` COUNTER (index 1,
`ImmunityCooldownID.cs:76`), assigned per-type at two consumer sites:
* `Player.Update_NPCCollision` (`Player.cs:31332-31349`): the Moon Lord
  parts 396/397/398/400/401 + the Empress 636 ride the counter; the 636
  arm ALSO skips contact entirely while `ai[0]` is 0 (materialize) or 10

  462 group + the 871/872/873/874/919/923/924 empress group.

The semantics (`Player.cs:38208` + `:38391-38394`): a BossNoCheese hit
reads/writes its OWN `hurtCooldowns[1]` window, NOT the General `immune`
flag — so the boss's hits land THROUGH the cross-dodge i-frames a normal
hit arms (the "no cheese" name), and their window does not block other
lanes. The `:14799`/`:31350` gates (`!immune || num != General`) are the
read side; `UpdateImmunity`'s tail (`:18887-18893`) decrements every
positive counter once per tick.

**What landed**: `Player.hurt_cooldowns: [i32; 6]` (the
`ImmunityCooldownID.Count` array, `Player.cs:3160`); the
`hurt_inner_cooldown(.., cooldown_counter)` seam (the `Hurt`
`cooldownCounter` parameter, default −1 = General) — the General lane
keeps the collapsed `immune`/`hurt_cd` shape byte-identical, the
BossNoCheese lane reads/writes `hurt_cooldowns[1]`; `update_immunity`'s
per-counter decrement tail; the `COOLDOWN_GENERAL`/`COOLDOWN_BOSS_NO_CHEESE`
constants. `npc.rs::contact` gains the `specialHitSetter` kind-match (the
Moon Lord parts + the Empress), the 636 ai[0] 0/10 skip, the
BossNoCheese-aware thorns gate (`flag4`, `:31392-31396`) and the
counter-routed `Hurt`. `projectile.rs::damage_player` gains the
`Damage_EVP` kind-match + the counter-routed hurt. The non-boss lanes
stay byte-identical (no blanket `immune` early-return added — the bypass
rides the counter routing alone). Witnesses:

`the_moon_lord_parts_share_the_group` (world_sim/npcs.rs) +

## The waterfowl sweep (W4-c10 phase 4, 2026-11-21, code-only mode)

### The 1080 BirdDroppings DUP — arm-by-arm vs W4-d20, keep-one recommendation

**Cross-note to the d20b sweep (reads `origin/task/W4-d20-proj-ai-191-200`
tip 13de9ccf).** Both branches independently landed the aiStyle-200 arm;
the merge needs ONE survivor. Compared arm-by-arm against the C#
(`Projectile.cs:39985-40017` AI / `:18921-18928` HandleMovement /
`:70926-70954` Kill):

| piece | W4-c10 (`projectile_bird_droppings.rs`) | W4-d20 (`projectile_ai_misc.rs::ai_bird_droppings`) | C# | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `proj_data` row | 10x10 / 200 / -1 / alpha 255 / ignoreWater overlay, stock tileCollide+timeLeft | identical fields (d20 `data.rs:3606` + the `:4275` overlay) | `:10078-10086` | EQUAL — either row stands; keep ONE const + ONE row + ONE overlay arm |
| gravity + cap | `+0.3`, cap 16 | identical | `:39987-39991` | EQUAL |
| dust census | 2 × (`Next(2)` then `NextFloat`) | identical (the if/else draws the same one float per branch) | `:39992-40008` | EQUAL — stream-identical |
| player-intersect kill | `player_rect: Option<(i32,i32,i32,i32)>` seam, dead pre-filtered at the dispatch | `player: Option<&Player>` seam, `!pl.dead` gate inside | `:40009-40016` (`active && !dead`) | EQUAL behaviour — d20's Player-ref seam is the pool's native shape; c10's dispatch pre-filters dead |
| post-kill drift | LANDED in the sweep: kill → `pos += vel` in-module (the C# UpdatePosition runs before the `!active` return, `:17015`/`:20445`/`:17027`) | the arm returns without integrating; the dispatch's unconditional `kill_step` tail integrates the corpse once | `:20445` | EQUAL net effect by different routes — c10's module owns the drift, d20's `kill_step` tail supplies it |
| movement | in-module splat: blocked-axis probe → integrate → kill (`:18921-18928` shape, the frost-shot granularity) | dispatch tail calls `kill_step(world)` after the arm — the SAME probe shape in the pool | `:18921-18928` | EQUAL |
| Kill hook (buff/cue/dust) | LANDED in the sweep: Stinky 120/600 + Item177 + the 90-draw census, pool death hook (commit 8bd6afeb) | ABSENT (d20 landed only the AI arm) | `:70926-70954` | c10 is the superset |
| dispatch | `200 =>` passes the pre-built rect; module owns AI+movement | `200 =>` passes `player.as_deref()`, then `kill_step` | `:36763-36766` | both faithful |
| witnesses | 6 (row, fall+census, strict-edge kill+drift, splat, kill census, pool hook) | 4 (row, fall+census, contact kill, dispatch) | — | c10 superset |

**Recommendation: KEEP W4-c10's `projectile_bird_droppings.rs` as the
survivor; DROP d20's `ai_bird_droppings` fn + its 4 witnesses + its
`200 =>` dispatch arm + its duplicate `BIRD_DROPPINGS` const/row/overlay.**
Rationale: (1) c10 carries the Kill hook (the Stinky debuff is gameplay —
the town flee gate reads buff 120, `NPC.cs:53534`); (2) the module owns
AI + movement + death together (the spear/frost-shot one-module shape),
so the merge deletes one fn instead of reconciling two call graphs;
(3) the census streams are draw-identical, so no RNG re-pin is needed on
either side. If d20b prefers its Player-ref seam, the alternative is:
keep d20's fn, move c10's `bird_droppings_kill_draws` + the pool hook
beside it, and delete c10's module — but then d20's dispatch must ALSO
gain the corpse-drift order check. The first form is the smaller diff.
The `handles()` fn is c10-only (d20 dispatches on style directly) — it
dies with whichever module loses. NOTE the const collision: both
branches define `BIRD_DROPPINGS` (c10 in `projectile/data.rs:253`, d20
in its `data.rs:4547`) — the merge keeps one; the pool's `1080` literals
in d20's witnesses ride the surviving const either way.

## The mana machinery (S1-P-i19)

**Headline finding — `DebugOptions.ManaV2` is the SHIPPED mana machine.** The
static ctor sets `ManaV2 = true` (`Testing/DebugOptions.cs:85`) and a census of
the whole decompile (game + ReLogic) finds NO write that ever sets it false —
no command, no config, no menu. The earlier ANALYSIS note ("a debug cheat, not
ported") was wrong: the 1.4.5 mana rework IS the default behaviour, and the
port's pre-i19 `CheckMana` implemented the legacy V1 refusal the source never
uses. `regen.rs::MANA_V2` folds the flag to a `true` constant; the V1 lanes
stay unreachable exactly as in the source.

## The animated-tile light chain (W4-d56, 2026-11-20)

`crates/tr-render/src/animated_tiles.rs` ports the per-tile light chain the
animated-tile draw passes share — the half of `DrawSingleTile` between
`GetTileDrawData` and the light test that the torch/candle flame quads
(`tr-core/flame.rs`, TILE-DRAW-2) and the waterfall/lavafall fall-block rows
(`drawdata.rs` case-326 group + the wired `TileAnimator`, S1-G-1f) already
render around:

* `DrawAnimatedTile_AdjustForVisionChangers` (`TileDrawing.cs:8481-8552`,
  duplicated inline in `DrawSingleTile` :897-963; the deferred `DrawGrass`
  :8348 / `DrawMultiTileVines` :8976 call the same function) — the
  Dangersense R255/G50/B50, Spelunker R200/G170 and Biome Sight per-channel
  floors, in that order, plus the three `Dust.NewDust` arms (60/204/267).
* The predicates: `IsTileDangerous` (`:4435-4447` + `CheckTouchDamage`
  `:4449-4457` + `CheckHot` `:4459-4467`), `Main.IsTileSpelunkable`
  (`Main.cs:21783-21798`, the 49-row `tileSpelunker` table `:9420-9467` +
  `:9651` and the 185/186 frame windows) and `Main.IsTileBiomeSightable`
  (`Main.cs:21800-21818`, the three `TileID.Sets` biome lists + the remix
  474/195 exceptions).
* `DrawTiles_GetLightOverride` (`TileDrawing.cs:6624-6686`) — fullbright
  white, 541/631 white, platform-19 row-48 white, the fireblossom 83/84
  pulse arms, the lily 61/703 `245 - mouseTextColor*1.5` repaint and the
  cracked-brick 481-483 `1 + sin(t/1.5·2π)·0.15` breathe.

Deliberate deviations:

* **UNWIRED, code-only.** The `render/tiles.rs::draw_tiles` seam is contested
  by the in-flight W4-d57/d58/d59/d60 tile-draw siblings, so the pure
  decision maths lands in `tr-render` first (the W4-d58 `chest_frames`
  pattern — no `tr-core` dependency, every world/engine input a parameter).
  The intended call sites are documented in the module header: the vision
  floors after `GetTileDrawData` and before the `flag` light test
  (`:897-963`), `light_override` right after (`:969`). No pixel changes until
  the wiring step.
* **The dust rolls ride the caller.** The three `Next(30)/Next(60)/Next(480)`
  gates are returned as `VisionDust` requests (the d60 particles convention)
  — the module never touches RNG. The per-arm roll conditions differ and are
  documented verbatim: danger/biome roll only when
  `_isActiveAndNotPaused & canDoDust`, but the spelunker arm's bitwise `&`
  (`(Next(60) == 0) & canDoDust`, `:8516`) rolls whenever active even with
  dust suppressed — the wiring must reproduce that consumption.
* **The `TileID.Sets` tables are inlined** from `TileID.cs` (`tr-render`
  cannot read `tr-core::tiledata`); the census witnesses pin every row
  against the C# factory lists. The `Boulders`/`TouchDamageHot`/
  `TouchDamageImmediate`/`CorruptBiomeSight`/`CrimsonBiomeSight`/
  `HallowBiomeSight` lists match the generated sets' membership.
* **The lily byte cast wraps, not clamps.** `(byte)(245f - mouseTextColor *
  1.5f)` (`:6671`) goes negative for `mouseTextColor >= 164`; the C#
  unchecked cast truncates toward zero to int then wraps (225 → −92.5 → −92
  → 164). Rust's saturating float→u8 `as` would clamp to 0, so the port
  casts through i32 (the `xna_scale_color` convention) — pinned by
  `light_override_lily_wraps_the_negative_byte_cast`.
* **The breathe truncates per channel.** `Color operator*(Color, float)`
  (`:6680`) is `(int)(channel * factor)` toward zero with the alpha restored
  afterwards; the f32 factor rounds to nearest before the product (the
  1.15 factor is 1.149999976158142 in f32, so 100→115, 200→230, 250→287).
  The C# evaluates `Math.Sin` in double on the f32-rounded argument then
  casts; the port uses f32 `sin` (the house convention, `wind.rs`/
  `flame.rs`) — a ≤1-ulp factor difference can flip a truncation boundary
  byte on rare inputs, the same class as the other f32-sin ports.
* `Minecart.IsPressurePlate`'s `tile.active()` gate (`Minecart.cs:553`) is
  guaranteed by every `IsTileDangerous` call site (active tiles only), so
  the port's predicate takes only the frameX 20/21 test.

## The orb keep-one prep (W4-g27, 2026-11-20)

Five branches implemented the 18 lunar-orb `UpdateBuffs` arms
(`Player.cs:10342-10461` + `UpdateBuffs_NebulaBuffs` `:12070-12079`):
c16 (`buff_effects_orbs.rs`, request accumulator), c17
(`buff_effects_potions_sets.rs`, slot driver), c18 (no orb arms — the
summon block), d73 (`buff_effects_boosters.rs`, direct slot mutation),
d74 (`buff_effects_tail.rs`, request accumulator). The keep-one decision
(the full per-quirk diff + the merger contract) lives in
`docs/research/W4-g27-orb-keep-one.md`; the canonical module is
`crates/tr-app/src/buff_effects_orbs.rs` on `task/W4-g27-orb-keep-one-prep`.

- **Pick: d73's arm core** — the only implementation preserving the
  adjusted-`j` double-delete quirk verbatim (the downgrade's `j--` feeds
  the gate-failure's second delete; the C# `DelBuff(-1)` crash path is
  guarded, a documented deviation). c17 collapses it to one rescan;
  c16/d74's unadjusted delete requests would replay it at the wrong slot.
- **Correction ported: c17's zero-seeding.** `ResetEffects` zeroes
  `beetleOrbs`/`solarShields`/the nebula trio every frame
  (`Player.cs:18501`/`:18505`/`:18755`) — d73's `BoosterState` "persists
  across ticks" claim is WRONG; the canonical `OrbScanState::reset_effects()`
  makes the per-frame zeroing explicit.
- **Request vocabulary kept for the accumulator-shaped mergers**:
  `orb_arm_requests` derives the c16/d74 request view from the SAME arm
  core on a one-slot scratch bar (no second implementation); `next_index`
  is the authoritative quirk encoding, `purge_band` is inclusive-of-self
  with no outer `j--`.
- **Deliberate deviations**: the negative-index delete guard (the C#
  throws `IndexOutOfRangeException`; unreachable in retail play — the
  counters reset to 0 every frame, so a downgrade needs an earlier kept
  slot whose own set flag was on). The set flags
  (`beetleDefense`/`beetleOffense`/`setSolar`) stay false until the
  armor-set lane lands (`ApplySetBonus_*` `:16366`/`:16499`/`:16529`
  unported) — the arms then zero + delete exactly like the C# without the
  set. c17's swapped chestpiece doc (Scale Mail ↔ Shell) is corrected to
  c16's mapping.
- **RNG census**: zero draws in the whole block — stream-neutral.
- Code-only: 22 `w4_g27_*` witnesses WRITTEN, NOT RUN — no
  cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/graphify invoked. The f12/merger step wires
  the module and drops the four duplicate orb copies.

The `powerups.rs` machine rides the boss-spawner/recall press-edge shape:
the use START arms the swing on the press edge, the grant fires at
`ItemTimeIsZero && itemAnimation > 0` mid-swing, `ApplyItemTime` re-arms
the cadence and the generic consume tail (`:43280-43326`) pays ONE only
when the grant fired. Refused arms keep re-checking each action tick and
never consume.

  `HandleSpecialEvent` completes ONE row's condition

1. **Dust/sound RNG skipped pool-wide.** The C# projectile AI arms draw
   `Main.rand` for dust/gore/sound only (AI_005's :23883/:23973/:23983/
   :24035/:24039, AI_021's :25594, the 459 orb's :54678, the 442 Kill's

   precedent, `projectile_ai001_a.rs` module doc), so these draws are NOT
   consumed - the `UpdateProjectiles` stream stays untouched BY
   CONSTRUCTION. The ONE exception is the NettleBurst head's `Next(2)` type
   flip (`Projectile.cs:23709-23713`), which changes STATE (the kind), so it
   IS consumed on the pool's rng (the `ai_style4` arm takes the rng arg).
   The use-pass draws (the harp/guitar/poison/starfury/sky-fracture rolls)
   ride `UpdatePlayers` in C# order - the witnesses replay them.

## The minion target command (S1-P-i27)

The summoner target lane, verbatim against `Player.cs`/`Projectile.cs`
(code-only mode — no compiler invoked, 28 witnesses written not run).

**The aim + maintenance.** `minion_npc_target_aim`
(`Player.MinionNPCTargetAim`, `Player.cs:56914-56933`) measures
`NPC.Hitbox.Distance(mouseWorld)` — the rectangle-to-point distance
(`Utils.cs:1507-1542`: 0 inside/touching, the axis bands, the four corner
distances), shared as `npc_ai_style64::rect_distance` (`pub(crate)`).
The scan re-reads the current best's distance each iteration (the C#
shape); the hitbox anchors are the `(int)` position/size
(`Entity.cs:171-176`). The `doNotDisableIfTheTargetIsTheSame` parameter
mirrors the C# signature — the only caller passes false
(`ItemCheck_MinionAltFeatureUse`, `:49777`); the whip's aiStyle-165
retarget is a plain write and never calls it. `update_minion_target`
(`UpdateMinionTarget`, `:56999-57028`) replaces the old invalidation
half: the rest point drops past 1000 px CENTRE distance
(`base.Distance`, `Entity.cs:195-198`), the attack target drops when
unchaseable or its HITBOX is past 3000 px from the player's centre. The
`whoAmI == Main.myPlayer` gate folds to the single local player.

**The rest-spot command.** `minion_rest_target_aim`
(`MinionRestTargetAim`, `:56935-56997`) walks the mouse's tile column:
the full-solid test (`nactive && tileSolid && !tileSolidTop`), the ≤20
up-scan (bounded `num2+num5 > 1`) and 20 down-scan, the clearance pick
`num3 = (num7 <= -num4) ? num7+3 : num4-2`, then the unbounded drop
until a 5-tile window holds a `WorldGen.SolidTileAllowBottomSlope`
(`WorldGen.cs:70167-70189` — the FULL form: solid-or-solidTop, the
platform-top-frame clause, no half-brick, not actuated; shared
`pub(crate)` from the AI_026 slice-C copy). The port caps the drop at
the world's bottom row (the out-of-world probe reads solid, so the C#
loop terminates there too). The spot `(tileX*16+8, row*16)` is kept
only within 1000 px of the player. Triggers: `key_double_tap_down`
(`KeyDoubleTap`, `:56764-56787`) fires the aim for `setForbidden`;
`key_hold_down` (`KeyHoldDown`, `:56894-56912`) clears the spot at
holdTime ≥ 60 for `setStardust`/`setForbidden`. The driver
(`update_minion_rest_command`, `:25022-25073`'s down-cardinal half)
mirrors the 15-tick double-tap window, the press edge
(`controlDown && releaseDown`) and the hold counter; the
`releaseDown = !controlDown` latch refresh (`:27636`) folds to the
driver's tail (the only down-cardinal consumer in the port).
`Main.ReversedUpDownArmorSetBonuses` (`Main.cs:273`, the settings
toggle) flips the cardinal to UP, disabling the DOWN command. Both set
flags re-derive per tick (`ResetEffects` `:18743`/`:18745`, the
armor-set block's Forbidden 3776/3777/3778 + Stardust 3381/3382/3383
triples, `DataStructures/ArmorSetBonuses.cs:482-483`).

**The summoner accessory fold.** The `UpdateEquips` tail
(`Player.cs:12970-12984`): `accSilverBracer` adds `tagEffectDuration +=
2f` + `maxTagEffects++` (the `minionDamage += 0f` half is a verbatim
no-op), `accMobiusStrip` adds `maxTagEffects++` + `whipRangeMultiplier
+= 0.1f`, `accWickedArmlet` adds `maxTagEffects++`. Grants: 6156 Silver
Bracer (`:14510`), 6158 Mobius Strip (`:14513`), 6159 Wicked Armlet
(`:14516`), 6162 Ouroboros Ring (`:14519` — the Mobius flag; the
`accSnakeBand` half unported), 6163 Twilight Grasp (`:14523` — BOTH
flags), 6179 Armlet of Ruin (`:14585` — the armlet flag; the
`accArmletOfRuin` tag-damage half unported), 6182 Wicked Claws
(`:14601-14603` — the armlet flag + `meleeSpeed += 0.12f`; the
`autoReuseGlove` half unported, the Titan Glove precedent), 6183 Silver
Shield (`:14605-14609` — the bracer flag beside its knockback/fire-walk
row in `accessory_defense.rs`). The C# `TagEffectStack` reads the
PLAYER's `maxTagEffects`/`tagEffectDuration` live
(`TagEffectStack.cs:47`/`:133`); the port keeps copies on the stack, so

### What was WRONG / missing in the port (the census verdicts)

1. **WRONG — the mining model was time-per-tile, not damage-per-hit.** The
   pre-i29 arm accumulated `mine_timer += dt` to a `hardness` threshold
   (`base * 35/pick * pickSpeed`). The C# accumulates `GetPickaxeDamage`
   damage into the `HitTile` book until 100. **Fixed**: `tr_core::hit_tile`
   ports the book; `pick_tile_hit` accumulates the real damage; the break
   fires at `>= 100`.
2. **WRONG — `pick_can_mine` was a partial gate table.** It missed the
   chlorophyte-200, mythril/orichalcum-110, adamantite/titanium-150,
   lihzahrd-210, hellforge-underworld, trap-row and dungeon-x-band gates, and
   the whole damage-multiplier ladder. **Fixed**: `tr_core::tool::pickaxe_damage`
   ports `GetPickaxeDamage` verbatim; `pick_can_mine` is now the
   `damage > 0` projection (the depth-only dungeon approximation kept for the
   tile-target gate, the full path carries the x-band).
3. **WRONG — the reach was a circle.** The pre-i29 gate used
   `(tile_range_x + 1) * TILE_PX` radius. The C# is a rectangle
   (`tileRangeX + tileBoost` × `tileRangeY + tileBoost`, clamped 20).
   **Fixed**: `tile_in_reach_rect` ports `GetTileRegion` + `InTileBounds`;
   `mining_tile_range` adds the Extendo Grip/Gizmo Pack/Grand Design +3/+2
   (`:13040-13044`) and the held Toolbox +1/+1 (`:14954-14958`).
4. **WRONG — the mining cadence ignored `useTime`/`toolTime`.** **Fixed**:
   the `toolTime` mirror/countdown (`:43576-43587`) + the
   `itemTime = (int)(useTime * pickSpeed)` re-arm (`:45779`).
5. **MISSING — the drill channel.** The drills (385/386/388/1189/1196/1203/
   1231/2774/2779/2784/3464/579/2798) are `channel` items with `pick > 0`;
   the port treated them as generic throws. **Fixed**: `drill_channel_start`
   spawns the aiStyle-20 drill projectile once on the press; `ai_drill`
   (`projectile.rs`) ports the hold/aim/release; the channel block holds the
   swing at the dummy 2 ticks. The drill `proj_data` rows + the aiStyle-20/75
   dispatch arms are added.
6. **MISSING — the grass/moss conversion.** `DoesPickTargetTransformOnKill`
   (`:54047`) + `KillTile(fail: true)` (`WorldGen.cs:63715-63735`) convert a
   grass tile to its soil at 100 damage instead of breaking it. **Fixed**:
   `does_pick_target_transform` + `convert_grass_tile`.
7. **MISSING — the `pickSpeed` 0.3 floor** (`:25972-25975`) and the Mining
   buff 104 (`:10136`) / Ancient Chisel (`:13032-13035`) folds. **Fixed**:
   `Player::pick_speed` clamps at 0.3; the buff/accessory arms add to
   `pick_speed_bonus`.

### Deliberate deviations (recorded)

- **The axe/hammer arms keep the time-based pacing.** The i30 (axe) and i31
  (hammer/slope) tasks own the `tileAxe`/`tileHammer` hit-buffer models
  (`Player.cs:45665-45771`). The demon-altar smash keeps its pre-i29
  `SmashAltar` wiring; the wall hammer keeps its time-based dig. A pick
  refuses the axe/hammer tiles (the `:45656` match), so the pick side is
  faithful even though the chop/slope pacing is not yet the C#'s.
- **The `HitTile` draw-side fields are render-only.** `crackStyle`'s roll
  (`HitTile.cs:36-45`, the static `HitTile.rand` + the no-repeat loop) stays
  in the crack overlay's world-seeded `mine_crack_rng` (the S1-G-1 wave C
  determinism deviation); the `AddDamage` wobble-direction `Main.rand.
  NextFloat()` draw (`:66`) and the `DrawFreshAnimations` miner's wobble
  (`:335-471`) are not drawn. The sim book therefore takes **no RNG** — the
  mining tick adds no draws to any stream. The C#'s wobble draw rides the
  `UpdatePlayers` swap; its absence is a render-only deviation (the same
  class as the crack-style seed).
- **The drill projectile's per-tick jitter + dust are render-only.** The
  `velocity.X *= 1 + Next(-3,4)*0.01` wobble (`Projectile.cs:25575`) and the
  1-in-6 dust (`:25576-25583`) are not ported (the port draws no drill dust);
  the `ai_drill` hold/aim/release/position-pin are faithful. The Laser Drill
  (445, aiStyle 75) holds its channel like the drills; its full `AI_075`
  laser AI (the tile-target snap, the reach clamp, the beam light,
  `:66244-66358`) is a follow-up.
- **The `pick_can_mine` dungeon gate stays depth-only** for the tile-target
  gate (`cursor_cell_is_tile_target`); the full `pickaxe_damage` path carries
  the 0.35/0.65 x-band. The two agree on every tile the port's worldgen
  produces at the surface band; the divergence is the deep-dungeon edge.
- **The `noBuilding` gate is unmodelled** (the port has no `noBuilding`
  state — the frozen/webbed gate already refuses the use); the DD2
  `ShouldBlockBuilding` arm (`:25963-25970`) is a follow-up.
- **The per-tick `KillTile(fail: true)` sound/dust** has no port path (the
  pre-i29 recorded deviation); the damage still accumulates and the crack
  overlay projects it.

### RNG order (S1-A-10 contract)

The mining tick itself draws **no RNG** (the `HitTile` book is RNG-free in
the port — the crack-style/wobble draws are render-side, see above). The
break's loot draws ride `stream(UpdatePlayers)` exactly as the pre-i29
`break_tile` (the C# `KillTile` runs in `Player.ItemCheck` under the
`Main.cs:17754` swap). The drill spawn's crit roll rides
`stream(UpdatePlayers)` (the use-start seam). The altar smash keeps its
`stream(UpdatePlayers)` ore draws. **No stream is reordered**; the only new
draws are the drill spawn's crit (a new use-start, the C# fires it too).

### Deliberate deviations / deferred

- **Cross-system WIDTH reads**: the player-generic `self.x + WIDTH` reads became
  `self.width`, but OTHER systems (npc.rs targeting, projectile collision,
  render) still read the `WIDTH` constant — a Pixie's 8-wide body is narrower
  than those probes assume. Threading the live width through every consumer is
  out of scope (the mount hitbox change is the player's own physics/probes).

  channel yet (visual seam, the S1-E-1 convention).
- **Shellphone force-clear latency**: the clear queues as `pending_force_clear`
  and drains after the player tick (the kills need `&mut App`); the C# clears
  before the teleport. Same tick, nothing probes the spawn area in between —
  observation-identical. The `netMode != 1` gate folds to always-clear (SP).
- **Teleport shimmer strip**: only the ported `shimmer_wet` half fires; the
  `shimmering` absorbed-state write + buff-353 clear ride S1-E-16.
- **CanSnapToPosition's Collision.CanHit reach half** (`:33420`) + fallbacks:
  the standing stand-in (the solid-box + default-box probes are the ported core).
- **Early-dismount cursor gate**: the C# runs `TryEarlyDismount` from
  `Player.Update` (`:24992`) regardless of cursor reach; the port folds item
  use into `update_editing`, so the dismount fires only when the cursor passes
  the reach gate (the editing path's documented stand-in).
- **RNG**: the mount use path itself is draw-free. The only new draws are the
  cited Dig variation/pitch (UpdatePlayers, after the attenuation gate) and the
  PalChillet NextFloat (audio-only `sound_style_random`, before the gate —
  `SoundEngine.cs:93-99` computes the pitch first). No gameplay-stream order

## The light-item family (S1-P-i42, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

Branch `task/S1-P-i42-torch-glowstick` (worktree TR-i42). **CODE-ONLY mode**:
file reads/writes + git only — no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests/dotnet/graphify,
**no compiler invoked**. Scope: the torch/glowstick/flare LIGHT items — the
torch placement (wall/tile/underwater variants), the glowstick throw (aiStyle
14, sticky/bouncy), the flare gun (aiStyle 33), and the held-light source.
Census first; the WRONGs fixed verbatim with C# cites.

### Census verdicts

**Torch placement — three WRONGs fixed.**
1. *The style never rode the tile.* The legacy single-tile write
   (`edit/place.rs::place_tile`) wrote `frameX = frameY = 0` for every torch,
   dropping `Item.placeStyle`. The C# `WorldGen.PlaceTile` case 4
   (`WorldGen.cs:59798-59842`) writes `frameY = 22 * style` (`:59839`) — the
   style column `CheckTorch` preserves and `TileLightScanner` reads
   (`tile_light/scanner.rs`'s `fy / 22` arm). A Blue Torch (427, style 1)
   placed as a plain torch and lit white. **Fix**: a dedicated
   `edit::place_torch` arm (`place_item_tile` dispatches kind 4 to it) writes
   `frameY = 22 * style`, runs the support gate (`:59835`) and the liquid gate
   (`:59454-59467`), then `CheckTorch` for the attachment frameX.
2. *The liquid gate was absent.* The C# refuses a torch in a liquid cell
   unless the style is 8/11/17 (the `ItemID.Sets.WaterTorches`,
   `ItemID.cs:1372` — Cursed/Ichor/Coral), and even those check the sub-tile's
   `WaterPlacement` (`:59462-59466`). The port placed any torch underwater.
   **Fix**: `place_torch`'s liquid gate — styles 8/11/17 resolve their
   `D_4_S8/S11/S17` sub-tiles (all `WaterPlacement.Allowed`), every other
   style refuses. The `tile.checkingLiquid()` half (`:59454`) folds to false
   (the port's tile flags carry no checking bit).
3. *The wall-only cell refused.* The app pre-check `can_place`
   (`world_sim/editing.rs`) scanned only the four neighbours, never the
   TARGET cell's own wall — so a torch on a wall with no adjacent block/wall
   was refused. The C# `PlaceThing_Tiles_BlockPlacementForAssortedThings`
   (`Player.cs:41106-41198`) reads `tile.wall > 0` first (`:41108-41111`),
   then the `SolidTileNoAttach` below/left/right support (`:41186-41197`) and
   the tree-trunk/beam side arms. **Fix**: `can_place`'s torch arm reads the
   target wall + the C# support conjunctions; the sloped-support flatten
   (`Player.cs:41114-41146` → `WorldGen.SlopeTile`) runs in the mutable route
   (`flatten_torch_supports`, the new `tr_core::edit::slope_tile` +
   `solid_tile_no_attach`).
4. *CheckTorch erased the style column.* `torch.rs::check_torch` wrote
   `frame_y = 0` on every re-frame; the C# `CheckTorch`
   (`WorldGen.cs:86095-86180`) writes ONLY `frameX` (`:86160-86175`) — the
   `22 * style` frameY survives every attachment change. **Fix**: the write
   removed; the `TopEdgeCanBeAttachedTo` gate also regained its missing
   `!tile.inActive()` conjunct (`WorldGen.cs:70389`).

**Biome-torch place style — the missing conversion ported.**
`PlaceThing_Tiles_PlaceIt` (`Player.cs:40129-40132`) converts a plain torch
(style 0) to the biome style when `UsingBiomeTorches` (the Torch God's favour)

the unlock (`player_lights.rs::biome_torch_hold_style`); the placement half was

`place_tile` conversion. The temple (`Zones.temple`) and remix
(`SeedFlags::REMIX`) arms ARE ported, the remaining arms keep their C# order

### The bounce chain order (load-bearing)

`HandleMovement`'s blocked-move chain (`Projectile.cs:18398-19853`) checks the
outer TYPE chain before the aiStyle chain. The 515-517 arm (`:18479-18489`,
both axes ×−0.9 gated |last|>1) takes the bouncy glowstick BEFORE the
aiStyle-14 arm. Inside the aiStyle-14 arm (`:19626-19745`): 870 pre-flip
(`:19663-19669`, the full −lastVelocity + ai[1]=1), 50 (`:19671-19681`, X ×−0.2,
Y ×−0.2 only when lastY>1.5), `type >= 1089` (`:19682-19702`, the ×0.99 reverse
with the <1 snaps), and the generic tail (`:19725-19744`, X ×−0.5, Y ×−0.5 only
when lastY>1) which takes the spelunker (473). Once the fairy flips to aiStyle
170, the later `type == 870` arm (`:19787-19797`) takes its blocked moves
(X ×−0.2, Y ×−0.2 when lastY>0). The fairy's flip (`:24832-24835`) is observed
the tick AFTER the bounce set ai[1]=1; the flip tick still runs the aiStyle-14
tail (the C# stays inside the entered arm), the hover starts next tick — the
port models the persistent style in `local_ai[2]` (a spare slot; the C# 870
never reads localAI[2]).

### RNG order (the load-bearing invariant)

- The glowstick/flare AI arms draw **zero** `Main.rand` (the dust spawns are
  skipped — the pool has no dust layer, the frostmoon/ai026 precedent).
- The movement's blocked-move prologue consumes exactly ONE `Next(3)`
  (`Projectile.cs:17948`, the FIRST operand of the `&&` — the ai026_c
  precedent): C#'s left-to-right evaluation rolls it on EVERY blocked move
  even when the trailing gates (`owner == myPlayer && CanCutTiles() &&
  (friendly || hostile) && damage > 0`) fail — the glowsticks' damage −1
  skips only the cut BODY (`:17950-17985`), never the roll; the flares
  (damage 2) pass the gates too. The cut bodies skip with the unported layer.
  The fairy's post-flip movement folds the same draw. Witness
  `the_blocked_move_consumes_exactly_one_next_3` pins it.
- The flare's `StatusNPC` OnFire `Next(3)` (`:11680`) is a HIT-time draw on the
  `UpdateProjectiles` stream, wired at the whip-debuff site (the C# order:
  `StatusNPC` runs after the strike, `:13580`).
- The torch placement draws nothing new (the support flatten's Dig sound rides
  the existing `UpdatePlayers` placement stream, the `place_tile` precedent).
- The biome-torch conversion draws nothing (a pure zone read).

## The broadsword melee swing (S1-P-i04, 2026-11-19)

Code-only round (no compiler invoked; witnesses WRITTEN NOT RUN). The
census of the useStyle-1 melee interaction found three verdicts:

* **WRONG - the melee hitbox.** The live arm
  (`world_sim/editing.rs:1120-1365`) hits the CURSOR POINT within four
  tiles of the player centre. The C# never reads the cursor for the melee
  hit: `ItemCheck_GetMeleeHitbox` (`Player.cs:45099-45190`) grows an
  integer `itemRectangle` off the swing's `itemLocation` per animation
  third, and `ItemCheck_MeleeHitNPCs` (`:44241-44253`) intersects it
  against every NPC box under the `immune[whoAmI] == 0 &&
  CanHitNPCWithMeleeHit(i) && attackCD <= 0` gate (`:44246`). The ported
  module (`melee_swing.rs`) carries the whole rect math verbatim: the DST
  frame shrinks (5094/5095 -10, 5096 -12, 5097 -8, `:45107-45125`), the
  `GetAdjustedItemScale` multiply (`:45128-45130`, `:42566-42582` - the
  1.1 meleeScaleGlove term rides a caller flag, the glove has no port
  owner), the facing/gravity flips (`:45131-45138`), the END third's
  `w*1.4`/`h*1.1` growth + the left-facing `(int)(w*1.4-w)` pull + the

### S1-P-i07 — the flail physics census (2026-11-20)
A line-by-line census of `AI_015_Flails` + `AI_015_HandleMovementCollision`
+ the `Player.ItemCheck_Shoot` launch arm against the M4-PROJ-3b port found
and fixed the following WRONGs (all C#-cited, tests written not run —
code-only swarm):
1. **Reel-in overshoot kill sign-flipped** (`:44011`). The C# dot is
   `vector4 · Utils.DirectionFrom(Target: Center+velocity, Origin:
   mountedCenter)`, and `Utils.DirectionFrom(Origin, Target)` =
   `Normalize(Origin - Target)` (`Utils.cs:1960-1963`) — the BACK vector.
   The port computed `ahead - mounted` (forward), killing approaching
   flails and sparing overshot ones. Fixed to `mounted - (head + vel)`.
2. **Flight/retract ×2 damage missing** (`:14462-14465`). States 1 and 2
   deal double; the port applied no multiplier. Added.
3. **Dual ×0.8 discount leaked out of the held state** (`:14450-14460`).
   The sibling scan sits inside the `ai[0]==0` arm; the port applied it in
   every state. Moved inside.
4. **`ResetLocalNPCHitImmunity` zeroed the wrong field** (`:43883` →
   `:43719-43722`). The C# clears `localNPCImmunity` (the per-slot NPC
   immunity array); the port zeroed `localAI[1]` (the orbit counter). Now
   rides `FlailTick.reset_immunity` → the pool clears the array; the orbit
   counter survives the release.
5. **Re-grab arms read `channel` instead of `controlUseItem`**
   (`:43905/43942/43959/44035`). `FlailInputs` gains `control_use_item`
   (the raw `mine_down`); `channel` stays for the state-0 release gate only.
6. **State-3/6 bail `break`s fell through** (`:43964`, `:44040`). The C#
   `break`s skip the orbit physics / gravity / `ChangeDir` on the bail
   tick; the port ran them. Restructured to if/else.
7. **State-3 `tileCollide` latch not re-armed per tick** (`:43967`). The
   C# sets `tileCollide = ai[1]==1` every tick before the flag4 compare;
   the port only wrote on the compare. Fixed.
8. **`mapFullscreen` kill missing** (`:43732-43736`). `FlailInputs` gains
   `map_fullscreen` (`app.map.open`); the local owner's flails die.
9. **Wet drag missing** (`HandleMovement` `:17612-17655`, `UpdatePosition`
   `:20439-20446`). Water ×0.5 / honey ×0.25 / shimmer ×0.375 position
   advance. Ported via `flail_wet_factor` (mid-tile idiom); the C# scales
   the velocity before the probe and restores a blocked component — the
   port probes full then scales the surviving displacement (the family's
   documented liquid approximation).
10. **Shimmer gravity skip missing** (`:44042`). State 6 adds +0.8 Y only
    when `!shimmerWet`; ported via `flail_shimmer_wet`.
11. **Flower Pow scan used a partial gate** (`:44121`). Now
    `Npc::can_be_chased_by` (`NPC.cs:90030-90041`: chaseable && lifeMax>5
    && !dontTakeDamage && !friendly && !immortal) instead of hp>0 &&
    !dontTakeDamage.
12. **`player.itemRotation` never written** (`:44162-44167`). Rides
    `FlailTick.item_rotation` (DirectionFrom + the left-of-mount π +
    WrapAngle); the dispatch applies it. `spriteDirection` now mirrors
    `direction` (`:44145`, `:44074`).
13. **`flag5` ignored the selected-item gate** (`:43850`). The dual-flail
    sibling flag only arms when `inventory[selectedItem].shoot != type`;
    `FlailInputs` gains `selected_shoot`.
14. **Dual-flail sibling launch missing** (`Player.cs:49413-49425`).
    Throwing Blue Moon/Sunfury with the other in the inventory now spawns
    it at the mirrored velocity, its own GetWeaponDamage/GetWeaponKnockback
    (`Player::weapon_knockback` added, `Player.cs:53346-53369`), `ai[2]=1`,
    before the primary spawn.
15. **Flairon bubble jitter used f32 `next_float`** (`:44093`). The C#
    `NextDouble()` is f64; `DropRng` gains `next_double` (one Sample draw,
    same stream) and the jitter multiplies in f64 before the f32 cast.
16. **`netUpdate` writes missing** on the state transitions / bounce
    (`:43882/43909/43922/43946/43963/43973/44024/44039`, `:43691/43701/
    43711`). Added (the pool's `clear_net_update_flags` owns the reset).
Remaining deviations (unchanged, decor/render follow-ups): the dust /
impact-explosion / HitTiles / sound arms, `player.heldProj` /
`SetDummyItemTime`, `ownerHitCheck` / `drawLayer`, the `noItems` gate, the
chain render, and the Flairon head 404 (aiStyle 69, a separate family that

## The bow launch (S1-P-i13)
**Mode.** Code-only: no `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt`/test runs, no dotnet, no
graphify — file reads/writes + git only. The C# arms were re-read whole and
compared line-by-line against the landed Rust; the 24 witness tests are
WRITTEN, NOT RUN. **No compiler invoked.**
**Assignment.** The bow use (`useAmmo=true`, `ammoType Arrow`) — the
`Player.ItemCheck_Shoot` bow launch arms vs the port. Scope: the bow LAUNCH
only. The arrow flight (aiStyle 1, `AI_001`) already landed with the
projectile-AI tasks; the ammo consumption is the i15 task's.
**Census (the WRONGs and the MISSING).** The pre-i13 shooter wire
(`world_sim/editing.rs`) fired every arrow/stake shooter through one generic
spawn: `center + dir*10`, the aim normalized to the fused speed, no per-bow
arm. Against `Player.cs:47056-49468` that was WRONG on three counts and
MISSING the whole special-arm family:
* **WRONG — the spawn anchor.** The C# spawns at
  `pointPosition = RotatedRelativePoint(MountedCenter)` (`:47196`), not the
  body centre + 10 px. For a stationary unmounted player the two coincide
  (`fullRotation=0`, `gfxOffY=0`, `mount.PlayerOffset=0` fold the rotation to
  the identity), but a mounted/rotated player diverges. The bow path now
  reads the real anchor.
* **WRONG — the facing flip.** The C# flips `base.direction` toward the
  cursor via `Dot(UnitX.RotatedBy(fullRotation), normalize(MouseWorld −
  pointPosition))` (`:47202-47224`) before the aim. The wire never flipped.
* **WRONG — the post-pick `projToShoot` overrides.** `:47157-47176` runs
  AFTER `PickAmmo` resolved the ammo's own `shoot`: the Molten Fury 120
  converts the wooden-arrow default 1 → the FireArrow 2 (the without-quiver
  path; the Molten Quiver's `:53537` already did it when armed), the Marrow
  682 → the Bone Arrow 117, the Ice Bow 725 → the FrostArrow 120, the Pulse
  Bow 2223 → the PulseBolt 357 — all unconditional except the Molten Fury's
  `proj == 1` gate. The wire fired the raw resolved kind, so the Marrow fired
  a wooden arrow, the Ice Bow a wooden arrow, the Pulse Bow a wooden arrow.
* **MISSING — the per-bow launch arms.** The Tsunami 2624's five-arrow π/10
  fan (`:47784-47809`), the Daedalus Stormbow 3029's rain (`:47424-47465`),
  the Blood Rain Bow 4381's rain (`:47466-47500`), the Hellwing 3019's dual
  `RotatedByRandom` (`:47573-47579`), the Chlorophyte Shotbow 1229's
  cumulative spread (`:48278-48308`), the DD2 Betsy Bow 3859's six-arrow fan
  forcing 710 (`:48748-48760`), the Fairy Queen 4953's aimed shot with the
  fan index and the `num61 == 2` prism double (`:47910-47957`). All fired as
  a single generic arrow before.
* **MISSING — the arrow `proj_data` rows.** The overrides and the arrow
  ammo's own `Item.shoot` resolve to kinds with NO row, so the data-carrying
  spawn declined them (the Marrow's 117 existed, but 120/357/710/323 and the
  arrow-ammo family 4/5/41/91/103/172/225/278/282/474/1006 did not). Added
  field-cited from the `SetDefaults` bodies (`Projectile.cs:837-863`,
  `:1237-1247`, `:1743-1752`, `:1904-1914`, `:2093-2104`, `:2579-2590`,
  `:3100-3110`, `:3638-3698`, `:4160-4171`, `:4474-4486`, `:5474-5484`,
  `:7521-7535`, `:9570-9579`), with the `ignoreWater` (5/710) and `light`
  (4/5/41/103/172/278) overlays.
**The port.** `crates/tr-app/src/bow_launch.rs` — `fire` applies the
post-pick overrides, builds the launch frame (the anchor, the facing flip,
the aim normalized to `speed` with the zero/NaN direction fallback
`:47291-47296`), dispatches the per-bow arm and spawns the arrows. The wire
routes arrow/stake shooters (`is_arrow_shooter`) through it; the `gunProj`
four and the non-arrow shooters keep the generic spawn (their launch arms
are their own tasks). `Projectile.no_drop_item` + `set_no_drop_item` carry
the multi-shot stamp (`Player.cs:47806`/`:48305`/`:47497`/`:47955`), which
the kill path's ammo-recovery drop reads (`Projectile.cs:77367`).
**RNG order.** No crit rolls at THROW time — the gate reconciliation with
S1-P-i11 moved the projectile crit to the per-hit roll
(`Projectile.cs:12883-12917`, `damage_pve`'s `projectile_hit_crit` on the
`UpdateProjectiles` stream), matching the C# (`ItemCheck_Shoot` never rolls
a ranged crit at spawn). The throw's `UpdatePlayers` stream spends no crit
draw; the launch arm's count roll is the first draw.
Within each arm the `Main.rand` draws are consumed in the C#'s exact order:
the Stormbow's count `Next(3)` then six per shot (`Next(201)`,
`Next(-100,101)`, `Next(-40,41)` vx, `Next(-40,41)` vy, `Next(75,150)`,
`Next(-50,51)`); the Blood Rain's `Next(1,3)` + `Next(3)` then seven per shot
(`Next(61)`, `Next(-30,31)`, `NextFloat`, `Next(-20,21)`, `Next(-40,41)`,
`Next(55,80)`, `Next(-50,51)`); the Chlorophyte's `Next(3)` then two per
spread shot; the Hellwing's FOUR `NextDouble` (the π/8 ai-spin pair then the
π/16 velocity pair, `Utils.cs:1697-1700`). The Tsunami/Betsy/Fairy Queen
draw NOTHING. The draw-count witness tests pin each against a replayed
stream.
**Documented folds.** `gravDir = 1` (no gravity flip) — the `:47285-47288`
reverse-gravity aim arm folds to a plain add. `ChangeDir`'s pulley
reposition (`Player.cs:42097-42110`) and its `itemRotation`/composite-arm
mirrors (`:42112-42115`) are transient in the port: `item_rotation` is
recomputed from `swing_aim` each frame (`world_sim/player.rs`) and the
composite arms are re-set by `ApplyUseStyle`, so only the persistent
`base.direction = dir` (`:42111`) lands. `MountedCenter == center` and
`ApplyItemPositionOffsetFromMount` is a no-op without an active mount
(`Player.cs:51387-51390`).
**Out of scope (recorded, not changed).** `GetWeaponKnockback`
(`Player.cs:53346-53369`: the summon `minionKB`, the `kbGlove`/`kbBuff`,
the Shroomite/Vortex stealth scales) is not called by the shooter wire — a

## S1-P-i18 special bullets (2026-11-20, code-only)
The eleven special-bullet projectile kinds (36 MeteorShot, 89
CrystalBullet, 104 CursedBullet, 207 ChlorophyteBullet, 242
BulletHighVelocity, 279 IchorBullet, 283 VenomBullet, 284 PartyBullet,
285 NanoBullet, 286 ExplosiveBullet, 287 GoldenBullet) plus the 90
CrystalShard spawn. Census + port: `docs/research/63-special-bullets-census.md`,
branch `task/S1-P-i18-special-bullets`. **Code-only mode — no compiler
invoked; the 13 `s1_p_i18_*` witnesses are WRITTEN NOT RUN.**
**The structural finding.** At the base (`aa147ce0`) NONE of the eleven
kinds had a `proj_data` row, so `spawn_with_data_ai_owned`'s
`proj_data(kind)?` (`projectile.rs:13102`) returned `None` and the shoot
wire's spawn (`editing.rs:1927`) silently declined every special bullet —
the shots never spawned. The specials were therefore MISSING (not WRONG):
there was no behaviour to diverge. Only 14 (musket ball) and 638
(Luminite, S1-D-4's `projectile_ai_moonlord`, FAITHFUL) had rows. The fix
is additive: the twelve `SetDefaults` rows + the per-type `AI_001` arms +
the on-hit debuffs + the death hooks.
**The split of labour (Lead coordination, `LEAD-I15-COORD.md`).** The Lead
staged the data rows + constants + `ProjLight` colour arms + the pool-side
death hooks (`special_bullet_kill` / `venom_burst_spread` /
`exploding_bullet_burst`) + the HighVelocity gun override (`ammo.rs`,
`Player.cs:47107-47118`) + the `npc_buffs` witness helpers; this worker
ported `projectile_special_bullets.rs` (the per-type AI arms + the on-hit
/ spread debuff arms). The two halves are kind-disjoint and compile
together.
**The Nanite ×1.25 is i15's, NOT this task's.** The i03 census A1
double-scale (resolver `ammo.rs:680-685` + wire `editing.rs:1892-1897`)
was fixed by i15 (`task/S1-P-i15-ammo-consumption`, `6df7e170`): the
resolver returns the unscaled `num`, the wire carries the single fused
`(int)(Damage * 1.25f)` after the add (`Player.cs:53552-53559`). That fix
lives on i15's branch, not in this base. Per the Lead's coord note this
task does NOT re-fix the scaling — re-fixing it here would conflict at
merge. The 285 row + effects land here; the single fused scale lands with
i15.
**The per-type arms (`projectile_special_bullets.rs`).** `step` mirrors
`AI_001`'s block order: the 242 speed fade (`:55660-55671`, the double
sqrt cast back to float, the `(byte)(speed * 0.9)` truncation), the
`flag3` counter (every special rests EXCEPT 207, which counts but its
homing block consumes the gravity else-if chain), the 207 homing block
(`:56778-56887`: the Manhattan-300 acquire with `Collision.CanHit`, the
1-based `ai[1]` lock, the Manhattan-1000 hold validity with
`CanBeChasedBy(ignoreDontTakeDamage: true) && !dontTakeDamage`, the
`(v * 7 + d) / 8` steer at the LATCHED `localAI[0]` speed), the default
rotation `Atan2(vy,vx) + 1.57f` (`:57748-57751`, no special has a
per-type rotation arm) + the exact C# +16 clamp (`:57753-57768`, slice
A/C's convention), then the `HandleMovement` probe with the 36 one-bounce
reflect (`:19278-19298`, penetrate 2 → reflect + spend one → die at 1)
and the 285 bounce (`:18563-18591`, `ai[1]++`, first bounce ×0.66 `(int)`,
second kills BEFORE the reflect, then `FindTargetWithLineOfSight` re-aim
at the latched speed). The on-hit debuffs (`bullet_on_hit_debuffs`) are
the `StatusNPC` arms (`:11537-11551` + `:11665-11677`), called from
`damage_pve`'s `special_bullet_status_npc` at `:13580`'s position (BEFORE
`StrikeNPC` `:13649`); the 283 spread's debuff-only re-hit
(`venom_burst_debuffs`) is the `type == 283 && !active` early arm
(`:12810-12814`).
**RNG (S1-A-10).** The AI arms take NO rng parameter — every `Main.rand`
in these kinds' `AI_001` blocks feeds dust alone (the ai001_a/b/c
dust-skip convention), so the flight is RNG-free by construction. The
state-bearing draws ride the pool's `UpdateProjectiles` pass stream
(`Main.cs:17775-17777`): the 285 Confused roll is ONE `Next(3)` per landed
hit (`:11543`, 180 on a zero else 60) at the StatusNPC position; the 89
split's 8 ranges (per shard `Next(40,70)` then `Next(-20,21)` for X, then
the same pair for Y, `:75264-75265`, argument evaluation order) ride
inline in `special_bullet_kill` (they place AND velocity the shard).
**The death-burst dust/gore convention (the Lead's choice).** The 283's
three 10-dust-171 loops (`:75913-75939`), the 284 confetti's 10 dust + 5
gore (`:75977-75998`, purely visual — no state, no spawn, no damage), the
286's 7 dust-31 + 6 dust-6 + 1 gore (`:76003-76018`) and the common arm's
HitTiles + Item10 (`:76035-76039`) are SKIPPED with their layers — bodies
AND draws. This is the ai001 convention (the pool has no dust/gore draw
layer), NOT the `projectile_ai_misc` draw-census convention that keeps
explicit visual draws. The 286 burst's DAMAGE half draws only the
per-NPC `DamageVar` the boxed walk already spends. The choice is recorded
here so a later dust-layer wiring knows these sites owe their draws.
**Deliberate stand-ins.** (1) `appliesImmunityTimeOnSingleHits` (the
286's `:3754`) has no `ProjData` field — the pool's idStatic gate reads a
kind check (`max_penetrate != 1 || kind == EXPLODING_BULLET`) in both
`damage_pve` and `damage_pve_boxed`. (2) The 283's `localAI[1] = -1f`
(`:75942`) is a verbatim DEAD write (no C# reader) — ported for its shape.
(3) The 285 PvP Confused arm (`StatusPlayer` `:12288-12298`) — no
projectile-PVP layer (single-player); recorded, not ported. (4) The 207
`Collision.CanHit` is the port's `can_hit` walk; the 285 re-target uses
the shared `find_target_with_line_of_sight` (`:45627-45660`). (5) The
movement probe kills without the C#'s final `position += velocity` on the
blocked tick (the port-wide `ai_style1_flight` stand-in, byte-identical to
slices A/B/C); the bounce arms integrate the reflected velocity on the
bounce tick (the typhoon 409 precedent). (6) The 283 burst's
`oldVelocity.ToRotation()` reads `p.vel` (no `oldVelocity` field); the
bullet rests its counter and flies straight, so `oldVelocity == velocity`
at death — faithful for every reachable 283. (7) The 90 shard flies the
existing `ai_crystal_storm` arm — its generic 0.96/15-tick drag/fade IS
the 90's C# arm (`:26004-26013`); the 1134 melee shard's first-tick
sound/dust block (`:25938-25952`) is kind-gated to 1134, so the 90 skips
it correctly. (8) The `Kill()` sound cues are skipped with the pool's
death-hook sound convention (`moonlord_arrow_kill`); the 36 bounce's
`SoundID.Item10` rides `wants_sound`.

## The thrown consumables (S1-P-i28, task/S1-P-i28-thrown-consumables, 2026-11-20, code-only mode)

The twelve thrown consumable weapons — Shuriken (42), Throwing Knife (279),
Poisoned Knife (287), Bone Javelin (3378), Molotov Cocktail (2590), Grenade
(168), Sticky Grenade (2586), Bouncy Grenade (3116), Beenade (1130), Holy
Water (422), Unholy Water (423), Blood Water (3477) — censused against
`Player.ItemCheck_Shoot` (`Player.cs:47056-49468`), the `ItemCheck` consumable
arm (`:43280-43326`), and the projectile `SetDefaults`/`AI`/`Kill`/`StatusNPC`
arms. The Javelin (3094) rides the same throwing arm and the same 507
projectile family as the Bone Javelin, so it is covered too.

### The census verdicts

**Item rows — OK (all twelve).** `itemdata.rs`'s generated rows match
`Item.cs` field-for-field (the `useStyle`/`shoot`/`shootSpeed`/`useTime`/
`useAnimation`/`consumable`/`ranged`/`crit`/`knockBack`/`autoReuse` values).
The three water bottles carry NO `ranged` flag (`Item.cs:6285-6318`,
`:31200-31216`); the other nine are `ranged`. The Poisoned Knife (287) and the
Bone Javelin (3378) are `autoReuse`; the rest are not. No row changed.

**The throwing arm — three WRONGs fixed (`world_sim/editing.rs`):**
1. The consumable decrement was unconditional (`count.saturating_sub(1)`).
   The C# (`Player.cs:43283-43300`) runs four not-consume rolls for a `ranged`
   consumable, each flag-gated and each consuming its draw even when an
   earlier roll already saved the stack (the `if`s are independent):
   `huntressAmmoCost90 → Next(10)==0`, `chloroAmmoCost80 → Next(5)==0`,
   `ammoCost80 → Next(5)==0`, `ammoCost75 → Next(4)==0`. The port now runs the
   chain on the `UpdatePlayers` stream in that order. `CanConsumeConsumableItem`
   is const-true (`:5496-5499`) and none of the twelve is in
   `ItemID.Sets.ForceConsumption` (`ItemID.cs:413-427`), so those gates pass.
   The water bottles skip the chain (no `ranged` flag) and always consume.
2. The javelin spawn-Y override was missing (`Player.cs:47225-47228`): the
   Javelin (3094) / Bone Javelin (3378) throw from `position.Y + height/3`
   (the integer division truncates 42/3 = 14), not the centre. Added.
3. The stack-empty cadence latch was missing (`Player.cs:43321-43324`):
   `if (item.stack <= 0) itemTime = itemAnimation`. The last throw now locks
   `item_time` to the remaining swing so the empty slot cannot re-fire.

**Projectile rows — MISSING, landed (`projectile/data.rs`).** Only the
Shuriken (3) and Throwing Knife (48) had rows. Added: Poisoned Knife (54,
aiStyle 2), the three waters (69/70/621, aiStyle 2), the three grenades
(30/397/517, aiStyle 16, `timeLeft 180`, the sticky's `tileCollide=false`),

### RNG order (the `UpdatePlayers` / `UpdateProjectiles` streams)

- The throwing arm's not-consume chain rides `UpdatePlayers`
  (`Player.ItemCheck` under the `Main.cs:17754` swap), in the C# order:
  huntress `Next(10)`, chloro `Next(5)`, ammoCost80 `Next(5)`, ammoCost75
  `Next(4)` — each flag-gated, no short-circuit. The crit roll precedes it
  (the throw's existing roll). The water bottles draw nothing (no `ranged`).
- The flight arms (68/113/36/507) draw ZERO `Main.rand` — their only rand
  riders are dust/sound, skipped whole with their draws (the `ai_style2` /
  frostmoon precedent).
- The on-hit debuffs ride `UpdateProjectiles` in C# order: the poisoned
  knife's `Next(2)`, the molotov/fire's `Next(3,7)`. The Daybroken is
  unconditional.
- The beenade death burst: 4 gore rows (`Next(61,64)` type + the `NewGore`
  kicks `Next(10,31)` Y-then-`Next(-20,21)` X, the G3 draw-census), then
  `Next(15,25)` count, then per bee the velocity `Next(-35,36)` X-then-Y, the
  `beeType` coin flip, `beeDamage`, `beeKB` (the `hurt_modifiers` order).
- The molotov death burst: per fire the X offset `Next(20,50)` +
  `Next(-20,21)`, the Y offset `Next(30,50)` + `Next(-20,5)`, then the
  fire-type `Next(3)` — six fires.

- Dust, gore bodies, `Lighting.AddLight`, sound bodies (the cues ride

  `UseGroupStaticImmunity(181)`, `Projectile.cs:2684`/`:6183`) folds to the

- The water splash uses `convert_cell_flavor` (the per-cell map, the
