   `!(vy < -0.5) || gravDir != -1`): e1 proceeds while rising fast.
3. `:10171` the wallslide `:21777` gate, same bug (clings at rest).
4. `:10186` `else if (wall && vy > 0.5) || vy < -0.5` — the second disjunct
   is the C# `:21814` gravDir −1 arm, UNGUARDED in e1: a rising player
   slides with NO wall.
5. `:10130` `climb_probe_solid` divides (`(probe.x / TILE_PX) as i32`)
   where `ToTileCoordinates` is `(int)v >> 4` (`Utils.cs:1807-1810`) — the
   arithmetic shift differs on negative probe coordinates.
f3's copy has none of these (the folds are cited per-arm). e1's
`WallClingDust`/`wall_cling_puff`/`take_wall_cling_dust` + the two host
machines are dropped wholesale; f3's `WallDust`/`drain_wall_dust` survive.

**(e) Stealth — KEEP f3's chain; e1's spawn default is WRONG.** C#
`Player.cs:1562`: `public float stealth = 1f;` — f3 spawns `stealth: 1.0`
(`player.rs:3306`), e1 spawns `stealth: 0.0` (its `:3063`). f3's
`update_stealth` is the FULL `:25733-25899` else-if chain (shroomite arm +
vortex arm + the `else stealth = 1` reset); e1's `update_vortex_stealth`
(`:10290-10331`) is the vortex arm only, with the reset deferred to "the
shroomite lane" (its own comment) — but f3 IS that lane, already landed.
The ring drains are chain-identical (f3 `drain_vortex_stealth`
`player_dust.rs:985` × e1 `vortex_stealth_rings` `player_dust2.rs:1117`,
both replay `:25874-25893` draw-for-draw); KEEP f3's queue + drain, drop
e1's `VortexRingDust` + `update_vortex_stealth`. e1's set-loss disarm
(`3245d624`, `:16315-16321`) is already f3's (`player.rs:7056`).

**(f) The shared-site overlaps beyond wall/carpet/stealth — merge verdicts.**
* `DoubleJumpVisuals` (`:21892-22021`): THREE copies (f3
  `drain_double_jump_dust` `player_dust.rs:748`, g66
  `player_trail_dust::drain_double_jump_visuals`, e1
  `player_dust2::double_jump_visuals`). KEEP f3's (the d51-merged
  performing-jump lifecycle + the cancel sites are f3's); the g66/e1
  drains are the same six-arm chain.

  capture** — e1 `3245d624` captures `falling` at the movement head
  (`:28073-28081`) so landing ticks fire the 20-dust burst; f3's capture
  sits on the REST path (`player.rs:8453`, `vy == 0` gate) where
  `vy > gravity || vy < -gravity` is always false — f3's landing burst
  never fires. At the e1b merge the f3/g66 floor drains survive but the
  `falling` input MUST come from e1's head capture (a one-line re-site,
  not a machine rewrite). e1's drain-order fidelity round (hair-dye/

* e1's pre-21654 lanes (Yoraiz0r eye, GlassSlipper, Solar, teleport,
  regen sparkles, MowTheLawn, hair-dye, manaHeat, stoned, drowning,
  splash) have NO f3/g66 counterpart — they land as-is.

**Net e1b-141 merge recipe (player-move family):** f3's machines + grants +

## The expert/master boss bag open trees (W4-f35, code-only mode)
The census (`docs/research/184-expert-drop-trees-census.md`) splits the
boss loot into two trees. The DEATH side — `NPC.NPCLoot`
(`NPC.cs:78830-78899`) → `NPCLoot_DropItems` (`:78925-78937`) → the
`ItemDropDatabase` boss registrations, where `ItemDropRule.BossBag`
(`ItemDropRule.cs:10-13`) is a `DropBasedOnExpertMode(DropNothing,
DropLocalPerClientAndResetsNPCMoneyTo0)` (the bag ONLY in expert, its
`CommonCode` zeroes `npc.value`) and the master relics/pets ride
`Conditions.IsMasterMode` — already runs through `tr_core::loot` +
`loot_db_gen` (S1-E-14a, 1599 registrations). This task ports the OTHER
half: what OPENING the bag grants.
### The port (`crates/tr-app/src/boss_bags.rs`)
`open_boss_bag(bag, env, rng, out)` ports `Player.OpenBossBag`
(`Player.cs:7202-7883`) verbatim for all 19 openable bags (3318-3332,
3860, 4782, 4957, 5111). The C# keeps two sequential switches
(`:7206-7674` and `:7675-7743`); they are disjoint per type, so one
match keeps the same per-bag order. The grant-less Ogre/Dark Mage bags
(3861/3862, in `ItemID.Sets.BossBag` but with no case) run only the
money tail. Every grant rides `quick_spawn` = `QuickSpawnItem`
(`Player.cs:7170-7180`): the `stack > 0` gate, then `SetDefaults` →
`Prefix(-1)` (the natural roll, `Item.cs:504-618`, on the SAME stream)
→ the stack write — so a prefixable grant's prefix draws interleave
between the bag's chance rolls (the loot-slot RNG order).
The verbatim details kept: the EoW/BoC DISCARDED `num5`/`num6` draws
(`:7257`/`:7287`, the stream advances though the value is never read);
the master-mode ore/ingot bumps (EoW `Next(110,136)`/`Next(30,51)` vs
classic `Next(80,111)`/`Next(20,41)`, BoC the same on 880/1329); the
King Slime do-while re-picks the SECOND piece (`:7218-7222`) while the
Queen Slime re-picks the FIRST (`:7664-7669`) — the asymmetry; the Moon
Lord `Next(count)`+`RemoveAt` two-distinct-weapon bundle (`:7734-7740`)
and the `HasItem(3384)` Portal Gun gate (`:7726`); the WoF Demon Heart
gated `!extraAccessory` (`:7380`); the Fishron remix-seed option-6 swap
(Aqua Scepter 157 vs Bubble Gun 2623, `:7560-7567`); the EoC ore stack
is THREE `Next(21)+10` draws summed in argument order (`:7250`).
`try_getting_dev_armor` (`Player.cs:7885-8026`) leads the hardmode bags
(3325-3332, 3860, 4782 — NOT the Queen Slime/Deerclops): the
`Next(tenthAnniversary ? 8 : 16) == 0` gate, then `Next(21)` picks one
of the 21 dev sets, each piece its own `QuickSpawnItem`; sets 10/11
carry the torch tails (3024×4 / 3599×4).
### The money tail and the e25 boundary
`bag_money` (`Player.cs:7833-7882`) builds a FRESH `NPC.SetDefaults(num9)`
— whose `ScaleStats` tail (`NPC.cs:17856`) scales `value` by the
difficulty money curve in expert/master (×2.5, e25's lane, UNWIRED).
`BagEnv::value_multiplier` is that seam: the wiring passes 1.0 (the
classic world the port models today), and the `(int)` truncation of
`ScaleStats_ByDifficulty` (`NPC.cs:18176`) is kept. The base values are
the classic `SetDefaults` table (the census; `Item.buyPrice(0,g)` =
`g*10000`, `Item.cs:49417-49420`). Then the ±20 % spread, the 1/5, 1/10,
1/15, 1/20 bonus chains, and the platinum/gold/silver/copper split —
NO >50 shrink rolls here (unlike `NPCLoot_DropMoney`), the `(int)`
truncations and the copper `< 1 → 1` floor verbatim. The zero-value
bosses (Betsy/Ogre/Dark Mage) draw the 5 gates and mint nothing.
### The wiring (`app/clicks.rs::open_boss_bag_click` + `open_container_click`)
The `ItemSlot.RightClick` `OpenableBag` arm (`UI/ItemSlot.cs:1660-1667`)
fires on the press edge (`Main.mouseRightRelease`) with an air cursor or
one that cannot stack with the cell, BEFORE the `HasItemSwap` cycle
(`:1668`). The arm now covers ALL 58 `ItemID.Sets.OpenableBag` kinds
(`ItemID.cs:1384`): the 21 boss bags dispatch to `open_boss_bag_click`,
the other 37 (26 crates + 11 misc/present kinds) to
`open_container_click`, which ports `TryOpenContainer_GrantItems`'
else-if order (`:1806-1865`) — the fishing crates → the herb bag 3093 →
the can of worms 4345 → the oyster 4410 → the goodie bag 1774 → the
chillet egg 6142 → the Lock Box 3085 (the Golden Key 327 CONSUME gate,
`ConsumeItem(327, reverseOrder: false, includeVoidBag: true)` — a miss
returns false: NO decrement, NO sound, NO cooldown) → the Shadow
Lockbox 4879 (the Shadow Key 329 PRESENCE gate,
`HasItemInInventoryOrOpenVoidBag` — NOT consumed) → the Present 1869 →
the legacy presents 599/600/601. `TryOpenContainer` (`:1786-1804`)
grants FIRST, then the bag stack decrements (`:1795-1799`), sound 7
(`:1800`), `stackSplit = 30` (`:1801`), `mouseRightRelease = false`
(`:1802`) — the shared `finish_container_open` tail. Every grant rides
`GetOrDropItem(PickupItemFromWorld)` (`Player.cs:7187-7199`): the
`Player.GetItem` fill (the coin rows + `DoCoins` per fill for coins, the
`deposit_pickup` ammo/occupied/hotbar/reverse-empty walk for non-coins —
the shared `fill_quick_spawn_grants`), the void vault as the last
resort (`GetItemSettings.cs:57`'s `CanGoIntoVoidVault`), the overflow a
world drop at the player's centre (`Item.RequestNewItem`, `:7198`, the
prefix preserved — no fresh roll). The whole open is a UI click OUTSIDE
every `SwapRandom` block, so the bag rolls AND the fill chimes ride
`NamedRngs::global()` (the bare-`Main.rand` stand-in, the
`quick_transfer_from_slot` precedent); every named stage stream stays
pristine.

`crates/tr-app/src/proj_trail_dust.rs` ports the REPEATING in-flight dust
sites of `Projectile.AI()`'s per-kind arms for **kinds ≥ 401** — 41 kinds in
5 commits of ≤ 10 (the claim ledger `docs/research/196-proj-trail-dust-claims-g64.md`

d50 foundation). The branch base fast-forwards onto
`origin/task/W4-d50-dust-type-table` (`2e243a2d`) for the DustPool contract.

**Scope rule:** a "trail" is the dust a kind sheds while it flies. One-shot
spawn-latch bursts (`localAI[0] == 0` / `ai[1] == 0` first-tick blocks) stay
with the general proj-site co-lanes and are cited per kind in the ledger;
death bursts are g65's (596's `timeLeft < 4` burst, 1053's HandleMovement
bounce pair). Deferred within ≥ 401 (cited in the ledger): 813 (the 13-site
four-phase machine), 957 (the behaviour-coupled spelunker tile scan), 670
(the style-126 sites are style-generic, not kind-gated), 644 (the prism-hue
orbit), 493/494, 836, 968, 1134 (one-shots), 1044/624 (the flag60 arm is
ParticleOrchestrator-only; flag59 is the ai[0]==1 explosion), 590 (the
census rows at :34272+ belong to 644 — the `type != 644` return precedes
them; 590's own block is light-only).

**Contract:** every draw rides the caller's **UpdateProjectiles** stream
(`Main.cs:17775`'s `SwapRandom`), per-slot C# statement order — explicit
argument draws FIRST, then the `NewDust` internals (`Dust.cs:75-256` via
`DustPool::new_dust`/`new_dust_perfect`/`new_dust_direct`), then the
post-spawn writes; the sentinel slot (6000) takes the writes exactly like
the C#. The C# `Dust dustN = Main.dust[idx]` aliases are class references —
ported as `slot_mut` chains in statement order.

**Deliberate deviations / drops (each cited at its site):**

* **UNWIRED** (the d50 / `npc_ai_*` code-only precedent): the wiring wave
  threads `app.dust` + the frame's `spawn_ctx()` into
  `world_sim/projectiles.rs` and calls each fn at its cited site with the

## The buff HUD verbatim round (W4-c26, 2026-11-20)

Code-only follow-up on S1-E-6 + S1-P-i53 (`task/W4-c26-buff-hud`).

### The three verbatim draw deltas (fixed)

`Main.DrawBuffIcon` (`Main.cs:43307-43368`) draws the icon text at
`:43327` on `FontAssets.ItemStack.Value`, scale `0.8f`, at
`(x, y + Buff[num].Height())`, in the SAME `color` the icon used —
the four-channel `Main.buffAlpha[slot]` colour built at `:43314`.
The S1-E-6 pass drew it white `[1;4]` at 0.85 through `hud_text`
(the Mouse_Text font). All three are verbatim deltas; the draw now
calls `text::hud_item_text` (the ItemStack seam) at 0.8 with
`[a,a,a,a]`. The selection (`:43316-43324`: the
`BuffTextHandlers` counter wins, else the `TryGetBuffTime`-gated
duration when `> 2` ticks, `buffTimeValue / 60` seconds) is split
into `resources::buff_icon_text` so the gates witness without a
renderer.

### GetBuffTooltip's percent arms (the S1-E-6 drops closed)

`Main.cs:43282`: `text + ((int)(player.manaSickReduction * 100f) + 1) + "%"`
— the f32 multiply, the truncating `(int)`, then the `+ 1` AFTER
the cast (a 0.0 reduction still appends "1%"). `:43285`:
`text + (int)(Math.Ceiling(player.manaHeat * 100f) - 100.0) + "%"` —
the multiply is f32, `Math.Ceiling` promotes the product to double,
minus the double `100.0`, then the `(int)` truncation. Both fields
exist on the port's Player since i19/i52 (`mana_sick_reduction`
starts 0.0, `mana_heat` starts 1.0 — `Player.cs:16994`/`:18593`),
so `buff_tooltip`'s two match arms append the computed percent.
`DebugOptions.ManaPotionDelay` (`:43278-43281`) is the developer
test toggle — constants-off false, the plain arm always runs. The
old S1-E-6 witness that pinned 396 to the bare description row was
repointed: default `manaHeat == 1.0` ceils to 100, so the appended
text is "0%".

### The atlas placeholder (deliberate deviation)

The C# never misses an icon: `TextureAssets.Buff[num]` is requested
eagerly for the whole id range. The port's atlas is enumeration-only
(`Buff_<id>.xnb` present in the content dir), and the S1-E-6 draw
`continue`d on a missing sheet — the slot silently vanished AND
skipped its hover/cancel block (a real behavioural loss, not just a
pixel one). Now a missing sheet draws a grey 32x32 box on
`SpriteRenderer::white_uv` tinted `0.5 * a` (the crafting-slot
placeholder convention, `ui/crafting.rs`), sized 32x32 because the
retail buff icons are 32x32 sheets (every sampled `Buff_<id>.xnb` —
1/24/111/147/396 — decompresses to 4273 bytes = a 173-byte reader
header + the i32 pixel-block length + 4096 = 32*32*4 RGBA); the slot
keeps its grid cell,
alpha fade, icon text, hover tooltip and right-click cancel. This is
a stand-in for unextracted content, never a substitute for a present
sheet.

### The cancel hit-test seam (i53 wired)

The gate half is i53's `App::buff_cancel_gate` (`Main.cs:43333`'s
`mouseRight && mouseRightRelease` + the `:62458-62465` end-of-draw
latch); `draw_region` computes it once and feeds `draw_buffs`'
`right_click`. The rect half (`:43329`) is strict `<`/`>` on
ALL four edges — the shared `ui::in_rect_strict` seam, which the
draw now calls instead of a private four-comparison copy (identical
semantics, one copy per the house rule). On hit: hovered slot +
alpha +0.1 + the slot pushed onto `buff_removals` when the gate is
true; the tick drains through `Player::try_removing_buff`
(`world_sim/player.rs`, ahead of the dead branch). The hover NAME
row reads `lang::buff_name` direct (`Lang.GetBuffName`,
`Lang.cs:241-244`) — the c21 accessor lane owns any deeper
rework; this lane only pins the read.

### The witnesses (written, NOT run)

`ui/resources.rs` (`s1_e_6_tests`): the repointed 396 default-0%
arm; `w4_c26_the_mana_percent_arms_append_the_player_computed_text`
(the +1-after-truncation, the ceil-then-minus-100 order, the 1%/0%
floors); `w4_c26_the_icon_text_prefers_the_counter_then_the_duration`
(counter-only 64, the no-time-display hide, the 100 s -> "2 m"
ceiling, the >2-tick gate incl. the drawn "0 s", the vampire-seed
hide); `w4_c26_the_hover_name_reads_the_buff_name_row_directly`;
`w4_c26_the_cancel_hit_test_is_strict_on_every_edge` (all four open
edges + the 6-px inter-icon gap). The gate-conjunction witness stays
`app/frame/draw.rs::s1_p_i53_the_cancel_gate_fires_on_press_not_on_release`.

### Verification

Code-only: no cargo/rustc/rustfmt/tests invoked (worker rules). Every
delta re-read against `Main.cs:43203-43404` and `:62450-62465`;

### The seam: the kill_tail_cue death-hook map

The C# plays these cues inside `Kill()` while the slot is STILL active
(`active = false` lands at `:77262`, after every death arm). The port's
death hook (`projectile.rs`'s `!active` block, after the sub-steps) is the
same once-per-death seam: the new `ProjectilePool::kill_tail_cue` runs
inside the `!died_out_of_world` gate (the out-of-world guard's direct
deactivate never reaches `Kill()`, the S1-P-i23 precedent) and pushes
straight into `pending_proj_sounds` — NOT the slot's `wants_sound` field,
whose forward runs earlier (before the death hook). Every mapped arm
plays before its own state writes or has none, so the hook's PRE-hook
position read is the C#'s play position. The drain
(`world_sim/projectiles.rs`) now routes id 13/6 to the wall-break facade

gameplay draws ride the pass-tail `UpdateProjectiles` stream (the 21h
batch convention — relative order among the tick's sound draws preserved,
interleaving with gameplay draws not).

### The achievement census — GAIN_TORCH_GODS_FAVOR is a USE flag, not a progression
The brief's "f30 progression-45?" question resolves at census: the f30 tail
(`origin/task/W4-f30-achievement-notify-2`, research/30) covers progression
ids 21/33-46 — id 45 is TRASH_COMPACTOR (`CheckResearchAchievement`), and
**no progression id names the torch row**. `GAIN_TORCH_GODS_FAVOR` is
`CustomFlagCondition.Create("Use")` (`AchievementInitializer.cs:360-362`,
the registry's one `Category::None` row, icon 109). Its ONLY notify site in
the whole C# is the 5043 use's `HandleSpecialEvent(this, 24)`
(`Player.cs:45233` → `AchievementsHelper.cs:367-369`'s
`GetCondition("GAIN_TORCH_GODS_FAVOR", "Use").Complete()`).
**The event-end grant fires NO achievement.** `TorchAttack`'s survival arm
(`Player.cs:17870-17873`) drops the 5043 item and nothing else — no
`HandleSpecialEvent`, no `NotifyProgressionEvent`; the item PICKUP is not a
condition either (the row is a Use flag, not `ItemPickupCondition(5043)`).
So the achievement completes when the player USES the favor, not when they
survive the event — the port's `torch_god.rs` event-end correctly stays
silent, and the use arm's `handle_special_event(24)` is the one wire.
Witnesses: `achievements.rs::w4_f33_the_torch_god_row_is_a_use_flag_not_a_progression`
(the row's condition shape + no progression id completes it) and
`w4_f33_special_event_24_completes_only_the_torch_row` (the named complete
leaves the other eight "Use" rows open, queues the completion event once,
the second 24 is a no-op).

the two gate forms (`!forced.HasValue || !forced.Value != flag` ≡
`forced.is_none() || forced == Some(off)`; the early-return
`forced.HasValue && !forced.Value == flag` ≡
`forced.is_some() && forced != Some(off)`) are logically identical, the
anchor decodes match (the single-`if` wraps in `Toggle2x2Light`/
`ToggleChandelier` are the C#'s own, not `while` loops), and the OFF flags
key on the same cell (clicked vs anchor) as the C#.
**Keep-one recommendation: the d6 free-function family is the canonical
superset — KEEP IT.** It is the only port of the `TryToggleLight` dispatch
and of `ToggleTorch`/`ToggleCampFire` as forced-state statics; the base
`Wiring` methods cover only 8 of the 10 statics and hard-code the wire
lane's null-forced/`doSkipWires=true` call shape. The two lanes are NOT
duplicates to delete blindly:
* The base methods (e20's witnesses pin them, incl. the 2322af90 lantern
  fixture fix — both cells share the lit state, the return trip keys on
  the hit cell's `frameX`) carry the `SkipWire` flood bookkeeping the free
  functions deliberately skip (every gun-stream caller passes
  `skipWires: false`, `Projectile.cs:29080`/`:29110`). KEEP the methods +
  the e20 witnesses for the `HitWireSingle` lane.
* c42's case-4 torch arm and `toggle_camp_fire` duplicate the d6 statics'
  maths for the wire lane. At merge, dedupe them onto the d6 free
  functions with a skip-set parameter (the campfire drops ride
  `actuation_drops` there, the free fn's `drops` out-param here — the
  same `ObjectDrop` shape); until that refactor the two copies are
  behaviour-identical under null forced state (verified above).
* The d6 `toggle_campfire`'s literal `kind != 215` gate vs c42's
  `SET_CAMPFIRES.has`: the set is exactly {215} (`TileID.cs:616`), so they
  are equivalent today; prefer the set read at the dedupe.

## The wind leaf particles (W4-g68, 2026-11-20, code-only)

The wind-driven leaf layer now rides the real gore machinery end to end:
spawn (`TileDrawing.EmitTreeLeaves` `TileDrawing.cs:7779-7891` and
`EmitLivingTreeLeaf`/`_Below`/`_Sideways` `:7549-7592`), physics
(`Gore_UpdateLeaf` `Gore.cs:1085-1209`, the S1-E-4 `GorePool::update_leaf`)
and draw (`Main.DrawGore` `Main.cs:21873-21907`, the S1-E-4b
`render/gore.rs` pass). CODE-ONLY MODE: no compiler invoked; the 17
witnesses (8 foliage + 8 tr-core leaf physics + 1 sand wind coupling) are
WRITTEN NOT RUN.

**The d60-flagged 192-leaf deviation is reconciled.** The W4-d60 census
(77429fe1) flagged the inline `render/tiles.rs` arm: it gated on
`wind.sway_enabled` (the C# does NOT), drew the sideways `Next(2)` only
when the wind pick was non-zero (the C# draws it UNCONDITIONALLY after
the below-spawn), used a one-cell downwind probe (the C# needs TWO open
cells), dropped the paint column and never handled type 384. The arm now
calls the faithful `emit_living_tree_leaf` trio in `render/foliage.rs`
(the same body d60's unwired `tile_draw_particles.rs` carries — when that
module lands, the wiring wave dedupes onto one copy):

* the gate is `emit_effects && kind in {192, 384}` then
  `_rand.Next(leafFrequency / 4) == 0` (`:6848-6855`); 192 sheds gore 910,
  384 sheds 914;
* below (`:7558-7569`): the tile under must be non-strict-solid and dry;
  wind < −0.2 needs (x−1, x−2) open at y+1, wind > 0.2 needs (x+1, x+2);
  `NewGorePerfect` at `(x*16, y*16+16)`, zero velocity, scale 1;
* sideways (`:7571-7592`): the unconditional `Next(2)`; `num` = the wind
  sign above 0.2 else 0 (dead wind probes the tile's OWN cell — a 192
  block is walk-through, so both gores spawn); the −10 px left-shift
  quirk; position `(x*16 + 8 + 4*num + num2, y*16 + 8)`;
* both writes set `Frame.CurrentColumn = tile.color()` (the paint column
  the `Main.DrawGore` framed source rect reads).

**The private leaf pool is retired.** The old `LeafGore` Vec (400-cap,
`App.leaves`) with its draw-time `tick_leaves` approximation is deleted:
its fall/rest math re-derived `Gore_UpdateLeaf` with a simplified probe
(no liquid-rect intersection, no honey/lava arms, no `DisappearSpeed`
rows, a floor() tile probe instead of the `(int)x >> 4` shift). Every
leaf is now a `GorePool` slot: the 600-slot pressure (`Gore.NewGore`'s
first-inactive scan + refuse sentinel) replaces the 400-cap drain, the
`gores` phase (`Main.cs:17971`, between NPCs and projectiles) ticks the
faithful physics, and `Main.DrawGore` draws it with `Gore.GetAlpha` and
the 32-column paint frame. `App.leaves`, `foliage::draw_leaves`,
`Lookups::leaf_gores/leaf_sheet/leaf_uv/leaf_frame` are removed (the
`gore_sheets` map already carries every `Gore_<id>` sheet, 914 included).

**RNG census — two streams kept separate (the d60 precedent).** The gate
draws (`Next(frequency)`, the 192/384 `Next(maxValue)`, the sideways
`Next(2)`) ride `TileDrawing._rand` — the port's per-frame pinned
`FastRandom` stand-in (`sparkle_seed ^ 0x9E37…`, the TILE-DRAW-3
convention). The `Main.rand` draws ride the App's bare global
`UnifiedRandom` (`NamedRngs::global`): the C# tile-draw emission runs
OUTSIDE every `SwapRandom` block (`Main.cs:17811-17812` sits after the
`UpdateServerOrClient` wrapper closes), so the global stream is the
faithful home. In C# order: `EmitTreeLeaves`' hallowed height pick
`Next(0, 28)` (`:7884` — previously mis-rolled on the gate stream), then
the `NewGoreDirect` ARGUMENT draws `RandomVector2(Main.rand, −2, 2)`
(two `NextFloat`, X then Y, `Utils.cs:2431-2434`) and the scale roll
`0.7 + NextFloat()*0.6` (`:7889`), then `NewGore`'s internals
(`Gore.cs:1327-1328` velocity jitter, the SpecialAI-3 four-draw leaf
init `:1393-1401`). The `RandomVector2` velocity is DISCARDED by the
leaf init but its draws still fire (argument evaluation precedes the
call). `NewGorePerfect` (the living-wood arms) burns the same internals
then overwrites position/velocity — zero velocity survives.

**Deliberate deviations / deferred seams.**
* The emission gate `_isActiveAndNotPaused`
  (`FocusHelper.AllowTileDrawingToEmitEffects`, `TileDrawing.cs:469`)
  reads `!game_paused && !TR_NO_WIND` — the focus gate is unported; the
  A/B switch keeps the whole wind feature screenshotable. **The exact C#
  contract (W4-g68 deferred-2 census): the gate is NOT `!gamePaused`** —
  `FocusHelper.cs:27` reads `!WorldUpdateStepper.DrawnThisUpdate`, a flag
  cleared at the top of every world update (`Main.cs:17747`) and set at
  the END of the first draw after it (`Main.cs:62478`, inside `DoDraw`).
  So vanilla emits on the FIRST DRAW PER WORLD UPDATE — at 60 Hz update +
  60 Hz draw that is once per frame; at a 144 Hz display the extra draws
  emit NOTHING (the flag is already set); during a multi-update catch-up
  frame only the draws after the LAST update's clear can emit. Pause is
  orthogonal: a paused game still draws, but `ShouldUpdateWorld` gates
  the update, so the flag stays set and emission stops — the port's
  `!game_paused` approximates the steady state, not the mechanism.
* **The per-rebuild emission cadence — the exact d60 wiring contract
  (W4-g68 deferred-2; site 1's leaf arm GATED by wiring-3, 2026-11-21).**
  C# runs the emission bodies from THREE draw-pass
  sites, each with its own cadence:
  1. `DrawSingleTile` (`TileDrawing.cs:965-968`): the
     `_isActiveAndNotPaused && (!Lighting.UpdateEveryFrame ||
     FastRandom(Main.TileFrameSeed).WithModifier(x,y).Next(4)==0)` gate.
     `Lighting.UpdateEveryFrame` (`Lighting.cs:77-87`) is FALSE whenever
     render targets are required (the normal path) — so the quarter-roll
     normally APPLIES: each tile emits on ~1/4 of the eligible draws.
     `TileFrameSeed` re-seeds every FIFTH draw (`Main.cs:61719-61723`,
     `_drawCycleCounter % 5`, `Utils.RandomNextSeed`), so the eligible
     tile set rotates on a 5-draw cycle. The roll is a THROWAWAY
     `FastRandom` per tile — it does NOT step `TileDrawing._rand`.
  2. `DrawGrass`/`DrawAnyDirectionalGrass` (`:8346-8352`, `:8403-8409`)
     and the two multi-tile-grass-in-wind passes (`:8974-8980`,
     `:9485-9491`): `flag = _rand.Next(4)==0` — a REAL `_rand` draw per
     special-point tile per draw, then `_isActiveAndNotPaused & flag`.
     These ride the `PostDrawTiles(solidLayer: false)` chain
     (`:414-434`), NOT the G6-cacheable tile range.
  3. `EmitTreeLeaves` (`:7779-7891`, from `DrawTrees` `:8121/8166/8214`):
     NO quarter-roll — only `_isActiveAndNotPaused` (`:7781`) plus its
     own `Next(frequency)` gate (`:7830`). `DrawTrees` also rides
     `PostDrawTiles` (`:428`).
  The port fires all three from the G6-cached `draw_tiles` rebuild
  (`render/tiles.rs` + `foliage.rs`), so the shed cadence is per-REBUILD:
  a windy world rebuilds every frame (the sway counters ride the key) and
  the cadence approximates vanilla's; a CALM world caches and emits only
  on camera/liquid/light changes — vanilla would still shed at
  1/14000-per-tile-draw in dead calm. `_leafFrequency` itself is ticked
  per world update in C# (`TilesRenderer.Update()`, `Main.cs:17812`,
  `TileDrawing.cs:376`); the port re-derives it from the live wind each
  call (`wind::leaf_frequency`) — same value, no state. **Contract for
  the d60 wiring wave:** move the emission calls OUT of the cached range
  into a per-frame pass (the `tile_cracks.rs` precedent, `draw.rs:1198-
  1206`: per-frame world-range overlay, `WorldFrameKey` untouched), gate
  site 1 on the throwaway `FastRandom(tile_frame_seed).with_modifier
  (x,y).next(4)==0` with the 5-draw seed cycle, sites 2/3 on their own
  gates; the `_rand` stand-in must then become a PERSISTENT stream (C#
  `TileDrawing._rand` is one `UnifiedRandom` for the renderer's lifetime,
  `:191` — the port's per-frame `FastRandom` pin is a determinism
  stand-in, not the C# stream), and the `DrawnThisUpdate` flag needs a
  port field cleared per world tick / set after the first draw. Do NOT
  widen the G6 key to force per-frame rebuilds — that re-tiles the whole
  world every frame (the cache exists to avoid exactly that).
  **Wiring-3 cadence verify (2026-11-21):** the frequency chain is 1:1 —
  `wind::leaf_frequency` matches `UpdateLeafFrequency`
  (`TileDrawing.cs:7719-7771`) band-for-band incl. the ×7, and
  `emit_tree_leaves`' hallowed /2 → height-10000 → branch ×3 order matches
  `:7816-7833` exactly (`Main.WindForVisuals` = `windSpeedCurrent`,
  `Main.cs:2823`, so the live re-derivation equals the per-update tick).
  The DIVERGENCE found + fixed: the inline 192/384 arm lacked site 1's
  quarter-roll — the C# wraps the whole `DrawTiles_EmitParticles` call
  (the leaf arms included) in the throwaway
  `FastRandom(TileFrameSeed).WithModifier(x,y).Next(4)==0` gate
  (`:965-968`), so the port shed 4× too often. The arm now carries the

## The wind seal (W4-g68, 2026-11-21, code-only) — research/328 SEALED

The g68-side close of the d130 WEATHER-FAMILY bible (research/83 §9.4,
`b8f655708`): **g68 is the SINGLE wind-flag owner** — `tr-core/wind.rs`'s
`Wind` is the only integrator of `windSpeedCurrent`/`windSpeedTarget`,
every family consumer read-only (d130 rain velocity `wind*18,14`, the
folded g67 Eyebrella drip `wind*3,9`, c40's wind-only Sandstorm severity,
g68's own leaf cadence `WindForVisuals == windSpeedCurrent`
`Main.cs:2823`). The full receipts + the wind-family bible live in
`docs/research/328-g68-wind-seal.md` (registry 328 FINAL per §9.2 —
renumbered from provisional 247, d10 EXECUTED keeps 247).

**The final-phase missing arms (landed `32ee28ca5` + `2075c3aaa`):** the
in-flight dirty state at resume was g68's OWN stale work (co-lane probe:
no live writer, mtimes ~4.5 h old, every hunk cites W4-g68 — NOT an
alive-advancing foreign co-lane). Adjudicated hunk-by-hunk:
* **KEPT (wind.rs, g68-unique, hunk-disjoint from d130's `lanterns_up`
  graft):** (1) the remix branch of `UpdateWindyDayState`
  (`Main.cs:13021-13027` — remix clears the STORM flag, leaves windy-day

## The projectile death dust (W4-g65, task/W4-g65-proj-death-dust, code-only)
The per-kind dust bursts inside `Projectile.Kill()`
(`Projectile.cs:70642-77262`) — the dust that fires ONCE when a slot dies,
distinct from the per-tick TRAIL dust (the g63/g64 lanes) and from the i17/i18
special-arrow/bullet deaths (which stay with their main-landed modules). Only
UNCLAIMED arms are ported, in ~10-kind commits.
### The seam (the gallop-dust queue→drain convention)
`crates/tr-app/src/projectile_death_dust.rs` owns the per-kind arms. The pool
cannot borrow the App's `DustPool` or hold the live `UpdateProjectiles` stream
alongside its `rng: &mut dyn DropRng` parameter (the pool-only tests pass a
`FastRandom`), so the wiring splits exactly like the Horseman gallop dust
(`world_sim/npcs.rs`, "W-10 unicorn tails"):
* **Death hook** (`projectile.rs`, the `!active` block, inside the
  `!died_out_of_world` gate beside the channel cancel): SNAPSHOTS the dying
  corpse (`DeathSnapshot::of` — kind/pos/box/velocity/scale) into
  `ProjectilePool::death_dust`. NO draws there; the snapshot is taken before
  any other death hook (gem/turret resize) mutates the slot, matching the C#
  `Kill()` reading the live slot throughout its body. The out-of-world guard's
  direct deactivate (`:16696`, no `Kill()`) never snapshots — same gate as the
  channel cancel.
* **Pass-tail drain** (`world_sim/projectiles.rs`, after the golf writeback):
  `drain_death_dust()` hands the snapshots to `projectile_death_dust::drain`,
  which resolves each C# arm onto the real `DustPool::new_dust` on the LIVE
  `UpdateProjectiles` stream (`app.rngs.stream`), with the App's `spawn_ctx`
  (the `Dust.cs:77-101` guards/cull). Every explicit `Main.rand` draw the arm
  takes AND the `new_dust` internals run there, in C# order, per death in slot
  order.
### Deviations (recorded)
* **Pass-tail draw placement.** The C# rolls the death dust mid-`Kill()`; the
  port defers ALL death-dust draws (explicit + internals) to the pass tail —
  the same recorded deviation as the gallop dust and the golf/celeb2 sound
  drains. Stream-neutral for the port's per-consumer streams; the
  `UpdateProjectiles` stream advances by the same total draw count, just at the
  tail rather than mid-walk.
* **The DustPool contract** (`origin/task/W4-d50-dust-type-table`): the bodies
  ride the verbatim `new_dust` family (guards, cull, pressure bands, default
  block, ChildSafety re-type, per-type tweak chain). The module only resolves
  the arm's arguments + post-spawn writes (`noGravity`, `velocity *=`,
  `scale *=`, `fadeIn`); the drain applies them to whatever slot `new_dust`
  returned — the sentinel 6000 included (the C# writes `Main.dust[6000]` too).
* **Sounds/gore skipped.** The `SoundEngine.PlaySound` cues and `Gore.NewGore`
  bodies in the death arms are the sound/gore lanes' (the pool-wide skip); only
  the dust is ported here. Where a gore draw sits BETWEEN dust draws in the C#
  body, the arm is deferred to a later commit that ports the gore census too
  (none in batch 1 — every batch-1 arm is dust-only).
